verses.text:
मनुम् एकाग्रम् आसीनम् अभिगम्य महर्षयः ।
प्रतिपूज्य यथान्यायम् इदं वचनम् अब्रुवन् ॥ १ ॥
verses.english: The great sages approached Manu, who was seated with a collected mind, and, having duly worshipped him, spoke as follows:

verses.text:
भगवन् सर्ववर्णानां यथावद् अनुपूर्वशः ।
अन्तरप्रभवानां च धर्मान् नो वक्तुम् अर्हसि ॥ २ ॥
verses.english: 'Deign, divine one, to declare to us precisely and in due order the sacred laws of each of the (four chief) castes (varna) and of the intermediate ones.

verses.text:
त्वम् एको ह्य् अस्य सर्वस्य विधानस्य स्वयम्भुवः ।
अचिन्त्यस्य-अप्रमेयस्य कार्यतत्त्वार्थवित् प्रभो ॥ ३ ॥
verses.english: 'For thou, O Lord, alone knowest the purport, (i.e.) the rites, and the knowledge of the soul, (taught) in this whole ordinance of the Self-existent (Svayambhu), which is unknowable and unfathomable.'

verses.text:
स तैः पृष्टस् तथा सम्यग् अमित.ओजा महात्मभिः ।
प्रत्युवाच-अर्च्य तान् सर्वान् महर्षीन्-श्रूयताम् इति ॥ ४ ॥
verses.english: He, whose power is measureless, being thus asked by the high-minded great sages, duly honoured them, and answered, 'Listen!'

verses.text:
आसीद् इदम् तमोभूतम् अ.प्रज्ञातम् अ.लक्षणम् ।
अ.प्रतर्क्यम् अ.विज्ञेयं प्रसुप्तम् इव सर्वतः ॥ ५ ॥
verses.english: This (universe) existed in the shape of Darkness, unperceived, destitute of distinctive marks, unattainable by reasoning, unknowable, wholly immersed, as it were, in deep sleep.

verses.text:
ततः स्वयम्भूर् भगवान् अव्यक्तो व्यञ्जयन्न् इदम् ।
महाभूतादि वृत्त.ओजाः प्रादुर् आसीत् तमोनुदः ॥ ६ ॥
verses.english: Then the divine Self-existent (Svayambhu, himself) indiscernible, (but) making (all) this, the great elements and the rest, discernible, appeared with irresistible (creative) power, dispelling the darkness.

verses.text:
यो ऽसाव् अतीन्द्रियग्राह्यः सूक्ष्मो ऽव्यक्तः सनातनः ।
सर्वभूतमयो ऽचिन्त्यः स एव स्वयम् उद्बभौ ॥ ७ ॥ १.०७च्व्/ म्: स
                                एष ॥ 1.7 ॥
verses.english: He who can be perceived by the internal organ (alone), who is subtile, indiscernible, and eternal, who contains all created beings and is inconceivable, shone forth of his own (will).

verses.text:
सो ऽभिध्याय शरीरात् स्वात् सिसृक्षुर् विविधाः प्रजाः ।
अप एव ससर्ज-आदौ तासु वीर्यम् अवासृजत् ॥ ८ ॥
verses.english: He, desiring to produce beings of many kinds from his own body, first with a thought created the waters, and placed his seed in them.

verses.text:
तद् अण्डम् अभवद्द् हैमं सहस्रांशुसम.प्रभम् ।
तस्मिञ् जज्ञे स्वयं ब्रह्मा सर्वलोकपितामहः ॥ ९ ॥
verses.english: That (seed) became a golden egg, in brilliancy equal to the sun; in that (egg) he himself was born as Brahman, the progenitor of the whole world.

verses.text:
आपो नरा इति प्रोक्ता आपो वै नरसूनवः ।
ता यद् अस्यायनं पूर्वं तेन नारायणः स्मृतः ॥ १० ॥
verses.english: The waters are called narah, (for) the waters are, indeed, the offspring of Nara; as they were his first residence (ayana), he thence is named Narayana.

verses.text:
यत् तत् कारणम् अव्यक्तं नित्यं सद्.असद्.आत्मकं ।
तद्.विसृष्टः स पुरुषो लोके ब्रह्मा-इति कीर्त्यते ॥ ११ ॥
verses.english: From that (first) cause, which is indiscernible, eternal, and both real and unreal, was produced that male (Purusha), who is famed in this world (under the appellation of) Brahman.

verses.text:
तस्मिन्न् अण्डे स भगवान् उषित्वा परिवत्सरम् ।
स्वयम् एवात्मनो ध्यानात् तद् अण्डम् अकरोद् द्विधा ॥ १२ ॥
verses.english: The divine one resided in that egg during a whole year, then he himself by his thought (alone) divided it into two halves;

verses.text:
ताभ्यां स शकलाभ्यां च दिवं भूमिं च निर्ममे ।
मध्ये व्योम दिशश् च-अष्टाव् अपां स्थानं च शाश्वतं ॥ १३ ॥
verses.english: And out of those two halves he formed heaven and earth, between them the middle sphere, the eight points of the horizon, and the eternal abode of the waters.

verses.text:
उद्बबर्ह-आत्मनश् च-एव मनः सद्.असद्.आत्मकम् ।
मनसश् च-अप्य् अहङ्कारम् अभिमन्तारम् ईश्वरम् ॥ १४ ॥ १.१४च्व्/ म्: 
                                अहङ्कारम् ॥ 1.14 ॥
verses.english: From himself (atmanah) he also drew forth the mind, which is both real and unreal, likewise from the mind egoism, which possesses the function of self-consciousness (and is) lordly;

verses.text:
महान्तम् एव च-आत्मानं सर्वाणि त्रि.गुणानि च ।
विषयाणां ग्रहीतॄणि शनैः पञ्च.इन्द्रियाणि च ॥ १५ ॥
verses.english: Moreover, the great one, the soul, and all (products) affected by the three qualities, and, in their order, the five organs which perceive the objects of sensation.

verses.text:
तेषां त्व् अवयवान् सूक्ष्मान् षण्णाम् अप्य् अमित.ओजसाम् ।
सन्निवेश्य-आत्ममात्रासु सर्वभूतानि निर्ममे ॥ १६ ॥ १.१६च्व्/ म्: 
                                सन्निवेश्य ॥ 1.16 ॥
verses.english: But, joining minute particles even of those six, which possess measureless power, with particles of himself, he created all beings.

verses.text:
यन् मूर्ति.अवयवाः सूक्ष्मास् तानि-इमान्य् आश्रयन्ति षट् ।
तस्मात्-शरीरम् इत्य् आहुस् तस्य मूर्तिं मनीषिणः ॥ १७ ॥
verses.english: Because those six (kinds of) minute particles, which form the (creator's) frame, enter (a-sri) these (creatures), therefore the wise call his frame sarira, (the body.)

verses.text:
तद् आविशन्ति भूतानि महान्ति सह कर्मभिः ।
मनश् च-अवयवैः सूक्ष्मैः सर्वभूतकृद् अव्ययम् ॥ १८ ॥
verses.english: That the great elements enter, together with their functions and the mind, through its minute parts the framer of all beings, the imperishable one.

verses.text:
तेषाम् इदं तु सप्तानां पुरुषाणां महा.ओजसाम् ।
सूक्ष्माभ्यो मूर्तिमात्राभ्यः सम्भवत्य् अव्ययाद् व्ययम् ॥ १९ ॥
verses.english: But from minute body (-framing) particles of these seven very powerful Purushas springs this (world), the perishable from the imperishable.

verses.text:
आद्याद्यस्य गुणं त्व् एषाम् अवाप्नोति परः परः ।
यो यो यावतिथश् च-एषां स स तावद् गुणः स्मृतः ॥ २० ॥
verses.english: Among them each succeeding (element) acquires the quality of the preceding one, and whatever place (in the sequence) each of them occupies, even so many qualities it is declared to possess.

verses.text:
सर्वेषां तु स नामानि कर्माणि च पृथक् पृथक् ।
वेदशब्देभ्य एव-आदौ पृथक् संस्थाश् च निर्ममे ॥ २१ ॥
verses.english: But in the beginning he assigned their several names, actions, and conditions to all (created beings), even according to the words of the Veda.

verses.text:
कर्मात्मनां च देवानां सो ऽसृजत् प्राणिनां प्रभुः ।
साध्यानां च गणं सूक्ष्मं यज्ञं च-एव सनातनम् ॥ २२ ॥
verses.english: He, the Lord, also created the class of the gods, who are endowed with life, and whose nature is action; and the subtile class of the Sadhyas, and the eternal sacrifice.

verses.text:
अग्नि.वायु.रविभ्यस् तु त्रयं ब्रह्म सनातनम् ।
दुदोह यज्ञसिद्धि.अर्थम् ऋच्.यजुस्.साम.लक्षणम् ॥ २३ ॥
verses.english: But from fire, wind, and the sun he drew forth the threefold eternal Veda, called Rik, Yagus, and Saman, for the due performance of the sacrifice.

verses.text:
कालं कालविभक्तीश् च नक्षत्राणि ग्रहांस् तथा ।
सरितः सागरान्-शैलान् समानि विषमानि च ॥ २४ ॥
verses.english: Time and the divisions of time, the lunar mansions and the planets, the rivers, the oceans, the mountains, plains, and uneven ground.

verses.text:
तपो वाचं रतिं च-एव कामं च क्रोधम् एव च ।
सृष्टिं ससर्ज च-एव-इमां स्रष्टुम् इच्छन्न् इमाः प्रजाः ॥ २५
                            ॥
verses.english: Austerity, speech, pleasure, desire, and anger, this whole creation he likewise produced, as he desired to call these beings into existence.

verses.text:
कर्मणां च विवेकार्थं धर्म.अधर्मौ व्यवेचयत् । १.२६अव्/ क्:
                                विवेकाय
द्वन्द्वैर् अयोजयच् च-इमाः सुख.दुःखादिभिः प्रजाः ॥ २६ ॥
verses.english: Moreover, in order to distinguish actions, he separated merit from demerit, and he caused the creatures to be affected by the pairs (of opposites), such as pain and pleasure.

verses.text:
अण्व्यो मात्रा विनाशिन्यो दशार्धानां तु याः स्मृताः ।
ताभिः सार्धम् इदं सर्वं सम्भवत्य् अनुपूर्वशः ॥ २७ ॥
verses.english: But with the minute perishable particles of the five (elements) which have been mentioned, this whole (world) is framed in due order.

verses.text:
यं तु कर्मणि यस्मिन् स न्ययुङ्क्त प्रथमं प्रभुः ।
स तद् एव स्वयं भेजे सृज्यमानः पुनः पुनः ॥ २८ ॥
verses.english: But to whatever course of action the Lord at first appointed each (kind of beings), that alone it has spontaneously adopted in each succeeding creation.

verses.text:
हिंस्र.अहिंस्रे मृदु.क्रूरे धर्म.अधर्माव् ऋत.अन्.ऋते ।
यद् यस्य सो ऽदधात् सर्गे तत् तस्य स्वयम् आविशत् ॥ २९ ॥
verses.english: Whatever he assigned to each at the (first) creation, noxiousness or harmlessness, gentleness or ferocity, virtue or sin, truth or falsehood, that clung (afterwards) spontaneously to it.

verses.text:
यथा-ऋतु.लिङ्गान्य् ऋतवः स्वयम् एव-ऋतुपर्यये ।
स्वानि स्वान्य् अभिपद्यन्ते तथा कर्माणि देहिनः ॥ ३० ॥
verses.english: As at the change of the seasons each season of its own accord assumes its distinctive marks, even so corporeal beings (resume in new births) their (appointed) course of action.

verses.text:
लोकानां तु विवृद्धि.अर्थं मुख.बाहु.ऊरु.पादतः ।
ब्राह्मणं क्षत्रियं वैश्यं शूद्रं च निरवर्तयत् ॥ ३१ ॥
verses.english: But for the sake of the prosperity of the worlds he caused the Brahmana, the Kshatriya, the Vaisya, and the Sudra to proceed from his mouth, his arms, his thighs, and his feet.

verses.text:
द्विधा कृत्वा-आत्मनो देहम् अर्धेन पुरुषो ऽभवत् ।
अर्धेन नारी तस्यां स विराजम् असृजत् प्रभुः ॥ ३२ ॥
verses.english: Dividing his own body, the Lord became half male and half female; with that (female) he produced Virag.

verses.text:
तपस् तप्त्वा-असृजद् यं तु स स्वयं पुरुषो विराट् ।
तं मां वित्त-अस्य सर्वस्य स्रष्टारं द्विजसत्तमाः ॥ ३३ ॥
verses.english: But know me, O most holy among the twice-born, to be the creator of this whole (world), whom that male, Virag, himself produced, having performed austerities.

verses.text:
अहं प्रजाः सिसृक्षुस् तु तपस् तप्त्वा सु.दुश्चरम् ।
पतीन् प्रजानाम् असृजं महर्षीन् आदितो दश ॥ ३४ ॥
verses.english: Then I, desiring to produce created beings, performed very difficult austerities, and (thereby) called into existence ten great sages, lords of created beings,

verses.text:
मरीचिम् अत्रि.अङ्गिरसौ पुलस्त्यं पुलहं क्रतुम् ।
प्रचेतसं वसिष्ठं च भृगुं नारदम् एव च ॥ ३५ ॥
verses.english: Mariki, Atri, Angiras, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, Praketas, Vasishtha, Bhrigu, and Narada.

verses.text:
एते मनूंस् तु सप्तान् यान् असृजन् भूरितेजसः ।
देवान् देवनिकायांश् च महर्षींश् च-अमित.ओजसः ॥ ३६ ॥
verses.english: They created seven other Manus possessing great brilliancy, gods and classes of gods and great sages of measureless power,

verses.text:
यक्ष.रक्षस्.पिशाचांश् च गन्धर्व.अप्सरसो ऽसुरान् ।
नागान् सर्पान् सुपर्णांश् च पितॄणांश् च पृथग्गणम् ॥ ३७ ॥ १.३७च्व्/ म्: 
                                पितॄणां ॥ 1.37 ॥
verses.english: Yakshas (the servants of Kubera, the demons called) Rakshasas and Pisakas, Gandharvas (or musicians of the gods), Apsarases (the dancers of the gods), Asuras, (the snake-deities called) Nagas and Sarpas, (the bird-deities called) Suparnas and the several classes of the manes,

verses.text:
विद्युतो ऽशनि.मेघांश् च रोहित.इन्द्रधनूंषि च ।
उल्का.निर्घात.केतूंश् च ज्योतींष्य् उच्चावचानि च ॥ ३८ ॥
verses.english: Lightnings, thunderbolts and clouds, imperfect (rohita) and perfect rainbows, falling meteors, supernatural noises, comets, and heavenly lights of many kinds,

verses.text:
किन्नरान् वानरान् मत्स्यान् विविधांश् च विहङ्गमान् ।
पशून् मृगान् मनुष्यांश् च व्यालांश् च-उभयतोदतः ॥ ३९ ॥

कृमि.कीट.पतङ्गांश् च यूका.मक्षिक.मत्कुणम् ।
सर्वं च दंश.मशकं स्थावरं च पृथग्विधम् ॥ ४० ॥
verses.english: Small and large worms and beetles, moths, lice, flies, bugs, all stinging and biting insects and the several kinds of immovable things.

verses.text:
एवम् एतैर् इदं सर्वं मद्.नियोगान् महात्मभिः ।
यथाकर्म तपोयोगात् सृष्टं स्थावर.जङ्गमम् ॥ ४१ ॥
verses.english: Thus was this whole (creation), both the immovable and the movable, produced by those high-minded ones by means of austerities and at my command, (each being) according to (the results of) its actions.

verses.text:
येषां तु यादृषं कर्म भूतानाम् इह कीर्तितम् ।
तत् तथा वो ऽभिधास्यामि क्रमयोगं च जन्मनि ॥ ४२ ॥
verses.english: But whatever act is stated (to belong) to (each of) those creatures here below, that I will truly declare to you, as well as their order in respect to birth.

verses.text:
पशवश् च मृगाश् च-एव व्यालाश् च-उभयतोदतः ।
रक्षांसि च पिशाचाश् च मनुष्याश् च जरायुजाः ॥ ४३ ॥ १.४३च्व्/ म्: मनुषाश्
                                च ॥ 1.43 ॥
verses.english: Cattle, deer, carnivorous beasts with two rows of teeth, Rakshasas, Pisakas, and men are born from the womb.

verses.text:
अण्डाजाः पक्षिणः सर्पा नक्रा मत्स्याश् च कच्छपाः ।
यानि च-एवं.प्रकाराणि स्थलजान्य् औदकानि च ॥ ४४ ॥
verses.english: From eggs are born birds, snakes, crocodiles, fishes, tortoises, as well as similar terrestrial and aquatic (animals).

verses.text:
स्वेदजं दंश.मशकं यूका.मक्षिक.मत्कुणम् ।
ऊष्मणश् च-उपजायन्ते यच् च-अन्यत् किं चिद् ईदृषम् ॥ ४५ ॥
verses.english: From hot moisture spring stinging and biting insects, lice, flies, bugs, and all other (creatures) of that kind which are produced by heat.

verses.text:
उद्भिज्जाः स्थावराः सर्वे बीज.काण्डप्ररोहिणः ।
ओषध्यः फलपाकान्ता बहु.पुष्प.फल.उपगाः ॥ ४६ ॥
verses.english: All plants, propagated by seed or by slips, grow from shoots; annual plants (are those) which, bearing many flowers and fruits, perish after the ripening of their fruit;

verses.text:
अपुष्पाः फलवन्तो ये ते वनस्पतयः स्मृताः ।
पुष्पिणः फलिनश् च-एव वृक्षास् तु-उभयतः स्मृताः ॥ ४७ ॥
verses.english: (Those trees) which bear fruit without flowers are called vanaspati (lords of the forest); but those which bear both flowers and fruit are called vriksha.

verses.text:
गुच्छ.गुल्मं तु विविधं तथा-एव तृणजातयः ।
बीज.काण्डरुहाण्य् एव प्रताना वल्ल्य एव च ॥ ४८ ॥
verses.english: But the various plants with many stalks, growing from one or several roots, the different kinds of grasses, the climbing plants and the creepers spring all from seed or from slips.

verses.text:
तमसा बहु.रूपेण वेष्टिताः कर्महेतुना ।
अन्तः.सञ्ज्ञा भवन्त्य् एते सुख.दुःख.समन्विताः ॥ ४९ ॥
verses.english: These (plants) which are surrounded by multiform Darkness, the result of their acts (in former existences), possess internal consciousness and experience pleasure and pain.

verses.text:
एतद्.अन्तास् तु गतयो ब्रह्माद्याः समुदाहृताः ।
घोरे ऽस्मिन् भूतसंसारे नित्यं सततयायिनि ॥ ५० ॥
verses.english: The (various) conditions in this always terrible and constantly changing circle of births and deaths to which created beings are subject, are stated to begin with (that of) Brahman, and to end with (that of) these (just mentioned immovable creatures).

verses.text:
एवं सर्वं स सृष्ट्वा-इदं मां च-अचिन्त्य.पराक्रमः ।
आत्मन्य् अन्तर्दधे भूयः कालं कालेन पीडयन् ॥ ५१ ॥
verses.english: When he whose power is incomprehensible, had thus produced the universe and men, he disappeared in himself, repeatedly suppressing one period by means of the other.

verses.text:
यदा स देवो जागर्ति तद् एवं चेष्टते जगत् ।
यदा स्वपिति शान्त.आत्मा तदा सर्वं निमीलति ॥ ५२ ॥
verses.english: When that divine one wakes, then this world stirs; when he slumbers tranquilly, then the universe sinks to sleep.

verses.text:
तस्मिन् स्वपिति तु स्वस्थे कर्म.आत्मानः शरीरिणः । १.५३अव्/ म्: 
                                स्वपति
स्वकर्मभ्यो निवर्तन्ते मनश् च ग्लानिम् ऋच्छति ॥ ५३ ॥
verses.english: But when he reposes in calm sleep, the corporeal beings whose nature is action, desist from their actions and mind becomes inert.

verses.text:
युगपत् तु प्रलीयन्ते यदा तस्मिन् महात्मनि ।
तदा-अयं सर्वभूतात्मा सुखं स्वपिति निर्वृतः ॥ ५४ ॥
verses.english: When they are absorbed all at once in that great soul, then he who is the soul of all beings sweetly slumbers, free from all care and occupation.

verses.text:
तमो ऽयं तु समाश्रित्य चिरं तिष्ठति स.इन्द्रियः ।
न च स्वं कुरुते कर्म तदा-उत्क्रामति मूर्तितः ॥ ५५ ॥
verses.english: When this (soul) has entered darkness, it remains for a long time united with the organs (of sensation), but performs not its functions; it then leaves the corporeal frame.

verses.text:
यदा-अणुमात्रिको भूत्वा बीजं स्थास्नु चरिष्णु च ।
समाविशति संसृष्टस् तदा मूर्तिं विमुञ्चति ॥ ५६ ॥
verses.english: When, being clothed with minute particles (only), it enters into vegetable or animal seed, it then assumes, united (with the fine body), a (new) corporeal frame.

verses.text:
एवं स जाग्रत्.स्वप्नाभ्याम् इदं सर्वं चर.अचरम् ।
सञ्जीवयति च-अजस्रं प्रमापयति च-अव्ययः ॥ ५७ ॥
verses.english: Thus he, the imperishable one, by (alternately) waking and slumbering, incessantly revivifies and destroys this whole movable and immovable (creation).

verses.text:
इदं शास्त्रं तु कृत्वा-असौ माम् एव स्वयम् आदितः ।
विधिवद् ग्राहयाम् आस मरीचि.आदींस् त्व् अहं मुनीन् ॥ ५८ ॥
verses.english: But he having composed these Institutes (of the sacred law), himself taught them, according to the rule, to me alone in the beginning; next I (taught them) to Mariki and the other sages.

verses.text:
एतद् वो ऽयं भृगुः शास्त्रं श्रावयिष्यत्य् अशेसतः ।
एतद्द् हि मत्तो ऽधिजगे सर्वम् एषो ऽखिलं मुनिः ॥ ५९ ॥
verses.english: Bhrigu, here, will fully recite to you these Institutes; for that sage learned the whole in its entirety from me.

verses.text:
ततस् तथा स तेन-उक्तो महर्षि.मनुना भृगुः ।
तान् अब्रवीद् ऋषीन् सर्वान् प्रीतात्मा श्रूयताम् इति ॥ ६० ॥
verses.english: Then that great sage Bhrigu, being thus addressed by Manu, spoke, pleased in his heart, to all the sages, 'Listen!'

verses.text:
स्वायम्भुवस्य-अस्य मनोः षड्वंश्या मनवो ऽपरे ।
सृष्टवन्तः प्रजाः स्वाः स्वा महात्मानो महा.ओजसः ॥ ६१ ॥
verses.english: Six other high-minded, very powerful Manus, who belong to the race of this Manu, the descendant of the Self-existent (Svayambhu), and who have severally produced created beings,

verses.text:
स्वारोचिषश् च-उत्तमश् च तामसो रैवतस् तथा ।
चाक्षुषश् च महातेजा विवस्वत्.सुत एव च ॥ ६२ ॥
verses.english: (Are) Svarokisha, Auttami, Tamasa, Raivata, Kakshusha, possessing great lustre, and the son of Vivasvat.

verses.text:
स्वायम्भुव.आद्याः सप्त-एते मनवो भूरितेजसः ।
स्वे स्वे ऽन्तरे सर्वम् इदम् उत्पाद्य-आपुश् चर.अचरम् ॥ ६३ ॥
verses.english: These seven very glorious Manus, the first among whom is Svayambhuva, produced and protected this whole movable and immovable (creation), each during the period (allotted to him).

verses.text:
निमेषा दश च-अष्टौ च काष्ठा त्रिंशत् तु ताः कला ।
त्रिंशत् कला मुहूर्तः स्याद् अहोरात्रं तु तावतः ॥ ६४ ॥
verses.english: Eighteen nimeshas (twinklings of the eye, are one kashtha), thirty kashthas one kala, thirty kalas one muhurta, and as many (muhurtas) one day and night.

verses.text:
अहोरात्रे विभजते सूर्यो मानुष.दैविके ।
रात्रिः स्वप्नाय भूतानां चेष्टायै कर्मणाम् अहः ॥ ६५ ॥
verses.english: The sun divides days and nights, both human and divine, the night (being intended) for the repose of created beings and the day for exertion.

verses.text:
पित्र्ये रात्रि.अहनी मासः प्रविभागस् तु पक्षयोः ।
कर्म.चेष्टास्व् अहः कृष्णः शुक्लः स्वप्नाय शर्वरी ॥ ६६ ॥
verses.english: A month is a day and a night of the manes, but the division is according to fortnights. The dark (fortnight) is their day for active exertion, the bright (fortnight) their night for sleep.

verses.text:
दैवे रात्रि.अहनी वर्षं प्रविभागस् तयोः पुनः ।
अहस् तत्र-उदगयनं रात्रिः स्याद् दक्षिणायनम् ॥ ६७ ॥
verses.english: A year is a day and a night of the gods; their division is (as follows): the half year during which the sun progresses to the north will be the day, that during which it goes southwards the night.

verses.text:
ब्राह्मस्य तु क्षपाहस्य यत् प्रमाणं समासतः ।
एकैकशो युगानां तु क्रमशस् तन् निबोधत ॥ ६८ ॥
verses.english: But hear now the brief (description of) the duration of a night and a day of Brahman and of the several ages (of the world, yuga) according to their order.

verses.text:
चत्वार्य् आहुः सहस्राणि वर्साणां तत् कृतं युगम् ।
तस्य तावत्-शती सन्ध्या सन्ध्यांशश् च तथाविधः ॥ ६९ ॥
verses.english: They declare that the Krita age (consists of) four thousand years (of the gods); the twilight preceding it consists of as many hundreds, and the twilight following it of the same number.

verses.text:
इतरेषु स.सन्ध्येषु स.सन्ध्यांशेषु च त्रिषु ।
एकापायेन वर्तन्ते सहस्राणि शतानि च ॥ ७० ॥
verses.english: In the other three ages with their twilights preceding and following, the thousands and hundreds are diminished by one (in each).

verses.text:
यद् एतत् परिसङ्ख्यातम् आदाव् एव चतुर्युगम् ।
एतद् द्वादशसाहस्रं देवानां युगम् उच्यते ॥ ७१ ॥
verses.english: These twelve thousand (years) which thus have been just mentioned as the total of four (human) ages, are called one age of the gods.

verses.text:
दैविकानां युगानां तु सहस्रं परिसङ्ख्यया ।
ब्राह्मम् एकम् अहर् ज्ञेयं तावतीं रात्रिम् एव च ॥ ७२ ॥ १.७२च्व्/ म्: तावती
                                रात्रिर् एव च ॥ 1.72 ॥
verses.english: But know that the sum of one thousand ages of the gods (makes) one day of Brahman, and that his night has the same length.

verses.text:
तद् वै युगसहस्रान्तं ब्राह्मं पुण्यम् अहर् विदुः ।
रात्रिं च तावतीम् एव ते ऽहोरात्रविदो जनाः ॥ ७३ ॥
verses.english: Those (only, who) know that the holy day of Brahman, indeed, ends after (the completion of) one thousand ages (of the gods) and that his night lasts as long, (are really) men acquainted with (the length of) days and nights.

verses.text:
तस्य सो ऽहर्.निशस्य-अन्ते प्रसुप्तः प्रतिबुध्यते ।
प्रतिबुद्धश् च सृजति मनः सद्.असद्.आत्मकम् ॥ ७४ ॥
verses.english: At the end of that day and night he who was asleep, awakes and, after awaking, creates mind, which is both real and unreal.

verses.text:
मनः सृष्टिं विकुरुते चोद्यमानं सिसृक्षया ।
आकाशं जायते तस्मात् तस्य शब्दं गुणं विदुः ॥ ७५ ॥
verses.english: Mind, impelled by (Brahman's) desire to create, performs the work of creation by modifying itself, thence ether is produced; they declare that sound is the quality of the latter.

verses.text:
आकाशात् तु विकुर्वाणात् सर्वगन्धवहः शुचिः ।
बलवाञ् जायते वायुः स वै स्पर्श.गुणो मतः ॥ ७६ ॥
verses.english: But from ether, modifying itself, springs the pure, powerful wind, the vehicle of all perfumes; that is held to possess the quality of touch.

verses.text:
वायोर् अपि विकुर्वाणाद् विरोचिष्णु तमोनुदम् ।
ज्योतिर् उत्पद्यते भास्वत् तद् रूप.गुणम् उच्यते ॥ ७७ ॥
verses.english: Next from wind modifying itself, proceeds the brilliant light, which illuminates and dispels darkness; that is declared to possess the quality of colour;

verses.text:
ज्योतिषश् च विकुर्वाणाद् आपो रस.गुणाः स्मृताः ।
अद्भ्यो गन्ध.गुणा भूमिर् इत्य् एषा सृष्टिर् आदितः ॥ ७८ ॥
verses.english: And from light, modifying itself, (is produced) water, possessing the quality of taste, from water earth which has the quality of smell; such is the creation in the beginning.

verses.text:
यद् प्राग् द्वादशसाहस्रम् उदितं दैविकं युगम् ।
तद् एकसप्तति.गुणं मन्वन्तरम् इह-उच्यते ॥ ७९ ॥
verses.english: The before-mentioned age of the gods, (or) twelve thousand (of their years), being multiplied by seventy-one, (constitutes what) is here named the period of a Manu (Manvantara).

verses.text:
मन्वन्तराण्य् असङ्ख्यानि सर्गः संहार एव च ।
क्रीडन्न् इव-एतत् कुरुते परमेष्ठी पुनः पुनः ॥ ८० ॥
verses.english: The Manvantaras, the creations and destructions (of the world, are) numberless; sporting, as it were, Brahman repeats this again and again.

verses.text:
चतुष्पात् सकलो धर्मः सत्यं च-एव कृते युगे ।
न-अधर्मेण-आगमः कश् चिन् मनुष्यान् प्रति वर्तते ॥ ८१ ॥ १.८१च्व्/ म्: 
                                उपवर्तते ॥ 1.81 ॥
verses.english: In the Krita age Dharma is four-footed and entire, and (so is) Truth; nor does any gain accrue to men by unrighteousness.

verses.text:
इतरेष्व् आगमाद् धर्मः पादशस् त्व् अवरोपितः ।
चौरिक.अनृत.मायाभिर् धर्मश् च-अपैति पादशः ॥ ८२ ॥
verses.english: In the other (three ages), by reason of (unjust) gains (agama), Dharma is deprived successively of one foot, and through (the prevalence of) theft, falsehood, and fraud the merit (gained by men) is diminished by one fourth (in each).

verses.text:
अ.रोगाः सर्वसिद्धार्थाश् चतुर्वर्षशत.आयुषः ।
कृते त्रेतादिषु ह्य् एषां आयुर् ह्रसति पादशः ॥ ८३ ॥ १.८३च्व्/ व्: वयो
                                ह्रसति ॥ 1.83 ॥
verses.english: (Men are) free from disease, accomplish all their aims, and live four hundred years in the Krita age, but in the Treta and (in each of) the succeeding (ages) their life is lessened by one quarter.

verses.text:
वेद.उक्तम् आयुर् मर्त्यानाम् आशिषश् च-एव कर्मणाम् ।
फलन्त्य् अनुयुगं लोके प्रभावश् च शरीरिणाम् ॥ ८४ ॥
verses.english: The life of mortals, mentioned in the Veda, the desired results of sacrificial rites and the (supernatural) power of embodied (spirits) are fruits proportioned among men according to (the character of) the age.

verses.text:
अन्ये कृतयुगे धर्मास् त्रेतायां द्वापरे ऽपरे । १.८५अव्/ म्: 
                            परे
अन्ये कलियुगे नॄणां युगह्रासानुरूपतः ॥ ८५ ॥
verses.english: One set of duties (is prescribed) for men in the Krita age, different ones in the Treta and in the Dvapara, and (again) another (set) in the Kali, in a proportion as (those) ages decrease in length.

verses.text:
तपः परं कृतयुगे त्रेतायां ज्ञानम् उच्यते ।
द्वापरे यज्ञम् एवाहुर् दानम् एकं कलौ युगे ॥ ८६ ॥
verses.english: In the Krita age the chief (virtue) is declared to be (the performance of) austerities, in the Treta (divine) knowledge, in the Dvapara (the performance of) sacrifices, in the Kali liberality alone.

verses.text:
सर्वस्य-अस्य तु सर्गस्य गुप्ति.अर्थं स महा.द्युतिः ।
मुख.बाहु.ऊरु.पज्जानां पृथक्कर्माण्य् अकल्पयत् ॥ ८७ ॥
verses.english: But in order to protect this universe He, the most resplendent one, assigned separate (duties and) occupations to those who sprang from his mouth, arms, thighs, and feet.

verses.text:
अध्यापनम् अध्ययनं यजनं याजनं तथा ।
दानं प्रतिग्रहं च-एव ब्राह्मणानाम् अकल्पयत् ॥ ८८ ॥
verses.english: To Brahmanas he assigned teaching and studying (the Veda), sacrificing for their own benefit and for others, giving and accepting (of alms).

verses.text:
प्रजानां रक्षणं दानम् इज्या.अध्ययनम् एव च ।
विषयेष्व् अ.प्रसक्तिश् च क्षत्रियस्य समासतः ॥ ८९ ॥ १.८९च्व्/ म्: 
                                समादिशत् ॥ 1.89 ॥
verses.english: The Kshatriya he commanded to protect the people, to bestow gifts, to offer sacrifices, to study (the Veda), and to abstain from attaching himself to sensual pleasures;

verses.text:
पशूनां रक्षणं दानम् इज्या.अध्ययनम् एव च ।
वणिक्पथं कुसीदं च वैश्यस्य कृषिम् एव च ॥ ९० ॥
verses.english: The Vaisya to tend cattle, to bestow gifts, to offer sacrifices, to study (the Veda), to trade, to lend money, and to cultivate land.

verses.text:
एकम् एव तु शूद्रस्य प्रभुः कर्म समादिशत् ।
एतेषाम् एव वर्णानां शुश्रूषाम् अनसूयया ॥ ९१ ॥
verses.english: One occupation only the lord prescribed to the Sudra, to serve meekly even these (other) three castes.

verses.text:
ऊर्ध्वं नाभेर् मेध्यतरः पुरुषः परिकीर्तितः ।
तस्मान् मेध्यतमं त्व् अस्य मुखम् उक्तं स्वयम्भुवा ॥ ९२ ॥
verses.english: Man is stated to be purer above the navel (than below); hence the Self-existent (Svayambhu) has declared the purest (part) of him (to be) his mouth.

verses.text:
उत्तमाङ्ग.उद्भवाज् ज्येष्ठ्याद् ब्रह्मणश् च-एव धारणात् । १.९३अव्/ म्: 
                                ज्यैष्ठ्याद्
सर्वस्य-एव-अस्य सर्गस्य धर्मतो ब्राह्मणः प्रभुः ॥ ९३
                            ॥
verses.english: As the Brahmana sprang from (Brahman's) mouth, as he was the first-born, and as he possesses the Veda, he is by right the lord of this whole creation.

verses.text:
तं हि स्वयम्भूः स्वाद् आस्यात् तपस् तप्त्वा-आदितो ऽसृजत् ।
हव्य.कव्याभिवाह्याय सर्वस्य-अस्य च गुप्तये ॥ ९४ ॥
verses.english: For the Self-existent (Svayambhu), having performed austerities, produced him first from his own mouth, in order that the offerings might be conveyed to the gods and manes and that this universe might be preserved.

verses.text:
यस्य-आस्येन सदा-अश्नन्ति हव्यानि त्रिदिव.ओकसः ।
कव्यानि च-एव पितरः किं भूतम् अधिकं ततः ॥ ९५ ॥
verses.english: What created being can surpass him, through whose mouth the gods continually consume the sacrificial viands and the manes the offerings to the dead?

verses.text:
भूतानां प्राणिनः श्रेष्ठाः प्राणिनां बुद्धिजीविनः ।
बुद्धिमत्सु नराः श्रेष्ठा नरेषु ब्राह्मणाः स्मृताः ॥ ९६ ॥
verses.english: Of created beings the most excellent are said to be those which are animated; of the animated, those which subsist by intelligence; of the intelligent, mankind; and of men, the Brahmanas;

verses.text:
ब्राह्मणेषु च विद्वांसो विद्वत्सु कृत.बुद्धयः ।
कृत.बुद्धिषु कर्तारः कर्तृषु ब्रह्मवेदिनः ॥ ९७ ॥
verses.english: Of Brahmanas, those learned (in the Veda); of the learned, those who recognise (the necessity and the manner of performing the prescribed duties); of those who possess this knowledge, those who perform them; of the performers, those who know the Brahman.

verses.text:
उत्पत्तिर् एव विप्रस्य मूर्तिर् धर्मस्य शाश्वती ।
स हि धर्मार्थम् उत्पन्नो ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते ॥ ९८ ॥
verses.english: The very birth of a Brahmana is an eternal incarnation of the sacred law; for he is born to (fulfil) the sacred law, and becomes one with Brahman.

verses.text:
ब्राह्मणो जायमानो हि पृथिव्याम् अधिजायते ।
ईश्वरः सर्वभूतानां धर्मकोशस्य गुप्तये ॥ ९९ ॥
verses.english: A Brahmana, coming into existence, is born as the highest on earth, the lord of all created beings, for the protection of the treasury of the law.

verses.text:
सर्वं स्वं ब्राह्मणस्य-इदं यत् किं चित्-जगतीगतं ।
श्रैष्ठ्येन-अभिजनेन-इदं सर्वं वै ब्राह्मणो ऽर्हति ॥ १००
                            ॥
verses.english: Whatever exists in the world is, the property of the Brahmana; on account of the excellence of his origin The Brahmana is, indeed, entitled to all.

verses.text:
स्वम् एव ब्राह्मणो भुङ्क्ते स्वं वस्ते स्वं ददाति च ।
आनृशंस्याद् ब्राह्मणस्य भुञ्जते हि-इतरे जनाः ॥ १०१ ॥
verses.english: The Brahmana eats but his own food, wears but his own apparel, bestows but his own in alms; other mortals subsist through the benevolence of the Brahmana.

verses.text:
तस्य कर्मविवेक.अर्थं शेषाणाम् अनुपूर्वशः ।
स्वायम्भुवो मनुर् धीमान् इदं शास्त्रम् अकल्पयत् ॥ १०२ ॥
verses.english: In order to clearly settle his duties those of the other (castes) according to their order, wise Manu sprung from the Self-existent, composed these Institutes (of the sacred Law).

verses.text:
विदुषा ब्राह्मणेन-इदम् अध्येतव्यं प्रयत्नतः ।
शिश्येभ्यश् च प्रवक्तव्यं सम्यङ् न-अन्येन केन चित् ॥ १०३
                            ॥
verses.english: A learned Brahmana must carefully study them, and he must duly instruct his pupils in them, but nobody else (shall do it).

verses.text:
इदं शास्त्रम् अधीयानो ब्राह्मणः शंसित.व्रतः ।
मनस्.वाच्.देहजैर् नित्यं कर्मदोषैर् न लिप्यते ॥ १०४ ॥
verses.english: A Brahmana who studies these Institutes (and) faithfully fulfils the duties (prescribed therein), is never tainted by sins, arising from thoughts, words, or deeds.

verses.text:
पुनाति पङ्क्तिं वंश्यांश् च सप्त.सप्त पर.अवरान् ।
पृथिवीम् अपि च-एव-इमां कृत्स्नाम् एको ऽपि सो ऽर्हति ॥ १०५ ॥
verses.english: He sanctifies any company (which he may enter), seven ancestors and seven descendants, and he alone deserves (to possess) this whole earth.

verses.text:
इदं स्वस्त्ययनं श्रेष्ठम् इदं बुद्धिविवर्धनम् ।
इदं यशस्यम् आयुष्यम् इदं निःश्रेयसं परम् ॥ १०६ ॥ १.१०६च्व्/ म्: इदं
                                यशस्यं सततम् ॥ 1.106 ॥
verses.english: (To study) this (work) is the best means of securing welfare, it increases understanding, it procures fame and long life, it (leads to) supreme bliss.

verses.text:
अस्मिन् धर्मो ऽखिलेन-उक्तो गुण.दोषौ च कर्मणाम् ।
चतुर्णाम् अपि वर्णानाम् आचारश् च-एव शाश्वतः ॥ १०७ ॥
verses.english: In this (work) the sacred law has been fully stated as well as the good and bad qualities of (human) actions and the immemorial rule of conduct, (to be followed) by all the four castes (varna).

verses.text:
आचारः परमो धर्मः श्रुति.उक्तः स्मार्त एव च ।
तस्माद् अस्मिन् सदा युक्तो नित्यं स्याद् आत्मवान् द्विजः ॥ १०८ ॥
verses.english: The rule of conduct is transcendent law, whether it be taught in the revealed texts or in the sacred tradition; hence a twice-born man who possesses regard for himself, should be always careful to (follow) it.

verses.text:
आचाराद् विच्युतो विप्रो न वेदफलम् अश्नुते ।
आचारेण तु संयुक्तः सम्पूर्णफलभाज् भवेत् ॥ १०९ ॥ १.१०९च्व्/ म्: 
                                सम्पूर्णफलभाक् स्मृतः ॥ 1.109 ॥
verses.english: A Brahmana who departs from the rule of conduct, does not reap the fruit of the Veda, but he who duly follows it, will obtain the full reward.

verses.text:
एवम् आचारतो दृष्ट्वा धर्मस्य मुनयो गतिं ।
सर्वस्य तपसो मूलम् आचारं जगृहुः परम् ॥ ११० ॥
verses.english: The sages who saw that the sacred law is thus grounded on the rule of conduct, have taken good conduct to be the most excellent root of all austerity.

verses.text:
जगतश् च समुत्पत्तिं संस्कारविधिम् एव च ।
व्रतचर्या.उपचारं च स्नानस्य च परं विधिम् ॥ १११ ॥
verses.english: The creation of the universe, the rule of the sacraments, the ordinances of studentship, and the respectful behaviour (towards Gurus), the most excellent rule of bathing (on return from the teacher's house),

verses.text:
दाराधिगमनं च-एव विवाहानां च लक्षणम् ।
महायज्ञविधानं च श्राद्धकल्पं च शाश्वतम् ॥ ११२ ॥
verses.english: (The law of) marriage and the description of the (various) marriage-rites, the regulations for the great sacrifices and the eternal rule of the funeral sacrifices,

verses.text:
वृत्तीनां लक्षणं च-एव स्नातकस्य व्रतानि च ।
भक्ष्य.अभक्ष्यं च शौचं च द्रव्याणां शुद्धिम् एव च ॥ ११३
                            ॥
verses.english: The description of the modes of (gaining) subsistence and the duties of a Snataka, (the rules regarding) lawful and forbidden food, the purification of men and of things,

verses.text:
स्त्रीधर्म.योगं तापस्यं मोक्षं सन्न्यासम् एव च ।
राज्ञश् च धर्मम् अखिलं कार्याणां च विनिर्णयम् ॥ ११४ ॥
verses.english: The laws concerning women, (the law) of hermits, (the manner of gaining) final emancipation and (of) renouncing the world, the whole duty of a king and the manner of deciding lawsuits,

verses.text:
साक्षिप्रश्न.विधानं च धर्मं स्त्री.पुंसयोर् अपि ।
विभागधर्मं द्यूतं च कण्टकानां च शोधनम् ॥ ११५ ॥
verses.english: The rules for the examination of witnesses, the laws concerning husband and wife, the law of (inheritance and) division, (the law concerning) gambling and the removal of (men nocuous like) thorns,

verses.text:
वैश्य.शूद्र.उपचारं च सङ्कीर्णानां च सम्भवम् ।
आपद्.धर्मं च वर्णानां प्रायश्चित्त.विधिं तथा ॥ ११६ ॥
verses.english: (The law concerning) the behaviour of Vaisyas and Sudras, the origin of the mixed castes, the law for all castes in times of distress and the law of penances,

verses.text:
संसारगमनं च-एव त्रिविधं कर्म.सम्भवम् ।
निःश्रेयसं कर्मणां च गुण.दोषपरीक्षणम् ॥ ११७ ॥
verses.english: The threefold course of transmigrations, the result of (good or bad) actions, (the manner of attaining) supreme bliss and the examination of the good and bad qualities of actions,

verses.text:
देशधर्मान्-जातिधर्मान् कुलधर्मांश् च शाश्वतान् ।
पाषण्ड.गणधर्मांश् च शास्त्रे ऽस्मिन्न् उक्तवान् मनुः ॥ ११८
                            ॥
verses.english: The primeval laws of countries, of castes (gati), of families, and the rules concerning heretics and companies (of traders and the like)- (all that) Manu has declared in these Institutes.

verses.text:
यथा-इदम् उक्तवान्-शास्त्रं पुरा पृष्टो मनुर् मया ।
तथा-इदं यूयम् अप्य् अद्य मत्.सकाशात्-निबोधत ॥ ११९ ॥
verses.english: As Manu, in reply to my questions, formerly promulgated these Institutes, even so learn ye also the (whole work) from me.

verses.text:
विद्वद्भिः सेवितः सद्भिर् नित्यम् अ.द्वेष.रागिभिः ।
हृदयेन-अभ्यनुज्ञातो यो धर्मस् तं निबोधत ॥ १ ॥
verses.english: Learn that sacred law which is followed by men learned (in the Veda) and assented to in their hearts by the virtuous, who are ever exempt from hatred and inordinate affection.

verses.text:
कामात्मता न प्रशस्ता न च-एव-इह-अस्त्य् अकामता ।
काम्यो हि वेदाधिगमः कर्मयोगश् च वैदिकः ॥ २ ॥
verses.english: To act solely from a desire for rewards is not laudable, yet an exemption from that desire is not (to be found) in this (world): for on (that) desire is grounded the study of the Veda and the performance of the actions, prescribed by the Veda.

verses.text:
सङ्कल्प.मूलः कामो वै यज्ञाः सङ्कल्प.सम्भवाः ।
व्रतानि यमधर्माश् च सर्वे सङ्कल्पजाः स्मृताः ॥ ३ ॥
verses.english: The desire (for rewards), indeed, has its root in the conception that an act can yield them, and in consequence of (that) conception sacrifices are performed; vows and the laws prescribing restraints are all stated to be kept through the idea that they will bear fruit.

verses.text:
अ.कामस्य क्रिया का चिद् दृश्यते न-इह कर्हि चित् ।
यद् यद्द् हि कुरुते किं चित् तत् तत् कामस्य चेष्टितम् ॥ ४
                                ॥
verses.english: Not a single act here (below) appears ever to be done by a man free from desire; for whatever (man) does, it is (the result of) the impulse of desire.

verses.text:
तेषु सम्यग् वर्तमानो गच्छत्य् अमरलोकताम् ।
यथा सङ्कल्पितांश् च-इह सर्वान् कामान् समश्नुते ॥ ५ ॥
verses.english: He who persists in discharging these (prescribed duties) in the right manner, reaches the deathless state and even in this (life) obtains (the fulfilment of) all the desires that he may have conceived.

verses.text:
वेदो ऽखिलो धर्ममूलं स्मृति.शीले च तद्विदाम् ।
आचारश् च-एव साधूनाम् आत्मनस् तुष्टिर् एव च ॥ ६ ॥
verses.english: The whole Veda is the (first) source of the sacred law, next the tradition and the virtuous conduct of those who know the (Veda further), also the customs of holy men, and (finally) self-satisfaction.

verses.text:
यः कश् चित् कस्य चिद् धर्मो मनुना परिकीर्तितः ।
स सर्वो ऽभिहितो वेदे सर्वज्ञानमयो हि सः ॥ ७ ॥
verses.english: Whatever law has been ordained for any (person) by Manu, that has been fully declared in the Veda: for that (sage was) omniscient.

verses.text:
सर्वं तु समवेक्ष्य-इदं निखिलं ज्ञानचक्षुषा ।
श्रुतिप्रामाण्यतो विद्वान् स्वधर्मे निविशेत वै ॥ ८ ॥
verses.english: But a learned man after fully scrutinising all this with the eye of knowledge, should, in accordance with the authority of the revealed texts, be intent on (the performance of) his duties.

verses.text:
श्रुति.स्मृति.उदितं धर्मम् अनुतिष्ठन् हि मानवः ।
इह कीर्तिम् अवाप्नोति प्रेत्य च-अनुत्तमं सुखम् ॥ ९ ॥
verses.english: For that man who obeys the law prescribed in the revealed texts and in the sacred tradition, gains fame in this (world) and after death unsurpassable bliss.

verses.text:
श्रुतिस् तु वेदो विज्ञेयो धर्मशास्त्रं तु वै स्मृतिः ।
ते सर्वार्थेष्व् अ.मीमांस्ये ताभ्यां धर्मो हि निर्बभौ ॥ १०
                                ॥
verses.english: But by Sruti (revelation) is meant the Veda, and by Smriti (tradition) the Institutes of the sacred law: those two must not be called into question in any matter, since from those two the sacred law shone forth.

verses.text:
यो ऽवमन्येत ते मूले हेतुशास्त्राश्रयाद् द्विजः ।
स साधुभिर् बहिष्कार्यो नास्तिको वेदनिन्दकः ॥ ११ ॥
verses.english: Every twice-born man, who, relying on the Institutes of dialectics, treats with contempt those two sources (of the law), must be cast out by the virtuous, as an atheist and a scorner of the Veda.

verses.text:
वेदः स्मृतिः सदाचारः स्वस्य च प्रियम् आत्मनः ।
एतच् चतुर्विधं प्राहुः साक्षाद् धर्मस्य लक्षणम् ॥ १२
                                ॥
verses.english: The Veda, the sacred tradition, the customs of virtuous men, and one's own pleasure, they declare to be visibly the fourfold means of defining the sacred law.

verses.text:
अर्थ.कामेष्व् अ.सक्तानां धर्मज्ञानं विधीयते ।
धर्मं जिज्ञासमानानां प्रमाणं परमं श्रुतिः ॥ १३ ॥
verses.english: The knowledge of the sacred law is prescribed for those who are not given to the acquisition of wealth and to the gratification of their desires; to those who seek the knowledge of the sacred law the supreme authority is the revelation (Sruti).

verses.text:
श्रुतिद्वैधं तु यत्र स्यात् तत्र धर्माव् उभौ स्मृतौ ।
उभाव् अपि हि तौ धर्मौ सम्यग् उक्तौ मनीषिभिः ॥ १४ ॥
verses.english: But when two sacred texts (Sruti) are conflicting, both are held to be law; for both are pronounced by the wise (to be) valid law.

verses.text:
उदिते ऽनुदिते च-एव समयाध्युषिते तथा ।
सर्वथा वर्तते यज्ञ इति-इयं वैदिकी श्रुतिः ॥ १५ ॥
verses.english: (Thus) the (Agnihotra) sacrifice may be (optionally) performed, at any time after the sun has risen, before he has risen, or when neither sun nor stars are visible; that (is declared) by Vedic texts.

verses.text:
निषेक.आदि.श्मशान.अन्तो मन्त्रैर् यस्य-उदितो विधिः ।
तस्य शास्त्रे ऽधिकारो ऽस्मिञ् ज्ञेयो न-अन्यस्य कस्य चित् ॥ १६
                                ॥
verses.english: Know that he for whom (the performance of) the ceremonies beginning with the rite of impregnation (Garbhadhana) and ending with the funeral rite (Antyeshti) is prescribed, while sacred formulas are being recited, is entitled (to study) these Institutes, but no other man whatsoever.

verses.text:
सरस्वती.दृशद्वत्योर् देवनद्योर् यद् अन्तरम् ।
तं देवनिर्मितं देशं ब्रह्मावर्तं प्रचक्षते ॥ १७ ॥
verses.english: That land, created by the gods, which lies between the two divine rivers Sarasvati and Drishadvati, the (sages) call Brahmavarta.

verses.text:
तस्मिन् देशे य आचारः पारम्पर्यक्रमागतः ।
वर्णानां स.अन्तरालानां स सदाचार उच्यते ॥ १८ ॥
verses.english: The custom handed down in regular succession (since time immemorial) among the (four chief) castes (varna) and the mixed (races) of that country, is called the conduct of virtuous men.

verses.text:
कुरुक्षेत्रं च मत्स्याश् च पञ्चालाः शूरसेनकाः ।
एष ब्रह्मर्षिदेशो वै ब्रह्मावर्ताद् अनन्तरः ॥ १९ ॥
verses.english: The plain of the Kurus, the (country of the) Matsyas, Pankalas, and Surasenakas, these (form), indeed, the country of the Brahmarshis (Brahmanical sages, which ranks) immediately after Brahmavarta.

verses.text:
एतद् देशप्रसूतस्य सकाशाद् अग्रजन्मनः ।
स्वं स्वं चरित्रं शिक्षेरन् पृथिव्यां सर्वमानवाः ॥ २०
                                ॥
verses.english: From a Brahmana, born in that country, let all men on earth learn their several usages.

verses.text:
हिमवद्.विन्ध्ययोर् मध्यं यत् प्राग् विनशनाद् अपि ।
प्रत्यग् एव प्रयागाच् च मध्यदेशः प्रकीर्तितः ॥ २१ ॥
verses.english: That (country) which (lies) between the Himavat and the Vindhya (mountains) to the east of Prayaga and to the west of Vinasana (the place where the river Sarasvati disappears) is called Madhyadesa (the central region).

verses.text:
आ समुद्रात् तु वै पूर्वाद् आ समुद्राच् च पश्चिमात् ।
तयोर् एव-अन्तरं गिर्योर् आर्यावर्तं विदुर् बुधाः ॥ २२ ॥
verses.english: But (the tract) between those two mountains (just mentioned), which (extends) as far as the eastern and the western oceans, the wise call Aryavarta (the country of the Aryans).

verses.text:
कृष्णसारस् तु चरति मृगो यत्र स्वभावतः ।
स ज्ञेयो यज्ञियो देशो म्लेच्छदेशस् त्व् अतः परः ॥ २३ ॥
verses.english: That land where the black antelope naturally roams, one must know to be fit for the performance of sacrifices; (the tract) different from that (is) the country of the Mlekkhas (barbarians).

verses.text:
एताण् द्विजातयो देशान् संश्रयेरन् प्रयत्नतः ।
शूद्रस् तु यस्मिन् कस्मिन् वा निवसेद् वृत्तिकर्शितः ॥ २४ ॥
                                    २.२४च्व्/ म्: 
                                    यस्मिंस् तस्मिन् वा ॥ 2.24 ॥
verses.english: Let twice-born men seek to dwell in those (above-mentioned countries); but a Sudra, distressed for subsistence, may reside anywhere.

verses.text:
एषा धर्मस्य वो योनिः समासेन प्रकीर्तिता ।
सम्भवश् च-अस्य सर्वस्य वर्णधर्मान् निबोधत ॥ २५
                                ॥
verses.english: Thus has the origin of the sacred law been succinctly described to you and the origin of this universe; learn (now) the duties of the castes (varna).

verses.text:
वैदिकैः कर्मभिः पुण्यैर् निषेकादिर् द्विजन्मनाम् ।
कार्यः शरीरसंस्कारः पावनः प्रेत्य च-इह च ॥ २६ ॥
verses.english: With holy rites, prescribed by the Veda, must the ceremony on conception and other sacraments be performed for twice-born men, which sanctify the body and purify (from sin) in this (life) and after death.

verses.text:
गार्भैर् होमैर् जातकर्म.चौड.मौञ्जी.निबन्धनैः ।
बैजिकं गार्भिकं च-एनो द्विजानाम् अपमृज्यते ॥ २७ ॥
verses.english: By burnt oblations during (the mother's) pregnancy, by the Gatakarman (the ceremony after birth), the Kauda (tonsure), and the Maungibandhana (the tying of the sacred girdle of Munga grass) is the taint, derived from both parents, removed from twice-born men.

verses.text:
स्वाध्यायेन व्रतैर् होमैस् त्रैविद्येन-इज्यया सुतैः ।
महायज्ञैश् च यज्ञैश् च ब्राह्मी-इयं क्रियते तनुः ॥ २८
                                ॥
verses.english: By the study of the Veda, by vows, by burnt oblations, by (the recitation of) sacred texts, by the (acquisition of the) threefold sacred science, by offering (to the gods, Rishis, and manes), by (the procreation of) sons, by the great sacrifices, and by (Srauta) rites this (human) body is made fit for (union with) Brahman.

verses.text:
प्राङ् नाभिवर्धनात् पुंसो जातकर्म विधीयते ।
मन्त्रवत् प्राशनं च-अस्य हिरण्य.मधु.सर्पिषाम् ॥ २९
                                ॥
verses.english: Before the navel-string is cut, the Gatakarman (birth-rite) must be performed for a male (child); and while sacred formulas are being recited, he must be fed with gold, honey, and butter.

verses.text:
नामधेयं दशम्यां तु द्वादश्यां वा-अस्य कारयेत् ।
पुण्ये तिथौ मुहूर्ते वा नक्षत्रे वा गुणान्विते ॥ ३० ॥
verses.english: But let (the father perform or) cause to be performed the Namadheya (the rite of naming the child), on the tenth or twelfth (day after birth), or on a lucky lunar day, in a lucky muhurta, under an auspicious constellation.

verses.text:
मङ्गल्यं ब्राह्मणस्य स्यात् क्षत्रियस्य बलान्वितम् ।
वैश्यस्य धनसंयुक्तं शूद्रस्य तु जुगुप्सितम् ॥ ३१ ॥
verses.english: Let (the first part of) a Brahmana's name (denote something) auspicious, a Kshatriya's be connected with power, and a Vaisya's with wealth, but a Sudra's (express something) contemptible.

verses.text:
शर्मवद् ब्राह्मणस्य स्याद् राज्ञो रक्षासमन्वितम् । २.३२अव्/ म्: राज्ञा
                                    ?
वैश्यस्य पुष्टि.संयुक्तं शूद्रस्य प्रेष्यसंयुतम् ॥ ३२
                                ॥
verses.english: (The second part of) a Brahmana's (name) shall be (a word) implying happiness, of a Kshatriya's (a word) implying protection, of a Vaisya's (a term) expressive of thriving, and of a Sudra's (an expression) denoting service.

verses.text:
स्त्रीणां सुख.उद्यम् अ.क्रूरं विस्पष्ट.अर्थं मनोहरम् ।
मङ्गल्यं दीर्घवर्ण.अन्तम् आशीर्वाद.अभिधानवत् ॥ ३३
                                ॥
verses.english: The names of women should be easy to pronounce, not imply anything dreadful, possess a plain meaning, be pleasing and auspicious, end in long vowels, and contain a word of benediction.

verses.text:
चतुर्थे मासि कर्तव्यं शिशोर् निष्क्रमणं गृहात् ।
षष्ठे ऽन्नप्राशनं मासि यद् वा-इष्टं मङ्गलं कुले ॥ ३४
                                ॥
verses.english: In the fourth month the Nishkramana (the first leaving of the house) of the child should be performed, in the sixth month the Annaprasana (first feeding with rice), and optionally (any other) auspicious ceremony required by (the custom of) the family.

verses.text:
चूडाकर्म द्विजातीनां सर्वेषाम् एव धर्मतः ।
प्रथमे ऽब्दे तृतीये वा कर्तव्यं श्रुतिचोदनात् ॥ ३५ ॥ २.३५च्व्/ म्: 
                                    श्रुतिनोदनात् ॥ 2.35 ॥
verses.english: According to the teaching of the revealed texts, the Kudakarman (tonsure) must be performed, for the sake of spiritual merit, by all twice-born men in the first or third year.

verses.text:
गर्भाष्टमे ऽब्दे कुर्वीत ब्राह्मणस्य-उपनायनम् ।
गर्भाद् एकादशे राज्ञो गर्भात् तु द्वादशे विशः ॥ ३६
                                    ॥
verses.english: In the eighth year after conception, one should perform the initiation (upanayana) of a Brahmana, in the eleventh after conception (that) of a Kshatriya, but in the twelfth that of a Vaisya.

verses.text:
ब्रह्मवर्चस.कामस्य कार्यो विप्रस्य पञ्चमे ।
राज्ञो बल.अर्थिनः षष्ठे वैश्यस्य-इह-अर्थिनो ऽष्टमे
                                    ॥ ३७ ॥
verses.english: (The initiation) of a Brahmana who desires proficiency in sacred learning should take place in the fifth (year after conception), (that) of a Kshatriya who wishes to become powerful in the sixth, (and that) of a Vaisya who longs for (success in his) business in the eighth.

verses.text:
आ षोदशाद् ब्राह्मणस्य सावित्री न-अतिवर्तते ।
आ द्वाविंशात् क्षत्रबन्धोर् आ चतुर्विंशतेर् विशः ॥ ३८
                                    ॥
verses.english: The (time for the) Savitri (initiation) of a Brahmana does not pass until the completion of the sixteenth year (after conception), of a Kshatriya until the completion of the twenty-second, and of a Vaisya until the completion of the twenty-fourth.

verses.text:
अत ऊर्ध्वं त्रयो ऽप्य् एते यथाकालम् अ.संस्कृताः ।
सावित्रीपतिता व्रात्या भवन्त्य् आर्यविगर्हिताः ॥ ३९ ॥
verses.english: After those (periods men of) these three (castes) who have not received the sacrament at the proper time, become Vratyas (outcasts), excluded from the Savitri (initiation) and despised by the Aryans.

verses.text:
न-एतैर् अ.पूतैर् विधिवद् आपद्य् अपि हि कर्हि चित् ।
ब्राह्मान् यौनांश् च सम्बन्धान् न-आचरेद् ब्राह्मणः सह ॥
                                    ४० ॥ २.४०च्व्/ म्: ब्राह्मणैः सह ॥ 2.40 ॥
verses.english: With such men, if they have not been purified according to the rule, let no Brahmana ever, even in times of distress, form a connexion either through the Veda or by marriage.

verses.text:
कार्ष्ण.रौरव.बास्तानि चर्माणि ब्रह्मचारिणः ।
वसीरन्न् आनुपूर्व्येण शाण.क्षौम.आविकानि च ॥ ४१ ॥
verses.english: Let students, according to the order (of their castes), wear (as upper dresses) the skins of black antelopes, spotted deer, and he-goats, and (lower garments) made of hemp, flax or wool.

verses.text:
मौञ्जी त्रिवृत् समा श्लक्ष्णा कार्या विप्रस्य मेखला ।
क्षत्रियस्य तु मौर्वी ज्या वैश्यस्य शणतान्तवी ॥ ४२
                                    ॥
verses.english: The girdle of a Brahmana shall consist of a of a triple cord of Munga grass, smooth and soft; (that) of a Kshatriya, of a bowstring, made of Murva fibres; (that) of a Vaisya, of hempen threads.

verses.text:
मुञ्जालाभे तु कर्तव्याः कुश.अश्मन्तक.बल्वजैः ।
त्रिवृता ग्रन्थिना-एकेन त्रिभिः पञ्चभिर् एव वा ॥ ४३
                                    ॥
verses.english: If Munga grass (and so forth) be not procurable, (the girdles) may be made of Kusa, Asmantaka, and Balbaga (fibres), with a single threefold knot, or with three or five (knots according to the custom of the family).

verses.text:
कार्पासम् उपवीतं स्याद् विप्रस्य-ऊर्ध्ववृतं त्रिवृत् ।
शण.सूत्रमयं राज्ञो वैश्यस्य-आविकसौत्रिकम् ॥ ४४
                                    ॥
verses.english: The sacrificial string of a Brahmana shall be made of cotton, (shall be) twisted to the right, (and consist) of three threads, that of a Kshatriya of hempen threads, (and) that of a Vaisya of woollen threads.

verses.text:
ब्राह्मणो बैल्व.पालाशौ क्षत्रियो वाट.खादिरौ ।
पैलव.औदुम्बरौ वैश्यो दण्डान् अर्हन्ति धर्मतः ॥ ४५
                                    ॥
verses.english: A Brahmana shall (carry), according to the sacred law, a staff of Bilva or Palasa; a Kshatriya, of Vata or Khadira; (and) a Vaisya, of Pilu or Udumbara.

verses.text:
केशान्तिको ब्राह्मणस्य दण्डः कार्यः प्रमाणतः ।
ललाटसम्मितो राज्ञः स्यात् तु नासान्तिको विशः ॥ ४६ ॥
verses.english: The staff of a Brahmana shall be made of such length as to reach the end of his hair; that of a Kshatriya, to reach his forehead;

verses.text:
ऋजवस् ते तु सर्वे स्युर् अ.व्रणाः सौम्य.दर्शनाः ।
अन्.उद्वेगकरा नॄणां स.त्वचो ऽनग्निदूषिताः ॥ ४७ ॥
verses.english: Let all the staves be straight, without a blemish, handsome to look at, not likely to terrify men, with their bark perfect, unhurt by fire.

verses.text:
प्रतिगृह्य-ईप्सितं दण्डम् उपस्थाय च भास्करम् ।
प्रदक्षिणं परीत्य-अग्निं चरेद् भैक्षं यथाविधि ॥ ४८
                                    ॥
verses.english: Having taken a staff according to his choice, having worshipped the sun and walked round the fire, turning his right hand towards it, (the student) should beg alms according to the prescribed rule.

verses.text:
भवत्.पूर्वं चरेद् भैक्षम् उपनीतो द्विजोत्तमः ।
भवन्.मध्यं तु राजन्यो वैश्यस् तु भवद्.उत्तरम् ॥ ४९
                                    ॥
verses.english: An initiated Brahmana should beg, beginning (his request with the word) lady (bhavati); a Kshatriya, placing (the word) lady in the middle, but a Vaisya, placing it at the end (of the formula).

verses.text:
मातरं वा स्वसारं वा मातुर् वा भगिनीं निजाम् ।
भिक्षेत भिक्षाम् प्रथमं या च-एनं न-अवमानयेत् ॥ ५०
                                    ॥
verses.english: Let him first beg food of his mother, or of his sister, or of his own maternal aunt, or of (some other) female who will not disgrace him (by a refusal).

verses.text:
समाहृत्य तु तद् भैक्षं यावदन्नम् अ.मायया । २.५१अव्/ म्: 
                                        यावदर्थम्
निवेद्य गुरवे ऽश्नीयाद् आचम्य प्राङ्मुखः शुचिः ॥ ५१
                                    ॥
verses.english: Having collected as much food as is required (from several persons), and having announced it without guile to his teacher, let him eat, turning his face towards the east, and having purified himself by sipping water.

verses.text:
आयुष्यं प्राङ्.मुखो भुङ्क्ते यशस्यं दक्षिणा.मुखः ।
श्रियं प्रत्यङ्.मुखो भुङ्क्ते ऋतं भुङ्क्ते ह्य् उदङ्.मुखः
                                    ॥ ५२ ॥
verses.english: (His meal will procure) long life, if he eats facing the east; fame, if he turns to the south; prosperity, if he turns to the west; truthfulness, if he faces the east.

verses.text:
उपस्पृश्य द्विजो नित्यम् अन्नम् अद्यात् समाहितः ।
भुक्त्वा च-उपस्पृशेत् सम्यग् अद्भिः खानि च संस्पृशेत् ॥
                                    ५३ ॥
verses.english: Let a twice-born man always eat his food with concentrated mind, after performing an ablution; and after he has eaten, let him duly cleanse himself with water and sprinkle the cavities (of his head).

verses.text:
पूजयेद् अशनं नित्यम् अद्याच् च-एतद् अ.कुत्सयन् ।
दृष्ट्वा हृष्येत् प्रसीदेच् च प्रतिनन्देच् च सर्वशः ॥ ५४
                                    ॥
verses.english: Let him always worship his food, and eat it without contempt; when he sees it, let him rejoice, show a pleased face, and pray that he may always obtain it.

verses.text:
पूजितं ह्य् अशनं नित्यं बलम् ऊर्जं च यच्छति ।
अ.पूजितं तु तद् भुक्तम् उभयं नाशयेद् इदम् ॥ ५५
                                    ॥
verses.english: Food, that is always worshipped, gives strength and manly vigour; but eaten irreverently, it destroys them both.

verses.text:
न-उच्छिष्टं कस्य चिद् दद्यान् न-अद्याद् एतत् तथा-अन्तरा
                                    ।
न च-एव-अत्यशनं कुर्यान् न च-उच्छिष्टः क्व चिद् व्रजेत्
                                    ॥ ५६ ॥
verses.english: Let him not give to any man what he leaves, and beware of eating between (the two meal-times); let him not over-eat himself, nor go anywhere without having purified himself (after his meal).

verses.text:
अन्.आरोग्यम् अन्.आयुष्यम् अ.स्वर्ग्यं च-अतिभोजनम् ।
अपुण्यं लोकविद्विष्टं तस्मात् तत् परिवर्जयेत् ॥ ५७
                                    ॥
verses.english: Excessive eating is prejudicial to health, to fame, and to (bliss in) heaven; it prevents (the acquisition of) spiritual merit, and is odious among men; one ought, for these reasons, to avoid it carefully.

verses.text:
ब्राह्मेण विप्रस् तीर्थेन नित्यकालम् उपस्पृशेत् ।
काय.त्रैदशिकाभ्यां वा न पित्र्येण कदा चन ॥ ५८
                                    ॥
verses.english: Let a Brahmana always sip water out of the part of the hand (tirtha) sacred to Brahman, or out of that sacred to Ka (Pragapati), or out of (that) sacred to the gods, never out of that sacred to the manes.

verses.text:
अङ्गुष्ठमूलस्य तले ब्राह्मं तीर्थं प्रचक्षते ।
कायम् अङ्गुलिमूले ऽग्रे देवं पित्र्यं तयोर् अधः ॥ ५९
                                    ॥
verses.english: They call (the part) at the root of the thumb the tirtha sacred to Brahman, that at the root of the (little) finger (the tirtha) sacred to Ka (Pragapati), (that) at the tips (of the fingers, the tirtha) sacred to the gods, and that below (between the index and the thumb, the tirtha) sacred to the manes.

verses.text:
त्रिर् आचामेद् अपः पूर्वं द्विः प्रमृज्यात् ततो मुखम् ।
खानि च-एव स्पृशेद् अद्भिर् आत्मानं शिर एव च ॥ ६०
                                    ॥
verses.english: Let him first sip water thrice; next twice wipe his mouth; and, lastly, touch with water the cavities (of the head), (the seat of) the soul and the head.

verses.text:
अन्.उष्णाभिर् अ.फेनाभिर् अद्भिस् तीर्थेन धर्मवित् ।
शौच.ईप्सुः सर्वदा-आचामेद् एकान्ते प्राग्.उदङ्.मुखः ॥ ६१
                                    ॥
verses.english: He who knows the sacred law and seeks purity shall always perform the rite of sipping with water neither hot nor frothy, with the (prescribed) tirtha, in a lonely place, and turning to the east or to the north.

verses.text:
हृद्गाभिः पूयते विप्रः कण्ठगाभिस् तु भूमिपः ।
वैश्यो ऽद्भिः प्राशिताभिस् तु शूद्रः स्पृष्टाभिर् अन्ततः ॥
                                    ६२ ॥
verses.english: A Brahmana is purified by water that reaches his heart, a Kshatriya by water reaching his throat, a Vaisya by water taken into his mouth, (and) a Sudra by water touched with the extremity (of his lips).

verses.text:
उद्धृते दक्षिने पाणाव् उपवीती-उच्यते द्विजः ।
सव्ये प्राचीनावीती निवीती कण्ठसज्जने ॥ ६३ ॥
verses.english: A twice-born man is called upavitin when his right arm is raised (and the sacrificial string or the dress, passed under it, rests on the left shoulder); (when his) left (arm) is raised (and the string, or the dress, passed under it, rests on the right shoulder, he is called) prakinavitin; and nivitin when it hangs down (straight) from the neck.

verses.text:
मेखलाम् अजिनं दण्डम् उपवीतं कमण्डलुम् ।
अप्सु प्रास्य विनष्टानि गृह्णीत-अन्यानि मन्त्रवत् ॥ ६४
                                    ॥
verses.english: His girdle, the skin (which serves as his upper garment), his staff, his sacrificial thread, (and) his water-pot he must throw into water, when they have been damaged, and take others, reciting sacred formulas.

verses.text:
केशान्तः षोडशे वर्षे ब्राह्मणस्य विधीयते ।
राजन्यबन्धोर् द्वाविंशे वैश्यस्य द्व्यधिके मतः ॥ ६५
                                ॥
verses.english: (The ceremony called) Kesanta (clipping the hair) is ordained for a Brahmana in the sixteenth year (from conception); for a Kshatriya, in the twenty-second; and for a Vaisya, two (years) later than that.

verses.text:
अ.मन्त्रिका तु कार्या-इयं स्त्रीणाम् आवृद् अशेषतः ।
संस्कारार्थं शरीरस्य यथाकालं यथाक्रमम् ॥ ६६ ॥
verses.english: This whole series (of ceremonies) must be performed for females (also), in order to sanctify the body, at the proper time and in the proper order, but without (the recitation of) sacred texts.

verses.text:
वैवाहिको विधिः स्त्रीणां संस्कारो वैदिकः स्मृतः ।
पतिसेवा गुरौ वासो गृहार्थो ऽग्नि.परिक्रिया ॥ ६७ ॥
verses.english: The nuptial ceremony is stated to be the Vedic sacrament for women (and to be equal to the initiation), serving the husband (equivalent to) the residence in (the house of the) teacher, and the household duties (the same) as the (daily) worship of the sacred fire.

verses.text:
एष प्रोक्तो द्विजातीनाम् औपनायनिको विधिः ।
उत्पत्ति.व्यञ्जकः पुण्यः कर्मयोगं निबोधत ॥ ६८ ॥
verses.english: Thus has been described the rule for the initiation of the twice-born, which indicates a (new) birth, and sanctifies; learn (now) to what duties they must afterwards apply themselves.

verses.text:
उपनीय गुरुः शिष्यं शिक्षयेत्-शौचम् आदितः ।
आचारम् अग्निकार्यं च सन्ध्या.उपासनम् एव च ॥ ६९ ॥
verses.english: Having performed the (rite of) initiation, the teacher must first instruct the (pupil) in (the rules of) personal purification, of conduct, of the fire-worship, and of the twilight devotions.

verses.text:
अध्येष्यमाणस् त्व् आचान्तो यथाशास्त्रम् उदङ्.मुखः ।
ब्रह्माञ्जलि.कृतो ऽध्याप्यो लघु.वासा जित.इन्द्रियः ॥ ७०
                                ॥
verses.english: But (a student) who is about to begin the Study (of the Veda), shall receive instruction, after he has sipped water in accordance with the Institutes (of the sacred law), has made the Brahmangali, (has put on) a clean dress, and has brought his organs under due control.

verses.text:
ब्रह्मारम्भे ऽवसाने च पादौ ग्राह्यौ गुरोः सदा ।
संहत्य हस्ताव् अध्येयं स हि ब्रह्माञ्जलिः स्मृतः ॥ ७१
                                ॥
verses.english: At the beginning and at the end of (a lesson in the) Veda he must always clasp both the feet of his teacher, (and) he must study, joining his hands; that is called the Brahmangali (joining the palms for the sake of the Veda).

verses.text:
व्यत्यस्त.पाणिना कार्यम् उपसङ्ग्रहणं गुरोः ।
सव्येन सव्यः स्प्रष्टव्यो दक्षिणेन च दक्षिणः ॥ ७२ ॥
verses.english: With crossed hands he must clasp (the feet) of the teacher, and touch the left (foot) with his left (hand), the right (foot) with his right (hand).

verses.text:
अध्येष्यमाणं तु गुरुर् नित्यकालम् अ.तन्द्रितः ।
अधीष्व भो इति ब्रूयाद् विरामो ऽस्त्व् इति च-आरमेत् ॥ ७३ ॥
verses.english: But to him who is about to begin studying, the teacher always unwearied, must say: Ho, recite! He shall leave off (when the teacher says): Let a stoppage take place!

verses.text:
ब्रह्मनः प्रणवं कुर्याद् आदाव् अन्ते च सर्वदा ।
स्रवत्य् अन्.ओङ्कृतं पूर्वं परस्ताच् च विशीर्यति ॥ ७४ ॥
verses.english: Let him always pronounce the syllable Om at the beginning and at the end of (a lesson in) the Veda; (for) unless the syllable Om precede (the lesson) will slip away (from him), and unless it follow it will fade away.

verses.text:
प्राक्.कूलान् पर्युपासीनः पवित्रैश् च-एव पावितः ।
प्राणायामैस् त्रिभिः पूतस् तत ॐ.कारम् अर्हति ॥ ७५ ॥
verses.english: Seated on (blades of Kusa grass) with their points to the east, purified by Pavitras (blades of Kusa grass), and sanctified by three suppressions of the breath (Pranayama), he is worthy (to pronounce) the syllable Om.

verses.text:
अ.कारं च-अप्य् उ.कारं च म.कारं च प्रजापतिः ।
वेदत्रयात्-निरदुहद् भूर् भुवः स्वर् इति-इति च ॥ ७६
                                    ॥
verses.english: Pragapati (the lord of creatures) milked out (as it were) from the three Vedas the sounds A, U, and M, and (the Vyahritis) Bhuh, Bhuvah, Svah.

verses.text:
त्रिभ्य एव तु वेदेभ्यः पादं पादम् अदूदुहत् ।
तद् इत्य् ऋचो ऽस्याः सावित्र्याः परमेष्ठी प्रजापतिः ॥ ७७
                                    ॥
verses.english: Moreover from the three Vedas Pragapati, who dwells in the highest heaven (Parameshthin), milked out (as it were) that Rik-verse, sacred to Savitri (Savitri), which begins with the word tad, one foot from each.

verses.text:
एतद् अक्षरम् एतां च जपन् व्याहृति.पूर्विकाम् ।
सन्ध्ययोर् वेदविद् विप्रो वेदपुण्येन युज्यते ॥ ७८ ॥
verses.english: A Brahmana, learned in the Veda, who recites during both twilights that syllable and that (verse), preceded by the Vyahritis, gains the (whole) merit which (the recitation of) the Vedas confers.

verses.text:
सहस्रकृत्वस् त्व् अभ्यस्य बहिर् एतत् त्रिकं द्विजः ।
महतो ऽप्य् एनसो मासात् त्वचा-इव-अहिर् विमुच्यते ॥ ७९
                                    ॥
verses.english: A twice-born man who (daily) repeats those three one thousand times outside (the village), will be freed after a month even from great guilt, as a snake from its slough.

verses.text:
एतया-ऋचा विसंयुक्तः काले च क्रियया स्वया ।
ब्रह्म.क्षत्रिय.विश्.योनिर् गर्हणां याति साधुषु ॥ ८०
                                    ॥
verses.english: The Brahmana, the Kshatriya, and the Vaisya who neglect (the recitation of) that Rik-verse and the timely (performance of the) rites (prescribed for) them, will be blamed among virtuous men.

verses.text:
ॐ.कार.पूर्विकास् तिस्रो महाव्याहृतयो ऽव्ययाः । २.८१अव्/ म्: 
                                        ओङ्कार.
त्रि.पदा च-एव सावित्री विज्ञेयं ब्रह्मणो मुखम् ॥ ८१
                                    ॥
verses.english: Know that the three imperishable Mahavyahritis, preceded by the syllable Om, and (followed) by the three-footed Savitri are the portal of the Veda and the gate leading (to union with) Brahman.

verses.text:
यो ऽधीते ऽहन्य् अहन्य् एतां त्रीणि वर्षाण्य् अ.तन्द्रितः
                                    ।
स ब्रह्म परम् अभ्येति वायुभूतः ख.मूर्तिमान् ॥ ८२
                                    ॥
verses.english: He who daily recites that (verse), untired, during three years, will enter (after death) the highest Brahman, move as free as air, and assume an ethereal form.

verses.text:
एकाक्षरं परं ब्रह्म प्राणायामः परं तपः ।
सावित्र्यास् तु परं न-अस्ति मौनात् सत्यं विशिष्यते ॥ ८३
                                    ॥
verses.english: The monosyllable (Om) is the highest Brahman, (three) suppressions of the breath are the best (form of) austerity, but nothing surpasses the Savitri truthfulness is better than silence.

verses.text:
क्षरन्ति सर्वा वैदिक्यो जुहोति.यजति.क्रियाः ।
अक्षरं दुष्करं ज्ञेयं ब्रह्म च-एव प्रजापतिः ॥ ८४ ॥
                                        २.८४च्व्/
                                        म्: अक्षरं त्व् अक्षरं ज्ञेयं ॥ 2.84 ॥
verses.english: All rites ordained in the Veda, burnt oblations and (other) sacrifices, pass away; but know that the syllable (Om) is imperishable, and (it is) Brahman, (and) the Lord of creatures (Pragapati).

verses.text:
विधियज्ञाज् जपयज्ञो विशिष्टो दशभिर् गुणैः ।
उपांशुः स्यात्-शतगुणः साहस्रो मानसः स्मृतः ॥ ८५
                                    ॥
verses.english: An offering, consisting of muttered prayers, is ten times more efficacious than a sacrifice performed according to the rules (of the Veda); a (prayer) which is inaudible (to others) surpasses it a hundred times, and the mental (recitation of sacred texts) a thousand times.

verses.text:
ये पाकयज्ञास् चत्वारो विधियज्ञसमन्विताः ।
सर्वे ते जपयज्ञस्य कलां न-अर्हन्ति षोडशीम् ॥ ८६
                                    ॥
verses.english: The four Pakayagnas and those sacrifices which are enjoined by the rules (of the Veda) are all together not equal in value to a sixteenth part of the sacrifice consisting of muttered prayers.

verses.text:
जप्येन-एव तु संसिध्येद् ब्राह्मणो न-अत्र संशयः ।
कुर्याद् अन्यन् न वा कुर्यान् मैत्रो ब्राह्मण उच्यते ॥ ८७
                                    ॥
verses.english: But, undoubtedly, a Brahmana reaches the highest goal by muttering prayers only; (whether) he perform other (rites) or neglect them, he who befriends (all creatures) is declared (to be) a (true) Brahmana.

verses.text:
इन्द्रियाणां विचरतां विषयेष्व् अपहारिषु ।
संयमे यत्नम् आतिष्ठेद् विद्वान् यन्ता-इव वाजिनाम् ॥ ८८ ॥
verses.english: A wise man should strive to restrain his organs which run wild among alluring sensual objects, like a charioteer his horses.

verses.text:
एकादश-इन्द्रियाण्य् आहुर् यानि पूर्वे मनीषिणः ।
तानि सम्यक् प्रवक्ष्यामि यथावद् अनुपूर्वशः ॥ ८९ ॥
verses.english: Those eleven organs which former sages have named, I will properly (and) precisely enumerate in due order,

verses.text:
श्रोत्रं त्वक् चक्षुषी जिह्वा नासिका च-एव पञ्चमी ।
पायु.उपस्थं हस्त.पादं वाक् च-एव दशमी स्मृता ॥ ९०
                                ॥
verses.english: (Viz.) the ear, the skin, the eyes, the tongue, and the nose as the fifth, the anus, the organ of generation, hands and feet, and the (organ of) speech, named as the tenth.

verses.text:
बुद्धीन्द्रियाणि पञ्च-एषां श्रोत्रादीन्य् अनुपूर्वशः ।
कर्म.इन्द्रियाणि पञ्च-एषां पायु.आदीनि प्रचक्षते ॥ ९१ ॥
verses.english: Five of them, the ear and the rest according to their order, they call organs of sense, and five of them, the anus and the rest, organs of action.

verses.text:
एकादशं मनो ज्ञेयं स्वगुणेन-उभय.आत्मकम् ।
यस्मिन् जिते जिताव् एतौ भवतः पञ्चकौ गणौ ॥ ९२ ॥
verses.english: Know that the internal organ (manas) is the eleventh, which by its quality belongs to both (sets); when that has been subdued, both those sets of five have been conquered.

verses.text:
इन्द्रियाणां प्रसङ्गेन दोषम् ऋच्छत्य् अ.संशयम् ।
सन्नियम्य तु तान्य् एव ततः सिद्धिं निगच्छति ॥ ९३ ॥
verses.english: Through the attachment of his organs (to sensual pleasure) a man doubtlessly will incur guilt; but if he keep them under complete control, he will obtain success (in gaining all his aims).

verses.text:
न जातु कामः कामानाम् उपभोगेन शाम्यति ।
हविषा कृष्णवर्त्मा-इव भूय एव-अभिवर्धते ॥ ९४ ॥
verses.english: Desire is never extinguished by the enjoyment of desired objects; it only grows stronger like a fire (fed) with clarified butter.

verses.text:
यश् च-एतान् प्राप्नुयात् सर्वान् यश् च-एतान् केवलांस् त्यजेत्
                                ।
प्रापणात् सर्वकामानां परित्यागो विशिष्यते ॥ ९५ ॥
verses.english: If one man should obtain all those (sensual enjoyments) and another should renounce them all, the renunciation of all pleasure is far better than the attainment of them.

verses.text:
न तथा-एतानि शक्यन्ते सन्नियन्तुम् असेवया ।
विषयेषु प्रजुष्टानि यथा ज्ञानेन नित्यशः ॥ ९६ ॥
verses.english: Those (organs) which are strongly attached to sensual pleasures, cannot so effectually be restrained by abstinence (from enjoyments) as by a constant (pursuit of true) knowledge.

verses.text:
वेदास् त्यागश् च यज्ञाश् च नियमाश् च तपांसि च ।
न विप्रदुष्ट.भावस्य सिद्धिं गच्छति कर्हि चित् ॥ ९७
                                ॥
verses.english: Neither (the study of) the Vedas, nor liberality, nor sacrifices, nor any (self-imposed) restraint, nor austerities, ever procure the attainment (of rewards) to a man whose heart is contaminated (by sensuality).

verses.text:
श्रुत्वा स्पृष्ट्वा च दृष्ट्वा च भुक्त्वा घ्रात्वा च यो नरः ।
न हृष्यति ग्लायति वा स विज्ञेयो जित.इन्द्रियः ॥ ९८ ॥
verses.english: That man may be considered to have (really) subdued his organs, who on hearing and touching and seeing, on tasting and smelling (anything) neither rejoices nor repines.

verses.text:
इन्द्रियाणां तु सर्वेषां यद्य् एकं क्षरति-इन्द्रियम् ।
तेन-अस्य क्षरति प्रज्ञा दृतेः पादाद् इव-उदकम् ॥ ९९ ॥
verses.english: But when one among all the organs slips away (from control), thereby (man's) wisdom slips away from him, even as the water (flows) through the one (open) foot of a (water-carrier's) skin.

verses.text:
वशे कृत्वा-इन्द्रियग्रामं संयम्य च मनस् तथा ।
सर्वान् संसाधयेद् अर्थान् अ.क्षिण्वन् योगतस् तनुम् ॥ १००
                                ॥
verses.english: If he keeps all the (ten) organs as well as the mind in subjection, he may gain all his aims, without reducing his body by (the practice) of Yoga.

verses.text:
पूर्वां सन्ध्यां जपांस् तिष्ठेत् सावित्रीम् आ.अर्कदर्शनात् ।
पश्चिमां तु समासीनः सम्यग् ऋक्षविभावनात् ॥ १०१ ॥ २.१०१च्व्/ म्: 
                                    पश्चिमां तु सदासीत ॥ 2.101 ॥
verses.english: Let him stand during the morning twilight, muttering the Savitri until the sun appears, but (let him recite it), seated, in the evening until the constellations can be seen distinctly.

verses.text:
पूर्वां सन्ध्यां जपंस् तिष्ठन् नैशम् एनो व्यपोहति ।
पश्चिमाम् तु समासीनो मलं हन्ति दिवाकृतम् ॥ १०२ ॥
verses.english: He who stands during the morning twilight muttering (the Savitri), removes the guilt contracted during the (previous) night; but he who (recites it), seated, in the evening, destroys the sin he committed during the day.

verses.text:
न तिष्ठति तु यः पूर्वां न-उपास्ते यश् च पश्चिमाम् ।
स शूद्रवद् बहिष्कार्यः सर्वस्माद् द्विजकर्मणः ॥ १०३
                                ॥
verses.english: But he who does not (worship) standing in the morning, nor sitting in the evening, shall be excluded, just like a Sudra, from all the duties and rights of an Aryan.

verses.text:
अपां समीपे नियतो नैत्यकं विधिम् आस्थितः ।
सावित्रीम् अप्य् अधीयीत गत्वा-अरण्यं समाहितः ॥ १०४ ॥
verses.english: He who (desires to) perform the ceremony (of the) daily (recitation), may even recite the Savitri near water, retiring into the forest, controlling his organs and concentrating his mind.

verses.text:
वेद.उपकरणे च-एव स्वाध्याये च-एव नैत्यके ।
न-अनुरोधो ऽस्त्य् अनध्याये होममन्त्रेषु च-एव हि ॥ १०५
                                ॥
verses.english: Both when (one studies) the supplementary treatises of the Veda, and when (one recites) the daily portion of the Veda, no regard need be paid to forbidden days, likewise when (one repeats) the sacred texts required for a burnt oblation.

verses.text:
नैत्यके न-अस्त्य् अनध्यायो ब्रह्मसत्त्रं हि तत् स्मृतम् ।
ब्रह्माहुति.हुतं पुण्यम् अन्.अध्याय.वषट्कृतम् ॥ १०६ ॥
verses.english: There are no forbidden days for the daily recitation, since that is declared to be a Brahmasattra (an everlasting sacrifice offered to Brahman); at that the Veda takes the place of the burnt oblations, and it is meritorious (even), when (natural phenomena, requiring) a cessation of the Veda-study, take the place of the exclamation Vashat.

verses.text:
यः स्वाध्यायम् अधीते ऽब्दं विधिना नियतः शुचिः ।
तस्य नित्यं क्षरत्य् एष पयो दधि घृतं मधु ॥ १०७
                                ॥
verses.english: For him who, being pure and controlling his organs, during a year daily recites the Veda according to the rule, that (daily recitation) will ever cause sweet and sour milk, clarified butter and honey to flow.

verses.text:
अग्नीन्धनं भैक्षचर्याम् अधःशय्यां गुरोर् हितम् ।
आ समावर्तनात् कुर्यात् कृत.उपनयनो द्विजः ॥ १०८ ॥
verses.english: Let an Aryan who has been initiated, (daily) offer fuel in the sacred fire, beg food, sleep on the ground and do what is beneficial to this teacher, until (he performs the ceremony of) Samavartana (on returning home).

verses.text:
आचार्यपुत्रः शुश्रूषुर् ज्ञानदो धार्मिकः शुचिः ।
आप्तः शक्तो ऽर्थदः साधुः स्वो ऽध्याप्या दश धर्मतः ॥
                                १०९ ॥
verses.english: According to the sacred law the (following) ten (persons, viz.) the teacher's son, one who desires to do service, one who imparts knowledge, one who is intent on fulfilling the law, one who is pure, a person connected by marriage or friendship, one who possesses (mental) ability, one who makes presents of money, one who is honest, and a relative, may be instructed (in the Veda).

verses.text:
न-अपृष्टः कस्य चिद् ब्रूयान् न च-अन्यायेन पृच्छतः ।
जानन्न् अपि हि मेधावी जडवल् लोक आचरेत् ॥ ११० ॥
verses.english: Unless one be asked, one must not explain (anything) to anybody, nor (must one answer) a person who asks improperly; let a wise man, though he knows (the answer), behave among men as (if he were) an idiot.

verses.text:
अधर्मेण च यः प्राह यश् च-अधर्मेण पृच्छति ।
तयोर् अन्यतरः प्रैति विद्वेषं वा-अधिगच्छति ॥ १११
                                ॥
verses.english: Of the two persons, him who illegally explains (anything), and him who illegally asks (a question), one (or both) will die or incur (the other's) enmity.

verses.text:
धर्म.अर्थौ यत्र न स्यातां शुश्रूषा वा-अपि तद्विधा ।
तत्र विद्या न वप्तव्या शुभं बीजम् इव-ऊषरे ॥ ११२ ॥
verses.english: Where merit and wealth are not (obtained by teaching) nor (at least) due obedience, in such (soil) sacred knowledge must not be sown, just as good seed (must) not (be thrown) on barren land.

verses.text:
विद्यया-एव समं कामं मर्तव्यं ब्रह्मवादिना ।
आपद्य् अपि हि घोरायां न त्व् एनाम् इरिणे वपेत् ॥ ११३ ॥
verses.english: Even in times of dire distress a teacher of the Veda should rather die with his knowledge than sow it in barren soil.

verses.text:
विद्या ब्राह्मणम् एत्य-आह शेवधिस् ते ऽस्मि रक्ष माम् । २.११४अव्/ म्: 
                                    शेवधिष् टे
असूयकाय मां मादास् तथा स्यां वीर्यवत्तमा ॥ ११४ ॥
verses.english: Sacred Learning approached a Brahmana and said to him: 'I am thy treasure, preserve me, deliver me not to a scorner; so (preserved) I shall become supremely strong.'

verses.text:
यम् एव तु शुचिं विद्यान् नियत.ब्रह्मचारिणम् । २.११५अव्/ म्: विद्या
                                    नियतं ब्रह्मचारिणम्
तस्मै मां ब्रूहि विप्राय निधिपाय-अ.प्रमादिने ॥ ११५ ॥
verses.english: 'But deliver me, as to the keeper of thy treasure, to a Brahmana whom thou shalt know to be pure, of subdued senses, chaste and attentive.'

verses.text:
ब्रह्म यस् त्व् अननुज्ञातम् अधीयानाद् अवाप्नुयात् ।
स ब्रह्मस्तेयसंयुक्तो नरकं प्रतिपद्यते ॥ ११६ ॥
verses.english: But he who acquires without permission the Veda from one who recites it, incurs the guilt of stealing the Veda, and shall sink into hell.

verses.text:
लौकिकं वैदिकं वा-अपि तथा-अध्यात्मिकम् एव वा ।
आददीत यतो ज्ञानं तं पूर्वम् अभिवादयेत् ॥ ११७ ॥
verses.english: (A student) shall first reverentially salute that (teacher) from whom he receives (knowledge), referring to worldly affairs, to the Veda, or to the Brahman.

verses.text:
सावित्रीमात्र.सारो ऽपि वरं विप्रः सुयन्त्रितः ।
न-अ.यन्त्रितस् त्रिवेदो ऽपि सर्वाशी सर्वविक्रयी ॥ ११८
                                ॥
verses.english: A Brahmana who completely governs himself, though he know the Savitri only, is better than he who knows the three Vedas, (but) does not control himself, eats all (sorts of) food, and sells all (sorts of goods).

verses.text:
शय्या.आसने ऽध्याचरिते श्रेयसा न समाविशेत् ।
शय्या.आसनस्थश् च-एव-एनं प्रत्युत्थाय-अभिवादयेत् ॥ ११९
                                ॥
verses.english: One must not sit down on a couch or seat which a superior occupies; and he who occupies a couch or seat shall rise to meet a (superior), and (afterwards) salute him.

verses.text:
ऊर्ध्वं प्राणा ह्य् उत्क्रामन्ति यूनः स्थविर आयति ।
प्रत्युत्थान.अभिवादाभ्यां पुनस् तान् प्रतिपद्यते ॥ १२०
                                ॥
verses.english: For the vital airs of a young man mount upwards to leave his body when an elder approaches; but by rising to meet him and saluting he recovers them.

verses.text:
अभिवादन.शीलस्य नित्यं वृद्ध.उपसेविनः ।
चत्वारि तस्य वर्धन्ते आयुर् धर्मो यशो बलम् ॥ १२१ ॥
                                    २.१२१च्व्/ म्: 
                                    चत्वारि सम्प्रवर्धन्ते ॥ 2.121 ॥
verses.english: He who habitually salutes and constantly pays reverence to the aged obtains an increase of four (things), (viz.) length of life, knowledge, fame, (and) strength.

verses.text:
अभिवादात् परं विप्रो ज्यायांसम् अभिवादयन् ।
असौ नाम-अहम् अस्मि-इति स्वं नाम परिकीर्तयेत् ॥ १२२ ॥
verses.english: After the (word of) salutation, a Brahmana who greets an elder must pronounce his name, saying, 'I am N. N.'

verses.text:
नामधेयस्य ये के चिद् अभिवादं न जानते ।
तान् प्राज्ञो ऽहम् इति ब्रूयात् स्त्रियः सर्वास् तथा-एव च ॥
                                १२३ ॥
verses.english: To those (persons) who, when a name is pronounced, do not understand (the meaning of) the salutation, a wise man should say, 'It is I;' and (he should address) in the same manner all women.

verses.text:
भोःशब्दं कीर्तयेद् अन्ते स्वस्य नाम्नो ऽभिवादने ।
नाम्नाम् स्वरूप.भावो हि भो.भाव ऋषिभिः स्मृतः ॥ १२४
                                ॥
verses.english: In saluting he should pronounce after his name the word bhoh; for the sages have declared that the nature of bhoh is the same as that of (all proper) names.

verses.text:
आयुष्मान् भव सौम्य-इति वाच्यो विप्रो ऽभिवादने ।
अ.कारश् च-अस्य नाम्नो ऽन्ते वाच्यः पूर्वाक्षरः प्लुतः ॥ १२५
                                ॥
verses.english: A Brahmana should thus be saluted in return, 'May'st thou be long-lived, O gentle one!' and the vowel 'a' must be added at the end of the name (of the person addressed), the syllable preceding it being drawn out to the length of three moras.

verses.text:
यो न वेत्त्य् अभिवादस्य विप्रः प्रत्यभिवादनम् ।
न-अभिवाद्यः स विदुषा यथा शूद्रस् तथा-एव सः ॥ १२६
                                ॥
verses.english: A Brahmana who does not know the form of returning a salutation, must not be saluted by a learned man; as a Sudra, even so is he.

verses.text:
ब्राह्मणं कुशलं पृच्छेत् क्षत्रबन्धुम् अन्.आमयम् ।
वैश्यं क्षेमं समागम्य शूद्रम् आरोग्यम् एव च ॥ १२७ ॥
verses.english: Let him ask a Brahmana, on meeting him, after (his health, with the word) kusala, a Kshatriya (with the word) anamaya, a Vaisya (with the word) kshema, and a Sudra (with the word) anarogya.

verses.text:
अ.वाच्यो दीक्षितो नाम्ना यवीयान् अपि यो भवेत् ।
भो.भवत्.पूर्वकं त्व् एनम् अभिभाषेत धर्मवित् ॥ १२८
                                ॥
