verses.english: He who has been initiated (to perform a Srauta sacrifice) must not be addressed by his name, even though he be a younger man; he who knows the sacred law must use in speaking to such (a man the particle) bhoh and (the pronoun) bhavat (your worship).

verses.text:
परपत्नी तु या स्त्री स्याद् अ.सम्बन्धा च योनितः ।
तां ब्रूयाद् भवति-इत्य् एवं सुभगे भगिनि-इति च ॥ १२९
                                ॥
verses.english: But to a female who is the wife of another man, and not a blood-relation, he must say, 'Lady' (bhavati) or 'Beloved sister!'

verses.text:
मातुलांश् च पितृव्यांश् च श्वशुरान् ऋत्विजो गुरून् ।
असाव् अहम् इति ब्रूयात् प्रत्युत्थाय यवीयसः ॥ १३० ॥
verses.english: To his maternal and paternal uncles, fathers-in-law, officiating priests, (and other) venerable persons, he must say, 'I am N. N.,' and rise (to meet them), even though they be younger (than himself).

verses.text:
मातृश्वसा मातुलानी श्वश्रूर् अथ पितृश्वसा ।
सम्पूज्या गुरुपत्नीवत् समास् ता गुरुभार्यया ॥ १३१ ॥
verses.english: A maternal aunt, the wife of a maternal uncle, a mother-in-law, and a paternal aunt must be honoured like the wife of one's teacher; they are equal to the wife of one's teacher.

verses.text:
भ्रातुर् भार्या-उपसङ्ग्राह्या स.वर्णा-अहन्य् अहन्य् अपि ।
विप्रोष्य तु-उपसङ्ग्राह्या ज्ञाति.सम्बन्धि.योषितः ॥ १३२
                                ॥
verses.english: (The feet of the) wife of one's brother, if she be of the same caste (varna), must be clasped every day; but (the feet of) wives of (other) paternal and maternal relatives need only be embraced on one's return from a journey.

verses.text:
पितुर् भगिन्यां मातुश् च ज्यायस्यां च स्वसर्य् अपि ।
मातृवद् वृत्तिम् आतिष्ठेन् माता ताभ्यो गरीयसी ॥ १३३ ॥
verses.english: Towards a sister of one's father and of one's mother, and towards one's own elder sister, one must behave as towards one's mother; (but) the mother is more venerable than they.

verses.text:
दशाब्द.आख्यं पौरसख्यं पञ्चाब्द.आख्यं कलाभृताम् ।
त्र्यब्दपूर्वं श्रोत्रियाणां स्वल्पेन-अपि स्वयोनिषु ॥ १३४
                                ॥
verses.english: Fellow-citizens are called friends (and equals though one be) ten years (older than the other), men practising (the same) fine art (though one be) five years (older than the other), Srotriyas (though) three years (intervene between their ages), but blood-relations only (if the) difference of age be very small.

verses.text:
ब्राह्मणं दशवर्षं तु शतवर्षं तु भूमिपम् ।
पिता.पुत्रौ विजानीयाद् ब्राह्मणस् तु तयोः पिता ॥ १३५ ॥
verses.english: Know that a Brahmana of ten years and Kshatriya of a hundred years stand to each other in the relation of father and son; but between those two the Brahmana is the father.

verses.text:
वित्तं बन्धुर् वयः कर्म विद्या भवति पञ्चमी ।
एतानि मान्यस्थानानि गरीयो यद् यद् उत्तरम् ॥ १३६ ॥ २.१३६च्व्/ म्: 
                                    मानस्थानानि ॥ 2.136 ॥
verses.english: Wealth, kindred, age, (the due performance of) rites, and, fifthly, sacred learning are titles to respect; but each later-named (cause) is more weighty (than the preceding ones).

verses.text:
पञ्चानां त्रिषु वर्णेषु भूयांसि गुणवन्ति च ।
यत्र स्युः सो ऽत्र मान.अर्हः शूद्रो ऽपि दशमीं गतः ॥ १३७
                                ॥
verses.english: Whatever man of the three (highest) castes possesses most of those five, both in number and degree, that man is worthy of honour among them; and (so is) also a Sudra who has entered the tenth (decade of his life).

verses.text:
चक्रिणो दशमीस्थस्य रोगिणो भारिणः स्त्रियाः ।
स्नातकस्य च राज्ञश् च पन्था देयो वरस्य च ॥ १३८ ॥
verses.english: Way must be made for a man in a carriage, for one who is above ninety years old, for one diseased, for the carrier of a burden, for a woman, for a Snataka, for the king, and for a bridegroom.

verses.text:
तेषां तु समावेतानां मान्यौ स्नातक.पार्थिवौ ।
राज.स्नातकयोश् च-एव स्नातको नृपमानभाक् ॥ १३९ ॥
verses.english: Among all those, if they meet (at one time), a Snataka and the king must be (most) honoured; and if the king and a Snataka (meet), the latter receives respect from the king.

verses.text:
उपनीय तु यः शिष्यं वेदम् अध्यापयेद् द्विजः ।
स.कल्पं स.रहस्यं च तम् आचार्यं प्रचक्षते ॥ १४०
                                ॥
verses.english: They call that Brahmana who initiates a pupil and teaches him the Veda together with the Kalpa and the Rahasyas, the teacher (akarya, of the latter).

verses.text:
एकदेशं तु वेदस्य वेदाङ्गान्य् अपि वा पुनः ।
यो ऽध्यापयति वृत्त्यर्थम् उपाध्यायः स उच्यते ॥ १४१
                                ॥
verses.english: But he who for his livelihood teaches a portion only of the Veda, or also the Angas of the Veda, is called the sub-teacher (upadhyaya).

verses.text:
निषेक.आदीनि कर्माणि यः करोति यथाविधि ।
सम्भावयति च-अन्नेन स विप्रो गुरुर् उच्यते ॥ १४२ ॥
verses.english: That Brahmana, who performs in accordance with the rules (of the Veda) the rites, the Garbhadhana (conception-rite), and so forth, and gives food (to the child), is called the Guru (the venerable one).

verses.text:
अग्न्याधेयं पाकयज्ञान् अग्निष्टोम.आदिकान् मखान् ।
यः करोति वृतो यस्य स तस्य-ऋत्विग् इह-उच्यते ॥ १४३
                                ॥
verses.english: He who, being (duly) chosen (for the purpose), performs the Agnyadheya, the Pakayagnas, (and) the (Srauta) sacrifices, such as the Agnishtoma (for another man), is called (his) officiating priest.

verses.text:
य आवृणोत्य् अ.वितथं ब्रह्मणा श्रवणाव् उभौ ।
स माता स पिता ज्ञेयस् तं न द्रुह्येत् कदा चन ॥ १४४
                                ॥
verses.english: That (man) who truthfully fills both his ears with the Veda, (the pupil) shall consider as his father and mother; he must never offend him.

verses.text:
उपाध्यायान् दश-आचार्य आचार्याणां शतं पिता ।
सहस्रं तु पितॄन् माता गौरवेण-अतिरिच्यते ॥ १४५ ॥
verses.english: The teacher (akarya) is ten times more venerable than a sub-teacher (upadhyaya), the father a hundred times more than the teacher, but the mother a thousand times more than the father.

verses.text:
उत्पादक.ब्रह्मदात्रोर् गरीयान् ब्रह्मदः पिता ।
ब्रह्मजन्म हि विप्रस्य प्रेत्य च-इह च शाश्वतम् ॥ १४६
                                ॥
verses.english: Of him who gives natural birth and him who gives (the knowledge of) the Veda, the giver of the Veda is the more venerable father; for the birth for the sake of the Veda (ensures) eternal (rewards) both in this (life) and after death.

verses.text:
कामान् माता पिता च-एनं यद् उत्पादयतो मिथः ।
सम्भूतिं तस्य तां विद्याद् यद् योनाव् अभिजायते ॥ १४७
                                ॥
verses.english: Let him consider that (he received) a (mere animal) existence, when his parents begat him through mutual affection, and when he was born from the womb (of his mother).

verses.text:
आचार्यस् त्व् अस्य यां जातिं विधिवद् वेदपारगः ।
उत्पादयति सावित्र्या सा सत्या सा-अजरा-अमरा ॥ १४८ ॥
verses.english: But that birth which a teacher acquainted with the whole Veda, in accordance with the law, procures for him through the Savitri, is real, exempt from age and death.

verses.text:
अल्पं वा बहु वा यस्य श्रुतस्य-उपकरोति यः ।
तम् अपीह गुरुं विद्यात्-श्रुत.उपक्रियया तया ॥ १४९ ॥
verses.english: (The pupil) must know that that man also who benefits him by (instruction in) the Veda, be it little or much, is called in these (Institutes) his Guru, in consequence of that benefit (conferred by instruction in) the Veda.

verses.text:
ब्राह्मस्य जन्मनः कर्ता स्वधर्मस्य च शासिता ।
बालो ऽपि विप्रो वृद्धस्य पिता भवति धर्मतः ॥ १५०
                                ॥
verses.english: That Brahmana who is the giver of the birth for the sake of the Veda and the teacher of the prescribed duties becomes by law the father of an aged man, even though he himself be a child.

verses.text:
अध्यापयाम् आस पितॄन् शिशुर् आङ्गिरसः कविः ।
पुत्रका इति ह-उवाच ज्ञानेन परिगृह्य तान् ॥ १५१ ॥
verses.english: Young Kavi, the son of Angiras, taught his (relatives who were old enough to be) fathers, and, as he excelled them in (sacred) knowledge, he called them 'Little sons.'

verses.text:
ते तम् अर्थम् अपृच्छन्त देवान् आगत.मन्यवः ।
देवाश् च-एतान् समेत्य-ऊचुर् न्याय्यं वः शिशुर् उक्तवान् ॥ १५२
                                ॥
verses.english: They, moved with resentment, asked the gods concerning that matter, and the gods, having assembled, answered, 'The child has addressed you properly.'

verses.text:
अज्ञो भवति वै बालः पिता भवति मन्त्रदः ।
अज्ञं हि बालम् इत्य् आहुः पिता-इत्य् एव तु मन्त्रदम् ॥ १५३
                                ॥
verses.english: 'For (a man) destitute of (sacred) knowledge is indeed a child, and he who teaches him the Veda is his father; for (the sages) have always said "child" to an ignorant man, and "father" to a teacher of the Veda.'

verses.text:
न हायनैर् न पलितैर् न वित्तेन न बन्धुभिः ।
ऋषयश् चक्रिरे धर्मं यो ऽनूचानः स नो महान् ॥ १५४ ॥
verses.english: Neither through years, nor through white (hairs), nor through wealth, nor through (powerful) kinsmen (comes greatness). The sages have made this law, 'He who has learnt the Veda together with the Angas (Anukana) is (considered) great by us.'

verses.text:
विप्राणां ज्ञानतो ज्यैष्ठ्यं क्षत्रियाणां तु वीर्यतः ।
वैश्यानां धान्यधनतः शूद्राणाम् एव जन्मतः ॥ १५५ ॥
verses.english: The seniority of Brahmanas is from (sacred) knowledge, that of Kshatriyas from valour, that of Vaisyas from wealth in grain (and other goods), but that of Sudras alone from age.

verses.text:
न तेन वृद्धो भवति येनास्य पलितं शिरः ।
यो वै युवा-अप्य् अधीयानस् तं देवाः स्थविरं विदुः ॥ १५६
                                ॥
verses.english: A man is not therefore (considered) venerable because his head is gray; him who, though young, has learned the Veda, the gods consider to be venerable.

verses.text:
यथा काष्ठमयो हस्ती यथा चर्ममयो मृगः ।
यश् च विप्रो ऽन्.अधीयानस् त्रयस् ते नाम बिभ्रति ॥ १५७
                                ॥
verses.english: As an elephant made of wood, as an antelope made of leather, such is an unlearned Brahmana; those three have nothing but the names (of their kind).

verses.text:
यथा षण्ढो ऽ.फलः स्त्रीषु यथा गौर् गवि च-अ.फला
                                ।
यथा च-अज्ञे ऽ.फलं दानं तथा विप्रो ऽन्.ऋचो ऽ.फलः ॥
                                १५८ ॥
verses.english: As a eunuch is unproductive with women, as a cow with a cow is unprolific, and as a gift made to an ignorant man yields no reward, even so is a Brahmana useless, who (does) not (know) the Rikas.

verses.text:
अहिंसया-एव भूतानां कार्यं श्रेयो ऽनुशासनम् ।
वाक् च-एव मधुरा श्लक्ष्णा प्रयोज्या धर्मम् इच्छता ॥ १५९
                                ॥
verses.english: Created beings must be instructed in (what concerns) their welfare without giving them pain, and sweet and gentle speech must be used by (a teacher) who desires (to abide by) the sacred law.

verses.text:
यस्य वाच्.मनसी शुद्धे सम्यग्गुप्ते च सर्वदा ।
स वै सर्वम् अवाप्नोति वेदान्त.उपगतं फलम् ॥ १६० ॥
verses.english: He, forsooth, whose speech and thoughts are pure and ever perfectly guarded, gains the whole reward which is conferred by the Vedanta.

verses.text:
न-अरुन्तुदः स्याद् आर्तो ऽपि न परद्रोह.कर्म.धीः ।
यया-अस्य-उद्विजते वाचा न-अलोक्यां ताम् उदीरयेत् ॥ १६१
                                ॥
verses.english: Let him not, even though in pain, (speak words) cutting (others) to the quick; let him not injure others in thought or deed; let him not utter speeches which make (others) afraid of him, since that will prevent him from gaining heaven.

verses.text:
सम्मानाद् ब्राह्मणो नित्यम् उद्विजेत विषाद् इव ।
अमृतस्य-इव च-आकाङ्क्षेद् अवमानस्य सर्वदा ॥ १६२ ॥
verses.english: A Brahmana should always fear homage as if it were poison; and constantly desire (to suffer) scorn as (he would long for) nectar.

verses.text:
सुखं ह्य् अवमतः शेते सुखं च प्रतिबुध्यते ।
सुखं चरति लोके ऽस्मिन्न् अवमन्ता विनश्यति ॥ १६३ ॥
verses.english: For he who is scorned (nevertheless may) sleep with an easy mind, awake with an easy mind, and with an easy mind walk here among men; but the scorner utterly perishes.

verses.text:
अनेन क्रमयोगेन संस्कृत.आत्मा द्विजः शनैः ।
गुरौ वसन् सञ्चिनुयाद् ब्रह्माधिगमिकं तपः ॥ १६४ ॥
verses.english: A twice-born man who has been sanctified by the (employment of) the means, (described above) in due order, shall gradually and cumulatively perform the various austerities prescribed for (those who) study the Veda.

verses.text:
तपो.विशेषैर् विविधैर् व्रतैश् च विधिचोदितैः ।
वेदः कृत्स्नो ऽधिगन्तव्यः स.रहस्यो द्विजन्मना ॥ १६५
                                ॥
verses.english: An Aryan must study the whole Veda together with the Rahasyas, performing at the same time various kinds of austerities and the vows prescribed by the rules (of the Veda).

verses.text:
वेदम् एव सदा-अभ्यस्येत् तपस् तप्स्यन् द्विजोत्तमः ।
वेदाभ्यासो हि विप्रस्य तपः परम् इह-उच्यते ॥ १६६ ॥
verses.english: Let a Brahmana who desires to perform austerities, constantly repeat the Veda; for the study of the Veda is declared (to be) in this world the highest austerity for a Brahmana.

verses.text:
आ ह-एव स नखाग्रेभ्यः परमं तप्यते तपः ।
यः स्रग्व्य् अपि द्विजो ऽधीते स्वाध्यायं शक्तितो ऽन्वहम् ॥
                                १६७ ॥
verses.english: Verily, that twice-born man performs the highest austerity up to the extremities of his nails, who, though wearing a garland, daily recites the Veda in private to the utmost of his ability.

verses.text:
यो ऽन्.अधीत्य द्विजो वेदम् अन्यत्र कुरुते श्रमम् ।
स जीवन्न् एव शूद्रत्वम् आशु गच्छति स.अन्वयः ॥ १६८
                                ॥
verses.english: A twice-born man who, not having studied the Veda, applies himself to other (and worldly study), soon falls, even while living, to the condition of a Sudra and his descendants (after him).

verses.text:
मातुर् अग्रे ऽधिजननं द्वितीयं मौञ्जिबन्धने ।
तृतीयं यज्ञदीक्षायां द्विजस्य श्रुतिचोदनात् ॥ १६९ ॥
verses.english: According to the injunction of the revealed texts the first birth of an Aryan is from (his natural) mother, the second (happens) on the tying of the girdle of Munga grass, and the third on the initiation to (the performance of) a (Srauta) sacrifice.

verses.text:
तत्र यद् ब्रह्मजन्म-अस्य मौञ्जीबन्धनचिह्नितम् ।
तत्र-अस्य माता सावित्री पिता त्व् आचार्य उच्यते ॥ १७० ॥
verses.english: Among those (three) the birth which is symbolised by the investiture with the girdle of Munga grass, is his birth for the sake of the Veda; they declare that in that (birth) the Sivitri (verse) is his mother and the teacher his father.

verses.text:
वेदप्रदानाद् आचार्यं पितरं परिचक्षते ।
न ह्य् अस्मिन् युज्यते कर्म किञ् चिद् आ मौञ्जिबन्धनात् ॥ १७१
                                ॥
verses.english: They call the teacher (the pupil's) father because he gives the Veda; for nobody can perform a (sacred) rite before the investiture with the girdle of Munga grass.

verses.text:
न-अभिव्याहारयेद् ब्रह्म स्वधानिनयनाद् ऋते ।
शूद्रेण हि समस् तावद् यावद् वेदे न जायते ॥ १७२ ॥
verses.english: (He who has not been initiated) should not pronounce (any) Vedic text excepting (those required for) the performance of funeral rites, since he is on a level with a Sudra before his birth from the Veda.

verses.text:
कृत.उपनयनस्य-अस्य व्रतादेशनम् इष्यते ।
ब्रह्मणो ग्रहणं च-एव क्रमेण विधि.पूर्वकम् ॥ १७३
                                ॥
verses.english: The (student) who has been initiated must be instructed in the performance of the vows, and gradually learn the Veda, observing the prescribed rules.

verses.text:
यद्य् अस्य विहितं चर्म यत् सूत्रं या च मेखला ।
यो दण्डो यत्-च वसनं तत् तद् अस्य व्रतेष्व् अपि ॥ १७४
                                ॥
verses.english: Whatever dress of skin, sacred thread, girdle, staff, and lower garment are prescribed for a (student at the initiation), the like (must again be used) at the (performance of the) vows.

verses.text:
सेवेत-इमांस् तु नियमान् ब्रह्मचारी गुरौ वसन् ।
सन्नियम्य-इन्द्रियग्रामं तपोवृद्धि.अर्थम् आत्मनः ॥ १७५
                                ॥
verses.english: But a student who resides with his teacher must observe the following restrictive rules, duly controlling all his organs, in order to increase his spiritual merit.

verses.text:
नित्यं स्नात्वा शुचिः कुर्याद् देव.ऋषि.पितृतर्पणम् ।
देवताभ्यर्चनं च-एव समिदाधानम् एव च ॥ १७६ ॥
verses.english: Every day, having bathed, and being purified, he must offer libations of water to the gods, sages and manes, worship (the images of) the gods, and place fuel on (the sacred fire).

verses.text:
वर्जयेन् मधु मांसं च गन्धं माल्यं रसान् स्त्रियः ।
शुक्तानि यानि सर्वाणि प्राणिनां च-एव हिंसनम् ॥ १७७ ॥
verses.english: Let him abstain from honey, meat, perfumes, garlands, substances (used for) flavouring (food), women, all substances turned acid, and from doing injury to living creatures.

verses.text:
अभ्यङ्गम् अञ्जनं चाक्ष्णोर् उपानह्.छत्रधारणम् ।
कामं क्रोधं च लोभं च नर्तनं गीतवादनम् ॥ १७८
                                ॥
verses.english: From anointing (his body), applying collyrium to his eyes, from the use of shoes and of an umbrella (or parasol), from (sensual) desire, anger, covetousness, dancing, singing, and playing (musical instruments),

verses.text:
द्यूतं च जनवादं च परिवादं तथा-अनृतम् ।
स्त्रीणां च प्रेक्षणालम्भम् उपघातं परस्य च ॥ १७९ ॥
                                    २.१७९च्व्/ म्: 
                                    -आलम्भाअव् ॥ 2.179 ॥
verses.english: From gambling, idle disputes, backbiting, and lying, from looking at and touching women, and from hurting others.

verses.text:
एकः शयीत सर्वत्र न रेतः स्कन्दयेत् क्व चित् ।
कामाद्द् हि स्कन्दयन् रेतो हिनस्ति व्रतम् आत्मनः ॥ १८०
                                ॥
verses.english: Let him always sleep alone, let him never waste his manhood; for he who voluntarily wastes his manhood, breaks his vow.

verses.text:
स्वप्ने सिक्त्वा ब्रह्मचारी द्विजः शुक्रम् अ.कामतः ।
स्नात्वा-अर्कम् अर्चयित्वा त्रिः पुनर् माम् इत्य् ऋचं जपेत् ॥ १८१
                                ॥
verses.english: A twice-born student, who has involuntarily wasted his manly strength during sleep, must bathe, worship the sun, and afterwards thrice mutter the Rik-verse (which begins), 'Again let my strength return to me.'

verses.text:
उदकुम्भं सुमनसो गोशकृत्.मृत्तिका.कुशान् ।
आहरेद् यावद् अर्थानि भैक्षं च-अहर्.अहश् चरेत् ॥ १८२
                                    ॥
verses.english: Let him fetch a pot full of water, flowers, cowdung, earth, and Kusa grass, as much as may be required (by his teacher), and daily go to beg food.

verses.text:
वेद.यज्ञैर् अहीनानां प्रशस्तानां स्वकर्मसु ।
ब्रह्मचार्य् आहरेद् भैक्षं गृहेभ्यः प्रयतो ऽन्वहम् ॥
                                    १८३ ॥
verses.english: A student, being pure, shall daily bring food from the houses of men who are not deficient in (the knowledge of) the Veda and in (performing) sacrifices, and who are famous for (following their lawful) occupations.

verses.text:
गुरोः कुले न भिक्षेत न ज्ञाति.कुल.बन्धुषु ।
अ.लाभे त्व् अन्यगेहानां पूर्वं पूर्वं विवर्जयेत् ॥ १८४
                                    ॥
verses.english: Let him not beg from the relatives of his teacher, nor from his own or his mother's blood-relations; but if there are no houses belonging to strangers, let him go to one of those named above, taking the last-named first;

verses.text:
सर्वं वापि चरेद् ग्रामं पूर्व.उक्तानाम् अ.सम्भवे ।
नियम्य प्रयतो वाचम् अभिशस्तांस् तु वर्जयेत् ॥ १८५
                                    ॥
verses.english: Or, if there are no (virtuous men of the kind) mentioned above, he may go to each (house in the) village, being pure and remaining silent; but let him avoid Abhisastas (those accused of mortal sin).

verses.text:
दूराद् आहृत्य समिधः सन्निदध्याद् विहायसि ।
सायं.प्रातश् च जुहुयात् ताभिर् अग्निम् अतन्द्रितः ॥ १८६
                                    ॥
verses.english: Having brought sacred fuel from a distance, let him place it anywhere but on the ground, and let him, unwearied, make with it burnt oblations to the sacred fire, both evening and morning.

verses.text:
अ.कृत्वा भैक्षचरणम् अ.समिध्य च पावकं ।
अन्.आतुरः सप्तरात्रम् अवकीर्णिव्रतं चरेत् ॥ १८७ ॥
verses.english: He who, without being sick, neglects during seven (successive) days to go out begging, and to offer fuel in the sacred fire, shall perform the penance of an Avakirnin (one who has broken his vow).

verses.text:
भैक्षेण वर्तयेन् नित्यं न-एकान्न.अदी भवेद् व्रती
                                    ।
भैक्षेण व्रतिनो वृत्तिर् उपवास.समा स्मृता ॥ १८८
                                    ॥
verses.english: He who performs the vow (of studentship) shall constantly subsist on alms, (but) not eat the food of one (person only); the subsistence of a student on begged food is declared to be equal (in merit) to fasting.

verses.text:
व्रतवद् देव.दैवत्ये पित्र्ये कर्मण्य् अथ-ऋषिवत् ।
कामम् अभ्यर्थितो ऽश्नीयाद् व्रतम् अस्य न लुप्यते ॥ १८९
                                    ॥
verses.english: At his pleasure he may eat, when invited, the food of one man at (a rite) in honour of the gods, observing (however the conditions on his vow, or at a (funeral meal) in honor of the manes, behaving (however) like a hermit.

verses.text:
ब्राह्मणस्य-एव कर्म-एतद् उपदिष्टं मनीषिभिः ।
राजन्य.वैश्ययोस् त्व् एवं न-एतत् कर्म विधीयते ॥ १९०
                                    ॥
verses.english: This duty is prescribed by the wise for a Brahmana only; but no such duty is ordained for a Kshatriya and a Vaisya.

verses.text:
चोदितो गुरुणा नित्यम् अ.प्रचोदित एव वा ।
कुर्याद् अध्ययने यत्नम् आचार्यस्य हितेषु च ॥ १९१ ॥ २.१९१च्व्/ म्: 
                                    अध्ययने योगम् ॥ 2.191 ॥
verses.english: Both when ordered by his teacher, and without a (special) command, (a student) shall always exert himself in studying (the Veda), and in doing what is serviceable to his teacher.

verses.text:
शरीरं च-एव वाचं च बुद्धीन्द्रिय.मनांसि च ।
नियम्य प्राञ्जलिस् तिष्ठेद् वीक्षमाणो गुरोर् मुखम् ॥ १९२
                                ॥
verses.english: Controlling his body, his speech, his organs (of sense), and his mind, let him stand with joined hands, looking at the face of his teacher.

verses.text:
नित्यम् उद्धृत.पाणिः स्यात् साधु.आचारः सु.संवृतः ।
आस्यताम् इति च-उक्तः सन्न् आसीत-अभिमुखं गुरोः ॥ १९३
                                ॥
verses.english: Let him always keep his right arm uncovered, behave decently and keep his body well covered, and when he is addressed (with the words), 'Be seated,' he shall sit down, facing his teacher.

verses.text:
हीन.अन्न.वस्त्र.वेषः स्यात् सर्वदा गुरुसन्निधौ ।
उत्तिष्ठेत् प्रथमं चास्य चरमं च-एव संविशेत् ॥ १९४
                                ॥
verses.english: In the presence of his teacher let him always eat less, wear a less valuable dress and ornaments (than the former), and let him rise earlier (from his bed), and go to rest later.

verses.text:
प्रतिश्रावण.सम्भाषे शयानो न समाचरेत् ।
न-आसीनो न च भुञ्जानो न तिष्ठन् न पराङ्.मुखः ॥ १९५
                                ॥
verses.english: Let him not answer or converse with (his teacher), reclining on a bed, nor sitting, nor eating, nor standing, nor with an averted face.

verses.text:
आसीनस्य स्थितः कुर्याद् अभिगच्छंस् तु तिष्ठतः ।
प्रत्युद्गम्य त्व् आव्रजतः पश्चाद् धावंस् तु धावतः ॥ १९६
                                ॥
verses.english: Let him do (that), standing up, if (his teacher) is seated, advancing towards him when he stands, going to meet him if he advances, and running after him when he runs;

verses.text:
पराङ्.मुखस्य-अभिमुखो दूरस्थस्य-एत्य च.अन्तिकम् ।
प्रणम्य तु शयानस्य निदेशे च-एव तिष्ठतः ॥ १९७ ॥
verses.english: Going (round) to face (the teacher), if his face is averted, approaching him if he stands at a distance, but bending towards him if he lies on a bed, and if he stands in a lower place.

verses.text:
नीचं शय्या.आसनं च.अस्य नित्यं स्याद् गुरुसन्निधौ ।
गुरोस् तु चक्षुर्विषये न यथा.इष्ट.आसनो भवेत् ॥ १९८
                                ॥
verses.english: When his teacher is nigh, let his bed or seat be low; but within sight of his teacher he shall not sit carelessly at ease.

verses.text:
न-उदाहरेद् अस्य नाम परोक्षम् अपि केवलम् ।
न च-एव-अस्य.अनुकुर्वीत गति.भाषित.चेष्टितम् ॥ १९९
                                ॥
verses.english: Let him not pronounce the mere name of his teacher (without adding an honorific title) behind his back even, and let him not mimic his gait, speech, and deportment.

verses.text:
गुरोर् यत्र परिवादो निन्दा वा.अपि प्रवर्तते ।
कर्णौ तत्र पिधातव्यौ गन्तव्यं वा ततो ऽन्यतः ॥ २००
                                ॥
verses.english: Wherever (people) justly censure or falsely defame his teacher, there he must cover his ears or depart thence to another place.

verses.text:
परीवादात् खरो भवति श्वा वै भवति निन्दकः ।
परिभोक्ता कृमिर् भवति कीटो भवति मत्सरी ॥ २०१ ॥
verses.english: By censuring (his teacher), though justly, he will become (in his next birth) an ass, by falsely defaming him, a dog; he who lives on his teacher's substance, will become a worm, and he who is envious (of his merit), a (larger) insect.

verses.text:
दूरस्थो न-अर्चयेद् एनं न क्रुद्धो न-अन्तिके स्त्रियाः ।
यान.आसनस्थश् च-एव-एनम् अवरुह्य-अभिवादयेत् ॥ २०२
                                ॥
verses.english: He must not serve the (teacher by the intervention of another) while he himself stands aloof, nor when he (himself) is angry, nor when a woman is near; if he is seated in a carriage or on a (raised) seat, he must descend and afterwards salute his (teacher).

verses.text:
प्रतिवाते ऽनुवाते च न-आसीत गुरुणा सह । २.२०३अव्/ म्: 
                                    प्रतिवातानुवाते
अ.संश्रवे च-एव गुरोर् न किं चिद् अपि कीर्तयेत् ॥ २०३
                                ॥
verses.english: Let him not sit with his teacher, to the leeward or to the windward (of him); nor let him say anything which his teacher cannot hear.

verses.text:
गो.ऽश्व.उष्ट्र.यान.प्रासाद.प्रस्तरेषु कटेषु च ।
आसीत गुरुणा सार्धं शिला.फलक.नौषु च ॥ २०४ ॥
verses.english: He may sit with his teacher in a carriage drawn by oxen, horses, or camels, on a terrace, on a bed of grass or leaves, on a mat, on a rock, on a wooden bench, or in a boat.

verses.text:
गुरोर् गुरौ सन्निहिते गुरुवद् वृत्तिम् आचरेत् ।
न च-अ.निसृष्टो गुरुणा स्वान् गुरून् अभिवादयेत् ॥ २०५
                                    ॥
verses.english: If his teacher's teacher is near, let him behave (towards him) as towards his own teacher; but let him, unless he has received permission from his teacher, not salute venerable persons of his own (family).

verses.text:
विद्यागुरुष्व् एवम् एव नित्या वृत्तिः स्वयोनिषु ।
प्रतिषेधत्सु च-अधर्माद्द् हितं च-उपदिशत्स्व् अपि ॥
                                    २०६ ॥
verses.english: This is likewise (ordained as) his constant behaviour towards (other) instructors in science, towards his relatives (to whom honour is due), towards all who may restrain him from sin, or may give him salutary advice.

verses.text:
श्रेयःसु गुरुवद् वृत्तिं नित्यम् एव समाचरेत् ।
गुरुपुत्रेषु च-आर्येषु गुरोश् च-एव स्वबन्धुषु ॥ २०७ ॥
                                        २.२०७च्व्/
                                        म्: गुरुपुत्रे तथाचार्ये ॥ 2.207 ॥
verses.english: Towards his betters let him always behave as towards his teacher, likewise towards sons of his teacher, born by wives of equal caste, and towards the teacher's relatives both on the side of the father and of the mother.

verses.text:
बालः समान.जन्मा वा शिष्यो वा यज्ञकर्मणि ।
अध्यापयन् गुरुसुतो गुरुवत्-मानम् अर्हति ॥ २०८ ॥
verses.english: The son of the teacher who imparts instruction (in his father's stead), whether younger or of equal age, or a student of (the science of) sacrifices (or of other Angas), deserves the same honour as the teacher.

verses.text:
उत्सादनं च गात्राणां स्नापन.उच्छिष्टभोजने ।
न कुर्याद् गुरुपुत्रस्य पादयोश् च-अवनेजनम् ॥ २०९
                                    ॥
verses.english: (A student) must not shampoo the limbs of his teacher's son, nor assist him in bathing, nor eat the fragments of his food, nor wash his feet.

verses.text:
गुरुवत् प्रतिपूज्याः स्युः स.वर्णा गुरुयोषितः ।
अ.सवर्णास् तु सम्पूज्याः प्रत्युत्थान.अभिवादनैः ॥ २१०
                                    ॥
verses.english: The wives of the teacher, who belong to the same caste, must be treated as respectfully as the teacher; but those who belong to a different caste, must be honoured by rising and salutation.

verses.text:
अभ्यञ्जनं स्नापनं च गात्र.उत्सादनम् एव च ।
गुरुपत्न्या न कार्याणि केशानां च प्रसाधनम् ॥ २११
                                    ॥
verses.english: Let him not perform for a wife of his teacher (the offices of) anointing her, assisting her in the bath, shampooing her limbs, or arranging her hair.

verses.text:
गुरुपत्नी तु युवतिर् न-अभिवाद्या-इह पादयोः ।
पूर्णविंशतिवर्षेण गुण.दोषौ विजानता ॥ २१२ ॥
verses.english: (A pupil) who is full twenty years old, and knows what is becoming and unbecoming, shall not salute a young wife of his teacher (by clasping) her feet.

verses.text:
स्वभाव एष नारीणां नराणाम् इह दूषणम् ।
अतो ऽर्थान् न प्रमाद्यन्ति प्रमदासु विपश्चितः ॥ २१३
                                    ॥
verses.english: It is the nature of women to seduce men in this (world); for that reason the wise are never unguarded in (the company of) females.

verses.text:
अ.विद्वांसम् अलं लोके विद्वांसम् अपि वा पुनः ।
प्रमदा ह्य् उत्पथं नेतुं काम.क्रोधवशानुगम् ॥ २१४
                                    ॥
verses.english: For women are able to lead astray in (this) world not only a fool, but even a learned man, and (to make) him a slave of desire and anger.

verses.text:
मात्रा स्वस्रा दुहित्रा वा न विविक्तासनो भवेत् ।
बलवान् इन्द्रियग्रामो विद्वांसम् अपि कर्षति ॥ २१५ ॥
verses.english: One should not sit in a lonely place with one's mother, sister, or daughter; for the senses are powerful, and master even a learned man.

verses.text:
कामं तु गुरुपत्नीनां युवतीनां युवा भुवि ।
विधिवद् वन्दनं कुर्याद् असाव् अहम् इति ब्रुवन् ॥ २१६
                                    ॥
verses.english: But at his pleasure a young student may prostrate himself on the ground before the young wife of a teacher, in accordance with the rule, and say, 'I, N. N., (worship thee, O lady).'

verses.text:
विप्रोष्य पादग्रहणम् अन्वहं च-अभिवादनम् ।
गुरुदारेषु कुर्वीत सतां धर्मम् अनुस्मरन् ॥ २१७ ॥
verses.english: On returning from a journey he must clasp the feet of his teacher's wife and daily salute her (in the manner just mentioned), remembering the duty of the virtuous.

verses.text:
यथा खनन् खनित्रेण नरो वार्य् अधिगच्छति ।
तथा गुरुगतां विद्यां शुश्रूषुर् अधिगच्छति ॥ २१८
                                    ॥
verses.english: As the man who digs with a spade (into the ground) obtains water, even so an obedient (pupil) obtains the knowledge which lies (hidden) in his teacher.

verses.text:
मुण्डो वा जटिलो वा स्याद् अथ वा स्यात्-शिखा.जटः ।
न-एनं ग्रामे ऽभिनिम्लोचेत् सूर्यो न-अभ्युदियात् क्व चित् ॥
                                २१९ ॥
verses.english: A (student) may either shave his head, or wear his hair in braids, or braid one lock on the crown of his head; the sun must never set or rise while he (lies asleep) in the village.

verses.text:
तं चेद् अभ्युदियात् सूर्यः शयानं कामचारतः ।
निम्लोचेद् वा-अप्य् अ.विज्ञानाज् जपन्न् उपवसेद् दिनम् ॥ २२०
                                ॥
verses.english: If the sun should rise or set while he is sleeping, be it (that he offended) intentionally or unintentionally, he shall fast during the (next) day, muttering (the Savitri).

verses.text:
सूर्येण ह्य् अभिनिर्मुक्तः शयानो ऽभ्युदितश् च यः । २.२२१अव्/ म्: 
                                    अभिनिम्लुक्तः
प्रायश्चित्तम् अ.कुर्वाणो युक्तः स्यान् महता-एनसा ॥ २२१
                                ॥
verses.english: For he who lies (sleeping), while the sun sets or rises, and does not perform (that) penance, is tainted by great guilt.

verses.text:
आचम्य प्रयतो नित्यम् उभे सन्ध्ये समाहितः ।
शुचौ देशे जपञ् जप्यम् उपासीत यथाविधि ॥ २२२ ॥
verses.english: Purified by sipping water, he shall daily worship during both twilights with a concentrated mind in a pure place, muttering the prescribed text according to the rule.

verses.text:
यदि स्त्री यद्य् अवरजः श्रेयः किं चित् समाचरेत् ।
तत् सर्वम् आचरेद् युक्तो यत्र च-अस्य रमेन् मनः ॥ २२३
                                ॥
verses.english: If a woman or a man of low caste perform anything (leading to) happiness, let him diligently practise it, as well as (any other permitted act) in which his heart finds pleasure.

verses.text:
धर्म.अर्थाव् उच्यते श्रेयः काम.अर्थौ धर्म एव च ।
अर्थ एव-इह वा श्रेयस् त्रिवर्ग इति तु स्थितिः ॥ २२४
                                ॥
verses.english: (Some declare that) the chief good consists in (the acquisition of) spiritual merit and wealth, (others place it) in (the gratification of) desire and (the acquisition of) wealth, (others) in (the acquisition of) spiritual merit alone, and (others say that the acquisition of) wealth alone is the chief good here (below); but the (correct) decision is that it consists of the aggregate of (those) three.

verses.text:
आचार्यश् च पिता च-एव माता भ्राता च पूर्वजः ।
न-आर्तेन-अप्य् अवमन्तव्या ब्राह्मणेन विशेषतः ॥ २२५
                                    ॥
verses.english: The teacher, the father, the mother, and an elder brother must not be treated with disrespect, especially by a Brahmana, though one be grievously offended (by them).

verses.text:
आचार्यो ब्रह्मणो मूर्तिः पिता मूर्तिः प्रजापतेः ।
माता पृथिव्या मूर्तिस् तु भ्राता स्वो मूर्तिर् आत्मनः ॥ २२६
                                    ॥
verses.english: The teacher is the image of Brahman, the father the image of Pragipati (the lord of created beings), the mother the image of the earth, and an (elder) full brother the image of oneself.

verses.text:
यं माता.पितरौ क्लेशं सहेते सम्भवे नृणाम् ।
न तस्य निष्कृतिः शक्या कर्तुं वर्षशतैर् अपि ॥ २२७
                                    ॥
verses.english: That trouble (and pain) which the parents undergo on the birth of (their) children, cannot be compensated even in a hundred years.

verses.text:
तयोर् नित्यं प्रियं कुर्याद् आचार्यस्य च सर्वदा ।
तेष्व् एव त्रिषु तुष्टेषु तपः सर्वं समाप्यते ॥ २२८
                                    ॥
verses.english: Let him always do what is agreeable to those (two) and always (what may please) his teacher; when those three are pleased, he obtains all (those rewards which) austerities (yield).

verses.text:
तेषां त्रयाणां शुश्रूषा परमं तप उच्यते ।
न तैर् अन्.अभ्यनुज्ञातो धर्मम् अन्यं समाचरेत् ॥ २२९
                                    ॥
verses.english: Obedience towards those three is declared to be the best (form of) austerity; let him not perform other meritorious acts without their permission.

verses.text:
त एव हि त्रयो लोकास् त एव त्रय आश्रमाः ।
त एव हि त्रयो वेदास् त एव-उक्तास् त्रयो ऽग्नयः ॥ २३०
                                    ॥
verses.english: For they are declared to be the three worlds, they the three (principal) orders, they the three Vedas, and they the three sacred fires.

verses.text:
पिता वै गार्हपत्यो ऽग्निर् माता-अग्निर् दक्षिणः स्मृतः
                                    ।
गुरुर् आहवनीयस् तु सा-अग्नित्रेता गरीयसी ॥ २३१ ॥
verses.english: The father, forsooth, is stated to be the Garhapatya fire, the mother the Dakshinagni, but the teacher the Ahavaniya fire; this triad of fires is most venerable.

verses.text:
त्रिष्व् अ.प्रमाद्यन्न् एतेषु त्रीन् लोकान् विजयेद् गृही ।
दीप्यमानः स्ववपुषा देववद् दिवि मोदते ॥ २३२ ॥
verses.english: He who neglects not those three, (even after he has become) a householder, will conquer the three worlds and, radiant in body like a god, he will enjoy bliss in heaven.

verses.text:
इमं लोकं मातृभक्त्या पितृभक्त्या तु मध्यमम् ।
गुरुशुश्रूषया त्व् एवं ब्रह्मलोकं समश्नुते ॥ २३३
                                    ॥
verses.english: By honouring his mother he gains this (nether) world, by honouring his father the middle sphere, but by obedience to his teacher the world of Brahman.

verses.text:
सर्वे तस्य-आदृता धर्मा यस्य-एते त्रय आदृताः ।
अन्.आदृतास् तु यस्य-एते सर्वास् तस्य-अ.फलाः क्रियाः ॥
                                    २३४ ॥
verses.english: All duties have been fulfilled by him who honours those three; but to him who honours them not, all rites remain fruitless.

verses.text:
यावत् त्रयस् ते जीवेयुस् तावत्-न-अन्यं समाचरेत् ।
तेष्व् एव नित्यं शुश्रूषां कुर्यात् प्रियहिते रतः ॥ २३५
                                    ॥
verses.english: As long as those three live, so long let him not (independently) perform any other (meritorious acts); let him always serve them, rejoicing (to do what is) agreeable and beneficial (to them).

verses.text:
तेषाम् अन्.उपरोधेन पारत्र्यं यद् यद् आचरेत् ।
तत् तन् निवेदयेत् तेभ्यो मनो.वचन.कर्मभिः ॥ २३६
                                    ॥
verses.english: He shall inform them of everything that with their consent he may perform in thought, word, or deed for the sake of the next world.

verses.text:
त्रिष्व् एतेष्व् इतिकृत्यं हि पुरुषस्य समाप्यते ।
एष धर्मः परः साक्षाद् उपधर्मो ऽन्य उच्यते ॥ २३७
                                    ॥
verses.english: By (honouring) these three all that ought to be done by man, is accomplished; that is clearly the highest duty, every other (act) is a subordinate duty.

verses.text:
श्रद्दधानः शुभां विद्याम् आददीत-अवराद् अपि ।
अन्याद् अपि परं धर्मं स्त्रीरत्नं दुष्कुलाद् अपि ॥ २३८
                                    ॥
verses.english: He who possesses faith may receive pure learning even from a man of lower caste, the highest law even from the lowest, and an excellent wife even from a base family.

verses.text:
विषाद् अप्य् अमृतं ग्राह्यं बालाद् अपि सुभाषितम् ।
अमित्राद् अपि सद्वृत्तम् अमेध्याद् अपि काञ्चनम् ॥ २३९
                                    ॥
verses.english: Even from poison nectar may be taken, even from a child good advice, even from a foe (a lesson in) good conduct, and even from an impure (substance) gold.

verses.text:
स्त्रियो रत्नान्य् अथो विद्या धर्मः शौचं सुभाषितम्
                                    ।
विविधानि च शील्पानि समादेयानि सर्वतः ॥ २४० ॥
verses.english: Excellent wives, learning, (the knowledge of) the law, (the rules of) purity, good advice, and various arts may be acquired from anybody.

verses.text:
अ.ब्राह्मणाद् अध्यायनम् आपत्काले विधीयते ।
अनुव्रज्या च शुश्रूषा यावद् अध्यायनं गुरोः ॥ २४१
                                    ॥
verses.english: It is prescribed that in times of distress (a student) may learn (the Veda) from one who is not a Brahmana; and that he shall walk behind and serve (such a) teacher, as long as the instruction lasts.

verses.text:
न-अ.ब्राह्मणे गुरौ शिष्यो वासम् आत्यन्तिकं वसेत् ।
ब्राह्मणे वा-अन्.अनूचाने काङ्क्षन् गतिम् अन्.उत्तमाम् ॥ २४२
                                    ॥
verses.english: He who desires incomparable bliss (in heaven) shall not dwell during his whole life in (the house of) a non-Brahmanical teacher, nor with a Brahmana who does not know the whole Veda and the Angas.

verses.text:
यदि त्व् आत्यन्तिकं वासं रोचयेत गुरोः कुले ।
युक्तः परिचरेद् एनम् आ शरीरविमोक्षणात् ॥ २४३ ॥
verses.english: But if (a student) desires to pass his whole life in the teacher's house, he must diligently serve him, until he is freed from this body.

verses.text:
आ समाप्तेः शरीरस्य यस् तु शुश्रूषते गुरुम् ।
स गच्छत्य् अञ्जसा विप्रो ब्रह्मणः सद्म शाश्वतम् ॥ २४४
                                ॥
verses.english: A Brahmana who serves his teacher till the dissolution of his body, reaches forthwith the eternal mansion of Brahman.

verses.text:
न पूर्वं गुरवे किं चिद् उपकुर्वीत धर्मवित् ।
स्नास्यंस् तु गुरुणा-आज्ञप्तः शक्त्या गुरु.अर्थम् आहरेत् ॥ २४५
                                ॥
verses.english: He who knows the sacred law must not present any gift to his teacher before (the Samavartana); but when, with the permission of his teacher, he is about to take the (final) bath, let him procure (a present) for the venerable man according to his ability,

verses.text:
क्षेत्रं हिरण्यं गाम् अश्वं छत्र.उपानहम् आसनम् । २.२४६अव्/ म्: 
                                    छत्रोपानहम् अन्ततः
धान्यं शाकं च वासांसि गुरवे प्रीतिम् आवहेत् ॥ २४६ ॥
                                    २.२४६च्व्/ म्: 
                                    धान्यं वासांसि शाकं वा गुरवे प्रीतिम् आहरन् ॥ 2.246 ॥
verses.english: (Viz.) a field, gold, a cow, a horse, a parasol and shoes, a seat, grain, (even) vegetables, (and thus) give pleasure to his teacher.

verses.text:
आचार्ये तु खलु प्रेते गुरुपुत्रे गुणान्विते ।
गुरुदारे सपिण्डे वा गुरुवद् वृत्तिम् आचरेत् ॥ २४७ ॥
verses.english: (A perpetual student) must, if his teacher dies, serve his son (provided he be) endowed with good qualities, or his widow, or his Sapinda, in the same manner as the teacher.

verses.text:
एतेष्व् अ.विद्यमानेषु स्थान.आसन.विहारवान् ।
प्रयुञ्जानो ऽग्निशुश्रूषां साधयेद् देहम् आत्मनः ॥ २४८ ॥
verses.english: Should none of these be alive, he must serve the sacred fire, standing (by day) and sitting (during the night), and thus finish his life.

verses.text:
एवं चरति यो विप्रो ब्रह्मचर्यम् अ.विप्लुतः ।
स गच्छत्य् उत्तमस्थानं न च-इह जायते पुनः ॥ २४९
                                ॥
verses.english: A Brahmana who thus passes his life as a student without breaking his vow, reaches (after death) the highest abode and will not be born again in this world.

verses.text:
षट्त्रिंशद्.आब्दिकं चर्यं गुरौ त्रैवेदिकं व्रतम् ।
तदर्धिकं पादिकं वा ग्रहणान्तिकम् एव वा ॥ १ ॥
verses.english: The vow (of studying) the three Vedas under a teacher must be kept for thirty-six years, or for half that time, or for a quarter, or until the (student) has perfectly learnt them.

verses.text:
वेदान् अधीत्य वेदौ वा वेदं वा-अपि यथाक्रमम् ।
अ.विप्लुत.ब्रह्मचर्यो गृहस्थाश्रमम् आवसेत् ॥ २ ॥
verses.english: (A student) who has studied in due order the three Vedas, or two, or even one only, without breaking the (rules of) studentship, shall enter the order of householders.

verses.text:
तं प्रतीतं स्वधर्मेण ब्रह्मदायहरं पितुः ।
स्रग्विणं तल्प आसीनम् अर्हयेत् प्रथमं गवा ॥ ३ ॥
verses.english: He who is famous for (the strict performance of) his duties and has received his heritage, the Veda, from his father, shall be honoured, sitting on a couch and adorned with a garland, with (the present of) a cow (and the honey-mixture).

verses.text:
गुरुणानुमतः स्नात्वा समावृत्तो यथाविधि ।
उद्वहेत द्विजो भार्यां स.वर्णां लक्षणान्विताम् ॥ ४ ॥
verses.english: Having bathed, with the permission of his teacher, and performed according to the rule the Samavartana (the rite on returning home), a twice-born man shall marry a wife of equal caste who is endowed with auspicious (bodily) marks.

verses.text:
अ.सपिण्डा च या मातुर् अ.सगोत्रा च या पितुः ।
सा प्रशस्ता द्विजातीनां दारकर्मणि मैथुने ॥ ५ ॥ ३.०५च्व्/ म्: 
                                    अ.मैथिनी ॥ 3.5 ॥
verses.english: A damsel who is neither a Sapinda on the mother's side, nor belongs to the same family on the father's side, is recommended to twice-born men for wedlock and conjugal union.

verses.text:
महान्त्य् अपि समृद्धानि गो.ऽज.अवि.धन.धान्यतः ।
स्त्रीसम्बन्धे दश-एतानि कुलानि परिवर्जयेत् ॥ ६ ॥
verses.english: In connecting himself with a wife, let him carefully avoid the ten following families, be they ever so great, or rich in kine, horses, sheep, grain, or (other) property,

verses.text:
हीन.क्रियं निष्.पुरुषं निश्.छन्दो रोमश.अर्शसम् ।
क्षय.आमयाव्य्.अपस्मारि.श्वित्रि.कुष्ठि.कुलानि च ॥ ७ ॥
verses.english: (Viz.) one which neglects the sacred rites, one in which no male children (are born), one in which the Veda is not studied, one (the members of) which have thick hair on the body, those which are subject to hemorrhoids, phthisis, weakness of digestion, epilepsy, or white or black leprosy.

verses.text:
न-उद्वहेत् कपिलां कन्यां न-अधिकाङ्गीं न रोगिणीम् ।
न-अ.लोमिकां न-अति.लोमां न वाचाटां न पिङ्गलाम् ॥ ८ ॥
                                    ३.०८च्व्/ म्: 
                                    वाचालां ॥ 3.8 ॥
verses.english: Let him not marry a maiden (with) reddish (hair), nor one who has a redundant member, nor one who is sickly, nor one either with no hair (on the body) or too much, nor one who is garrulous or has red (eyes),

verses.text:
न-ऋक्ष.वृक्ष.नदी.नाम्नीं न-अन्त्य.पर्वत.नामिकाम् ।
न पक्षि.अहि.प्रेष्य.नाम्नीं न च भीषन.नामिकाम् ॥ ९ ॥
verses.english: Nor one named after a constellation, a tree, or a river, nor one bearing the name of a low caste, or of a mountain, nor one named after a bird, a snake, or a slave, nor one whose name inspires terror.

verses.text:
अ.व्यङ्ग.अङ्गीं सौम्य.नाम्नीं हंस.वारण.गामिनीम् ।
तनुलोम.केश.दशनां मृद्व्.अङ्गीम् उद्वहेत् स्त्रियम् ॥ १० ॥
verses.english: Let him wed a female free from bodily defects, who has an agreeable name, the (graceful) gait of a Hamsa or of an elephant, a moderate (quantity of) hair on the body and on the head, small teeth, and soft limbs.

verses.text:
यस्यास् तु न भवेद् भ्राता न विज्ञायेत वा पिता । ३.११अव्/ म्: वै(वा
                                    पिता
न-उपयच्छेत तां प्राज्ञः पुत्रिका.अधर्मशङ्कया ॥ ११
                                ॥
verses.english: But a prudent man should not marry (a maiden) who has no brother, nor one whose father is not known, through fear lest (in the former case she be made) an appointed daughter (and in the latter) lest (he should commit) sin.

verses.text:
सवर्णा-अग्रे द्विजातीनां प्रशस्ता दारकर्मणि ।
कामतस् तु प्रवृत्तानाम् इमाः स्युः क्रमशो ऽवराः ॥ १२ ॥
verses.english: For the first marriage of twice-born men (wives) of equal caste are recommended; but for those who through desire proceed (to marry again) the following females, (chosen) according to the (direct) order (of the castes), are most approved.

verses.text:
शूद्रा-एव भार्या शूद्रस्य सा च स्वा च विशः स्मृते ।
ते च स्वा च-एव राज्ञश् च ताश् च स्वा च-अग्र.जन्मनः ॥ १३
                                ॥
verses.english: It is declared that a Sudra woman alone (can be) the wife of a Sudra, she and one of his own caste (the wives) of a Vaisya, those two and one of his own caste (the wives) of a Kshatriya, those three and one of his own caste (the wives) of a Brahmana.

verses.text:
न ब्राह्मण.क्षत्रिययोर् आपद्य् अपि हि तिष्ठतोः ।
कस्मिंश् चिद् अपि वृत्तान्ते शूद्रा भार्या-उपदिश्यते ॥ १४
                                    ॥
verses.english: A Sudra woman is not mentioned even in any (ancient) story as the (first) wife of a Brahmana or of a Kshatriya, though they lived in the (greatest) distress.

verses.text:
हीनजाति.स्त्रियं मोहाद् उद्वहन्तो द्विजातयः ।
कुलान्य् एव नयन्त्य् आशु स.सन्तानानि शूद्रताम् ॥ १५ ॥
verses.english: Twice-born men who, in their folly, wed wives of the low (Sudra) caste, soon degrade their families and their children to the state of Sudras.

verses.text:
शूद्रावेदी पतत्य् अत्रेर् उतथ्यतनयस्य च ।
शौनकस्य सुत.उत्पत्त्या तद्.अपत्यतया भृगोः ॥ १६
                                    ॥
verses.english: According to Atri and to (Gautama) the son of Utathya, he who weds a Sudra woman becomes an outcast, according to Saunaka on the birth of a son, and according to Bhrigu he who has (male) offspring from a (Sudra female, alone).

verses.text:
शूद्रां शयनम् आरोप्य ब्राह्मणो यात्य् अधोगतिम् ।
जनयित्वा सुतं तस्यां ब्राह्मण्याद् एव हीयते ॥ १७ ॥
verses.english: A Brahmana who takes a Sudra wife to his bed, will (after death) sink into hell; if he begets a child by her, he will lose the rank of a Brahmana.

verses.text:
दैव.पित्र्य.आतिथेयानि तत्.प्रधानानि यस्य तु ।
न-अश्नन्ति पितृ.देवास् तन् न च स्वर्गं स गच्छति ॥ १८
                                    ॥
verses.english: The manes and the gods will not eat the (offerings) of that man who performs the rites in honour of the gods, of the manes, and of guests chiefly with a (Sudra wife's) assistance, and such (a man) will not go to heaven.

verses.text:
वृषलीफेन.पीतस्य निःश्वास.उपहतस्य च ।
तस्यां च-एव प्रसूतस्य निष्कृतिर् न विधीयते ॥ १९
                                    ॥
verses.english: For him who drinks the moisture of a Sudra's lips, who is tainted by her breath, and who begets a son on her, no expiation is prescribed.

verses.text:
चतुर्णाम् अपि वर्णानं प्रेत्य च-इह हित.अहितान् ।
अष्टाव् इमान् समासेन स्त्रीविवाहान् निबोधत ॥ २० ॥
verses.english: Now listen to (the) brief (description of) the following eight marriage-rites used by the four castes (varna) which partly secure benefits and partly produce evil both in this life and after death.

verses.text:
ब्राह्मो दैवस् तथा-एव-आर्षः प्राजापत्यस् तथा-असुरः ।
गान्धर्वो राक्षसश् च-एव पैशाचश् च-अष्टमो ऽधमः ॥ २१
                                ॥
verses.english: (They are) the rite of Brahman (Brahma), that of the gods (Daiva), that of the Rishis (Arsha), that of Pragapati (Pragapatya), that of the Asuras (Asura), that of the Gandharvas (Gandharva), that of the Rhashasas (Rakshasa), and that of the Pisakas (Paisaka).

verses.text:
यो यस्य धर्म्यो वर्णस्य गुण.दोषौ च यस्य यौ ।
तद् वः सर्वं प्रवक्ष्यामि प्रसवे च गुण.अगुणान् ॥ २२
                                ॥
verses.english: Which is lawful for each caste (varna) and which are the virtues or faults of each (rite), all this I will declare to you, as well as their good and evil results with respect to the offspring.

verses.text:
षड् आनुपूर्व्या विप्रस्य क्षत्रस्य चतुरो ऽवरान् ।
विश्.शूद्रयोस् तु तान् एव विद्याद् धर्म्यान् अ.राक्षसान् ॥ २३ ॥
                                    ३.२३च्व्/ म्: 
                                    धर्म्यान् न राक्षसान् ॥ 3.23 ॥
verses.english: One may know that the first six according to the order (followed above) are lawful for a Brahmana, the four last for a Kshatriya, and the same four, excepting the Rakshasa rite, for a Vaisya and a Sudra.

verses.text:
चतुरो ब्राह्मणस्य-आद्यान् प्रशस्तान् कवयो विदुः ।
राक्षसं क्षत्रियस्य-एकम् आसुरं वैश्य.शूद्रयोः ॥ २४ ॥
verses.english: The sages state that the first four are approved (in the case) of a Brahmana, one, the Rakshasa (rite in the case) of a Kshatriya, and the Asura (marriage in that) of a Vaisya and of a Sudra.

verses.text:
पञ्चानां तु त्रयो धर्म्या द्वाव् अधर्म्यौ स्मृताव् इह ।
पैशाचश् च-असुरश् च-एव न कर्तव्यौ कदा चन ॥ २५ ॥
verses.english: But in these (Institutes of the sacred law) three of the five (last) are declared to be lawful and two unlawful; the Paisaka and the Asura (rites) must never be used.

verses.text:
पृथक् पृथग् वा मिश्रौ वा विवाहौ पूर्वचोदितौ ।
गान्धर्वो राक्षसश् च-एव धर्म्यौ क्षत्रस्य तौ स्मृतौ ॥ २६
                                ॥
verses.english: For Kshatriyas those before-mentioned two rites, the Gandharva and the Rakshasa, whether separate or mixed, are permitted by the sacred tradition.

verses.text:
आच्छाद्य च-अर्चयित्वा च श्रुत.शीलवते स्वयम् ।
आहूय दानं कन्याया ब्राह्मो धर्मः प्रकीर्तितः ॥ २७ ॥
verses.english: The gift of a daughter, after decking her (with costly garments) and honouring (her by presents of jewels), to a man learned in the Veda and of good conduct, whom (the father) himself invites, is called the Brahma rite.

verses.text:
यज्ञे तु वितते सम्यग् ऋत्विजे कर्म कुर्वते ।
अलङ्कृत्य सुतादानं दैवं धर्मं प्रचक्षते ॥ २८ ॥
verses.english: The gift of a daughter who has been decked with ornaments, to a priest who duly officiates at a sacrifice, during the course of its performance, they call the Daiva rite.

verses.text:
एकं गोमिथुनं द्वे वा वराद् आदाय धर्मतः ।
कन्याप्रदानं विधिवद् आर्षो धर्मः स उच्यते ॥ २९ ॥
verses.english: When (the father) gives away his daughter according to the rule, after receiving from the bridegroom, for (the fulfilment of) the sacred law, a cow and a bull or two pairs, that is named the Arsha rite.

verses.text:
सह-उभौ चरतां धर्मम् इति वाचा-अनुभाष्य च ।
कन्याप्रदानम् अभ्यर्च्य प्राजापत्यो विधिः स्मृतः ॥ ३० ॥
verses.english: The gift of a daughter (by her father) after he has addressed (the couple) with the text, 'May both of you perform together your duties,' and has shown honour (to the bridegroom), is called in the Smriti the Pragapatya rite.

verses.text:
ज्ञातिभ्यो द्रविणं दत्त्वा कन्यायै च-एव शक्तितः ।
कन्याप्रदानं स्वाच्छन्द्याद् आसुरो धर्म उच्यते ॥ ३१ ॥
verses.english: When (the bridegroom) receives a maiden, after having given as much wealth as he can afford, to the kinsmen and to the bride herself, according to his own will, that is called the Asura rite.

verses.text:
इच्छया-अन्योन्यसंयोगः कन्यायाश् च वरस्य च ।
गान्धर्वः स तु विज्ञेयो मैथुन्यः काम.सम्भवः ॥ ३२
                                ॥
verses.english: The voluntary union of a maiden and her lover one must know (to be) the Gandharva rite, which springs from desire and has sexual intercourse for its purpose.

verses.text:
हत्वा छित्त्वा च भित्त्वा च क्रोशन्तीं रुदन्तीं गृहात् ।
प्रसह्य कन्याहरणं राक्षसो विधिर् उच्यते ॥ ३३ ॥
verses.english: The forcible abduction of a maiden from her home, while she cries out and weeps, after (her kinsmen) have been slain or wounded and (their houses) broken open, is called the Rakshasa rite.

verses.text:
सुप्तां मत्तां प्रमत्तां वा रहो यत्र-उपगच्छति ।
स पापिष्ठो विवाहानां पैशाचश् च-अष्टमो ऽधमः ॥ ३४ ॥
                                    ३.३४च्व्/ म्: 
                                    पैशाचः प्रथितो ऽधमः ॥ 3.34 ॥
verses.english: When (a man) by stealth seduces a girl who is sleeping, intoxicated, or disordered in intellect, that is the eighth, the most base and sinful rite of the Pisakas.

verses.text:
अद्भिर् एव द्विज.अग्र्याणां कन्यादानं विशिष्यते ।
इतरेषां तु वर्णानाम् इतरेतरकाम्यया ॥ ३५ ॥
verses.english: The gift of daughters among Brahmanas is most approved, (if it is preceded) by (a libation of) water; but in the case of other castes (it may be performed) by (the expression of) mutual consent.

verses.text:
यो यस्य-एषां विवाहानां मनुना कीर्तितो गुणः ।
सर्वं शृणुत तं विप्राः सर्वं कीर्तयतो मम ॥ ३६ ॥
                                        ३.३६च्व्/
                                        म्: सम्यक् कीर्तयतो ॥ 3.36 ॥
verses.english: Listen now to me, ye Brahmanas, while I fully declare what quality has been ascribed by Manu to each of these marriage-rites.

verses.text:
दश पूर्वान् परान् वंश्यान् आत्मानं च-एकविंशकम् ।
ब्राह्मीपुत्रः सुकृतकृत्-मोचयत्य् एनसः पितॄन् ॥ ३७ ॥
verses.english: The son of a wife wedded according to the Brahma rite, if he performs meritorious acts, liberates from sin ten ancestors, ten descendants and himself as the twenty-first.

verses.text:
दैव.ऊढाजः सुतश् च-एव सप्त सप्त पर.अवरान् ।
आर्ष.ऊढाजः सुतस् त्रींस् त्रीन् षट् षट् काय.ऊढजः सुतः
                                    ॥ ३८ ॥
verses.english: The son born of a wife, wedded according to the Daiva rite, likewise (saves) seven ancestors and seven descendants, the son of a wife married by the Arsha rite three (in the ascending and descending lines), and the son of a wife married by the rite of Ka (Pragapati) six (in either line).

verses.text:
ब्राह्म.आदिषु विवाहेषु चतुर्ष्व् एव-अनुपूर्वशः ।
ब्रह्मवर्चस्विनः पुत्रा जायन्ते शिष्टसम्मताः ॥ ३९ ॥
                                        ३.३९च्व्/
                                        म्: ब्रह्मवर्चसिनः ॥ 3.39 ॥
verses.english: From the four marriages, (enumerated) successively, which begin with the Brahma rite spring sons, radiant with knowledge of the Veda and honoured by the Sishtas (good men).

verses.text:
रूप.सत्त्व.गुण.उपेता धनवन्तो यशस्विनः ।
पर्याप्त.भोगा धर्मिष्ठा जीवन्ति च शतं समाः ॥ ४०
                                    ॥
verses.english: Endowded with the qualities of beauty and goodness, possessing wealth and fame, obtaining as many enjoyments as they desire and being most righteous, they will live a hundred years.

verses.text:
इतरेषु तु शिष्टेषु नृशंसा.अनृतवादिनः ।
जायन्ते दुर्विवाहेषु ब्रह्म.धर्म.द्विषः सुताः ॥ ४१
                                    ॥
verses.english: But from the remaining (four) blamable marriages spring sons who are cruel and speakers of untruth, who hate the Veda and the sacred law.

verses.text:
अनिन्दितैः स्त्रीविवाहैर् अनिन्द्या भवति प्रजा ।
निन्दितैर् निन्दिता नॄणां तस्मान् निन्द्यान् विवर्जयेत् ॥ ४२
                                    ॥
verses.english: In the blameless marriages blameless children are born to men, in blamable (marriages) blamable (offspring); one should therefore avoid the blamable (forms of marriage).

verses.text:
पाणिग्रहणसंस्कारः स.वर्णासु-उपदिश्यते ।
अ.सवर्णास्व् अयं ज्ञेयो विधिर् उद्वाहकर्मणि ॥ ४३ ॥
verses.english: The ceremony of joining the hands is prescribed for (marriages with) women of equal caste (varna); know that the following rule (applies) to weddings with females of a different caste (varna).

verses.text:
शरः क्षत्रियया ग्राह्यः प्रतोदो वैश्यकन्यया ।
वसनस्य दशा ग्राह्या शूद्रया-उत्कृष्टवेदने ॥ ४४ ॥
verses.english: On marrying a man of a higher caste a Kshatriya bride must take hold of an arrow, a Vaisya bride of a goad, and a Sudra female of the hem of the (bridegroom's) garment.

verses.text:
ऋतुकालाभिगामी स्यात् स्वदारनिरतः सदा ।
पर्ववर्जं व्रजेच् च-एनां तद्.व्रतो रतिकाम्यया ॥ ४५ ॥
verses.english: Let (the husband) approach his wife in due season, being constantly satisfied with her (alone); he may also, being intent on pleasing her, approach her with a desire for conjugal union (on any day) excepting the Parvans.

verses.text:
ऋतुः स्वाभाविकः स्त्रीणां रात्रयः षोडश स्मृताः ।
चतुर्भिर् इतरैः सार्धम् अहोभिः सद्विगर्हितैः ॥ ४६ ॥
verses.english: Sixteen (days and) nights (in each month), including four days which differ from the rest and are censured by the virtuous, (are called) the natural season of women.

verses.text:
तासाम् आद्याश् चतस्रस् तु निन्दिता-एकादशी च या ।
त्रयोदशी च शेषास् तु प्रशस्ता दशरात्रयः ॥ ४७ ॥
verses.english: But among these the first four, the eleventh and the thirteenth are (declared to be) forbidden; the remaining nights are recommended.

verses.text:
युग्मासु पुत्रा जायन्ते स्त्रियो ऽयुग्मासु रात्रिषु ।
तस्माद् युग्मासु पुत्रार्थी संविशेद् आर्तवे स्त्रियम् ॥ ४८ ॥
verses.english: On the even nights sons are conceived and daughters on the uneven ones; hence a man who desires to have sons should approach his wife in due season on the even (nights).

verses.text:
पुमान् पुंसो ऽधिके शुक्रे स्त्री भवत्य् अधिके स्त्रियाः ।
समे ऽपुमान् पुं.स्त्रियौ वा क्षीणे ऽल्पे च विपर्ययः ॥ ४९
                                ॥
verses.english: A male child is produced by a greater quantity of male seed, a female child by the prevalence of the female; if (both are) equal, a hermaphrodite or a boy and a girl; if (both are) weak or deficient in quantity, a failure of conception (results).

verses.text:
निन्द्यास्व् अष्टासु च-अन्यासु स्त्रियो रात्रिषु वर्जयन् ।
ब्रह्मचार्य् एव भवति यत्र तत्र-आश्रमे वसन् ॥ ५० ॥
verses.english: He who avoids women on the six forbidden nights and on eight others, is (equal in chastity to) a student, in whichever order he may live.

verses.text:
न कन्यायाः पिता विद्वान् गृह्णीयात्-शुल्कम् अणु-अपि ।
गृह्णन्-शुल्कं हि लोभेन स्यान् नरो ऽपत्यविक्रयी ॥ ५१ ॥
verses.english: No father who knows (the law) must take even the smallest gratuity for his daughter; for a man who, through avarice, takes a gratuity, is a seller of his offspring.

verses.text:
स्त्रीधनानि तु ये मोहाद् उपजीवन्ति बान्धवाः ।
नारी यानानि वस्त्रं वा ते पापा यान्त्य् अधोगतिम् ॥ ५२ ॥
verses.english: But those (male) relations who, in their folly, live on the separate property of women, (e.g. appropriate) the beasts of burden, carriages, and clothes of women, commit sin and will sink into hell.

verses.text:
आर्षे गोमिथुनं शुल्कं के चिद् आहुर् मृषा-एव तत् ।
अल्पो ऽप्य् एवं महान् वा-अपि विक्रयस् तावद् एव सः ॥ ५३ ॥
                                    ३.५३च्व्/ म्: 
                                    तावान् एव स विक्रयः ॥ 3.53 ॥
verses.english: Some call the cow and the bull (given) at an Arsha wedding 'a gratuity;' (but) that is wrong, since (the acceptance of) a fee, be it small or great, is a sale (of the daughter).

verses.text:
यासां न-आददते शुल्कं ज्ञातयो न स विक्रयः ।
अर्हणं तत् कुमारीणाम् आनृशंस्यं च केवलम् ॥ ५४ ॥ ३.५४च्व्/ म्: न
                                    केवलम् ॥ 3.54 ॥
verses.english: When the relatives do not appropriate (for their use) the gratuity (given), it is not a sale; (in that case) the (gift) is only a token of respect and of kindness towards the maidens.

verses.text:
पितृभिर् भ्रातृभिश् च-एताः पतिभिर् देवरैस् तथा ।
पूज्या भूषयितव्याश् च बहुकल्याणम् ईप्सुभिः ॥ ५५ ॥
verses.english: Women must be honoured and adorned by their fathers, brothers, husbands, and brothers-in-law, who desire (their own) welfare.

verses.text:
यत्र नार्यस् तु पूज्यन्ते रमन्ते तत्र देवताः ।
यत्र-एतास् तु न पूज्यन्ते सर्वास् तत्र-अ.फलाः क्रियाः ॥ ५६
                                ॥
verses.english: Where women are honoured, there the gods are pleased; but where they are not honoured, no sacred rite yields rewards.

verses.text:
शोचन्ति जामयो यत्र विनश्यत्य् आशु तत् कुलम् । ३.५७अव्/ नोत् इन्
                                    म्
न शोचन्ति तु यत्र-एता वर्धते तद्द् हि सर्वदा ॥ ५७ ॥
                                    ३.५७च्व्/ नोत्
                                    इन् म् ॥ 3.57 ॥
verses.english: Where the female relations live in grief, the family soon wholly perishes; but that family where they are not unhappy ever prospers.

verses.text:
जामयो यानि गेहानि शपन्त्य् अ.प्रतिपूजिताः । ३.५८अव्/ नोत् इन्
                                    म्
तानि कृत्याहतानि-इव विनश्यन्ति समन्ततः ॥ ५८ ॥ ३.५८च्व्/ नोत् इन्
                                    म् ॥ 3.58 ॥
verses.english: The houses on which female relations, not being duly honoured, pronounce a curse, perish completely, as if destroyed by magic.

verses.text:
तस्माद् एताः सदा पूज्या भूषण.आच्छादन.अशनैः । ३.५९अव्/ नोत् इन्
                                    म्
भूति.कामैर् नरैर् नित्यं सत्करेषु-उत्सवेषु च ॥ ५९ ॥
                                    ३.५९च्व्/ नोत्
                                    इन् म् ॥ 3.59 ॥
verses.english: Hence men who seek (their own) welfare, should always honour women on holidays and festivals with (gifts of) ornaments, clothes, and (dainty) food.

verses.text:
सन्तुष्टो भार्यया भर्ता भर्त्रा भार्या तथ-एव च । ३.६०अव्/ नोत् इन्
                                    म्
यस्मिन्न् एव कुले नित्यं कल्याणं तत्र वै ध्रुवम् ॥ ६० ॥
                                    ३.६०च्व्/ नोत्
                                    इन् म् ॥ 3.60 ॥
verses.english: In that family, where the husband is pleased with his wife and the wife with her husband, happiness will assuredly be lasting.

verses.text:
यदि हि स्त्री न रोचेत पुमांसं न प्रमोदयेत् । ३.६१अव्/ नोत् इन्
                                    म्
अप्रमोदात् पुनः पुंसः प्रजनं न प्रवर्तते ॥ ६१ ॥ ३.६१च्व्/ नोत् इन्
                                    म् ॥ 3.61 ॥
verses.english: For if the wife is not radiant with beauty, she will not attract her husband; but if she has no attractions for him, no children will be born.

verses.text:
स्त्रियां तु रोचमानायां सर्वं तद् रोचते कुलं । ३.६२अव्/ नोत् इन्
                                    म्
तस्यां त्व् अरोचमानायां सर्वम् एव न रोचते ॥ ६२ ॥ ३.६२च्व्/ नोत् इन्
                                    म् ॥ 3.62 ॥
verses.english: If the wife is radiant with beauty, the whole house is bright; but if she is destitute of beauty, all will appear dismal.

verses.text:
कु.विवाहैः क्रिया.लोपैर् वेदानध्ययनेन च । ३.६३अव्/ नोत् इन्
                                    म्
कुलान्य् अकुलतां यान्ति ब्राह्मणातिक्रमेण च ॥ ६३ ॥ ३.६३च्व्/ नोत् इन्
                                    म् ॥ 3.63 ॥
verses.english: By low marriages, by omitting (the performance of) sacred rites, by neglecting the study of the Veda, and by irreverence towards Brahmanas, (great) families sink low.

verses.text:
शिल्पेन व्यवहारेण शूद्रापत्यैश् च केवलैः । ३.६४अव्/ नोत् इन्
                                    म्
गोभिर् अश्वैश् च यानैश् च कृष्या राज.उपसेवया ॥ ६४ ॥
                                    ३.६४च्व्/ नोत्
                                    इन् म् ॥ 3.64 ॥
verses.english: By (practising) handicrafts, by pecuniary transactions, by (begetting) children on Sudra females only, by (trading in) cows, horses, and carriages, by (the pursuit of) agriculture and by taking service under a king,

verses.text:
अयाज्ययाजनैश् च-एव नास्तिक्येन च कर्मणाम् । ३.६५अव्/ नोत् इन्
                                    म्
कुलान्य् आशु विनश्यन्ति यानि हीनानि मन्त्रतः ॥ ६५ ॥ ३.६५च्व्/ नोत् इन्
                                    म् ॥ 3.65 ॥
verses.english: By sacrificing for men unworthy to offer sacrifices and by denying (the future rewards for good) works, families, deficient in the (knowledge of the) Veda, quickly perish.

verses.text:
मन्त्रतस् तु समृद्धानि कुलान्य् अल्प.धनान्य् अपि । ३.६६अव्/ नोत् इन्
                                    म्
कुलसङ्ख्यां च गच्छन्ति कर्षन्ति च महद् यशः ॥ ६६ ॥
                                    ३.६६च्व्/ नोत्
                                    इन् म् ॥ 3.66 ॥
verses.english: But families that are rich in the knowledge of the Veda, though possessing little wealth, are numbered among the great, and acquire great fame.

verses.text:
[५७म] वैवाहिके ऽग्नौ कुर्वीत गृह्यं कर्म यथाविधि ।
[५७म्च्] पञ्चयज्ञविधानं च पक्तिं च-अन्वाहिकीं गृही ॥ ६७ ॥
verses.english: With the sacred fire, kindled at the wedding, a householder shall perform according to the law the domestic ceremonies and the five (great) sacrifices, and (with that) he shall daily cook his food.

verses.text:
[५८म] पञ्च सूना गृहस्थस्य चुल्ली पेषण्य् उपस्करः ।
[५८म्च्] कण्डनी च-उदकुम्भश् च बध्यते यास् तु वाहयन् ॥ ६८
                                ॥ ३.६८च्[५८म्च्]व्/
                                    म्: वध्यते ॥ 3.68 ॥
verses.english: A householder has five slaughter-houses (as it were, viz.) the hearth, the grinding-stone, the broom, the pestle and mortar, the water-vessel, by using which he is bound (with the fetters of sin).

verses.text:
[५९म] तासां क्रमेण सर्वासां निष्कृत्यर्थं महर्षिभिः ।
[५९म्च्] पञ्च कॢप्ता महायज्ञाः प्रत्यहं गृहमेधिनाम् ॥ ६९
                                ॥
verses.english: In order to successively expiate (the offences committed by means) of all these (five) the great sages have prescribed for householders the daily (performance of the five) great sacrifices.

verses.text:
[६०म] अध्यापनं ब्रह्मयज्ञः पितृयज्ञस् तु तर्पणम् ।
[६०म्च्] होमो दैवो बलिर् भौतो नृयज्ञो ऽतिथिपूजनम् ॥ ७०
                                ॥
verses.english: Teaching (and studying) is the sacrifice (offered) to Brahman, the (offerings of water and food called) Tarpana the sacrifice to the manes, the burnt oblation the sacrifice offered to the gods, the Bali offering that offered to the Bhutas, and the hospitable reception of guests the offering to men.

verses.text:
[६१म] पञ्च-एतान् यो महाअयज्ञान् न हापयति शक्तितः ।
[६१म्च्] स गृहे ऽपि वसन् नित्यं सूनादोषैर् न लिप्यते ॥ ७१
                                ॥
verses.english: He who neglects not these five great sacrifices, while he is able (to perform them), is not tainted by the sins (committed) in the five places of slaughter, though he constantly lives in the (order of) house (-holders).

verses.text:
[६२म] देवता.अतिथि.भृत्यानां पितॄणाम् आत्मनश् च यः ।
[६२म्च्] न निर्वपति पञ्चानाम् उच्छ्वसन् न स जीवति ॥ ७२
                                ॥
verses.english: But he who does not feed these five, the gods, his guests, those whom he is bound to maintain, the manes, and himself, lives not, though he breathes.

verses.text:
[६३म] अ.हुतं च हुतं च-एव तथा प्रहुतम् एव च ।
[६३म्च्] ब्राह्म्यं हुतं प्राशितं च पञ्चयज्ञान् प्रचक्षते ॥ ७३
                                ॥
verses.english: They call (these) five sacrifices also, Ahuta, Huta, Prahuta, Brahmya-huta, and Prasita.

verses.text:
[६४म] जपो ऽहुतो हुतो होमः प्रहुतो भौतिको बलिः ।
[६४म्च्] ब्राह्म्यं हुतं द्विजाग्र्यार्चा प्राशितं पितृतर्पणम् ॥ ७४
                                ॥
verses.english: Ahuta (not offered in the fire) is the muttering (of Vedic texts), Huta the burnt oblation (offered to the gods), Prahuta (offered by scattering it on the ground) the Bali offering given to the Bhutas, Brahmya-huta (offered in the digestive fire of Brahmanas), the respectful reception of Brahmana (guests), and Prasita (eaten) the (daily oblation to the manes, called) Tarpana.

verses.text:
[६५म] स्वाध्याये नित्ययुक्तः स्याद् दैवे च-एव-इह कर्मणि
                                ।
[६५म्च्] दैवकर्मणि युक्तो हि बिभर्ति-इदं चर.अचरम् ॥ ७५
                                ॥
verses.english: Let (every man) in this (second order, at least) daily apply himself to the private recitation of the Veda, and also to the performance of the offering to the gods; for he who is diligent in the performance of sacrifices, supports both the movable and the immovable creation.

verses.text:
[६६म] अग्नौ प्रास्ता-आहुतिः सम्यग् आदित्यम् उपतिष्ठते ।
[६६म्च्] आदित्याज् जायते वृष्तिर् वृष्तेर् अन्नं ततः प्रजाः ॥ ७६
                                ॥
verses.english: An oblation duly thrown into the fire, reaches the sun; from the sun comes rain, from rain food, therefrom the living creatures (derive their subsistence).

verses.text:
[६७म] यथा वायुं समाश्रित्य वर्तन्ते सर्वजन्तवः । ३.७७अ[६७म]व्/ म्: 
                                    सर्वे जीवन्ति जन्तवः
[६७म्च्] तथा गृहस्थम् आश्रित्य वर्तन्ते सर्व आश्रमाः ॥ ७७ ॥
                                    ३.७७च्[६७म्च्]व्/ म्: वर्तन्त इतराश्रमः ॥ 3.77 ॥
verses.english: As all living creatures subsist by receiving support from air, even so (the members of) all orders subsist by receiving support from the householder.

verses.text:
[६८म] यस्मात् त्रयो ऽप्य् आश्रमिणो ज्ञानेन-अन्नेन च-अन्वहम्
                                ।
[६८म्च्] गृहस्थेन-एव धार्यन्ते तस्माज् ज्येष्ठाश्रमो गृही ॥ ७८
                                ॥ ३.७८च्[६८म्च्]व्/
                                    क्: गृहम् ॥ 3.78 ॥
verses.english: Because men of the three (other) orders are daily supported by the householder with (gifts of) sacred knowledge and food, therefore (the order of) householders is the most excellent order.

verses.text:
[६९म] स सन्धार्यः प्रयत्नेन स्वर्गम् अक्षयम् इच्छता ।
[६९म्च्] सुखं च-इह-इच्छता-अत्यन्तं यो ऽधार्यो
                                दुर्बल.इन्द्रियैः ॥ ७९ ॥
verses.english: (The duties of) this order, which cannot be practised by men with weak organs, must be carefully observed by him who desires imperishable (bliss in) heaven, and constant happiness in this (life).

verses.text:
[७०म] ऋषयः पितरो देवा भूतान्य् अतिथयस् तथा ।
[७०म्च्] आशासते कुटुम्बिभ्यस् तेभ्यः कार्यं विजानता ॥ ८०
                                ॥
verses.english: The sages, the manes, the gods, the Bhutas, and guests ask the householders (for offerings and gifts); hence he who knows (the law), must give to them (what is due to each).

verses.text:
[७१म] स्वाध्यायेन-अर्चयेत-ऋषीन् होमैर् देवान् यथाविधि ।
[७१म्च्] पितॄन्-श्राद्धैश् च नॄन् अन्नैर् भूतानि बलिकर्मणा ॥ ८१
                                ॥
verses.english: Let him worship, according to the rule, the sages by the private recitation of the Veda, the gods by burnt oblations, the manes by funeral offerings (Sraddha), men by (gifts of) food, and the Bhutas by the Bali offering.

verses.text:
[७२म] कुर्याद् अहर्.अहः श्राद्धम् अन्नाद्येन-उदकेन वा ।
                                        ३.८२अ[७२म]व्/ म्: दद्याद् अहर्.अहः
[७२म्च्] पयो.मूल.फलैर् वा-अपि पितृभ्यः प्रीतिम् आवहन् ॥
                                    ८२ ॥
verses.english: Let him daily perform a funeral sacrifice with food, or with water, or also with milk, roots, and fruits, and (thus) please the manes.

verses.text:
[७३म] एकम् अप्य् आशयेद् विप्रं पितृ.अर्थे पाञ्चयज्ञिके ।
                                        ३.८३अ[७३म]व्/ म्: पितृ.अर्थं
[७३म्च्] न च-एव-अत्र-आशयेत् किं चिद् वैश्वदेवं प्रति
                                    द्विजम् ॥ ८३ ॥
verses.english: Let him feed even one Brahmana in honour of the manes at (the Sraddha), which belongs to the five great sacrifices; but let him not feed on that (occasion) any Brahmana on account of the Vaisvadeva offering.

verses.text:
[७४म] वैश्वदेवस्य सिद्धस्य गृह्ये ऽग्नौ विधिपूर्वकम्
                                    ।
[७४म्च्] आभ्यः कुर्याद् देवताभ्यो ब्राह्मणो होमम् अन्वहम् ॥
                                    ८४ ॥
verses.english: A Brahmana shall offer according to the rule (of his Grihya-sutra a portion) of the cooked food destined for the Vaisvadeva in the sacred domestic fire to the following deities:

verses.text:
[७५म] अग्नेः सोमस्य च-एव-आदौ तयोश् च-एव समस्तयोः
                                    ।
[७५म्च्] विश्वेभ्यश् च-एव देवेभ्यो धन्वन्तरय एव च ॥
                                    ८५ ॥
verses.english: First to Agni, and (next) to Soma, then to both these gods conjointly, further to all the gods (Visve Devah), and (then) to Dhanvantari,

verses.text:
[७६म] कुह्वै च-एव-अनुमत्यै च प्रजापतय एव च ।
[७६म्च्] सह द्यावापृथिव्योश् च तथा स्विष्टकृते ऽन्ततः ॥
                                    ८६ ॥
verses.english: Further to Kuhu (the goddess of the new-moon day), to Anumati (the goddess of the full-moon day), to Pragapati (the lord of creatures), to heaven and earth conjointly, and finally to Agni Svishtakrit (the fire which performs the sacrifice well).

verses.text:
[७७म] एवं सम्यग्ग् हविर् हुत्वा सर्वदिक्षु प्रदक्षिणम्
                                    ।
[७७म्च्] इन्द्र.अन्तक.अप्पति.इन्दुभ्यः स.अनुगेभ्यो बलिं
                                    हरेत् ॥ ८७ ॥
verses.english: After having thus duly offered the sacrificial food, let him throw Bali offerings in all directions of the compass, proceeding (from the east) to the south, to Indra, Yama, Varuna, and Soma, as well as to the servants (of these deities).

verses.text:
[७८म] मरुद्भ्य इति तु द्वारि क्षिपेद् अप्स्व् अद्भ्य इत्य् अपि
                                    ।
[७८म्च्] वनस्पतिभ्य इत्य् एवं मुसल.उलूखले हरेत् ॥ ८८
                                    ॥
verses.english: Saying, '(Adoration) to the Maruts,' he shall scatter (some food) near the door, and (some) in water, saying, '(Adoration to the waters;' he shall throw (some) on the pestle and the mortar, speaking thus, '(Adoration) to the trees.'

verses.text:
[७९म] उच्छीर्षके श्रियै कुर्याद् भद्रकाल्यै च पादतः
                                    ।
[७९म्च्] ब्रह्म.वास्तोष्पतिभ्यां तु वास्तुमध्ये बलिं हरेत्
                                    ॥ ८९ ॥
verses.english: Near the head (of the bed) he shall make an offering to Sri (fortune), and near the foot (of his bed) to Bhadrakali; in the centre of the house let him place a Bali for Brahman and for Vastoshpati (the lord of the dwelling) conjointly.

verses.text:
[८०म] विश्वेभ्यश् च-एव देवेभ्यो बलिम् आकाश उत्क्षिपेत्
                                    ।
[८०म्च्] दिवाचरेभ्यो भूतेभ्यो नक्तञ्चारिभ्य एव च ॥ ९०
                                    ॥
verses.english: Let him throw up into the air a Bali for all the gods, and (in the day-time one) for the goblins roaming about by day, (and in the evening one) for the goblins that walk at night.

verses.text:
[८१म] पृष्ठवास्तुनि कुर्वीत बलिं सर्वात्मभूतये । ३.९१अ[८१म]व्/
                                        म्: सर्वान्नभूतये
[८१म्च्] पितृभ्यो बलिशेषं तु सर्वं दक्षिणतो हरेत् ॥ ९१
                                    ॥
verses.english: In the upper story let him offer a Bali to Sarvatmabhuti; but let him throw what remains (from these offerings) in a southerly direction for the manes.

verses.text:
[८२म] शूनां च पतितानां च श्वपचां पाप.रोगिणाम् ।
[८२म्च्] वयसानां कृमीणां च शनकैर् निर्वपेद् भुवि ॥ ९२
                                    ॥ ३.९२च्[८२म्च्]व्/ म्: वयसां च ॥ 3.92 ॥
verses.english: Let him gently place on the ground (some food) for dogs, outcasts, Kandalas (Svapak), those afflicted with diseases that are punishments of former sins, crows, and insects.

verses.text:
[८३म] एवं यः सर्वभूतानि ब्राह्मणो नित्यम् अर्चति ।
[८३म्च्] स गच्छति परं स्थानं तेजोमूर्तिः पथा-ऋजुना ॥
                                    ९३ ॥
verses.english: That Brahmana who thus daily honours all beings, goes, endowed with a resplendent body, by a straight road to the highest dwelling-place (i.e. Brahman).

verses.text:
[८४म] कृत्वा-एतद् बलिकर्म-एवम् अतिथिं पूर्वम् आशयेत्
                                    ।
[८४म्च्] भिक्षां च भिक्षवे दद्याद् विधिवद् ब्रह्मचारिणे ॥
                                    ९४ ॥
verses.english: Having performed this Bali offering, he shall first feed his guest and, according to the rule, give alms to an ascetic (and) to a student.

verses.text:
[८५म] यत् पुण्यफलम् आप्नोति गां दत्त्वा विधिवद् गुरोः
                                    ।
[८५म्च्] तत् पुण्यफलम् आप्नोति भिक्षां दत्त्वा द्विजो गृही ॥
                                    ९५ ॥
verses.english: A twice-born householder gains, by giving alms, the same reward for his meritorious act which (a student) obtains for presenting, in accordance with the rule, a cow to his teacher.

verses.text:
[८६म] भिक्षाम् अप्य् उदपात्रं वा सत्कृत्य विधिपूर्वकम्
                                    ।
[८६म्च्] वेदतत्त्वार्थविदुषे ब्राह्मणाय-उपपादयेत् ॥ ९६
                                    ॥
verses.english: Let him give, in accordance with the rule, to a Brahmana who knows the true meaning of the Veda, even (a small portion of food as) alms, or a pot full of water, having garnished (the food with seasoning, or the pot with flowers and fruit).

verses.text:
[८७म] नश्यन्ति हव्य.कव्यानि नराणाम् अ.विजानताम् ।
[८७म्च्] भस्मीभूतेषु विप्रेषु मोहाद् दत्तानि दातृभिः ॥ ९७
                                    ॥ ३.९७च्[८७म्च्]व्/ म्: भस्मभूतेषु ॥ 3.97 ॥
verses.english: The oblations to gods and manes, made by men ignorant (of the law of gifts), are lost, if the givers in their folly present (shares of them) to Brahmanas who are mere ashes.

verses.text:
[८८म] विद्या.तपः.समृद्धेषु हुतं विप्रमुखाग्निषु ।
[८८म्च्] निस्तारयति दुर्गाच् च महतश् च-एव किल्बिषात् ॥ ९८
                                    ॥
verses.english: An offering made in the mouth-fire of Brahmanas rich in sacred learning and austerities, saves from misfortune and from great guilt.

verses.text:
[८९म] सम्प्राप्ताय त्व् अतिथये प्रदद्याद् आसन.उदके ।
[८९म्च्] अन्नं च-एव यथाशक्ति सत्कृत्य विधिपूर्वकम् ॥
                                    ९९ ॥ ३.९९च्[८९म्च्]व्/ क्: संस्कृत्य ॥ 3.99 ॥
verses.english: But let him offer, in accordance with the rule, to a guest who has come (of his own accord) a seat and water, as well as food, garnished (with seasoning), according to his ability.

verses.text:
[९०म] शिलान् अप्य् उञ्छतो नित्यं पञ्चाग्नीन् अपि जुह्वतः
                                    ।
[९०म्च्] सर्वं सुकृतम् आदत्ते ब्राह्मणो ऽनर्चितो वसन् ॥
                                    १०० ॥
verses.english: A Brahmana who stays unhonoured (in the house), takes away (with him) all the spiritual merit even of a man who subsists by gleaning ears of corn, or offers oblations in five fires.

verses.text:
[९१म] तृणानि भूमिर् उदकं वाक् चतुर्थी च सूनृता ।
[९१म्च्] एतान्य् अपि सतां गेहे न-उच्छिद्यन्ते कदा चन ॥
                                    १०१ ॥
verses.english: Grass, room (for resting), water, and fourthly a kind word; these (things) never fail in the houses of good men.

verses.text:
[९२म] एकरात्रं तु निवसन्न् अतिथिर् ब्राह्मणः स्मृतः
                                    ।
[९२म्च्] अनित्यं हि स्थितो यस्मात् तस्माद् अतिथिर् उच्यते ॥
                                    १०२ ॥
verses.english: But a Brahmana who stays one night only is declared to be a guest (atithi); for because he stays (sthita) not long (anityam), he is called atithi (a guest).

verses.text:
[९३म] न-एकग्रामीणम् अतिथिं विप्रं साङ्गतिकं तथा
                                    ।
[९३म्च्] उपस्थितं गृहे विद्याद् भार्या यत्र-अग्नयो ऽपि वा
                                    ॥ १०३ ॥
verses.english: One must not consider as a guest a Brahmana who dwells in the same village, nor one who seeks his livelihood by social intercourse, even though he has come to a house where (there is) a wife, and where sacred fires (are kept).

verses.text:
[९४म] उपासते ये गृहस्थाः परपाकम् अ.बुद्धयः ।
[९४म्च्] तेन ते प्रेत्य पशुतां व्रजन्त्य् अन्नादिदायिनः ॥
                                    १०४ ॥
verses.english: Those foolish householders who constantly seek (to live on) the food of others, become, in consequence of that (baseness), after death the cattle of those who give them food.

verses.text:
[९५म] अ.प्रणोद्यो ऽतिथिः सायं सूर्य.ऊढो गृहमेधिना
                                    ।
[९५म्च्] काले प्राप्तस् त्व् अकाले वा न-अस्य-अन्.अश्नन् गृहे
                                    वसेत् ॥ १०५ ॥
verses.english: A guest who is sent by the (setting) sun in the evening, must not be driven away by a householder; whether he have come at (supper-) time or at an inopportune moment, he must not stay in the house without entertainment.

verses.text:
[९६म] न वै स्वयं तद् अश्नीयाद् अतिथिं यन् न भोजयेत्
