                                    ।
[९६म्च्] धन्यं यशस्यम् आयुष्यं स्वर्ग्यं वा-अतिथिपूजनम्
                                    ॥ १०६ ॥
verses.english: Let him not eat any (dainty) food which he does not offer to his guest; the hospitable reception of guests procures wealth, fame, long life, and heavenly bliss.

verses.text:
[९७म] आसन.आवसथौ शय्याम् अनुव्रज्याम् उपासनाम् ।
[९७म्च्] उत्तमेषु-उत्तमं कुर्याद्द् हीइने हीनं समे समम् ॥
                                    १०७ ॥
verses.english: Let him offer (to his guests) seats, rooms, beds, attendance on departure and honour (while they stay), to the most distinguished in the best form, to the lower ones in a lower form, to equals in an equal manner.

verses.text:
[९८म] वैश्वदेवे तु निर्वृत्ते यद्य् अन्यो ऽतिथिर् आव्रजेत्
                                    ।
[९८म्च्] तस्य-अप्य् अन्नं यथाशक्ति प्रदद्यान् न बलिं
                                    हरेत् ॥ १०८ ॥
verses.english: But if another guest comes after the Vaisvadeva offering has been finished, (the householder) must give him food according to his ability, (but) not repeat the Bali offering.

verses.text:
[९९म] न भोजनार्थं स्वे विप्रः कुल.गोत्रे निवेदयेत्
                                    ।
[९९म्च्] भोजनार्थं हि ते शंसन् वान्ताशी-इत्य् उच्यते
                                    बुधैः ॥ १०९ ॥
verses.english: A Brahmana shall not name his family and (Vedic) gotra in order to obtain a meal; for he who boasts of them for the sake of a meal, is called by the wise a foul feeder (vantasin).

verses.text:
[१००म] न ब्राह्मणस्य त्व् अतिथिर् गृहे राजन्य उच्यते
                                    ।
[१००म्च्] वैश्य.शूद्रौ सखा च-एव ज्ञातयो गुरुर् एव च
                                    ॥ ११० ॥
verses.english: But a Kshatriya (who comes) to the house of a Brahmana is not called a guest (atithi), nor a Vaisya, nor a Sudra, nor a personal friend, nor a relative, nor the teacher.

verses.text:
[१०१म] यदि त्व् अतिथिधर्मेण क्षत्रियो गृहम् आव्रजेत्
                                    ।
[१०१म्च्] भुक्तवत्सु च विप्रेषु कामं तम् अपि भोजयेत् ॥
                                    १११ ॥
verses.english: But if a Kshatriya comes to the house of a Brahmana in the manner of a guest, (the house-holder) may feed him according to his desire, after the above-mentioned Brahmanas have eaten.

verses.text:
[१०२म] वैश्य.शूद्राव् अपि प्राप्तौ कुटुम्बे
                                    ऽतिथि.धर्मिणौ ।
[१०२म्च्] भोजयेत् सह भृत्यैस् ताव् आनृशंस्यं प्रयोजयन्
                                    ॥ ११२ ॥
verses.english: Even a Vaisya and a Sudra who have approached his house in the manner of guests, he may allow to eat with his servants, showing (thereby) his compassionate disposition.

verses.text:
[१०३म] इतरान् अपि सखि.आदीन् सम्प्रीत्या गृहम् आगतान्
                                    ।
[१०३म्च्] प्रकृत्य-अन्नं यथाशक्ति भोजयेत् सह भार्यया
                                    ॥ ११३ ॥
verses.english: Even to others, personal friends and so forth, who have come to his house out of affection, he may give food, garnished (with seasoning) according to his ability, (at the same time) with his wife.

verses.text:
[१०४म] सुवासिनीः कुमारीश् च रोगिणो गर्भिणीः स्त्रियः
                                    ।
[१०४म्च्] अतिथिभ्यो ऽग्र एव-एतान् भोजयेद् अविचारयन् ॥
                                    ११४ ॥ ३.११४च्[१०४म्च्]व्/ म्: अतिथिभ्यो ऽन्वग् एव-एतान् ॥ 3.114 ॥
verses.english: Without hesitation he may give food, even before his guests, to the following persons, (viz.) to newly-married women, to infants, to the sick, and to pregnant women.

verses.text:
[१०५म] अ.दत्त्वा तु य एतेभ्यः पूर्वं भुङ्क्ते
                                    ऽ.विचक्षणः ।
[१०५म्च्] स भुञ्जानो न जानाति श्व.गृध्रैर् जग्धिम्
                                    आत्मनः ॥ ११५ ॥
verses.english: But the foolish man who eats first without having given food to these (persons) does, while he crams, not know that (after death) he himself will be devoured by dogs and vultures.

verses.text:
[१०६म] भुक्तवत्स्व् अथ विप्रेषु स्वेषु भृत्येषु च-एव हि
                                    ।
[१०६म्च्] भुञ्जीयातां ततः पश्चाद् अवशिष्टं तु दम्पती ॥
                                    ११६ ॥
verses.english: After the Brahmanas, the kinsmen, and the servants have dined, the householder and his wife may afterwards eat what remains.

verses.text:
[१०७म] देवान् ऋषीन् मनुष्यांश् च पितॄन् गृह्याश् च देवताः
                                    ।
[१०७म्च्] पूजयित्वा ततः पश्चाद् गृहस्थः शेषभुग् भवेत्
                                    ॥ ११७ ॥
verses.english: Having honoured the gods, the sages, men, the manes, and the guardian deities of the house, the householder shall eat afterwards what remains.

verses.text:
[१०८म] अघं स केवलं भुङ्क्ते यः पचत्य् आत्मकारणात्
                                    ।
[१०८म्च्] यज्ञशिष्टाशनं ह्य् एतत् सताम् अन्नं विधीयते ॥
                                    ११८ ॥
verses.english: He who prepares food for himself (alone), eats nothing but sin; for it is ordained that the food which remains after (the performance of) the sacrifices shall be the meal of virtuous men.

verses.text:
[१०९म] राज.ऋत्विज्.स्नातक.गुरून् प्रिय.श्वशुर.मातुलान्
                                    ।
[१०९म्च्] अर्हयेन् मधुपर्केण परिसंवत्सरात् पुनः ॥ ११९
                                    ॥
verses.english: Let him honour with the honey-mixture a king, an officiating priest, a Snataka, the teacher, a son-in-law, a father-in-law, and a maternal uncle, (if they come) again after a full year (has elapsed since their last visit).

verses.text:
[११०म] राजा च श्रोत्रियश् च-एव यज्ञकर्मण्य् उपस्थितौ
                                    । ३.१२०अ[११०म]व्/ म्: उपस्थिते
[११०म्च्] मधुपर्केण सम्पूज्यौ न त्व् अयज्ञ इति स्थितिः
                                    ॥ १२० ॥
verses.english: A king and a Srotriya, who come on the performance of a sacrifice, must be honoured with the honey-mixture, but not if no sacrifice is being performed; that is a settled rule.

verses.text:
[१११म] सायं त्व् अन्नस्य सिद्धस्य पत्न्य् अ.मन्त्रं बलिं
                                    हरेत् ।
[१११म्च्] वैश्वदेवं हि नाम-एतत् सायं प्रातर् विधीयते
                                    ॥ १२१ ॥
verses.english: But the wife shall offer in the evening (a portion) of the dressed food as a Bali-oblation, without (the recitation of) sacred formulas; for that (rite which is called the) Vaisvadeva is prescribed both for the morning and the evening.

verses.text:
[११२म] पितृयज्ञं तु निर्वर्त्य विप्रश् चन्द्रक्षये ऽग्निमान् ।
                                    ३.१२२अ[११२म]व्/ क्: च-इन्दुक्षये
[११२म्च्] पिण्डान्वाहार्यकं श्राद्धं कुर्यान् मास.अनुमासिकम् ॥
                                १२२ ॥
verses.english: After performing the Pitriyagna, a Brahmana who keeps a sacred fire shall offer, month by month, on the new-moon day, the funeral sacrifice (Sraddha, called) Pindanvaharyaka.

verses.text:
[११३म] पितॄणां मासिकं श्राद्धम् अन्वाहार्यं विदुर् बुधाः
                                ।
[११३म्च्] तच् च-आमिषेणा कर्तव्यं प्रशस्तेन प्रयत्नतः ॥
                                १२३ ॥
verses.english: The wise call the monthly funeral offering to the manes Anvaharya (to be offered after the cakes), and that must be carefully performed with the approved (sorts of) flesh (mentioned below).

verses.text:
[११४म] तत्र ये भोजनीयाः स्युर् ये च वर्ज्या द्विजोत्तमाः
                                ।
[११४म्च्] यावन्तश् च-एव यैश् च-अन्नैस् तान् प्रवक्ष्याम्य्
                                अशेषतः ॥ १२४ ॥
verses.english: I will fully declare what and how many (Brahmanas) must be fed on that (occasion), who must be avoided, and on what kinds of food (they shall dine).

verses.text:
[११५म] द्वौ दैवे पितृकार्ये त्रीन् एकैकम् उभयत्र वा ।
                                        ३.१२५अ[११५म]व्/ म्: पितृकृत्ये
[११५म्च्] भोजयेत् सु.समृद्धो ऽपि न प्रसज्जेत विस्तरे ॥
                                    १२५ ॥ ३.१२५च्[११५म्च्]व्/ म्: न प्रवर्तेत ॥ 3.125 ॥
verses.english: One must feed two (Brahmanas) at the offering to the gods, and three at the offering to the manes, or one only on either occasion; even a very wealthy man shall not be anxious (to entertain) a large company.

verses.text:
[११६म] सत्क्रियां देश.कालौ च शौचं ब्राह्मणसम्पदः
                                    ।
[११६म्च्] पञ्च-एतान् विस्तरो हन्ति तस्मान् न-ईहेत विस्तरम्
                                    ॥ १२६ ॥
verses.english: A large company destroys these five (advantages) the respectful treatment (of the invited, the propriety of) place and time, purity and (the selection of) virtuous Brahmana (guests); he therefore shall not seek (to entertain) a large company.

verses.text:
[११७म] प्रथिता प्रेतकृत्या-एषा पित्र्यं नाम विधुक्षये
                                    ।
[११७म्च्] तस्मिन् युक्तस्य-एति नित्यं प्रेतकृत्या-एव लौकिकी
                                    ॥ १२७ ॥
verses.english: Famed is this rite for the dead, called (the sacrifice sacred to the manes (and performed) on the new-moon day; if a man is diligent in (performing) that, (the reward of) the rite for the dead, which is performed according to Smarta rules, reaches him constantly.

verses.text:
[११८म] श्रोत्रियाय-एव देयानि हव्य.कव्यानि दातृभिः
                                    ।
[११८म्च्] अर्हत्तमाय विप्राय तस्मै दत्तं महाफलम् ॥
                                    १२८ ॥
verses.english: Oblations to the gods and manes must be presented by the givers to a Srotriya alone; what is given to such a most worthy Brahmana yields great reward.

verses.text:
[११९म] एकैकम् अपि विद्वांसं दैवे पित्र्ये च भोजयेत् ।
                                        ३.१२९अ[११९म]व्/ म्: भोजयन्
[११९म्च्] पुष्कलं फलम् आप्नोति न-अमन्त्रज्ञान् बहून् अपि
                                    ॥ १२९ ॥
verses.english: Let him feed even one learned man at (the sacrifice) to the gods, and one at (the sacrifice) to the manes; (thus) he will gain a rich reward, not (if he entertains) many who are unacquainted with the Veda.

verses.text:
[१२०म] दूराद् एव परीक्षेत ब्राह्मणं वेदपारगम् ।
[१२०म्च्] तीर्थं तद्द् हव्य.कव्यानां प्रदाने सो ऽतिथिः
                                    स्मृतः ॥ १३० ॥
verses.english: Let him make inquiries even regarding the remote (ancestors of) a Brahmana who has studied an entire (recension of the) Veda;

verses.text:
[१२१म] सहस्रं हि सहस्राणाम् अन्.ऋचां यत्र भुञ्जते
                                    ।
[१२१म्च्] एकस् तान् मन्त्रवित् प्रीतः सर्वान् अर्हति धर्मतः
                                    ॥ १३१ ॥
verses.english: Though a million of men, unaquainted with the Rikas, were to dine at a (funeral sacrifice), yet a single man, learned in the Veda, who is satisfied (with his entertainment), is worth them all as far as the (production of) spiritual merit (is concerned).

verses.text:
[१२२म] ज्ञान.उत्कृष्टाय देयानि कव्यानि च हवींषि च
                                    ।
[१२२म्च्] न हि हस्ताव् असृग्दिग्धौ रुधिरेण-एव शुध्यतः
                                    ॥ १३२ ॥
verses.english: Food sacred to the manes or to the gods must be given to a man distinguished by sacred knowledge; for hands, smeared with blood, cannot be cleansed with blood.

verses.text:
[१२३म] यावतो ग्रसते ग्रासान् हव्य.कव्येष्व् अ.मन्त्रवित्
                                    ।
[१२३म्च्] तावतो ग्रसते प्रेतो दीप्तशूल.ऋष्टि.अयोगुडान् ॥
                                    १३३ ॥
verses.english: As many mouthfuls as an ignorant man swallows at a sacrifice to the gods or to the manes, so many red-hot spikes, spears, and iron balls must (the giver of the repast) swallow after death.

verses.text:
[१२४म] ज्ञाननिष्ठा द्विजाः के चित् तपोनिष्ठास् तथा-अपरे
                                    ।
[१२४म्च्] तपः.स्वाध्यायनिष्ठाश् च कर्मनिष्ठास्
                                    तथा-अपरे ॥ १३४ ॥
verses.english: Some Brahmanas are devoted to (the pursuit of) knowledge, and others to (the performance of) austerities; some to austerities and to the recitation of the Veda, and others to (the performance of) sacred rites.

verses.text:
[१२५म] ज्ञाननिष्ठेषु कव्यानि प्रतिष्ठाप्यानि यत्नतः
                                    ।
[१२५म्च्] हव्यानि तु यथान्यायं सर्वेष्व् एव चतुर्ष्व् अपि ॥
                                    १३५ ॥
verses.english: Oblations to the manes ought to be carefully presented to those devoted to knowledge, but offerings to the gods, in accordance with the reason (of the sacred law), to (men of) all the four (above-mentioned classes).

verses.text:
[१२६म] अश्रोत्रियः पिता यस्य पुत्रः स्याद् वेदपारगः
                                    ।
[१२६म्च्] अश्रोत्रियो वा पुत्रः स्यात् पिता स्याद् वेदपारगः ॥
                                    १३६ ॥
verses.english: If there is a father ignorant of the sacred texts whose son has learned one whole recension of the Veda and the Angas, and a son ignorant of the sacred texts whose father knows an entire recension of the Veda and the Angas,

verses.text:
[१२७म] ज्यायांसम् अनयोर् विद्याद् यस्य स्यात्-श्रोत्रियः पिता
                                    ।
[१२७म्च्] मन्त्रसम्पूजनार्थं तु सत्कारम् इतरो ऽर्हति ॥
                                    १३७ ॥
verses.english: Know that he whose father knows the Veda, is the more venerable one (of the two); yet the other one is worthy of honour, because respect is due to the Veda (which he has learned).

verses.text:
[१२८म] न श्राद्धे भोजयेन् मित्रं धनैः कार्यो ऽस्य
                                    सङ्ग्रहः ।
[१२८म्च्] नारिं न मित्रं यं विद्यात् तं श्राद्धे भोजयेद्
                                    द्विजम् ॥ १३८ ॥
verses.english: Let him not entertain a personal friend at a funeral sacrifice; he may gain his affection by (other) valuable gifts; let him feed at a Sraddha a Brahmana whom he considers neither as a foe nor as a friend.

verses.text:
[१२९म] यस्य मित्र.प्रधानानि श्राद्धानि च हवींषि च
                                    ।
[१२९म्च्] तस्य प्रेत्य फलं न-अस्ति श्राद्धेषु च हविःषु
                                    च ॥ १३९ ॥
verses.english: He who performs funeral sacrifices and offerings to the gods chiefly for the sake of (gaining) friends, reaps after death no reward for Sraddhas and sacrifices.

verses.text:
[१३०म] यः सङ्गतानि कुरुते मोहात्-श्राद्धेन मानवः
                                    ।
[१३०म्च्] स स्वर्गाच् च्यवते लोकात्-श्राद्ध.मित्रो
                                    द्विजाधमः ॥ १४० ॥
verses.english: That meanest among twice-born men who in his folly contracts friendships through a funeral sacrifice, loses heaven, because he performed a Sraddha for the sake of friendship.

verses.text:
[१३१म] सम्भोजानि सा-अभिहिता पैशाची दक्षिणा द्विजैः
                                    ।
[१३१म्च्] इह-एव-आस्ते तु सा लोके गौर् अन्धा-इव-एकवेश्मनि
                                    ॥ १४१ ॥
verses.english: A gift (of food) by twice-born men, consumed with (friends and relatives), is said to be offered to the Pisakas; it remains in this (world) alone like a blind cow in one stable.

verses.text:
[१३२म] यथा-इरिणे बीजम् उप्त्वा न वप्ता लभते फलम्
                                    ।
[१३२म्च्] तथा-अन्.ऋचे हविर् दत्त्वा न दाता लभते फलम्
                                    ॥ १४२ ॥
verses.english: As a husbandman reaps no harvest when he has sown the seed in barren soil, even so the giver of sacrificial food gains no reward if he presented it to a man unacquainted with the Rikas.

verses.text:
[१३३म] दातॄन् प्रतिग्रहीतॄंश् च कुरुते फलभागिनः
                                    ।
[१३३म्च्] विदुषे दक्षिणां दत्त्वा विधिवत् प्रेत्य च-इह च
                                    ॥ १४३ ॥
verses.english: But a present made in accordance with the rules to a learned man, makes the giver and the recipient partakers of rewards both in this (life) and after death.

verses.text:
[१३४म] कामं श्राद्धे ऽर्चयेन् मित्रं न-अभिरूपम् अपि त्व्
                                    अरिम् ।
[१३४म्च्] द्विषता हि हविर् भुक्तं भवति प्रेत्य
                                    निष्.फलम् ॥ १४४ ॥
verses.english: (If no learned Brahmana be at hand), he may rather honour a (virtuous) friend than an enemy, though the latter may be qualified (by learning and so forth); for sacrificial food, eaten by a foe, bears no reward after death.

verses.text:
[१३५म] यत्नेन भोजयेत्-श्राद्धे बह्वृचं वेदपारगम्
                                    ।
[१३५म्च्] शाखान्तगम् अथ-अध्वर्युं छन्दोगं तु
                                    समाप्तिकम् ॥ १४५ ॥
verses.english: Let him (take) pains (to) feed at a Sraddha an adherent of the Rig-veda who has studied one entire (recension of that) Veda, or a follower of the Yagur-veda who has finished one Sakha, or a singer of Samans who (likewise) has completed (the study of an entire recension).

verses.text:
[१३६म] एषाम् अन्यतमो यस्य भुञ्जीत श्राद्धम् अर्चितः
                                    ।
[१३६म्च्] पितॄणां तस्य तृप्तिः स्यात्-शाश्वती साप्तपौरुषी ॥
                                    १४६ ॥
verses.english: If one of these three dines, duly honoured, at a funeral sacrifice, the ancestors of him (who gives the feast), as far as the seventh person, will be satisfied for a very long time.

verses.text:
[१३७म] एष वै प्रथमः कल्पः प्रदाने हव्य.कव्ययोः
                                    ।
[१३७म्च्] अनुकल्पस् त्व् अयं ज्ञेयः सदा सद्भिर् अनुष्ठितः
                                    ॥ १४७ ॥
verses.english: This is the chief rule (to be followed) in offering sacrifices to the gods and manes; know that the virtuous always observe the following subsidiary rule.

verses.text:
[१३८म] मातामहं मातुलं च स्वस्रीयं श्वशुरं गुरुम्
                                    ।
[१३८म्च्] दौहित्रं विट्पतिं बन्धुम् ऋत्विग् याज्यौ च
                                    भोजयेत् ॥ १४८ ॥
verses.english: One may also entertain (on such occasions) one's maternal grandfather, a maternal uncle, a sister's son, a father-in-law, one's teacher, a daughter's son, a daughter's husband, a cognate kinsman, one's own officiating priest or a man for whom one offers sacrifices.

verses.text:
[१३९म] न ब्राह्मणं परीक्षेत दैवे कर्मणि धर्मवित्
                                    ।
[१३९म्च्] पित्र्ये कर्मणि तु प्राप्ते परीक्षेत प्रयत्नतः ॥
                                    १४९ ॥
verses.english: For a rite sacred to the gods, he who knows the law will not make (too close) inquiries regarding an (invited) Brahmana; but when one performs a ceremony in honour of the manes, one must carefully examine (the qualities and parentage of the guest).

verses.text:
[१४०म] ये स्तेन.पतित.क्लीबा ये च नास्तिकवृत्तयः ।
[१४०म्च्] तान् हव्य.कव्ययोर् विप्रान् अनर्हान् मनुर् अब्रवीत्
                                    ॥ १५० ॥
verses.english: Manu has declared that those Brahmanas who are thieves, outcasts, eunuchs, or atheists are unworthy (to partake) of oblations to the gods and manes.

verses.text:
[१४१म] जटिलं च-अनधीयानं दुर्बालं कितवं तथा
                                    ।
[१४१म्च्] याजयन्ति च ये पूगांस् तांश् च श्राद्धे न
                                    भोजयेत् ॥ १५१ ॥
verses.english: Let him not entertain at a Sraddha one who wears his hair in braids (a student), one who has not studied (the Veda), one afflicted with a skin-disease, a gambler, nor those who sacrifice for a multitude (of sacrificers).

verses.text:
[१४२म] चिकित्सकान् देवलकान् मांसविक्रयिणस् तथा ।
                                        ३.१५२अ[१४२म]व्/ म्: चिकित्सकादेवलकामांसविक्रयिणस्
                                        तथा
[१४२म्च्] विपणेन च जीवन्तो वर्ज्याः स्युर् हव्य.कव्ययोः
                                    ॥ १५२ ॥
verses.english: Physicians, temple-priests, sellers of meat, and those who subsist by shop-keeping must be avoided at sacrifices offered to the gods and to the manes.

verses.text:
[१४३म] प्रेष्यो ग्रामस्य राज्ञश् च कुनखी श्यावदन्तकः
                                    ।
[१४३म्च्] प्रतिरोद्धा गुरोश् च-एव त्यक्त.अग्निर् वार्धुषिस्
                                    तथा ॥ १५३ ॥
verses.english: A paid servant of a village or of a king, man with deformed nails or black teeth, one who opposes his teacher, one who has forsaken the sacred fire, and a usurer;

verses.text:
[१४४म] यक्ष्मी च पशुपालश् च परिवेत्ता निराकृतिः ।
[१४४म्च्] ब्रह्मद्विष्-परिवित्तिश् च गणाभ्यन्तर एव च ॥
                                    १५४ ॥
verses.english: One suffering from consumption, one who subsists by tending cattle, a younger brother who marries or kindles the sacred fire before the elder, one who neglects the five great sacrifices, an enemy of the Brahmana race, an elder brother who marries or kindles the sacred fire after the younger, and one who belongs to a company or corporation,

verses.text:
[१४५म] कुशीलवो ऽवकीर्णी च वृषलीपतिर् एव च ।
[१४५म्च्] पौनर्भवश् च काणश् च यस्य च-उपपतिर् गृहे
                                    ॥ १५५ ॥
verses.english: An actor or singer, one who has broken the vow of studentship, one whose (only or first) wife is a Sudra female, the son of a remarried woman, a one-eyed man, and he in whose house a paramour of his wife (resides);

verses.text:
[१४६म] भृतकाध्यापको यश् च भृतकाध्यापितस् तथा
                                    ।
[१४६म्च्] शूद्र.शिष्यो गुरुश् च-एव वाग्दुष्टः कुण्ड.गोलकौ
                                    ॥ १५६ ॥
verses.english: He who teaches for a stipulated fee and he who is taught on that condition, he who instructs Sudra pupils and he whose teacher is a Sudra, he who speaks rudely, the son of an adulteress, and the son of a widow,

verses.text:
[१४७म] अकारणे परित्यक्ता माता.पित्रोर् गुरोस् तथा ।
                                        ३.१५७अ[१४७म]व्/ क्: अकारणपरित्यक्ता
[१४७म्च्] ब्राह्मैर् यौनैश् च सम्बन्धैः संयोगं पतितैर्
                                    गतः ॥ १५७ ॥
verses.english: He who forsakes his mother, his father, or a teacher without a (sufficient) reason, he who has contracted an alliance with outcasts either through the Veda or through a marriage,

verses.text:
[१४८म] अगारदाही गरदः कुण्डाशी सोमविक्रयी ।
[१४८म्च्] समुद्रयायी बन्दी च तैलिकः कूटकारकः ॥ १५८
                                    ॥
verses.english: An incendiary, a prisoner, he who eats the food given by the son of an adulteress, a seller of Soma, he who undertakes voyages by sea, a bard, an oil-man, a suborner to perjury,

verses.text:
[१४९म] पित्रा विवदमानश् च कितवो मद्यपस् तथा ।
[१४९म्च्] पापरोग्य् अभिशस्तश् च दाम्भिको रसविक्रयी ॥
                                    १५९ ॥
verses.english: He who wrangles or goes to law with his father, the keeper of a gambling-house, a drunkard, he who is afflicted with a disease (in punishment of former) crimes, he who is accused of a mortal sin, a hypocrite, a seller of substances used for flavouring food,

verses.text:
[१५०म] धनुः.शराणां कर्ता च यश् च-अग्रेदिधिषूपतिः
                                    ।
[१५०म्च्] मित्रध्रुग् द्यूत.वृत्तिश् च पुत्र.आचार्यस्
                                    तथा-एव च ॥ १६० ॥
verses.english: A maker of bows and of arrows, he who lasciviously dallies with a brother's widow, the betrayer of a friend, one who subsists by gambling, he who learns (the Veda) from his son,

verses.text:
[१५१म] भ्रामरी गन्डमाली च श्वित्र्य् अथो पिशुनस् तथा
                                    ।
[१५१म्च्] उन्मत्तो ऽन्धश् च वर्ज्याः स्युर् वेदनिन्दक एव च
                                    ॥ १६१ ॥
verses.english: An epileptic man, who suffers from scrofulous swellings of the glands, one afflicted with white leprosy, an informer, a madman, a blind man, and he who cavils at the Veda must (all) be avoided.

verses.text:
[१५२म] हस्ति.गो.ऽश्व.उष्ट्रदमको नक्षत्रैर् यश् च
                                    जीवति ।
[१५२म्च्] पक्षिणां पोषको यश् च युद्धाचार्यस् तथा-एव च
                                    ॥ १६२ ॥
verses.english: A trainer of elephants, oxen, horses, or camels, he who subsists by astrology, a bird-fancier, and he who teaches the use of arms,

verses.text:
[१५३म] स्रोतसां भेदको यश् च तेषां च-आवरणे रतः
                                    ।
[१५३म्च्] गृहसंवेशको दूतो वृक्षारोपक एव च ॥ १६३
                                    ॥
verses.english: He who diverts water-courses, and he who delights in obstructing them, an architect, a messenger, and he who plants trees (for money),

verses.text:
[१५४म] श्वक्रीडी श्येनजीवी च कन्यादूषक एव च ।
[१५४म्च्] हिंस्रो वृषल.वृत्तिश् च गणानां च-एव याजकः ॥
                                    १६४ ॥
verses.english: A breeder of sporting-dogs, a falconer, one who defiles maidens, he who delights in injuring living creatures, he who gains his subsistence from Sudras, and he who offers sacrifices to the Ganas,

verses.text:
[१५५म] आचार.हीनः क्लीबश् च नित्यं याचनकस् तथा
                                    ।
[१५५म्च्] कृषिजीवी श्लीपदी च सद्भिर् निन्दित एव च ॥ १६५
                                    ॥
verses.english: He who does not follow the rule of conduct, a (man destitute of energy like a) eunuch, one who constantly asks (for favours), he who lives by agriculture, a club-footed man, and he who is censured by virtuous men,

verses.text:
[१५६म] औरभ्रिको माहिषिकः परपूर्वापतिस् तथा ।
[१५६म्च्] प्रेतनिर्यापकश् च-एव वर्जनीयाः प्रयत्नतः ॥
                                    १६६ ॥
verses.english: A shepherd, a keeper of buffaloes, the husband of a remarried woman, and a carrier of dead bodies, (all these) must be carefully avoided.

verses.text:
[१५७म] एतान् विगर्हित.आचारान् अपाङ्क्तेयान् द्विजाधमान्
                                    ।
[१५७म्च्] द्विजातिप्रवरो विद्वान् उभयत्र विवर्जयेत् ॥ १६७
                                    ॥
verses.english: A Brahmana who knows (the sacred law) should shun at (sacrifices) both (to the gods and to the manes) these lowest of twice-born men, whose conduct is reprehensible, and who are unworthy (to sit) in the company (at a repast).

verses.text:
[१५८म] ब्राह्मणो त्व् अन्.अधीयानस् तृणाग्निर् इव शाम्यति ।
                                        ३.१६८अ[१५८म]व्/ म्: ब्राह्मणस् ह्य् अन्.अधीयानस्
[१५८म्च्] तस्मै हव्यं न दातव्यं न हि भस्मनि हूयते
                                    ॥ १६८ ॥
verses.english: As a fire of dry grass is (unable to consume the offerings and is quickly) extinguished, even so (is it with) an unlearned Brahmana; sacrificial food must not be given to him, since it (would be) offered in ashes.

verses.text:
[१५९म] अपाङ्क्तदाने यो दातुर् भवत्य् ऊर्ध्वं फल.उदयः
                                    । ३.१६९अ[१५९म]व्/ म्: अपङ्क्त्यदाने
[१५९म्च्] दैवे हविषि पित्र्ये वा तं प्रवक्स्याम्य् अशेषतः
                                    ॥ १६९ ॥ ३.१६९च्[१५९म्च्]व्/ म्: दैवे कर्मणि ॥ 3.169 ॥
verses.english: I will fully declare what result the giver obtains after death, if he gives food, destined for the gods or manes, to a man who is unworthy to sit in the company.

verses.text:
[१६०म] अ.व्रतैर् यद् द्विजैर् भुक्तं परिवेतृ.आदिभिस्
                                    तथा ।
[१६०म्च्] अपाङ्क्तेयैर् यद् अन्यैश् च तद् वै रक्षांसि
                                    भुञ्जते ॥ १७० ॥
verses.english: The Rakshasas, indeed, consume (the food) eaten by Brahmanas who have not fulfilled the vow of studentship, by a Parivettri and so forth, and by other men not admissible into the company.

verses.text:
[१६१म] दाराग्निहोत्रसंयोगं कुरुते यो ऽग्रजे स्थिते
                                    ।
[१६१म्च्] परिवेत्ता स विज्ञेयः परिवित्तिस् तु पूर्वजः ॥
                                    १७१ ॥
verses.english: He must be considered as a Parivettri who marries or begins the performance of the Agnihotra before his elder brother, but the latter as a Parivitti.

verses.text:
[१६२म] परिवित्तिः परिवेत्ता यया च परिविद्यते ।
[१६२म्च्] सर्वे ते नरकं यान्ति दातृयाजक.पञ्चमाः ॥ १७२
                                    ॥
verses.english: The elder brother who marries after the younger, the younger brother who marries before the elder, the female with whom such a marriage is contracted, he who gives her away, and the sacrificing priest, as the fifth, all fall into hell.

verses.text:
[१६३म] भ्रातुर् मृतस्य भार्यायां यो ऽनुरज्येत कामतः
                                    ।
[१६३म्च्] धर्मेण-अपि नियुक्तायां स ज्ञेयो दिधिषूपतिः ॥
                                    १७३ ॥
verses.english: He who lasciviously dallies with the widow of a deceased brother, though she be appointed (to bear a child by him) in accordance with the sacred law, must be known to be a Didhishupati.

verses.text:
[१६४म] परदारेषु जायेते द्वौ सुतौ कुण्ड.गोलकौ ।
[१६४म्च्] पत्यौ जीवति कुण्डः स्यान् मृते भर्तरि गोलकः
                                    ॥ १७४ ॥
verses.english: Two (kinds of) sons, a Kunda and a Golaka, are born by wives of other men; (he who is born) while the husband lives, will be a Kunda, and (he who is begotten) after the husband's death, a Golaka.

verses.text:
[१६५म] तौ तु जातौ परक्षेत्रे प्राणिनौ प्रेत्य च-इह च
                                    । ३.१७५अ[१६५म]व्/ म्: ते तु जाताः परक्षेत्रे
                                    प्राणिनः
[१६५म्च्] दत्तानि हव्य.कव्यानि नाशयन्ति प्रदायिनाम् ॥ १७५
                                    ॥
verses.english: But those two creatures, who are born of wives of other men, cause to the giver the loss (of the rewards), both in this life and after death, for the food sacred to gods or manes which has been given (to them).

verses.text:
[१६६म] अपाङ्क्त्यो यावतः पङ्क्त्यान् भुञ्जानान् अनुपश्यति ।
                                        ३.१७६अ[१६६म]व्/ म्: अ.पङ्क्त्यो यावतः
[१६६म्च्] तावतां न फलं तत्र दाता प्राप्नोति बालिशः ॥
                                    १७६ ॥
verses.english: The foolish giver (of a funeral repast) does not reap the reward for as many worthy guests as a man, inadmissible into company, can look on while they are feeding.

verses.text:
[१६७म] वीक्ष्य-अन्धो नवतेः काणः षष्टेः श्वित्री शतस्य
                                    तु । ३.१७७अ[१६७म]व्/ म्: शतस्य च
[१६७म्च्] पापरोगी सहस्रस्य दातुर् नाशयते फलम् ॥ १७७
                                    ॥
verses.english: A blind man by his presence causes to the giver (of the feast) the loss of the reward for ninety (guests), a one-eyed man for sixty, one who suffers from white leprosy for a hundred, and one punished by a (terrible) disease for a thousand.

verses.text:
[१६८म] यावतः संस्पृशेद् अङ्गैर् ब्राह्मणान्-शूद्रयाजकः
                                    ।
[१६८म्च्] तावतां न भवेद् दातुः फलं दानस्य पौर्तिकम्
                                    ॥ १७८ ॥
verses.english: The giver (of a Sraddha) loses the reward, due for such a non-sacrificial gift, for as many Brahmanas as a (guest) who sacrifices for Sudras may touch (during the meal) with his limbs.

verses.text:
[१६९म] वेदविद्-च-अपि विप्रो ऽस्य लोभात् कृत्वा
                                    प्रतिग्रहम् ।
[१६९म्च्] विनाशं व्रजति क्षिप्रम् आमपात्रम् इव-अम्भसि ॥
                                    १७९ ॥
verses.english: And if a Brahmana, though learned in the Veda, accepts through covetousness a gift from such (a man), he will quickly perish, like a vessel of unburnt clay in water.

verses.text:
[१७०म] सोमविक्रयिणे विष्ठा भिषजे पूय.शोणितम् ।
[१७०म्च्] नष्टं देवलके दत्तम् अ.प्रतिष्ठं तु वार्धुषौ
                                    ॥ १८० ॥

[१७१म] यत् तु वाणिजके दत्तं न-इह न-अमुत्र तद्
                                    भवेत् ।
[१७१म्च्] भस्मनि-इव हुतं द्रव्यं तथा पौनर्भवे
                                    द्विजे ॥ १८१ ॥
verses.english: What has been given to a Brahmana who lives by trade that is not (useful) in this world and the next, and (a present) to a Brahmana born of a remarried woman (resembles) an oblation thrown into ashes.

verses.text:
[१७२म] इतरेषु त्व् अपाङ्क्त्येषु यथा.उद्दिष्टेष्व् अ.साधुषु
                                    ।
[१७२म्च्] मेदो.ऽसृङ्.मांस.मज्जा.अस्थि वदन्त्य् अन्नं
                                    मनीषिणः ॥ १८२ ॥
verses.english: But the wise declare that the food which (is offered) to other unholy, inadmissible men, enumerated above, (is turned into) adipose secretions, blood, flesh, marrow, and bone.

verses.text:
[१७३म] अपाङ्क्त्य.उपहता पङ्क्तिः पाव्यते यैर्
                                    द्विजोत्तमैः । ३.१८३अ[१७३म]व्/ म्: अ.पङ्क्त्य.उपहता
                                        पङ्क्तिः
[१७३म्च्] तान् निबोधत कार्त्स्न्येन द्विजाग्र्यान् पङ्क्तिपावनान्
                                    ॥ १८३ ॥
verses.english: Now hear by what chief of twice-born men a company defiled by (the presence of) unworthy (guests) is purified, and the full (description of) the Brahmanas who sanctify a company.

verses.text:
[१७४म] अग्र्याः सर्वेषु वेदेषु सर्वप्रवचनेषु च ।
[१७४म्च्] श्रोत्रियान्वयजाश् च-एव विज्ञेयाः पङ्क्तिपावनाः ॥
                                    १८४ ॥
verses.english: Those men must be considered as the sanctifiers of a company who are most learned in all the Vedas and in all the Angas, and who are the descendants of Srotriyas.

verses.text:
[१७५म] त्रिणाचिकेतः पञ्च.अग्निस् त्रिसुपर्णः षडङ्गवित्
                                    ।
[१७५म्च्] ब्रह्मदेयात्मसन्तानो ज्येष्ठसामग एव च ॥ १८५
                                    ॥ ३.१८५च्[१७५म्च्]व्/ म्: ब्रह्मदेयानुसन्तानो ॥ 3.185 ॥
verses.english: A Trinakiketa, one who keeps five sacred fires, a Trisuparna, one who is versed in the six Angas, the son of a woman married according to the Brahma rite, one who sings the Gyeshthasaman,

verses.text:
[१७६म] वेदार्थ.वित् प्रवक्ता च ब्रह्मचारी सहस्रदः
                                    ।
[१७६म्च्] शतायुश् च-एव विज्ञेया ब्राह्मणाः पङ्क्तिपावनाः ॥
                                    १८६ ॥
verses.english: One who knows the meaning of the Veda, and he who expounds it, a student, one who has given a thousand (cows), and a centenarian must be considered as Brahmanas who sanctify a company.

verses.text:
[१७७म] पूर्वेद्युर् अपरेद्युर् वा श्राद्धकर्मण्य् उपस्थिते
                                    ।
[१७७म्च्] निमन्त्रयेत त्र्य्.अवरान् सम्यग् विप्रान्
                                    यथा.उदितान् ॥ १८७ ॥ ३.१८७च्[१७७म्च्]व्/ म्: निमन्त्रयीत ॥ 3.187 ॥
verses.english: On the day before the Sraddha-rite is performed, or on the day when it takes place, let him invite with due respect at least three Brahmanas, such as have been mentioned above.

verses.text:
[१७८म] निमन्त्रितो द्विजः पित्र्ये नियतात्मा भवेत् सदा
                                    ।
[१७८म्च्] न च छन्दांस्य् अधीयीत यस्य श्राद्धं च तद्
                                    भवेत् ॥ १८८ ॥
verses.english: A Brahmana who has been invited to a (rite) in honour of the manes shall always control himself and not recite the Veda, and he who performs the Sraddha (must act in the same manner).

verses.text:
[१७९म] निमन्त्रितान् हि पितर उपतिष्ठन्ति तान् द्विजान्
                                    ।
[१७९म्च्] वायुवत्-च-अनुगच्छन्ति तथा-आसीनान् उपासते ॥
                                    १८९ ॥
verses.english: For the manes attend the invited Brahmanas, follow them (when they walk) like the wind, and sit near them when they are seated.

verses.text:
[१८०म] केतितस् तु यथान्यायं हव्ये कव्ये द्विजोत्तमः
                                    ।
[१८०म्च्] कथं चिद् अप्य् अतिक्रामन् पापः सूकरतां व्रजेत्
                                    ॥ १९० ॥
verses.english: But a Brahmana who, being duly invited to a rite in honour of the gods or of the manes, in any way breaks (the appointment), becomes guilty (of a crime), and (in his next birth) a hog.

verses.text:
[१८१म] आमन्त्रितस् तु यः श्राद्धे वृशल्या सह मोदते
                                    ।
[१८१म्च्] दातुर् यद् दुष्कृतं किं चित् तत् सर्वं
                                    प्रतिपद्यते ॥ १९१ ॥
verses.english: But he who, being invited to a Sraddha, dallies with a Sudra woman, takes upon himself all the sins which the giver (of the feast) committed.

verses.text:
[१८२म] अ.क्रोधनाः शौच.पराः सततं ब्रह्मचारिणः
                                    ।
[१८२म्च्] न्यस्त.शस्त्रा महा.भागाः पितरः पूर्वदेवताः ॥
                                    १९२ ॥
verses.english: The manes are primeval deities, free from anger, careful of purity, ever chaste, averse from strife, and endowed with great virtues.

verses.text:
[१८३म] यस्माद् उत्पत्तिर् एतेषां सर्वेषाम् अप्य् अशेषतः
                                    ।
[१८३म्च्] ये च यैर् उपचर्याः स्युर् नियमैस् तान् निबोधत
                                    ॥ १९३ ॥
verses.english: Now learn fully from whom all these (manes derive) their origin, and with what ceremonies they ought to be worshipped.

verses.text:
[१८४म] मनोर् हैरण्यगर्भस्य ये मरीचि.आदयः सुताः
                                    ।
[१८४म्च्] तेषाम् ऋषीणां सर्वेषां पुत्राः पितृगणाः स्मृताः ॥
                                    १९४ ॥
verses.english: The (various) classes of the manes are declared to be the sons of all those sages, Mariki and the rest, who are children of Manu, the son of Hiranyagarbha.

verses.text:
[१८५म] विराज्.सुताः सोमसदः साध्यानां पितरः स्मृताः
                                    ।
[१८५म्च्] अग्निष्वात्ताश् च देवानां मारीचा लोकविश्रुताः ॥ १९५
                                    ॥
verses.english: The Somasads, the sons of Virag, are stated to be the manes of the Sadhyas, and the Agnishvattas, the children of Mariki, are famous in the world (as the manes) of the gods.

verses.text:
[१८६म] दैत्य.दानव.यक्षाणां गन्धर्व.उरग.रक्षसाम्
                                    ।
[१८६म्च्] सुपर्ण.किन्नराणां च स्मृता बर्हिषदो ऽत्रिजाः ॥
                                    १९६ ॥
verses.english: The Barhishads, born of Atri, are recorded to be (the manes) of the Daityas, Danavas, Yakshas, Gandharvas, Snake-deities,

verses.text:
[१८७म] सोमपा नाम विप्राणां क्षत्रियाणां हविर्भुजः
                                    ।
[१८७म्च्] वैश्यानाम् आज्यपा नाम शूद्राणां तु सुकालिनः ॥
                                    १९७ ॥
verses.english: The Somapas those of the Brahmanas, the Havirbhugs those of the Kshatriyas, the Agyapas those of the Vaisyas, but the Sukalins those of the Sudras.

verses.text:
[१८८म] सोमपास् तु कवेः पुत्रा हविष्मन्तो ऽङ्गिरःसुताः
                                    ।
[१८८म्च्] पुलस्त्यस्य-आज्यपाः पुत्रा वसिष्ठस्य सुकालिनः
                                    ॥ १९८ ॥
verses.english: The Somapas are the sons of Kavi (Bhrigu), the Havishmats the children of Angiras, the Agyapas the offspring of Pulastya, but the Sukalins (the issue) of Vasishtha.

verses.text:
[१८९म] अग्निदग्ध.अनग्निदग्धान् काव्यान् बर्हिषदस् तथा
                                    । ३.१९९अ[१८९म]व्/ म्: अन्.अग्निदग्ध.अन्.अग्निदग्धान्
[१८९म्च्] अग्निष्वात्तांश् च सौम्यांश् च विप्राणाम् एव निर्दिशेत्
                                    ॥ १९९ ॥
verses.english: One should know that (other classes), the Agnidagdhas, the Anagnidagdhas, the Kavyas, the Barhishads, the Agnishvattas, and the Saumyas, are (the manes) of the Brahmanas alone.

verses.text:
[१९०म] य एते तु गणा मुख्याः पितॄणां परिकीर्तिताः ।
[१९०म्च्] तेषाम् अपि-इह विज्ञेयं पुत्र.पौत्रम् अन्.अन्तकम्
                                    ॥ २०० ॥
verses.english: But know also that there exist in this (world) countless sons and grandsons of those chief classes of manes which have been enumerated.

verses.text:
[१९१म] ऋषिभ्यः पितरो जाताः पितृभ्यो देव.मानवाः ।
[१९१म्च्] देवेभ्यस् तु जगत् सर्वं चरं स्थाण्व्
                                    अनुपूर्वशः ॥ २०१ ॥
verses.english: From the sages sprang the manes, from the manes the gods and the Danavas, but from the gods the whole world, both the movable and the immovable in due order.

verses.text:
[१९२म] राजतैर् भाजनैर् एषाम् अथो वा रजतान्वितैः
                                    ।
[१९२म्च्] वार्य् अपि श्रद्धया दत्तम् अक्षयाय-उपकल्पते ॥
                                    २०२ ॥
verses.english: Even water offered with faith (to the manes) in vessels made of silver or adorned with silver, produces endless (bliss).

verses.text:
[१९३म] दैवकार्याद् द्विजातीनां पितृकार्यं विशिष्यते ।
[१९३म्च्] दैवं हि पितृकार्यस्य पूर्वम् आप्यायनं स्मृतम् ॥
                                    २०३ ॥
verses.english: For twice-born men the rite in honour of the manes is more important than the rite in honour of the gods; for the offering to the gods which precedes (the Sraddhas), has been declared to be a means of fortifying (the latter).

verses.text:
[१९४म] तेषाम् आरक्षभूतं तु पूर्वं दैवं नियोजयेत्
                                    ।
[१९४म्च्] रक्सांसि विप्रलुम्पन्ति श्राद्धम् आरक्षवर्जितम् ॥
                                    २०४ ॥
verses.english: Let him first invite a (Brahmana) in honour of the gods as a protection for the (offering to the manes); for the Rakshasas destroy a funeral sacrifice which is left without such a protection.

verses.text:
[१९५म] दैव.आद्यन्तं तद् ईहेत पितृ.आद्यन्तं न तद्
                                    भवेत् ।
[१९५म्च्] पितृ.आद्यन्तं त्व् ईहमानः क्षिप्रं नश्यति
                                    स.अन्वयः ॥ २०५ ॥
verses.english: Let him make (the Sraddha) begin and end with (a rite) in honour of the gods; it shall not begin and end with a (rite) to the manes; for he who makes it begin and end with a (rite) in honour of the manes, soon perishes together with his progeny.

verses.text:
[१९६म] शुचिं देशं विविक्तं च गोमयेन-उपलेपयेत् ।
[१९६म्च्] दक्षिना.प्रवणं च-एव प्रयत्नेन-उपपादयेत् ॥
                                    २०६ ॥
verses.english: Let him smear a pure and secluded place with cowdung, and carefully make it sloping towards the south.

verses.text:
[१९७म] अवकाशेषु चोक्षेषु जलतीरेषु च-एव हि ।
[१९७म्च्] विविक्तेषु च तुष्यन्ति दत्तेन पितरः सदा ॥ २०७
                                    ॥
verses.english: The manes are always pleased with offerings made in open, naturally pure places, on the banks of rivers, and in secluded spots.

verses.text:
[१९८म] आसनेषु-उपकॢप्तेषु बर्हिष्मत्सु पृथक्.पृथक्
                                    ।
[१९८म्च्] उपस्पृष्ट.उदकान् सम्यग् विप्रांस् तान् उपवेशयेत् ॥
                                    २०८ ॥
verses.english: The (sacrificer) shall make the (invited) Brahmanas, who have duly performed their ablutions, sit down on separate, prepared seats, on which blades of Kusa grass have been placed.

verses.text:
[१९९म] उपवेश्य तु तान् विप्रान् आसनेष्व् अजुगुप्सितान् ।
[१९९म्च्] गन्ध.माल्यैः सुरभिभिर् अर्चयेद् दैवपूर्वकम्
                                    ॥ २०९ ॥
verses.english: Having placed those blameless Brahmanas on their seats, he shall honour them with fragrant garlands and perfumes, beginning with (those who are invited in honour of) the gods.

verses.text:
[२००म] तेषाम् उदकम् आनीय स.पवित्रांस् तिलान् अपि ।
[२००म्च्] अग्नौ कुर्याद् अनुज्ञातो ब्राह्मणो ब्राह्मणैः सह ॥
                                    २१० ॥
verses.english: Having presented to them water, sesamum grains, and blades of Kusa grass, the Brahmana (sacrificer) shall offer (oblations) in the sacred fire, after having received permission (to do so) from (all) the Brahmana (guests) conjointly.

verses.text:
[२०१म] अग्नेः सोम.यमाभ्यां च कृत्वा-आप्यायनम् आदितः
                                    ।
[२०१म्च्] हविर्दानेन विधिवत् पश्चात् सन्तर्पयेत् पितॄन् ॥
                                    २११ ॥
verses.english: Having first, according to the rule, performed, as a means of protecting (the Sraddha), oblations to Agni, to Soma, and to Yama, let him afterwards satisfy the manes by a gift of sacrificial food.

verses.text:
[२०२म] अग्नि.अभावे तु विप्रस्य पाणाव् एव-उपपादयेत्
                                    ।
[२०२म्च्] यो ह्य् अग्निः स द्विजो विप्रैर् मन्त्रदर्शिभिर्
                                    उच्यते ॥ २१२ ॥
verses.english: But if no (sacred) fire (is available), he shall place (the offerings) into the hand of a Brahmana; for Brahmanas who know the sacred texts declare, 'What fire is, even such is a Brahmana.'

verses.text:
[२०३म] अ.क्रोधनान् सु.प्रसादान् वदन्त्य् एतान् पुरातनान्
                                    ।
[२०३म्च्] लोकस्य-आप्यायने युक्तान् श्राद्ध.देवान् द्विजोत्तमान्
                                    ॥ २१३ ॥ ३.२१३च्[२०३म्च्]व्/ म्: श्राद्धे देवान् द्विजोत्तमान् ॥ 3.213 ॥
verses.english: They (also) call those first of twice-born men the ancient deities of the funeral sacrifice, free from anger, easily pleased, employed in making men prosper.

verses.text:
[२०४म] अपसव्यम् अग्नौ कृत्वा सर्वम् आवृत्य विक्रमम् ।
                                        ३.२१४अ[२०४म]व्/ म्: आवृत्.परिक्रमम्
[२०४म्च्] अपसव्येन हस्तेन निर्वपेद् उदकं भुवि ॥ २१४
                                    ॥
verses.english: After he has performed (the oblations) in the fire, (and) the whole series of ceremonies in such a manner that they end in the south, let him sprinkle water with his right hand on the spot (where the cakes are to be placed).

verses.text:
[२०५म] त्रींस् तु तस्माद्द् हविःशेषात् पिण्डान् कृत्वा
                                    समाहितः ।
[२०५म्च्] औदकेन-एव विधिना निर्वपेद् दक्षिणा.मुखः ॥
                                    २१५ ॥
verses.english: But having made three cakes out of the remainder of that sacrificial food, he must, concentrating his mind and turning towards the south, place them on (Kusa grass) exactly in the same manner in which (he poured out the libations of) water.

verses.text:
[२०६म] न्युप्य पिण्डांस् ततस् तांस् तु प्रयतो
                                    विधिपूर्वकम् ।
[२०६म्च्] तेषु दर्भेषु तं हस्तं निर्मृज्यात्-लेपभागिनाम्
                                    ॥ २१६ ॥
verses.english: Having offered those cakes according to the (prescribed) rule, being pure, let him wipe the same hand with (the roots of) those blades of Kusa grass for the sake of the (three ancestors) who partake of the wipings (lepa).

verses.text:
[२०७म] आचम्य-उदक्परावृत्य त्रिर् आयम्य शनैर् असून्
                                    ।
[२०७म्च्] षड् ऋतूंश् च नमस्कुर्यात् पितॄन् एव च मन्त्रवत्
                                    ॥ २१७ ॥
verses.english: Having (next) sipped water, turned round (towards the north), and thrice slowly suppressed his breath, (the sacrificer) who knows the sacred texts shall worship (the guardian deities of) the six seasons and the manes.

verses.text:
[२०८म] उदकं निनयेत्-शेषं शनैः पिण्डान्तिके पुनः
                                    ।
[२०८म्च्] अवजिघ्रेच् च तान् पिण्डान् यथान्युप्तान् समाहितः
                                    ॥ २१८ ॥
verses.english: Let him gently pour out the remainder of the water near the cakes, and, with fixed attention, smell those cakes, in the order in which they were placed (on the ground).

verses.text:
[२०९म] पिण्डेभ्यस् त्व् अल्पिकां मात्रां समादाय-अनुपूर्वशः
                                    । ३.२१९अ[२०९म]व्/ म्: पिण्डेभ्यः स्वल्पिकां
[२०९म्च्] तान् एव विप्रान् आसीनान् विधिवत् पूर्वम् आशयेत् ॥
                                    २१९ ॥
verses.english: But taking successively very small portions from the cakes, he shall make those seated Brahmana eat them, in accordance with the rule, before (their dinner).

verses.text:
[२१०म] ध्रियमाणे तु पितरि पूर्वेषाम् एव निर्वपेत् ।
[२१०म्च्] विप्रवद् वा-अपि तं श्राद्धे स्वकं पितरम् आशयेत्
                                    ॥ २२० ॥ ३.२२०च्[२१०म्च्]व्/ म्: श्राद्धं ॥ 3.220 ॥
verses.english: But if the (sacrificer's) father is living, he must offer (the cakes) to three remoter (ancestors); or he may also feed his father at the funeral sacrifice as (one of the) Brahmana (guests).

verses.text:
[२११म] पिता यस्य निवृत्तः स्याज् जीवेच् च-अपि पितामहः ।
                                        ३.२२१अ[२११म]व्/ म्: पिता यस्य तु वृत्तः स्याज्
[२११म्च्] पितुः स नाम सङ्कीर्त्य कीर्तयेत् प्रपितामहम् ॥
                                    २२१ ॥
verses.english: But he whose father is dead, while his grandfather lives, shall, after pronouncing his father's name, mention (that of) his great-grandfather.

verses.text:
[२१२म] पितामहो वा तत्.श्राद्धं भुञ्जीत-इत्य् अब्रवीन्
                                    मनुः ।
[२१२म्च्] कामं वा समनुज्ञातः स्वयम् एव समाचरेत् ॥ २२२
                                    ॥
verses.english: Manu has declared that either the grandfather may eat at that Sraddha (as a guest), or (the grandson) having received permission, may perform it, as he desires.

verses.text:
[२१३म] तेषां दत्त्वा तु हस्तेषु स.पवित्रं तिल.उदकम्
                                    ।
[२१३म्च्] तत्पिण्डाग्रं प्रयच्छेत स्वधा-एषाम् अस्त्व् इति
                                    ब्रुवन् ॥ २२३ ॥ ३.२२३च्[२१३म्च्]व्/ म्: प्रयच्छेत् तु ॥ 3.223 ॥
verses.english: Having poured water mixed with sesamum, in which a blade of Kusa grass has been placed, into the hands of the (guests), he shall give (to each) that (above-mentioned) portion of the cake, saying, 'To those, Svadha!'

verses.text:
[२१४म] पाणिभ्यां तु-उपसङ्गृह्य स्वयम् अन्नस्य वर्धितम्
                                    । ३.२२४अ[२१४म]व्/ म्: वर्द्धितम्
[२१४म्च्] विप्रान्तिके पितॄन् ध्यायन् शनकैर् उपनिक्षिपेत् ॥
                                    २२४ ॥
verses.english: But carrying (the vessel) filled with food with both hands, the (sacrificer) himself shall gently place it before the Brahmanas, meditating on the manes.

verses.text:
[२१५म] उभयोर् हस्तयोर् मुक्तं यद् अन्नम् उपनीयते ।
[२१५म्च्] तद् विप्रलुम्पन्त्य् असुराः सहसा दुष्ट.चेतसः ॥
                                    २२५ ॥
verses.english: The malevolent Asuras forcibly snatch away that food which is brought without being held with both hands.

verses.text:
[२१६म] गुणांश् च सूप.शाकाद्यान् पयो दधि घृतं मधु
                                    ।
[२१६म्च्] विन्यसेत् प्रयतः पूर्वं भूमाव् एव समाहितः ॥
                                    २२६ ॥
verses.english: Let him, being pure and attentive, carefully place on the ground the seasoning (for the rice), such as broths and pot herbs, sweet and sour milk, and honey,

verses.text:
[२१७म] भक्ष्यं भोज्यं च विविधं मूलानि च फलानि च
                                    ।
[२१७म्च्] हृद्यानि च-एव मांसानि पानानि सु.रभीणि च ॥
                                    २२७ ॥
verses.english: (As well as) various (kinds of) hard food which require mastication, and of soft food, roots, fruits, savoury meat, and fragrant drinks.

verses.text:
[२१८म] उपनीय तु तत् सर्वं शनकैः सुसमाहितः ।
[२१८म्च्] परिवेषयेत प्रयतो गुणान् सर्वान् प्रचोदयन् ॥
                                    २२८ ॥
verses.english: All this he shall present (to his guests), being pure and attentive, successively invite them to partake of each (dish), proclaiming its qualities.

verses.text:
[२१९म] न-अस्रम् आपातयेज् जातु न कुप्येन् न-अनृतं वदेत्
                                    ।
[२१९म्च्] न पादेन स्पृशेद् अन्नं न च-एतद् अवधूनयेत् ॥
                                    २२९ ॥
verses.english: Let him on no account drop a tear, become angry or utter an untruth, nor let him touch the food with his foot nor violently shake it.

verses.text:
[२२०म] अस्रं गमयति प्रेतान् कोपो ऽरीन् अनृतं शुनः
                                    ।
[२२०म्च्] पादस्पर्शस् तु रक्षांसि दुष्कृतीन् अवधूननम् ॥
                                    २३० ॥
verses.english: A tear sends the (food) to the Pretas, anger to his enemies, a falsehood to the dogs, contact with his foot to the Rakshasas, a shaking to the sinners.

verses.text:
[२२१म] यद् यद् रोचेत विप्रेभ्यस् तत् तद् दद्याद्
                                    अ.मत्सरः ।
[२२१म्च्] ब्रह्मोद्याश् च कथाः कुर्यात् पितॄणाम् एतद् ईप्सितम्
                                    ॥ २३१ ॥
verses.english: Whatever may please the Brahmanas, let him give without grudging it; let him give riddles from the Veda, for that is agreeable to the manes.

verses.text:
[२२२म] स्वाध्यायं श्रावयेत् पित्र्ये धर्मशास्त्राणि च-एव
                                    हि ।
[२२२म्च्] आख्यानानि-इतिहासांश् च पुराणानि खिलानि च ॥ २३२
                                    ॥
verses.english: At a (sacrifice in honour) of the manes, he must let (his guests) hear the Veda, the Institutes of the sacred law, legends, tales, Puranas, and Khilas.

verses.text:
[२२३म] हर्षयेद् ब्राह्मणांस् तुष्टो भोजयेच् च
                                    शनैः.शनैः ।
[२२३म्च्] अन्नाद्येन-असकृच् च-एतान् गुणैश् च परिचोदयेत् ॥
                                    २३३ ॥
verses.english: Himself being delighted, let him give delight to the Brahmanas, cause them to partake gradually and slowly (of each dish), and repeatedly invite (them to eat) by (offering) the food and (praising) its qualities.

verses.text:
[२२४म] व्रतस्थम् अपि दौहित्रं श्राद्धे यत्नेन भोजयेत्
                                    ।
[२२४म्च्] कुतपं च.आसनं दद्यात् तिलैश् च विकिरेन् महीम्
                                    ॥ २३४ ॥
verses.english: Let him eagerly entertain at a funeral sacrifice a daughter's son, though he be a student, and let him place a Nepal blanket on the on the seat (of each guest), scattering sesamum grains on the ground.

verses.text:
[२२५म] त्रीणि श्राद्धे पवित्राणि दौहित्रः कुतपस् तिलाः
                                    ।
[२२५म्च्] त्रीणि च-अत्र प्रशंसन्ति शौचम् अ.क्रोधम्
                                    अ.त्वराम् ॥ २३५ ॥
verses.english: There are three means of sanctification, (to be used) at a Sraddha, a daughter's son, a Nepal blanket, and sesamum grains; and they recommend three (other things) for it, cleanliness, suppression of anger, and absence of haste.

verses.text:
[२२६म] अत्युष्णं सर्वम् अन्नं स्याद् भुञ्जीरंस् ते च
                                    वाग्यताः ।
[२२६म्च्] न च द्विजातयो ब्रूयुर् दात्रा पृष्टा हविर्गुणान् ॥
                                    २३६ ॥
verses.english: All the food must be very hot, and the (guests) shall eat in silence; (even though) asked by the giver (of the feast), the Brahmanas shall not proclaim the qualities of the sacrificial food.

verses.text:
[२२७म] यावद् उष्मा भवत्य् अन्नं यावद् अश्नन्ति वाग्यताः
                                    ।
[२२७म्च्] पितरस् तावद् अश्नन्ति यावत्-न-उक्ता हविर्गुणाः ॥
                                    २३७ ॥
verses.english: As long as the food remains warm, as long as they eat in silence, as long as the qualities of the food are not proclaimed, so long the manes partake (of it).

verses.text:
[२२८म] यद् वेष्टित.शिरा भुङ्क्ते यद् भुङ्क्ते
                                    दक्षिणा.मुखः ।
[२२८म्च्] स.उपानत्कश् च यद् भुङ्क्ते तद् वै रक्षांसि
                                    भुञ्जते ॥ २३८ ॥
verses.english: What (a guest) eats, covering his head, what he eats with his face turned towards the south, what he eats with sandals on (his feet), that the Rakshasas consume.

verses.text:
[२२९म] चाण्डालश् च वराहश् च कुक्कुटः श्वा तथा-एव च
                                    ।
[२२९म्च्] रजस्वला च षण्ढश् च न-ईक्षेरन्न् अश्नतो द्विजान्
                                    ॥ २३९ ॥
verses.english: A Kandala, a village pig, a cock, a dog, a menstruating woman, and a eunuch must not look at the Brahmanas while they eat.

verses.text:
[२३०म] होमे प्रदाने भोज्ये च यद् एभिर् अभिवीक्ष्यते
                                    ।
[२३०म्च्] दैवे हविषि पित्र्ये वा तद् गच्छत्य् अयथातथम्
                                    ॥ २४० ॥
verses.english: What (any of) these sees at a burnt-oblation, at a (solemn) gift, at a dinner (given to Brahmanas), or at any rite in honour of the gods and manes, that produces not the intended result.

verses.text:
[२३१म] घ्राणेन सूकरो हन्ति पक्षवातेन कुक्कुटः ।
                                        ३.२४१अ[२३१म]व्/ म्: शूकरो
[२३१म्च्] श्वा तु दृष्टिनिपातेन स्पर्शेण-अवरवर्णजः ॥
                                    २४१ ॥
verses.english: A boar makes (the rite) useless by inhaling the smell (of the offerings), a cock by the air of his wings, a dog by throwing his eye (on them), a low-caste man by touching (them).

verses.text:
[२३२म] खञ्जो वा यदि वा काणो दातुः प्रेष्यो ऽपि वा भवेत्
                                    ।
[२३२म्च्] हीन.अतिरिक्त.गात्रो वा तम् अप्य् अपनयेत् पुनः ॥
                                    २४२ ॥
verses.english: If a lame man, a one-eyed man, one deficient in a limb, or one with a redundant limb, be even the servant of the performer (of the Sraddha), he must be removed from that place (where the Sraddha is held).

verses.text:
[२३३म] ब्राह्मणं भिक्षुकं वा-अपि भोजनार्थम्
                                    उपस्थितम् ।
[२३३म्च्] ब्राह्मणैर् अभ्यनुज्ञातः शक्तितः प्रतिपूजयेत् ॥
                                    २४३ ॥
verses.english: To a Brahmana (householder), or to an ascetic who comes for food, he may, with the permission of (his) Brahmana (guests), show honour according to his ability.

verses.text:
[२३४म] सार्ववर्णिकम् अन्नाद्यं सन्नीय-आप्लाव्य वारिणा
                                    ।
[२३४म्च्] समुत्सृजेद् भुक्तवताम् अग्रतो विकिरन् भुवि ॥
                                    २४४ ॥
verses.english: Let him mix all the kinds of food together, sprinkle them with water and put them, scattering them (on Kusa grass), down on the ground in front of (his guests), when they have finished their meal.

verses.text:
[२३५म] असंस्कृत.प्रमीतानां त्यागिनां कुलयोषिताम् ।
[२३५म्च्] उच्छिष्टं भागधेयं स्याद् दर्भेषु विकिरश् च
                                    यः ॥ २४५ ॥
verses.english: The remnant (in the dishes), and the portion scattered on Kusa grass, shall be the share of deceased (children) who received not the sacrament (of cremation) and of those who (unjustly) forsook noble wives.

verses.text:
[२३६म] उच्छेषणां भूमिगतम् अ.जिह्मस्य-अ.शठस्य च
                                    ।
[२३६म्च्] दासवर्गस्य तत् पित्र्ये भागधेयं प्रचक्षते ॥
                                    २४६ ॥
verses.english: They declare the fragments which have fallen on the ground at a (Sraddha) to the manes, to be the share of honest, dutiful servants.

verses.text:
[२३७म] आ.सपिण्डक्रियाकर्म द्विजातेः संस्थितस्य तु
                                    ।
[२३७म्च्] अ.दैवं भोजयेत्-श्राद्धं पिण्डम् एकं च
                                    निर्वपेत् ॥ २४७ ॥
verses.english: But before the performance of the Sapindikarana, one must feed at the funeral sacrifice in honour of a (recently-) deceased Aryan (one Brahmana) without (making an offering) to the gods, and give one cake only.

verses.text:
[२३८म] सहपिण्डक्रियायां तु कृतायाम् अस्य धर्मतः ।
[२३८म्च्] अनया-एव-आवृता कार्यं पिण्डनिर्वपनं सुतैः ॥
                                    २४८ ॥
verses.english: But after the Sapindikarana of the (deceased father) has been performed according to the sacred law, the sons must offer the cakes with those ceremonies, (described above.)

verses.text:
[२३९म] श्राद्धं भुक्त्वा य उच्छिष्टं वृषलाय
                                    प्रयच्छति ।
[२३९म्च्] स मूढो नरकं याति कालसूत्रम् अ.वाक्शिराः ॥
                                    २४९ ॥
verses.english: The foolish man who, after having eaten a Sraddha (-dinner), gives the leavings to a Sudra, falls headlong into the Kalasutra hell.

verses.text:
[२४०म] श्राद्धभुग् वृषलीतल्पं तद् अहर् यो ऽधिगच्छति
                                    ।
[२४०म्च्] तस्याः पुरीषे तं मासं पितरस् तस्य शेरते ॥
                                    २५० ॥
verses.english: If the partaker of a Sraddha (-dinner) enters on the same day the bed of a Sudra female, the manes of his (ancestors) will lie during that month in her ordure.

verses.text:
[२४१म] पृष्ट्वा स्वदितम् इत्य् एवं तृप्तान् आचामयेत् ततः
                                    ।
[२४१म्च्] आचान्तांश् च-अनुजानीयाद् अभितो रम्यताम् इति ॥ २५१
                                    ॥
verses.english: Having addressed the question, 'Have you dined well?' (to his guests), let him give water for sipping to them who are satisfied, and dismiss them, after they have sipped water, (with the words) 'Rest either (here or at home)!'

verses.text:
[२४२म] स्वधा-अस्त्व् इत्य् एव तं ब्रूयुर् ब्राह्मणास्
                                    तदनन्तरम् ।
[२४२म्च्] स्वधाकारः परा ह्य् आषीः सर्वेषु पितृकर्मसु ॥
                                    २५२ ॥
verses.english: The Brahmana (guests) shall then answer him, 'Let there be Svadha;' for at all rites in honour of the manes the word Svadha is the highest benison.

verses.text:
[२४३म] ततो भुक्तवतां तेषाम् अन्नशेषं निवेदयेत् ।
[२४३म्च्] यथा ब्रूयुस् तथा कुर्याद् अनुज्ञातस् ततो द्विजैः
                                    ॥ २५३ ॥
verses.english: Next let him inform (his guests) who have finished their meal, of the food which remains; with the permission of the Brahmanas let him dispose (of that), as they may direct.

verses.text:
[२४४म] पित्र्ये स्वदितम् इत्य् एव वाच्यं गोष्ठे तु सुशृतम्
                                    ।
[२४४म्च्] सम्पन्नम् इत्य् अभ्युदये दैवे रुचितम् इत्य् अपि ॥
                                    २५४ ॥ ३.२५४च्[२४४म्च्]व्/ म्: सम्पन्नम् ॥ 3.254 ॥
verses.english: At a (Sraddha) in honour of the manes one must use (in asking of the guests if they are satisfied, the word) svaditam; at a Goshthi-sraddha, (the word) susrutam; at a Vriddhi-sraddha, (the word) sampannam; and at (a rite) in honour of the gods, (the word) rukitam.

verses.text:
[२४५म] अपराह्णस् तथा दर्भा वास्तुसम्पादनं तिलाः ।
                                        ३.२५५अ[२४५म]व्/ म्: सम्पादनं
[२४५म्च्] सृष्टिर् मृष्टिर् द्विजाश् च-अग्र्याः श्राद्धकर्मसु
                                    सम्पदः ॥ २५५ ॥
verses.english: The afternoon, Kusa grass, the due preparation of the dwelling, sesamum grains, liberality, the careful preparation of the food, and (the company of) distinguished Brahmanas are true riches at all funeral sacrifices.

verses.text:
[२४६म] दर्भाः पवित्रं पूर्वाह्णो हविष्याणि च सर्वशः
                                    ।
[२४६म्च्] पवित्रं यच् च पूर्व.उक्तं विज्ञेया हव्यसम्पदः
                                    ॥ २५६ ॥
verses.english: Know that Kusa grass, purificatory (texts), the morning, sacrificial viands of all kinds, and those means of purification, mentioned above, are blessings at a sacrifice to the gods.

verses.text:
[२४७म] मुनि.अन्नानि पयः सोमो मांसं यच् च-अन्.उपस्कृतम्
                                    ।
[२४७म्च्] अक्सार.लवणं च-एव प्रकृत्या हविर् उच्यते ॥
                                    २५७ ॥
verses.english: The food eaten by hermits in the forest, milk, Soma-juice, meat which is not prepared (with spices), and salt unprepared by art, are called, on account of their nature, sacrificial food.

verses.text:
[२४८म] विसृज्य ब्राह्मणांस् तांस् तु नियतो वाग्यतः शुचिः
                                    । ३.२५८अ[२४८म]व्/ म्: विसर्ज्य ब्राह्मनांस् तांस् तु प्रयतो
                                        विधिपूर्वकम्
[२४८म्च्] दक्षिणां दिशम् आकाङ्क्षन् याचेत-इमान् वरान् पितॄन्
                                    ॥ २५८ ॥
verses.english: Having dismissed the (invited) Brahmanas, let him, with a concentrated mind, silent and pure, look towards the south and ask these blessings of the manes:

verses.text:
[२४९म] दातारो नो ऽभिवर्धन्तां वेदाः सन्ततिर् एव च
                                    ।
[२४९म्च्] श्रद्धा च नो मा व्यगमद् बहुदेयं च नो ऽस्त्व्
                                    इति ॥ २५९ ॥
verses.english: 'May liberal men abound with us! May (our knowledge of) the Vedas and (our) progeny increase! May faith not forsake us! May we have much to give (to the needy)!'

verses.text:
[२५०म] एवं निर्वपणं कृत्वा पिण्डांस् तांस् तदनन्तरम्
                                    ।
[२५०म्च्] गां विप्रम् अजम् अग्निं वा प्राशयेद् अप्सु वा क्षिपेत्
                                    ॥ २६० ॥
verses.english: Having thus offered (the cakes), let him, after (the prayer), cause a cow, a Brahmana, a goat, or the sacred fire to consume those cakes, or let him throw them into water.

verses.text:
[२५१म] पिण्डनिर्वपणं के चित् परस्ताद् एव कुर्वते ।
[२५१म्च्] वयोभिः खादयन्त्य् अन्ये प्रक्षिपन्त्य् अनले ऽप्सु
                                    वा ॥ २६१ ॥
verses.english: Some make the offering of the cakes after (the dinner); some cause (them) to be eaten by birds or throw them into fire or into water.

verses.text:
[२५२म] पति.व्रता धर्मपत्नी पितृपूजन.तत्परा ।
[२५२म्च्] मध्यमं तु ततः पिण्डम् अद्यात् सम्यक् सुतार्थिनी
                                    ॥ २६२ ॥
verses.english: The (sacrificer's) first wife, who is faithful and intent on the worship of the manes, may eat the middle-most cake, (if she be) desirous of bearing a son.

verses.text:
[२५३म] आयुष्मन्तं सुतं सूते यशो.मेधासमन्वितम् ।
[२५३म्च्] धनवन्तं प्रजावन्तं सात्त्विकं धार्मिकं तथा
                                    ॥ २६३ ॥
verses.english: (Thus) she will bring forth a son who will be long-lived, famous, intelligent, rich, the father of numerous offspring, endowed with (the quality of) goodness, and righteous.

verses.text:
[२५४म] प्रक्साल्य हस्ताव् आचाम्य ज्ञातिप्रायं प्रकल्पयेत्
                                    ।
[२५४म्च्] ज्ञातिभ्यः सत्कृतं दत्त्वा बान्धवान् अपि भोजयेत्
                                    ॥ २६४ ॥ ३.२६४च्[२५४म्च्]व्/ म्: दत्वा ॥ 3.264 ॥
verses.english: Having washed his hands and sipped water, let him prepare (food) for his paternal relations and, after giving it to them with due respect, let him feed his maternal relatives also.

verses.text:
[२५५म] उच्छेषणं तु तत् तिष्ठेद् यावद् विप्रा विसर्जिताः
                                    । ३.२६५अ[२५५म]व्/ क्: यत् तिष्ठेद्
[२५५म्च्] ततो गृहबलिं कुर्याद् इति धर्मो व्यवस्थितः ॥
                                    २६५ ॥
verses.english: But the remnants shall be left (where they lie) until the Brahmanas have been dismissed; afterwards he shall perform the (daily) domestic Bali-offering; that is a settled (rule of the) sacred law.

verses.text:
[२५६म] हविर् यच् चिररात्राय यच् च-आनन्त्याय कल्पते
                                    ।
[२५६म्च्] पितृभ्यो विधिवद् दत्तं तत् प्रवक्ष्याम्य् अशेषतः
                                    ॥ २६६ ॥
verses.english: I will now fully declare what kind of sacrificial food, given to the manes according to the rule, will serve for a long time or for eternity.

verses.text:
[२५७म] तिलैर् व्रीहि.यवैर् माषैर् अद्भिर् मूल.फलेन वा
                                    ।
[२५७म्च्] दत्तेन मासं तृप्यन्ति विधिवत् पितरो नृनाम् ॥
                                    २६७ ॥
verses.english: The ancestors of men are satisfied for one month with sesamum grains, rice, barley, masha beans, water, roots, and fruits, which have been given according to the prescribed rule,

verses.text:
[२५८म] द्वौ मासौ मत्स्यमांसेन त्रीन् मासान् हारिणेन तु
                                    ।
[२५८म्च्] औरभ्रेण-अथ चतुरः शाकुनेन-अथ पञ्च वै
                                    ॥ २६८ ॥
verses.english: Two months with fish, three months with the meat of gazelles, four with mutton, and five indeed with the flesh of birds,

verses.text:
[२५९म] षण्मासांश् छागमांसेन पार्षतेन च सप्त वै
                                    ।
[२५९म्च्] अष्टाव् एनस्य मांसेन रौरवेण नव-एव तु ॥ २६९
                                    ॥ ३.२६९च्[२५९म्च्]व्/ म्: ऐणेयमांसेन ॥ 3.269 ॥
verses.english: Six months with the flesh of kids, seven with that of spotted deer, eight with that of the black antelope, but nine with that of the (deer called) Ruru,

verses.text:
[२६०म] दशमासांस् तु तृप्यन्ति वराह.महिषामिषैः ।
[२६०म्च्] शश.कूर्मयोस् तु मांसेन मासान् एकादश-एव तु ॥
                                    २७० ॥
verses.english: Ten months they are satisfied with the meat of boars and buffaloes, but eleven months indeed with that of hares and tortoises,

verses.text:
[२६१म] संवत्सरं तु गव्येन पयसा पायसेन च । ३.२७१अ[२६१म]व्/ म्: संवत्सरे
[२६१म्च्] वार्ध्रीणसस्य मांसेन तृप्तिर् द्वादशवार्षिकी ॥
                                    २७१ ॥
verses.english: One year with cow-milk and milk-rice; from the flesh of a long-eared white he-goat their satisfaction endures twelve years.

verses.text:
[२६२म] कालशाकं महाशल्काः खङ्ग.लोहामिषं मधु ।
[२६२म्च्] आनन्त्याय-एव कल्प्यन्ते मुनि.अन्नानि च सर्वशः
                                    ॥ २७२ ॥
verses.english: The (vegetable called) Kalasaka, (the fish called) Mahasalka, the flesh of a rhinoceros and that of a red goat, and all kinds of food eaten by hermits in the forest serve for an endless time.

verses.text:
[२६३म] यत् किं चिन् मधुना मिश्रं प्रदद्यात् तु
                                    त्रयोदशीम् ।
[२६३म्च्] तद् अप्य् अक्षयम् एव स्याद् वर्षासु च मघासु च ॥
                                    २७३ ॥
verses.english: Whatever (food), mixed with honey, one gives on the thirteenth lunar day in the rainy season under the asterism of Maghah, that also procures endless (satisfaction).

verses.text:
[२६४म] अपि नः स कुले भूयाद् यो नो दद्यात् त्रयोदशीम्
                                    ।
[२६४म्च्] पायसं मधु.सर्पिर्भ्यां प्राक् छाये कुञ्जरस्य
                                    च ॥ २७४ ॥
verses.english: 'May such a man (the manes say) be born in our family who will give us milk-rice, with honey and clarified butter, on the thirteenth lunar day (of the month of Bhadrapada) and (in the afternoon) when the shadow of an elephant falls towards the east.'

verses.text:
[२६५म] यद् यद् ददाति विधिवत् सम्यक् श्रद्धासमन्वितः
                                    ।
[२६५म्च्] तत् तत् पितॄणां भवति परत्र-अनन्तम् अक्षयम्
                                    ॥ २७५ ॥
verses.english: Whatever (a man), full of faith, duly gives according to the prescribed rule, that becomes in the other world a perpetual and imperishable (gratification) for the manes.

verses.text:
[२६६म] कृष्णपक्षे दशम्यादौ वर्जयित्वा चतुर्दशीम् ।
[२६६म्च्] श्राद्धे प्रशस्तास् तिथयो यथा-एता न
                                    तथा-इतराः ॥ २७६ ॥
verses.english: The days of the dark half of the month, beginning with the tenth, but excepting the fourteenth, are recommended for a funeral sacrifice; (it is) not thus (with) the others.

verses.text:
[२६७म] युक्षु कुर्वन् दिन.ऋक्षेषु सर्वान् कामान् समश्नुते
                                    ।
[२६७म्च्] अयुक्षु तु पितॄन् सर्वान् प्रजां प्राप्नोति पुष्कलाम्
                                    ॥ २७७ ॥
verses.english: He who performs it on the even (lunar) days and under the even constellations, gains (the fulfilment of) all his wishes; he who honours the manes on odd (lunar days) and under odd (constellations), obtains distinguished offspring.

verses.text:
[२६८म] यथा च-एव-अपरः पक्षः पूर्वपक्षाद् विशिष्यते
                                    ।
[२६८म्च्] तथा श्राद्धस्य पूर्वाह्णाद् अपराह्णो विशिष्यते ॥
                                    २७८ ॥
verses.english: As the second half of the month is preferable to the first half, even so the afternoon is better for (the performance of) a funeral sacrifice than the forenoon.

verses.text:
[२६९म] प्राचीनावीतिना सम्यग् अपसव्यम् अ.तन्द्रिणा ।
[२६९म्च्] पित्र्यम् आ निधनात् कार्यं विधिवद् दर्भ.पाणिना
                                    ॥ २७९ ॥
verses.english: Let him, untired, duly perform the (rites) in honour of the manes in accordance with the prescribed rule, passing the sacred thread over the right shoulder, proceeding from the left to the right (and) holding Kusa grass in his hands, up to the end (of the ceremony).

verses.text:
[२७०म] रात्रौ श्राद्धं न कुर्वीत राक्षसी कीर्तिता हि सा
                                    ।
[२७०म्च्] सन्ध्ययोर् उभयोश् च-एव सूर्ये
                                    च-एव-अचिर.उदिते ॥ २८० ॥
verses.english: Let him not perform a funeral sacrifice at night, because the (night) is declared to belong to the Rakshasas, nor in the twilight, nor when the sun has just risen.

verses.text:
[२७१म] अनेन विधिना श्राद्धं त्रिर् अब्दस्य-इह निर्वपेत्
                                    ।
[२७१म्च्] हेमन्त.ग्रीष्म.वर्षासु पाञ्चयज्ञिकम् अन्वहम् ॥
                                    २८१ ॥
verses.english: Let him offer here below a funeral sacrifice, according to the rule given above, (at least) thrice a year, in winter, in summer, and in the rainy season, but that which is included among the five great sacrifices, every day.

verses.text:
[२७२म] न पैतृयज्ञियो होमो लौकिके ऽग्नौ विधीयते
                                    ।
[२७२म्च्] न दर्शेन विना श्राद्धम् आहित.अग्नेर् द्विजन्मनः
                                    ॥ २८२ ॥
verses.english: The burnt-oblation, offered at a sacrifice to the manes, must not be made in a common fire; a Brahmana who keeps a sacred fire (shall) not (perform) a funeral sacrifice except on the new-moon day.

verses.text:
[२७३म] यद् एव तर्पयत्य् अद्भिः पितॄन् स्नात्वा द्विजोत्तमः
                                    ।
[२७३म्च्] तेन-एव कृत्स्नम् आप्नोति पितृयज्ञक्रियाफलम् ॥
                                    २८३ ॥
verses.english: Even when a Brahmana, after bathing, satisfies the manes with water, he obtains thereby the whole reward for the performance of the (daily) Sraddha.

verses.text:
[२७४म] वसून् वदन्ति तु पितॄन् रुद्रांश् च-एव पितामहान्
                                    ।
[२७४म्च्] प्रपितामहांस् तथा-आदित्यान् श्रुतिर् एषा सनातनी
                                    ॥ २८४ ॥
verses.english: They call (the manes of) fathers Vasus, (those of) grandfathers Rudras, and (those of) great-grandfathers Adityas; thus (speaks) the eternal Veda.

verses.text:
[२७५म] विघसाशी भवेन् नित्यं नित्यं वा-अमृत.भोजनः
                                ।
[२७५म्च्] विघसो भुक्तशेषं तु यज्ञशेषं तथा-अमृतम् ॥ २८५
                                ॥
verses.english: Let him daily partake of the vighasa and daily eat amrita (ambrosia); but vighasa is what remains from the meal (of Brahmana guests) and the remainder of a sacrifice (is called) amrita.

verses.text:
[२७६म] एतद् वो ऽभिहितं सर्वं विधानं पाञ्चयज्ञिकम् ।
[२७६म्च्] द्विजातिमुख्यवृत्तीनां विधानं श्रूयताम् इति ॥ २८६
                                ॥
verses.english: Thus all the ordinances relating to the five (daily great) sacrifices have been declared to you; hear now the law for the manner of living fit for Brahmanas.

verses.text:
चतुर्थम् आयुषो भागम् उषित्वा-आद्यं गुरौ द्विजाः ।
द्वितीयम् आयुषो भागं कृत.दारो गृहे वसेत् ॥ १ ॥
verses.english: Having dwelt with a teacher during the fourth part of (a man's) life, a Brahmana shall live during the second quarter (of his existence) in his house, after he has wedded a wife.

verses.text:
अद्रोहेण-एव भूतानाम् अल्पद्रोहेण वा पुनः ।
या वृत्तिस् तां समास्थाय विप्रो जीवेद् अनापदि ॥ २ ॥
verses.english: A Brahmana must seek a means of subsistence which either causes no, or at least little pain (to others), and live (by that) except in times of distress.

verses.text:
यात्रामात्रप्रसिद्धि.अर्थं स्वैः कर्मभिर् अगर्हितैः ।
अक्लेशेन शरीरस्य कुर्वीत धनसञ्चयम् ॥ ३ ॥
verses.english: For the purpose of gaining bare subsistence, let him accumulate property by (following those) irreproachable occupations (which are prescribed for) his (caste), without (unduly) fatiguing his body.

verses.text:
ऋत.अमृताभ्यां जीवेत् तु मृतेन प्रमृतेन वा ।
सत्य.अनृताभ्याम् अपि वा न श्ववृत्त्या कदा चन ॥ ४ ॥
verses.english: He may subsist by Rita (truth), and Amrita (ambrosia), or by Mrita (death) and by Pramrita (what causes many deaths); or even by (the mode) called Satyanrita (a mixture of truth and falsehood), but never by Svavritti (a dog's mode of life).

verses.text:
ऋतम् उञ्छ.शिलं ज्ञेयम् अमृतं स्याद् अयाचितम् ।
मृतं तु याचितं भैक्षं प्रमृतं कर्षणं स्मृतम् ॥ ५
                                ॥
verses.english: By Rita shall be understood the gleaning of corn; by Amrita, what is given unasked; by Mrita, food obtained by begging and agriculture is declared to be Pramrita.

verses.text:
सत्य.अनृतं तु वाणिज्यं तेन च-एव-अपि जीव्यते ।
सेवा श्ववृत्तिर् आख्याता तस्मात् तां परिवर्जयेत् ॥ ६ ॥
verses.english: But trade and (money-lending) are Satyanrita, even by that one may subsist. Service is called Svavritti; therefore one should avoid it.

verses.text:
कुसूल.धान्यको वा स्यात् कुम्भी.धान्यक एव वा ।
त्र्यह.एहिको वा-अपि भवेद् अ.श्वस्तनिक एव वा ॥ ७ ॥
verses.english: He may either possess enough to fill a granary, or a store filling a grain-jar; or he may collect what suffices for three days, or make no provision for the morrow.

verses.text:
चतुर्णाम् अपि च-एतेषां द्विजानां गृहमेधिनाम् ।
ज्यायान् परः परो ज्ञेयो धर्मतो लोकजित्तमः ॥ ८ ॥
verses.english: Moreover, among these four Brahmana householders, each later-(named) must be considered more distinguished, and through his virtue to have conquered the world more completely.

verses.text:
षट्.कर्म-एको भवत्य् एषां त्रिभिर् अन्यः प्रवर्तते ।
द्वाभ्याम् एकश् चतुर्थस् तु ब्रह्मसत्त्रेण जीवति ॥ ९ ॥
verses.english: One of these follows six occupations, another subsists by three, one by two, but the fourth lives by the Brahmasattra.

verses.text:
वर्तयंश् च शिल.उञ्छाभ्याम् अग्निहोत्र.परायणः ।
इष्टीः पार्वायणान्तीयाः केवला निर्वपेत् सदा ॥ १० ॥
verses.english: He who maintains himself by picking up grains and ears of corn, must be always intent on (the performance of) the Agnihotra, and constantly offer those Ishtis only, which are prescribed for the days of the conjunction and opposition (of the moon), and for the solstices.

verses.text:
न लोकवृत्तं वर्तेत वृत्तिहेतोः कथं चन ।
अ.जिह्माम् अ.शथां शुद्धाम् जीवेद् ब्राह्मणजीविकाम् ॥ ११ ॥
verses.english: Let him never, for the sake of subsistence, follow the ways of the world; let him live the pure, straightforward, honest life of a Brahmana.

verses.text:
सन्तोषं परम् आस्थाय सुखार्थी संयतो भवेत् ।
सन्तोष.मूलं हि सुखं दुःख.मूलं विपर्ययः ॥ १२ ॥
verses.english: He who desires happiness must strive after a perfectly contented disposition and control himself; for happiness has contentment for its root, the root of unhappiness is the contrary (disposition).

verses.text:
अतो ऽन्यतमया वृत्त्या जीवंस् तु स्नातको द्विजः ।
स्वर्ग.आयुष्य.यशस्यानि व्रताणि-इमानि धारयेत् ॥ १३ ॥ ४.१३च्व्/ म्: 
                                    स्वर्ग्य.आयुष्य. ॥ 4.13 ॥
verses.english: A Brahmana, who is a Snataka and subsists by one of the (above-mentioned) modes of life, must discharge the (following) duties which secure heavenly bliss, long life, and fame.

verses.text:
वेद.उदितं स्वकं कर्म नित्यं कुर्याद् अतन्द्रितः ।
तद्द् हि कुर्वन् यथाशक्ति प्राप्नोति परमां गतिम् ॥ १४ ॥
verses.english: Let him, untired, perform daily the rites prescribed for him in the Veda; for he who performs those according to his ability, attains to the highest state.

verses.text:
न-ईहेत-अर्थान् प्रसङ्गेन न विरुद्धेन कर्मणा ।
न विद्यमानेष्व् अर्थेषु न-आर्त्याम् अपि यतस् ततः ॥ १५ ॥
                                    ४.१५च्व्/ म्: 
                                    न कल्पमानेष्व् अर्थेषु ॥ 4.15 ॥
verses.english: Whether he be rich or even in distress, let him not seek wealth through pursuits to which men cleave, nor by forbidden occupations, nor (let him accept presents) from any (giver whosoever he may be).

verses.text:
इन्द्रियार्थेषु सर्वेषु न प्रसज्येत कामतः ।
अतिप्रसक्तिं च-एतेषां मनसा सन्निवर्तयेत् ॥ १६ ॥
verses.english: Let him not, out of desire (for enjoyments), attach himself to any sensual pleasures, and let him carefully obviate an excessive attachment to them, by (reflecting on their worthlessness in) his heart.

verses.text:
सर्वान् परित्यजेद् अर्थान् स्वाध्यायस्य विरोधिनः ।
यथा तथा-अध्यापयंस् तु सा ह्य् अस्य कृतकृत्यता ॥ १७
                                ॥
verses.english: Let him avoid all (means of acquiring) wealth which impede the study of the Veda; (let him maintain himself) anyhow, but study, because that (devotion to the Veda-study secures) the realisation of his aims.

verses.text:
वयसः कर्मणो ऽर्थस्य श्रुतस्य-अभिजनस्य च ।
वेष.वाच्.बुद्धि.सारूप्यम् आचरन् विचरेद् इह ॥ १८ ॥
verses.english: Let him walk here (on earth), bringing his dress, speech, and thoughts to a conformity with his age, his occupation, his wealth, his sacred learning, and his race.

verses.text:
बुद्धि.वृद्धि.कराण्य् आशु धन्यानि च हितानि च ।
नित्यं शास्त्राण्य् अवेक्षेत निगमांश् च-एव वैदिकान् ॥ १९
                                ॥
verses.english: Let him daily pore over those Institutes of science which soon give increase of wisdom, those which teach the acquisition of wealth, those which are beneficial (for other worldly concerns), and likewise over the Nigamas which explain the Veda.

verses.text:
यथा यथा हि पुरुषः शास्त्रं समधिगच्छति ।
तथा तथा विजानाति विज्ञानं च-अस्य रोचते ॥ २० ॥
verses.english: For the more a man completely studies the Institutes of science, the more he fully understands (them), and his great learning shines brightly.

verses.text:
ऋषियज्ञं देवयज्ञं भूतयज्ञं च सर्वदा ।
नृयज्ञं पितृयज्ञं च यथाशक्ति न हापयेत् ॥ २१ ॥
verses.english: Let him never, if he is able (to perform them), neglect the sacrifices to the sages, to the gods, to the Bhutas, to men, and to the manes.

verses.text:
एतान् एके महायज्ञान् यज्ञशास्त्रविदो जनाः ।
अन्.ईहमानाः सततम् इन्द्रियेष्व् एव जुह्वति ॥ २२ ॥
verses.english: Some men who know the ordinances for sacrificial rites, always offer these great sacrifices in their organs (of sensation), without any (external) effort.

verses.text:
वाच्य् एके जुह्वति प्राणं प्राणे वाचं च सर्वदा ।
वाचि प्राणे च पश्यन्तो यज्ञनिर्वृत्तिम् अक्षयाम् ॥ २३ ॥
verses.english: Knowing that the (performance of the) sacrifice in their speech and their breath yields imperishable (rewards), some always offer their breath in their speech, and their speech in their breath.

verses.text:
