ज्ञानेन-एव-अपरे विप्रा यजन्त्य् एतैर् मखैः सदा । ४.२४अव्/ म्: यजन्ते
                                    तैर् मखैः सदा
ज्ञान.मूलाम् क्रियाम् एषां पश्यन्तो ज्ञानचक्षुषा ॥ २४ ॥
verses.english: Other Brahmanas, seeing with the eye of knowledge that the performance of those rites has knowledge for its root, always perform them through knowledge alone.

verses.text:
अग्निहोत्रं च जुहुयाद् आदि.अन्ते द्यु.निशोः सदा ।
दर्शेन च-अर्धमासान्ते पौर्णामासेन च-एव हि ॥ २५ ॥
verses.english: A Brahmana shall always offer the Agnihotra at the beginning or at the end of the day and of the night, and the Darsa and Paurnamasa (Ishtis) at the end of each half-month,

verses.text:
सस्यान्ते नवसस्य.इष्ट्या तथा-ऋतु.अन्ते द्विजो ऽध्वरैः ।
पशुना त्व् अयनस्य-आदौ समान्ते सौमिकैर् मखैः ॥ २६ ॥
                                    ४.२६च्व्/ म्: 
                                    अयनान्ते तु समान्ते ॥ 4.26 ॥
verses.english: When the old grain has been consumed the (Agrayana) Ishti with new grain, at the end of the (three) seasons the (Katurmasya-) sacrifices, at the solstices an animal (sacrifice), at the end of the year Soma-offerings.

verses.text:
न-अन्.इष्ट्वा नवसस्य.इष्ट्या पशुना च-अग्निमान् द्विजः ।
नवान्नम् अद्यात्-मांसं वा दीर्घम् आयुर् जिजीविषुः ॥ २७ ॥
verses.english: A Brahmana, who keeps sacred fires, shall, if he desires to live long, not eat new grain or meat, without having offered the (Agrayana) Ishti with new grain and an animal-(sacrifice).

verses.text:
नवेन-अन्.अर्चिता ह्य् अस्य पशुहव्येन च-अग्नयः ।
प्राणान् एव-अत्तुम् इच्छन्ति नवान्न.आमिषगर्धिनः ॥ २८ ॥
verses.english: For his fires, not being worshipped by offerings of new grain and of an animal, seek to devour his vital spirits, (because they are) greedy for new grain and flesh.

verses.text:
आसन.अशन.शय्याभिर् अद्भिर् मूल.फलेन वा ।
न-अस्य कश् चिद् वसेद् गेहे शक्तितो ऽन्.अर्चितो ऽतिथिः ॥ २९
                                ॥
verses.english: No guest must stay in his house without being honoured, according to his ability, with a seat, food, a couch, water, or roots and fruits.

verses.text:
पाषाण्डिनो विकर्मस्थान् बैडाल.व्रतिकान्-शठान् ।
हैतुकान् बक.वृत्तींश् च वाच्.मात्रेण-अपि न-अर्चयेत् ॥ ३०
                                ॥
verses.english: Let him not honour, even by a greeting, heretics, men who follow forbidden occupations, men who live like cats, rogues, logicians, (arguing against the Veda,) and those who live like herons.

verses.text:
वेदविद्या.व्रत.स्नातान्-श्रोत्रियान् गृहमेधिनः ।
पूजयेद्द् हव्य.कव्येन विपरीतांश् च वर्जयेत् ॥ ३१ ॥
verses.english: Those who have become Snatakas after studying the Veda, or after completing their vows, (and) householders, who are Srotriyas, one must worship by (gifts of food) sacred to gods and manes, but one must avoid those who are different.

verses.text:
शक्तितो ऽ.पचमानेभ्यो दातव्यं गृहमेधिना ।
संविभागश् च भूतेभ्यः कर्तव्यो ऽन्.उपरोधतः ॥ ३२
                                ॥
verses.english: A householder must give (as much food) as he is able (to spare) to those who do not cook for themselves, and to all beings one must distribute (food) without detriment (to one's own interest).

verses.text:
राजतो धनम् अन्विच्छेत् संसीदन् स्नातकः क्षुधा ।
याज्य.अन्तेवासिनोर् वा-अपि न त्व् अन्यत इति स्थितिः ॥ ३३
                                ॥
verses.english: A Snataka who pines with hunger, may beg wealth of a king, of one for whom he sacrifices, and of a pupil, but not of others; that is a settled rule.

verses.text:
न सीदेत् स्नातको विप्रः क्षुधा शक्तः कथं चन ।
न जीर्ण.मलवद्.वासा भवेच् च विभवे सति ॥ ३४ ॥
verses.english: A Snataka who is able (to procure food) shall never waste himself with hunger, nor shall he wear old or dirty clothes, if he possesses property.

verses.text:
कॢप्तकेश.नख.श्मश्रुर् दान्तः शुक्ल.अम्बरः शुचिः ।
स्वाध्याये च-एव युक्तः स्यान् नित्यम् आत्महितेषु च ॥ ३५
                                ॥
verses.english: Keeping his hair, nails, and beard clipped, subduing his passions by austerities, wearing white garments and (keeping himself) pure, he shall be always engaged in studying the Veda and (such acts as are) conducive to his welfare.

verses.text:
वैणवीं धारयेद् यष्टिं स.उदकं च कमण्डलुम् ।
यज्ञोपवीतं वेदं च शुभं रौक्मे च कुण्डले ॥ ३६ ॥
verses.english: He shall carry a staff of bamboo, a pot full of water, a sacred string, a bundle of Kusa grass, and (wear) two bright golden ear-rings.

verses.text:
न-ईक्षेत-उद्यन्तम् आदित्यं न-अस्तं यान्तं कदा चन ।
न-उपसृष्टं न वारिस्थं न मध्यं नभसो गतम् ॥ ३७
                                ॥
verses.english: Let him never look at the sun, when he sets or rises, is eclipsed or reflected in water, or stands in the middle of the sky.

verses.text:
न लङ्घयेद् वत्सतन्त्रीं न प्रधावेच् च वर्षति ।
न च-उदके निरीक्षेत स्वरूपम् इति धारणा ॥ ३८ ॥
verses.english: Let him not step over a rope to which a calf is tied, let him not run when it rains, and let him not look at his own image in water; that is a settled rule.

verses.text:
मृदं गां दैवतं विप्रं घृतं मधु चतुष्पथम् ।
प्रदक्षिणानि कुर्वीत प्रज्ञातांश् च वनस्पतीन् ॥ ३९ ॥
verses.english: Let him pass by (a mound of) earth, a cow, an idol, a Brahmana, clarified butter, honey, a crossway, and well-known trees, turning his right hand towards them.

verses.text:
न-उपगच्छेत् प्रमत्तो ऽपि स्त्रियम् आर्तवदर्शने ।
समानशयने च-एव न शयीत तया सह ॥ ४० ॥
verses.english: Let him, though mad with desire, not approach his wife when her courses appear; nor let him sleep with her in the same bed.

verses.text:
रजसा-अभिप्लुतां नारीं नरस्य ह्य् उपगच्छतः ।
प्रज्ञा तेजो बलं चक्षुर् आयुश् च-एव प्रहीयते ॥ ४१ ॥
verses.english: For the wisdom, the energy, the strength, the sight, and the vitality of a man who approaches a woman covered with menstrual excretions, utterly perish.

verses.text:
तां विवर्जयतस् तस्य रजसा समभिप्लुताम् ।
प्रज्ञा तेजो बलं चक्षुर् आयुश् च-एव प्रवर्धते ॥ ४२ ॥
verses.english: If he avoids her, while she is in that condition, his wisdom, energy, strength, sight, and vitality will increase.

verses.text:
न-अश्नीयाद् भार्यया सार्धं न-एनाम् ईक्षेत च-अश्नतीम् ।
क्षुवतीं जृम्भमाणां वा न च-आसीनां यथासुखम् ॥ ४३ ॥
verses.english: Let him not eat in the company of his wife, nor look at her, while she eats, sneezes, yawns, or sits at her ease.

verses.text:
न-अञ्जयन्तीं स्वके नेत्रे न च-अभ्यक्ताम् अनावृताम् ।
न पश्येत् प्रसवन्तीं च तेजस्.कामो द्विजोत्तमः ॥ ४४ ॥
verses.english: A Brahmana who desires energy must not look at (a woman) who applies collyrium to her eyes, has anointed or uncovered herself or brings forth (a child).

verses.text:
न-अन्नम् अद्याद् एकवासा न नग्नः स्नानम् आचरेत् ।
न मूत्रं पथि कुर्वीत न भस्मनि न गोव्रजे ॥ ४५ ॥
verses.english: Let him not eat, dressed with one garment only; let him not bathe naked; let him not void urine on a road, on ashes, or in a cow-pen,

verses.text:
न फालकृष्टे न जले न चित्यां न च पर्वते ।
न जीर्णदेवायतने न वल्मीके कदा चन ॥ ४६ ॥
verses.english: Nor on ploughed land, in water, on an altar of bricks, on a mountain, on the ruins of a temple, nor ever on an ant-hill,

verses.text:
न स.सत्त्वेषु गर्तेषु न गच्छन्न् अपि न स्थितः ।
न नदीतीरम् आसाद्य न च पर्वतमस्तके ॥ ४७ ॥
verses.english: Nor in holes inhabited by living creatures, nor while he walks or stands, nor on reaching the bank of a river, nor on the top of a mountain.

verses.text:
वायु.अग्नि.विप्रम् आदित्यम् अपः पश्यंस् तथा-एव गाः ।
न कदा चन कुर्वीत विष्.मूत्रस्य विसर्जनम् ॥ ४८ ॥
verses.english: Let him never void faeces or urine, facing the wind, or a fire, or looking towards a Brahmana, the sun, water, or cows.

verses.text:
[५०म] तिरस्कृत्य-उच्चरेत् काष्ठ.लोष्ठ.पत्र.तृणादिना ।
                                    ४.४९अ[५०म]व्/ म्: तृणादि च
[५०म्च्] नियम्य प्रयतो वाचं संवीताङ्गो ऽवगुण्ठितः ॥ ४९
                                ॥
verses.english: He may ease himself, having covered (the ground) with sticks, clods, leaves, grass, and the like, restraining his speech, (keeping himself) pure, wrapping up his body, and covering his head.

verses.text:
[५१म] मूत्र.उच्चार.समुत्सर्गं दिवा कुर्याद् उदङ्.मुखः ।
[५१म्च्] दक्षिणा.अभिमुखो रात्रौ सन्ध्यायोश् च यथा दिवा ॥
                                ५० ॥
verses.english: Let him void faeces and urine, in the daytime turning to the north, at night turning towards the south, during the two twilights in the same (position) as by day.

verses.text:
[५२म] छायायाम् अन्धकारे वा रात्राव् अहनि वा द्विजः ।
[५२म्च्] यथासुख.मुखः कुर्यात् प्राणबाध.भयेषु च ॥ ५१
                                ॥
verses.english: In the shade or in darkness a Brahmana may, both by day and at night, do it, assuming any position he pleases; likewise when his life is in danger.

verses.text:
[४९म] प्रति.अग्निं प्रति.सूर्यं च प्रति.सोम.उदक.द्विजम्
                                ।
[४९म्च्] प्रति.गु प्रति.वातं च प्रज्ञा नश्यति मेहतः ॥ ५२
                                ॥ ४.५२च्[४९म्च्]व्/ क्: प्रति.गां प्रति.वातं ॥ 4.52 ॥
verses.english: The intellect of (a man) who voids urine against a fire, the sun, the moon, in water, against a Brahmana, a cow, or the wind, perishes.

verses.text:
न-अग्निं मुखेन-उपधमेन् नग्नां न-ईक्षेत च स्त्रियम् ।
न-अमेध्यं प्रक्षिपेद् अग्नौ न च पादौ प्रतापयेत् ॥ ५३
                                ॥
verses.english: Let him not blow a fire with his mouth; let him not look at a naked woman; let him not throw any impure substance into the fire, and let him not warm his feet at it.

verses.text:
अधस्तान् न-उपदध्याच् च न च-एनम् अभिलङ्घयेत् ।
न च-एनं पादतः कुर्यान् न प्राण.आबाधम् आचरेत् ॥ ५४
                                ॥
verses.english: Let him not place (fire) under (a bed or the like); nor step over it, nor place it (when he sleeps) at the foot-(end of his bed); let him not torment living creatures.

verses.text:
न-अश्नीयात् सन्धिवेलायां न गच्छेन् न-अपि संविशेत् ।
न च-एव प्रलिखेद् भूमिं न-आत्मनो ऽपहरेत् स्रजम् ॥ ५५
                                ॥
verses.english: Let him not eat, nor travel, nor sleep during the twilight; let him not scratch the ground; let him not take off his garland.

verses.text:
न-अप्सु मूत्रं पुरीषं वा ष्ठीवनं वा समुत्सृजेत् ।
अमेध्यलिप्तम् अन्यद् वा लोहितं वा विषाणि वा ॥ ५६ ॥
verses.english: Let him not throw urine or faeces into the water, nor saliva, nor (clothes) defiled by impure substances, nor any other (impurity), nor blood, nor poisonous things.

verses.text:
न-एकः सुप्यात्-शून्यगेहे न श्रेयांसं प्रबोधयेत् । ४.५७अव्/ शून्यगृहे
                                    स्वप्यान्
न-उदक्यया-अभिभाषेत यज्ञं गच्छेन् न च-अवृतः ॥ ५७
                                ॥
verses.english: Let him not sleep alone in a deserted dwelling; let him not wake (a superior) who is sleeping; let him not converse with a menstruating woman; nor let him go to a sacrifice, if he is not chosen (to be officiating priest).

verses.text:
अग्न्यगारे गवां गोष्ठे ब्राह्मणानां च सन्निधौ ।
स्वाध्याये भोजने च-एव दक्षिनं पाणिम् उद्धरेत् ॥ ५८ ॥
verses.english: Let him keep his right arm uncovered in a place where a sacred fire is kept, in a cow-pen, in the presence of Brahmanas, during the private recitation of the Veda, and at meals.

verses.text:
न वारयेद् गां धयन्तीं न च-आचक्षीत कस्य चित् ।
न दिवि-इन्द्रायुधं दृष्ट्वा कस्य चिद् दर्शयेद् बुधः ॥ ५९
                                ॥
verses.english: Let him not interrupt a cow who is suckling (her calf), nor tell anybody of it. A wise man, if he sees a rainbow in the sky, must not point it out to anybody.

verses.text:
न-अधर्मिके वसेद् ग्रामे न व्याधि.बहुले भृशम् ।
न-एकः प्रपद्येत-अध्वानं न चिरं पर्वते वसेत् ॥ ६०
                                ॥
verses.english: Let him not dwell in a village where the sacred law is not obeyed, nor (stay) long where diseases are endemic; let him not go alone on a journey, nor reside long on a mountain.

verses.text:
न शूद्रराज्ये निवसेन् न-अधार्मिकजनावृते ।
न पाषण्डिगणाक्रान्ते न-उपस्षृटे ऽन्त्यजैर् नृभिः ॥ ६१
                                ॥
verses.english: Let him not dwell in a country where the rulers are Sudras, nor in one which is surrounded by unrighteous men, nor in one which has become subject to heretics, nor in one swarming with men of the lowest castes.

verses.text:
न भुञ्जीत-उद्धृत.स्नेहं न-अतिसौहित्यम् आचरेत् ।
न-अतिप्रगे न-अतिसायं न सायं प्रातर्.आशितः ॥ ६२ ॥
verses.english: Let him not eat anything from which the oil has been extracted; let him not be a glutton; let him not eat very early (in the morning), nor very late (in the evening), nor (take any food) in the evening, if he has eaten (his fill) in the morning.

verses.text:
न कुर्वीत वृथाचेष्टां न वार्य् अञ्जलिना पिबेत् ।
न-उत्सङ्गे भक्षयेद् भक्ष्यान् न जातु स्यात् कुतूहली ॥ ६३
                                ॥
verses.english: Let him not exert himself without a purpose; let him not drink water out of his joined palms; let him not eat food (placed) in his lap; let him not show (idle) curiosity.

verses.text:
न नृत्येद् अथ वा गायेन् न वादित्राणि वादयेत् । ४.६४अव्/ म्: न
                                    नृत्येन् न-एव गायेच् च न वादित्राणि वादयेत्
न-आस्फोटयेन् न च क्ष्वेडेन् न च रक्तो विरावयेत् ॥ ६४ ॥
                                    ४.६४च्व्/ म्: 
                                    न च रक्तो विरोधयेत् ॥ 4.64 ॥
verses.english: Let him not dance, nor sing, nor play musical instruments, nor slap (his limbs), nor grind his teeth, nor let him make uncouth noises, though he be in a passion.

verses.text:
न पादौ धावयेत् कांस्ये कदा चिद् अपि भाजने ।
न भिन्नभाण्डे भुञ्जीत न भावप्रतिदूषिते ॥ ६५ ॥
verses.english: Let him never wash his feet in a vessel of white brass; let him not eat out of a broken (earthen) dish, nor out of one that (to judge) from its appearance (is) defiled.

verses.text:
उपानहौ च वासश् च धृतम् अन्यैर् न धारयेत् ।
उपवीतम् अलङ्कारं स्रजं करकम् एव च ॥ ६६ ॥
verses.english: Let him not use shoes, garments, a sacred string, ornaments, a garland, or a water-vessel which have been used by others.

verses.text:
न-अ.विनीतैर् भजेद् धुर्यैर् न च क्षुध्.व्याधि.पीडितैः ।
                                    ४.६७अव्/ म्: 
                                    न-अविनीतैर् व्रजेद्
न भिन्न.शृङ्ग.अक्षि.खुरैर् न वालधिविरूपितैः ॥ ६७
                                ॥
verses.english: Let him not travel with untrained beasts of burden, nor with (animals) that are tormented by hunger or disease, or whose horns, eyes, and hoofs have been injured, or whose tails have been disfigured.

verses.text:
विनीतैस् तु व्रजेन् नित्यम् आशुगैर् लक्षणान्वितैः ।
वर्ण.रूप.उपसम्पन्नैः प्रतोदेन-आतुदन् भृशम् ॥ ६८ ॥
                                    ४.६८च्व्/ म्: 
                                    प्रतोदेन-आक्षिपन् ॥ 4.68 ॥
verses.english: Let him always travel with (beasts) which are well broken in, swift, endowed with lucky marks, and perfect in colour and form, without urging them much with the goad.

verses.text:
बालातपः प्रेतधूमो वर्ज्यं भिन्नं तथा-आसनम् ।
न छिन्द्यान् नख.रोमाणि दन्तैर् न-उत्पाटयेन् नखान् ॥ ६९ ॥
                                    ४.६९च्व्/ म्: 
                                    न च्छिन्द्यान् ॥ 4.69 ॥
verses.english: The morning sun, the smoke rising from a (burning) corpse, and a broken seat must be avoided. Let him not clip his nails or hair, and not tear his nails with his teeth.

verses.text:
न मृत्.लोष्ठं च मृद्नीयान् न छिन्द्यात् करजैस् तृणम् । ४.७०अव्/ म्: 
                                    च्छिन्द्यात्
न कर्म निष्फलं कुर्यान् न-आयत्याम् अ.सुख.उदयम् ॥ ७०
                                ॥
verses.english: Let him not crush earth or clods, nor tear off grass with his nails; let him not do anything that is useless or will have disagreeable results in the future.

verses.text:
लोष्ठमर्दी तृणच्छेदी नखखादी च यो नरः ।
स विनाशं व्रजत्य् आशु सूचका-अशुचिर् एव च ॥ ७१ ॥ ४.७१च्व्/ म्: सूचको
                                    ऽशुचिर् एव च ॥ 4.71 ॥
verses.english: A man who crushes clods, tears off grass, or bites his nails, goes soon to perdition, likewise an informer and he who neglects (the rules of) purification.

verses.text:
न विगर्ह्य कथां कुर्याद् बहिर् माल्यं न धारयेत् । ४.७२अव्/ म्: न
                                    विगृह्य कथां कुर्याद्
गवां च यानं पृष्ठेन सर्वथा-एव विगर्हितम् ॥ ७२ ॥
verses.english: Let him not wrangle; let him not wear a garland over (his hair). To ride on the back of cows (or of oxen) is anyhow a blamable act.

verses.text:
अ.द्वारेण च न-अतीयाद् ग्रामं वा वेश्म वा-आवृतम् ।
रात्रौ च वृक्षमूलानि दूरतः परिवर्जयेत् ॥ ७३ ॥
verses.english: Let him not enter a walled village or house except by the gate, and by night let him keep at a long distance from the roots of trees.

verses.text:
न-अक्षैर् दीव्येत् कदा चित् तु स्वयं न-उपानहौ हरेत् ।
शयनस्थो न भुञ्जीत न पाणिस्थं न च-आसने ॥ ७४ ॥
verses.english: Let him never play with dice, nor himself take off his shoes; let him not eat, lying on a bed, nor what has been placed in his hand or on a seat.

verses.text:
सर्वं च तिलसम्बद्धं न-अद्याद् अस्तम् इते रवौ ।
न च नग्नः शयीत-इह न च-उच्छिष्टः क्व चिद् व्रजेत् ॥ ७५
                                ॥
verses.english: Let him not eat after sunset any (food) containing sesamum grains; let him never sleep naked, nor go anywhere unpurified (after meals).

verses.text:
आर्द्र.पादस् तु भुञ्जीत न-आर्द्र.पादस् तु संविशेत् ।
आर्द्र.पादस् तु भुञ्जानो दीर्घम् आयुर् अवाप्नुयात् ॥ ७६ ॥
verses.english: Let him eat while his feet are (yet) wet (from the ablution), but let him not go to bed with wet feet. He who eats while his feet are (still) wet, will attain long life.

verses.text:
अ.चक्षुर्विषयं दुर्गं न प्रपद्येत कर्हि चित् ।
न विष्.मूत्रम् उदीक्षेत न बाहुभ्यां नदीं तरेत् ॥ ७७ ॥
verses.english: Let him never enter a place, difficult of access, which is impervious to his eye; let him not look at urine or ordure, nor cross a river (swimming) with his arms.

verses.text:
अधितिष्ठेन् न केशांस् तु न भस्म.अस्थि.कपालिकाः ।
न कार्पास.अस्थि न तुषान् दीर्घम् आयुर् जिजीविषुः ॥ ७८ ॥
verses.english: Let him not step on hair, ashes, bones, potsherds, cotton-seed or chaff, if he desires long life.

verses.text:
न संवसेच् च पतितैर् न चाण्डालैर् न पुल्कसैः ।
न मूर्खैर् न-अवलिप्तैश् च न-अन्त्यैर् न-अन्त्यावसायिभिः ॥
                                ७९ ॥
verses.english: Let him not stay together with outcasts, nor with Kandalas, nor with Pukkasas, nor with fools, nor with overbearing men, nor with low-caste men, nor with Antyavasayins.

verses.text:
न शूद्राय मतिं दद्यान् न-उच्छिष्टं न हविष्कृतम् ।
न च-अस्य-उपदिशेद् धर्मं न च-अस्य व्रतम् आदिशेत् ॥ ८०
                                ॥
verses.english: Let him not give to a Sudra advice, nor the remnants (of his meal), nor food offered to the gods; nor let him explain the sacred law (to such a man), nor impose (upon him) a penance.

verses.text:
यो ह्य् अस्य धर्मम् आचष्टे यश् च-एव-आदिशति व्रतम् ।
सो ऽसंवृतं नाम तमः सह तेन-एव मज्जति ॥ ८१ ॥
verses.english: For he who explains the sacred law (to a Sudra) or dictates to him a penance, will sink together with that (man) into the hell (called) Asamvrita.

verses.text:
न संहताभ्यां पाणिभ्यां कण्डूयेद् आत्मनः शिरः ।
न स्पृशेच् च-एतद् उच्छिष्टो न च स्नायाद् विना ततः ॥ ८२
                                ॥
verses.english: Let him not scratch his head with both hands joined; let him not touch it while he is impure, nor bathe without (submerging) it.

verses.text:
केशग्रहान् प्रहारांश् च शिरस्य् एतान् विवर्जयेत् ।
शिरःस्नातश् च तैलेन न-अङ्गं किं चिद् अपि स्पृशेत् ॥ ८३
                                ॥
verses.english: Let him avoid (in anger) to lay hold of (his own or other men's) hair, or to strike (himself or others) on the head. When he has bathed (submerging) his head, he shall not touch any of his limbs with oil.

verses.text:
न राज्ञः प्रतिगृह्णीयाद् अराजन्यप्रसूतितः ।
सूना.चक्र.ध्वजवतां वेशेन-एव च जीवताम् ॥ ८४ ॥
verses.english: Let him not accept presents from a king who is not descended from the Kshatriya race, nor from butchers, oil-manufacturers, and publicans, nor from those who subsist by the gain of prostitutes.

verses.text:
दशसूना.समं चक्रं दशचक्र.समो ध्वजः ।
दशध्वज.समो वेशो दशवेश.समो नृपः ॥ ८५ ॥
verses.english: One oil-press is as (bad) as ten slaughter-houses, one tavern as (bad as) ten oil-presses, one brothel as (bad as) ten taverns, one king as (bad as) ten brothels.

verses.text:
दश सूणासहस्राणि यो वाहयति सौनिकः ।
तेन तुल्यः स्मृतो राजा घोरस् तस्य प्रतिग्रहः ॥ ८६ ॥
verses.english: A king is declared to be equal (in wickedness) to a butcher who keeps a hundred thousand slaughter-houses; to accept presents from him is a terrible (crime).

verses.text:
यो राज्ञः प्रतिगृह्णाति लुब्धस्य-उच्छास्त्रवर्तिनः ।
स पर्यायेण याति-इमान् नरकान् एकविंशतिम् ॥ ८७ ॥
verses.english: He who accepts presents from an avaricious king who acts contrary to the Institutes (of the sacred law), will go in succession to the following twenty-one hells:

verses.text:
तामिस्रम् अन्धतामिस्रं महारौरव.रौरवौ ।
नरकं कालसूत्रं च महानरकम् एव च ॥ ८८ ॥
verses.english: Tamisra, Andhatamisra, Maharaurava, Raurava, the Kalasutra hell, Mahanaraka,

verses.text:
सञ्जीवनं महावीचिं तपनं सम्प्रतापनम् ।
संहातं च स.काकोलं कुड्मलं प्रतिमूर्तिकम् ॥ ८९ ॥ ४.८९च्व्/ म्: 
                                    पूतिमृत्तिकम् ॥ 4.89 ॥
verses.english: Samgivana, Mahaviki, Tapana, Sampratapana, Samghata, Sakakola, Kudmala, Putimrittika,

verses.text:
लोहशङ्कुम् ऋजीषं च पन्थानं शाल्मलीं नदीम् ।
असिपत्रवनं च-एव लोहदारकम् एव च ॥ ९० ॥
verses.english: Lohasanku, Rigisha, Pathin, the (flaming) river, Salmala, Asipatravana, and Lohakaraka.

verses.text:
एतद् विदन्तो विद्वांसो ब्राह्मणा ब्रह्मवादिनः ।
न राज्ञः प्रतिगृह्णन्ति प्रेत्य श्रेयो ऽभिकाङ्क्षिणः ॥ ९१
                                ॥
verses.english: Learned Brahmanas, who know that, who study the Veda and desire bliss after death, do not accept presents from a king.

verses.text:
ब्राह्मे मुहूर्ते बुध्येत धर्म.अर्थौ च-अनुचिन्तयेत् ।
कायक्लेशांश् च तन्.मूलान् वेदतत्त्वार्थम् एव च ॥ ९२ ॥
verses.english: Let him wake in the muhurta, sacred to Brahman, and think of (the acquisition of) spiritual merit and wealth, of the bodily fatigue arising therefrom, and of the true meaning of the Veda.

verses.text:
उत्थाय-आवश्यकं कृत्वा कृत.शौचः समाहितः ।
पूर्वां सन्ध्यां जपंस् तिष्ठेत् स्वकाले च-अपरां चिरम् ॥ ९३
                                ॥
verses.english: When he has risen, has relieved the necessities of nature and carefully purified himself, let him stand during the morning twilight, muttering for a long time (the Gayatri), and at the proper time (he must similarly perform) the evening (devotion).

verses.text:
ऋषयो दीर्घसन्ध्यत्वाद् दीर्घम् आयुर् अवाप्नुयुः ।
प्रज्ञां यशश् च कीर्तिं च ब्रह्मवर्चसम् एव च ॥ ९४ ॥
verses.english: By prolonging the twilight devotions, the sages obtained long life, wisdom, honour, fame, and excellence in Vedic knowledge.

verses.text:
श्रावण्यां प्रौष्ठपद्यां वा-अप्य् उपाकृत्य यथाविधि ।
युक्तश् छन्दांस्य् अधीयीत मासान् विप्रो ऽर्धपञ्चमान् ॥ ९५
                                ॥
verses.english: Having performed the Upakarman according to the prescribed rule on (the full moon of the month) Sravana, or on that of Praushthapada (Bhadrapada), a Brahmana shall diligently study the Vedas during four months and a half.

verses.text:
पुष्ये तु छन्दसां कुर्याद् बहिर् उत्सर्जनं द्विजः ।
माघशुक्लस्य वा प्राप्ते पूर्वाह्णे प्रथमे ऽहनि ॥ ९६ ॥
verses.english: When the Pushya-day (of the month Pausha), or the first day of the bright half of Magha has come, a Brahmana shall perform in the forenoon the Utsargana of the Vedas.

verses.text:
यथाशास्त्रं तु कृत्वा-एवम् उत्सर्गं छन्दसां बहिः ।
विरमेत् पक्षिणीं रात्रिं तद् एव-एकम् अहर्.निशम् ॥ ९७ ॥
verses.english: Having performed the Utsarga outside (the village), as the Institutes (of the sacred law) prescribe, he shall stop reading during two days and the intervening night, or during that day (of the Utsarga) and (the following) night.

verses.text:
अत ऊर्ध्वं तु छन्दांसि शुक्लेषु नियतः पठेत् ।
वेदाङ्गानि च सर्वाणि कृष्णपक्षेषु सम्पठेत् ॥ ९८ ॥
verses.english: Afterwards he shall diligently recite the Vedas during the bright (halves of the months), and duly study all the Angas of the Vedas during the dark fortnights.

verses.text:
न-अविस्पष्टम् अधीयीत न शूद्रजनसन्निधौ ।
न निशान्ते परिश्रान्तो ब्रह्म-अधीत्य पुनः स्वपेत् ॥ ९९
                                ॥
verses.english: Let him not recite (the texts) indistinctly, nor in the presence of Sudras; nor let him, if in the latter part of the night he is tired with reciting the Veda, go again to sleep.

verses.text:
यथा.उदितेन विधिना नित्यं छन्दस्कृतं पठेत् ।
ब्रह्म छन्दस्कृतं च-एव द्विजो युक्तो ह्य् अनापदि ॥ १००
                                ॥
verses.english: According to the rule declared above, let him recite the daily (portion of the) Mantras, and a zealous Brahmana, (who is) not in distress, (shall study) the Brahmana and the Mantrasamhita.

verses.text:
इमान् नित्यम् अनध्यायान् अधीयानो विवर्जयेत् ।
अध्यापनं च कुर्वाणः शिष्याणां विधिपूर्वकम् ॥ १०१ ॥
verses.english: Let him who studies always avoid (reading) on the following occasions when the Veda-study is forbidden, and (let) him who teaches pupils according to the prescribed rule (do it likewise).

verses.text:
कर्णश्रवे ऽनिले रात्रौ दिवा पांसुसमूहने ।
एतौ वर्षास्व् अन्.अध्यायाव् अध्यायज्ञाः प्रचक्षते ॥ १०२
                                ॥
verses.english: Those who know the (rules of) recitation declare that in the rainy season the Veda-study must be stopped on these two (occasions), when the wind is audible at night, and when it whirls up the dust in the day-time.

verses.text:
विद्युत्.स्तनित.वर्षेषु महा.उल्कानां च सम्प्लवे ।
आकालिकम् अनध्यायम् एतेषु मनुर् अब्रवीत् ॥ १०३ ॥
verses.english: Manu has stated, that when lightning, thunder, and rain (are observed together), or when large fiery meteors fall on all sides, the recitation must be interrupted until the same hour (on the next day, counting from the occurrence of the event).

verses.text:
एतांस् त्व् अभ्युदितान् विद्याद् यदा प्रादुष्कृताग्निषु ।
तदा विद्याद् अनध्यायम् अन्.ऋतौ च-अभ्रदर्शने ॥ १०४ ॥
verses.english: When one perceives these (phenomena) all together (in the twilight), after the sacred fires have been made to blaze (for the performance of the Agnihotra), then one must know the recitation of the Veda to be forbidden, and also when clouds appear out of season.

verses.text:
निर्घाते भूमिचलने ज्योतिषां च-उपसर्जने ।
एतान् आकालिकान् विद्याद् अनध्यायान् ऋताव् अपि ॥ १०५ ॥
verses.english: On (the occasion of) a preternatural sound from the sky, (of) an earthquake, and when the lights of heaven are surrounded by a halo, let him know that (the Veda-study must be) stopped until the same hour (on the next day), even if (these phenomena happen) in the (rainy) season.

verses.text:
प्रादुष्कृतेष्व् अग्निषु तु विद्युत्.स्तनित.निःस्वने ।
स.ज्योतिः स्याद् अनध्यायः शेषे रात्रौ यथा दिवा ॥ १०६
                                ॥
verses.english: But when lightning and the roar of thunder (are observed) after the sacred fires have been made to blaze, the stoppage shall last as long as the light (of the sun or of the stars is visible); if the remaining (above-named phenomenon, rain, occurs, the reading shall cease), both in the day-time and at night.

verses.text:
नित्य.अनध्याय एव स्याद् ग्रामेषु नगरेषु च ।
धर्मनैपुण्य.कामानां पूतिगन्धे च सर्वदा ॥ १०७ ॥ ४.१०७च्व्/ म्: 
                                    सर्वशः ॥ 4.107 ॥
verses.english: For those who wish to acquire exceedingiy great merit, a continual interruption of the Veda-study (is prescribed) in villages and in towns, and (the Veda-study must) always (cease) when any kind of foul smell (is perceptible).

verses.text:
अन्तर्गत.शवे ग्रामे वृषलस्य च सन्निधौ ।
अनध्यायो रुद्यमाने समवाये जनस्य च ॥ १०८ ॥
verses.english: In a village where a corpse lies, in the presence of a (man who lives as unrighteously as a) Sudra, while (the sound of) weeping (is heard), and in a crowd of men the (recitation of the Veda must be) stopped.

verses.text:
उदके मध्यरात्रे च विष्.मूत्रस्य विसर्जने ।
उच्छिष्टः श्राद्धभुक् च-एव मनसा-अपि न चिन्तयेत् ॥ १०९
                                ॥
verses.english: In water, during the middle part of the night, while he voids excrements, or is impure, and after he has partaken of a funeral dinner, a man must not even think in his heart (of the sacred texts).

verses.text:
प्रतिगृह्य द्विजो विद्वान् एकोद्दिष्टस्य केतनम् । ४.११०अव्/ म्: 
                                    एकोद्दिष्ट.निकेतनम्
त्र्यहं न कीर्तयेद् ब्रह्म राज्ञो राहोश् च सूतके ॥ ११०
                                ॥
verses.english: A learned Brahmana shall not recite the Veda during three days, when he has accepted an invitation to a (funeral rite) in honour of one ancestor (ekoddishta), or when the king has become impure through a birth or death in his family (sutaka), or when Rahu by an eclipse makes the moon impure.

verses.text:
यावद् एकानुदिष्टस्य गन्धो लेपश् च तिष्ठति ।
विप्रस्य विदुषो देहे तावद् ब्रह्म न कीर्तयेत् ॥ १११ ॥
verses.english: As long as the smell and the stains of the (food given) in honour of one ancestor remain on the body of a learned Brahmana, so long he must not recite the Veda.

verses.text:
शयानः प्रौढ.पादश् च कृत्वा च-एव-अवसक्थिकाम् ।
न-अधीयीत-आमिषं जग्ध्वा सूतकान्नाद्यम् एव च ॥ ११२
                                ॥
verses.english: While lying on a bed, while his feet are raised (on a bench), while he sits on his hams with a cloth tied round his knees, let him not study, nor when he has eaten meat or food given by a person impure on account of a birth or a death,

verses.text:
नीहारे बाणशब्दे च सन्ध्ययोर् एव च-उभयोः ।
अमावास्या.चतुर्दश्योः पौर्णमास्य्.अष्टकासु च ॥ ११३ ॥
verses.english: Nor during a fog, nor while the sound of arrows is audible, nor during both the twilights, nor on the new-moon day, nor on the fourteenth and the eighth (days of each half-month), nor on the full-moon day.

verses.text:
अमावास्या गुरुं हन्ति शिष्यं हन्ति चतुर्दशी ।
ब्रह्म-अष्टक.पौर्णमास्यौ तस्मात् ताः परिवर्जयेत् ॥ ११४
                                ॥
verses.english: The new-moon day destroys the teacher, the fourteenth (day) the pupil, the eighth and the full-moon days (destroy all remembrance of) the Veda; let him therefore avoid (reading on) those (days).

verses.text:
पांसुवर्षे दिशां दाहे गोमायुविरुते तथा ।
श्व.खर.उष्ट्रे च रुवति पङ्क्तौ च न पठेद् द्विजः ॥ ११५
                                ॥
verses.english: A Brahmana shall not recite (the Veda) during a dust-storm, nor while the sky is preternaturally red, nor while jackals howl, nor while the barking of dogs, the braying of donkeys, or the grunting of camels (is heard), nor while (he is seated) in a company.

verses.text:
न-अधीयीत श्मशानान्ते ग्रामान्ते गोव्रजे ऽपि वा ।
वसित्वा मैथुनं वासः श्राद्धिकं प्रतिगृह्य च ॥ ११६
                                ॥
verses.english: Let him not study near a burial-ground, nor near a village, nor in a cow-pen, nor dressed in a garment which he wore during conjugal intercourse, nor after receiving a present at a funeral sacrifice.

verses.text:
प्राणि वा यदि वा-अप्राणि यत् किं चित्-श्राद्धिकं भवेत् ।
तद् आलभ्य-अप्य् अनध्यायः पाण्य्.आस्यो हि द्विजः स्मृतः ॥ ११७
                                ॥
verses.english: Be it an animal or a thing inanimate, whatever be the (gift) at a Sraddha, let him not, having just accepted it, recite the Veda; for the hand of a Brahmana is his mouth.

verses.text:
चोरैर् उपद्रुते ग्रामे सम्भ्रमे च-अग्निकारिते ।]४.११८अव्/ म्: 
                                    चौरैर् उपप्लुते, सम्भ्रमे
आकालिकम् अनध्यायं विद्यात् सर्वाद्भुतेषु च ॥ ११८ ॥
verses.english: When the village has been beset by robbers, and when an alarm has been raised by fire, let him know that (the Veda-study must be) interrupted until the same hour (on the next day), and on (the occurrence of) all portents.

verses.text:
उपाकर्मणि च-उत्सर्गे त्रिरात्रं क्षेपणं स्मृतम् ।
अष्टकासु त्व् अहोरात्रम् ऋत्वन्तासु च रात्रिषु ॥ ११९ ॥
verses.english: On (the occasion of) the Upakarman and (of) the Vedotsarga an omission (of the Veda-study) for three days has been prescribed, but on the Ashtakas and on the last nights of the seasons for a day and a night.

verses.text:
न-अधीयीत-अश्वम् आरूढो न वृक्षं न च हस्तिनम् ।
न नावं न खरं न-उष्ट्रं न-इरिणस्थो न यानगः ॥ १२०
                                ॥
verses.english: Let him not recite the Veda on horseback, nor on a tree, nor on an elephant, nor in a boat (or ship), nor on a donkey, nor on camel, nor standing on barren ground, nor riding in a carriage,

verses.text:
न विवादे न कलहे न सेनायां न सङ्गरे ।
न भुक्तमात्रे न-अजीर्णे न वमित्वा न शुक्तके ॥ १२१ ॥
verses.english: Nor during a verbal altercation, nor during a mutual assault, nor in a camp, nor during a battle, nor when he has just eaten, nor during an indigestion, nor after vomiting, nor with sour eructations,

verses.text:
अतिथिं च-अन्.अनुज्ञाप्य मारुते वाति वा भृशम् ।
रुधिरे च स्रुते गात्रात्-शस्त्रेण च परिक्षते ॥ १२२ ॥
verses.english: Nor without receiving permission from a guest (who stays in his house), nor while the wind blows vehemently, nor while blood flows from his body, nor when he is wounded by a weapon.

verses.text:
सामध्वनाव् ऋच्.यजुषी न-अधीयीत कदा चन ।
वेदस्य-अधीत्य वा-अप्य् अन्तम् आरण्यकम् अधीत्य च ॥ १२३
                                ॥
verses.english: Let him never recite the Rig-veda or the Yagur-veda while the Saman (melodies) are heard; (let him stop all Veda-study for a day and a night) after finishing a Veda or after reciting an Aranyaka.

verses.text:
ऋग्वेदो देव.दैवत्यो यजुर्वेदस् तु मानुषः ।
सामवेदः स्मृतः पित्र्यस् तस्मात् तस्य-अशुचिर् ध्वनिः ॥ १२४
                                ॥
verses.english: The Rig-veda is declared to be sacred to the gods, the Yagur-veda sacred to men, and the Sama-veda sacred to the manes; hence the sound of the latter is impure (as it were).

verses.text:
एतद् विद्वन्तो विद्वांसस् त्रयीनिष्कर्षम् अन्वहम् ।
क्रमतः पूर्वम् अभ्यस्य पश्चाद् वेदम् अधीयते ॥ १२५ ॥
verses.english: Knowing this, the learned daily repeat first in due order the essence of the three (Vedas) and afterwards the (text of the) Veda.

verses.text:
पशु.मण्डूक.मार्जार.श्व.सर्प.नकुल.आखुभिः ।
अन्तरागमने विद्याद् अनध्यायम् अहर्.निशम् ॥ १२६ ॥
verses.english: Know that (the Veda-study must be) interrupted for a day and a night, when cattle, a frog, a cat, a dog, a snake, an ichneumon, or a rat pass between (the teacher and his pupil).

verses.text:
द्वाव् एव वर्जयेन् नित्यम् अनध्यायौ प्रयत्नतः ।
स्वाध्यायभूमिं च-अशुद्धम् आत्मानं च-अशुचिं द्विजः ॥ १२७
                                ॥
verses.english: Let a twice-born man always carefully interrupt the Veda-study on two (occasions, viz.) when the place where he recites is impure, and when he himself is unpurified.

verses.text:
अमावास्याम् अष्टमीं च पौर्णमासीं चतुर्दशीम् ।
ब्रह्मचारी भवेन् नित्यम् अप्य् ऋतौ स्नातको द्विजः ॥ १२८
                                ॥
verses.english: A twice-born man who is a Snataka shall remain chaste on the new-moon day, on the eighth (lunar day of each half-month), on the full-moon day, and on the fourteenth, even (if they fall) in the period (proper for conjugal intercourse).

verses.text:
न स्नानम् आचरेद् भुक्त्वा न-आतुरो न महानिशि ।
न वासोभिः सह-अजस्रं न-अविज्ञाते जलाशये ॥ १२९ ॥
verses.english: Let him not bathe (immediately) after a meal, nor when he is sick, nor in the middle of the night, nor frequently dressed in all his garments, nor in a pool which he does not perfectly know.

verses.text:
देवतानां गुरो राज्ञः स्नातक.आचार्ययोस् तथा ।
न-आक्रामेत् कामतश् छायां बभ्रुणो दीक्षितस्य च ॥ १३०
                                ॥
verses.english: Let him not intentionally step on the shadow of (images of) the gods, of a Guru, of a king, of a Snataka, of his teacher, of a reddish-brown animal, or of one who has been initiated to the performance of a Srauta sacrifice (Dikshita).

verses.text:
मध्यन्दिने ऽर्धरात्रे च श्राद्धं भुक्त्वा च स.आमिषम्
                                ।
सन्ध्ययोर् उभयोश् च-एव न सेवेत चतुष्पथम् ॥ १३१
                                ॥
verses.english: At midday and at midnight, after partaking of meat at a funeral dinner, and in the two twilights let him not stay long on a cross-road.

verses.text:
उद्वर्तनम् अपस्नानं विष्.मूत्रे रक्तम् एव च ।
श्लेश्म.निष्ठ्यूत.वान्तानि न-अधितिष्ठेत् तु कामतः ॥ १३२
                                ॥
verses.english: Let him not step intentionally on things used for cleansing the body, on water used for a bath, on urine or ordure, on blood, on mucus, and on anything spat out or vomited.

verses.text:
वैरिणं न-उपसेवेत सहायं च-एव वैरिणः ।
अधार्मिकं तस्करं च परस्य-एव च योषितं ॥ १३३ ॥
verses.english: Let him not show particular attention to an enemy, to the friend of an enemy, to a wicked man, to a thief, or to the wife of another man.

verses.text:
न हि-ईदृशम् अन्.आयुष्यं लोके किं चन विद्यते ।
यादृशं पुरुषस्य-इह परदार.उपसेवनम् ॥ १३४ ॥
verses.english: For in this world there is nothing so detrimental to long life as criminal conversation with another man's wife.

verses.text:
क्षत्रियं च-एव सर्पं च ब्राह्मणं च बहु.श्रुतम् ।
न-अवमन्येत वै भूष्णुः कृशान् अपि कदा चन ॥ १३५ ॥
verses.english: Let him who desires prosperity, indeed, never despise a Kshatriya, a snake, and a learned Brahmana, be they ever so feeble.

verses.text:
एतत् त्रयं हि पुरुषं निर्दहेद् अवमानितम् ।
तस्माद् एतत् त्रयं नित्यं न-अवमन्येत बुद्धिमान् ॥ १३६
                                ॥
verses.english: Because these three, when treated with disrespect, may utterly destroy him; hence a wise man must never despise them.

verses.text:
न-आत्मानम् अवमन्येत पुर्वाभिर् अ.समृद्धिभिः ।
आ मृत्योः श्रियम् अन्विच्छेन् न-एनां मन्येत दुर्.लभाम् ॥ १३७
                                ॥
verses.english: Let him not despise himself on account of former failures; until death let him seek fortune, nor despair of gaining it.

verses.text:
सत्यं ब्रूयात् प्रियं ब्रूयान् न ब्रूयात् सत्यम् अप्रियम् ।
प्रियं च न-अनृतं ब्रूयाद् एष धर्मः सनातनः ॥ १३८
                                ॥
verses.english: Let him say what is true, let him say what is pleasing, let him utter no disagreeable truth, and let him utter no agreeable falsehood; that is the eternal law.

verses.text:
भद्रं भद्रम् इति ब्रूयाद् भद्रम् इत्य् एव वा वदेत् ।
शुष्क.वैरं विवादं च न कुर्यात् केन चित् सह ॥ १३९
                                ॥
verses.english: (What is) well, let him call well, or let him say 'well' only; let him not engage in a useless enmity or dispute with anybody.

verses.text:
न-अतिकल्यं न-अतिसायं न-अतिमध्यन्दिने स्थिते ।
न-अज्ञातेन समं गच्छेन् न-एको न वृषलैः सह ॥ १४०
                                ॥
verses.english: Let him not journey too early in the morning, nor too late in the evening, nor just during the midday (heat), nor with an unknown (companion), nor alone, nor with Sudras.

verses.text:
हीन.अङ्गान् अतिरिक्त.अङ्गान् विद्या.हीनान् वयो.ऽधिकान् । ४.१४१अव्/ म्: 
                                    वयोऽतिगान्
रूप.द्रविण.हीनांश् च जाति.हीनांश् च न-आक्षिपेत् ॥ १४१ ॥
                                    ४.१४१च्व्/ म्: 
                                    रूपद्रव्य.हीनांश् च ॥ 4.141 ॥
verses.english: Let him not insult those who have redundant limbs or are deficient in limbs, nor those destitute of knowledge, nor very aged men, nor those who have no beauty or wealth, nor those who are of low birth.

verses.text:
न स्पृशेत् पाणिना-उच्छिष्टो विप्रो गो.ब्राह्मण.अनलाण् ।
न च-अपि पश्येद् अशुचिः सुस्थो ज्योतिर्गणान् दिवा ॥ १४२ ॥
                                    ४.१४२च्व्/ म्: 
                                    स्वस्थो ज्योतिर्गणान् दिवि ॥ 4.142 ॥
verses.english: A Brahmana who is impure must not touch with his hand a cow, a Brahmana, or fire; nor, being in good health, let him look at the luminaries in the sky, while he is impure.

verses.text:
स्पृष्ट्वा-एतान् अशुचिर् नित्यम् अद्भिः प्राणान् उपस्पृशेत् ।
गात्राणि च-एव सर्वाणि नाभिं पाणितलेन तु ॥ १४३ ॥
verses.english: If he has touched these, while impure, let him always sprinkle with his hand water on the organs of sensation, all his limbs, and the navel.

verses.text:
अन्.आतुरः स्वानि खानि न स्पृशेद् अनिमित्ततः ।
रोमाणि च रहस्यानि सर्वाण्य् एव विवर्जयेत् ॥ १४४ ॥
verses.english: Except when sick he must not touch the cavities (of the body) without a reason, and he must avoid (to touch) the hair on the secret (parts).

verses.text:
मङ्गल.आचारयुक्तः स्यात् प्रयत.आत्मा जित.इन्द्रियः ।
जपेच् च जुहुयाच् च-एव नित्यम् अग्निम् अतन्द्रितः ॥ १४५
                                ॥
verses.english: Let him eagerly follow the (customs which are) auspicious and the rule of good conduct, be careful of purity, and control all his organs, let him mutter (prayers) and, untired, daily offer oblations in the fire.

verses.text:
मङ्गल.आचारयुक्तानां नित्यं च प्रयत.आत्मनाम् ।
जपतां जुह्वतां च-एव विनिपातो न विद्यते ॥ १४६ ॥
verses.english: No calamity happens to those who eagerly follow auspicious customs and the rule of good conduct, to those who are always careful of purity, and to those who mutter (sacred texts) and offer burnt-oblations.

verses.text:
वेदम् एव-अभ्यसेन् नित्यं यथाकालम् अतन्द्रितः । ४.१४७अव्/ म्: वेदम्
                                    एव जपेन्
तं ह्य् अस्य-आहुः परं धर्मम् उपधर्मो ऽन्य उच्यते ॥ १४७
                                ॥
verses.english: Let him, without tiring, daily mutter the Veda at the proper time; for they declare that to be one's highest duty; (all) other (observances) are called secondary duties.

verses.text:
वेदाभ्यासेन सततं शौचेन तपसा-एव च ।
अद्रोहेण च भूतानां जातिं स्मरति पौर्विकीम् ॥ १४८ ॥
verses.english: By daily reciting the Veda, by (the observance of the rules of) purification, by (practising) austerities, and by doing no injury to created beings, one (obtains the faculty of) remembering former births.

verses.text:
पौर्विकीं संस्मरन् जातिं ब्रह्म-एव-अभ्यस्यते पुनः ।
                                    ४.१४९अव्/ म्: 
                                    द्विजः
ब्रह्माभ्यासेन च-अजस्रम् अनन्तं सुखम् अश्नुते ॥ १४९
                                ॥
verses.english: He who, recollecting his former existences, again recites the Veda, gains endless bliss by the continual study of the Veda.

verses.text:
सावित्रान्-शान्तिहोमांश् च कुर्यात् पर्वसु नित्यशः । ४.१५०अव्/ म्: 
                                    सावित्रान् शान्तिहोमांश्
पितॄंश् च-एव-अष्टकास्व् अर्चेन् नित्यम् अन्वष्टकासु च ॥ १५०
                                ॥
verses.english: Let him always offer on the Parva-days oblations to Savitri and such as avert evil omens, and on the Ashtakas and Anvashtakas let him constantly worship the manes.

verses.text:
दूराद् आवसथान् मूत्रं दूरात् पादावसेचनम् ।
उच्छिष्तान्न.निषेकं च दूराद् एव समाचरेत् ॥ १५१ ॥
verses.english: Far from his dwelling let him remove urine (and ordure), far (let him remove) the water used for washing his feet, and far the remnants of food and the water from his bath.

verses.text:
मैत्रं प्रसाधनं स्नानं दन्तधावनम् अञ्जनम् ।
पूर्वाह्ण एव कुर्वीत देवतानां च पूजनम् ॥ १५२ ॥
verses.english: Early in the morning only let him void faeces, decorate (his body), bathe, clean his teeth, apply collyrium to his eyes, and worship the gods.

verses.text:
दैवतान्य् अभिगच्छेत् तु धार्मिकांश् च द्विजोत्तमान् ।
ईश्वरं च-एव रक्षार्थं गुरून् एव च पर्वसु ॥ १५३ ॥
verses.english: But on the Parva-days let him go to visit the (images of the) gods, and virtuous Brahmanas, and the ruler (of the country), for the sake of protection, as well as his Gurus.

verses.text:
अभिवादयेद् वृद्धांश् च दद्याच् च-एव-आसनं स्वकम् ।
कृत.अञ्जलिर् उपासीत गच्छतः पृष्ठतो ऽन्वियात् ॥ १५४
                                ॥
verses.english: Let him reverentially salute venerable men (who visit him), give them his own seat, let him sit near them with joined hands and, when they leave, (accompany them), walking behind them.

verses.text:
श्रुति.स्मृति.उदितं सम्यङ् निबद्धं स्वेषु कर्मसु ।
धर्ममूलं निषेवेत सद्.आचारम् अतन्द्रितः ॥ १५५ ॥
verses.english: Let him, untired, follow the conduct of virtuous men, connected with his occupations, which has been fully declared in the revealed texts and in the sacred tradition (Smriti) and is the root of the sacred law.

verses.text:
आचारात्-लभते ह्य् आयुर् आचाराद् ईप्सिताः प्रजाः ।
आचाराद् धनम् अक्षय्यम् आचारो हन्त्य् अलक्षणम् ॥ १५६ ॥
verses.english: Through virtuous conduct he obtains long life, through virtuous conduct desirable offspring, through virtuous conduct imperishable wealth; virtuous conduct destroys (the effect of) inauspicious marks.

verses.text:
दुर्.आचारो हि पुरुषो लोके भवति निन्दितः ।
दुःखभागी च सततं व्याधितो ऽल्प.आयुर् एव च ॥ १५७
                                ॥
verses.english: For a man of bad conduct is blamed among people, constantly suffers misfortunes, is afflicted with diseases, and short-lived.

verses.text:
सर्वलक्षण.हीनो ऽपि यः सदाचारवान् नरः ।
श्रद्दधानो ऽन्.असूयश् च शतं वर्षाणि जीवति ॥ १५८ ॥
verses.english: A man who follows the conduct of the virtuous, has faith and is free from envy, lives a hundred years, though he be entirely destitute of auspicious marks.

verses.text:
यद् यत् परवशं कर्म तत् तद् यत्नेन वर्जयेत् ।
यद् यद् आत्मवशं तु स्यात् तत् तत् सेवेत यत्नतः ॥ १५९
                                ॥
verses.english: Let him carefully avoid all undertakings (the success of) which depends on others; but let him eagerly pursue that (the accomplishment of) which depends on himself.

verses.text:
सर्वं परवशं दुःखं सर्वम् आत्मवशं सुखम् ।
एतद् विद्यात् समासेन लक्षणं सुख.दुःखयोः ॥ १६० ॥
verses.english: Everything that depends on others (gives) pain, everything that depends on oneself (gives) pleasure; know that this is the short definition of pleasure and pain.

verses.text:
यत् कर्म कुर्वतो ऽस्य स्यात् परितोषो ऽन्तरात्मनः ।
तत् प्रयत्नेन कुर्वीत विपरीतं तु वर्जयेत् ॥ १६१ ॥
verses.english: When the performance of an act gladdens his heart, let him perform it with diligence; but let him avoid the opposite.

verses.text:
आचार्यं च प्रवक्तारं पितरं मातरं गुरुम् ।
न हिंस्याद् ब्राह्मणान् गाश् च सर्वांश् च-एव तपस्विनः ॥ १६२
                                ॥
verses.english: Let him never offend the teacher who initiated him, nor him who explained the Veda, nor his father and mother, nor (any other) Guru, nor cows, nor Brahmanas, nor any men performing austerities.

verses.text:
नास्तिक्यं वेदनिन्दां च देवतानां च कुत्सनम् ।
द्वेषं दम्भं च मानं च क्रोधं तैक्ष्ण्यं च वर्जयेत् ॥
                                १६३ ॥ ४.१६३च्व्/
                                    म्: द्वेषं स्तम्भं च ॥ 4.163 ॥
verses.english: Let him avoid atheism, cavilling at the Vedas, contempt of the gods, hatred, want of modesty, pride, anger, and harshness.

verses.text:
परस्य दण्डं न-उद्यच्छेत् क्रुद्धो न-एनं निपातयेत् ।
अन्यत्र पुत्रात्-शिष्याद् वा शिष्टि.अर्थं ताडयेत् तु तौ ॥ १६४
                                ॥
verses.english: Let him, when angry, not raise a stick against another man, nor strike (anybody) except a son or a pupil; those two he may beat in order to correct them.

verses.text:
ब्राह्मणाय-अवगुर्य-एव द्विजातिर् वधकाम्यया ।
शतं वर्षाणि तामिस्रे नरके परिवर्तते ॥ १६५ ॥
verses.english: A twice-born man who has merely threatened a Brahmana with the intention of (doing him) a corporal injury, will wander about for a hundred years in the Tamisra hell.

verses.text:
ताडयित्वा तृणेन-अपि संरम्भात्-मतिपूर्वकम् ।
एकविंशतीम् आजातीः पापयोनिषु जायते ॥ १६६ ॥
verses.english: Having intentionally struck him in anger, even with a blade of grass, he will be born during twenty-one existences in the wombs (of such beings where men are born in punishment of their) sins.

verses.text:
अयुध्यमानस्य-उत्पाद्य ब्राह्मणस्य-असृग् अङ्गतः ।
दुःखं सुमहद् आप्नोति प्रेत्य-अप्राज्ञतया नरः ॥ १६७
                                ॥
verses.english: A man who in his folly caused blood to flow from the body of a Brahmana who does not attack him, will suffer after death exceedingly great pain.

verses.text:
शोणितं यावतः पांसून् सङ्गृह्णाति महीतलात् ।
तावतो ऽब्दान् अमुत्र-अन्यैः शोणित.उत्पादको ऽद्यते ॥ १६८
                                ॥
verses.english: As many particles of dust as the blood takes up from the ground, during so many years the spiller of the blood will be devoured by other (animals) in the next world.

verses.text:
न कदा चिद् द्विजे तस्माद् विद्वान् अवगुरेद् अपि ।
न ताडयेत् तृणेन-अपि न गात्रात् स्रावयेद् असृक् ॥ १६९ ॥
verses.english: A wise man should therefore never threaten a Brahmana, nor strike him even with a blade of grass, nor cause his blood to flow.

verses.text:
अ.धार्मिको नरो यो हि यस्य च-अप्य् अनृतं धनम् ।
हिंसारतश् च यो नित्यं न-इह-असौ सुखम् एधते ॥ १७० ॥
                                    ४.१७०च्व्/ म्: 
                                    हिंसारतिश् ॥ 4.170 ॥
verses.english: Neither a man who (lives) unrighteously, nor he who (acquires) wealth (by telling) falsehoods, nor he who always delights in doing injury, ever attain happiness in this world.

verses.text:
न सीदन्न् अपि धर्मेण मनो ऽधर्मे निवेशयेत् ।
अ.धार्मिकानां पापानाम् आशु पश्यन् विपर्ययम् ॥ १७१ ॥
verses.english: Let him, though suffering in consequence of his righteousness, never turn his heart to unrighteousness; for he will see the speedy overthrow of unrighteous, wicked men.

verses.text:
न-अधर्मश् चरितो लोके सद्यः फलति गौर् इव ।
शनैर् आवर्त्यमानस् तु कर्तुर् मूलानि कृन्तति ॥ १७२ ॥
verses.english: Unrighteousness, practised in this world, does not at once produce its fruit, like a cow; but, advancing slowly, it cuts off the roots of him who committed it.

verses.text:
यदि न-आत्मनि पुत्रेषु न चेत् पुत्रेषु नप्तृषु ।
न त्व् एव तु कृतो ऽधर्मः कर्तुर् भवति निष्.फलः ॥ १७३
                                ॥ ४.१७३च्व्/ म्: 
                                    कृतो धर्मः? ॥ 4.173 ॥
verses.english: If (the punishment falls) not on (the offender) himself, (it falls) on his sons, if not on the sons, (at least) on his grandsons; but an iniquity (once) committed, never fails to produce fruit to him who wrought it.

verses.text:
अधर्मेण-एधते तावत् ततो भद्राणि पश्यति ।
ततः सपत्नान् जयति स.मूलस् तु विनश्यति ॥ १७४ ॥
verses.english: He prospers for a while through unrighteousness, then he gains great good fortune, next he conquers his enemies, but (at last) he perishes (branch and) root.

verses.text:
सत्य.धर्म.आर्यवृत्तेषु शौचे च-एव-आरमेत् सदा ।
शिष्यांश् च शिष्याद् धर्मेण वाच्.बाहु.उदर.संयतः ॥ १७५
                                ॥
verses.english: Let him always delight in truthfulness, (obedience to) the sacred law, conduct worthy of an Aryan, and purity; let him chastise his pupils according to the sacred law; let him keep his speech, his arms, and his belly under control.

verses.text:
परित्यजेद् अर्थ.कामौ यौ स्यातां धर्मवर्जितौ ।
धर्मं च-अप्य् असुख.उदर्कं लोकसङ्क्रुष्टम् एव च ॥ १७६
                                ॥
verses.english: Let him avoid (the acquisition of) wealth and (the gratification of his) desires, if they are opposed to the sacred law, and even lawful acts which may cause pain in the future or are offensive to men.

verses.text:
न पाणि.पाद.चपलो न नेत्र.चपलो ऽन्.ऋजुः ।
न स्याद् वाक्.चपलश् च-एव न परद्रोहकर्म.धीः ॥ १७७
                                ॥
verses.english: Let him not be uselessly active with his hands and feet, or with his eyes, nor crooked (in his ways), nor talk idly, nor injure others by deeds or even think of it.

verses.text:
येन-अस्य पितरो याता येन याताः पितामहाः ।
तेन यायात् सतां मार्गं तेन गच्छन् न रिष्यति ॥ १७८
                                ॥
verses.english: Let him walk in that path of holy men which his fathers and his grandfathers followed; while he walks in that, he will not suffer harm.

verses.text:
ऋत्विक्.पुरोहित.आचार्यैर् मातुल.अतिथिसंश्रितैः ।
बाल.वृद्ध.आतुरैर् वैद्यैर् ज्ञाति.सम्बन्धि.बान्धवैः ॥
                                १७९ ॥
verses.english: With an officiating or a domestic priest, with a teacher, with a maternal uncle, a guest and a dependant, with infants, aged and sick men, with learned men, with his paternal relatives, connexions by marriage and maternal relatives,

verses.text:
माता.पितृभ्यां जामीभिर् भ्रात्रा पुत्रेण भार्यया ।
दुहित्रा दासवर्गेण विवादं न समाचरेत् ॥ १८० ॥
verses.english: With his father and his mother, with female relatives, with a brother, with his son and his wife, with his daughter and with his slaves, let him not have quarrels.

verses.text:
एतैर् विवादान् सन्त्यज्य सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते ।
एतैर् जितैश् च जयति सर्वान्-लोकान् इमान् गृही ॥ १८१ ॥
verses.english: If he avoids quarrels with these persons, he will be freed from all sins, and by suppressing (all) such (quarrels) a householder conquers all the following worlds.

verses.text:
आचार्यो ब्रह्मलोक.ईशः प्राजापत्ये पिता प्रभुः ।
अतिथिस् त्व् इन्द्रलोक.ईशो देवलोकस्य च-ऋत्विजः ॥ १८२
                                ॥
verses.english: The teacher is the lord of the world of Brahman, the father has power over the world of the Lord of created beings (Pragapati), a guest rules over the world of Indra, and the priests over the world of the gods.

verses.text:
जामयो ऽप्सरसाम् लोके वैश्वदेवस्य बान्धवाः ।
सम्बन्धिनो ह्य् अपां लोके पृथिव्यां मातृ.मातुलौ ॥ १८३
                                ॥
verses.english: The female relatives (have power) over the world of the Apsarases, the maternal relatives over that of the Visve Devas, the connexions by marriage over that of the waters, the mother and the maternal uncle over the earth.

verses.text:
आकाश.ईशास् तु विज्ञेया बाल.वृद्ध.कृश.आतुराः ।
भ्राता ज्येष्ठः समः पित्रा भार्या पुत्रः स्वका तनुः ॥ १८४
                                ॥
verses.english: Infants, aged, poor and sick men must be considered as rulers of the middle sphere, the eldest brother as equal to one's father, one's wife and one's son as one's own body,

verses.text:
छाया स्वो दासवर्गश् च दुहिता कृपणं परम् ।
तस्माद् एतैर् अधिक्षिप्तः सहेत-अ.सञ्ज्वरः सदा ॥ १८५
                                ॥
verses.english: One's slaves as one's shadow, one's daughter as the highest object of tenderness; hence if one is offended by (any one of) these, one must bear it without resentment.

verses.text:
प्रतिग्रहसमर्थो ऽपि प्रसङ्गं तत्र वर्जयेत् ।
प्रतिग्रहेण ह्य् अस्य-आशु ब्राह्मं तेजः प्रशाम्यति ॥ १८६
                                ॥
verses.english: Though (by his learning and sanctity) he may be entitled to accept presents, let him not attach himself (too much) to that (habit); for through his accepting (many) presents the divine light in him is soon extinguished.

verses.text:
न द्रव्याणाम् अ.विज्ञाय विधिं धर्म्यं प्रतिग्रहे ।
प्राज्ञः प्रतिग्रहं कुर्याद् अवसीदन्न् अपि क्षुधा ॥ १८७
                                ॥
verses.english: Without a full knowledge of the rules, prescribed by the sacred law for the acceptance of presents, a wise man should not take anything, even though he may pine with hunger.

verses.text:
हिरण्यं भूमिम् अश्वं गाम् अन्नं वासस् तिलान् घृतम् ।
प्रतिगृह्णन्न् अ.विद्वांस् तु भस्मी.भवति दारुवत् ॥ १८८
                                ॥
verses.english: But an ignorant (man) who accepts gold, land, a horse, a cow, food, a dress, sesamum-grains, (or) clarified butter, is reduced to ashes like (a piece of) wood.

verses.text:
हिरण्यम् आयुर् अन्नं च भूर् गौश् च-अप्य् ओषतस् तनुम् ।
अश्वश् चक्षुस् त्वचं वासो घृतं तेजस् तिलाह् प्रजाः ॥ १८९
                                ॥
verses.english: Gold and food destroy his longevity, land and a cow his body, a horse his eye (sight), a garment his skin, clarified butter his energy, sesamum-grains his offspring.

verses.text:
अ.तपास् त्व् अन्.अधीयानः प्रतिग्रह.रुचिर् द्विजः ।
अम्भस्य् अश्मप्लवेन-इव सह तेन-एव मज्जति ॥ १९० ॥
verses.english: A Brahmana who neither performs austerities nor studies the Veda, yet delights in accepting gifts, sinks with the (donor into hell), just as (he who attempts to cross over in) a boat made of stone (is submerged) in the water.

verses.text:
तस्माद् अ.विद्वान् बिभियाद् यस्मात् तस्मात् प्रतिग्रहात् ।
स्वल्पकेन-अप्य् अ.विद्वान् हि पङ्के गौर् इव सीदति ॥ १९१
                                ॥
verses.english: Hence an ignorant (man) should be afraid of accepting any presents; for by reason of a very small (gift) even a fool sinks (into hell) as a cow into a morass.

verses.text:
न वार्य् अपि प्रयच्छेत् तु बैडालव्रतिके द्विजे ।
न बकव्रतिके पापे न-अ.वेदविदि धर्मवित् ॥ १९२ ॥
verses.english: (A man) who knows the law should not offer even water to a Brahmana who acts like a cat, nor to a Brahmana who acts like a heron, nor to one who is unacquainted with the Veda.

verses.text:
त्रिष्व् अप्य् एतेषु दत्तं हि विधिना-अप्य् अर्जितं धनम् ।
दातुर् भवत्य् अनर्थाय परत्र-आदातुर् एव च ॥ १९३ ॥
verses.english: For property, though earned in accordance with prescribed rules, which is given to these three (persons), causes in the next world misery both to the giver and to the recipient.

verses.text:
यथा प्लवेन-औपलेन निमज्जत्य् उदके तरन् ।
तथा निमज्जतो ऽधस्ताद् अज्ञौ दातृ.प्रतीच्छकौ ॥ १९४
                                ॥
verses.english: As he who (attempts to) cross water in a boat of stone sinks (to the bottom), even so an ignorant donor and an ignorant donee sink low.

verses.text:
धर्मध्वजी सदा लुब्धश् छाद्मिको लोकदम्भकः । ।
बैडालव्रतिको ज्ञेयो हिंस्रः सर्वाभिसन्धकः ॥ १९५ ॥
verses.english: (A man) who, ever covetous, displays the flag of virtue, (who is) a hypocrite, a deceiver of the people, intent on doing injury, (and) a detractor (from the merits) of all men, one must know to be one who acts like a cat.

verses.text:
[१९७म] अधो.दृष्टिर् नैष्कृतिकः स्वार्थसाधन.तत्परः ।
[१९७म्च्] शठो मिथ्याविनीतश् च बकव्रतचरो द्विजः ॥ १९६
                                ॥
verses.english: That Brahmana, who with downcast look, of a cruel disposition, is solely intent on attaining his own ends, dishonest and falsely gentle, is one who acts like a heron.

verses.text:
[१९८म] ये बकव्रतिनो विप्रा ये च मार्जारलिङ्गिनः ।
[१९८म्च्] ते पतन्त्य् अन्धतामिस्रे तेन पापेन कर्मणा ॥ १९७
                                ॥
verses.english: Those Brahmanas who act like herons, and those who display the characteristics of cats, fall in consequence of that wicked mode of acting into (the hell called) Andhatamisra.

verses.text:
[१९९म] न धर्मस्य-अपदेशेन पापं कृत्वा व्रतं चरेत् ।
[१९९म्च्] व्रतेन पापं प्रच्छाद्य कुर्वन् स्त्री.शूद्र.दम्भनम्
                                ॥ १९८ ॥
verses.english: When he has committed a sin, let him not perform a penance under the pretence (that the act is intended to gain) spiritual merit, (thus) hiding his sin under (the pretext of) a vow and deceiving women and Sudras.

verses.text:
[२००म] प्रेत्य-इह च-ईदृशा विप्रा गर्ह्यन्ते ब्रह्मवादिभिः
                                ।
[२००म्च्] छद्मना चरितं यच् च व्रतं रक्षांसि गच्छति ॥
                                १९९ ॥
verses.english: Such Brahmanas are reprehended after death and in this (life) by those who expound the Veda, and a vow, performed under a false pretence, goes to the Rakshasas.

verses.text:
[२०१म] अलिङ्गी लिङ्गिवेषेण यो वृत्तिम् उपजीवति ।
[२०१म्च्] स लिङ्गिनां हरत्य् एनस् तिर्यग्योनौ च जायते ॥ २००
                                ॥
verses.english: He who, without being a student, gains his livelihood by (wearing) the dress of a student, takes upon himself the guilt of (all) students and is born again in the womb of an animal.

verses.text:
[२०२म] परकीयनिपानेषु न स्नायाद्द् हि कदा चन । ४.२०१अ[२०२म]व्/ क्:
                                    स्नायाच् च कदा चन
[२०२म्च्] निपानकर्तुः स्नात्वा तु दुष्कृतांशेन लिप्यते ॥ २०१
                                ॥
verses.english: Let him never bathe in tanks belonging to other men; if he bathes (in such a one), he is tainted by a portion of the guilt of him who made the tank.

verses.text:
[२०३म] यान.शय्या.आसनान्य् अस्य कूप.उद्यान.गृहाणि च ।
[२०३म्च्] अ.दत्तान्य् उपयुञ्जान एनसः स्यात् तुरीय.भाक् ॥ २०२
                                ॥
verses.english: He who uses without permission a carriage, a bed, a seat, a well, a garden or a house belonging to an (other man), takes upon himself one fourth of (the owner's) guilt.

verses.text:
[२०४म] नदीषु देवखातेषु तडागेषु सरःसु च ।
[२०४म्च्] स्नानं समाचरेन् नित्यं गर्त.प्रस्रवणेषु च ॥ २०३
                                ॥
verses.english: Let him always bathe in rivers, in ponds, dug by the gods (themselves), in lakes, and in waterholes or springs.

verses.text:
[२०५म] यमान् सेवेत सततं न नित्यं नियमान् बुधः ।
[२०५म्च्] यमान् पतत्य् अ.कुर्वाणो नियमान् केवलान् भजन् ॥ २०४
                                ॥
verses.english: A wise man should constantly discharge the paramount duties (called yama), but not always the minor ones (called niyama); for he who does not discharge the former, while he obeys the latter alone, becomes an outcast.

verses.text:
[२०६म] न-अश्रोत्रियतते यज्ञे ग्रामयाजिकृते तथा ।
[२०६म्च्] स्त्रिया क्लीबेन च हुते भुञ्जीत ब्राह्मणः क्व चित् ॥
                                २०५ ॥
verses.english: A Brahmana must never eat (a dinner given) at a sacrifice that is offered by one who is not a Srotriya, by one who sacrifices for a multitude of men, by a woman, or by a eunuch.

verses.text:
[२०७म] अश्लीकम् एतत् साधूनां यत्र जुह्वत्य् अमी हविः । ४.२०६अ[२०७म]व्/ म्: 
                                    अ.श्लीलम्
[२०७म्च्] प्रतीपम् एतद् देवानां तस्मात् तत् परिवर्जयेत् ॥ २०६
                                ॥
verses.english: When those persons offer sacrificial viands in the fire, it is unlucky for holy (men) it displeases the gods; let him therefore avoid it.

verses.text:
[२०८म] मत्त.क्रुद्ध.आतुराणां च न भुञ्जीत कदा चन ।
[२०८म्च्] केश.कीटावपन्नं च पदा स्पृष्टं च कामतः ॥ २०७
                                ॥
verses.english: Let him never eat (food given) by intoxicated, angry, or sick (men), nor that in which hair or insects are found, nor what has been touched intentionally with the foot,

verses.text:
[२०९म] भ्रूणघ्न.अवेक्षितं च-एव संस्पृष्टं च-अप्य्
                                उदक्यया ।
[२०९म्च्] पतत्रिण.अवलीढं च शुना संस्पृष्टम् एव च ॥ २०८
                                ॥
verses.english: Nor that at which the slayer of a learned Brahmana has looked, nor that which has been touched by a menstruating woman, nor that which has been pecked at by birds or touched by a dog,

verses.text:
[२१०म] गवा च-अन्नम् उपघ्रातं घुष्टान्नं च विशेषतः
                                ।
[२१०म्च्] गणान्नं गणिकान्नं च विदुषा च जुगुप्सितम् ॥ २०९
                                ॥
verses.english: Nor food at which a cow has smelt, nor particularly that which has been offered by an invitation to all comers, nor that (given) by a multitude or by harlots, nor that which is declared to be had by a learned (man),

verses.text:
[२११म] स्तेन.गायनयोश् च-अन्नं तक्ष्णो वार्धुषिकस्य च
                                ।
[२११म्च्] दीक्षितस्य कदर्यस्य बद्धस्य निगडस्य च ॥ २१०
                                ॥
verses.english: Nor the food (given) by a thief, a musician, a carpenter, a usurer, one who has been initiated (for the performance of a Srauta sacrifice), a miser, one bound with fetters,

verses.text:
[२१२म] अभिशस्तस्य षण्ढस्य पुंश्चल्या दाम्भिकस्य च ।
[२१२म्च्] शुक्तं पर्युषितं च-एव शूद्रस्य-उच्छिष्टम् एव च ॥
                                २११ ॥
verses.english: By one accused of a mortal sin (Abhisasta), a hermaphrodite, an unchaste woman, or a hypocrite, nor (any sweet thing) that has turned sour, nor what has been kept a whole night, nor (the food) of a Sudra, nor the leavings (of another man),

verses.text:
[२१३म] चिकित्सकस्य मृगयोः क्रूरस्य-उच्छिष्ट.भोजिनः ।
[२१३म्च्] उग्रान्नं सूतिकान्नं च पर्याचान्तम् अ.निर्दशम् ॥ २१२
                                ॥
verses.english: Nor (the food given) by a physician, a hunter, a cruel man, one who eats the fragments (of another's meal), nor the food of an Ugra, nor that prepared for a woman in childbed, nor that (given at a dinner) where (a guest rises) prematurely (and) sips water, nor that (given by a woman) whose ten days of impurity have not elapsed,

verses.text:
[२१४म] अन्.अर्चितं वृथामांसम् अ.वीरायाश् च योषितः ।
[२१४म्च्] द्विषदन्नं नगरी.अन्नं पतितान्नम् अवक्षुतम् ॥ २१३
                                ॥
verses.english: Nor (food) given without due respect, nor (that which contains) meat eaten for no sacred purpose, nor (that given) by a female who has no male (relatives), nor the food of an enemy, nor that (given) by the lord of a town, nor that (given) by outcasts, nor that on which anybody has sneezed;

verses.text:
[२१५म] पिशुन.अनृतिनोश् च-अन्नं क्रतुविक्रयिणस् तथा ।
                                    ४.२१४अ[२१५म]व्/ म्: क्रतुविक्रयकस्य च
[२१५म्च्] शैलूष.तुन्नवाय.अन्नं कृतघ्नस्य-अन्नम् एव च ॥
                                २१४ ॥
verses.english: Nor the food (given) by an informer, by one who habitually tells falsehoods, or by one who sells (the rewards for) sacrifices, nor the food (given) by an actor, a tailor, or an ungrateful (man),

verses.text:
[२१६म] कर्मारस्य निषादस्य रङ्गावतारकस्य च ।
[२१६म्च्] सुवर्णकर्तुर् वेणस्य शस्त्रविक्रयिणस् तथा ॥ २१५
                                ॥
verses.english: By a blacksmith, a Nishada, a stage-player, a goldsmith, a basket-maker, or a dealer in weapons,

verses.text:
[२१७म] श्ववतां शौण्डिकानां च चैल.निर्णेजकस्य च ।
[२१७म्च्] रञ्जकस्य नृशंसस्य यस्य च-उपपतिर् गृहे ॥ २१६
                                ॥ ४.२१६च्[२१७म्च्]व्/ म्: रजकस्य ॥ 4.216 ॥
verses.english: By trainers of hunting dogs, publicans, a washerman, a dyer, a pitiless (man), and a man in whose house (lives) a paramour (of his wife),

verses.text:
[२१८म] मृष्यन्ति ये च-उपपतिं स्त्रीजितानाम् च सर्वशः ।
[२१८म्च्] अ.निर्दशं च प्रेतान्नम् अ.तुष्टिकरम् एव च ॥ २१७
                                ॥
verses.english: Nor (the food given) by those who knowingly bear with paramours (of their wives), and by those who in all matters are ruled by women, nor food (given by men) whose ten days of impurity on account of a death have not passed, nor that which is unpalatable.

verses.text:
[२१९म] राजान्नं तेज आदत्ते शूद्रान्नं ब्रह्मवर्चसम् ।
[२१९म्च्] आयुः सुवर्णकारान्नं यशश् चर्मावकर्तिनः ॥ २१८
                                ॥
verses.english: The food of a king impairs his vigour, the food of a Sudra his excellence in sacred learning, the food of a goldsmith his longevity, that of a leather-cutter his fame;

verses.text:
[२२०म] कारुकान्नं प्रजां हन्ति बलं निर्णेजकस्य च ।
[२२०म्च्] गणान्नं गणिकान्नं च लोकेभ्यः परिकृन्तति ॥ २१९
                                ॥
verses.english: The food of an artisan destroys his offspring, that of a washerman his (bodily) strength; the food of a multitude and of harlots excludes him from (the higher) worlds.

verses.text:
[२२१म] पूयं चिकित्सकस्य-अन्नं पुंश्चल्यास् त्व् अन्नम् इन्द्रियम्
                                ।
[२२१म्च्] विष्ठा वार्धुषिकस्य-अन्नं शस्त्रविक्रयिणो मलम् ॥
                                २२० ॥
verses.english: The food of a physician (is as vile as) pus, that of an unchaste woman (equal to) semen, that of a usurer (as vile as) ordure, and that of a dealer in weapons (as bad as) dirt.

verses.text:
[२२२म] य एते ऽन्ये त्व् अभोज्य.अन्नाः क्रमशः परिकीर्तिताः
                                ।
[२२२म्च्] तेषां त्वग्.अस्थि.रोमाणि वदन्त्य् अन्नं मनीषिणः ॥
                                २२१ ॥
verses.english: The food of those other persons who have been successively enumerated as such whose food must not be eaten, the wise declare (to be as impure as) skin, bones, and hair.

verses.text:
[२२३म] भुक्त्वा-अतो ऽन्यतम् अस्य-अन्नम् अमत्या क्षपणं
                                त्र्यहम् ।
[२२३म्च्] मत्या भुक्त्वा-आचरेत् कृच्छ्रं रेतस्.विष्.मूत्रम् एव च
                                ॥ २२२ ॥
verses.english: If he has unwittingly eaten the food of one of those, (he must) fast for three days; if he has eaten it intentionally, or (has swallowed) semen, ordure, or urine, he must perform a Krikkhra penance.

verses.text:
[२२४म] न-अद्यात्-शूद्रस्य पक्वान्नं विद्वान् अ.श्राद्धिनो द्विजः
                                ।
[२२४म्च्] आददीत-आमम् एव-अस्माद् अवृत्ताव् एकरात्रिकम् ॥ २२३
                                ॥
verses.english: A Brahmana who knows (the law) must not eat cooked food (given) by a Sudra who performs no Sraddhas; but, on failure of (other) means of subsistence, he may accept raw (grain), sufficient for one night (and day).

verses.text:
[२२५म] श्रोत्रियस्य कदर्यस्य वदान्यस्य च वार्धुषेः ।
[२२५म्च्] मीमांसित्वा-उभयं देवाः समम् अन्नम् अकल्पयन् ॥ २२४
                                ॥
verses.english: The gods, having considered (the respective merits) of a niggardly Srotriya and of a liberal usurer, declared the food of both to be equal (in quality).

verses.text:
[२२६म] तान् प्रजापतिर् आह-एत्य मा कृध्वं विषमं समम्
                                ।
[२२६म्च्] श्रद्धापूतं वदान्यस्य हतम् अ.श्रद्धया-इतरत् ॥
                                २२५ ॥
verses.english: The Lord of created beings (Pragapati) came and spake to them, 'Do not make that equal, which is unequal. The food of that liberal (usurer) is purified by faith; (that of the) of the) other (man) is defiled by a want of faith.'

verses.text:
[२२७म] श्रद्धया-इष्टं च पूर्तं च नित्यं कुर्याद् अतन्द्रितः
                                ।
[२२७म्च्] श्रद्धाकृते ह्य् अक्षये ते भवतः स्वागतैर् धनैः
                                ॥ २२६ ॥
verses.english: Let him, without tiring, always offer sacrifices and perform works of charity with faith; for offerings and charitable works made with faith and with lawfully-earned money, (procure) endless rewards.

verses.text:
[२२८म] दानधर्मं निषेवेत नित्यम् ऐष्टिक.पौर्तिकम् ।
[२२८म्च्] परितुष्टेन भावेन पात्रम् आसाद्य शक्तितः ॥ २२७
                                ॥
verses.english: Let him always practise, according to his ability, with a cheerful heart, the duty of liberality, both by sacrifices and by charitable works, if he finds a worthy recipient (for his gifts.)

verses.text:
[२२९म] यत् किं चिद् अपि दातव्यं याचितेन-अन्.असूयया । ४.२२८अ[२२९म]व्/ म्: 
                                    अनसूयता?
[२२९म्च्] उत्पत्स्यते हि तत् पात्रं यत् तारयति सर्वतः ॥ २२८
                                ॥
verses.english: If he is asked, let him always give something, be it ever so little, without grudging; for a worthy recipient will (perhaps) be found who saves him from all (guilt).

verses.text:
[२३०म] वारिदस् तृप्तिम् आप्नोति सुखम् अक्षय्यम् अन्नदः । ४.२२९अ[२३०म]व्/ म्: 
                                    अक्षयम्
[२३०म्च्] तिलप्रदः प्रजाम् इष्टां दीपदश् चक्षुर् उत्तमम् ॥ २२९
                                ॥
verses.english: A giver of water obtains the satisfaction (of his hunger and thirst), a giver of food imperishable happiness, a giver of sesamum desirable offspring, a giver of a lamp a most excellent eyesight.

verses.text:
[२३१म] भूमिदो भूमिम् आप्नोति दीर्घम् आयुर् हिरण्यदः ।
[२३१म्च्] गृहदो ऽग्र्याणि वेश्मानि रूप्यदो रूपम् उत्तमम् ॥ २३०
                                ॥
verses.english: A giver of land obtains land, a giver of gold long life, a giver of a house most excellent mansions, a giver of silver (rupya) exquisite beauty (rupa),

verses.text:
[२३२म] वासोदश् चन्द्रसालोक्यम् अश्विसालोक्यम् अश्वदः ।
[२३२म्च्] अनडुहः श्रियं पुष्टां गोदो ब्रध्नस्य विष्टपम् ॥
                                २३१ ॥
verses.english: A giver of a garment a place in the world of the moon, a giver of a horse (asva) a place in the world of the Asvins, a giver of a draught-ox great good fortune, a giver of a cow the world of the sun;

verses.text:
[२३३म] यान.शय्याप्रदो भार्याम् ऐश्वर्यम् अभयप्रदः ।
[२३३म्च्] धान्यदः शाश्वतं सौख्यं ब्रह्मदो ब्रह्मसार्ष्टिताम्
                                ॥ २३२ ॥
verses.english: A giver of a carriage or of a bed a wife, a giver of protection supreme dominion, a giver of grain eternal bliss, a giver of the Veda (brahman) union with Brahman;

verses.text:
[२३४म] सर्वेषाम् एव दानानां ब्रह्मदानं विशिष्यते ।
[२३४म्च्] वारि.अन्न.गो.मही.वासस्.तिल.काञ्चन.सर्पिषाम् ॥ २३३
                                ॥
verses.english: The gift of the Veda surpasses all other gifts, water, food, cows, land, clothes, sesamum, gold, and clarified butter.

verses.text:
[२३५म] येन येन तु भावेन यद् यद् दानं प्रयच्छति ।
[२३५म्च्] तत् तत् तेन-एव भावेन प्राप्नोति प्रतिपूजितः ॥ २३४
                                ॥
verses.english: For whatever purpose (a man) bestows any gift, for that same purpose he receives (in his next birth) with due honour its (reward).

verses.text:
[२३६म] यो ऽर्चितं प्रतिगृह्णाति ददात्य् अर्चितम् एव वा ।
[२३६म्च्] ताव् उभौ गच्छतः स्वर्गं नरकं तु विपर्यये ॥
                                २३५ ॥
verses.english: Both he who respectfully receives (a gift), and he who respectfully bestows it, go to heaven; in the contrary case (they both fall) into hell.

verses.text:
[२३७म] न विस्मयेत तपसा वदेद् इष्ट्वा च न-अनृतम् ।
[२३७म्च्] न-आर्तो ऽप्य् अपवदेद् विप्रान् न दत्त्वा परिकीर्तयेत् ॥
                                २३६ ॥ ४.२३६च्[२३७म्च्]व्/ म्: दत्वा ॥ 4.236 ॥
verses.english: Let him not be proud of his austerities; let him not utter a falsehood after he has offered a sacrifice; let him not speak ill of Brahmanas, though he be tormented (by them); when he has bestowed (a gift), let him not boast of it.

verses.text:
[२३८म] यज्ञो ऽनृतेन क्षरति तपः क्षरति विस्मयात् ।
[२३८म्च्] आयुर् विप्रापवादेन दानं च परिकीर्तनात् ॥ २३७
                                ॥
verses.english: By falsehood a sacrifice becomes vain, by self-complacency (the reward for) austerities is lost, longevity by speaking evil of Brahmanas, and (the reward of) a gift by boasting.

verses.text:
[२३९म] धर्मं शनैः सञ्चिनुयाद् वल्मीकम् इव पुत्तिकाः ।
                                    ४.२३८अ[२३९म]व्/ म्: सञ्चिनुयाद्
[२३९म्च्] परलोकसहायार्थं सर्वभूतान्य् अ.पीडयन् ॥ २३८
                                ॥
verses.english: Giving no pain to any creature, let him slowly accumulate spiritual merit, for the sake (of acquiring) a companion to the next world, just as the white ant (gradually raises its) hill.

verses.text:
[२४०म] न-अमुत्र हि सहायार्थं पिता माता च तिष्ठतः ।
[२४०म्च्] न पुत्रदारं न ज्ञातिर् धर्मस् तिष्ठति केवलः ॥
                                २३९ ॥
verses.english: For in the next world neither father, nor mother, nor wife, nor sons, nor relations stay to be his companions; spiritual merit alone remains (with him).

verses.text:
[२४१म] एकः प्रजायते जन्तुर् एक एव प्रलीयते ।
[२४१म्च्] एको ऽनुभुङ्क्ते सुकृतम् एक एव च दुष्कृतम् ॥ २४०
                                ॥
verses.english: Single is each being born; single it dies; single it enjoys (the reward of its) virtue; single (it suffers the punishment of its) sin.

verses.text:
[२४२म] मृतं शरीरम् उत्सृज्य काष्ठ.लोष्टसमं क्षितौ ।
[२४२म्च्] विमुखा बान्धवा यान्ति धर्मस् तम् अनुगच्छति ॥ २४१
                                ॥
verses.english: Leaving the dead body on the ground like a log of wood, or a clod of earth, the relatives depart with averted faces; but spiritual merit follows the (soul).

verses.text:
[२४३म] तस्माद् धर्मं सहायार्थं नित्यं सञ्चिनुयात्- शनैः
                                ।
[२४३म्च्] धर्मेण हि सहायेन तमस् तरति दुस्तरम् ॥ २४२
                                ॥
verses.english: Let him therefore always slowly accumulate spiritual merit, in order (that it may be his) companion (after death); for with merit as his companion he will traverse a gloom difficult to traverse.

verses.text:
[२४४म] धर्म.प्रधानं पुरुषं तपसा हत.किल्बिषम् ।
[२४४म्च्] परलोकं नयत्य् आशु भास्वन्तं ख.शरीरिणम् ॥ २४३
                                ॥
verses.english: (That companion) speedily conducts the man who is devoted to duty and effaces his sins by austerities, to the next world, radiant and clothed with an ethereal body.

verses.text:
[२४५म] उत्तमैर् उत्तमैर् नित्यं सम्बन्धान् आचरेत् सह ।
                                    ४.२४४अ[२४५म]व्/ म्: सम्भन्धान्
[२४५म्च्] निनीषुः कुलम् उत्कर्षम् अधमान् अधमांस् त्यजेत् ॥ २४४
                                ॥
verses.english: Let him, who desires to raise his race, ever form connexions with the most excellent (men), and shun all low ones.

verses.text:
[२४६म] उत्तमान् उत्तमान् एव गच्छन् हीनांस् तु वर्जयन् ।
[२४६म्च्] ब्राह्मणः श्रेष्ठताम् एति प्रत्यवायेन शूद्रताम् ॥ २४५
                                ॥
verses.english: A Brahmana who always connects himself with the most excellent (ones), and shuns all inferior ones, (himself) becomes most distinguished; by an opposite conduct he becomes a Sudra.

verses.text:
[२४७म] दृढकारी मृदुर् दान्तः क्रूर.आचारैर् अ.संवसन् ।
[२४७म्च्] अहिंस्रो दम.दानाभ्यां जयेत् स्वर्गं तथा.व्रतः ॥
                                २४६ ॥
verses.english: He who is persevering, gentle, (and) patient, shuns the company of men of cruel conduct, and does no injury (to living creatures), gains, if he constantly lives in that manner, by controlling his organs and by liberality, heavenly bliss.

verses.text:
[२४८म] एध.उदकं मूल.फलम् अन्नम् अभ्युद्यतं च यत्
                                ।
[२४८म्च्] सर्वतः प्रतिगृह्णीयात्- मधु-अथ-अभयदक्षिणाम् ॥
                                २४७ ॥
verses.english: He may accept from any (man), fuel, water, roots, fruit, food offered without asking, and honey, likewise a gift (which consists in) a promise of protection.

verses.text:
[२४९म] आहृत.अभ्युद्यतां भिक्षां पुरस्ताद् अ.प्रचोदिताम् ।
[२४९म्च्] मेने प्रजापतिर् ग्राह्याम् अपि दुष्कृत.कर्मणः ॥ २४८
                                ॥
verses.english: The Lord of created beings (Pragapati) has declared that alms freely offered and brought (by the giver himself) may be accepted even from a sinful man, provided (the gift) had not been (asked for or) promised beforehand.

verses.text:
[२५०म] न-अश्नन्ति पितरस् तस्य दशवर्षाणि पञ्च च ।
[२५०म्च्] न च हव्यं वहत्य् अग्निर् यस् ताम् अभ्यवमन्यते ॥
                                २४९ ॥
verses.english: During fifteen years the manes do not eat (the food) of that man who disdains a (freely-offered gift), nor does the fire carry his offerings (to the gods).

verses.text:
[२५१म] शय्यां गृहान् कुशान् गन्धान् अपः पुष्पं मणीन् दधि
                                ।
[२५१म्च्] धाना मत्स्यान् पयो मांसं शाकं च-एव न निर्णुदेत् ॥
                                २५० ॥
verses.english: A couch, a house, Kusa grass, perfumes, water, flowers, jewels, sour milk, grain, fish, sweet milk, meat, and vegetables let him not reject, (if they are voluntarily offered.)

verses.text:
[२५२म] गुरून् भृत्यांश् च-उज्जिहीर्षन्न् अर्चिष्यन् देवता.अतिथीन्
                                ।
[२५२म्च्] सर्वतः प्रतिगृह्णीयान् न तु तृप्येत् स्वयं ततः ॥
                                २५१ ॥
verses.english: He who desires to relieve his Gurus and those whom he is bound to maintain, or wishes to honour the gods and guests, may accept (gifts) from anybody; but he must not satisfy his (own hunger) with such (presents).

verses.text:
[२५३म] गुरुषु त्व् अभ्यतीतेषु विना वा तैर् गृहे वसन् ।
[२५३म्च्] आत्मनो वृत्तिम् अन्विच्छन् गृह्णीयात् साधुतः सदा ॥ २५२
                                ॥
verses.english: But if his Gurus are dead, or if he lives separate from them in (another) house, let him, when he seeks a subsistence, accept (presents) from good men alone.

verses.text:
[२५४म] आर्धिकः कुलमित्रं च गोपालो दास.नापितौ ।
[२५४म्च्] एते शूद्रेषु भोज्य.अन्ना याश् च-आत्मानं निवेदयेत् ॥
                                २५३ ॥
verses.english: His labourer in tillage, a friend of his family, his cow-herd, his slave, and his barber are, among Sudras, those whose food he may eat, likewise (a poor man) who offers himself (to be his slave).

verses.text:
[२५५म] यादृशो ऽस्य भवेद् आत्मा यादृशं च चिकीर्षितम् ।
[२५५म्च्] यथा च-उपचरेद् एनं तथा-आत्मानं निवेदयेत् ॥ २५४
                                ॥
verses.english: As his character is, as the work is which he desires to perform, and as the manner is in which he means to serve, even so (a voluntary slave) must offer himself.

verses.text:
[२५६म] यो ऽन्यथा सन्तम् आत्मानम् अन्यथा सत्सु भाषते ।
[२५६म्च्] स पापकृत्तमो लोके स्तेन आत्म.अपहारकः ॥ २५५
                                ॥
verses.english: He who describes himself to virtuous (men), in a manner contrary to truth, is the most sinful (wretch) in this world; he is a thief who makes away with his own self.
All things (have their nature) determined by speech; speech is their root, and from speech they proceed; but he who is dishonest with respect to speech, is dishonest in everything.

verses.text:
[२५८म] महर्षि.पितृ.देवानां गत्वा-आनृण्यं यथाविधि ।
[२५८म्च्] पुत्रे सर्वं समासज्य वसेन् माध्यस्थ्यम् आस्श्रितः ॥
                                २५७ ॥ ४.२५७च्[२५८म्च्]व्/ म्: आस्थितः ॥ 4.257 ॥
