verses.english: When he has paid, according to the law, his debts to the great sages, to the manes, and to the gods, let him make over everything to his son and dwell (in his house), not caring for any worldly concerns.

verses.text:
[२५९म] एकाकी चिन्तयेन् नित्यं विविक्ते हितम् आत्मनः । ४.२५८अ[२५९म]व्/ म्: 
                                    हितम् आत्मनि
[२५९म्च्] एकाकी चिन्तयानो हि परं श्रेयो ऽधिगच्छति ॥ २५८
                                ॥
verses.english: Alone let him constantly meditate in solitude on that which is salutary for his soul; for he who meditates in solitude attains supreme bliss.

verses.text:
[२६०म] एषा-उदिता गृहस्थस्य वृत्तिर् विप्रस्य शाश्वती ।
[२६०म्च्] स्नातकव्रतकल्पश् च सत्त्ववृद्धिकरः शुभः ॥ २५९
                                ॥
verses.english: Thus have been declared the means by which a Brahmana householder must always subsist, and the summary of the ordinances for a Snataka, which cause an increase of holiness and are praiseworthy.

verses.text:
[२६१म] अनेन विप्रो वृत्तेन वर्तयन् वेद.शास्त्रवित् ।
[२६१म्च्] व्यपेत.कल्मषो नित्यं ब्रह्मलोके महीयते ॥ २६०
                                ॥
verses.english: A Brahmana who, being learned in the lore of the Vedas, conducts himself in this manner and daily destroys his sins, will be exalted in Brahman's world.

verses.text:
श्रुत्वा-एतान् ऋषयो धर्मान् स्नातकस्य यथा.उदितान् ।
इदम् ऊचुर् महात्मानम् अनल.प्रभवं भृगुम् ॥ १ ॥
verses.english: The sages, having heard the duties of a Snataka thus declared, spoke to great-souled Bhrigu, who sprang from fire:

verses.text:
एवं यथा.उक्तं विप्राणां स्वधर्मम् अनुतिष्ठताम् ।
कथं मृत्युः प्रभवति वेद.शास्त्रविदां प्रभो ॥ २ ॥
verses.english: 'How can Death have power over Brahmanas who know the sacred science, the Veda, (and) who fulfil their duties as they have been explained (by thee), O Lord? '

verses.text:
स तान् उवाच धर्म.आत्मा महर्षीन् मानवो भृगुः ।
श्रूयतां येन दोषेण मृत्युर् विप्रान् जिघांसति ॥ ३ ॥
verses.english: Righteous Bhrigu, the son of Manu, (thus) answered the great sages: 'Hear, (in punishment) of what faults Death seeks to shorten the lives of Brahmanas!'

verses.text:
अनभ्यासेन वेदानाम् आचारस्य च वर्जनात् ।
आलस्याद् अन्नदोषाच् च मृत्युर् विप्राञ् जिघांसति ॥ ४ ॥ ५.०४च्व्/ म्: 
                                विप्रान् ॥ 5.4 ॥
verses.english: 'Through neglect of the Veda-study, through deviation from the rule of conduct, through remissness (in the fulfilment of duties), and through faults (committed by eating forbidden) food, Death becomes eager to shorten the lives of Brahmanas.'

verses.text:
लशुनं गृञ्जनं च-एव पलाण्डुं कवकानि च ।
अभक्ष्याणि द्विजातीनाम् अमेध्य.प्रभवानि च ॥ ५ ॥
verses.english: Garlic, leeks and onions, mushrooms and (all plants), springing from impure (substances), are unfit to be eaten by twice-born men.

verses.text:
लोहितान् वृक्षनिर्यासान् वृश्चन.प्रभवांस् तथा । ५.०६अव्/ म्: 
                                व्रश्चन.प्रभवांस्
शेलुं गव्यं च पेयूषं प्रयत्नेन विवर्जयेत् ॥ ६ ॥ ५.०६च्व्/ म्: 
                                पीयूषं ॥ 5.6 ॥
verses.english: One should carefully avoid red exudations from trees and (juices) flowing from incisions, the Selu (fruit), and the thickened milk of a cow (which she gives after calving).

verses.text:
वृथा कृसर.संयावं पायस.अपूपम् एव च ।
अन्.उपाकृतमांसानि देवान्नानि हवींषि च ॥ ७ ॥
verses.english: Rice boiled with sesamum, wheat mixed with butter, milk and sugar, milk-rice and flour-cakes which are not prepared for a sacrifice, meat which has not been sprinkled with water while sacred texts were recited, food offered to the gods and sacrificial viands,

verses.text:
अ.निर्दशाया गोः क्षीरम् औष्ट्रम् ऐकशफं तथा ।
आविकं सन्धिनीक्षीरं वि.वत्सायाश् च गोः पयः ॥ ८ ॥ ५.०८च्व्/ म्: 
                                सन्धिनीक्षीरं ॥ 5.8 ॥
verses.english: The milk of a cow (or other female animal) within ten days after her calving, that of camels, of one-hoofed animals, of sheep, of a cow in heat, or of one that has no calf with her,

verses.text:
आरण्यानां च सर्वेषां मृगाणां माहिषं विना ।
स्त्रीक्षीरं च-एव वर्ज्यानि सर्वशुक्तानि च-एव हि ॥ ९ ॥
verses.english: (The milk) of all wild animals excepting buffalo-cows, that of women, and all (substances turned) sour must be avoided.

verses.text:
दधि भक्ष्यं च शुक्तेषु सर्वं च दधि.सम्भवम् । ५.१०अव्/ म्: 
                                दधि.सम्भवम्
यानि च-एव-अभिषूयन्ते पुष्प.मूल.फलैः शुभैः ॥ १० ॥
verses.english: Among (things turned) sour, sour milk, and all (food) prepared of it may be eaten, likewise what is extracted from pure flowers, roots, and fruit.

verses.text:
क्रव्यादाञ् शकुनान् सर्वान्-तथा ग्रामनिवासिनः । ५.११अव्/ म्: क्रव्यादः
                                शकुनीन्
अ.निर्दिष्टांश् च-एकशफांष् टिट्टिभं च विवर्जयेत् ॥ ११ ॥
verses.english: Let him avoid all carnivorous birds and those living in villages, and one-hoofed animals which are not specially permitted (to be eaten), and the Tittibha (Parra Jacana),

verses.text:
कलविङ्कं प्लवं हंसं चक्राह्वं ग्रामकुक्कुटम् ।
सारसं रज्जुवालं च दात्यूहं शुक.सारिके ॥ १२ ॥ ५.१२च्व्/ म्: 
                                रज्जुदालं ॥ 5.12 ॥
verses.english: The sparrow, the Plava, the Hamsa, the Brahmani duck, the village-cock, the Sarasa crane, the Raggudala, the woodpecker, the parrot, and the starling,

verses.text:
प्रतुदाञ् जालपादांश् च कोयष्टि.नखविष्किरान् । ५.१३अव्/ म्: 
                                प्रतुदान्
निमज्जतश् च मत्स्यादान् सौनं वल्लूरम् एव च ॥ १३ ॥
verses.english: Those which feed striking with their beaks, web-footed birds, the Koyashti, those which scratch with their toes, those which dive and live on fish, meat from a slaughter-house and dried meat,

verses.text:
बकं च-एव बलाकां च काकोलं खञ्जरीटकम् ।
मत्स्यादान् विड्वराहांश् च मत्स्यान् एव च सर्वशः ॥ १४ ॥
verses.english: The Baka and the Balaka crane, the raven, the Khangaritaka, (animals) that eat fish, village-pigs, and all kinds of fishes.

verses.text:
यो यस्य मांसम् अश्नाति स तन्मांसाद उच्यते ।
मत्स्यादः सर्वमांसादस् तस्मान् मत्स्यान् विवर्जयेत् ॥ १५ ॥
verses.english: He who eats the flesh of any (animal) is called the eater of the flesh of that (particular creature), he who eats fish is an eater of every (kind of) flesh; let him therefore avoid fish.

verses.text:
पाठीन.रोहिताव् आद्यौ नियुक्तौ हव्य.कव्ययोः ।
राजीवान् सिंहतुण्डाश् च स.शल्काश् च-एव सर्वशः ॥ १६ ॥ ५.१६च्व्/ म्: 
                                राजीवाः ॥ 5.16 ॥
verses.english: (But the fish called) Pathina and (that called) Rohita may be eaten, if used for offerings to the gods or to the manes; (one may eat) likewise Ragivas, Simhatundas, and Sasalkas on all (occasions).

verses.text:
न भक्षयेद् एकचरान् अज्ञातांश् च मृग.द्विजान् ।
भक्ष्येष्व् अपि समुद्दिष्टान् सर्वान् पञ्चनखांस् तथा ॥ १७ ॥
verses.english: Let him not eat solitary or unknown beasts and birds, though they may fall under (the categories of) eatable (creatures), nor any five-toed (animals).

verses.text:
श्वाविधं शल्यकं गोधां खड्ग.कूर्म.शशांस् तथा ।
भक्ष्यान् पञ्चनखेष्व् आहुर् अनुष्ट्रांश् च-एकतोदतह् ॥ १८ ॥
verses.english: The porcupine, the hedgehog, the iguana, the rhinoceros, the tortoise, and the hare they declare to be eatable; likewise those (domestic animals) that have teeth in one jaw only, excepting camels.

verses.text:
छत्राकं विड्वराहं च लशुनं ग्रामकुक्कुटम् ।
पलाण्डुं गृञ्जनं च-एव मत्या जग्ध्वा पतेद् द्विजः ॥ १९ ॥
verses.english: A twice-born man who knowingly eats mushrooms, a village-pig, garlic, a village-cock, onions, or leeks, will become an outcast.

verses.text:
अ.मत्या-एतानि षड् जग्ध्वा कृच्छ्रं सान्तपनं चरेत् ।
यतिचान्द्रायाणं वा-अपि शेषेषु-उपवसेद् अहः ॥ २० ॥
verses.english: He who unwittingly partakes of (any of) these six, shall perform a Samtapana (Krikkhra) or the lunar penance (Kandrayana) of ascetics; in case (he who has eaten) any other (kind of forbidden food) he shall fast for one day (and a night ).

verses.text:
संवत्सरस्य-एकम् अपि चरेत् कृच्छ्रं द्विजोत्तमः ।
अ.ज्ञातभुक्तशुद्धि.अर्थं ज्ञातस्य तु विषेशतः ॥ २१ ॥
verses.english: Once a year a Brahmana must perform a Krikkhra penance, in order to atone for unintentionally eating (forbidden food) but for intentionally (eating forbidden food he must perform the penances prescribed) specially.

verses.text:
यज्ञार्थं ब्राह्मणैर् वध्याः प्रशस्ता मृग.पक्षिणः ।
भृत्यानां च-एव वृत्ति.अर्थम् अगस्त्यो ह्य् आचरत् पुरा ॥ २२ ॥
verses.english: Beasts and birds recommended (for consumption) may be slain by Brahmanas for sacrifices, and in order to feed those whom they are bound to maintain; for Agastya did this of old.

verses.text:
बभूवुर् हि पुरोडाशा भक्ष्याणां मृग.पक्षिणाम् ।
पुराणेष्व् अपि यज्ञेषु ब्रह्म.क्षत्रसवेषु च ॥ २३ ॥ ५.२३च्व्/ म्: पुराणेष्व्
                                ऋषियज्ञेषु ॥ 5.23 ॥
verses.english: For in ancient (times) the sacrificial cakes were (made of the flesh) of eatable beasts and birds at the sacrifices offered by Brahmanas and Kshatriyas.

verses.text:
यत् किं चित् स्नेहसंयुक्तं भक्ष्यं भोज्यम् अ.गर्हितम् ।
तत् पर्युषितम् अप्य् आद्यं हविःशेषं च यद् भवेत् ॥ २४ ॥
verses.english: All lawful hard or soft food may be eaten, though stale, (after having been) mixed with fatty (substances), and so may the remains of sacrificial viands.

verses.text:
चिरस्थितम् अपि त्व् आद्यम् अ.स्नेहाक्तं द्विजातिभिः ।
यव.गोधूमजं सर्वं पयसश् च-एव विक्रिया ॥ २५ ॥
verses.english: But all preparations of barley and wheat, as well as preparations of milk, may be eaten by twice-born men without being mixed with fatty (substances), though they may have stood for a long time.

verses.text:
एतद् उक्तं द्विजातीनां भक्ष्य.अभक्ष्यम् अ.शेषतः ।
मांसस्य-अतः प्रवक्ष्यामि विधिं भक्षणवर्जने ॥ २६ ॥
verses.english: Thus has the food, allowed and forbidden to twice-born men, been fully described; I will now propound the rules for eating and avoiding meat.

verses.text:
प्रोक्षितं भक्षयेन् मांसं ब्राह्मणानां च काम्यया ।
यथाविधि नियुक्तस् तु प्राणानाम् एव च-अत्यये ॥ २७ ॥
verses.english: One may eat meat when it has been sprinkled with water, while Mantras were recited, when Brahmanas desire (one's doing it), when one is engaged (in the performance of a rite) according to the law, and when one's life is in danger.

verses.text:
प्राणस्य-अन्नम् इदं सर्वं प्रजापतिर् अकल्पयत् ।
स्थावरं जङ्गमं च-एव सर्वं प्राणस्य भोजनम् ॥ २८ ॥
verses.english: The Lord of creatures (Pragapati) created this whole (world to be) the sustenance of the vital spirit; both the immovable and the movable (creation is) the food of the vital spirit.

verses.text:
चराणाम् अन्नम् अ.चरा दंष्ट्रिणाम् अप्य् अ.दंष्ट्रिणः ।
अ.हस्ताश् च स.हस्तानां शूराणां च-एव भीरवः ॥ २९ ॥
verses.english: What is destitute of motion is the food of those endowed with locomotion; (animals) without fangs (are the food) of those with fangs, those without hands of those who possess hands, and the timid of the bold.

verses.text:
न-अत्ता दुष्यत्य् अदन्न् आद्यान् प्राणिनो ऽहन्य्.अहन्य् अपि ।
धात्रा-एव सृष्टा ह्य् आद्याश् च प्राणिनो ऽत्तार एव च ॥ ३० ॥
verses.english: The eater who daily even devours those destined to be his food, commits no sin; for the creator himself created both the eaters and those who are to be eaten (for those special purposes).

verses.text:
यज्ञाय जग्धिर् मांसस्य-इत्य् एष दैवो विधिः स्मृतः ।
अतो ऽन्यथा प्रवृत्तिस् तु राक्षसो विधिर् उच्यते ॥ ३१ ॥
verses.english: 'The consumption of meat (is befitting) for sacrifices,' that is declared to be a rule made by the gods; but to persist (in using it) on other (occasions) is said to be a proceeding worthy of Rakshasas.

verses.text:
क्रीत्वा स्वयं वा-अप्य् उत्पाद्य पर.उपकृतम् एव वा ।
देवान् पितॄंश् च-अर्चयित्वा खादन् मांसं न दुष्यति ॥ ३२ ॥
verses.english: He who eats meat, when he honours the gods and manes, commits no sin, whether he has bought it, or himself has killed (the animal), or has received it as a present from others.

verses.text:
न-अद्याद् अविधिना मांसं विधिज्ञो ऽनापदि द्विजः ।
जग्ध्वा ह्य् अ.विधिना मांसं प्रेतस् तैर् अद्यते ऽ.वशः ॥ ३३
                            ॥
verses.english: A twice-born man who knows the law, must not eat meat except in conformity with the law; for if he has eaten it unlawfully, he will, unable to save himself, be eaten after death by his (victims).

verses.text:
न तादृशं भवत्य् एनो मृगहन्तुर् धनार्थिनः ।
यादृशं भवति प्रेत्य वृथामांसानि खादतः ॥ ३४ ॥
verses.english: After death the guilt of one who slays deer for gain is not as (great) as that of him who eats meat for no (sacred) purpose.

verses.text:
नियुक्तस् तु यथान्यायं यो मांसं न-अत्ति मानवः ।
स प्रेत्य पशुतां याति सम्भवान् एकविंशतिम् ॥ ३५ ॥
verses.english: But a man who, being duly engaged (to officiate or to dine at a sacred rite), refuses to eat meat, becomes after death an animal during twenty-one existences.

verses.text:
असंस्कृतान् पशून् मन्त्रैर् न-अद्याद् विप्रः कदा चन ।
मन्त्रैस् तु संस्कृतान् अद्यात्-शाश्वतं विधिम् आस्थितः ॥ ३६ ॥
verses.english: A Brahmana must never eat (the flesh of animals unhallowed by Mantras; but, obedient to the primeval law, he may eat it, consecrated with Vedic texts.

verses.text:
कुर्याद् घृतपशुं सङ्गे कुर्यात् पिष्टपशुं तथा ।
न त्व् एव तु वृथा हन्तुं पशुम् इच्छेत् कदा चन ॥ ३७ ॥
verses.english: If he has a strong desire (for meat) he may make an animal of clarified butter or one of flour, (and eat that); but let him never seek to destroy an animal without a (lawful) reason.

verses.text:
यावन्ति पशुरोमाणि तावत्कृत्वो ह मारणम् ।
वृथापशुघ्नः प्राप्नोति प्रेत्य जन्मनि जन्मनि ॥ ३८ ॥
verses.english: As many hairs as the slain beast has, so often indeed will he who killed it without a (lawful) reason suffer a violent death in future births.

verses.text:
यज्ञार्थं पशवः सृष्टाः स्वयम् एव स्वयम्भुवा ।
यज्ञो ऽस्य भूत्यै सर्वस्य तस्माद् यज्ञे वधो ऽ.वधः ॥ ३९
                            ॥
verses.english: Svayambhu (the Self-existent) himself created animals for the sake of sacrifices; sacrifices (have been instituted) for the good of this whole (world); hence the slaughtering (of beasts) for sacrifices is not slaughtering (in the ordinary sense of the word).

verses.text:
ओषध्यः पशवो वृक्षास् तिर्यञ्चः पक्षिणस् तथा ।
यज्ञार्थं निधनं प्राप्ताः प्राप्नुवन्त्य् उत्सृतीः पुनः ॥ ४० ॥
                                ५.४०च्व्/ म्: 
                                उच्छ्रितीः ॥ 5.40 ॥
verses.english: Herbs, trees, cattle, birds, and (other) animals that have been destroyed for sacrifices, receive (being reborn) higher existences.

verses.text:
मधुपर्के च यज्ञे च पितृ.दैवतकर्मणि ।
अत्र-एव पशवो हिंस्या न-अन्यत्र-इत्य् अब्रवीन् मनुः ॥ ४१ ॥
verses.english: On offering the honey-mixture (to a guest), at a sacrifice and at the rites in honour of the manes, but on these occasions only, may an animal be slain; that (rule) Manu proclaimed.

verses.text:
एष्व् अर्थेषु पशून् हिंसन् वेदतत्त्वार्थविद् द्विजः ।
आत्मानं च पशुं च-एव गमयत्य् उत्तमं गतिम् ॥ ४२ ॥
verses.english: A twice-born man who, knowing the true meaning of the Veda, slays an animal for these purposes, causes both himself and the animal to enter a most blessed state.

verses.text:
गृहे गुराव् अरण्ये वा निवसन्न् आत्मवान् द्विजः ।
न-अ.वेदविहितां हिंसाम् आपद्य् अपि समाचरेत् ॥ ४३ ॥
verses.english: A twice-born man of virtuous disposition, whether he dwells in (his own) house, with a teacher, or in the forest, must never, even in times of distress, cause an injury (to any creature) which is not sanctioned by the Veda.

verses.text:
या वेदविहिता हिंसा नियता-अस्मिंश् चर.अचरे ।
अहिंसाम् एव तां विद्याद् वेदाद् धर्मो हि निर्बभौ ॥ ४४ ॥
verses.english: Know that the injury to moving creatures and to those destitute of motion, which the Veda has prescribed for certain occasions, is no injury at all; for the sacred law shone forth from the Veda.

verses.text:
यो ऽहिंसकानि भूतानि हिनस्त्य् आत्मसुख.इच्छया ।
स जीवांश् च मृतश् च-एव न क्व चित् सुखम् एधते ॥ ४५ ॥
verses.english: He who injures innoxious beings from a wish to (give) himself pleasure, never finds happiness, neither living nor dead.

verses.text:
यो बन्धनवधक्लेशान् प्राणिनां न चिकीर्षति ।
स सर्वस्य हितप्रेप्सुः सुखम् अत्यन्तम् अश्नुते ॥ ४६ ॥
verses.english: He who does not seek to cause the sufferings of bonds and death to living creatures, (but) desires the good of all (beings), obtains endless bliss.

verses.text:
यद् ध्यायति यत् कुरुते रतिं बध्नाति यत्र च ।
तद् अवाप्नोत्य् अयत्नेन यो हिनस्ति न किं चन ॥ ४७ ॥
verses.english: He who does not injure any (creature), attains without an effort what he thinks of, what he undertakes, and what he fixes his mind on.

verses.text:
न-अ.कृत्वा प्राणिनां हिंसां मांसम् उत्पद्यते क्व चित् ।
न च प्राणिवधः स्वर्ग्यस् तस्मान् मांसं विवर्जयेत् ॥ ४८ ॥
verses.english: Meat can never be obtained without injury to living creatures, and injury to sentient beings is detrimental to (the attainment of) heavenly bliss; let him therefore shun (the use of) meat.

verses.text:
समुत्पत्तिं च मांसस्य वध.बन्धौ च देहिनाम् ।
प्रसमीक्ष्य निवर्तेत सर्वमांसस्य भक्षणात् ॥ ४९ ॥
verses.english: Having well considered the (disgusting) origin of flesh and the (cruelty of) fettering and slaying corporeal beings, let him entirely abstain from eating flesh.

verses.text:
न भक्षयति यो मांसं विधिं हित्वा पिशाचवत् ।
न लोके प्रियतां याति व्याधिभिश् च न पीड्यते ॥ ५० ॥
verses.english: He who, disregarding the rule (given above), does not eat meat like a Pisaka, becomes dear to men, and will not be tormented by diseases.

verses.text:
अनुमन्ता विशसिता निहन्ता क्रय.विक्रयी ।
संस्कर्ता च-उपहर्ता च खादकश् च-इति घातकाः ॥ ५१ ॥
verses.english: He who permits (the slaughter of an animal), he who cuts it up, he who kills it, he who buys or sells (meat), he who cooks it, he who serves it up, and he who eats it, (must all be considered as) the slayers (of the animal).

verses.text:
स्वमांसं परमांसेन यो वर्धयितुम् इच्छति ।
अन्.अभ्यर्च्य पितॄन् देवांस् ततो ऽन्यो न-अस्त्य् अपुण्यकृत् ॥ ५२
                            ॥
verses.english: There is no greater sinner than that (man) who, though not worshipping the gods or the manes, seeks to increase (the bulk of) his own flesh by the flesh of other (beings).

verses.text:
वर्षे वर्षे ऽश्वमेधेन यो यजेत शतं समाः ।
मांसानि च न खादेद् यस् तयोः पुण्यफलं समम् ॥ ५३ ॥
verses.english: He who during a hundred years annually offers a horse-sacrifice, and he who entirely abstains from meat, obtain the same reward for their meritorious (conduct).

verses.text:
फल.मूल.अशनैर् मेध्यैर् मुनि.अन्नानां च भोजनैः ।
न तत् फलम् अवाप्नोति यत्-मांसपरिवर्जनात् ॥ ५४ ॥
verses.english: By subsisting on pure fruit and roots, and by eating food fit for ascetics (in the forest), one does not gain (so great) a reward as by entirely avoiding (the use of) flesh.

verses.text:
मां स भक्षयिता-अमुत्र यस्य मांसम् इह-अद्म्य् अहम् ।
एतत्-मांसस्य मांसत्वं प्रवदन्ति मनीषिणः ॥ ५५ ॥
verses.english: 'Me he (mam sah)' will devour in the next (world), whose flesh I eat in this (life); the wise declare this (to be) the real meaning of the word 'flesh' (mamsah).

verses.text:
न मांसभक्षणे दोषो न मद्ये न च मैथुने ।
प्रवृत्तिर् एषा भूतानां निवृत्तिस् तु महाफला ॥ ५६ ॥
verses.english: There is no sin in eating meat, in (drinking) spirituous liquor, and in carnal intercourse, for that is the natural way of created beings, but abstention brings great rewards.

verses.text:
प्रेतशुद्धिं प्रवक्ष्यामि द्रव्यशुद्धिं तथा-एव च ।
चतुर्णाम् अपि वर्णानां यथावद् अनुपूर्वशः ॥ ५७ ॥
verses.english: I will now in due order explain the purification for the dead and the purification of things as they are prescribed for the four castes (varna).

verses.text:
दन्तजाते ऽनुजाते च कृत.चूडे च संस्थिते ।
अशुद्धा बान्धवाः सर्वे सूतके च तथा-उच्यते ॥ ५८ ॥
verses.english: When (a child) dies that has teethed, or that before teething has received (the sacrament of) the tonsure (Kudakarana) or (of the initiation), all relatives (become) impure, and on the birth (of a child) the same (rule) is prescribed.

verses.text:
दशाहं शावम् आशौचं सपिण्डेषु विधीयते ।
अर्वाक् सञ्चयनाद् अस्थ्नां त्र्यहम् एकाहम् एव वा ॥ ५९ ॥
verses.english: It is ordained (that) among Sapindas the impurity on account of a death (shall last) ten days, (or) until the bones have been collected, (or) three days or one day only.

verses.text:
सपिण्डता तु पुरुषे सप्तमे विनिवर्तते ।
समानोदकभावस् तु जन्म.नाम्नोर् अ.वेदने ॥ ६० ॥
verses.english: But the Sapinda-relationship ceases with the seventh person (in the ascending and descending lines), the Samanodaka-relationship when the (common) origin and the (existence of a common family)-name are no (longer) known.

verses.text:
यथा-इदं शावम् आशौचं सपिण्डेषु विधीयते । ५.६१अव्/ नोत् इन्
                                    म्
जनने ऽप्य् एवम् एव स्यात्-निपुणं शुद्धिम् इच्छताम् ॥ ६१ ॥
                                    ५.६१च्व्/ नोत्
                                    इन् म् ॥ 5.61 ॥
verses.english: As this impurity on account of a death is prescribed for (all) Sapindas, even so it shall be (held) on a birth by those who desire to be absolutely pure.

verses.text:
[६१म] सर्वेषां शावम् आशौचं माता.पित्रोस् तु सूतकम् । ५.६२अ[६१म]व्/ म्: 
                                    जनने ऽप्य् एवम् एव स्यान् माता.पित्रोस् तु सूतकम्
[६१म्च्] सूतकं मातुर् एव स्याद् उपस्पृश्य पिता शुचिः ॥ ६२
                                ॥
verses.english: (Or while) the impurity on account of a death is common to all (Sapindas), that caused by a birth (falls) on the parents alone; (or) it shall fall on the mother alone, and the father shall become pure by bathing;

verses.text:
[६२म] निरस्य तु पुमान्-शुक्रम् उपस्पृस्य-एव शुध्यति ।
[६२म्च्] बैजिकाद् अभिसम्बन्धाद् अनुरुन्ध्याद् अघं त्र्यहम् ॥ ६३
                                ॥
verses.english: But a man, having spent his strength, is purified merely by bathing; after begetting a child (on a remarried female), he shall retain the impurity during three days.

verses.text:
[६३म] अह्ना च-एकेन रात्र्या च त्रिरात्रैर् एव च त्रिभिः ।
[६३म्च्] शव.स्पृशो विशुध्यन्ति त्र्यहाद् उदकदायिनः ॥ ६४
                                ॥
verses.english: Those who have touched a corpse are purified after one day and night (added to) three periods of three days; those who give libations of water, after three days.

verses.text:
[६४म] गुरोः प्रेतस्य शिष्यस् तु पितृमेधं समाचरन् ।
[६४म्च्] प्रेतहारैः समं तत्र दशरात्रेण शुध्यति ॥ ६५ ॥
                                    ५.६५च्[६४म्च्]व्/ म्: प्रेताहारैः ॥ 5.65 ॥
verses.english: A pupil who performs the Pitrimedha for his deceased teacher, becomes also pure after ten days, just like those who carry the corpse out (to the burial-ground).

verses.text:
[६५म] रात्रिभिर् मास.तुल्याभिर् गर्भस्रावे विशुध्यति ।
[६५म्च्] रजस्य् उपरते साध्वी स्नानेन स्त्री रजस्वला ॥ ६६
                                ॥
verses.english: (A woman) is purified on a miscarriage in as many (days and) nights as months (elapsed after conception), and a menstruating female becomes pure by bathing after the menstrual secretion has ceased (to flow).

verses.text:
[६६म] नृणाम् अ.कृतचूडानां विशुद्धिर् नैशिकी स्मृता ।
[६६म्च्] निर्वृत्त.चूडकानां तु त्रिरात्रात्-शुद्धिर् इष्यते ॥ ६७ ॥
                                    ५.६७च्[६६म्च्]व्/ म्: निर्वृत्त.मुण्डकानां ॥ 5.67 ॥
verses.english: (On the death) of children whose tonsure (Kudakarman) has not been performed, the (Sapindas) are declared to become pure in one (day and) night; (on the death) of those who have received the tonsure (but not the initiation, the law) ordains (that) the purification (takes place) after three days.

verses.text:
[६७म] ऊन.द्विवार्षिकं प्रेतं निदध्युर् बान्धवा बहिः ।
[६७म्च्] अलङ्कृत्य शुचौ भूमाव् अस्थिसञ्चयनाद् ऋते ॥ ६८ ॥
verses.english: A child that has died before the completion of its second year, the relatives shall carry out (of the village), decked (with flowers, and bury it) in pure ground, without collecting the bones (afterwards).

verses.text:
[६८म] न-अस्य कार्यो ऽग्निसंस्कारो न च कार्या-उदकक्रिया ।
[६८म्च्] अरण्ये काष्ठवत् त्यक्त्वा क्षपेयुस् त्र्यहम् एव तु ॥ ६९
                                ॥ ५.६९च्[६८म्च्]व्/
                                    म्: क्षपेत त्र्यहम् एव च ॥ 5.69 ॥
verses.english: Such (a child) shall not be burnt with fire, and no libations of water shall be offered to it; leaving it like a (log of) wood in the forest, (the relatives) shall remain impure during three days only.

verses.text:
[६९म] न-अ.त्रिवर्षस्य कर्तव्या बान्धवैर् उदकक्रिया ।
[६९म्च्] जात.दन्तस्य वा कुर्युर् नाम्नि वा.अपि कृते सति ॥ ७०
                                ॥
verses.english: The relatives shall not offer libations to (a child) that has not reached the third year; but if it had teeth, or the ceremony of naming it (Namakarman) had been performed, (the offering of water is) optional.

verses.text:
[७०म] स.ब्रह्मचारिण्य् एकाहम् अतीते क्षपणम् स्मृतम् ।
[७०म्च्] जन्मन्य् एक.उदकानां तु त्रिरात्रात्-शुद्धिर् इष्यते ॥ ७१
                                ॥
verses.english: If a fellow-student has died, the Smriti prescribes an impurity of one day; on a birth the purification of the Samanodakas is declared (to take place) after three (days and) nights.

verses.text:
[७१म] स्त्रीणाम् अ.संस्कृतानां तु त्र्यहात्-शुध्यन्ति बान्धवाः
                                ।
[७१म्च्] यथा.उक्तेन-एव कल्पेन शुध्यन्ति तु स.नाभयः ॥ ७२
                                ॥
verses.english: (On the death) of females (betrothed but) not married (the bridegroom and his) relatives are purified after three days, and the paternal relatives become pure according to the same rule.

verses.text:
[७२म] अ.क्षार.लवण.अन्नाः स्युर् निमज्जेयुश् च ते त्र्यहम् ।
[७२म्च्] मांसाशनं च न-अश्नीयुः शयीरंश् च पृथक् क्षितौ ॥
                                ७३ ॥
verses.english: Let (mourners) eat food without factitious salt, bathe during three days, abstain from meat, and sleep separate on the ground.

verses.text:
[७३म] सन्निधाव् एष वै कल्पः शाव.आशौचस्य कीर्तितः
                                    ।
[७३म्च्] अ.सन्निधाव् अयं ज्ञेयो विधिः सम्बन्धि.बान्धवैः
                                    ॥ ७४ ॥
verses.english: The above rule regarding impurity on account of a death has been prescribed (for cases where the kinsmen live) near (the deceased); (Sapinda) kinsmen and (Samanodaka) relatives must know the following rule (to refer to cases where deceased lived) at a distance (from them).

verses.text:
[७४म] विगतं तु विदेशस्थं शृणुयाद् यो ह्य् अ.निर्दशम्
                                    ।
[७४म्च्] यत्-शेषं दशरात्रस्य तावद् एव-अशुचिर् भवेत् ॥
                                    ७५ ॥
verses.english: He who may hear that (a relative) residing in a distant country has died, before ten (days after his death have elapsed), shall be impure for the remainder of the period of ten (days and) nights only.

verses.text:
[७५म] अतिक्रान्ते दशाहे च त्रिरात्रम् अशुचिर् भवेत् ।
[७५म्च्] संवत्सरे व्यतीते तु स्पृष्ट्वा-एव-आपो विशुध्यति ॥
                                    ७६ ॥
verses.english: If the ten days have passed, he shall be impure during three (days and) nights; but if a year has elapsed (since the occurrence of the death), he becomes pure merely by bathing.

verses.text:
[७६म] निर्दशं ज्ञातिमरणं श्रुत्वा पुत्रस्य जन्म च
                                    ।
[७६म्च्] स.वासा जलम् आप्लुत्य शुद्धो भवति मानवः ॥ ७७
                                    ॥
verses.english: A man who hears of a (Sapinda) relative's death, or of the birth of a son after the ten days (of impurity have passed), becomes pure by bathing, dressed in his garments.

verses.text:
[७७म] बाले देशान्तरस्थे च पृथक्.पिण्डे च संस्थिते
                                    ।
[७७म्च्] स.वासा जलम् आप्लुत्य सद्य एव विशुध्यति ॥ ७८
                                    ॥
verses.english: If an infant (that has not teethed), or a (grownup relative who is) not a Sapinda, die in a distant country, one becomes at once pure after bathing in one's clothes.

verses.text:
[७८म] अन्तर्.दशाहे स्यातां चेत् पुनर् मरण.जन्मनी ।
                                        ५.७९अ[७८म]व्/ म्: चेत् स्यातां
[७८म्च्] तावत् स्याद् अ.शुचिर् विप्रो यावत् तत् स्याद् अ.निर्दशम्
                                    ॥ ७९ ॥
verses.english: If within the ten days (of impurity) another birth or death happens, a Brahmana shall remain impure only until the (first) period of ten days has expired.

verses.text:
[७९म] त्रिरात्रम् आहुर् आशौचम् आचार्ये संस्थिते सति ।
[७९म्च्] तस्य पुत्रे च पत्न्यां च दिवा.रात्रम् इति स्थितिः
                                    ॥ ८० ॥
verses.english: They declare that, when the teacher (akarya) has died, the impurity (lasts) three days; if the (teacher's) son or wife (is dead, it lasts) a day and a night; that is a settled (rule).

verses.text:
[८०म] श्रोत्रिये तु-उपसम्पन्ने त्रिरात्रम् अशुचिर् भवेत्
                                    ।
[८०म्च्] मातुले पक्षिणीं रात्रिं शिष्य.ऋत्विग्.बान्धवेषु च ॥
                                    ८१ ॥
verses.english: For a Srotriya who resides with (him out of affection), a man shall be impure for three days; for a maternal uncle, a pupil, an officiating priest, or a maternal relative, for one night together with the preceding and following days.

verses.text:
[८१म] प्रेते राजनि स.ज्योतिर् यस्य स्याद् विषये स्थितः
                                    ।
[८१म्च्] अ.श्रोत्रिये त्व् अहः कृत्स्नम् अनूचाने तथा गुरौ ॥
                                    ८२ ॥ ५.८२च्[८१म्च्]व्/ म्: कृत्स्नाम् ॥ 5.82 ॥
verses.english: If the king in whose realm he resides is dead, (he shall be impure) as long as the light (of the sun or stars shines), but for (an intimate friend) who is not a Srotriya (the impurity lasts) for a whole day, likewise for a Guru who knows the Veda and the Angas.

verses.text:
[८२म] शुद्ध्येद् विप्रो दशाहेन द्वादशाहेन भूमिपः ।
[८२म्च्] वैश्यः पञ्चदशाहेन शूद्रो मासेन शुध्यति ॥ ८३
                                    ॥
verses.english: A Brahmana shall be pure after ten days, a Kshatriya after twelve, a Vaisya after fifteen, and a Sudra is purified after a month.

verses.text:
[८३म] न वर्धयेद् अघ.अहानि प्रत्यूहेन् न-अग्निषु क्रियाः
                                    ।
[८३म्च्] न च तत्कर्म कुर्वाणः स.नाभ्यो ऽप्य् अशुचिर् भवेत्
                                    ॥ ८४ ॥
verses.english: Let him not (unnecessarily) lengthen the period of impurity, nor interrupt the rites to be performed with the sacred fires; for he who performs that (Agnihotra) rite will not be impure, though (he be) a (Sapinda) relative.

verses.text:
[८४म] दिवाकीर्तिम् उदक्यां च पतितं सूतिकां तथा ।
[८४म्च्] शवं तत्स्पृष्टिनं च-एव स्पृष्ट्वा स्नानेन शुध्यति
                                    ॥ ८५ ॥
verses.english: When he has touched a Kandala, a menstruating woman, an outcast, a woman in childbed, a corpse, or one who has touched a (corpse), he becomes pure by bathing.

verses.text:
[८५म] आचम्य प्रयतो नित्यं जपेद् अ.शुचिदर्शने ।
[८५म्च्] सौरान् मन्त्रान् यथा.उत्साहं पावमानीश् च शक्तितः
                                    ॥ ८६ ॥
verses.english: He who has purified himself by sipping water shall, on seeing any impure (thing or person), always mutter the sacred texts, addressed to Surya, and the Pavamani (verses).

verses.text:
[८६म] नारं स्पृष्ट्वा-अस्थि स.स्नेहं स्नात्वा विप्रो
                                    विशुध्यति ।
[८६म्च्] आचम्य-एव तु निःस्नेहं गाम् आलभ्य-अर्कम् ईक्ष्य वा
                                    ॥ ८७ ॥
verses.english: A Brahmana who has touched a human bone to which fat adheres, becomes pure by bathing; if it be free from fat, by sipping water and by touching (afterwards) a cow or looking at the sun.

verses.text:
[८७म] आदिष्टी न-उदकं कुर्याद् आ व्रतस्य समापनात् ।
[८७म्च्] समाप्ते तु-उदकं कृत्वा त्रिरात्रेण-एव शुध्यति ॥
                                    ८८ ॥
verses.english: He who has undertaken the performance of a vow shall not pour out libations (to the dead) until the vow has been completed; but when he has offered water after its completion, he becomes pure in three days only.

verses.text:
[८८म] वृथा.सङ्कर.जातानां प्रव्रज्यासु च तिष्ठताम्
                                    ।
[८८म्च्] आत्मनस् त्यागिनां च-एव निवर्तेत-उदकक्रिया ॥ ८९
                                    ॥
verses.english: Libations of water shall not be offered to those who (neglect the prescribed rites and may be said to) have been born in vain, to those born in consequence of an illegal mixture of the castes, to those who are ascetics (of heretical sects), and to those who have committed suicide,

verses.text:
[८९म] पाषण्डम् आश्रितानां च चरन्तीनां च कामतः ।
[८९म्च्] गर्भ.भर्तृ.द्रुहां च-एव सुरापीनां च योषिताम् ॥
                                    ९० ॥
verses.english: To women who have joined a heretical sect, who through lust live (with many men), who have caused an abortion, have killed their husbands, or drink spirituous liquor.

verses.text:
[९०म] आचार्यं स्वम् उपाध्यायं पितरं मातरं गुरुम् ।
[९०म्च्] निर्हृत्य तु व्रती प्रेतान् न व्रतेन वियुज्यते ॥ ९१
                                    ॥
verses.english: A student does not break his vow by carrying out (to the place of cremation) his own dead teacher (akarya), sub-teacher (upadhyaya), father, mother, or Guru.

verses.text:
[९१म] दक्षिणेन मृतं शूद्रं पुरद्वारेण निर्हरेत् ।
[९१म्च्] पश्चिम.उत्तर.पूर्वैस् तु यथायोगं द्विजन्मनः ॥
                                    ९२ ॥
verses.english: Let him carry out a dead Sudra by the southern gate of the town, but (the corpses of) twice-born men, as is proper, by the western, northern, or eastern (gates).

verses.text:
[९२म] न राज्ञाम् अघदोषो ऽस्ति व्रतिनां न च सत्त्रिणाम्
                                    ।
[९२म्च्] ऐन्द्रं स्थानम् उपासीना ब्रह्मभूता हि ते सदा ॥
                                    ९३ ॥
verses.english: The taint of impurity does not fall on kings, and those engaged in the performance of a vow, or of a Sattra; for the (first are) seated on the throne of Indra, and the (last two are) ever pure like Brahman.

verses.text:
[९३म] राज्ञो महात्मिके स्थाने सद्यःशौचं विधीयते ।
[९३म्च्] प्रजानां परिरक्षार्थम् आसनं च-अत्र कारणम् ॥
                                    ९४ ॥
verses.english: For a king, on the throne of magnanimity, immediate purification is prescribed, and the reason for that is that he is seated (there) for the protection of (his) subjects.

verses.text:
[९४म] डिम्भ.आहव.हतानां च विद्युता पार्थिवेन च ।
                                        ५.९५अ[९४म]व्/ म्: डिम्ब.आहव.हतानां
[९४म्च्] गो.ब्राह्मणस्य च-एव-अर्थे यस्य च-इच्छति
                                    पार्थिवः ॥ ९५ ॥
verses.english: (The same rule applies to the kinsmen) of those who have fallen in a riot or a battle, (of those who have been killed) by lightning or by the king, and (of those who perished fighting) for cows and Brahmanas, and to those whom the king wishes (to be pure).

verses.text:
[९५म] सोम.अग्नि.अर्क.अनिल.इन्द्राणां वित्त.अप्पत्योर्
                                    यमस्य च ।
[९५म्च्] अष्टानां लोकपालानां वपुर् धारयते नृपः ॥ ९६
                                    ॥
verses.english: A king is an incarnation of the eight guardian deities of the world, the Moon, the Fire, the Sun, the Wind, Indra, the Lords of wealth and water (Kubera and Varuna), and Yama.

verses.text:
[९६म] लोकेशाधिष्ठितो राजा न-अस्य-आशौचं विधीयते
                                    ।
[९६म्च्] शौच.आशौचं हि मर्त्यानां लोकेभ्यः
                                    प्रभव.अप्ययौ ॥ ९७ ॥
verses.english: Because the king is pervaded by those lords of the world, no impurity is ordained for him; for purity and impurity of mortals is caused and removed by (those) lords of the world.

verses.text:
[९७म] उद्यतैर् आहवे शस्त्रैः क्षत्रधर्महतस्य च
                                    ।
[९७म्च्] सद्यः सन्तिष्ठते यज्ञस् तथा-आशौचम् इति स्थितिः
                                    ॥ ९८ ॥
verses.english: By him who is slain in battle with brandished weapons according to the law of the Kshatriyas, a (Srauta) sacrifice is instantly completed, and so is the period of impurity (caused by his death); that is a settled rule.

verses.text:
[९८म] विप्रः शुध्यत्य् अपः स्पृष्ट्वा क्षत्रियो
                                    वाहन.आयुधम् ।
[९८म्च्] वैश्यः प्रतोदं रश्मीन् वा यष्टिं शूद्रः
                                    कृत.क्रियः ॥ ९९ ॥
verses.english: (At the end of the period of impurity) a Brahmana who has performed the necessary rites, becomes pure by touching water, a Kshatriya by touching the animal on which he rides, and his weapons, a Vaisya by touching his goad or the nose-string (of his oxen), a Sudra by touching his staff.

verses.text:
[९९म] एतद् वो ऽभिहितं शौचं सपिण्डेषु द्विजोत्तमाः
                                    ।
[९९म्च्] असपिण्डेषु सर्वेषु प्रेतशुद्धिं निबोधत ॥ १००
                                    ॥
verses.english: Thus the purification (required) on (the death of) Sapindas has been explained to you, O best of twice-born men; hear now the manner in which men are purified on the death of any (relative who is) not a Sapinda.

verses.text:
[१००म] असपिण्डं द्विजं प्रेतं विप्रो निर्हृत्य बन्धुवत्
                                ।
[१००म्च्] विशुध्यति त्रिरात्रेण मातुर् आप्तांश् च बान्धवान् ॥
                                १०१ ॥
verses.english: A Brahmana, having carried out a dead Brahmana who is not a Sapinda, as (if he were) a (near) relative, or a near relative of his mother, becomes pure after three days;

verses.text:
[१०१म] यद्य् अन्नम् अत्ति तेषां तु दशाहेन-एव शुध्यति ।
[१०१म्च्] अन्.अदन्न् अन्नम् अह्ना-एव न चेत् तस्मिन् गृहे वसेत् ॥
                                १०२ ॥
verses.english: But if he eats the food of the (Sapindas of the deceased), he is purified in ten days, (but) in one day, if he does not eat their food nor dwells in their house.

verses.text:
[१०२म] अनुगम्य-इच्छया प्रेतं ज्ञातिम् अज्ञातिम् एव च । ५.१०३अ[१०२म]व्/ म्: 
                                    अज्ञातिम् एव वा
[१०२म्च्] स्नात्वा स.चैलः स्पृष्ट्वा-अग्निं घृतं प्राश्य
                                विशुध्यति ॥ १०३ ॥ ५.१०३च्[१०२म्च्]व्/ म्: स.चैलं,
                                विशुद्ध्यति ॥ 5.103 ॥
verses.english: Having voluntarily followed a corpse, whether (that of) a paternal kinsman or (of) a stranger, he becomes pure by bathing, dressed in his clothes, by touching fire and eating clarified butter.

verses.text:
[१०३म] न विप्रं स्वेषु तिष्ठत्सु मृतं शूद्रेण नाययेत् ।
[१०३म्च्] अ.स्वर्ग्या ह्य् आहुतिः सा स्यात्-शूद्रसंस्पर्शदूषिता ॥
                                १०४ ॥
verses.english: Let him not allow a dead Brahmana to be carried out by a Sudra, while men of the same caste are at hand; for that burnt-offering which is defiled by a Sudra's touch is detrimental to (the deceased's passage to) heaven.

verses.text:
[१०४म] ज्ञानं तपो ऽग्निर् आहारो मृत्-मनो वार्य् उपाञ्जनम् ।
[१०४म्च्] वायुः कर्म-अर्क.कालौ च शुद्धेः कर्तॄणि देहिनाम् ॥
                                १०५ ॥
verses.english: The knowledge (of Brahman) austerities, fire, (holy) food, earth, (restraint of) the internal organ, water, smearing (with cowdung), the wind, sacred rites, the sun, and time are the purifiers of corporeal (beings).

verses.text:
[१०५म] सर्वेषाम् एव शौचानाम् अर्थशौचं परं स्मृतं ।
[१०५म्च्] यो ऽर्थे शुचिर् हि स शुचिर् न मृत्.वारि.शुचिः शुचिः ॥
                                १०६ ॥
verses.english: Among all modes of purification, purity in (the acquisition of) wealth is declared to be the best; for he is pure who gains wealth with clean hands, not he who purifies himself with earth and water.

verses.text:
[१०६म] क्षान्त्या शुध्यन्ति विद्वांसो दानेन-अ.कार्यकारिणः ।
                                    ५.१०७अ[१०६म]व्/ म्: शुद्ध्यन्ति
[१०६म्च्] प्रच्छन्न.पापा जप्येन तपसा वेदवित्तमाः ॥ १०७
                                ॥
verses.english: The learned are purified by a forgiving disposition, those who have committed forbidden actions by liberality, secret sinners by muttering (sacred texts), and those who best know the Veda by austerities.

verses.text:
[१०७म] मृत्.तोयैः शुध्यते शोध्यं नदी वेगेन शुध्यति
                                ।
[१०७म्च्] रजसा स्त्री मनोदुष्टा सन्न्यासेन द्विजोत्तमाः ॥ १०८
                                ॥
verses.english: By earth and water is purified what ought to be made pure, a river by its current, a woman whose thoughts have been impure by the menstrual secretion, a Brahmana by abandoning the world (samnyasa).

verses.text:
[१०८म] अद्भिर् गात्राणि शुध्यन्ति मनः सत्येन शुध्यति ।
[१०८म्च्] विद्या.तपोभ्यां भूतात्मा बुद्धिर् ज्ञानेन शुध्यति ॥
                                १०९ ॥ ५.१०९च्[१०८म्च्]व्/ म्: शुद्ध्यति ॥ 5.109 ॥
verses.english: The body is cleansed by water, the internal organ is purified by truthfulness, the individual soul by sacred learning and austerities, the intellect by (true) knowledge.

verses.text:
[१०९म] एष शौचस्य वः प्रोक्तः शरीरस्य विनिर्णयः ।
[१०९म्च्] नानाविधानां द्रव्याणां शुद्धेः शृणुत निर्णयम् ॥ ११०
                                ॥
verses.english: Thus the precise rules for the purification of the body have been declared to you; hear now the decision (of the law) regarding the purification of the various (inanimate) things.

verses.text:
[११०म] तैजसानां मणीनां च सर्वस्य-अश्ममयस्य च ।
[११०म्च्] भस्मना-अद्भिर् मृदा च-एव शुद्धिर् उक्ता मनीषिभिः ॥
                            १११ ॥
verses.english: The wise ordain that all (objects) made of metal, gems, and anything made of stone are to be cleansed with ashes, earth, and water.

verses.text:
[१११म] निर्लेपं काञ्चनं भाण्डम् अद्भिर् एव विशुध्यति । ५.११२अ[१११म]व्/ म्: 
                                विशुद्ध्यति
[१११म्च्] अप्.जम् अश्ममयं च-एव राजतं च-अन्.उपस्कृतम् ॥ ११२
                            ॥
verses.english: A golden vessel which shows no stains, becomes pure with water alone, likewise what is produced in water (as shells and coral), what is made of stone, and a silver (vessel) not enchased.

verses.text:
[११२म] अपाम् अग्नेश् च संयोगाद्द् हैमं रौप्यं च निर्बभौ ।
[११२म्च्] तस्मात् तयोः स्वयोन्या-एव निर्णेको गुणवत्तरः ॥ ११३
                            ॥
verses.english: From the union of water and fire arose the glittering gold and silver; those two, therefore, are best purified by (the elements) from which they sprang.

verses.text:
[११३म] ताम्र.अयस्.कांस्य.रैत्यानां त्रपुणः सीसकस्य च ।
[११३म्च्] शौचं यथार्हं कर्तव्यं क्षार.अम्लोदक.वारिभिः ॥ ११४
                            ॥
verses.english: Copper, iron, brass, pewter, tin, and lead must be cleansed, as may be suitable (for each particular case), by alkaline (substances), acids or water.

verses.text:
[११४म] द्रवाणां च-एव सर्वेषां शुद्धिर् उत्पवनं स्मृतम् ।
[११४म्च्] प्रोक्षणं संहतानां च दारवाणां च तक्षणम् ॥ ११५
                            ॥
verses.english: The purification prescribed for all (sorts of) liquids is by passing two blades of Kusa grass through them, for solid things by sprinkling (them with water), for (objects) made of wood by planing them.

verses.text:
[११५म] मार्जनं यज्ञपात्राणां पाणिना यज्ञकर्मणि ।
[११५म्च्] चमसानां ग्रहाणां च शुद्धिः प्रक्षालनेन तु ॥ ११६
                            ॥
verses.english: At sacrifices the purification of (the Soma cups called) Kamasas and Grahas, and of (other) sacrificial vessels (takes place) by rubbing (them) with the hand, and (afterwards) rinsing (them with water).

verses.text:
[११६म] चरूणां स्रुक्.स्रुवाणां च शुद्धिर् उष्णेन वारिणा ।
[११६म्च्] स्फ्य.शूर्प.शकटानां च मुसल.उलूखलस्य च ॥ ११७
                            ॥
verses.english: The Karu and (the spoons called) Sruk and Sruva must be cleaned with hot water, likewise (the wooden sword, called) Sphya, the winnowing-basket (Surpa), the cart (for bringing the grain), the pestle and the mortar.

verses.text:
[११७म] अद्भिस् तु प्रोक्षणं शौचं बहूनां धान्य.वाससाम् ।
[११७म्च्] प्रक्षालनेन त्व् अल्पानाम् अद्भिः शौचं विधीयते ॥ ११८
                            ॥
verses.english: The manner of purifying large quantities of grain and of cloth is to sprinkle them with water; but the purification of small quantities is prescribed (to take place) by washing them.

verses.text:
[११८म] चैलवत्-चर्मणां शुद्धिर् वैदलानां तथा-एव च ।
[११८म्च्] शाक.मूल.फलानां च धान्यवत्-शुद्धिर् इष्यते ॥ ११९ ॥
                                ५.११९च्[११८म्च्]व्/
                                म्: तु ॥ 5.119 ॥
verses.english: Skins and (objects) made of split cane must be cleaned like clothes; vegetables, roots, and fruit like grain;

verses.text:
[११९म] कौशेय.आविकयोर् ऊषैः कुतपानाम् अरिष्टकैः ।
[११९म्च्] श्रीफलैर् अंशुपट्टानां क्षौमाणां गौरसर्षपैः ॥ १२०
                            ॥
verses.english: Silk and woollen stuffs with alkaline earth; blankets with pounded Arishta (fruit); Amsupattas with Bel fruit; linen cloth with (a paste of) yellow mustard.

verses.text:
[१२०म] क्षौमवत्-शङ्ख.शृङ्गाणाम् अस्थि.दन्तमयस्य च ।
[१२०म्च्] शुद्धिर् विजानता कार्या गो.मूत्रेण-उदकेन वा ॥ १२१
                            ॥
verses.english: A man who knows (the law) must purify conch-shells, horn, bone and ivory, like linen cloth, or with a mixture of cow's urine and water.

verses.text:
[१२१म] प्रोक्षणात् तृण.काष्ठं च पलालं च-एव शुध्यति ।
[१२१म्च्] मार्जन.उपाञ्जनैर् वेश्म पुनःपाकेन मृत्.मयम् ॥ १२२
                            ॥
verses.english: Grass, wood, and straw become pure by being sprinkled (with water), a house by sweeping and smearing (it with cowdung or whitewash), an earthen (vessel) by a second burning.

verses.text:
मद्यैर् मूत्रैः पुरीषैर् वा ष्ठीवनैह् पूयशोणितैः । ५.१२३अव्/ नोत् इन्
                                म्
संस्पृष्टं न-एव शुद्ध्येत पुनःपाकेन मृत्.मयम् ॥ १२३ ॥
                                ५.१२३च्व्/ नोत्
                                इन् म् ॥ 5.123 ॥
verses.english: An earthen vessel which has been defiled by spirituous liquor, urine, ordure, saliva, pus or blood cannot be purified by another burning.

verses.text:
[१२२म] सम्मार्जन.उपाञ्जनेन सेकेन-उल्लेखनेन च ।
[१२२म्च्] गवां च परिवासेन भूमिः शुध्यति पञ्चभिः ॥ १२४ ॥
                                ५.१२४च्[१२२म्च्]व्/
                                म्: शुद्ध्यति ॥ 5.124 ॥
verses.english: Land is purified by (the following) five (modes, viz.) by sweeping, by smearing (it with cowdung), by sprinkling (it with cows' urine or milk), by scraping, and by cows staying (on it during a day and night).

verses.text:
[१२३म] पक्षि.जग्धं गवा घ्रातम् अवधूतम् अवक्षुतम् ।
[१२३म्च्] दूषितं केश.कीटैश् च मृत्.प्रक्षेपेण शुध्यति ॥ १२५
                            ॥
verses.english: (Food) which has been pecked at by birds, smelt at by cows, touched (with the foot), sneezed on, or defiled by hair or insects, becomes pure by scattering earth (over it).

verses.text:
[१२४म] यावत्-न-अपैत्य् अ.मेध्याक्ताद् गन्धो लेपश् च तत्.कृतः
                            ।
[१२४म्च्] तावन् मृद्.वारि च-आदेयं सर्वासु द्रव्यशुद्धिषु ॥ १२६
                            ॥
verses.english: As long as the (foul) smell does not leave an (object) defiled by impure substances, and the stain caused by them (does not disappear), so long must earth and water be applied in cleansing (inanimate) things.

verses.text:
[१२५म] त्रीणि देवाः पवित्राणि ब्राह्मणानाम् अकल्पयन् ।
[१२५म्च्] अ.दृष्टम् अद्भिर् निर्णिक्तं यच् च वाचा प्रशस्यते ॥ १२७
                            ॥
verses.english: The gods declared three things (to be) pure to Brahmanas, that (on which) no (taint is) visible, what has been washed with water, and what has been commended (as pure) by the word (of a Brahmana).

verses.text:
[१२६म] आपः शुद्धा भूमिगता वैतृष्ण्यं यासु गोर् भवेत्
                                ।
[१२६म्च्] अ.व्याप्ताश् चेद् अ.मेध्येन गन्ध.वर्ण.रस.अन्विताः ॥
                                १२८ ॥
verses.english: Water, sufficient (in quantity) in order to slake the thirst of a cow, possessing the (proper) smell, colour, and taste, and unmixed with impure substances, is pure, if it is collected on (pure) ground.

verses.text:
[१२७म] नित्यं शुद्धः कारु.हस्तः पण्ये यच् च प्रसारितम् ।
                                    ५.१२९अ[१२७म]व्/ म्: पण्यं
[१२७म्च्] ब्रह्मचारिगतं भैक्ष्यं नित्यं मेध्यम् इति स्थितिः
                                ॥ १२९ ॥
verses.english: The hand of an artisan is always pure, so is (every vendible commodity) exposed for sale in the market, and food obtained by begging which a student holds (in his hand) is always fit for use; that is a settled rule.

verses.text:
[१२८म] नित्यम् आस्यं शुचि स्त्रीणां शकुनिः फलपातने ।
[१२८म्च्] प्रस्रवे च शुचिर् वत्सः श्वा मृगग्रहणे शुचिः ॥ १३०
                                ॥
verses.english: The mouth of a woman is always pure, likewise a bird when he causes a fruit to fall; a calf is pure on the flowing of the milk, and a dog when he catches a deer.

verses.text:
[१२९म] श्वभिर् हतस्य यन् मांसं शुचि तन् मनुर् अब्रवीत्
                                ।
[१२९म्च्] क्रव्याद्भिश् च हतस्य-अन्यैश् चण्डालाद्यैश् च
                                दस्युभिः ॥ १३१ ॥
verses.english: Manu has declared that the flesh (of an animal) killed by dogs is pure, likewise (that) of a (beast) slain by carnivorous (animals) or by men of low caste (Dasyu), such as Kandalas.

verses.text:
[१३०म] ऊर्ध्वं नाभेर् यानि खानि तानि मेध्यानि सर्वशः
                                ।
[१३०म्च्] यान्य् अधस् तान्य् अ.मेध्यानि देहाच् च-एव मलाश् च्युताः
                                ॥ १३२ ॥
verses.english: All those cavities (of the body) which lie above the navel are pure, (but) those which are below the navel are impure, as well as excretions that fall from the body.

verses.text:
[१३१म] मक्षिका विप्रुषश् छाया गौर् अश्वः सूर्यरश्मयः ।
[१३१म्च्] रजो भूर् वायुर् अग्निश् च स्पर्शे मेध्यानि निर्दिशेत् ॥
                                १३३ ॥
verses.english: Flies, drops of water, a shadow, a cow, a horse, the rays of the sun, dust, earth, the wind, and fire one must know to be pure to the touch.

verses.text:
[१३२म] विष्.मूत्र.उत्सर्ग.शुद्धि.अर्थं मृत्.वार्य् आदेयम् अर्थवत्
                            ।
[१३२म्च्] दैहिकानां मलानां च शुद्धिषु द्वादशस्व् अपि ॥ १३४
                            ॥
verses.english: In order to cleanse (the organs) by which urine and faeces are ejected, earth and water must be used, as they may be required, likewise in removing the (remaining ones among) twelve impurities of the body.

verses.text:
[१३३म] वसा शुक्रम् असृज्-मज्जा मूत्र.विष्-घ्राण.कर्ण.विष्-(सिच्
                            ।
[१३३म्च्] श्लेश्म अश्रु दूषिका स्वेदो द्वादश-एते नृणां मलाः ॥ १३५
                            ॥
verses.english: Oily exudations, semen, blood, (the fatty substance of the) brain, urine, faeces, the mucus of the nose, ear-wax, phlegm, tears, the rheum of the eyes, and sweat are the twelve impurities of human (bodies).

verses.text:
[१३४म] एका लिङ्गे गुदे तिस्रस् तथा-एकत्र करे दश ।
[१३४म्च्] उभयोः सप्त दातव्या मृदः शुद्धिम् अभीप्सता ॥ १३६
                            ॥
verses.english: He who desires to be pure, must clean the organ by one (application of) earth, the anus by (applying earth) three (times), the (left) hand alone by (applying it) ten (times), and both (hands) by (applying it) seven (times).

verses.text:
[१३५म] एतत्-शौचं गृहस्थानां द्विगुणं ब्रह्मचारिणाम् ।
[१३५म्च्] त्रिगुणं स्याद् वनस्थानां यतीनां तु चतुर्गुणम् ॥ १३७
                            ॥
verses.english: Such is the purification ordained for householders; (it shall be) double for students, treble for hermits, but quadruple for ascetics.

verses.text:
[१३६म] कृत्वा मूत्रं पुरीषं वा खान्य् आचान्त उपस्पृशेत् ।
[१३६म्च्] वेदम् अध्येष्यमाणश् च अन्नम् अश्नंश् च सर्वदा ॥ १३८
                            ॥
verses.english: When he has voided urine or faeces, let him, after sipping water, sprinkle the cavities, likewise when he is going to recite the Veda, and always before he takes food.

verses.text:
[१३७म] त्रिर् आचामेद् अपः पूर्वं द्विः प्रमृज्यात् ततो मुखम् ।
[१३७म्च्] शरीरं शौचम् इच्छन् हि स्त्री शूद्रस् तु सकृत् सकृत् ॥
                            १३९ ॥
verses.english: Let him who desires bodily purity first sip water three times, and then twice wipe his mouth; but a woman and a Sudra (shall perform each act) once (only).

verses.text:
[१३८म] शूद्राणां मासिकं कार्यं वपनं न्यायवर्तिनाम् ।
[१३८म्च्] वैश्यवत्-शौचकल्पश् च द्विज.उच्छिष्टं च भोजनम् ॥
                            १४० ॥
verses.english: Sudras who live according to the law, shall each month shave (their heads); their mode of purification (shall be) the same as that of Vaisyas, and their food the fragments of an Aryan's meal.

verses.text:
[१३९म] न-उच्छिष्टं कुर्वते मुख्या विप्रुषो ऽङ्गं न यान्ति याः
                            ।
[१३९म्च्] न श्मश्रूणि गतान्य् आस्यं न दन्तान्तर्.अधिष्ठितम् ॥ १४१
                            ॥
verses.english: Drops (of water) from the mouth which do not fall on a limb, do not make (a man) impure, nor the hair of the moustache entering the mouth, nor what adheres to the teeth.

verses.text:
[१४०म] स्पृशन्ति बिन्दवः पादौ य आचामयतः परान् ।
[१४०म्च्] भौमिकैस् ते समा ज्ञेया न तैर् आप्रयतो भवेत् ॥ १४२
                            ॥ ५.१४२च्[१४०म्च्]व्/
                                म्: अ.प्रयतो ॥ 5.142 ॥
verses.english: Drops which trickle on the feet of him who offers water for sipping to others, must be considered as equal to (water collected on the ground; they render him not impure.

verses.text:
[१४१म] उच्छिष्टेन तु संस्पृष्टो द्रव्य.हस्तः कथं चन ।
[१४१म्च्] अ.निधाय-एव तद् द्रव्यम् आचान्तः शुचिताम् इयात् ॥ १४३
                            ॥
verses.english: He who, while carrying anything in any manner, is touched by an impure (person or thing), shall become pure, if he performs an ablution, without putting down that object.

verses.text:
[१४२म] वान्तो विरिक्तः स्नात्वा तु घृतप्राशनम् आचरेत् ।
[१४२म्च्] आचामेद् एव भुक्त्वा-अन्नं स्नानं मैथुनिनः स्मृतम् ॥ १४४
                            ॥
verses.english: He who has vomited or purged shall bathe, and afterwards eat clarified butter; but if (the attack comes on) after he has eaten, let him only sip water; bathing is prescribed for him who has had intercourse with a woman.

verses.text:
[१४३म] सुप्त्वा क्षुत्वा च भुक्त्वा च निष्ठीव्य-उक्त्वा-अनृतानि च
                            ।
[१४३म्च्] पीत्वा-अपो ऽध्येष्यमाणश् च आचामेत् प्रयतो ऽपि सन् ॥ १४५
                            ॥
verses.english: Though he may be (already) pure, let him sip water after sleeping, sneezing, eating, spitting, telling untruths, and drinking water, likewise when he is going to study the Veda.

verses.text:
[१४४म] एषां शौचविधिः कृत्स्नो द्रव्यशुद्धिस् तथा-एव च ।
                                ५.१४६अ[१४४म]व्/
                                म्: एष
[१४४म्च्] उक्तो वः सर्ववर्णानां स्त्रीणां धर्मान् निबोधत ॥ १४६
                            ॥
verses.english: Thus the rules of personal purification for men of all castes, and those for cleaning (inanimate) things, have been fully declared to you: hear now the duties of women.

verses.text:
[१४५म] बालया वा युवत्या वा वृद्धया वा-अपि योषिता ।
[१४५म्च्] न स्वातन्त्र्येण कर्तव्यं किं चिद् कार्यं गृहेष्व् अपि
                                ॥ १४७ ॥
verses.english: By a girl, by a young woman, or even by an aged one, nothing must be done independently, even in her own house.

verses.text:
[१४६म] बाल्ये पितुर् वशे तिष्ठेत् पाणिग्राहस्य यौवने ।
[१४६म्च्] पुत्राणां भर्तरि प्रेते न भजेत् स्त्री स्वतन्त्रताम्
                                ॥ १४८ ॥
verses.english: In childhood a female must be subject to her father, in youth to her husband, when her lord is dead to her sons; a woman must never be independent.

verses.text:
[१४७म] पित्रा भर्त्रा सुतैर् वा-अपि न-इच्छेद् विरहम् आत्मनः
                                ।
[१४७म्च्] एषां हि विरहेण स्त्री गर्ह्ये कुर्याद् उभे कुले ॥ १४९
                                ॥
verses.english: She must not seek to separate herself from her father, husband, or sons; by leaving them she would make both (her own and her husband's) families contemptible.

verses.text:
[१४८म] सदा प्रहृष्टया भाव्यं गृहकार्ये च दक्षया ।
[१४८म्च्] सुसंस्कृत.उपस्करया व्यये च-अमुक्त.हस्तया ॥ १५०
                                ॥
verses.english: She must always be cheerful, clever in (the management of her) household affairs, careful in cleaning her utensils, and economical in expenditure.

verses.text:
[१४९म] यस्मै दद्यात् पिता त्व् एनां भ्राता वा-अनुमते पितुः
                                ।
[१४९म्च्] तं शुश्रूषेत जीवन्तं संस्थितं च न लङ्घयेत् ॥
                                १५१ ॥
verses.english: Him to whom her father may give her, or her brother with the father's permission, she shall obey as long as he lives, and when he is dead, she must not insult (his memory).

verses.text:
[१५०म] मङ्गलार्थं स्वस्त्ययनं यज्ञश् च-आसां प्रजापतेः
                                ।
[१५०म्च्] प्रयुज्यते विवाहे तु प्रदानं स्वाम्य.कारणम् ॥ १५२
                                ॥
verses.english: For the sake of procuring good fortune to (brides), the recitation of benedictory texts (svastyayana), and the sacrifice to the Lord of creatures (Pragapati) are used at weddings; (but) the betrothal (by the father or guardian) is the cause of (the husband's) dominion (over his wife).

verses.text:
[१५१म] अन्.ऋताव् ऋतुकाले च मन्त्र.संस्कारकृत् पतिः ।
[१५१म्च्] सुखस्य नित्यं दाता-इह परलोके च योषितः ॥ १५३
                                ॥
verses.english: The husband who wedded her with sacred texts, always gives happiness to his wife, both in season and out of season, in this world and in the next.

verses.text:
[१५२म] वि.शीलः काम.वृत्तो वा गुणैर् वा परिवर्जितः ।
[१५२म्च्] उपचार्यः स्त्रिया साध्व्या सततं देववत् पतिः ॥ १५४
                                ॥
verses.english: Though destitute of virtue, or seeking pleasure (elsewhere), or devoid of good qualities, (yet) a husband must be constantly worshipped as a god by a faithful wife.

verses.text:
[१५३म] न-अस्ति स्त्रीणां पृथग् यज्ञो न व्रतं न-अप्य्
                                उपोषणम् । ५.१५५अ[१५३म]व्/ म्: उपोषितम्
[१५३म्च्] पतिं शुश्रूषते येन तेन स्वर्गे महीयते ॥ १५५
                                ॥
verses.english: No sacrifice, no vow, no fast must be performed by women apart (from their husbands); if a wife obeys her husband, she will for that (reason alone) be exalted in heaven.

verses.text:
[१५४म] पाणिग्राहस्य साध्वी स्त्री जीवतो वा मृतस्य वा ।
[१५४म्च्] पतिलोकम् अभीप्सन्ती न-आचरेत् किं चिद् अ.प्रियम् ॥
                                १५६ ॥
verses.english: A faithful wife, who desires to dwell (after death) with her husband, must never do anything that might displease him who took her hand, whether he be alive or dead.

verses.text:
[१५५म] कामं तु क्सपयेद् देहं पुष्प.मूल.फलैः शुभैः
                                ।
[१५५म्च्] न तु नाम-अपि गृह्णीयात् पत्यौ प्रेते परस्य तु ॥
                                १५७ ॥
verses.english: At her pleasure let her emaciate her body by (living on) pure flowers, roots, and fruit; but she must never even mention the name of another man after her husband has died.

verses.text:
[१५६म] आसीत-आ मरणात् क्सान्ता नियता ब्रह्मचारिणी ।
[१५६म्च्] यो धर्म एकपत्नीनां काङ्क्षन्ती तम् अनुत्तमम् ॥ १५८
                                ॥
verses.english: Until death let her be patient (of hardships), self-controlled, and chaste, and strive (to fulfil) that most excellent duty which (is prescribed) for wives who have one husband only.

verses.text:
[१५७म] अनेकानि सहस्राणि कुमार.ब्रह्मचारिणाम् ।
[१५७म्च्] दिवं गतानि विप्राणाम् अ.कृत्वा कुलसन्ततिम् ॥ १५९
                                ॥
verses.english: Many thousands of Brahmanas who were chaste from their youth, have gone to heaven without continuing their race.

verses.text:
[१५८म] मृते भर्तरि साढ्वी स्त्री ब्रह्मचर्ये व्यवस्थिता
                                ।
[१५८म्च्] स्वर्गं गच्छत्य् अ.पुत्रा-अपि यथा ते ब्रह्मचारिणः
                                ॥ १६० ॥
verses.english: A virtuous wife who after the death of her husband constantly remains chaste, reaches heaven, though she have no son, just like those chaste men.

verses.text:
[१५९म] अपत्यलोभाद् या तु स्त्री भर्तारम् अतिवर्तते ।
[१५९म्च्] सा-इह निन्दाम् अवाप्नोति परलोकाच् च हीयते ॥ १६१
                                ॥
verses.english: But a woman who from a desire to have offspring violates her duty towards her (deceased) husband, brings on herself disgrace in this world, and loses her place with her husband (in heaven).

verses.text:
[१६०म] न-अन्य.उत्पन्ना प्रजा-अस्ति-इह न च-अप्य्
                                अन्यपरिग्रहे । ५.१६२अ[१६०म]व्/ म्: न च-अन्यस्य परिग्रहे
[१६०म्च्] न द्वितीयश् च साध्वीनां क्व चिद् भर्ता-उपदिश्यते ॥
                                १६२ ॥
verses.english: Offspring begotten by another man is here not (considered lawful), nor (does offspring begotten) on another man's wife (belong to the begetter), nor is a second husband anywhere prescribed for virtuous women.

verses.text:
[१६१म] पतिं हित्वा-अपकृष्टं स्वम् उत्कृष्टं या निषेवते ।
                                    ५.१६३अ[१६१म]व्/ म्: हित्वा-अवकृष्टं
[१६१म्च्] निन्द्या-एव सा भवेल् लोके पर.पूर्वा-इति च-उच्यते ॥
                                १६३ ॥
verses.english: She who cohabits with a man of higher caste, forsaking her own husband who belongs to a lower one, will become contemptible in this world, and is called a remarried woman (parapurva).

verses.text:
[१६२म] व्यभिचारात् तु भर्तुः स्त्री लोके प्राप्नोति निन्द्यताम् ।
                                    ५.१६४अ[१६२म]व्/ म्: व्यभिचारे तु
[१६२म्च्] शृगाल.योनिं प्राप्नोति पाप.रोगैश् च पीड्यते ॥ १६४
                                ॥
verses.english: By violating her duty towards her husband, a wife is disgraced in this world, (after death) she enters the womb of a jackal, and is tormented by diseases (the punishment of) her sin.

verses.text:
[१६३म] पतिं या न-अभिचरति मनो.वाग्.देहसंयुता । ५.१६५अ[१६३म]व्/ म्: 
                                    .देहसंयता
[१६३म्च्] सा भर्तृलोकम् आप्नोति सद्भिः साध्वी-इति च-उच्यते ॥
                                १६५ ॥
verses.english: She who, controlling her thoughts, words, and deeds, never slights her lord, resides (after death) with her husband (in heaven), and is called a virtuous (wife).

verses.text:
[१६४म] अनेन नारी वृत्तेन मनो.वाग्.देहसंयता ।
[१६४म्च्] इह-अग्र्यां कीर्तिम् आप्नोति पतिलोकं परत्र च ॥ १६६
                                ॥
verses.english: In reward of such conduct, a female who controls her thoughts, speech, and actions, gains in this (life) highest renown, and in the next (world) a place near her husband.

verses.text:
[१६५म] एवं वृत्तां स.वर्णां स्त्रीं द्विजातिः पूर्वमारिणीम्
                                ।
[१६५म्च्] दाहयेद् अग्निहोत्रेण यज्ञपात्रैश् च धर्मवित् ॥ १६७
                                ॥
verses.english: A twice-born man, versed in the sacred law, shall burn a wife of equal caste who conducts herself thus and dies before him, with (the sacred fires used for) the Agnihotra, and with the sacrificial implements.

verses.text:
[१६६म] भार्यायै पूर्वमारिण्यै दत्त्वा-अग्नीन् अन्त्यकर्मणि
                                ।
[१६६म्च्] पुनर् दारक्रियां कुर्यात् पुनर् आधानम् एव च ॥ १६८
                                ॥
verses.english: Having thus, at the funeral, given the sacred fires to his wife who dies before him, he may marry again, and again kindle (the fires).

verses.text:
[१६७म] अनेन विधिना नित्यं पञ्चयज्ञान् न हापयेत् ।
[१६७म्च्] द्वितीयम् आयुषो भागं कृत.दारो गृहे वसेत् ॥ १६९ ॥
verses.english: (Living) according to the (preceding) rules, he must never neglect the five (great) sacrifices, and, having taken a wife, he must dwell in (his own) house during the second period of his life.

verses.text:
एवं गृहाश्रमे स्थित्वा विधिवत् स्नातको द्विजः ।
वने वसेत् तु नियतो यथावद् विजित.इन्द्रियः ॥ १ ॥
verses.english: A twice-born Snataka, who has thus lived according to the law in the order of householders, may, taking a firm resolution and keeping his organs in subjection, dwell in the forest, duly (observing the rules given below).

verses.text:
गृहस्थस् तु यथा पश्येद् वली.पलितम् आत्मनः ।
अपत्यस्य-एव च-अपत्यं तदा-अरण्यं समाश्रयेत् ॥ २ ॥
verses.english: When a householder sees his (skin) wrinkled, and (his hair) white, and. the sons of his sons, then he may resort to the forest.

verses.text:
सन्त्यज्य ग्राम्यम् आहारं सर्वं च-एव परिच्छदम् ।
पुत्रेषु भार्यां निक्षिप्य वनं गच्छेत् सह-एव वा ॥ ३
                                ॥
verses.english: Abandoning all food raised by cultivation, and all his belongings, he may depart into the forest, either committing his wife to his sons, or accompanied by her.

verses.text:
अग्निहोत्रं समादाय गृह्यं च-अग्निपरिच्छदम् ।
ग्रामाद् अरण्यं निःसृत्य निवसेन् नियत.इन्द्रियः ॥ ४ ॥ ६.०४च्व्/ म्: 
                                    निष्क्रम्य ॥ 6.4 ॥
verses.english: Taking with him the sacred fire and the implements required for domestic (sacrifices), he may go forth from the village into the forest and reside there, duly controlling his senses.

verses.text:
मुनि.अन्नैर् विविधैर् मेध्यैः शाक.मूल.फलेन वा ।
एतान् एव महायज्ञान् निर्वपेद् विधिपूर्वकम् ॥ ५ ॥
verses.english: Let him offer those five great sacrifices according to the rule, with various kinds of pure food fit for ascetics, or with herbs, roots, and fruit.

verses.text:
वसीत चर्म चीरं वा सायं स्नायात् प्रगे तथा ।
जटाश् च बिभृयान् नित्यं श्मश्रु.लोम.नखानि च ॥ ६ ॥
verses.english: Let him wear a skin or a tattered garment; let him bathe in the evening or in the morning; and let him always wear (his hair in) braids, the hair on his body, his beard, and his nails (being unclipped).

verses.text:
यद्.भक्ष्यं स्याद् ततो दद्याद् बलिं भिक्षां च शक्तितः ।
                                        ६.०७अव्/
                                        म्: यद्भक्षः
अप्.मूल.फल.भिक्षाभिर् अर्चयेद् आश्रमागतान् ॥ ७ ॥
                                        ६.०७च्व्/
                                        म्: आश्रमागतम् ॥ 6.7 ॥
verses.english: Let him perform the Bali-offering with such food as he eats, and give alms according to his ability; let him honour those who come to his hermitage with alms consisting of water, roots, and fruit.

verses.text:
स्वाध्याये नित्ययुक्तः स्याद् दान्तो मैत्रः समाहितः ।
दाता नित्यम् अन्.आदाता सर्वभूतानुकम्पकः ॥ ८ ॥
verses.english: Let him be always industrious in privately reciting the Veda; let him be patient of hardships, friendly (towards all), of collected mind, ever liberal and never a receiver of gifts, and compassionate towards all living creatures.

verses.text:
वैतानिकं च जुहुयाद् अग्निहोत्रं यथाविधि ।
दर्शम् अ.स्कन्दयन् पर्व पौर्णमासं च योगतः ॥ ९
                                    ॥
verses.english: Let him offer, according to the law, the Agnihotra with three sacred fires, never omitting the new-moon and full-moon sacrifices at the proper time.

verses.text:
ऋक्षेष्ट्य्.आग्रयणं च-एव चातुर्मास्यानि च-आहरेत् । ६.१०अव्/ म्: 
                                        दर्शेष्ट्य्.आग्रयणं
तुरायणं च क्रमशो दक्षस्यायनम् एव च ॥ १० ॥ ६.१०च्व्/ क्म्:
                                        दाक्षस्यायनम् ॥ 6.10 ॥
verses.english: Let him also offer the Nakshatreshti, the Agrayana, and the Katurmasya (sacrifices), as well as the Turayana and likewise the Dakshayana, in due order.

verses.text:
वासन्त.शारदैर् मेध्यैर् मुनि.अन्नैः स्वयम् आहृतैः
                                    ।
पुरोडाशांश् चरूंश् च-एव विधिवत्-निर्वपेत् पृथक् ॥ ११
                                    ॥
verses.english: With pure grains, fit for ascetics, which grow in spring and in autumn, and which he himself has collected, let him severally prepare the sacrificial cakes (purodasa) and the boiled messes (karu), as the law directs.

verses.text:
देवताभ्यस् तु तद्द् हुत्वा वन्यं मेध्यतरं हविः ।
शेषम् आत्मनि युञ्जीत लवणं च स्वयं कृतम् ॥ १२ ॥
verses.english: Having offered those most pure sacrificial viands, consisting of the produce of the forest, he may use the remainder for himself, (mixed with) salt prepared by himself.

verses.text:
स्थलज.औदकशाकानि पुष्प.मूल.फलानि च ।
मेध्यवृक्ष.उद्भवान्य् अद्यात् स्नेहांश् च फल.सम्भवान् ॥
                                    १३ ॥
verses.english: Let him eat vegetables that grow on dry land or in water, flowers, roots, and fruits, the productions of pure trees, and oils extracted from forest-fruits.

verses.text:
वर्जयेन् मधु मांसं च भौमानि कवकानि च ।
भूस्तृणं शिग्रुकं च-एव श्लेश्मातक.फलानि च ॥ १४
                                    ॥
verses.english: Let him avoid honey, flesh, and mushrooms growing on the ground (or elsewhere, the vegetables called) Bhustrina, and Sigruka, and the Sleshmantaka fruit.

verses.text:
त्यजेद् आश्वयुजे मासि मुनि.अन्नं पूर्वसञ्चितम् ।
जीर्णानि च-एव वासांसि शाक.मूल.फलानि च ॥ १५ ॥
verses.english: Let him throw away in the month of Asvina the food of ascetics, which he formerly collected, likewise his worn-out clothes and his vegetables, roots, and fruit.

verses.text:
न फालकृष्टम् अश्नीयाद् उत्सृष्टम् अपि केन चित् ।
न ग्रामजातान्य् आर्तो ऽपि मूलाणि च फलानि च ॥ १६ ॥
                                        ६.१६च्व्/
                                        म्: पुष्पानि च फलानि च ॥ 6.16 ॥
verses.english: Let him not eat anything (grown on) ploughed (land), though it may have been thrown away by somebody, nor roots and fruit grown in a village, though (he may be) tormented (by hunger).

verses.text:
अग्निपक्व.अशनो वा स्यात् कालपक्वभुज्-एव वा ।
अश्म.कुट्टो भवेद् वा-अपि दन्त.उलूखलिको ऽपि वा ॥ १७
                                    ॥
verses.english: He may eat either what has been cooked with fire, or what has been ripened by time; he either may use a stone for grinding, or his teeth may be his mortar.

verses.text:
सद्यः प्रक्षालको वा स्यान् मास.सञ्चयिको ऽपि वा ।
षण्मास.निचयो वा स्यात् समा.निचय एव वा ॥ १८ ॥
verses.english: He may either at once (after his daily meal) cleanse (his vessel for collecting food), or lay up a store sufficient for a month, or gather what suffices for six months or for a year.

verses.text:
नक्तं च-अन्नं समश्नीयाद् दिवा वा-आहृत्य शक्तितः ।
चतुर्थकालिको वा स्यात् स्याद् वा-अप्य् अष्टम.कालिकः ॥ १९
                                    ॥
verses.english: Having collected food according to his ability, he may either eat at night (only), or in the day-time (only), or at every fourth meal-time, or at every eighth.

verses.text:
चान्द्रायणविधानैर् वा शुक्ल.कृष्णे च वर्तयेत् ।
पक्षान्तयोर् वा-अप्य् अश्नीयाद् यवागूं क्वथितां सकृत् ॥ २०
                                    ॥
verses.english: Or he may live according to the rule of the lunar penance (Kandrayana, daily diminishing the quantity of his food) in the bright (half of the month) and (increasing it) in the dark (half); or he may eat on the last days of each fortnight, once (a day only), boiled barley-gruel.

verses.text:
पुष्प.मूल.फलैर् वा-अपि केवलैर् वर्तयेत् सदा ।
कालपक्वैः स्वयं शीर्णैर् वैखानसमते स्थितः ॥ २१
                                    ॥
verses.english: Or he may constantly subsist on flowers, roots, and fruit alone, which have been ripened by time and have fallen spontaneously, following the rule of the (Institutes) of Vikhanas.

verses.text:
भूमौ विपरिवर्तेत तिष्ठेद् वा प्रपदैर् दिनम् ।
स्थान.आसनाभ्यां विहरेत् सवनेषु-उपयन्न् अपः ॥ २२
                                    ॥
verses.english: Let him either roll about on the ground, or stand during the day on tiptoe, (or) let him alternately stand and sit down; going at the Savanas (at sunrise, at midday, and at sunset) to water in the forest (in order to bathe).

verses.text:
ग्रीष्मे पञ्च.तपास् तु स्याद् वर्षास्व् अभ्र.अवकाशिकः ।
आर्द्र.वासास् तु हेमन्ते क्रमशो वर्धयंस् तपः ॥ २३
                                    ॥
verses.english: In summer let him expose himself to the heat of five fires, during the rainy season live under the open sky, and in winter be dressed in wet clothes, (thus) gradually increasing (the rigour of) his austerities.

verses.text:
उपस्पृशंस् त्रिषवणं पितॄन् देवांश् च तर्पयेत् ।
तपस्-चरंश् च-उग्रतरं शोषयेद् देहम् आत्मनः ॥ २४
                                    ॥
verses.english: When he bathes at the three Savanas (sunrise, midday, and sunset), let him offer libations of water to the manes and the gods, and practising harsher and harsher austerities, let him dry up his bodily frame.

verses.text:
अग्नीन् आत्मनि वैतानान् समारोप्य यथाविधि ।
अन्.अग्निर् अ.निकेतः स्यान् मुनिर् मूल.फल.अशनः ॥ २५
                                    ॥
verses.english: Having reposited the three sacred fires in himself, according to the prescribed rule, let him live without a fire, without a house, wholly silent, subsisting on roots and fruit,

verses.text:
अप्रयत्नः सुखार्थेषु ब्रह्मचारी धरा.आशयः ।
शरणेष्व् अ.ममश् च-एव वृक्षमूल.निकेतनः ॥ २६ ॥
verses.english: Making no effort (to procure) things that give pleasure, chaste, sleeping on the bare ground, not caring for any shelter, dwelling at the roots of trees.

verses.text:
तापसेष्व् एव विप्रेषु यात्रिकं भैक्षम् आहरेत् ।
गृहमेधिषु च-अन्येषु द्विजेषु वनवासिषु ॥ २७ ॥
verses.english: From Brahmanas (who live as) ascetics, let him receive alms, (barely sufficient) to support life, or from other householders of the twice-born (castes) who reside in the forest.

verses.text:
ग्रामाद् आहृत्य वा-अश्नीयाद् अष्टौ ग्रासान् वने वसन् ।
प्रतिगृह्य पुटेन-एव पाणिना शकलेन वा ॥ २८ ॥
verses.english: Or (the hermit) who dwells in the forest may bring (food) from a village, receiving it either in a hollow dish (of leaves), in (his naked) hand, or in a broken earthen dish, and may eat eight mouthfuls.

verses.text:
एताश् च-अन्याश् च सेवेत दीक्षा विप्रो वने वसन् ।
विविधाश् च-औपनिषदीर् आत्मसंसिद्धये श्रुतीः ॥ २९ ॥
verses.english: These and other observances must a Brahmana who dwells in the forest diligently practise, and in order to attain complete (union with) the (supreme) Soul, (he must study) the various sacred texts contained in the Upanishads,

verses.text:
ऋषिभिर् ब्राह्मणैश् च-एव गृहस्थैर् एव सेविताः ।
विद्या.तपो.विवृद्ध्यर्थं शरीरस्य च शुद्धये ॥ ३० ॥
verses.english: (As well as those rites and texts) which have been practised and studied by the sages (Rishis), and by Brahmana householders, in order to increase their knowledge (of Brahman), and their austerity, and in order to sanctify their bodies;

verses.text:
अपराजितां वा-आस्थाय व्रजेद् दिशम् अजिह्मगः ।
आ निपातात्-शरीरस्य युक्तो वारि.अनिल.अशनः ॥ ३१ ॥
verses.english: Or let him walk, fully determined and going straight on, in a north-easterly direction, subsisting on water and air, until his body sinks to rest.

verses.text:
आसां महर्षिचर्याणां त्यक्त्वा-अन्यतमया तनुम् ।
वीत.शोक.भयो विप्रो ब्रह्मलोके महीयते ॥ ३२ ॥
verses.english: A Brahmana, having got rid of his body by one of those modes practised by the great sages, is exalted in the world of Brahman, free from sorrow and fear.

verses.text:
वनेषु च विहृत्य-एवं तृतीयं भागम् आयुषः ।
चतुर्थम् आयुषो भागं त्यक्वा सङ्गान् परिव्रजेत् ॥ ३३ ॥
verses.english: But having thus passed the third part of (a man's natural term of) life in the forest, he may live as an ascetic during the fourth part of his existence, after abandoning all attachment to worldly objects.

verses.text:
आश्रमाद् आश्रमं गत्वा हुत.होमो जित.इन्द्रियः ।
भिक्षा.बलि.परिश्रान्तः प्रव्रजन् प्रेत्य वर्धते ॥ ३४ ॥
verses.english: He who after passing from order to order, after offering sacrifices and subduing his senses, becomes, tired with (giving) alms and offerings of food, an ascetic, gains bliss after death.

verses.text:
ऋणानि त्रीण्य् अपाकृत्य मनो मोक्षे निवेशयेत् ।
अन्.अपाकृत्य मोक्षं तु सेवमानो व्रजत्य् अधः ॥ ३५ ॥
verses.english: When he has paid the three debts, let him apply his mind to (the attainment of) final liberation; he who seeks it without having paid (his debts) sinks downwards.

verses.text:
अधीत्य विधिवद् वेदान् पुत्रांश् च-उत्पाद्य धर्मतः ।
इष्ट्वा च शक्तितो यज्ञैर् मनो मोक्षे निवेशयेत् ॥ ३६ ॥
verses.english: Having studied the Vedas in accordance with the rule, having begat sons according to the sacred law, and having offered sacrifices according to his ability, he may direct his mind to (the attainment of) final liberation.

verses.text:
अन्.अधीत्य द्विजो वेदान् अन्.उत्पाद्य तथा सुतान् । ६.३७अव्/ म्: तथा
                                    प्रजाम्
अन्.इष्ट्वा च-एव यज्ञैश् च मोक्षम् इच्छन् व्रजत्य् अधः ॥ ३७
                                ॥
verses.english: A twice-born man who seeks final liberation, without having studied the Vedas, without having begotten sons, and without having offered sacrifices, sinks downwards.

verses.text:
प्राजापत्यं निरुप्य-इष्टिं सर्ववेदस.दक्षिणाम् । ६.३८अव्/ म्: 
                                    सार्ववेदसदक्षिणाम्
आत्मन्य् अग्नीन् समारोप्य ब्राह्मणः प्रव्रजेद् गृहात् ॥ ३८ ॥
verses.english: Having performed the Ishti, sacred to the Lord of creatures (Pragapati), where (he gives) all his property as the sacrificial fee, having reposited the sacred fires in himself, a Brahmana may depart from his house (as an ascetic).

verses.text:
यो दत्त्वा सर्वभूतेभ्यः प्रव्रजत्य् अभयं गृहात् ।
तस्य तेजोमया लोका भवन्ति ब्रह्मवादिनः ॥ ३९ ॥
verses.english: Worlds, radiant in brilliancy, become (the portion) of him who recites (the texts regarding) Brahman and departs from his house (as an ascetic), after giving a promise of safety to all created beings.

verses.text:
यस्माद् अणु-अपि भूतानां द्विजान् न-उत्पद्यते भयम् ।
तस्य देहाद् विमुक्तस्य भयं न-अस्ति कुतश् चन ॥ ४० ॥
verses.english: For that twice-born man, by whom not the smallest danger even is caused to created beings, there will be no danger from any (quarter), after he is freed from his body.

verses.text:
अगाराद् अभिनिष्क्रान्तः पवित्र.उपचितो मुनिः ।
समुपोढेषु कामेषु निर्.अपेक्षः परिव्रजेत् ॥ ४१ ॥
verses.english: Departing from his house fully provided with the means of purification (Pavitra), let him wander about absolutely silent, and caring nothing for enjoyments that may be offered (to him).

verses.text:
एक एव चरेन् नित्यं सिद्ध्यर्थम् असहायवान् ।
सिद्धिम् एकस्य सम्पश्यन् न जहाति न हीयते ॥ ४२ ॥ ६.४२च्व्/ म्: 
                                    सिद्धम् ॥ 6.42 ॥
verses.english: Let him always wander alone, without any companion, in order to attain (final liberation), fully understanding that the solitary (man, who) neither forsakes nor is forsaken, gains his end.

verses.text:
अन्.अग्निर् अ.निकेतः स्याद् ग्रामम् अन्नार्थम् आश्रयेत् ।
उपेक्षको ऽ.सङ्कुसुको मुनिर् भावसमाहितः ॥ ४३ ॥ ६.४३च्व्/ म्: 
                                    अ.साङ्कुसुको ॥ 6.43 ॥
verses.english: He shall neither possess a fire, nor a dwelling, he may go to a village for his food, (he shall be) indifferent to everything, firm of purpose, meditating (and) concentrating his mind on Brahman.

verses.text:
कपालं वृक्षमूलानि कुचेलम् असहायता । ६.४४अव्/ म्: कुचैलम्
समता च-एव सर्वस्मिन्न् एतत्-मुक्तस्य लक्षणम् ॥ ४४ ॥
verses.english: A potsherd (instead of an alms-bowl), the roots of trees (for a dwelling), coarse worn-out garments, life in solitude and indifference towards everything, are the marks of one who has attained liberation.

verses.text:
न-अभिनन्देत मरणं न-अभिनन्देत जीवितम् ।
कालम् एव प्रतीक्षेत निर्वेशं भृतको यथा ॥ ४५ ॥
verses.english: Let him not desire to die, let him not desire to live; let him wait for (his appointed) time, as a servant (waits) for the payment of his wages.

verses.text:
दृष्टिपूतं न्यसेत् पादं वस्त्रपूतं जलं पिबेत् ।
सत्यपूतां वदेद् वाचं मनःपूतं समाचरेत् ॥ ४६ ॥
verses.english: Let him put down his foot purified by his sight, let him drink water purified by (straining with) a cloth, let him utter speech purified by truth, let him keep his heart pure.

verses.text:
अतिवादांस् तितिक्षेत न-अवमन्येत कं चन ।
न च-इमं देहम् आश्रित्य वैरं कुर्वीत केन चित् ॥ ४७ ॥
verses.english: Let him patiently bear hard words, let him not insult anybody, and let him not become anybody's enemy for the sake of this (perishable) body.

verses.text:
क्रुद्ध्यन्तं न प्रतिक्रुध्येद् आक्रुष्टः कुशलं वदेत् ।
सप्तद्वारावकीर्णां च न वाचम् अनृतां वदेत् ॥ ४८ ॥
verses.english: Against an angry man let him not in return show anger, let him bless when he is cursed, and let him not utter speech, devoid of truth, scattered at the seven gates.

verses.text:
अध्यात्म.रतिर् आसीनो निर्.अपेक्षो निर्.आमिषः ।
आत्मना-एव सहायेन सुखार्थी विचरेद् इह ॥ ४९ ॥
verses.english: Delighting in what refers to the Soul, sitting (in the postures prescribed by the Yoga), independent (of external help), entirely abstaining from sensual enjoyments, with himself for his only companion, he shall live in this world, desiring the bliss (of final liberation).

verses.text:
न च-उत्पात.निमित्ताभ्यां न नक्षत्र.अङ्गविद्यया ।
न-अनुशासन.वादाभ्यां भिक्षां लिप्सेत कर्हि चित् ॥ ५० ॥
verses.english: Neither by (explaining) prodigies and omens, nor by skill in astrology and palmistry, nor by giving advice and by the exposition (of the Sastras), let him ever seek to obtain alms.

verses.text:
न तापसैर् ब्राह्मणैर् वा वयोभिर् अपि वा श्वभिः ।
