आकीर्णं भिक्षुकैर् वा-अन्यैर् अगारम् उपसंव्रजेत् ॥ ५१ ॥
verses.english: Let him not (in order to beg) go near a house filled with hermits, Brahmanas, birds, dogs, or other mendicants.

verses.text:
कॢप्त.केश.नख.श्मश्रुः पात्री दण्डी कुसुम्भवान् ।
विचरेन् नियतो नित्यं सर्वभूतान्य् अ.पीडयन् ॥ ५२ ॥
verses.english: His hair, nails, and beard being clipped, carrying an alms-bowl, a staff, and a water-pot, let him continually wander about, controlling himself and not hurting any creature.

verses.text:
अतैजसानि पात्राणि तस्य स्युर् निर्.व्रणानि च ।
तेषाम् अद्भिः स्मृतं शौचं चमसानाम् इव-अध्वरे ॥ ५३ ॥
verses.english: His vessels shall not be made of metal, they shall be free from fractures; it is ordained that they shall be cleansed with water, like (the cups, called) Kamasa, at a sacrifice.

verses.text:
अलाबुं दारुपात्रं च मृण्मयं वैदलं तथा ।
एताणि यतिपात्राणि मनुः स्वायम्भुवो ऽब्रवीत् ॥ ५४ ॥
verses.english: A gourd, a wooden bowl, an earthen (dish), or one made of split cane, Manu, the son of Svayambhu, has declared (to be) vessels (suitable) for an ascetic.

verses.text:
एककालं चरेद् भैक्षं न प्रसज्जेत विस्तरे ।
भैक्षे प्रसक्तो हि यतिर् विषयेष्व् अपि सज्जति ॥ ५५ ॥
verses.english: Let him go to beg once (a day), let him not be eager to obtain a large quantity (of alms); for an ascetic who eagerly seeks alms, attaches himself also to sensual enjoyments.

verses.text:
वि.धूमे सन्न.मुसले व्य्.अङ्गारे भुक्तवज्.जने ।
वृत्ते शरावसम्पाते भिक्षां नित्यं यतिश् चरेत् ॥ ५६ ॥
verses.english: When no smoke ascends from (the kitchen), when the pestle lies motionless, when the embers have been extinguished, when the people have finished their meal, when the remnants in the dishes have been removed, let the ascetic always go to beg.

verses.text:
अलाभे न विषदी स्यात्-लाभे च-एव न हर्षयेत् ।
प्राणयात्रिक.मात्रः स्यात्-मात्रासङ्गाद् विनिर्गतः ॥ ५७ ॥
verses.english: Let him not be sorry when he obtains nothing, nor rejoice when he obtains (something), let him (accept) so much only as will sustain life, let him not care about the (quality of his) utensils.

verses.text:
अभिपूजितलाभांस् तु जुगुप्सेत-एव सर्वशः ।
अभिपूजितलाभैश् च यतिर् मुक्तो ऽपि बध्यते ॥ ५८ ॥
verses.english: Let him disdain all (food) obtained in consequence of humble salutations, (for) even an ascetic who has attained final liberation, is bound (with the fetters of the Samsara) by accepting (food given) in consequence of humble salutations.

verses.text:
अल्पान्नाभ्यवहारेण रहःस्थान.आसनेन च ।
ह्रियमाणानि विषयैर् इन्द्रियाणि निवर्तयेत् ॥ ५९ ॥
verses.english: By eating little, and by standing and sitting in solitude, let him restrain his senses, if they are attracted by sensual objects.

verses.text:
इन्द्रियाणां निरोधेन राग.द्वेश.क्षयेण च ।
अहिंसया च भूतानाम् अमृतत्वाय कल्पते ॥ ६० ॥
verses.english: By the restraint of his senses, by the destruction of love and hatred, and by the abstention from injuring the creatures, he becomes fit for immortality.

verses.text:
अवेक्षेत गतीर् नॄणां कर्मदोष.समुद्भवाः ।
निरये च-एव पतनं यातनाश् च यमक्षये ॥ ६१ ॥
verses.english: Let him reflect on the transmigrations of men, caused by their sinful deeds, on their falling into hell, and on the torments in the world of Yama,

verses.text:
विप्रयोगं प्रियैश् च-एव संयोगं च तथा-अप्रियैः ।
जरया च-अभिभवनं व्याधिभिश् च-उपपीडनं ॥ ६२ ॥
verses.english: On the separation from their dear ones, on their union with hated men, on their being overpowered by age and being tormented with diseases,

verses.text:
देहाद् उत्क्रमणं च-अष्मात् पुनर् गर्भे च सम्भवम् ।
योनिकोटिसहस्रेषु सृतीश् च-अस्य-अन्तरात्मनः ॥ ६३ ॥
verses.english: On the departure of the individual soul from this body and its new birth in (another) womb, and on its wanderings through ten thousand millions of existences,

verses.text:
अधर्म.प्रभवं च-एव दुःखयोगं शरीरिणाम् ।
धर्मार्थ.प्रभवं च-एव सुखसंयोगम् अक्षयम् ॥ ६४
                                ॥
verses.english: On the infliction of pain on embodied (spirits), which is caused by demerit, and the gain of eternal bliss, which is caused by the attainment of their highest aim, (gained through) spiritual merit.

verses.text:
सूक्ष्मतां च-अन्ववेक्षेत योगेन परमात्मनः ।
देहेषु च समुत्पत्तिम् उत्तमेष्व् अधमेषु च ॥ ६५ ॥ ६.६५च्व्/ म्: देहेषु
                                    चैवोपपत्तिम् ॥ 6.65 ॥
verses.english: By deep meditation let him recognise the subtile nature of the supreme Soul, and its presence in all organisms, both the highest and the lowest.

verses.text:
दूषितो ऽपि चरेद् धर्मं यत्र तत्र-आश्रमे रतः । ६.६६अव्/ म्: 
                                        भूषितो ऽपि
समः सर्वेषु भूतेषु न लिङ्गं धर्मकारणम् ॥ ६६
                                    ॥
verses.english: To whatever order he may be attached, let him, though blemished (by a want of the external marks), fulfil his duty, equal-minded towards all creatures; (for) the external mark (of the order) is not the cause of (the acquisition of) merit.

verses.text:
फलं कतकवृक्षस्य यद्य् अप्य् अम्बुप्रसादकम् ।
न नामग्रहणाद् एव तस्य वारि प्रसीदति ॥ ६७ ॥
verses.english: Though the fruit of the Kataka tree (the clearing-nut) makes water clear, yet the (latter) does not become limpid in consequence of the mention of the (fruit's) name.

verses.text:
संरक्षणार्थं जन्तूनां रात्राव् अहनि वा सदा ।
शरीरस्य-अत्यये च-एव समीक्ष्य वसुधां चरेत् ॥ ६८
                                    ॥
verses.english: In order to preserve living creatures, let him always by day and by night, even with pain to his body, walk, carefully scanning the ground.

verses.text:
अह्ना रात्र्या च याञ् जन्तून् हिनस्त्य् अज्ञानतो यतिः ।
तेषां स्नात्वा विशुद्ध्यर्थं प्राणायामान् षड् आचरेत् ॥ ६९
                                    ॥
verses.english: In order to expiate (the death) of those creatures which he unintentionally injures by day or by night, an ascetic shall bathe and perform six suppressions of the breath.

verses.text:
प्राणायामा ब्राह्मणस्य त्रयो ऽपि विधिवत् कृताः ।
व्याहृति.प्रणवैर् युक्ता विज्ञेयं परमं तपः ॥ ७०
                                    ॥
verses.english: Three suppressions of the breath even, performed according to the rule, and accompanied with the (recitation of the) Vyahritis and of the syllable Om, one must know to be the highest (form of) austerity for every Brahmana.

verses.text:
दह्यन्ते ध्मायमानानां धातूनां हि यथा मलाः ।
तथा-इन्द्रियाणां दह्यन्ते दोषाः प्राणस्य निग्रहात् ॥ ७१
                                    ॥
verses.english: For as the impurities of metallic ores, melted in the blast (of a furnace), are consumed, even so the taints of the organs are destroyed through the suppression of the breath.

verses.text:
प्राणायमैर् दहेद् दोषान् धारणाभिश् च किल्बिषम् ।
प्रत्याहारेण संसर्गान् ध्यानेन-अन्.ईश्वरान् गुणान् ॥ ७२
                                    ॥
verses.english: Let him destroy the taints through suppressions of the breath, (the production of) sin by fixed attention, all sensual attachments by restraining (his senses and organs), and all qualities that are not lordly by meditation.

verses.text:
उच्चावचेषु भूतेषु दुर्ज्ञेयाम् अकृत.आत्मभिः ।
ध्यानयोगेन सम्पश्येद् गतिम् अस्य-अन्तरात्मनः ॥ ७३
                                    ॥
verses.english: Let him recognise by the practice of meditation the progress of the individual soul through beings of various kinds, (a progress) hard to understand for unregenerate men.

verses.text:
सम्यग्दर्शनसम्पन्नः कर्मभिर् न निबध्यते ।
दर्शनेन विहीनस् तु संसारं प्रतिपद्यते ॥ ७४ ॥
verses.english: He who possesses the true insight (into the nature of the world), is not fettered by his deeds; but he who is destitute of that insight, is drawn into the circle of births and deaths.

verses.text:
अहिंसया-इन्द्रिय.अ.सङ्गैर् वैदिकैश् च-एव कर्मभिः
                                    ।
तपसश् चरणैश् च-उग्रैः साधयन्ति-इह तत्पदम् ॥ ७५
                                    ॥
verses.english: By not injuring any creatures, by detaching the senses (from objects of enjoyment), by the rites prescribed in the Veda, and by rigorously practising austerities, (men) gain that state (even) in this (world).

verses.text:
अस्थि.स्थूणं स्नायुयुतं मांस.शोणित.लेपनम् ।
चर्मावनद्धं दुर्.गन्धि पूर्णं मूत्र.पुरीषयोः ॥ ७६
                                    ॥

जरा.शोकसमाविष्टं रोगायतनम् आतुरम् ।
रजस्वलम् अनित्यं च भूतावासम् इमं त्यजेत् ॥ ७७ ॥

नदीकूलं यथा वृक्षो वृक्षं वा शकुनिर् यथा ।
तथा त्यजन्न् इमं देहं कृच्छ्राद् ग्राहाद् विमुच्यते ॥ ७८
                                    ॥
verses.english: He who leaves this body, (be it by necessity) as a tree (that is torn from) the river-bank, or (freely) like a bird (that) quits a tree, is freed from the misery (of this world, dreadful like) a shark.

verses.text:
प्रियेषु स्वेषु सुकृतम् अप्रियेषु च दुष्कृतम् ।
विसृज्य ध्यानयोगेन ब्रह्म-अभ्येति सनातनम् ॥ ७९
                                    ॥
verses.english: Making over (the merit of his own) good actions to his friends and (the guilt of) his evil deeds to his enemies, he attains the eternal Brahman by the practice of meditation.

verses.text:
यदा भावेन भवति सर्वभावेषु निःस्पृहः ।
तदा सुखम् अवाप्नोति प्रेत्य च-इह च शाश्वतम् ॥ ८०
                                    ॥
verses.english: When by the disposition (of his heart) he becomes indifferent to all objects, he obtains eternal happiness both in this world and after death.

verses.text:
अनेन विधिना सर्वांस् त्यक्त्वा सङ्गान्-शनैः शनैः ।
सर्वद्वन्द्वविनिर्मुक्तो ब्रह्मण्य् एव-अवतिष्ठते ॥ ८१
                                    ॥
verses.english: He who has in this manner gradually given up all attachments and is freed from all the pairs (of opposites), reposes in Brahman alone.

verses.text:
ध्यानिकं सर्वम् एव-एतद् यद् एतद् अभिशब्दितम् ।
न ह्य् अन्.अध्यात्मवित् कश् चित् क्रियाफलम् उपाश्नुते ॥ ८२
                                    ॥
verses.english: All that has been declared (above) depends on meditation; for he who is not proficient in the knowledge of that which refers to the Soul reaps not the full reward of the performance of rites.

verses.text:
अधियज्ञं ब्रह्म जपेद् आधिदैविकम् एव च ।
आध्यात्मिकं च सततं वेदान्ताभिहितं च यत् ॥ ८३
                                    ॥
verses.english: Let him constantly recite (those texts of) the Veda which refer to the sacrifice, (those) referring to the deities, and (those) which treat of the Soul and are contained in the concluding portions of the Veda (Vedanta).

verses.text:
इदं शरणम् अज्ञानाम् इदम् एव विजानताम् ।
इदम् अन्विच्छतां स्वर्गम् इदम् आनन्त्यम् इच्छताम् ॥ ८४
                                    ॥
verses.english: That is the refuge of the ignorant, and even that (the refuse) of those who know (the meaning of the Veda); that is (the protection) of those who seek (bliss in) heaven and of those who seek endless (beatitude).

verses.text:
अनेन क्रमयोगेन परिव्रजति यो द्विजः ।
स विधूय-इह पाप्मानं परं ब्रह्म-अधिगच्छति ॥ ८५
                                    ॥
verses.english: A twice-born man who becomes an ascetic, after the successive performance of the above-mentioned acts, shakes off sin here below and reaches the highest Brahman.

verses.text:
एष धर्मो ऽनुशिष्टो वो यतीनां नियत.आत्मनाम् ।
वेदसन्न्यासिकानां तु कर्मयोगं निबोधत ॥ ८६ ॥
verses.english: Thus the law (valid) for self-restrained ascetics has been explained to you; now listen to the (particular) duties of those who give up (the rites prescribed by) the Veda.

verses.text:
ब्रह्मचारी गृहस्थश् च वानप्रस्थो यतिस् तथा ।
एते गृहस्थ.प्रभवाश् चत्वारः पृथग् आश्रमाः ॥ ८७ ॥
verses.english: The student, the householder, the hermit, and the ascetic, these (constitute) four separate orders, which all spring from (the order of) householders.

verses.text:
सर्वे ऽपि क्रमशस् त्व् एते यथाशास्त्रं निषेविताः ।
यथा.उक्त.कारिणं विप्रं नयन्ति परमां गतिम् ॥ ८८ ॥
verses.english: But all (or) even (any of) these orders, assumed successively in accordance with the Institutes (of the sacred law), lead the Brahmana who acts by the preceding (rules) to the highest state.

verses.text:
सर्वेषाम् अपि च-एतेषां वेद.स्मृतिविधानतः । ६.८९अव्/ म्: 
                                    वेद.श्रुतिविधानतः
गृहस्थ उच्यते श्रेष्ठः स त्रीन् एतान् बिभर्ति हि ॥ ८९
                                ॥
verses.english: And in accordance with the precepts of the Veda and of the Smriti, the housekeeper is declared to be superior to all of them; for he supports the other three.

verses.text:
यथा नदी.नदाः सर्वे सागरे यान्ति संस्थितिम् ।
तथा-एव-आश्रमिणः सर्वे गृहस्थे यान्ति संस्थितिम् ॥ ९०
                                ॥
verses.english: As all rivers, both great and small, find a resting-place in the ocean, even so men of all orders find protection with householders

verses.text:
चतुर्भिर् अपि च-एव-एतैर् नित्यम् आश्रमिभिर् द्विजैः ।
दश.लक्षणको धर्मः सेवितव्यः प्रयत्नतः ॥ ९१ ॥
verses.english: By twice-born men belonging to (any of) these four orders, the tenfold law must be ever carefully obeyed.

verses.text:
धृतिः क्षमा दमो ऽस्तेयं शौचम् इन्द्रियनिग्रहः ।
धीर् विद्या सत्यम् अक्रोधो दशकं धर्मलक्षणम् ॥ ९२ ॥
verses.english: Contentment, forgiveness, self-control, abstention from unrighteously appropriating anything, (obedience to the rules of) purification, coercion of the organs, wisdom, knowledge (of the supreme Soul), truthfulness, and abstention from anger, (form) the tenfold law.

verses.text:
दश लक्षणानि धर्मस्य ये विप्राः समधीयते ।
अधीत्य च-अनुवर्तन्ते ते यान्ति परमां गतिम् ॥ ९३ ॥
verses.english: Those Brahmanas who thoroughly study the tenfold law, and after studying obey it, enter the highest state.

verses.text:
दश.लक्षणकं धर्मम् अनुतिष्ठन् समाहितः ।
वेदान्तं विधिवत्-श्रुत्वा सन्न्यसेद् अन्.ऋणो द्विजः ॥ ९४ ॥
verses.english: A twice-born man who, with collected mind, follows the tenfold law and has paid his (three) debts, may, after learning the Vedanta according to the prescribed rule, become an ascetic.

verses.text:
सन्न्यस्य सर्वकर्माणि कर्मदोषान् अपानुदन् ।
नियतो वेदम् अभ्यस्य पुत्रैश्वर्ये सुखं वसेत् ॥ ९५ ॥
verses.english: Having given up (the performance of) all rites, throwing off the guilt of his (sinful) acts, subduing his organs and having studied the Veda, he may live at his ease under the protection of his son.

verses.text:
एवं सन्न्यस्य कर्माणि स्वकार्य.परमो ऽ.स्पृहः ।
सन्न्यासेन-अपहत्य-एनः प्राप्नोति परमं गतिम् ॥ ९६ ॥
verses.english: He who has thus given up (the performance of) all rites, who is solely intent on his own (particular) object, (and) free from desires, destroys his guilt by his renunciation and obtains the highest state.

verses.text:
एष वो ऽभिहितो धर्मो ब्राह्मणस्य चतुर्.विधः ।
पुण्यो ऽक्षय.फलः प्रेत्य राज्ञां धर्मं निबोधत ॥ ९७
                                ॥
verses.english: Thus the fourfold holy law of Brahmanas, which after death (yields) imperishable rewards, has been declared to you; now learn the duty of kings.

verses.text:
राजधर्मान् प्रवक्ष्यामि यथावृत्तो भवेन् नृपः ।
सम्भवश् च यथा तस्य सिद्धिश् च परमा यथा ॥ १ ॥
verses.english: I will declare the duties of kings, (and) show how a king should conduct himself, how he was created, and how (he can obtain) highest success.

verses.text:
ब्राह्मं प्राप्तेन संस्कारं क्षत्रियेण यथाविधि ।
सर्वस्य-अस्य यथान्यायं कर्तव्यं परिरक्षणम् ॥ २ ॥
verses.english: A Kshatriya, who has received according to the rule the sacrament prescribed by the Veda, must duly protect this whole (world).

verses.text:
अ.राजके हि लोके ऽस्मिन् सर्वतो विद्रुतो भयात् ।
रक्षार्थम् अस्य सर्वस्य राजानम् असृजत् प्रभुः ॥ ३ ॥
verses.english: For, when these creatures, being without a king, through fear dispersed in all directions, the Lord created a king for the protection of this whole (creation),

verses.text:
इन्द्र.अनिल.यम.अर्काणाम् अग्नेश् च वरुणस्य च ।
चन्द्र.वित्तेशयोश् च-एव मात्रा निर्हृत्य शाश्वतीः ॥ ४ ॥
verses.english: Taking (for that purpose) eternal particles of Indra, of the Wind, of Yama, of the Sun, of Fire, of Varuna, of the Moon, and of the Lord of wealth (Kubera).

verses.text:
यस्माद् एषां सुरेन्द्राणां मात्राभ्यो निर्मितो नृपः ।
तस्माद् अभिभवत्य् एष सर्वभूतानि तेजसा ॥ ५ ॥
verses.english: Because a king has been formed of particles of those lords of the gods, he therefore surpasses all created beings in lustre;

verses.text:
तपत्य् आदित्यवच् च-एष चक्षूंषि च मनांसि च ।
न च-एनं भुवि शक्नोति कश् चिद् अप्य् अभिवीक्षितुम् ॥ ६ ॥
verses.english: And, like the sun, he burns eyes and hearts; nor can anybody on earth even gaze on him.

verses.text:
सो ऽग्निर् भवति वायुश् च सो ऽर्कः सोमः स धर्मराट् ।
स कुबेरः स वरुणः स महेन्द्रः प्रभावतः ॥ ७ ॥ ७.०७च्व्/ म्: स
                                    च-इन्द्रः स्वप्रभावतः ॥ 7.7 ॥
verses.english: Through his (supernatural) power he is Fire and Wind, he Sun and Moon, he the Lord of justice (Yama), he Kubera, he Varuna, he great Indra.

verses.text:
बालो ऽपि न-अवमान्तव्यो मनुष्य इति भूमिपः ।
महती देवता ह्य् एषा नररूपेण तिष्ठति ॥ ८ ॥
verses.english: Even an infant king must not be despised, (from an idea) that he is a (mere) mortal; for he is a great deity in human form.

verses.text:
एकम् एव दहत्य् अग्निर् नरं दुरुपसर्पिणम् ।
कुलं दहति राजा-अग्निः स.पशु.द्रव्यसञ्चयम् ॥ ९ ॥
verses.english: Fire burns one man only, if he carelessly approaches it, the fire of a king's (anger) consumes the (whole) family, together with its cattle and its hoard of property.

verses.text:
कार्यं सो ऽवेक्ष्य शक्तिं च देश.कालौ च तत्त्वतः ।
कुरुते धर्मसिद्ध्यर्थं विश्वरूपं पुनः पुनः ॥ १० ॥
verses.english: Having fully considered the purpose, (his) power, and the place and the time, he assumes by turns many (different) shapes for the complete attainment of justice.

verses.text:
यस्य प्रसादे पद्मा श्रीर् विजयश् च पराक्रमे ।
मृत्युश् च वसति क्रोधे सर्वतेजोमयो हि सः ॥ ११ ॥
verses.english: He, in whose favour resides Padma, the goddess of fortune, in whose valour dwells victory, in whose anger abides death, is formed of the lustre of all (gods).

verses.text:
तं यस् तु द्वेष्टि सम्मोहात् स विनश्यत्य् असंशयम् ।
तस्य ह्य् आशु विनाशाय राजा प्रकुरुते मनः ॥ १२ ॥
verses.english: The (man), who in his exceeding folly hates him, will doubtlessly perish; for the king quickly makes up his mind to destroy such (a man).

verses.text:
तस्माद् धर्मं यम् इष्टेषु स व्यवस्येन् नराधिपः ।
अनिष्टं च-अप्य् अनिष्टेषु तं धर्मं न विचालयेत् ॥ १३ ॥
verses.english: Let no (man), therefore, transgress that law which favourites, nor (his orders) which inflict pain on those in disfavour.

verses.text:
तस्यार्थे सर्वभूतानां गोप्तारं धर्मम् आत्मजम् । ७.१४अव्/ म्: 
                                        तदर्थं
ब्रह्मतेजोमयं दण्डम् असृजत् पूर्वम् ईश्वरः ॥ १४ ॥
verses.english: For the (king's) sake the Lord formerly created his own son, Punishment, the protector of all creatures, (an incarnation of) the law, formed of Brahman's glory.

verses.text:
तस्य सर्वाणि भूतानि स्थावराणि चराणि च ।
भयाद् भोगाय कल्पन्ते स्वधर्मात्-न चलन्ति च ॥ १५
                                    ॥
verses.english: Through fear of him all created beings, both the immovable and the movable, allow themselves to be enjoyed and swerve not from their duties.

verses.text:
तं देश.कालौ शक्तिं च विद्यां च-अवेक्ष्य तत्त्वतः
                                    ।
यथार्हतः सम्प्रणयेन् नरेष्व् अन्याय.वर्तिषु ॥ १६
                                    ॥
verses.english: Having fully considered the time and the place (of the offence), the strength and the knowledge (of the offender), let him justly inflict that (punishment) on men who act unjustly.

verses.text:
स राजा पुरुषो दण्डः स नेता शासिता च सः ।
चतुर्णाम् आश्रमाणां च धर्मस्य प्रतिभूः स्मृतः ॥ १७
                                    ॥
verses.english: Punishment is (in reality) the king (and) the male, that the manager of affairs, that the ruler, and that is called the surety for the four orders' obedience to the law.

verses.text:
दण्डः शास्ति प्रजाः सर्वा दण्ड एव-अभिरक्षति ।
दण्डः सुप्तेषु जागर्ति दण्डं धर्मं विदुर् बुधाः ॥ १८
                                    ॥
verses.english: Punishment alone governs all created beings, punishment alone protects them, punishment watches over them while they sleep; the wise declare punishment (to be identical with) the law.

verses.text:
समीक्ष्य स धृतः सम्यक् सर्वा रञ्जयति प्रजाः ।
अ.समीक्ष्य प्रणीतस् तु विनाशयति सर्वतः ॥ १९ ॥
verses.english: If (punishment) is properly inflicted after (due) consideration, it makes all people happy; but inflicted without consideration, it destroys everything.

verses.text:
यदि न प्रणयेद् राजा दण्डं दण्ड्येष्व् अतन्द्रितः ।
शूले मत्स्यान् इव-अपक्ष्यन् दुर्बलान् बलवत्तराः ॥ २०
                                    ॥
verses.english: If the king did not, without tiring, inflict punishment on those worthy to be punished, the stronger would roast the weaker, like fish on a spit;

verses.text:
अद्यात् काकः पुरोडाशं श्वा च लिह्याद्द् हविस् तथा । ७.२१अव्/ म्: 
                                        श्वा-अवलिह्याद्द्
स्वाम्यं च न स्यात् कस्मिंश् चित् प्रवर्तेत-अधर.उत्तरम्
                                    ॥ २१ ॥
verses.english: The crow would eat the sacrificial cake and the dog would lick the sacrificial viands, and ownership would not remain with any one, the lower ones would (usurp the place of) the higher ones.

verses.text:
सर्वो दण्डजितो लोको दुर्लभो हि शुचिर् नरः ।
दण्डस्य हि भयात् सर्वं जगद् भोगाय कल्पते ॥ २२
                                    ॥
verses.english: The whole world is kept in order by punishment, for a guiltless man is hard to find; through fear of punishment the whole world yields the enjoyments (which it owes).

verses.text:
देव.दानव.गन्धर्वा रक्षांसि पतग.उरगाः ।
ते ऽपि भोगाय कल्पन्ते दण्डेन-एव निपीडिताः ॥ २३
                                    ॥
verses.english: The gods, the Danavas, the Gandharvas, the Rakshasas, the bird and snake deities even give the enjoyments (due from them) only, if they are tormented by (the fear of) punishment.

verses.text:
दुष्येयुः सर्ववर्णाश् च भिद्येरन् सर्वसेतवः ।
सर्वलोकप्रकोपश् च भवेद् दण्डस्य विभ्रमात् ॥ २४
                                    ॥
verses.english: All castes (varna) would be corrupted (by intermixture), all barriers would be broken through, and all men would rage (against each other) in consequence of mistakes with respect to punishment.

verses.text:
यत्र श्यामो लोहित.अक्षो दण्डश् चरति पापहा ।
प्रजास् तत्र न मुह्यन्ति नेता चेत् साधु पश्यति ॥ २५
                                    ॥
verses.english: But where Punishment with a black hue and red eyes stalks about, destroying sinners, there the subjects are not disturbed, provided that he who inflicts it discerns well.

verses.text:
तस्य-आहुः सम्प्रणेतारं राजानं सत्यवादिनम् ।
समीक्ष्यकारिणं प्राज्ञं धर्म.काम.अर्थ.कोविदम् ॥ २६
                                    ॥
verses.english: They declare that king to be a just inflicter of punishment, who is truthful, who acts after due consideration, who is wise, and who knows (the respective value of) virtue, pleasure, and wealth.

verses.text:
तं राजा प्रणयन् सम्यक् त्रिवर्गेण-अभिवर्धते ।
काम.आत्मा विषमः क्षुद्रो दण्डेन-एव निहन्यते ॥ २७ ॥
                                        ७.२७च्व्/
                                        म्: काम.अन्धो ॥ 7.27 ॥
verses.english: A king who properly inflicts (punishment), prospers with respect to (those) three (means of happiness); but he who is voluptuous, partial, and deceitful will be destroyed, even through the (unjust) punishment (which he inflicts).

verses.text:
दण्डो हि सुमहत्.तेजो दुर्धरश् च-अकृत.आत्मभिः ।
धर्माद् विचलितं हन्ति नृपम् एव स.बान्धवम् ॥ २८
                                    ॥
verses.english: Punishment (possesses) a very bright lustre, and is hard to be administered by men with unimproved minds; it strikes down the king who swerves from his duty, together with his relatives.

verses.text:
ततो दुर्गं च राष्ट्रं च लोकं च स.चर.अचरम् ।
अन्तरिक्षगतांश् च-एव मुनीन् देवांश् च पीडयेत् ॥ २९
                                    ॥
verses.english: Next it will afflict his castles, his territories, the whole world together with the movable and immovable (creation), likewise the sages and the gods, who (on the failure of offerings) ascend to the sky.

verses.text:
सो ऽसहायेन मूढेन लुब्धेन-अकृत.बुद्धिना ।
न शक्यो न्यायतो नेतुं सक्तेन विषयेषु च ॥ ३० ॥
verses.english: (Punishment) cannot be inflicted justly by one who has no assistant, (nor) by a fool, (nor) by a covetous man, (nor) by one whose mind is unimproved, (nor) by one addicted to sensual pleasures.

verses.text:
शुचिना सत्यसन्धेन यथाशास्त्र.अनुसारिणा ।
प्रणेतुं शक्यते दण्डः सुसहायेन धीमता ॥ ३१ ॥
verses.english: By him who is pure (and) faithful to his promise, who acts according to the Institutes (of the sacred law), who has good assistants and is wise, punishment can be (justly) inflicted.

verses.text:
स्वराष्ट्रे न्यायवृत्तः स्याद् भृश.दण्डश् च शत्रुषु ।
सुहृत्स्व् अजिह्मः स्निग्धेषु ब्राह्मणेषु क्षमान्वितः ॥ ३२
                                    ॥
verses.english: Let him act with justice in his own domain, with rigour chastise his enemies, behave without duplicity towards his friends, and be lenient towards Brahmanas.

verses.text:
एवंवृत्तस्य नृपतेः शिला.उञ्छेन-अपि जीवतः ।
विस्तीर्यते यशो लोके तैलबिन्दुर् इव-अम्भसि ॥ ३३ ॥
verses.english: The fame of a king who behaves thus, even though he subsist by gleaning, is spread in the world, like a drop of oil on water.

verses.text:
अतस् तु विपरीतस्य नृपतेर् अजित.आत्मनः ।
सङ्क्षिप्यते यशो लोके घृतबिन्दुर् इव-अम्भसि ॥ ३४
                                    ॥
verses.english: But the fame of a king who acts in a contrary manner and who does not subdue himself, diminishes in extent among men like a drop of clarified butter in water.

verses.text:
स्वे स्वे धर्मे निविष्टानां सर्वेषाम् अनुपूर्वशः ।
वर्णानाम् आश्रमाणां च राजा सृष्टो ऽभिरक्षिता ॥ ३५ ॥
verses.english: The king has been created (to be) the protector of the castes (varna) and orders, who, all according to their rank, discharge their several duties.

verses.text:
तेन यद् यत् स.भृत्येन कर्तव्यं रक्षता प्रजाः ।
तत् तद् वो ऽहं प्रवक्ष्यामि यथावद् अनुपूर्वशः ॥ ३६
                                    ॥
verses.english: Whatever must be done by him and by his servants for the protection of his people, that I will fully declare to you in due order.

verses.text:
ब्राह्मणान् पर्युपासीत प्रातर् उत्थाय पार्थिवः ।
त्रैविद्यवृद्धान् विदुषस् तिष्ठेत् तेषां च शासने ॥ ३७ ॥
verses.english: Let the king, after rising early in the morning, worship Brahmanas who are well versed in the threefold sacred science and learned (in polity), and follow their advice.

verses.text:
वृद्धांश् च नित्यं सेवेत विप्रान् वेदविदः शुचीन् ।
वृद्धसेवी हि सततं रक्षोभिर् अपि पूज्यते ॥ ३८ ॥
verses.english: Let him daily worship aged Brahmanas who know the Veda and are pure; for he who always worships aged men, is honoured even by Rakshasas.

verses.text:
तेभ्यो ऽधिगच्छेद् विनयं विनीत.आत्मा-अपि नित्यशः ।
विनीत.आत्मा हि नृपतिर् न विनश्यति कर्हि चित् ॥ ३९ ॥
verses.english: Let him, though he may already be modest, constantly learn modesty from them; for a king who is modest never perishes.

verses.text:
बहवो ऽविनयात्-नष्टा राजानः स.परिच्छदाः । ७.४०अव्/ म्: 
                                    स.परिग्रहाः
वनस्था अपि राज्यानि विनयात् प्रतिपेदिरे ॥ ४० ॥
verses.english: Through a want of modesty many kings have perished, together with their belongings; through modesty even hermits in the forest have gained kingdoms.

verses.text:
वेनो विनष्टो ऽविनयात्-नहुषश् च-एव पार्थिवः ।
सुदाः पैजवनश् च-एव सुमुखो निमिर् एव च ॥ ४१ ॥
verses.english: Through a want of humility Vena perished, likewise king Nahusha, Sudas, the son of Pigavana, Sumukha, and Nemi.

verses.text:
पृथुस् तु विनयाद् राज्यं प्राप्तवान् मनुर् एव च ।
कुबेरश् च धनैश्वर्यं ब्राह्मण्यं च-एव गाधिजः ॥ ४२
                                ॥
verses.english: But by humility Prithu and Manu gained sovereignty, Kubera the position of the Lord of wealth, and the son of Gadhi the rank of a Brahmana.

verses.text:
त्रैविद्येभ्यस् त्रयीं विद्यां दण्डनीतिं च शाश्वतीम् । ७.४३अव्/ म्: त्रयीं
                                    विद्यात्
आन्वीक्षिकीं च-आत्मविद्यां वार्तारम्भांश् च लोकतः ॥ ४३
                                ॥
verses.english: From those versed in the three Vedas let him learn the threefold (sacred science), the primeval science of government, the science of dialectics, and the knowledge of the (supreme) Soul; from the people (the theory of) the (various) trades and professions.

verses.text:
इन्द्रियाणां जये योगं समातिष्ठेद् दिवा.निशम् ।
जित.इन्द्रियो हि शक्नोति वशे स्थापयितुं प्रजाः ॥ ४४ ॥
verses.english: Day and night he must strenuously exert himself to conquer his senses; for he (alone) who has conquered his own senses, can keep his subjects in obedience.

verses.text:
दश काम.समुत्थानि तथा-अष्टौ क्रोधजानि च ।
व्यसनानि दुर्.अन्तानि प्रयत्नेन विवर्जयेत् ॥ ४५ ॥
verses.english: Let him carefully shun the ten vices, springing from love of pleasure, and the eight, proceeding from wrath, which (all) end in misery.

verses.text:
कामजेषु प्रसक्तो हि व्यसनेषु महीपतिः ।
वियुज्यते ऽर्थ.धर्माभ्यां क्रोधजेष्व् आत्मना-एव तु ॥ ४६
                                ॥
verses.english: For a king who is attached to the vices springing from love of pleasure, loses his wealth and his virtue, but (he who is given) to those arising from anger, (loses) even his life.

verses.text:
मृगया-अक्षो दिवास्वप्नः परिवादः स्त्रियो मदः ।
तौर्यत्रिकं वृथाट्या च कामजो दशको गणः ॥ ४७ ॥
verses.english: Hunting, gambling, sleeping by day, censoriousness, (excess with) women, drunkenness, (an inordinate love for) dancing, singing, and music, and useless travel are the tenfold set (of vices) springing from love of pleasure.

verses.text:
पैशुन्यं साहसं द्रोह ईर्ष्या.असूया.अर्थदूषणम् ।
वाग्दण्डजं च पारुष्यं क्रोधजो ऽपि गणो ऽष्टकः ॥ ४८
                                ॥
verses.english: Tale-bearing, violence, treachery, envy, slandering, (unjust) seizure of property, reviling, and assault are the eightfold set (of vices) produced by wrath.

verses.text:
द्वयोर् अप्य् एतयोर् मूलं यं सर्वे कवयो विदुः ।
तं यत्नेन जयेत्-लोभं तज्जाव् एताव् उभौ गणौ ॥ ४९ ॥
verses.english: That greediness which all wise men declare to be the root even of both these (sets), let him carefully conquer; both sets (of vices) are produced by that.

verses.text:
पानम् अक्षाः स्त्रियश् च-एव मृगया च यथाक्रमम् ।
एतत् कष्टतमं विद्यात्-चतुष्कं कामजे गणे ॥ ५० ॥
verses.english: Drinking, dice, women, and hunting, these four (which have been enumerated) in succession, he must know to be the most pernicious in the set that springs from love of pleasure.

verses.text:
दण्डस्य पातनं च-एव वाक्पारुष्य.अर्थदूषणे ।
क्रोधजे ऽपि गणे विद्यात् कष्टम् एतत् त्रिकं सदा ॥ ५१ ॥
verses.english: Doing bodily injury, reviling, and the seizure of property, these three he must know to be the most pernicious in the set produced by wrath.

verses.text:
सप्तकस्य-अस्य वर्गस्य सर्वत्र-एव-अनुषङ्गिणः ।
पूर्वं पूर्वं गुरुतरं विद्याद् व्यसनम् आत्मवान् ॥ ५२ ॥
verses.english: A self-controlled (king) should know that in this set of seven, which prevails everywhere, each earlier-named vice is more abominable (than those named later).

verses.text:
व्यसनस्य च मृत्योश् च व्यसनं कष्टम् उच्यते ।
व्यसन्य् अधो ऽधो व्रजति स्वर् यात्य् अव्यसनी मृतः ॥ ५३
                                ॥
verses.english: (On a comparison) between vice and death, vice is declared to be more pernicious; a vicious man sinks to the nethermost (hell), he who dies, free from vice, ascends to heaven.

verses.text:
मौलान्-शास्त्रविदः शूरान्-लब्ध.लक्षान् कुल.उद्भवान् । ७.५४अव्/ म्: 
                                    कुल.उद्गतान्
सचिवान् सप्त च-अष्टौ वा प्रकुर्वीत परीक्षितान् ॥ ५४ ॥
                                    ७.५४च्व्/ म्: 
                                    कुर्वीत सुपरीक्षितान् ॥ 7.54 ॥
verses.english: Let him appoint seven or eight ministers whose ancestors have been royal servants, who are versed in the sciences, heroes skilled in the use of weapons and descended from (noble) families and who have been tried.

verses.text:
अपि यत् सुकरं कर्म तद् अप्य् एकेन दुष्करम् ।
विशेषतो ऽसहायेन किं तु राज्यं महा.उदयम् ॥ ५५ ॥ ७.५५च्व्/ म्: किं
                                    नु ॥ 7.55 ॥
verses.english: Even an undertaking easy (in itself) is (sometimes) hard to be accomplished by a single man; how much (harder is it for a king), especially (if he has) no assistant, (to govern) a kingdom which yields great revenues.

verses.text:
तैः सार्धं चिन्तयेन् नित्यं सामान्यं सन्धि.विग्रहम् ।
स्थानं समुदयं गुप्तिं लब्धप्रशमनानि च ॥ ५६ ॥
verses.english: Let him daily consider with them the ordinary (business, referring to) peace and war, (the four subjects called) sthana, the revenue, the (manner of) protecting (himself and his kingdom), and the sanctification of his gains (by pious gifts).

verses.text:
तेषां स्वं स्वम् अभिप्रायम् उपलभ्य पृथक् पृथक् ।
समस्तानां च कार्येषु विदध्याद्द् हितम् आत्मनः ॥ ५७ ॥
verses.english: Having (first) ascertained the opinion of each (minister) separately and (then the views) of all together, let him do what is (most) beneficial for him in his affairs.

verses.text:
सर्वेषां तु विशिष्टेन ब्राह्मणेन विपश्चिता ।
मन्त्रयेत् परमं मन्त्रं राजा षाड्गुण्यसंयुतम् ॥ ५८ ॥
verses.english: But with the most distinguished among them all, a learned Brahmana, let the king deliberate on the most important affairs which relate to the six measures of royal policy.

verses.text:
नित्यं तस्मिन् समाश्वस्तः सर्वकार्याणि निःक्षिपेत् । ७.५९अव्/ म्: 
                                    निक्षिपेत्
तेन सार्धं विनिश्चित्य ततः कर्म समारभेत् ॥ ५९ ॥
verses.english: Let him, full of confidence, always entrust to that (official) all business; having taken his final resolution with him, let him afterwards begin to act.

verses.text:
अन्यान् अपि प्रकुर्वीत शुचीन् प्राज्ञान् अवस्थितान् ।
सम्यग् अर्थसमाहर्तॄन् अमात्यान् सुपरीक्षितान् ॥ ६० ॥
verses.english: He must also appoint other officials, (men) of integrity, (who are) wise, firm, well able to collect money, and well tried.

verses.text:
निर्वर्तेत-अस्य यावद्भिर् इतिकर्तव्यता नृभिः ।
तावतो ऽतन्द्रितान् दक्षान् प्रकुर्वीत विचक्षणान् ॥ ६१ ॥
verses.english: As many persons as the due performance of his business requires, so many skilful and clever (men), free from sloth, let him appoint.

verses.text:
तेषाम् अर्थे नियुञ्जीत शूरान् दक्षान् कुल.उद्गतान् ।
शुचीन् आकर.कर्मान्ते भीरून् अन्तर्निवेशने ॥ ६२ ॥
verses.english: Among them let him employ the brave, the skilful, the high-born, and the honest in (offices for the collection of) revenue, (e.g.) in mines, manufactures, and storehouses, (but) the timid in the interior of his palace.

verses.text:
दूतं च-एव प्रकुर्वीत सर्वशास्त्र.विशारदम् ।
इङ्गित.आकार.चेष्टज्ञं शुचिं दक्षं कुल.उद्गतम् ॥ ६३ ॥
verses.english: Let him also appoint an ambassador who is versed in all sciences, who understands hints, expressions of the face and gestures, who is honest, skilful, and of (noble) family.

verses.text:
अनुरक्तः शुचिर् दक्षः स्मृतिमान् देश.कालवित् ।
वपुष्मान् वीतभीर् वाग्मी दूतो राज्ञः प्रशस्यते ॥ ६४ ॥
verses.english: (Such) an ambassador is commended to a king (who is) loyal, honest, skilful, possessing a good memory, who knows the (proper) place and time (for action, who is) handsome, fearless, and eloquent.

verses.text:
अमात्ये दण्ड आयत्तो दण्डे वैनयिकी क्रिया ।
नृपतौ कोश.राष्ट्रे च दूते सन्धि.विपर्ययौ ॥ ६५ ॥
verses.english: The army depends on the official (placed in charge of it), the due control (of the subjects) on the army, the treasury and the (government of) the realm on the king, peace and its opposite (war) on the ambassador.

verses.text:
दूत एव हि सन्धत्ते भिनत्त्य् एव च संहतान् ।
दूतस् तत् कुरुते कर्म भिद्यन्ते येन मानवः ॥ ६६ ॥
verses.english: For the ambassador alone makes (kings') allies and separates allies; the ambassador transacts that business by which (kings) are disunited or not.

verses.text:
स विद्याद् अस्य कृत्येषु निर्गूढ.इङ्गित.चेष्टितैः ।
आकारम् इङ्गितं चेष्टां भृत्येषु च चिकीर्षितम् ॥ ६७ ॥
verses.english: With respect to the affairs let the (ambassador) explore the expression of the countenance, the gestures and actions of the (foreign king) through the gestures and actions of his confidential (advisers), and (discover) his designs among his servants.

verses.text:
बुद्ध्वा च सर्वं तत्त्वेन परराजचिकीर्षितम् ।
तथा प्रयत्नम् आतिष्ठेद् यथा-आत्मानं न पीडयेत् ॥ ६८
                                ॥
verses.english: Having learnt exactly (from his ambassador) the designs of the foreign king, let (the king) take such measures that he does not bring evil on himself.

verses.text:
जाङ्गलं सस्यसम्पन्नम् आर्य.प्रायम् अन्.आविलम् ।
रम्यम् आनत.सामन्तं स्वाजीव्यं देशम् आवसेत् ॥ ६९ ॥
verses.english: Let him settle in a country which is open and has a dry climate, where grain is abundant, which is chiefly (inhabited) by Aryans, not subject to epidemic diseases (or similar troubles), and pleasant, where the vassals are obedient and his own (people easily) find their livelihood.

verses.text:
धन्व.दुर्गं मही.दुर्गम् अब्.दुर्गं वार्क्षम् एव वा ।
नृदुर्गं गिरिदुर्गं वा समाश्रित्य वसेत् पुरम् ॥ ७० ॥
verses.english: Let him build (there) a town, making for his safety a fortress, protected by a desert, or a fortress built of (stone and) earth, or one protected by water or trees, or one (formed by an encampment of armed) men or a hill-fort.

verses.text:
सर्वेण तु प्रयत्नेन गिरिदुर्गं समाश्रयेत् ।
एषां हि बाहुगुण्येन गिरिदुर्गं विशिष्यते ॥ ७१ ॥
verses.english: Let him make every effort to secure a hill-fort, for amongst all those (fortresses mentioned) a hill-fort is distinguished by many superior qualities.

verses.text:
त्रिण्य् आद्यान्य् आश्रितास् त्व् एषां मृग.गर्ताश्रय.अप्चराः ।
त्रीण्य् उत्तराणि क्रमशः प्लवङ्गम.नर.अमराः ॥ ७२ ॥
verses.english: The first three of those (various kinds of fortresses) are inhabited by wild beasts, animals living in holes and aquatic animals, the last three by monkeys, men, and gods respectively.

verses.text:
यथा दुर्गाश्रितान् एतान् न-उपहिंसन्ति शत्रवः ।
तथा-अरयो न हिंसन्ति नृपं दुर्गसमाश्रितम् ॥ ७३ ॥
verses.english: As enemies do not hurt these (beings, when they are) sheltered by (their) fortresses, even so foes (can) not injure a king who has taken refuge in his fort.

verses.text:
एकः शतं योधयति प्राकारस्थो धनुर्धरः ।
शतं दशसहस्राणि तस्माद् दुर्गं विधीयते ॥ ७४ ॥
verses.english: One bowman, placed on a rampart, is a match in battle for one hundred (foes), one hundred for ten thousand; hence it is prescribed (in the Sastras that a king will posses) a fortress.

verses.text:
तत् स्याद् आयुधसम्पन्नं धन.धान्येन वाहनैः ।
ब्राह्मणैः शिल्पिभिर् यन्त्रैर् यवसेन-उदकेन च ॥ ७५
                                ॥
verses.english: Let that (fort) be well supplied with weapons, money, grain and beasts of burden, with Brahmanas, with artisans, with engines, with fodder, and with water.

verses.text:
तस्य मध्ये सुपर्याप्तं कारयेद् गृहम् आत्मनः ।
गुप्तं सर्व.ऋतुकं शुभ्रं जल.वृक्षसमन्वितम् ॥ ७६ ॥
verses.english: Let him cause to be built for himself, in the centre of it, a spacious palace, (well) protected, habitable in every season, resplendent (with whitewash), supplied with water and trees.

verses.text:
तद् अध्यास्य-उद्वहेद् भार्यां स.वर्णां लक्षणान्विताम् ।
कुले महति सम्भूतां हृद्यां रूप.गुणान्वीताम् ॥ ७७ ॥
verses.english: Inhabiting that, let him wed a consort of equal caste (varna), who possesses auspicious marks (on her body), and is born in a great family, who is charming and possesses beauty and excellent qualities.

verses.text:
पुरोहितं च कुर्वीत वृणुयाद् एव च-ऋत्विजः ।
ते ऽस्य गृह्याणि कर्माणि कुर्युर् वैतानिकानि च ॥ ७८ ॥
verses.english: Let him appoint a domestic priest (purohita) and choose officiating priests (ritvig); they shall perform his domestic rites and the (sacrifices) for which three fires are required.

verses.text:
यजेत राजा क्रतुभिर् विविधैर् आप्त.दक्षिणैः ।
धर्मार्थं च-एव विप्रेभ्यो दद्याद् भोगान् धनानि च ॥ ७९
                                ॥
verses.english: A king shall offer various (Srauta) sacrifices at which liberal fees (are distributed), and in order to acquire merit, he shall give to Brahmanas enjoyments and wealth.

verses.text:
सांवत्सरिकम् आप्तैश् च राष्ट्राद् आहारयेद् बलिम् ।
स्याच् च-आम्नाय.परो लोके वर्तेत पितृवत्-नृषु ॥ ८० ॥
verses.english: Let him cause the annual revenue in his kingdom to be collected by trusty (officials), let him obey the sacred law in (his transactions with) the people, and behave like a father towards all men.

verses.text:
अध्यक्षान् विविधान् कुर्यात् तत्र तत्र विपश्चितः ।
ते ऽस्य सर्वाण्य् अवेक्षेरन् नृणां कार्याणि कुर्वताम् ॥ ८१ ॥
verses.english: For the various (branches of business) let him appoint intelligent supervisors; they shall inspect all (the acts) of those men who transact his business.

verses.text:
आवृत्तानां गुरुकुलाद् विप्राणां पूजको भवेत् ।
नृपाणाम् अक्षयो ह्य् एष निधिर् ब्राह्मो ऽभिधीयते ॥ ८२ ॥
verses.english: Let him honour those Brahmanas who have returned from their teacher's house (after studying the Veda); for that (money which is given) to Brahmanas is declared to be an imperishable treasure for kings.

verses.text:
न तं स्तेना न च-अमित्रा हरन्ति न च नश्यति ।
तस्माद् राज्ञा निधातव्यो ब्राह्मणेष्व् अक्षयो निधिः ॥ ८३ ॥
verses.english: Neither thieves nor foes can take it, nor can it be lost; hence an imperishable store must be deposited by kings with Brahmanas.

verses.text:
न स्कन्दते न व्यथते न विनश्यति कर्हि चित् । ७.८४अव्/ म्: न
                                    स्कन्दति न च्यवते
वरिष्ठम् अग्निहोत्रेभ्यो ब्राह्मणस्य मुखे हुतम् ॥ ८४ ॥
verses.english: The offering made through the mouth of a Brahmana, which is neither spilt, nor falls (on the ground), nor ever perishes, is far more excellent than Agnihotras.

verses.text:
समम् अब्राह्मणे दानं द्विगुणं ब्राह्मणब्रुवे ।
प्राधीते शतसाहस्रम् अनन्तं वेदपारगे ॥ ८५ ॥ ७.८५च्व्/ म्: आचार्ये
                                    शतसाहस्रम् ज्: सहस्रगुणम् आचार्ये ॥ 7.85 ॥
verses.english: A gift to one who is not a Brahmana (yields) the ordinary (reward; a gift) to one who calls himself a Brahmana, a double (reward); a gift to a well-read Brahmana, a hundred-thousandfold (reward); (a gift) to one who knows the Veda and the Angas (Vedaparaga, a reward) without end.

verses.text:
पात्रस्य हि विशेषेण श्रद्दधानतया-एव च ।
अल्पं वा बहु वा प्रेत्य दानस्य फलम् अश्नुते ॥ ८६ ॥
verses.english: For according to the particular qualities of the recipient and according to the faith (of the giver) a small or a great reward will be obtained for a gift in the next world.

verses.text:
[८८म] सम.उत्तम.अधमै राजा त्व् आहूतः पालयन् प्रजाः ।
[८८म्च्] न निवर्तेत सङ्ग्रामात् क्षात्रं धर्मम् अनुस्मरन् ॥ ८७
                                ॥
verses.english: A king who, while he protects his people, is defied by (foes), be they equal in strength, or stronger, or weaker, must not shrink from battle, remembering the duty of Kshatriyas.

verses.text:
[८९म] सङ्ग्रामेष्व् अनिवर्तित्वं प्रजानां च-एव पालनम् ।
[८९म्च्] शुश्रूषा ब्राह्मणानां च राज्ञां श्रेयस्करं परम् ॥ ८८
                                ॥
verses.english: Not to turn back in battle, to protect the people, to honour the Brahmanas, is the best means for a king to secure happiness.

verses.text:
[९०म] आहवेषु मिथो ऽन्योन्यं जिघांसन्तो महीक्षितः ।
[९०म्च्] युध्यमानाः परं शक्त्या स्वर्गं यान्त्य् अ.पराङ्मुखाः ॥
                                ८९ ॥
verses.english: Those kings who, seeking to slay each other in battle, fight with the utmost exertion and do not turn back, go to heaven.

verses.text:
[९१म] न कूटैर् आयुधैर् हन्याद् युध्यमानो रणे रिपून् ।
[९१म्च्] न कर्णिभिर् न-अपि दिग्धैर् न-अग्निज्वलित.तेजनैः ॥
                                ९० ॥
verses.english: When he fights with his foes in battle, let him not strike with weapons concealed (in wood), nor with (such as are) barbed, poisoned, or the points of which are blazing with fire.

verses.text:
[९२म] न च हन्यात् स्थलारूढं न क्लीबं न कृत.अञ्जलिम्
                                ।
[९२म्च्] न मुक्त.केशं न-आसीनं न तव-अस्मि-इति वादिनम् ॥ ९१
                                ॥
verses.english: Let him not strike one who (in flight) has climbed on an eminence, nor a eunuch, nor one who joins the palms of his hands (in supplication), nor one who (flees) with flying hair, nor one who sits down, nor one who says 'I am thine;'

verses.text:
[९३म] न सुप्तं न वि.सन्नाहं न नग्नं न निर्.आयुधम् ।
[९३म्च्] न-अयुध्यमानं पश्यन्तं न परेण समागतम् ॥ ९२
                                ॥
verses.english: Nor one who sleeps, nor one who has lost his coat of mail, nor one who is naked, nor one who is disarmed, nor one who looks on without taking part in the fight, nor one who is fighting with another (foe);

verses.text:
[९४म] न-आयुधव्यसनप्राप्तं न-आर्तं न-अतिपरिक्षतं ।
[९४म्च्] न भीतं न परावृत्तं सतां धर्मम् अनुस्मरन् ॥ ९३
                                ॥
verses.english: Nor one whose weapons are broken, nor one afflicted (with sorrow), nor one who has been grievously wounded, nor one who is in fear, nor one who has turned to flight; (but in all these cases let him) remember the duty (of honourable warriors).

verses.text:
[९५म] यस् तु भीतः परावृत्तः सङ्ग्रामे हन्यते परैः ।
[९५म्च्] भर्तुर् यद् दुष्कृतं किं चित् तत् सर्वं प्रतिपद्यते ॥
                                ९४ ॥
verses.english: But the (Kshatriya) who is slain in battle, while he turns back in fear, takes upon himself all the sin of his master, whatever (it may be);

verses.text:
[९६म] यत्-च-अस्य सुकृतं किं चिद् अमुत्रार्थम् उपार्जितम् ।
[९६म्च्] भर्ता तत् सर्वम् आदत्ते परावृत्तहतस्य तु ॥ ९५
                                ॥
verses.english: And whatever merit (a man) who is slain in flight may have gained for the next (world), all that his master takes.

verses.text:
[९७म] रथ.अश्वं हस्तिनं छत्रं धनं धान्यं पशून्
                                    स्त्रियः ।
[९७म्च्] सर्वद्रव्याणि कुप्यं च यो यज् जयति तस्य तत् ॥
                                    ९६ ॥
verses.english: Chariots and horses, elephants, parasols, money, grain, cattle, women, all sorts of (marketable) goods and valueless metals belong to him who takes them (singly) conquering (the possessor).

verses.text:
[९८म] राज्ञश् च दद्युर् उद्धारम् इत्य् एषा वैदिकी श्रुतिः
                                    ।
[९८म्च्] राज्ञा च सर्वयोधेभ्यो दातव्यम् अपृथग्जितम् ॥ ९७
                                    ॥
verses.english: A text of the Veda (declares) that (the soldiers) shall present a choice portion (of the booty) to the king; what has not been taken singly, must be distributed by the king among all the soldiers.

verses.text:
[९९म] एषो ऽनुपस्कृतः प्रोक्तो योधधर्मः सनातनः ।
[९९म्च्] अस्माद् धर्मान् न च्यवेत क्षत्रियो घ्नन् रणे रिपून्
                                    ॥ ९८ ॥
verses.english: Thus has been declared the blameless, primeval law for warriors; from this law a Kshatriya must not depart, when he strikes his foes in battle.

verses.text:
[१००म] अलब्धं च-एव लिप्सेत लब्धं रक्षेत् प्रयत्नतः
                                ।
[१००म्च्] रक्षितं वर्धयेच् च-एव वृद्धं पात्रेषु निक्षिपेत् ॥
                                ९९ ॥
verses.english: Let him strive to gain what he has not yet gained; what he has gained let him carefully preserve; let him augment what he preserves, and what he has augmented let him bestow on worthy men.

verses.text:
[१०१म] एतच् चतुर्विधं विद्यात् पुरुषार्थप्रयोजनम् ।
[१०१म्च्] अस्य नित्यम् अनुष्ठानं सम्यक् कुर्याद् अतन्द्रितः ॥
                                १०० ॥
verses.english: Let him know that these are the four means for securing the aims of human (existence); let him, without ever tiring, properly employ them.

verses.text:
[१०२म] अलब्धम् इच्छेद् दण्डेन लब्धं रक्षेद् अवेक्षया ।
[१०२म्च्] रक्षितं वर्धयेद् वृद्ध्या वृद्धं पात्रेषु निक्षिपेत्
                                ॥ १०१ ॥
verses.english: What he has not (yet) gained, let him seek (to gain) by (his) army; what he has gained, let him protect by careful attention; what he has protected, let him augment by (various modes of) increasing it; and what he has augmented, let him liberally bestow (on worthy men).

verses.text:
[१०३म] नित्यम् उद्यत.दण्डः स्यान् नित्यं विवृत.पौरुषः
                                ।
[१०३म्च्] नित्यं संवृत.संवार्यो नित्यं छिद्रानुसार्य् अरेः ॥
                                १०२ ॥
verses.english: Let him be ever ready to strike, his prowess constantly displayed, and his secrets constantly concealed, and let him constantly explore the weaknesses of his foe.

verses.text:
[१०४म] नित्यम् उद्यत.दण्डस्य कृत्स्नम् उद्विजते जगत् ।
[१०४म्च्] तस्मात् सर्वाणि भूतानि दण्डेन-एव प्रसाधयेत् ॥ १०३
                                ॥
verses.english: Of him who is always ready to strike, the whole world stands in awe; let him therefore make all creatures subject to himself even by the employment of force.

verses.text:
[१०५म] अ.मायया-एव वर्तेत न कथं चन मायया ।
[१०५म्च्] बुध्येत-अरिप्रयुक्तां च मायां नित्यं सुसंवृतः ॥
                                १०४ ॥
verses.english: Let him ever act without guile, and on no account treacherously; carefully guarding himself, let him always fathom the treachery which his foes employ.

verses.text:
[१०६म] न-अस्य छिद्रं परो विद्याद् विद्यात्-छिद्रं परस्य च
                                ।
[१०६म्च्] गूहेत् कूर्म इव-अङ्गानि रक्षेद् विवरम् आत्मनः ॥ १०५
                                ॥
verses.english: His enemy must not know his weaknesses, but he must know the weaknesses of his enemy; as the tortoise (hides its limbs), even so let him secure the members (of his government against treachery), let him protect his own weak points.

verses.text:
[१०७म] बकवत्-चिन्तयेद् अर्थान् सिंहवत्-च पराक्रमे ।
[१०७म्च्] वृकवत्-च-अवलुम्पेत शशवत्-च विनिष्पतेत् ॥ १०६
                                ॥
verses.english: Let him plan his undertakings (patiently meditating) like a heron; like a lion, let him put forth his strength; like a wolf, let him snatch (his prey); like a hare, let him double in retreat.

verses.text:
[१०८म] एवम् विजयमानस्य ये ऽस्य स्युः परिपन्थिनः ।
[१०८म्च्] तान् आनयेद् वशं सर्वान् सामादिभिर् उपक्रमैः ॥ १०७
                                ॥
verses.english: When he is thus engaged in conquest, let him subdue all the opponents whom he may find, by the (four) expedients, conciliation and the rest.

verses.text:
[१०९म] यदि ते तु न तिष्ठेयुर् उपायैः प्रथमैस् त्रिभिः
                                ।
[१०९म्च्] दण्डेन-एव प्रसह्य-एतान्-शनकैर् वशम् आनयेत् ॥
                                १०८ ॥
verses.english: If they cannot be stopped by the three first expedients, then let him, overcoming them by force alone, gradually bring them to subjection.

verses.text:
[११०म] साम.अदीनाम् उपायानां चतुर्णाम् अपि पण्डिताः ।
[११०म्च्] साम.दण्डौ प्रशंसन्ति नित्यं राष्ट्राभिवृद्धये ॥
                                १०९ ॥
verses.english: Among the four expedients, conciliation and the rest, the learned always recommend conciliation and (the employment of) force for the prosperity of kingdoms.

verses.text:
[१११म] यथा-उद्धरति निर्दाता कक्षं धान्यं च रक्षति
                                ।
[१११म्च्] तथा रक्षेन् नृपो राष्ट्रं हन्याच् च परिपन्थिनः ॥
                                ११० ॥
verses.english: As the weeder plucks up the weeds and preserves the corn, even so let the king protect his kingdom and destroy his opponents.

verses.text:
[११२म] मोहाद् राजा स्वराष्ट्रं यः कर्षयत्य् अनवेक्षया ।
[११२म्च्] सो ऽचिराद् भ्रश्यते राज्यात्-जीवितात्-च स.बान्धवः ॥
                                १११ ॥
verses.english: That king who through folly rashly oppresses his kingdom, (will), together with his relatives, ere long be deprived of his life and of his kingdom.

verses.text:
[११३म] शरीरकर्षणात् प्राणाः क्षीयन्ते प्राणिनां यथा ।
[११३म्च्] तथा राज्ञाम् अपि प्राणाः क्षीयन्ते राष्ट्रकर्षणात् ॥
                                ११२ ॥
verses.english: As the lives of living creatures are destroyed by tormenting their bodies, even so the lives of kings are destroyed by their oppressing their kingdoms.

verses.text:
[११४म] राष्ट्रस्य सङ्ग्रहे नित्यं विधानम् इदम् आचरेत् ।
[११४म्च्] सुसङ्गृहीतराष्ट्रे हि पार्थिवः सुखम् एधते ॥ ११३
                                ॥
verses.english: In governing his kingdom let him always observe the (following) rules; for a king who governs his kingdom well, easily prospers.

verses.text:
[११५म] द्वयोस् त्रयाणां पञ्चानां मध्ये गुल्मम्
                                    अधिष्ठितम् ।
[११५म्च्] तथा ग्रामशतानां च कुर्याद् राष्ट्रस्य सङ्ग्रहम्
                                    ॥ ११४ ॥
verses.english: Let him place a company of soldiers, commanded (by a trusty officer), the midst of two, three, five or hundreds of villages, (to be) a protection of the kingdom.

verses.text:
[११६म] ग्रामस्य-अधिपतिं कुर्याद् दशग्रामपतिं तथा
                                    ।
[११६म्च्] विंशतीशं शत.ईशं च सहस्रपतिम् एव च ॥
                                    ११५ ॥
verses.english: Let him appoint a lord over (each) village, as well as lords of ten villages, lords of twenty, lords of a hundred, and lords of a thousand.

verses.text:
[११७म] ग्रामदोषान् समुत्पन्नान् ग्रामिकः शनकैः स्वयम्
                                    ।
[११७म्च्] शंसेद् ग्रामदश.ईशाय दश.ईशो विंशतीशिने ॥
                                    ११६ ॥
verses.english: The lord of one village himself shall inform the lord of ten villages of the crimes committed in his village, and the ruler of ten (shall make his report) to the ruler of twenty.

verses.text:
[११८म] विंशतीशस् तु तत् सर्वं शत.ईशाय निवेदयेत्
                                    ।
[११८म्च्] शंसेद् ग्रामशत.ईशस् तु सहस्रपतये स्वयम् ॥
                                    ११७ ॥
verses.english: But the ruler of twenty shall report all such (matters) to the lord of a hundred, and the lord of a hundred shall himself give information to the lord of a thousand.

verses.text:
[११९म] यानि राजप्रदेयानि प्रत्यहं ग्रामवासिभिः ।
[११९म्च्] अन्न.पान.इन्धनादीनि ग्रामिकस् तान्य् अवाप्नुयात् ॥
                                    ११८ ॥
verses.english: Those (articles) which the villagers ought to furnish daily to the king, such as food, drink, and fuel, the lord of one village shall obtain.

verses.text:
[१२०म] दशी कुलं तु भुञ्जीत विंशी पञ्च कुलानि च
                                    ।
[१२०म्च्] ग्रामं ग्रामशताध्यक्षः सहस्राधिपतिः पुरम् ॥
                                    ११९ ॥
verses.english: The ruler of ten (villages) shall enjoy one kula (as much land as suffices for one family), the ruler of twenty five kulas, the superintendent of a hundred villages (the revenues of) one village, the lord of a thousand (the revenues of) a town.

verses.text:
[१२१म] तेषां ग्राम्याणि कार्यानि पृथक्कार्याणि च-एव हि
                                    ।
[१२१म्च्] राज्ञो ऽन्यः सचिवः स्निग्धस् तानि पश्येद्
                                    अतन्द्रितः ॥ १२० ॥
verses.english: The affairs of these (officials), which are connected with (their) villages and their separate business, another minister of the king shall inspect, (who must be) loyal and never remiss;

verses.text:
[१२२म] नगरे नगरे च-एकं कुर्यात् सर्वार्थचिन्तकम्
                                    ।
[१२२म्च्] उच्चैःस्थानं घोररूपं नक्षत्राणाम् इव ग्रहम्
                                    ॥ १२१ ॥
verses.english: And in each town let him appoint one superintendent of all affairs, elevated in rank, formidable, (resembling) a planet among the stars.

verses.text:
[१२३म] स तान् अनुपरिक्रामेत् सर्वान् एव सदा स्वयम् ।
[१२३म्च्] तेषां वृत्तं परिणयेत् सम्यग् राष्ट्रेषु तत्.चरैः
                                    ॥ १२२ ॥
verses.english: Let that (man) always personally visit by turns all those (other officials); let him properly explore their behaviour in their districts through spies (appointed to) each.

verses.text:
[१२४म] राज्ञो हि रक्षाधिकृताः परस्वादायिनः शठाः
                                    ।
[१२४म्च्] भृत्या भवन्ति प्रायेण तेभ्यो रक्षेद् इमाः प्रजाः
                                    ॥ १२३ ॥
verses.english: For the servants of the king, who are appointed to protect (the people), generally become knaves who seize the property of others; let him protect his subjects against such (men).

verses.text:
[१२५म] ये कार्यिकेभ्यो ऽर्थम् एव गृह्णीयुः पापचेतसः
                                    ।
[१२५म्च्] तेषां सर्वस्वम् आदाय राजा कुर्यात् प्रवासनम् ॥
                                    १२४ ॥
verses.english: Let the king confiscate the whole property of those (officials) who, evil-minded, may take money from suitors, and banish them.

verses.text:
[१२६म] राजा कर्मसु युक्तानां स्त्रीणां प्रेष्यजनस्य च ।
                                        ७.१२५अ[१२६म]व्/ म्: राजकर्मसु
[१२६म्च्] प्रत्यहं कल्पयेद् वृत्तिं स्थानं कर्मानुरूपतः
                                    ॥ १२५ ॥ ७.१२५च्[१२६म्च्]व्/ म्: स्थान.कर्मानुरूपतः ॥ 7.125 ॥
verses.english: For women employed in the royal service and for menial servants, let him fix a daily maintenance, in proportion to their position and to their work.

verses.text:
[१२७म] पणो देयो ऽवकृष्टस्य षड् उत्कृष्टस्य वेतनम्
                                    ।
[१२७म्च्] षाण्मासिकस् तथा-आच्छादो धान्यद्रोणस् तु मासिकः
                                    ॥ १२६ ॥
verses.english: One pana must be given (daily) as wages to the lowest, six to the highest, likewise clothing every six months and one drona of grain every month.

verses.text:
[१२८म] क्रय.विक्रयम् अध्वानं भक्तं च स.परिव्ययम्
                                ।
[१२८म्च्] योगक्षेमं च सम्प्रेक्ष्य वणिजो दापयेत् करान् ॥ १२७
                                ॥
verses.english: Having well considered (the rates of) purchase and (of) sale, (the length of) the road, (the expense for) food and condiments, the charges of securing the goods, let the king make the traders pay duty.

verses.text:
[१२९म] यथा फलेन युज्येत राजा कर्ता च कर्मणाम् ।
[१२९म्च्] तथा-अवेक्ष्य नृपो राष्ट्रे कल्पयेत् सततं करान् ॥
                                १२८ ॥
verses.english: After (due) consideration the king shall always fix in his realm the duties and taxes in such a manner that both he himself and the man who does the work receive (their due) reward.

verses.text:
[१३०म] यथा-अल्पाल्पम् अदन्त्य् आद्यं वार्योको.वत्स.षट्पदाः
                                ।
[१३०म्च्] तथा-अल्पाल्पो ग्रहीतव्यो राष्ट्राद् राज्ञाब्दिकः करः ॥
                                १२९ ॥
verses.english: As the leech, the calf, and the bee take their food little by little, even so must the king draw from his realm moderate annual taxes.

verses.text:
[१३१म] पञ्चाशद्भाग आदेयो राज्ञा पशु.हिरण्ययोः ।
[१३१म्च्] धान्यानाम् अष्टमो भागः षष्ठो द्वादश एव वा ॥ १३०
                                ॥
verses.english: A fiftieth part of (the increments on) cattle and gold may be taken by the king, and the eighth, sixth, or twelfth part of the crops.

verses.text:
[१३२म] आददीत-अथ षड्भागं द्रु.मांस.मधु.सर्पिषाम् ।
[१३२म्च्] गन्ध.ओषधि.रसानां च पुष्प.मूल.फलस्य च ॥
                                १३१ ॥
verses.english: He may also take the sixth part of trees, meat, honey, clarified butter, perfumes, (medical) herbs, substances used for flavouring food, flowers, roots, and fruit;

verses.text:
[१३३म] पत्र.शाक.तृणानां च चर्मणां वैदलस्य च ।
[१३३म्च्] मृन्मयानां च भाण्डानां सर्वस्य-अश्ममयस्य च ॥
                                १३२ ॥
verses.english: Of leaves, pot-herbs, grass, (objects) made of cane, skins, of earthen vessels, and all (articles) made of stone.

verses.text:
[१३४म] म्रियमाणो ऽप्य् आददीत न राजा श्रोत्रियात् करम् ।
[१३४म्च्] न च क्षुधा-अस्य संसीदेत्-श्रोत्रियो विषये वसन् ॥
                                १३३ ॥
verses.english: Though dying (with want), a king must not levy a tax on Srotriyas, and no Srotriya, residing in his kingdom, must perish from hunger.

verses.text:
[१३५म] यस्य राज्ञस् तु विषये श्रोत्रियः सीदति क्षुधा ।
[१३५म्च्] तस्य-अपि तत् क्षुधा राष्ट्रम् अचिरेन-एव सीदति ॥
                                १३४ ॥
verses.english: The kingdom of that king, in whose dominions a Srotriya pines with hunger, will even, ere long, be afflicted by famine.

verses.text:
[१३६म] श्रुत.वृत्ते विदित्वा-अस्य वृत्तिं धर्म्यां प्रकल्पयेत्
                                ।
[१३६म्च्] संरक्षेत् सर्वतश् च-एनं पिता पुत्रम् इव-औरसम् ॥
                                १३५ ॥
verses.english: Having ascertained his learning in the Veda and (the purity of) his conduct, the king shall provide for him means of subsistence in accordance with the sacred law, and shall protect him in every way, as a father (protects) the lawful son of his body.

verses.text:
[१३७म] संरक्ष्यमाणो राज्ञा यं कुरुते धर्मम् अन्वहम् ।
                                    ७.१३६अ[१३७म]व्/ म्: राज्ञा-अयं
[१३७म्च्] तेन-आयुर् वर्धते राज्ञो द्रविणं राष्ट्रम् एव च ॥
                                १३६ ॥
verses.english: Whatever meritorious acts (such a Brahmana) performs under the full protection of the king, thereby the king's length of life, wealth, and kingdom increase.

verses.text:
[१३८म] यत् किं चिद् अपि वर्षस्य दापयेत् करसञ्ज्ञितम् ।
[१३८म्च्] व्यवहारेण जीवन्तं राजा राष्ट्रे पृथग्जनम् ॥ १३७
                                ॥
verses.english: Let the king make the common inhabitants of his realm who live by traffic, pay annually some trifle, which is called a tax.

verses.text:
[१३९म] कारुकान्-शिल्पिनश् च-एव शूद्रांस् चात्म.उपजीविनः
                                ।
[१३९म्च्] एकैकं कारयेत् कर्म मासि मासि महीपतिः ॥ १३८
                                ॥
verses.english: Mechanics and artisans, as well as Sudras who subsist by manual labour, he may cause to work (for himself) one (day) in each month.

verses.text:
[१४०म] न-उच्छिन्द्याद् आत्मनो मूलं परेषां च-अतितृष्णया
                                ।
[१४०म्च्] उच्छिन्दन् ह्य् आत्मनो मूलम् आट्मानं तांश् च पीदयेत् ॥
                                १३९ ॥
verses.english: Let him not cut up his own root (by levying no taxes), nor the root of other (men) by excessive greed; for by cutting up his own root (or theirs), he makes himself or them wretched.

verses.text:
[१४१म] तीक्ष्णश् च-एव मृदुश् च स्यात् कार्यं वीक्ष्य महीपतिः
                                ।
[१४१म्च्] तीक्ष्णश् च-एव मृदुश् च-एव राज भवति सम्मतः ॥
                                १४० ॥
verses.english: Let the king, having carefully considered (each) affair, be both sharp and gentle; for a king who is both sharp and gentle is highly respected.

verses.text:
[१४२म] अमात्यमुख्यं धर्मज्ञं प्राज्ञं दान्तं कुल.उद्गतम्
                                ।
[१४२म्च्] स्थापयेद् आसने तस्मिन् खिन्नः कार्य.ईक्षणे नृणाम् ॥
                                १४१ ॥
verses.english: When he is tired with the inspection of the business of men, let him place on that seat (of justice) his chief minister, (who must be) acquainted with the law, wise, self-controlled, and descended from a (noble) family.

verses.text:
[१४३म] एवं सर्वं विधाय-इदम् इतिकर्तव्यम् आत्मनः ।
[१४३म्च्] युक्तश् च-एव-अप्रमत्तश् च परिरक्षेद् इमाः प्रजाः ॥
                                १४२ ॥
verses.english: Having thus arranged all the affairs (of) his (government), he shall zealously and carefully protect his subjects.

verses.text:
[१४४म] विक्रोशन्त्यो यस्य राष्ट्राद् ह्रियन्ते दस्युभिः प्रजाः
                                ।
[१४४म्च्] सम्पश्यतः स.भृत्यस्य मृतः स न तु जीवति ॥ १४३
                                ॥
verses.english: That (monarch) whose subjects are carried off by robbers (Dasyu) from his kingdom, while they loudly call (for help), and he and his servants are (quietly) looking on, is a dead and not a living (king).

verses.text:
[१४५म] क्षत्रियस्य परो धर्मः प्राजानाम् एव पालनम् ।
[१४५म्च्] निर्दिष्टफलभोक्ता हि राजा धर्मेण युज्यते ॥ १४४
                                ॥
verses.english: The highest duty of a Kshatriya is to protect his subjects, for the king who enjoys the rewards, just mentioned, is bound to (discharge that) duty.

verses.text:
[१४६म] उत्थाय पश्चिमे यामे कृत.शौचः समाहितः ।
[१४६म्च्] हुताग्निर् ब्राह्मणांश् चार्च्य प्रविशेत् स शुभां सभाम्
                                ॥ १४५ ॥
verses.english: Having risen in the last watch of the night, having performed (the rite of) personal purification, having, with a collected mind, offered oblations in the fire, and having worshipped Brahmanas, he shall enter the hall of audience which must possess the marks (considered) auspicious (for a dwelling).

verses.text:
[१४७म] तत्र स्थितः प्रजाः सर्वाः प्रतिनन्द्य विसर्जयेत्
                                ।
[१४७म्च्] विसृज्य च प्रजाः सर्वा मन्त्रयेत् सह मन्त्रिभिः ॥
                                १४६ ॥
verses.english: Tarrying there, he shall gratify all subjects (who come to see him by a kind reception) and afterwards dismiss them; having dismissed his subjects, he shall take counsel with his ministers.

verses.text:
[१४८म] गिरिपृष्ठं समारुह्य प्रसादं वा रहोगतः ।
[१४८म्च्] अरण्ये निः.शलाके वा मन्त्रयेद् अ.विभावितः ॥
                                    १४७ ॥
verses.english: Ascending the back of a hill or a terrace, (and) retiring (there) in a lonely place, or in a solitary forest, let him consult with them unobserved.

verses.text:
[१४९म] यस्य मन्त्रं न जानन्ति समागम्य पृथग्जनाः
                                    ।
[१४९म्च्] स कृत्स्नां पृथिवीं भुङ्क्ते कोशहीनो ऽपि
                                    पार्थिवः ॥ १४८ ॥
verses.english: That king whose secret plans other people, (though) assembled (for the purpose), do not discover, (will) enjoy the whole earth, though he be poor in treasure.

verses.text:
[१५०म] जड.मूक.अन्ध.बधिरांस् तैर्यग्योनान्
                                    वयो.ऽतिगान् ।
[१५०म्च्] स्त्री.म्लेच्छ.व्याधित.व्यङ्गान् मन्त्रकाले
                                    ऽपसारयेत् ॥ १४९ ॥
verses.english: At the time of consultation let him cause to be removed idiots, the dumb, the blind, and the deaf, animals, very aged men, women, barbarians, the sick, and those deficient in limbs.

verses.text:
[१५१म] भिन्दन्त्य् अवमता मन्त्रं तैर्यग्योनास् तथा-एव
                                    च ।
[१५१म्च्] स्त्रियश् च-एव विशेषेण तस्मात् तत्रादृतो भवेत्
                                    ॥ १५० ॥
verses.english: (Such) despicable (persons), likewise animals, and particularly women betray secret council; for that reason he must be careful with respect to them.

verses.text:
[१५२म] मध्यन्दिने ऽर्धरात्रे वा विश्रान्तो विगतक्लमः
                                    ।
[१५२म्च्] चिन्तयेद् धर्म.काम.अर्थान् सार्धं तैर् एक एव
                                    वा ॥ १५१ ॥ ७.१५१च्[१५२म्च्]व्/ म्: सार्थं ॥ 7.151 ॥
verses.english: At midday or at midnight, when his mental and bodily fatigues are over, let him deliberate, either with himself alone or with his (ministers), on virtue, pleasure, and wealth,

verses.text:
[१५३म] परस्परविरुद्धानां तेषां च समुपार्जनम् ।
[१५३म्च्] कन्यानां सम्प्रदानं च कुमाराणां च रक्षणं ॥
                                    १५२ ॥
verses.english: On (reconciling) the attainment of these (aims) which are opposed to each other, on bestowing his daughters in marriage, and on keeping his sons (from harm),

verses.text:
[१५४म] दूतसम्प्रेषणं च-एव कार्यशेषं तथा-एव च
                                    ।
[१५४म्च्] अन्तःपुरप्रचारं च प्रणिधीनां च चेष्टितम् ॥
                                    १५३ ॥
verses.english: On sending ambassadors, on the completion of undertakings (already begun), on the behaviour of (the women in) his harem, and on the doings of his spies.

verses.text:
[१५५म] कृत्स्नं च-अष्टविधं कर्म पञ्चवर्गं च
                                    तत्त्वतः ।
[१५५म्च्] अनुराग.अपरागौ च प्रचारं मण्डलस्य च ॥ १५४
                                    ॥
verses.english: On the whole eightfold business and the five classes (of spies), on the goodwill or enmity and the conduct of the circle (of neighbours he must) carefully (reflect).

verses.text:
[१५६म] मध्यमस्य प्रचारं च विजीगिषोश् च चेष्टितम्
                                    ।
[१५६म्च्] उदासीनप्रचारं च शत्रोश् च-एव प्रयत्नतः ॥
                                    १५५ ॥
verses.english: On the conduct of the middlemost (prince), on the doings of him who seeks conquest, on the behaviour of the neutral (king), and (on that) of the foe (let him) sedulously (meditate).

verses.text:
[१५७म] एताः प्रकृतयो मूलं मण्डलस्य समासतः ।
[१५७म्च्] अष्टौ च-अन्याः समाख्याता द्वादश-एव तु ताः
                                    स्मृताः ॥ १५६ ॥
verses.english: These (four) constituents (prakriti, form), briefly (speaking), the foundation of the circle (of neighbours); besides, eight others are enumerated (in the Institutes of Polity) and (thus) the (total) is declared to be twelve.

verses.text:
[१५८म] अमात्य.राष्ट्र.दुर्ग.अर्थ.दण्डाख्याः पञ्च
                                    च-अपराः ।
[१५८म्च्] प्रत्येकं कथिता ह्य् एताः सङ्क्षेपेण द्विसप्ततिः
                                    ॥ १५७ ॥
verses.english: The minister, the kingdom, the fortress, the treasury, and the army are five other (constituent elements of the circle); for, these are mentioned in connexion with each (of the first twelve; thus the whole circle consists), briefly (speaking, of) seventy-two (constituent parts).

verses.text:
[१५९म] अनन्तरम् अरिं विद्याद् अरिसेविनम् एव च ।
[१५९म्च्] अरेर् अनन्तरं मित्रम् उदासीनं तयोः परम् ॥ १५८
                                    ॥
verses.english: Let (the king) consider as hostile his immediate neighbour and the partisan of (such a) foe, as friendly the immediate neighbour of his foe, and as neutral (the king) beyond those two.

verses.text:
[१६०म] तान् सर्वान् अभिसन्दध्यात् सामादिभिर् उपक्रमैः
                                    ।
[१६०म्च्] व्यस्तैश् च-एव समस्तैश् च पौरुषेण नयेन च
                                    ॥ १५९ ॥
verses.english: Let him overcome all of them by means of the (four) expedients, conciliation and the rest, (employed) either singly or conjointly, (or) by bravery and policy (alone).

verses.text:
[१६१म] सन्धिं च विग्रहं च-एव यानम् आसनम् एव च
                                    ।
[१६१म्च्] द्वैधीभावं संश्रयं च षड्गुणांश् चिन्तयेत्
                                    सदा ॥ १६० ॥
verses.english: Let him constantly think of the six measures of royal policy (guna, viz.) alliance, war, marching, halting, dividing the army, and seeking protection.

verses.text:
[१६२म] आसनं च-एव यानं च सन्धिं विग्रहम् एव च
                                    ।
[१६२म्च्] कार्यं वीक्ष्य प्रयुञ्जीत द्वैधं संश्रयम् एव
                                    च ॥ १६१ ॥
verses.english: Having carefully considered the business (in hand), let him resort to sitting quiet or marching, alliance or war, dividing his forces or seeking protection (as the case may require).

verses.text:
[१६३म] सन्धिं तु द्विविधं विद्याद् राजा विग्रहम् एव च
                                    ।
[१६३म्च्] उभे यान.आसने च-एव द्विविधः संश्रयः स्मृतः
                                    ॥ १६२ ॥
verses.english: But the king must know that there are two kinds of alliances and of wars, (likewise two) of both marching and sitting quiet, and two (occasions for) seeking protection.)

verses.text:
[१६४म] समान.यानकर्मा च विपरीतस् तथा-एव च ।
[१६४म्च्] तदा त्व् आयतिसंयुक्तः सन्धिर् ज्ञेयो द्विलक्षणः
                                    ॥ १६३ ॥
verses.english: An alliance which yields present and future advantages, one must know to be of two descriptions, (viz.) that when one marches together (with an ally) and the contrary (when the allies act separately).

verses.text:
[१६५म] स्वयङ्कृतश् च कार्यार्थम् अकाले काल एव वा ।
[१६५म्च्] मित्रस्य च-एव-अपकृते द्विविधो विग्रहः स्मृतः
                                    ॥ १६४ ॥
verses.english: War is declared to be of two kinds, (viz.) that which is undertaken in season or out of season, by oneself and for one's own purposes, and (that waged to avenge) an injury done to a friend.

verses.text:
[१६६म] एकाकिनश् च-आत्ययिके कार्ये प्राप्ते यदृच्छया
                                    ।
[१६६म्च्] संहतस्य च मित्रेण द्विविधं यानम् उच्यते ॥
                                    १६५ ॥
verses.english: Marching (to attack) is said to be twofold, (viz. that undertaken) by one alone when an urgent matter has suddenly arisen, and (that undertaken) by one allied with a friend.

verses.text:
[१६७म] क्षीणस्य च-एव क्रमशो दैवात् पूर्वकृतेन वा
                                    ।
[१६७म्च्] मित्रस्य च-अनुरोधेन द्विविधं स्मृतम् आसनम् ॥
                                    १६६ ॥
verses.english: Sitting quiet is stated to be of two kinds, (viz. that incumbent) on one who has gradually been weakened by fate or in consequence of former acts, and (that) in favour of a friend.

verses.text:
[१६८म] बलस्य स्वामिनश् च-एव स्थितिः कार्यार्थसिद्धये
                                    ।
[१६८म्च्] द्विविधं कीर्त्यते द्वैधं षाड्गुण्यगुणवेदिभिः
                                    ॥ १६७ ॥
verses.english: If the army stops (in one place) and its master (in another) in order to effect some purpose, that is called by those acquainted with the virtues of the measures of royal policy, the twofold division of the forces.

verses.text:
[१६९म] अर्थसम्पादनार्थं च पीड्यमानस्य शत्रुभिः
                                    ।
[१६९म्च्] साधुषु व्यपदेशश् च द्विविधः संश्रयः स्मृतः
                                    ॥ १६८ ॥
verses.english: Seeking refuge is declared to be of two kinds, (first) for the purpose of attaining an advantage when one is harassed by enemies, (secondly) in order to become known among the virtuous (as the protege of a powerful king).

verses.text:
[१७०म] यदा-अवगच्छेद् आयत्याम् आधिक्यं ध्रुवम् आत्मनः
                                    ।
[१७०म्च्] तदात्वे च-अल्पिकां पीडां तदा सन्धिं समाश्रयेत्
                                    ॥ १६९ ॥
verses.english: When (the king) knows (that) at some future time his superiority (is) certain, and (that) at the time present (he will suffer) little injury, then let him have recourse to peaceful measures.

verses.text:
[१७१म] यदा प्रहृष्टा मन्येत सर्वास् तु प्रकृतीर् भृशम्
                                    ।
[१७१म्च्] अत्युच्छ्रितं तथात्मानं तदा कुर्वीत विग्रहम् ॥
                                    १७० ॥
verses.english: But when he thinks all his subjects to be exceedingly contented, and (that he) himself (is) most exalted (in power), then let him make war.

verses.text:
[१७२म] यदा मन्येत भावेन हृष्टं पुष्टं बलं स्वकम्
                                    ।
[१७२म्च्] परस्य विपरीतं च तदा यायाद् रिपुं प्रति ॥
                                    १७१ ॥
verses.english: When he knows his own army to be cheerful in disposition and strong, and (that) of his enemy the reverse, then let him march against his foe.

verses.text:
[१७३म] यदा तु स्यात् परिक्षीणो वाहनेन बलेन च ।
[१७३म्च्] तदासीत प्रयत्नेन शनकैः सान्त्वयन्न् अरीन् ॥
                                    १७२ ॥
verses.english: But if he is very weak in chariots and beasts of burden and in troops, then let him carefully sit quiet, gradually conciliating his foes.

verses.text:
[१७४म] मन्येत-अरिं यदा राजा सर्वथा बलवत्तरम्
                                    ।
[१७४म्च्] तदा द्विधा बलं कृत्वा साधयेत् कार्यम् आत्मनः
                                    ॥ १७३ ॥
verses.english: When the king knows the enemy to be stronger in every respect, then let him divide his army and thus achieve his purpose.

verses.text:
[१७५म] यदा परबलानां तु गमनीयतमो भवेत् ।
[१७५म्च्] तदा तु संश्रयेत् क्षिप्रं धार्मिकं बलिनं नृपम्
                                    ॥ १७४ ॥
verses.english: But when he is very easily assailable by the forces of the enemy, then let him quickly seek refuge with a righteous, powerful king.

verses.text:
[१७६म] निग्रहं प्रकृतीनां च कुर्याद् यो ऽरिबलस्य च
                                    ।
[१७६म्च्] उपसेवेत तं नित्यं सर्वयत्नैर् गुरुं यथा ॥
                                    १७५ ॥
verses.english: That (prince) who will coerce both his (disloyal) subjects and the army of the foe, let him ever serve with every effort like a Guru.

verses.text:
[१७७म] यदि तत्र-अपि सम्पश्येद् दोषं संश्रयकारितम्
                                    ।
[१७७म्च्] सुयुद्धम् एव तत्र-अपि निर्विशङ्कः समाचरेत् ॥
                                    १७६ ॥
verses.english: When, even in that (condition), he sees (that) evil is caused by (such) protection, let him without hesitation have recourse to war.

verses.text:
[१७८म] सर्व.उपायैस् तथा कुर्यान् नीतिज्ञः पृथिवीपतिः
                                    ।
[१७८म्च्] यथा-अस्य-अभ्यधिका न स्युर्
                                    मित्र.उदासीन.शत्रवः ॥ १७७ ॥
verses.english: By all (the four) expedients a politic prince must arrange (matters so) that neither friends, nor neutrals, nor foes are superior to himself.

verses.text:
[१७९म] आयतिं सर्वकार्याणां तदात्वं च विचारयेत् ।
[१७९म्च्] अतीतानां च सर्वेषां गुण.दोषौ च तत्त्वतः ॥
                                    १७८ ॥
verses.english: Let him fully consider the future and the immediate results of all undertakings, and the good and bad sides of all past (actions).

verses.text:
[१८०म] आयत्यां गुण.दोषज्ञस् तदात्वे क्षिप्र.निश्चयः
                                    ।
[१८०म्च्] अतीते कार्यशेषज्ञः शत्रुभिर् न-अभिभूयते ॥
                                    १७९ ॥
verses.english: He who knows the good and the evil (which will result from his acts) in the future, is quick in forming resolutions for the present, and understands the consequences of past (actions), will not be conquered.

verses.text:
[१८१म] यथा-एनं न-अभिसन्दध्युर्
                                    मित्र.उदासीन.शत्रवः ।
[१८१म्च्] तथा सर्वं संविदध्याद् एष सामासिको नयः ॥
                                    १८० ॥
verses.english: Let him arrange everything in such a manner that no ally, no neutral or foe may injure him; that is the sum of political wisdom.

verses.text:
[१८२म] तदा तु यानम् आतिष्ठेद् अरिराष्ट्रं प्रति प्रभुः
                                    ।
[१८२म्च्] तदानेन विधानेन यायाद् अरिपुरं शनैः ॥ १८१
                                    ॥
verses.english: But if the king undertakes an expedition against a hostile kingdom, then let him gradually advance, in the following manner, against his foe's capital.

verses.text:
[१८३म] मार्गशीर्षे शुभे मासि यायाद् यात्रां महीपतिः
                                    ।
[१८३म्च्] फाल्गुनं वाथ चैत्रं वा मासौ प्रति यथाबलम्
                                    ॥ १८२ ॥
verses.english: Let the king undertake his march in the fine month Margasirsha, or towards the months of Phalguna and Kaitra, according to the (condition of his) army.

verses.text:
[१८४म] अन्येष्व् अपि तु कालेषु यदा पश्येद् ध्रुवं जयम्
                                    ।
[१८४म्च्] तदा यायाद् विगृह्य-एव व्यसने च-उत्थिते रिपोः
                                    ॥ १८३ ॥
verses.english: Even at other times, when he has a certain prospect of victory, or when a disaster has befallen his foe, he may advance to attack him.

verses.text:
[१८५म] कृत्वा विधानं मूले तु यात्रिकं च यथाविधि
                                    ।
[१८५म्च्] उपगृह्य-आस्पदं च-एव चारान् सम्यग् विधाय च
                                    ॥ १८४ ॥
verses.english: But having duly arranged (all affairs) in his original (kingdom) and what relates to the expedition, having secured a basis (for his operations) and having duly dispatched his spies;

verses.text:
[१८६म] संशोध्य त्रिविधं मार्गं षड्विधं च बलं
                                    स्वकम् ।
[१८६म्च्] साम्परायिककल्पेन यायाद् अरिपुरं प्रति ॥ १८५
                                    ॥
verses.english: Having cleared the three kinds of roads, and (having made) his sixfold army (efficient), let him leisurely proceed in the manner prescribed for warfare against the enemy's capital.

verses.text:
[१८७म] शत्रुसेविनि मित्रे च गूढे युक्ततरो भवेत् ।
[१८७म्च्] गत.प्रत्यागते च-एव स हि कष्टतरो रिपुः ॥
                                    १८६ ॥
verses.english: Let him be very much on his guard against a friend who secretly serves the enemy and against (deserters) who return (from the enemy's camp); for such (men are) the most dangerous foes.

verses.text:
[१८८म] दण्डव्यूहेन तन् मार्गं यायात् तु शकटेन वा
                                    ।
[१८८म्च्] वराह.मकराभ्यां वा सूच्या वा गरुडेन वा ॥ १८७
                                    ॥
verses.english: Let him march on his road, arraying (his troops) like a staff (i.e. in an oblong), or like a waggon (i.e. in a wedge), or like a boar (i.e. in a rhombus), or like a Makara (i.e. in two triangles, with the apices joined), or like a pin (i.e. in a long line), or like a Garuda (i.e. in a rhomboid with far-extended wings).

verses.text:
[१८९म] यतश् च भयम् आशङ्केत् ततो विस्तारयेद् बलम्
                                    ।
[१८९म्च्] पद्मेन च-एव व्यूहेन निविशेत सदा स्वयम् ॥
                                    १८८ ॥
