verses.english: From whatever (side) he apprehends danger, in that (direction) let him extend his troops, and let him always himself encamp in an array, shaped like a lotus.

verses.text:
[१९०म] सेनापति.बलाध्यक्षौ सर्वदिक्षु निवेशयेत् ।
[१९०म्च्] यतश् च भयम् आशङ्केत् प्राचीं तां कल्पयेद् दिशम्
                                    ॥ १८९ ॥
verses.english: Let him allot to the commander-in-chief, to the (subordinate) general, (and to the superior officers) places in all directions, and let him turn his front in that direction whence he fears danger.

verses.text:
[१९१म] गुल्मांश् च स्थापयेद् आप्तान् कृतसञ्ज्ञान् समन्ततः
                                    ।
[१९१म्च्] स्थाने युद्धे च कुशलान् अभीरून् अविकारिणः ॥
                                    १९० ॥
verses.english: On all sides let him place troops of soldiers, on whom he can rely, with whom signals have been arranged, who are expert both in sustaining a charge and in charging, fearless and loyal.

verses.text:
[१९२म] संहतान् योधयेद् अल्पान् कामं विस्तारयेद् बहून्
                                    ।
[१९२म्च्] सूच्या वज्रेण च-एव-एतान् व्यूहेन व्यूह्य योधयेत्
                                    ॥ १९१ ॥
verses.english: Let him make a small number of soldiers fight in close order, at his pleasure let him extend a large number in loose ranks; or let him make them fight, arranging (a small number) in the needle-array, (and a large number) in the thunderbolt-array.

verses.text:
[१९३म] स्यन्दन.अश्वैः समे युध्येद् अनूपे नौ द्विपैस्
                                    तथा ।
[१९३म्च्] वृक्ष.गुल्मावृते चापैर् असि.चर्म.आयुधैः स्थले
                                    ॥ १९२ ॥
verses.english: On even ground let him fight with chariots and horses, in water-bound places with boats and elephants, on (ground) covered with trees and shrubs with bows, on hilly ground with swords, targets, (and other) weapons.

verses.text:
[१९४म] कुरुक्षेत्रांश् च मत्स्यांश् च पञ्चालान्-शूरसेनजान्
                                    । ७.१९३अ[१९४म]व्/ म्: कौरक्षेत्रांश् च
[१९४म्च्] दीर्घांल् लघूंश् च-एव नरान् अग्रानीकेषु योजयेत्
                                    ॥ १९३ ॥
verses.english: (Men born in) Kurukshetra, Matsyas, Pankalas, and those born in Surasena, let him cause to fight in the van of the battle, as well as (others who are) tall and light.

verses.text:
[१९५म] प्रहर्षयेद् बलं व्यूह्य तांश् च सम्यक्
                                    परीक्षयेत् । ७.१९४अ[१९५म]व्/ म्: भृशं परीक्षयेत्
[१९५म्च्] चेष्टाश् च-एव विजानीयाद् अरीन् योधयताम् अपि ॥
                                    १९४ ॥
verses.english: After arranging his troops, he should encourage them (by an address) and carefully inspect them; he should also mark the behaviour (of the soldiers) when they engage the enemy.

verses.text:
[१९६म] उपरुध्य-अरिम् आसीत राष्ट्रं चास्य-उपपीडयेत्
                                    ।
[१९६म्च्] दूषयेच् चास्य सततं यवस.अन्न.उदक.इन्धनम्
                                    ॥ १९५ ॥
verses.english: When he has shut up his foe (in a town), let him sit encamped, harass his kingdom, and continually spoil his grass, food, fuel, and water.

verses.text:
[१९७म] भिन्द्याच् च-एव तडागानि प्राकार.परिखास् तथा
                                    ।
[१९७म्च्] समवस्कन्दयेच् च-एनं रात्रौ वित्रासयेत् तथा
                                    ॥ १९६ ॥
verses.english: Likewise let him destroy the tanks, ramparts, and ditches, and let him assail the (foe unawares) and alarm him at night.

verses.text:
[१९८म] उपजप्यान् उपजपेद् बुध्येत-एव च तत्कृतम् ।
[१९८म्च्] युक्ते च दैवे युध्येत जयप्रेप्सुर् अपेतभीः ॥
                                    १९७ ॥
verses.english: Let him instigate to rebellion those who are open to such instigations, let him be informed of his (foe's) doings, and, when fate is propitious, let him fight without fear, trying to conquer.

verses.text:
[१९९म] साम्ना दानेन भेदेन समस्तैर् अथ वा पृथक्
                                    ।
[१९९म्च्] विजेतुं प्रयतेत-अरीन् न युद्धेन कदा चन ॥
                                    १९८ ॥ ७.१९८च्[१९९म्च्]व्/ म्: -अरिं ॥ 7.198 ॥
verses.english: He should (however) try to conquer his foes by conciliation, by (well-applied) gifts, and by creating dissension, used either separately or conjointly, never by fighting, (if it can be avoided.)

verses.text:
[२००म] अनित्यो विजयो यस्माद् दृश्यते युध्यमानयोः ।
[२००म्च्] पराजयश् च सङ्ग्रामे तस्माद् युद्धं विवर्जयेत्
                                    ॥ १९९ ॥
verses.english: For when two (princes) fight, victory and defeat in the battle are, as experience teaches, uncertain; let him therefore avoid an engagement.

verses.text:
[२०१म] त्रयाणाम् अप्य् उपायानां पूर्व.उक्तानाम् असम्भवे
                                    ।
[२०१म्च्] तथा युध्येत सम्पन्नो विजयेत रिपून् यथा ॥
                                    २०० ॥
verses.english: (But) if even those three before-mentioned expedients fail, then let him, duly exerting himself, fight in such a manner that he may completely conquer his enemies.

verses.text:
[२०२म] जित्वा सम्पूजयेद् देवान् ब्राह्मणांश् च-एव
                                    धार्मिकान् ।
[२०२म्च्] प्रदद्यात् परिहारार्थं ख्यापयेद् अभयानि च ॥
                                    २०१ ॥
verses.english: When he has gained victory, let him duly worship the gods and honour righteous Brahmanas, let him grant exemptions, and let him cause promises of safety to be proclaimed.

verses.text:
[२०३म] सर्वेषां तु विदित्वा-एषां समासेन चिकीर्षितम्
                                    ।
[२०३म्च्] स्थापयेत् तत्र तद्वंश्यं कुर्याच् च समयक्रियाम्
                                    ॥ २०२ ॥
verses.english: But having fully ascertained the wishes of all the (conquered), let him place there a relative of the (vanquished ruler on the throne), and let him impose his conditions.

verses.text:
[२०४म] प्रमाणानि च कुर्वीत तेषां धर्मान् यथा.उदितान्
                                    ।
[२०४म्च्] रत्नैश् च पूजयेद् एनं प्रधानपुरुषैः सह ॥
                                    २०३ ॥
verses.english: Let him make authoritative the lawful (customs) of the (inhabitants), just as they are stated (to be), and let him honour the (new king) and his chief servants with precious gifts.

verses.text:
[२०५म] आदानम् अप्रियकरं दानं च प्रियकारकम् ।
[२०५म्च्] अभीप्सितानाम् अर्थानां काले युक्तं ॥ २०४ ॥ ७.२०४च्[२०५म्च्]व्/ म्: कालयुक्तं प्रशस्यते ॥ 7.204 ॥
verses.english: The seizure of desirable property which causes displeasure, and its distribution which causes pleasure, are both recommendable, (if they are) resorted to at the proper time.

verses.text:
[२०६म] सर्वं कर्म-इदम् आयत्तं विधाने दैव.मानुषे
                                    ।
[२०६म्च्] तयोर् दैवम् अचिन्त्यं तु मानुषे विद्यते क्रिया ॥
                                    २०५ ॥
verses.english: All undertakings (in) this (world) depend both on the ordering of fate and on human exertion; but among these two (the ways of) fate are unfathomable; in the case of man's work action is possible.

verses.text:
[२१०म] सह वा-अपि व्रजेद् युक्तः सन्धिं कृत्वा
                                    प्रयत्नतः ।
[२१०म्च्] मित्रं हिरण्यं भूमिं वा सम्पश्यंस् त्रिविधं
                                    फलम् ॥ २०६ ॥
verses.english: Or (the king, bent on conquest), considering a friend, gold, and land (to be) the triple result (of an expedition), may, using diligent care, make peace with (his foe) and return (to his realm).

verses.text:
[२११म] पार्ष्णिग्राहं च सम्प्रेक्ष्य तथाक्रन्दं च
                                    मण्डले ।
[२११म्च्] मित्राद् अथ-अप्य् अमित्राद् वा यात्राफलम् अवाप्नुयात्
                                    ॥ २०७ ॥
verses.english: Having paid due attention to any king in the circle (of neighbouring states) who might attack him in the rear, and to his supporter who opposes the latter, let (the conqueror) secure the fruit of the expedition from (the prince whom he attacks), whether (he may have become) friendly or (remained) hostile.

verses.text:
[२१२म] हिरण्य.भूमिसम्प्राप्त्या पार्थिवो न तथ-एधते
                                    ।
[२१२म्च्] यथा मित्रं ध्रुवं लब्ध्वा कृशम् अप्य्
                                    आयतिक्षमम् ॥ २०८ ॥
verses.english: By gaining gold and land a king grows not so much in strength as by obtaining a firm friend, (who), though weak, (may become) powerful in the future.

verses.text:
[२१३म] धर्मज्ञं च कृतज्ञं च तुष्टप्रकृतिम् एव च
                                    ।
[२१३म्च्] अनुरक्तं स्थिरारम्भं लघुमित्रं प्रशस्यते ॥
                                    २०९ ॥
verses.english: A weak friend (even) is greatly commended, who is righteous (and) grateful, whose people are contented, who is attached and persevering in his undertakings.

verses.text:
[२१४म] प्राज्ञं कुलीनं शूरं च दक्षं दातारम् एव च
                                    ।
[२१४म्च्] कृतज्ञं धृतिमन्तं च कष्टम् आहुर् अरिं बुधाः
                                    ॥ २१० ॥
verses.english: The wise declare him (to be) a most dangerous foe, who is wise, of noble race, brave, clever, liberal, grateful, and firm.

verses.text:
[२१५म] आर्यता पुरुषज्ञानं शौर्यं करुणवेदिता ।
[२१५म्च्] स्थौललक्ष्यं च सततम् उदासीनगुण.उदयः ॥
                                    २११ ॥
verses.english: Behaviour worthy of an Aryan, knowledge of men, bravery, a compassionate disposition, and great liberality are the virtues of a neutral (who may be courted).

verses.text:
[२१६म] क्सेम्यां सस्यप्रदां नित्यं पशुवृद्धिकरीम् अपि
                                    ।
[२१६म्च्] परित्यजेन् नृपो भूमिम् आत्मार्थम् अ.विचारयन् ॥
                                    २१२ ॥
verses.english: Let the king, without hesitation, quit for his own sake even a country (which is) salubrious, fertile, and causing an increase of cattle.

verses.text:
[२१७म] आपदर्थं धनं रक्षेद् दारान् रक्षेद् धनैर् अपि
                                    । ७.२१३अ[२१७म]व्/ म्: आपदर्थे
[२१७म्च्] आत्मानं सततं रक्षेद् दारैर् अपि धनैर् अपि ॥
                                    २१३ ॥
verses.english: For times of need let him preserve his wealth; at the expense of his wealth let him preserve his wife; let him at all events preserve himself even by (giving up) his wife and his wealth.

verses.text:
[२१८म] सह सर्वाः समुत्पन्नाः प्रसमीक्ष्य-आपदो भृशम्
                                    ।
[२१८म्च्] संयुक्तांश् च वियुक्तांश् च सर्व.उपायान् सृजेद्
                                    बुधः ॥ २१४ ॥
verses.english: A wise (king), seeing that all kinds of misfortunes violently assail him at the same time, should try all (the four) expedients, be it together or separately, (in order to save himself.)

verses.text:
[२१९म] उपेतारम् उपेयं च सर्व.उपायांश् च कृत्स्नशः
                                    ।
[२१९म्च्] एतत् त्रयं समाश्रित्य प्रयतेत-अर्थसिद्धये ॥
                                    २१५ ॥
verses.english: On the person who employs the expedients, on the business to be accomplished, and on all the expedients collectively, on these three let him ponder and strive to accomplish his ends.

verses.text:
[२२०म] एवं सर्वम् इदं राजा सह सम्मन्त्र्य मन्त्रिभिः
                                ।
[२२०म्च्] व्यायम्य-आप्लुत्य मध्याह्ने भोक्तुम् अन्तःपुरं विशेत्
                                ॥ २१६ ॥
verses.english: Having thus consulted with his ministers on all these (matters), having taken exercise, and having bathed afterwards, the king may enter the harem at midday in order to dine.

verses.text:
[२२१म] तत्र-आत्मभूतैः कालज्ञैर् अ.हार्यैः परिचारकैः
                                ।
[२२१म्च्] सुपरीक्षितम् अन्नाद्यम् अद्यान् मन्त्रैर् विषापहैः ॥
                                २१७ ॥
verses.english: There he may eat food, (which has been prepared) by faithful, incorruptible (servants) who know the (proper) time (for dining), which has been well examined (and hallowed) by sacred texts that destroy poison.

verses.text:
[२२२म] विषघ्नैर् अगदैश् च-अस्य सर्वद्रव्याणि योजयेत् ।
                                    ७.२१८अ[२२२म]व्/ म्: विषघ्नैर् उदकैश् च-अस्य सर्वद्रव्याणि
                                    शोधयेत्
[२२२म्च्] विषघ्नानि च रत्नानि नियतो धारयेत् सदा ॥ २१८
                                ॥
verses.english: Let him mix all his food with medicines (that are) antidotes against poison, and let him always be careful to wear gems which destroy poison.

verses.text:
[२२३म] परीक्षिताः स्त्रियश् च-एनं व्यजन.उदक.धूपनैः
                                ।
[२२३म्च्] वेषाभरणसंशुद्धाः स्पृशेयुः सुसमाहिताः ॥ २१९
                                ॥
verses.english: Well-tried females whose toilet and ornaments have been examined, shall attentively serve him with fans, water, and perfumes.

verses.text:
[२२४म] एवं प्रयत्नं कुर्वीत यान.शय्या.आसन.अशने ।
[२२४म्च्] स्नाने प्रसाधने च-एव सर्वालङ्कारकेषु च ॥ २२०
                                ॥
verses.english: In like manner let him be careful about his carriages, bed, seat, bath, toilet, and all his ornaments.

verses.text:
[२२५म] भुक्तवान् विहरेच् च-एव स्त्रीभिर् अन्तःपुरे सह
                                ।
[२२५म्च्] विहृत्य तु यथाकालं पुनः कार्याणि चिन्तयेत् ॥ २२१
                                ॥
verses.english: When he has dined, he may divert himself with his wives in the harem; but when he has diverted himself, he must, in due time, again think of the affairs of state.

verses.text:
[२२६म] अलङ्कृतश् च सम्पश्येद् आयुधीयं पुनर् जनम् ।
[२२६म्च्] वाहनानि च सर्वाणि शस्त्राण्य् आभरणानि च ॥ २२२
                                ॥
verses.english: Adorned (with his robes of state), let him again inspect his fighting men, all his chariots and beasts of burden, the weapons and accoutrements.

verses.text:
[२२७म] सन्ध्यां च-उपास्य शृणुयाद् अन्तर्वेश्मनि शस्त्रभृत्
                                ।
[२२७म्च्] रहस्य-आख्यायिनां च-एव प्रणिधीनां च चेष्टितम् ॥
                                २२३ ॥
verses.english: Having performed his twilight-devotions, let him, well armed, hear in an inner apartment the doings of those who make secret reports and of his spies.

verses.text:
[२२८म] गत्वा कक्षान्तरं त्व् अन्यत् समनुज्ञाप्य तं जनम्
                                ।
[२२८म्च्] प्रविशेद् भोजनार्थं च स्त्रीवृतो ऽन्तःपुरं पुनः ॥
                                २२४ ॥
verses.english: But going to another secret apartment and dismissing those people, he may enter the harem, surrounded by female (servants), in order to dine again.

verses.text:
[२२९म] तत्र भुक्त्वा पुनः किं चित् तूर्यघोषैः प्रहर्षितः
                                ।
[२२९म्च्] संविशेत् तं यथाकालम् उत्तिष्ठेच् च गतक्लमः ॥
                                २२५ ॥
verses.english: Having eaten there something for the second time, and having been recreated by the sound of music, let him go to rest and rise at the proper time free from fatigue.

verses.text:
[२३०म] एतद्विधानम् आतिष्ठेद् अरोगः पृथिवीपतिः ।
[२३०म्च्] अस्वस्थः सर्वम् एतत् तु भृत्येषु विनियोजयेत् ॥ २२६
                                ॥
verses.english: A king who is in good health must observe these rules; but, if he is indisposed, he may entrust all this (business) to his servants.

verses.text:
व्यवहारान् दिदृक्षुस् तु ब्राह्मणैः सह पार्थिवः ।
मन्त्रज्ञैर् मन्त्रिभिश् च-एव विनीतः प्रविशेत् सभाम् ॥ १
                                ॥
verses.english: A king, desirous of investigating law cases, must enter his court of justice, preserving a dignified demeanour, together with Brahmanas and with experienced councillors.

verses.text:
तत्र-आसीनः स्थितो वा-अपि पाणिम् उद्यम्य दक्षिणम् ।
विनीत.वेष.आभरणः पश्येत् कार्याणि कार्यिणाम् ॥ २ ॥
verses.english: There, either seated or standing, raising his right arm, without ostentation in his dress and ornaments, let him examine the business of suitors,

verses.text:
प्रत्यहं देशदृष्टैश् च शास्त्रदृष्टैश् च हेतुभिः ।
अष्टादशसु मार्गेषु निबद्धानि पृथक् पृथक् ॥ ३ ॥
verses.english: Daily (deciding) one after another (all cases) which fall under the eighteen titles (of the law) according to principles drawn from local usages. and from the Institutes of the sacred law.

verses.text:
तेषाम् आद्यम् ऋणादानं निक्षेपो ऽस्वामिविक्रयः ।
सम्भूय च समुत्थानं दत्तस्य-अनपकर्म च ॥ ४ ॥
verses.english: Of those (titles) the first is the non-payment of debts, (then follow), (2) deposit and pledge, (3) sale without ownership, (4) concerns among partners, and (5) resumption of gifts,

verses.text:
वेतनस्य-एव चादानं संविदश् च व्यतिक्रमः ।
क्रय.विक्रयानुशयो विवादः स्वामि.पालयोः ॥ ५ ॥
verses.english: (6) Non-payment of wages, (7) non-performance of agreements, (8) rescission of sale and purchase, (9) disputes between the owner (of cattle) and his servants,

verses.text:
सीमाविवादधर्मश् च पारुष्ये दण्डवाचिके ।
स्तेयं च साहसं च-एव स्त्रीसङ्ग्रहणम् एव च ॥ ६ ॥
verses.english: (10) Disputes regarding boundaries, (11) assault and (12) defamation, (13) theft, (14) robbery and violence, (15) adultery,

verses.text:
स्त्री.पुन्धर्मो विभागश् च द्यूतम् आह्वय एव च ।
पदान्य् अष्टादश-एतानि व्यवहारस्थिताव् इह ॥ ७ ॥
verses.english: (16) Duties of man and wife, (17) partition (of inheritance), (18) gambling and betting; these are in this world the eighteen topics which give rise to lawsuits.

verses.text:
एषु स्थानेषु भूयिष्ठं विवादं चरतां नृणाम् ।
धर्मं शाश्वतम् आश्रित्य कुर्यात् कार्यविनिर्णयम् ॥ ८ ॥
verses.english: Depending on the eternal law, let him decide the suits of men who mostly contend on the titles just mentioned.

verses.text:
यदा स्वयं न कुर्यात् तु नृपतिः कार्यदर्शनम् ।
तदा नियुञ्ज्याद् विद्वांसं ब्राह्मणं कार्यदर्शने ॥ ९
                                    ॥
verses.english: But if the king does not personally investigate the suits, then let him appoint a learned Brahmana to try them.

verses.text:
सो ऽस्य कार्याणि सम्पश्येत् सभ्यैर् एव त्रिभिर् वृतः
                                    ।
सभाम् एव प्रविश्य-अग्र्याम् आसीनः स्थित एव वा ॥ १०
                                    ॥
verses.english: That (man) shall enter that most excellent court, accompanied by three assessors, and fully consider (all) causes (brought) before the (king), either sitting down or standing.

verses.text:
यस्मिन् देशे निषीदन्ति विप्रा वेदविदस् त्रयः ।
राज्ञश् च-अधिकृतो विद्वान् ब्रह्मणस् तां सभां विदुः ॥
                                    ११ ॥
verses.english: Where three Brahmanas versed in the Vedas and the learned (judge) appointed by the king sit down, they call that the court of (four-faced) Brahman.

verses.text:
धर्मो विद्धस् त्व् अधर्मेण सभां यत्र-उपतिष्ठते
                                    ।
शल्यं च-अस्य न कृन्तन्ति विद्धास् तत्र सभासदः ॥ १२
                                    ॥
verses.english: But where justice, wounded by injustice, approaches and the judges do not extract the dart, there (they also) are wounded (by that dart of injustice).

verses.text:
सभां वा न प्रवेष्टव्यं वक्तव्यं वा समञ्जसम् । ८.१३अव्/ म्: 
                                        सभा वा न प्रवेष्टव्या
अब्रुवन् विब्रुवन् वा-अपि नरो भवति किल्बिषी ॥ १३ ॥
verses.english: Either the court must not be entered, or the truth must be spoken; a man who either says nothing or speaks falsely, becomes sinful.

verses.text:
यत्र धर्मो ह्य् अधर्मेण सत्यं यत्र-अनृतेन च ।
हन्यते प्रेक्षमाणानां हतास् तत्र सभासदः ॥ १४ ॥
verses.english: Where justice is destroyed by injustice, or truth by falsehood, while the judges look on, there they shall also be destroyed.

verses.text:
धर्म एव हतो हन्ति धर्मो रक्षति रक्षितः ।
तस्माद् धर्मो न हन्तव्यो मा नो धर्मो हतो ऽवधीत् ॥ १५
                                    ॥ ८.१५च्व्/
                                        म्: वधीत् ॥ 8.15 ॥
verses.english: 'Justice, being violated, destroys; justice, being preserved, preserves: therefore justice must not be violated, lest violated justice destroy us.'

verses.text:
वृषो हि भगवान् धर्मस् तस्य यः कुरुते ह्य् अलम् । ८.१६अव्/ म्: त्व्
                                        अलम्
वृषलं तं विदुर् देवास् तस्माद् धर्मं न लोपयेत् ॥ १६
                                    ॥
verses.english: For divine justice (is said to be) a bull (vrisha); that (man) who violates it (kurute 'lam) the gods consider to be (a man despicable like) a Sudra (vrishala); let him, therefore, beware of violating justice.

verses.text:
एक एव सुहृद् धर्मो निधाने ऽप्य् अनुयाति यः ।
शरीरेण समं नाशं सर्वम् अन्यद्द् हि गच्छति ॥ १७
                                    ॥
verses.english: The only friend who follows men even after death is justice; for everything else is lost at the same time when the body (perishes).

verses.text:
पादो ऽधर्मस्य कर्तारं पादः साक्षिणम् ऋच्छति ।
पादः सभासदः सर्वान् पादो राजानम् ऋच्छति ॥ १८ ॥
verses.english: One quarter of (the guilt of) an unjust (decision) falls on him who committed (the crime), one quarter on the (false) witness, one quarter on all the judges, one quarter on the king.

verses.text:
राजा भवत्य् अन्.एनास् तु मुच्यन्ते च सभासदः ।
एनो गच्छति कर्तारं निन्दा.अर्हो यत्र निन्द्यते ॥ १९
                                    ॥
verses.english: But where he who is worthy of condemnation is condemned, the king is free from guilt, and the judges are saved (from sin); the guilt falls on the perpetrator (of the crime alone).

verses.text:
जातिमात्र.उपजीवी वा कामं स्याद् ब्राह्मणब्रुवः ।
धर्मप्रवक्ता नृपतेर् न शूद्रः कथं चन ॥ २० ॥
verses.english: A Brahmana who subsists only by the name of his caste (gati), or one who merely calls himself a Brahmana (though his origin be uncertain), may, at the king's pleasure, interpret the law to him, but never a Sudra.

verses.text:
यस्य शूद्रस् तु कुरुते राज्ञो धर्मविवेचनम् ।
तस्य सीदति तद् राष्ट्रं पङ्के गौर् इव पश्यतः ॥ २१
                                    ॥
verses.english: The kingdom of that monarch, who looks on while a Sudra settles the law, will sink (low), like a cow in a morass.

verses.text:
यद् राष्ट्रं शूद्र.भूयिष्ठं नास्तिकाक्रान्तम् अ.द्विजम्
                                    ।
विनश्यत्य् आशु तत् कृत्स्नं दुर्भिक्ष.व्याधिपीडितम् ॥ २२
                                    ॥
verses.english: That kingdom where Sudras are very numerous, which is infested by atheists and destitute of twice-born (inhabitants), soon entirely perishes, afflicted by famine and disease.

verses.text:
धर्मासनम् अधिष्ठाय संवीत.अङ्गः समाहितः ।
प्रणम्य लोकपालेभ्यः कार्यदर्शनम् आरभेत् ॥ २३ ॥
verses.english: Having occupied the seat of justice, having covered his body, and having worshipped the guardian deities of the world, let him, with a collected mind, begin the trial of causes.

verses.text:
अर्थ.अनर्थाव् उभौ बुद्ध्वा धर्म.अधर्मौ च केवलौ
                                    ।
वर्णक्रमेण सर्वाणि पश्येत् कार्याणि कार्यिणाम् ॥ २४ ॥
verses.english: Knowing what is expedient or inexpedient, what is pure justice or injustice, let him examine the causes of suitors according to the order of the castes (varna).

verses.text:
बाह्यैर् विभावयेत्-लिङ्गैर् भावम् अन्तर्गतं नृणाम् ।
स्वर.वर्ण.इङ्गित.आकारैश् चक्षुषा चेष्टितेन च ॥ २५
                                    ॥
verses.english: By external signs let him discover the internal disposition of men, by their voice, their colour, their motions, their aspect, their eyes, and their gestures.

verses.text:
आकारैर् इङ्गितैर् गत्या चेष्टया भाषितेन च ।
नेत्र.वक्त्रविकारैश् च गृह्यते ऽन्तर्गतं मनः ॥ २६
                                    ॥
verses.english: The internal (working of the) mind is perceived through the aspect, the motions, the gait, the gestures, the speech, and the changes in the eye and of the face.

verses.text:
बालदाय.आदिकं रिक्थं तावद् राजा-अनुपालयेत् ।
यावत् स स्यात् समावृत्तो यावत्-च-अतीत.शैशवः] ॥ २७ ॥
                                        ८.२७च्व्/
                                        म्: यावद् वा-अतीत.शैशवः ॥ 8.27 ॥
verses.english: The king shall protect the inherited (and other) property of a minor, until he has returned (from his teacher's house) or until he has passed his minority.

verses.text:
वशा.अपुत्रासु च-एवं स्याद् रक्षणं निष्.कुलासु च ।
पति.व्रतासु च स्त्रीषु विधवास्व् आतुरासु च ॥ २८ ॥
verses.english: In like manner care must be taken of barren women, of those who have no sons, of those whose family is extinct, of wives and widows faithful to their lords, and of women afflicted with diseases.

verses.text:
जीवन्तीनां तु तासां ये तद्द् हरेयुः स्वबान्धवाः ।
तान्-शिष्यात्-चौरदण्डेन धार्मिकः पृथिवीपतिः ॥ २९
                                    ॥
verses.english: A righteous king must punish like thieves those relatives who appropriate the property of such females during their lifetime.

verses.text:
प्रणष्ट.स्वामिकं रिक्थं राजा त्र्यब्दं निधापयेत् ।
अर्वाक् त्र्यब्दाद्द् हरेत् स्वामी परेण नृपतिर् हरेत् ॥ ३०
                                    ॥
verses.english: Property, the owner of which has disappeared, the king shall cause to be kept as a deposit during three years; within the period of three years the owner may claim it, after (that term) the king may take it.

verses.text:
मम-इदम् इति यो ब्रूयात् सो ऽनुयोज्यो यथाविधि ।
संवाद्य रूप.सङ्ख्यादीन् स्वामी तद् द्रव्यम् अर्हति ॥ ३१
                                    ॥
verses.english: He who says, 'This belongs to me,' must be examined according to the rule; if he accurately describes the shape, and the number (of the articles found) and so forth, (he is) the owner, (and) ought (to receive) that property.

verses.text:
अ.वेदयानो नष्टस्य देशं कालं च तत्त्वतः ।
वर्णं रूपं प्रमाणं च तत्समं दण्डम् अर्हति ॥ ३२
                                    ॥
verses.english: But if he does not really know the time and the place (where it was) lost, its colour, shape, and size, he is worthy of a fine equal (in value) to the (object claimed).

verses.text:
आददीत-अथ षड्भागं प्रनष्ट.अधिगतान् नृपः ।
दशमं द्वादशं वा-अपि सतां धर्मम् अनुस्मरन् ॥ ३३
                                    ॥
verses.english: Now the king, remembering the duty of good men, may take one-sixth part of property lost and afterwards found, or one-tenth, or at least one-twelfth.

verses.text:
प्रनष्ट.अधिगतं द्रव्यं तिष्ठेद् युक्तैर् अधिष्ठितम्
                                    ।
यांस् तत्र चौरान् गृह्णीयात् तान् राजा-इभेन घातयेत् ॥ ३४
                                    ॥
verses.english: Property lost and afterwards found (by the king's servants) shall remain in the keeping of (special) officials; those whom the king may convict of stealing it, he shall cause to be slain by an elephant.

verses.text:
ममायम् इति यो ब्रूयान् निधिं सत्येन मानवः ।
तस्याददीत षड्भागं राजा द्वादशम् एव वा ॥ ३५ ॥
verses.english: From that man who shall truly say with respect to treasure-trove, 'This belongs to me,' the king may take one-sixth or one-twelfth part.

verses.text:
अनृतं तु वदन् दण्ड्यः स्ववित्तस्य-अंशम् अष्टमम् ।
तस्य-एव वा निधानस्य सङ्ख्यया-अल्पीयसीं कलाम् ॥ ३६
                                    ॥
verses.english: But he who falsely says (so), shall be fined in one-eighth of his property, or, a calculation of (the value of) the treasure having been made, in some smaller portion (of that).

verses.text:
विद्वांस् तु ब्राह्मणो दृष्ट्वा पूर्व.उपनिहितं निधिम् ।
अशेषतो ऽप्य् आददीत सर्वस्य-अधिपतिर् हि सः ॥ ३७
                                    ॥
verses.english: When a learned Brahmana has found treasure, deposited in former (times), he may take even the whole (of it); for he is master of everything.

verses.text:
यं तु पश्येन् निधिं राजा पुराणं निहितं क्षितौ ।
तस्माद् द्विजेभ्यो दत्त्वा-अर्धम् अर्धं कोशे प्रवेशयेत् ॥
                                    ३८ ॥
verses.english: When the king finds treasure of old concealed in the ground let him give one half to Brahmanas and place the (other) half in his treasury.

verses.text:
निधीनां तु पुराणानां धातूनाम् एव च क्षितौ ।
अर्धभाग् रक्षणाद् राजा भूमेर् अधिपतिर् हि सः ॥ ३९
                                    ॥
verses.english: The king obtains one half of ancient hoards and metals (found) in the ground, by reason of (his giving) protection, (and) because he is the lord of the soil.

verses.text:
दातव्यं सर्ववर्णेभ्यो राज्ञा चौरैर् हृतं धनम् ।
राजा तद् उपयुञ्जानश् चौरस्य-आप्नोति किल्बिषम् ॥ ४०
                                    ॥
verses.english: Property stolen by thieves must be restored by the king to (men of) all castes (varna); a king who uses such (property) for himself incurs the guilt of a thief.

verses.text:
जाति.जानपदान् धर्मान् श्रेणीधर्मांश् च धर्मवित् ।
समीक्ष्य कुलधर्मांश् च स्वधर्मं प्रतिपादयेत् ॥ ४१
                                    ॥
verses.english: (A king) who knows the sacred law, must inquire into the laws of castes (gati), of districts, of guilds, and of families, and (thus) settle the peculiar law of each.

verses.text:
स्वानि कर्माणि कुर्वाणा दूरे सन्तो ऽपि मानवाः ।
प्रिया भवन्ति लोकस्य स्वे स्वे कर्मण्य् अवस्थिताः ॥ ४२
                                    ॥
verses.english: For men who follow their particular occupations and abide by their particular duty, become dear to people, though they may live at a distance.

verses.text:
न-उत्पादयेत् स्वयं कार्यं राजा न-अप्य् अस्य पुरुषः ।
न च प्रापितम् अन्येन ग्रसेद् अर्थं कथं चन ॥ ४३ ॥
                                        ८.४३च्व्/
                                        म्: ग्रसेत-अर्थं ॥ 8.43 ॥
verses.english: Neither the king nor any servant of his shall themselves cause a lawsuit to be begun, or hush up one that has been brought (before them) by (some) other (man).

verses.text:
यथा नयत्य् असृक्पातैर् मृगस्य मृगयुः पदम् ।
नयेत् तथा-अनुमानेन धर्मस्य नृपतिः पदम् ॥ ४४
                                    ॥
verses.english: As a hunter traces the lair of a (wounded) deer by the drops of blood, even so the king shall discover on which side the right lies, by inferences (from the facts).

verses.text:
सत्यम् अर्थं च सम्पश्येद् आत्मानम् अथ साक्षिणः । ८.४५अव्/ म्: 
                                        साक्षिणम्
देशं रूपं च कालं च व्यवहारविधौ स्थितः ॥ ४५
                                    ॥
verses.english: When engaged in judicial proceedings he must pay full attention to the truth, to the object (of the dispute), (and) to himself, next to the witnesses, to the place, to the time, and to the aspect.

verses.text:
सद्भिर् आचरितं यत् स्याद् धार्मिकैश् च द्विजातिभिः ।
तद् देश.कुल.जातीनाम् अ.विरुद्धं प्रकल्पयेत् ॥ ४६
                                    ॥
verses.english: What may have been practised by the virtuous, by such twice-born men as are devoted to the law, that he shall establish as law, if it be not opposed to the (customs of) countries, families, and castes (gati).

verses.text:
अधमर्णार्थसिद्ध्यर्थम् उत्तमर्णेन चोदितः ।
दापयेद् धनिकस्य-अर्थम् अधमर्णाद् विभावितम् ॥ ४७ ॥
verses.english: When a creditor sues (before the king) for the recovery of money from a debtor, let him make the debtor pay the sum which the creditor proves (to be due).

verses.text:
यैर् यैर् उपायैर् अर्थं स्वं प्राप्नुयाद् उत्तमर्णिकः ।
तैर् तैर् उपायैः सङ्गृह्य दापयेद् अधमर्णिकम् ॥ ४८ ॥
verses.english: By whatever means a creditor may be able to obtain possession of his property, even by those means may he force the debtor and make him pay.

verses.text:
धर्मेण व्यवहारेण छलेन-आचरितेन च ।
प्रयुक्तं साधयेद् अर्थं पञ्चमेन बलेन च ॥ ४९ ॥
verses.english: By moral suasion, by suit of law, by artful management, or by the customary proceeding, a creditor may recover property lent; and fifthly, by force.

verses.text:
यः स्वयं साधयेद् अर्थम् उत्तमर्णो ऽधमर्णिकात् ।
न स राज्ञा-अभियोक्तव्यः स्वकं संसाधयन् धनम् ॥ ५०
                                ॥
verses.english: A creditor who himself recovers his property from his debtor, must not be blamed by the king for retaking what is his own.

verses.text:
अर्थे ऽपव्ययमानं तु करणेन विभावितम् ।
दापयेद् धनिकस्य-अर्थं दण्डलेशं च शक्तितः ॥ ५१ ॥
verses.english: But him who denies a debt which is proved by good evidence, he shall order to pay that debt to the creditor and a small fine according to his circumstances.

verses.text:
अपह्नवे ऽधमर्णस्य देहि-इत्य् उक्तस्य संसदि ।
अभियोक्ता दिशेद् देश्यं करणं वा-अन्यद् उद्दिशेत् ॥ ५२ ॥
verses.english: On the denial (of a debt) by a debtor who has been required in court to pay it, the complainant must call (a witness) who was present (when the loan was made), or adduce other evidence.

verses.text:
अदेश्यं यश् च दिशति निर्दिश्य-अपह्नुते च यः ।
यश् च-अधर.उत्तरान् अर्थान् विगीतान् न-अवबुध्यते ॥ ५३
                                ॥
verses.english: (The plaintiff) who calls a witness not present at the transaction, who retracts his statements, or does not perceive that his statements (are) confused or contradictory;

verses.text:
अपदिश्य-अपदेश्यं च पुनर् यस् त्व् अपधावति । ८.५४अव्/ म्: 
                                    अपदिश्य-अपदेशं
सम्यक् प्रणिहितं च-अर्थं पृष्टः सन् न-अभिनन्दति ॥ ५४
                                ॥
verses.english: Or who having stated what he means to prove afterwards varies (his case), or who being questioned on a fact duly stated by himself does not abide by it;

verses.text:
अ.सम्भाष्ये साक्षिभिश् च देशे सम्भाषते मिथः ।
निरुच्यमानं प्रश्नं च न-इच्छेद् यश् च-अपि निष्पतेत् ॥ ५५
                                ॥
verses.english: Or who converses with the witnesses in a place improper for such conversation; or who declines to answer a question, properly put, or leaves (the court);

verses.text:
ब्रूहि-इत्य् उक्तश् च न ब्रूयाद् उक्तं च न विभावयेत् ।
न च पूर्व.अपरं विद्यात् तस्माद् अर्थात् स हीयते ॥ ५६
                                ॥
verses.english: Or who, being ordered to speak, does not answer, or does not prove what he has alleged; or who does not know what is the first (point), and what the second, fails in his suit.

verses.text:
साक्षिणः सन्ति मेत्य् उक्त्वा दिश-इत्य् उक्तो दिशेन् न यः । ८.५७अव्/ म्: 
                                    ज्ञातारः सन्ति मेत्य्*] *{मेत्य् < म इत्य् ?}
धर्मस्थः कारणैर् एतैर् हीनं तम् अपि निर्दिशेत् ॥ ५७ ॥
                                    ८.५७च्व्/ म्: 
                                    तम् इति निर्दिशेत् ॥ 8.57 ॥
verses.english: Him also who says 'I have witnesses,' and, being ordered to produce them, produces them not, the judge must on these (same) grounds declare to be non-suited.

verses.text:
अभियोक्ता न चेद् ब्रूयाद् बध्यो दण्ड्यश् च धर्मतः । ८.५८अव्/ म्: बन्ध्यो
                                    दण्ड्यश् च
न चेत् त्रिपक्षात् प्रब्रूयाद् धर्मं प्रति पराजितः ॥ ५८
                                ॥
verses.english: If a plaintiff does not speak, he may be punished corporally or fined according to the law; if (a defendant) does not plead within three fortnights, he has lost his cause.

verses.text:
यो यावत्-निह्नुवीत-अर्थं मिथ्या यावति वा वदेत् ।
तौ नृपेण ह्य् अधर्मज्ञौ दाप्यो तद्द्विगुणं दमम् ॥ ५९
                                ॥
verses.english: In the double of that sum which (a defendant) falsely denies or on which (the plaintiff) falsely declares, shall those two (men) offending against justice be fined by the king.

verses.text:
पृष्टो ऽपव्ययमानस् तु कृत.अवस्थो धन.एषिणा ।
त्र्यवरैः साक्षिभिर् भाव्यो नृप.ब्राह्मणसन्निधौ ॥ ६०
                                ॥
verses.english: (A defendant) who, being brought (into court) by the creditor, (and) being questioned, denies (the debt), shall be convicted (of his falsehood) by at least three witnesses (who must depose) in the presence of the Brahmana (appointed by) the king.

verses.text:
यादृशा धनिभिः कार्या व्यवहारेषु साक्षिणः ।
तादृशान् सम्प्रवक्ष्यामि यथा वाच्यम् ऋतं च तैः ॥ ६१ ॥
verses.english: I will fully declare what kind of men may be made witnesses in suits by creditors, and in what manner those (witnesses) must give true (evidence).

verses.text:
गृहिणः पुत्रिणो मौलाः क्षत्र.विश्.शूद्र.योनयः ।
अर्थ्युक्ताः साक्ष्यम् अर्हन्ति न ये के चिद् अनापदि ॥ ६२
                                    ॥
verses.english: Householders, men with male issue, and indigenous (inhabitants of the country, be they) Kshatriyas, Vaisyas, or Sudras, are competent, when called by a suitor, to give evidence, not any persons whatever (their condition may be) except in cases of urgency.

verses.text:
आप्ताः सर्वेषु वर्णेषु कार्याः कार्येषु साक्षिणः ।
सर्वधर्मविदो ऽलुब्धा विपरीतांस् तु वर्जयेत् ॥ ६३
                                    ॥
verses.english: Trustworthy men of all the (four) castes (varna) may be made witnesses in lawsuits, (men) who know (their) whole duty, and are free from covetousness; but let him reject those (of an) opposite (character).

verses.text:
न-अर्थसम्बन्धिनो न-आप्ता न सहाया न वैरिणः ।
न दृष्टदोषाः कर्तव्या न व्याध्यार्ता न दूषिताः ॥ ६४
                                    ॥
verses.english: Those must not be made (witnesses) who have an interest in the suit, nor familiar (friends), companions, and enemies (of the parties), nor (men) formerly convicted (of perjury), nor (persons) suffering under (severe) illness, nor (those) tainted (by mortal sin).

verses.text:
न साक्षी नृपतिः कार्यो न कारुक.कुशीलवौ ।
न श्रोत्रियो न लिङ्गस्थो न सङ्गेभ्यो विनिर्गतः ॥ ६५
                                    ॥
verses.english: The king cannot be made a witness, nor mechanics and actors, nor a: Srotriya, nor a student of the Veda, nor (an ascetic) who has given up (all) connexion (with the world),

verses.text:
न-अध्यधीनो न वक्तव्यो न दस्युर् न विकर्मकृत् ।
न वृद्धो न शिशुर् न-एको न-अन्त्यो न विकल.इन्द्रियः ॥
                                    ६६ ॥
verses.english: Nor one wholly dependent, nor one of bad fame, nor a Dasyu, nor one who follows forbidden occupations, nor an aged (man), nor an infant, nor one (man alone), nor a man of the lowest castes, nor one deficient in organs of sense,

verses.text:
न-आर्तो न मत्तो न-उन्मत्तो न क्षुत्.तृष्णा.उपपीडितः
                                    ।
न श्रमार्तो न कामार्तो न क्रुद्धो न-अपि तस्करः ॥ ६७
                                    ॥
verses.english: Nor one extremely grieved, nor one intoxicated, nor a madman, nor one tormented by hunger or thirst, nor one oppressed by fatigue, nor one tormented by desire, nor a wrathful man, nor a thief.

verses.text:
स्त्रीणां साक्ष्यं स्त्रियः कुर्युर् द्विजानां सदृशा द्विजाः
                                    ।
शूद्राश् च सन्तः शूद्राणाम् अन्त्यानाम् अन्त्य.योनयः ॥ ६८
                                    ॥
verses.english: Women should give evidence for women, and for twice-born men twice-born men (of the) same (kind), virtuous Sudras for Sudras, and men of the lowest castes for the lowest.

verses.text:
अनुभावी तु यः कश् चित् कुर्यात् साक्ष्यं विवादिनाम् ।
अन्तर्वेश्मन्य् अरण्ये वा शरीरस्य-अपि च-अत्यये ॥ ६९
                                    ॥
verses.english: But any person whatsoever, who has personal knowledge (of an act committed) in the interior apartments (of a house), or in a forest, or of (a crime causing) loss of life, may give evidence between the parties.

verses.text:
स्त्रिया-अप्य् असम्भावे कार्यं बालेन स्थविरेण वा ।
शिष्येण बन्धुना वा-अपि दासेन भृतकेन वा ॥ ७० ॥
verses.english: On failure (of qualified witnesses, evidence) may given (in such cases) by a woman, by an infant, by an aged man, by a pupil, by a relative, by a slave, or by a hired servant.

verses.text:
बाल.वृद्ध.आतुराणां च साक्ष्येषु वदतां मृषा ।
जानीयाद् अस्थिरां वाचम् उत्सिक्त.मनसां तथा ॥ ७१ ॥
verses.english: But the (judge) should consider the evidence of infants, aged and diseased men, who (are apt to) speak untruly, as untrustworthy, likewise that of men with disordered minds.

verses.text:
साहसेषु च सर्वेषु स्तेय.सङ्ग्रहणेषु च ।
वाग्.दण्डयोश् च पारुष्ये न परीक्षेत साक्षिणः ॥ ७२
                                    ॥
verses.english: In all cases of violence, of theft and adultery, of defamation and assault, he must not examine the (competence of) witnesses (too strictly).

verses.text:
बहुत्वं परिगृह्णीयात् साक्षिद्वैधे नराधिपः ।
समेषु तु गुण.उत्कृष्टान् गुणिद्वैधे द्विजोत्तमान् ॥ ७३
                                    ॥
verses.english: On a conflict of the witnesses the king shall accept (as true) the evidence of the) majority; if (the conflicting parties are) equal in number, (that of) those distinguished by good qualities; on a difference between (equally) distinguished (witnesses, that of) the best among the twice-born.

verses.text:
समक्षदर्शनात् साक्ष्यं श्रवणाच् च-एव सिध्यति ।
तत्र सत्यं ब्रुवन् साक्षी धर्म.अर्थाभ्यां न हीयते ॥
                                    ७४ ॥
verses.english: Evidence in accordance with what has actually been seen or heard, is admissible; a witness who speaks truth in those (cases), neither loses spiritual merit nor wealth.

verses.text:
साक्षी दृष्ट.श्रुताद् अन्यद् विब्रुवन्न् आर्यसंसदि ।
अवाङ् नरकम् अभ्येति प्रेत्य स्वर्गाच् च हीयते ॥ ७५
                                    ॥
verses.english: A witness who deposes in an assembly of honourable men (Arya) anything else but what he has seen or heard, falls after death headlong into hell and loses heaven.

verses.text:
यत्र-अनिबद्धो ऽपीक्षेत शृणुयाद् वा-अपि किं चन ।
पृष्टस् तत्र-अपि तद् ब्रूयाद् यथादृष्टं यथाश्रुतम् ॥ ७६
                                    ॥
verses.english: When a man (originally) not appointed to be a witness sees or hears anything and is (afterwards) examined regarding it, he must declare it (exactly) as he saw or heard it.

verses.text:
एको ऽलुब्धस् तु साक्षी स्याद् बह्व्यः शुच्यो ऽपि न स्त्रियः ।
                                        ८.७७अव्/
                                        म्: त्व् असाक्षी
स्त्रीबुद्धेर् अस्थिरत्वात् तु दोषैश् च-अन्ये ऽपि ये वृताः ॥
                                    ७७ ॥
verses.english: One man who is free from covetousness may be (accepted as) witness; but not even many pure women, because the understanding of females is apt to waver, nor even many other men, who are tainted with sin.

verses.text:
स्वभावेन-एव यद् ब्रूयुस् तद् ग्राह्यं व्यावहारिकम् ।
अतो यद् अन्यद् विब्रूयुर् धर्मार्थं तद् अपार्थकम् ॥ ७८
                                    ॥
verses.english: What witnesses declare quite naturally, that must be received on trials; (depositions) differing from that, which they make improperly, are worthless for (the purposes of) justice.

verses.text:
सभान्तः साक्षिणः प्राप्तान् अर्थि.प्रत्यर्थि.सन्निधौ
                                    ।
प्राड्विवाको ऽनुयुञ्जीत विधिना-अनेन सान्त्वयन् ॥ ७९
                                    ॥
verses.english: The witnesses being assembled in the court in the presence of the plaintiff and of the defendant, let the judge examine them, kindly exhorting them in the following manner:

verses.text:
यद् द्वयोर् अनयोर् वेत्थ कार्ये ऽस्मिंश् चेष्टितं मिथः
                                    ।
तद् ब्रूत सर्वं सत्येन युष्माकं ह्य् अत्र साक्षिता ॥ ८०
                                    ॥
verses.english: 'What ye know to have been mutually transacted in this matter between the two men before us, declare all that in accordance with the truth; for ye are witnesses in this (cause).

verses.text:
सत्यं साक्ष्ये ब्रुवन् साक्षी लोकान् आप्नोत्य् पुष्कलान् । ८.८१अव्/ म्: 
                                        आप्नोत्य् अनिन्दितान्
इह च-अन्.उत्तमां कीर्तिं वाग् एषा ब्रह्मपूजिता ॥ ८१
                                    ॥
verses.english: 'A witness who speaks the truth in his evidence, gains (after death) the most excellent regions (of bliss) and here (below) unsurpassable fame; such testimony is revered by Brahman (himself).

verses.text:
साक्ष्ये ऽनृतं वदन् पाशैर् बध्यते वारुणैर् भृशम् ।
विवशः शतम् आजातीस् तस्मात् साक्ष्यं वदेद् ऋतम् ॥ ८२
                                    ॥
verses.english: 'He who gives false evidence is firmly bound by Varuna's fetters, helpless during one hundred existences; let (men therefore) give true evidence.

verses.text:
सत्येन पूयते साक्षी धर्मः सत्येन वर्धते ।
तस्मात् सत्यं हि वक्तव्यं सर्ववर्णेषु साक्षिभिः ॥ ८३
                                    ॥
verses.english: 'By truthfulness a witness is purified, through truthfulness his merit grows, truth must, therefore, be spoken by witnesses of all castes (varna).

verses.text:
आत्मा-एव ह्य् आत्मनः साक्षी गतिर् आत्मा तथा-आत्मनः ।
मा-अवमंस्थाः स्वम् आत्मानं नृणां साक्षिणम् उत्तमम् ॥ ८४
                                    ॥
verses.english: 'The Soul itself is the witness of the Soul, and the Soul is the refuge of the Soul; despise not thy own Soul, the supreme witness of men.

verses.text:
मन्यन्ते वै पापकृतो न कश् चित् पश्यति-इति नः ।
तांस् तु देवाः प्रपश्यन्ति स्वस्य-एव-अन्तरपूरुषः ॥ ८५
                                    ॥
verses.english: 'The wicked, indeed, say in their hearts, "Nobody sees us;" but the gods distinctly see them and the male within their own breasts.

verses.text:
द्यौर् भूमिर् आपो हृदयं चन्द्र.अर्क.अग्नि.यम.अनिलाः
                                    ।
रात्रिः सन्ध्ये च धर्मश् च वृत्तज्ञाः सर्वदेहिनाम् ॥ ८६
                                    ॥
verses.english: 'The sky, the earth, the waters, (the male in) the heart, the moon, the sun, the fire, Yama and the wind, the night, the two twilights, and justice know the conduct of all corporeal beings.'

verses.text:
देव.ब्राह्मणसान्निध्ये साक्ष्यं पृच्छेद् ऋतं द्विजान् ।
उदङ्.मुखान् प्राङ्.मुखान् वा पूर्वाह्णे वै शुचिः शुचीन् ॥ ८७
                                    ॥
verses.english: The (judge), being purified, shall ask in the forenoon the twice-born (witnesses) who (also have been) purified, (and stand) facing the north or the east, to give true evidence in the presence of (images of) the gods and of Brahmanas.

verses.text:
ब्रूहि-इति ब्राह्मणं पृच्छेत् सत्यं ब्रूहि-इति पार्थिवम्
                                    ।
गो.बीज.काञ्चनैर् वैश्यं शूद्रं सर्वैस् तु पातकैः ॥
                                    ८८ ॥
verses.english: Let him examine a Brahmana (beginning with) 'Speak,' a Kshatriya (beginning with) 'Speak the truth,' a Vaisya (admonishing him) by (mentioning) his kine, grain, and gold, a Sudra (threatening him) with (the guilt of) every crime that causes loss of caste;

verses.text:
ब्रह्मघ्नो ये स्मृता लोका ये च स्त्री.बाल.घातिनः ।
मित्रद्रुहः कृत.घ्नस्य ते ते स्युर् ब्रुवतो मृषा ॥ ८९
                                    ॥
verses.english: (Saying), 'Whatever places (of torment) are assigned (by the sages) to the slayer of a Brahmana, to the murderer of women and children, to him who betrays a friend, and to an ungrateful man, those shall be thy (portion), if thou speakest falsely.

verses.text:
जन्मप्रभृति यत् किं चित् पुण्यं भद्र त्वया कृतम् ।
तत् ते सर्वं शुनो गच्छेद् यदि ब्रूयास् त्वम् अन्यथा ॥ ९०
                                    ॥
verses.english: '(The reward) of all meritorious deeds which thou, good man, hast done since thy birth, shall become the share of the dogs, if in thy speech thou departest from the truth.

verses.text:
एको ऽहम् अस्मि-इत्य् आत्मानं यस् त्वं कल्याण मन्यसे ।
नित्यं स्थितस् ते हृद्य् एष पुण्य.पाप.ईक्षिता मुनिः ॥ ९१
                                    ॥
verses.english: 'If thou thinkest, O friend of virtue, with respect to thyself, "I am alone," (know that) that sage who witnesses all virtuous acts and all crimes, ever resides in thy heart.

verses.text:
यमो वैवस्वतो देवो यस् तव-एष हृदि स्थितः ।
तेन चेद् अविवादस् ते मा गङ्गां मा कुरून् गमः ॥ ९२
                                    ॥
verses.english: 'If thou art not at variance with that divine Yama, the son of Vivasvat, who dwells in thy heart, thou needest neither visit the Ganges nor the (land of the) Kurus.

verses.text:
नग्नो मुण्डः कपालेन च भिक्षार्थी क्षुत्.पिपासितः ।
                                        ८.९३अव्/
                                        म्: कपाली
अन्धः शत्रुकुलं गच्छेद् यः साक्ष्यम् अनृतं वदेत् ॥ ९३
                                    ॥
verses.english: 'Naked and shorn, tormented with hunger and thirst, and deprived of sight, shall the man who gives false evidence, go with a potsherd to beg food at the door of his enemy.

verses.text:
अवाक्.शिरास् तमस्य् अन्धे किल्बिषी नरकं व्रजेत् ।
यः प्रश्नं वितथं ब्रूयात् पृष्टः सन् धर्मनिश्चये ॥
                                    ९४ ॥
verses.english: 'Headlong, in utter darkness shall the sinful man tumble into hell, who being interrogated in a judicial inquiry answers one question falsely.

verses.text:
अन्धो मत्स्यान् इव-अश्नाति स नरः कण्टकैः सह ।
यो भाषते ऽर्थवैकल्यम् अ.प्रत्यक्षं सभां गतः ॥ ९५
                                    ॥
verses.english: 'That man who in a court (of justice) gives an untrue account of a transaction (or asserts a fact) of which he was not an eye-witness, resembles a blind man who swallows fish with the bones.

verses.text:
यस्य विद्वान् हि वदतः क्षेत्रज्ञो न-अभिशङ्कते । ८.९६अव्/ म्: 
                                        न-अतिशङ्कते
तस्मान् न देवाः श्रेयांसं लोके ऽन्यं पुरुषं विदुः ॥ ९६
                                    ॥
verses.english: 'The gods are acquainted with no better man in this world than him, of whom his conscious Soul has no distrust, when he gives evidence.

verses.text:
यावतो बान्धवान् यस्मिन् हन्ति साक्ष्ये ऽनृतं वदन् ।
तावतः सङ्ख्यया तस्मिन् शृणु सौम्य-अनुपूर्वशः ॥ ९७
                                    ॥
verses.english: 'Learn now, O friend, from an enumeration in due order, how many relatives he destroys who gives false evidence in several particular cases.

verses.text:
पञ्च पशु.अनृते हन्ति दश हन्ति गवानृते ।
शतम् अश्वानृते हन्ति सहस्रं पुरुषानृते ॥ ९८ ॥
verses.english: 'He kills five by false Testimony regarding (small) cattle, he kills ten by false testimony regarding kine, he kills a hundred by false evidence concerning horses, and a thousand by false evidence concerning men.

verses.text:
हन्ति जातान् अजातांश् च हिरण्यार्थे ऽनृतं वदन् ।
सर्वं भूमि.अनृते हन्ति मा स्म भूमि.अनृतं वदीः ॥ ९९
                                    ॥
verses.english: 'By speaking falsely in a cause regarding gold, he kills the born and the unborn; by false evidence concerning land, he kills everything; beware, therefore, of false evidence concerning land.

verses.text:
अप्सु भूमिवद् इत्य् आहुः स्त्रीणां भोगे च मैथुने ।
अब्जेषु च-एव रत्नेषु सर्वेष्व् अश्ममयेषु च ॥ १००
                                    ॥
verses.english: 'They declare (false evidence) concerning water, concerning the carnal enjoyment of women, and concerning all gems, produced in water, or consisting of stones (to be) equally (wicked) as a lie concerning land.

verses.text:
एतान् दोषान् अवेक्ष्य त्वं सर्वान् अनृतभाषणे ।
यथाश्रुतं यथादृष्टं सर्वम् एव-अञ्जसा वद ॥ १०१
                                    ॥
verses.english: 'Marking well all the evils (which are produced) by perjury, declare thou openly everything as (thou hast) heard or seen (it).'

verses.text:
गोरक्षकान् वाणिजिकांस् तथा कारु.कुशीलवान् । ८.१०२अव्/ म्: 
                                        वाणिजकांस्
प्रेष्यान् वार्धुषिकांश् च-एव विप्रान् शूद्रवद् आचरेत् ॥
                                    १०२ ॥
verses.english: Brahmanas who tend cattle, who trade, who are mechanics, actors (or singers), menial servants or usurers, the (judge) shall treat like Sudras.

verses.text:
तद् वदन् धर्मतो ऽर्थेषु जानन्न् अप्य् अन्य्था नरः ।
न स्वर्गाच् च्यवते लोकाद् दैवीं वाचं वदन्ति ताम् ॥ १०३
                                    ॥
verses.english: In (some) cases a man who, though knowing (the facts to be) different, gives such (false evidence) from a pious motive, does not lose heaven; such (evidence) they call the speech of the gods.

verses.text:
शूद्र.विश्.क्षत्र.विप्राणां यत्र-ऋत.उक्तौ भवेद् वधः
                                    ।
तत्र वक्तव्यम् अनृतं तद्द् हि सत्याद् विशिष्यते ॥ १०४
                                    ॥
verses.english: Whenever the death of a Sudra, of a Vaisya, of a Kshatriya, or of a Brahmana would be (caused) by a declaration of the truth, a falsehood may be spoken; for such (falsehood) is preferable to the truth.

verses.text:
वाच्.दैवत्यैश् च चरुभिर् यजेरंस् ते सरस्वतीम् ।
अनृतस्य-एनसस् तस्य कुर्वाणा निष्कृतिं पराम् ॥ १०५
                                    ॥
verses.english: Such (witnesses) must offer to Sarasvati oblations of boiled rice (karu) which are sacred to the goddess of speech, (thus) performing the best penance in order to expiate the guilt of that falsehood.

Or such (a witness) may offer according to the rule, clarified butter in the fire, reciting the Kushmanda texts, or the Rik, sacred to Varuna, 'Untie, O Varuna, the uppermost fetter,' or the three verses addressed to the Waters.

verses.text:
त्रिपक्षाद् अब्रुवन् साक्ष्यम् ऋणादिषु नरो ऽ.गदः ।
तदृणं प्राप्नुयात् सर्वं दशबन्धं च सर्वतः ॥ १०७
                                    ॥
verses.english: A man who, without being ill, does not give evidence in (cases of) loans and the like within three fortnights (after the summons), shall become responsible for the whole debt and (pay) a tenth part of the whole (as a fine to the king).

verses.text:
यस्य दृश्येत सप्ताहाद् उक्त.वाक्यस्य साक्षिणः ।
रोगो ऽग्निर् ज्ञातिमरणम् ऋणं दाप्यो दमं च सः ॥ १०८
                                    ॥
verses.english: The witness to whom, within seven days after he has given evidence, happens (a misfortune through) sickness, a fire, or the death of a relative, shall be made to pay the debt and a fine.

verses.text:
असाक्षिकेषु त्व् अर्थेषु मिथो विवादमानयोः ।
अविन्दंस् तत्त्वतः सत्यं शपथेन-अपि लम्भयेत् ॥ १०९
                                    ॥
verses.english: If two (parties) dispute about matters for which no witnesses are available, and the (judge) is unable to really ascertain the truth, he may cause it to be discovered even by an oath.

verses.text:
महर्षिभिश् च देवैश् च कार्यार्थं शपथाः कृताः ।
वसिष्ठश् च-अपि शपथं शेपे पैजवने नृपे ॥ ११०
                                    ॥
verses.english: Both by the great sages and the gods oaths have been taken for the purpose of (deciding doubtful) matters; and Vasishtha even swore an oath before king (Sudas), the son of Pigavana.

verses.text:
न वृथा शपथं कुर्यात् स्वल्पे ऽप्य् अर्थे नरो बुधः
                                    ।
वृथा हि शपथं कुर्वन् प्रेत्य च-इह च नश्यति ॥ १११
                                    ॥
verses.english: Let no wise man swear an oath falsely, even in a trifling matter; for he who swears an oath falsely is lost in this (world) and after death.

verses.text:
कामिनीषु विवाहेषु गवां भक्ष्ये तथा-इन्धने ।
ब्राह्मण.अभ्युपपत्तौ च शपथे न-अस्ति पातकम् ॥ ११२
                                    ॥
verses.english: No crime, causing loss of caste, is committed by swearing (falsely) to women, the objects of one's desire, at marriages, for the sake of fodder for a cow, or of fuel, and in (order to show) favour to a Brahmana.

verses.text:
सत्येन शापयेद् विप्रं क्षत्रियं वाहन.आयुधैः ।
गो.बीज.काञ्चनैर् वैश्यं शूद्रं सर्वैस् तु पातकैः ॥
                                    ११३ ॥
verses.english: Let the (judge) cause a Brahmana to swear by his veracity, a Kshatriya by his chariot or the animal he rides on and by his weapons, a Vaisya by his kine, grain, and gold, and a Sudra by (imprecating on his own head the guilt) of all grievous offences (pataka).

verses.text:
अग्निं वा-आहारयेद् एनम् अप्सु च-एनं निमज्जयेत् ।
पुत्र.दारस्य वा-अप्य् एनं शिरांसि स्पर्शयेत् पृथक् ॥
                                    ११४ ॥
verses.english: Or the (judge) may cause the (party) to carry fire or to dive under water, or severally to touch the heads of his wives and children.

verses.text:
यम् इद्धो न दहत्य् अग्निर् आपो न-उन्मज्जयन्ति च ।
न च-आर्तिम् ऋच्छति क्षिप्रं स ज्ञेयः शपथे शुचिः ॥
                                    ११५ ॥
verses.english: He whom the blazing fire burns not, whom the water forces not to come (quickly) up, who meets with no speedy misfortune, must be held innocent on (the strength of) his oath.

verses.text:
वत्सस्य ह्य् अभिशस्तस्य पुरा भ्रात्रा यवीयसा ।
न-अग्निर् ददाह रोम-अपि सत्येन जगतः स्पशः ॥ ११६
                                    ॥
verses.english: For formerly when Vatsa was accused by his younger brother, the fire, the spy of the world, burned not even a hair (of his) by reason of his veracity.

verses.text:
यस्मिन् यस्मिन् विवादे तु कौटसाक्ष्यं कृतं भवेत् ।
तत् तत् कार्यं निवर्तेत कृतं च-अप्य् अकृतं भवेत् ॥
                                    ११७ ॥
verses.english: Whenever false evidence has been given in any suit, let the (judge) reverse the judgment, and whatever has been done must be (considered as) undone.

verses.text:
लोभात्-मोहाद् भयात्-मैत्रात् कामात् क्रोधात् तथा-एव च
                                    ।
अज्ञानाद् बालभावात्-च साक्ष्यं वितथम् उच्यते ॥ ११८
                                    ॥
verses.english: Evidence (given) from covetousness, distraction, terror, friendship, lust, wrath, ignorance, and childishness is declared (to be) invalid.

verses.text:
एषाम् अन्यतमे स्थाने यः साक्ष्यम् अनृतं वदेत् ।
तस्य दण्डविशेषांस् तु प्रवक्ष्याम्य् अनुपूर्वशः ॥ ११९
                                    ॥
verses.english: I will propound in (due) order the particular punishments for him who gives false evidence from any one of these motives.

verses.text:
लोभात् सहस्रं दण्ड्यस् तु मोहात् पूर्वं तु साहसम् ।
भयाद् द्वौ मध्यमौ दण्डौ मैत्रात् पूर्वं चतुर्गुणम्
                                    ॥ १२० ॥
verses.english: (He who commits perjury) through covetousness shall be fined one thousand (panas), (he who does it) through distraction, in the lowest amercement; (if a man does it) through fear, two middling amercements shall be paid as a fine, (if he does it) through friendship, four times the amount of the lowest (amercement).

verses.text:
कामाद् दशगुणं पूर्वं क्रोधात् तु त्रिगुणं परम् ।
अज्ञानाद् द्वे शते पूर्णे बालिश्यात्-शतम् एव तु ॥ १२१
                                    ॥
verses.english: (He who does it) through lust, (shall pay) ten times the lowest amercement, but (he who does it) through wrath, three times the next (or second amercement); (he who does it) through ignorance, two full hundreds, but (he who does it) through childishness, one hundred (panas).

verses.text:
एतान् आहुः कौटसाक्ष्ये प्रोक्तान् दण्डान् मनीषिभिः ।
धर्मस्य-अव्यभिचारार्थम् अधर्मनियमाय च ॥ १२२
                                    ॥
verses.english: They declare that the wise have prescribed these fines for perjury, in order to prevent a failure of justice, and in order to restrain injustice.

verses.text:
कौटसाक्ष्यं तु कुर्वाणांस् त्रीन् वर्णान् धार्मिको नृपः
                                    ।
प्रवासयेद् दण्डयित्वा ब्राह्मणं तु विवासयेत् ॥ १२३
                                    ॥
verses.english: But a just king shall fine and banish (men of) the three (lower) castes (varna) who have given false evidence, but a Brahmana he shall (only) banish.

verses.text:
दश स्थानानि दण्डस्य मनुः स्वयम्भुवो ऽब्रवीत् ।
त्रिषु वर्णेषु यानि स्युर् अक्षतो ब्राह्मणो व्रजेत् ॥ १२४
                                    ॥
verses.english: Manu, the son of the Self-existent (Svayambhu), has named ten places on which punishment may be (made to fall) in the cases of the three (lower) castes (varna); but a Brahmana shall depart unhurt (from the country).

verses.text:
उपस्थम् उदरं जिह्वा हस्तौ पादौ च पञ्चमम् ।
चक्षुर् नासा च कर्णौ च धनं देहस् तथा-एव च ॥
                                    १२५ ॥
verses.english: (These are) the organ, the belly, the tongue, the two hands, and fifthly the two feet, the eye, the nose, the two ears, likewise the (whole) body.

verses.text:
अनुबन्धं परिज्ञाय देश.कालौ च तत्त्वतः ।
सार.अपराधो च-आलोक्य दण्डं दण्ड्येषु पातयेत् ॥ १२६
                                    ॥
verses.english: Let the (king), having fully ascertained the motive, the time and place (of the offence), and having considered the ability (of the criminal to suffer) and the (nature of the) crime, cause punishment to fall on those who deserve it.

verses.text:
अधर्मदण्डनं लोके यशोघ्नं कीर्तिनाशनम् ।
अस्वर्ग्यं च परत्र-अपि तस्मात् तत् परिवर्जयेत् ॥ १२७
                                    ॥
verses.english: Unjust punishment destroys reputation among men, and fame (after death), and causes even in the next world the loss of heaven; let him, therefore, beware of (inflicting) it.

verses.text:
अदण्ड्यान् दण्डयन् राजा दण्ड्यांश् च-एव-अप्य् अदण्डयन्
                                    ।
अयशो महद् आप्नोति नरकं च-एव गच्छति ॥ १२८ ॥
verses.english: A king who punishes those who do not deserve it, and punishes not those who deserve it, brings great infamy on himself and (after death) sinks into hell.

verses.text:
वाग्दण्डं प्रथमं कुर्याद् धिग्दण्डं तदनन्तरम् ।
तृतीयं धनदण्डं तु वधदण्डम् अतः परम् ॥ १२९
                                    ॥
verses.english: Let him punish first by (gentle) admonition, afterwards by (harsh) reproof, thirdly by a fine, after that by corporal chastisement.

verses.text:
वधेन-अपि यदा त्व् एतान् निग्रहीतुं न शक्नुयात् ।
तदा-एषु सर्वम् अप्य् एतत् प्रयुञ्जीत चतुष्टयम् ॥ १३०
                                    ॥
verses.english: But when he cannot restrain such (offenders) even by corporal punishment, then let him apply to them even all the four (modes cojointly).

verses.text:
लोकसंव्यवहारार्थं याः सञ्ज्ञाः प्रथिता भुवि ।
ताम्र.रूप्य.सुवर्णानां ताः प्रवक्ष्याम्य् अशेषतः ॥ १३१
                                    ॥
verses.english: Those technical names of (certain quantities of) copper, silver, and gold, which are generally used on earth for the purpose of business transactions among men, I will fully declare.

verses.text:
जालान्तरगते भानौ यत् सूक्ष्मं दृश्यते रजः ।
प्रथमं तत् प्रमाणानां त्रसरेणुं प्रचक्षते ॥ १३२
                                    ॥
verses.english: The very small mote which is seen when the sun shines through a lattice, they declare (to be) the least of (all) quantities and (to be called) a trasarenu (a floating particle of dust).

verses.text:
त्रसरेणवो ऽष्टौ विज्ञेया लिक्षा-एका परिमाणतः ।
ता राजसर्षपस् तिस्रस् ते त्रयो गौरसर्षपः ॥ १३३
                                    ॥
verses.english: Know (that) eight trasarenus (are equal) in bulk (to) a liksha (the egg of a louse), three of those to one grain of black mustard (ragasarshapa), and three of the latter to a white mustard-seed.

verses.text:
सर्षपाः षड् यवो मध्यस् त्रियवं त्व् एककृष्णलम् ।
पञ्चकृष्णलको माषस् ते सुवर्णस् तु षोडश ॥ १३४ ॥
verses.english: Six grains of white mustard are one middle-sized barley-corn, and three barley-corns one krishnala (raktika, or gunga-berry); five krishnalas are one masha (bean), and sixteen of those one suvarna.

verses.text:
पलं सुवर्णाश् चत्वारः पलानि धरणं दश ।
द्वे कृष्णले समधृते विज्ञेयो रौप्यमाषकः ॥ १३५ ॥
                                        ८.१३५च्व्/
                                        म्: रूप्यमाषकः ॥ 8.135 ॥
verses.english: Four suvarnas are one pala, and ten palas one dharana; two krishnalas (of silver), weighed together, must be considered one mashaka of silver.

verses.text:
ते षोडश स्याद् धरणं पुराणश् च-एव राजतः ।
कार्षापणस् तु विज्ञेयस् ताम्रिकः कार्षिकः पणः ॥ १३६
                                    ॥
verses.english: Sixteen of those make a silver dharana, or purana; but know (that) a karsha of copper is a karshapana, or pana.

verses.text:
धरणानि दश ज्ञेयः शतमानस् तु राजतः ।
चतुःसौवर्णिको निष्को विज्ञेयस् तु प्रमाणतः ॥ १३७
                                    ॥
verses.english: Know (that) ten dharanas of silver make one satamana; four suvarnas must be considered (equal) in weight to a nishka.

verses.text:
पणानां द्वे शते सार्धे प्रथमः साहसः स्मृतः ।
मध्यमः पञ्च विज्ञेयः सहस्रं त्व् एव च-उत्तमः ॥
                                    १३८ ॥
verses.english: Two hundred and fifty panas are declared (to be) the first (or lowest) amercement, five (hundred) are considered as the mean (or middlemost), but one thousand as the highest.

verses.text:
ऋणे देये प्रतिज्ञाते पञ्चकं शतम् अर्हति ।
अपह्नवे तद्द्विगुणं तन् मनोर् अनुशासनम् ॥ १३९ ॥
verses.english: A debt being admitted as due, (the defendant) shall pay five in the hundred (as a fine), if it be denied (and proved) twice as much; that is the teaching of Manu.

verses.text:
वसिष्ठविहितां वृद्धिं सृजेद् वित्तविवर्धिनीम् ।
अशीतिभागं गृह्णीयान् मासाद् वार्धुषिकः शते ॥ १४०
                                    ॥
verses.english: A money-lender may stipulate as an increase of his capital, for the interest, allowed by Vasishtha, and take monthly the eightieth part of a hundred.

verses.text:
द्विकं शतं वा गृह्णीयात् सतां धर्मम् अनुस्मरन् ।
द्विकं शतं हि गृह्णानो न भवत्य् अर्थकिल्बिषी ॥ १४१
                                    ॥
verses.english: Or, remembering the duty of good men, he may take two in the hundred (by the month), for he who takes two in the hundred becomes not a sinner for gain.

verses.text:
द्विकं त्रिकं चतुष्कं च पञ्चकं च शतं समम् ।
मासस्य वृद्धिं गृह्णीयाद् वर्णानाम् अनुपूर्वशः ॥ १४२
                                    ॥
verses.english: Just two in the hundred, three, four, and five (and not more), he may take as monthly interest according to the order of the castes (varna).

verses.text:
न त्व् एव-आधौ स.उपकारे कौसीदीं वृद्धिम् आप्नुयात्
                                    ।
न च-आधेः कालसंरोधात्-निसर्गो ऽस्ति न विक्रयः ॥
                                    १४३ ॥
verses.english: But if a beneficial pledge (i.e. one from which profit accrues, has been given), he shall receive no interest on the loan; nor can he, after keeping (such) a pledge for a very long time, give or sell it.

verses.text:
न भोक्तव्यो बलाद् आधिर् भुञ्जानो वृद्धिम् उत्सृजेत् ।
मूल्येन तोषयेच् च-एनम् आधिस्तेनो ऽन्यथा भवेत् ॥ १४४
                                    ॥
verses.english: A pledge (to be kept only) must not be used by force, (the creditor), so using it, shall give up his (whole) interest, or, (if it has been spoilt by use) he shall satisfy the (owner) by (paying its) original price; else he commits a theft of the pledge.

verses.text:
आधिश् च-उपनिधिश् च-उभौ न कालात्ययम् अर्हतः ।
अवहार्यौ भवेतां तौ दीर्घकालम् अवस्थितौ ॥ १४५
                                    ॥
verses.english: Neither a pledge nor a deposit can be lost by lapse of time; they are both recoverable, though they have remained long (with the bailee).

verses.text:
सम्प्रीत्या भुज्यमानानि न नश्यन्ति कदा चन ।
धेनुर् उष्ट्रो वहन्न् अश्वो यश् च दम्यः प्रयुज्यते ॥ १४६
                                    ॥
verses.english: Things used with friendly assent, a cow, a camel, a riding-horse, and (a beast) made over for breaking in, are never lost (to the owner).

verses.text:
यत् किं चिद् दशवर्षाणि सन्निधौ प्रेक्षते धनी ।
भुज्यमानं परैस् तूष्णीं न स तत्-लब्धुम् अर्हति ॥
                                    १४७ ॥
verses.english: (But in general) whatever (chattel) an owner sees enjoyed by others during ten years, while, though present, he says nothing, that (chattel) he shall not recover.

verses.text:
अजडश् चेद् अपोगण्डो विषये च-अस्य भुज्यते ।
भग्नं तद् व्यवहारेण भोक्ता तद् द्रव्यम् अर्हति ॥ १४८
                                    ॥ ८.१४८च्व्/
                                        म्: तद् धनम् अर्हति ॥ 8.148 ॥
verses.english: If (the owner is) neither an idiot nor a minor and if (his chattel) is enjoyed (by another) before his eyes, it is lost to him by law; the adverse possessor shall retain that property.

verses.text:
आधिः सीमा बालधनं निक्षेप.उपनिधिः स्त्रियः । ८.१४९अव्/ म्: 
                                        निक्षेप.उपनिधी
राजस्वं श्रोत्रियस्वं च न भोगेन प्रणश्यति ॥ १४९
                                    ॥
verses.english: A pledge, a boundary, the property of infants, an (open) deposit, a sealed deposit, women, the property of the king and the wealth of a Srotriya are not lost in consequence of (adverse) enjoyment.

verses.text:
यः स्वामिना-अननुज्ञातम् आधिं भूङ्क्ते ऽविचक्षणः ।
तेन-अर्धवृद्धिर् मोक्तव्या तस्य भोगस्य निष्कृतिः ॥
                                    १५० ॥
verses.english: The fool who uses a pledge without the permission of the owner, shall remit half of his interest, as a compensation for (such) use.

verses.text:
कुसीदवृद्धिर् द्वैगुण्यं न-अत्येति सकृद् आहृता । ८.१५१अव्/ म्: 
                                        सकृद् आहिता
धान्ये सदे लवे वाह्ये न-अतिक्रामति पञ्चताम् ॥ १५१
                                    ॥
verses.english: In money transactions interest paid at one time (not by instalments) shall never exceed the double (of the principal); on grain, fruit, wool or hair, (and) beasts of burden it must not be more than five times (the original amount).

verses.text:
कृतानुसाराद् अधिका व्यतिरिक्ता न सिध्यति ।
कुसीदपथम् आहुस् तं पञ्चकं शतम् अर्हति ॥ १५२
                                    ॥
verses.english: Stipulated interest beyond the legal rate, being against (the law), cannot be recovered; they call that a usurious way (of lending); (the lender) is (in no case) entitled to (more than) five in the hundred.

verses.text:
न-अति.सांवत्सरीं वृद्धिं न च-अदृष्टां पुनर् हरेत् ।
                                        ८.१५३अव्/
                                        म्: विनिर्हरेत्
चक्रवृद्धिः कालवृद्धिः कारिता कायिका च या ॥ १५३
                                    ॥
verses.english: Let him not take interest beyond the year, nor such as is unapproved, nor compound interest, periodical interest, stipulated interest, and corporal interest.

verses.text:
ऋणं दातुम् अशक्तो यः कर्तुम् इच्छेत् पुनः क्रियाम् ।
स दत्त्वा निर्जितां वृद्धिं करणं परिवर्तयेत् ॥ १५४
                                    ॥
verses.english: He who, unable to pay a debt (at the fixed time), wishes to make a new contract, may renew the agreement, after paying the interest which is due.

verses.text:
अ.दर्शयित्वा तत्र-एव हिरण्यं परिवर्तयेत् ।
यावती सम्भवेद् वृद्धिस् तावतीं दातुम् अर्हति ॥ १५५
                                    ॥
verses.english: If he cannot pay the money (due as interest), he may insert it in the renewed (agreement); he must pay as much interest as may be due.

verses.text:
चक्रवृद्धिं समारूढो देश.कालव्यवस्थितः ।
अतिक्रामन् देश.कालौ न तत्फलम् अवाप्नुयात् ॥ १५६
                                    ॥
verses.english: He who has made a contract to carry goods by a wheeled carriage for money and has agreed to a certain place or time, shall not reap that reward, if he does not keep to the place and the time (stipulated).

verses.text:
समुद्रयानकुशला देश.काल.अर्थदर्शिनः ।
स्थापयन्ति तु यां वृद्धिं सा तत्र-अधिगमं प्रति ॥
                                    १५७ ॥
verses.english: Whatever rate men fix, who are expert in sea-voyages and able to calculate (the profit) according to the place, the time, and the objects (carried), that (has legal force) in such cases with respect to the payment (to be made).

verses.text:
यो यस्य प्रतिभूस् तिष्ठेद् दर्शनाय-इह मानवः ।
अ.दर्शयन् स तं तस्य प्रयच्छेत् स्वधनाद् ऋणम् ॥ १५८
                                    ॥ ८.१५८च्व्/
                                        म्: तस्य यतेत ॥ 8.158 ॥
verses.english: The man who becomes a surety in this (world) for the appearance of a (debtor), and produces him not, shall pay the debt out of his own property.

verses.text:
प्रातिभाव्यं वृथादानम् आक्षिकं सौरिकां च यत् ।
दण्ड.शुल्कावशेषं च न पुत्रो दातुम् अर्हति ॥ १५९
                                    ॥
verses.english: But money due by a surety, or idly promised, or lost at play, or due for spirituous liquor, or what remains unpaid of a fine and a tax or duty, the son (of the party owing it) shall not be obliged to pay.

verses.text:
दर्शनप्रातिभाव्ये तु विधिः स्यात् पूर्वचोदितः ।
दानप्रतिभुवि प्रेते दायादान् अपि दापयेत् ॥ १६० ॥
verses.english: This just mentioned rule shall apply to the case of a surety for appearance (only); if a surety for payment should die, the (judge) may compel even his heirs to discharge the debt.

verses.text:
अदातरि पुनर् दाता विज्ञातप्रकृताव् ऋणम् ।
पश्चात् प्रतिभुवि प्रेते परीप्सेत् केन हेतुना ॥ १६१
                                    ॥
verses.english: On what account then is it that after the death of a surety other than for payment, whose affairs are fully known, the creditor may (in some cases) afterwards demand the debt (of the heirs)?

verses.text:
निरादिष्टधनश् चेत् तु प्रतिभूः स्याद् अलन्धनः ।
स्वधनाद् एव तद् दद्यान् निरादिष्ट इति स्थितिः ॥ १६२
                                    ॥
verses.english: If the surety had received money (from him for whom he stood bail) and had money enough (to pay), then (the heir of him) who received it, shall pay (the debt) out of his property; that is the settled rule.

verses.text:
मत्त.उन्मत्त.आर्त.अध्यधीनैर् बालेन स्थविरेण वा
                                    ।
असम्बद्धकृतश् च-एव व्यावहारो न सिध्यति ॥ १६३
                                    ॥
verses.english: A contract made by a person intoxicated, or insane, or grievously disordered (by disease and so forth), or wholly dependent, by an infant or very aged man, or by an unauthorised (party) is invalid.

verses.text:
सत्या न भाषा भवति यद्य् अपि स्यात् प्रतिष्ठिता ।
बहिश् चेद् भाष्यते धर्मात्-नियताद् व्यवहारिकात् ॥ १६४
                                    ॥
verses.english: That agreement which has been made contrary to the law or to the settled usage (of the virtuous), can have no legal force, though it be established (by proofs).

verses.text:
योगाधमनविक्रीतं योगदानप्रतिग्रहम् ।
यत्र वा-अप्य् उपधिं पश्येत् तत् सर्वं विनिवर्तयेत् ॥
                                    १६५ ॥
verses.english: A fraudulent mortgage or sale, a fraudulent gift or acceptance, and (any transaction) where he detects fraud, the (judge) shall declare null and void.

verses.text:
ग्रहीता यदि नष्टः स्यात् कुटुम्बार्थे कृतो व्ययः । ८.१६६अव्/ म्: 
                                        कुटुम्बे च
दातव्यं बान्धवैस् तत् स्यात् प्रविभक्तैर् अपि स्वतः ॥
                                    १६६ ॥
verses.english: If the debtor be dead and (the money borrowed) was expended for the family, it must be paid by the relatives out of their own estate even if they are divided.

verses.text:
कुटुम्बार्थे ऽध्यधीनो ऽपि व्यवहारं यम् आचरेत् ।
स्वदेशे वा विदेशे वा तं ज्यायान् न विचालयेत् ॥ १६७
                                    ॥
verses.english: Should even a person wholly dependent make a contract for the behoof of the family, the master (of the house), whether (living) in his own country or abroad, shall not rescind it.

verses.text:
बलाद् दत्तं बलाद् भुक्तं बलाद् यच् च-अपि लेखितम्
                                    ।
सर्वान् बलकृतान् अर्थान् अकृतान् मनुर् अब्रवीत् ॥ १६८
                                    ॥
verses.english: What is given by force, what is enjoyed by force, also what has been caused to be written by force, and all other transactions done by force, Manu has declared void.

verses.text:
त्रयः परार्थे क्लिश्यन्ति साक्षिणः प्रतिभूः कुलम् ।
चत्वारस् तु-उपचीयन्ते विप्र आढ्यो वणिङ् नृपः ॥ १६९
                                    ॥
verses.english: Three suffer for the sake of others, witnesses, a surety, and judges; but four enrich themselves (through others), a Brahmana, a money-lender, a merchant, and a king.

verses.text:
अन्.आदेयं न-आददीत परिक्षीणो ऽपि पार्थिवः ।
न च-आदेयं समृद्धो ऽपि सूक्ष्मम् अप्य् अर्थम् उत्सृजेत् ॥
                                    १७० ॥
verses.english: No king, however indigent, shall take anything that ought not to be taken, nor shall he, however wealthy, decline taking that which he ought to take, be it ever so small.

verses.text:
अन्.आदेयस्य च-आदानाद् आदेयस्य च वर्जनात् ।
दौर्बल्यं ख्याप्यते राज्ञः स प्रेत्य-इह च नश्यति ॥
                                    १७१ ॥
verses.english: In consequence of his taking what ought not to be taken, or of his refusing what ought to be received, a king will be accused of weakness and perish in this (world) and after death.

verses.text:
स्वादानाद् वर्णसंसर्गात् त्व् अबलानां च रक्षणात् ।
बलं सञ्जायते राज्ञः स प्रेत्य-इह च वर्धते ॥ १७२
                                    ॥
verses.english: By taking his due, by preventing the confusion of the castes (varna), and by protecting the weak, the power of the king grows, and he prospers in this (world) and after death.

verses.text:
तस्माद् यम इव स्वामी स्वयं हित्वा प्रिय.अप्रिये ।
वर्तेत याम्यया वृत्त्या जित.क्रोधो जित.इन्द्रियः ॥ १७३
                                    ॥
verses.english: Let the prince, therefore, like Yama, not heeding his own likings and dislikings, behave exactly like Yama, suppressing his anger and controlling himself.

verses.text:
यस् त्व् अधर्मेण कार्याणि मोहात् कुर्यान् नराधिपः ।
अचिरात् तं दुर्.आत्मानं वशे कुर्वन्ति शत्रवः ॥ १७४
                                    ॥
verses.english: But that evil-minded king who in his folly decides causes unjustly, his enemies soon subjugate.

verses.text:
काम.क्रोधौ तु संयम्य यो ऽर्थान् धर्मेण पश्यति
                                    ।
प्रजास् तम् अनुवर्तन्ते समुद्रम् इव सिन्धवः ॥ १७५
                                    ॥
verses.english: If, subduing love and hatred, he decides the causes according to the law, (the hearts of) his subjects turn towards him as the rivers (run) towards the ocean.

verses.text:
यः साधयन्तं छन्देन वेदयेद् धनिकं नृपे ।
स राज्ञा तत्-चतुर्भागं दाप्यस् तस्य च तद् धनम् ॥
                                    १७६ ॥
verses.english: (The debtor) who complains to the king that his creditor recovers (the debt) independently (of the court), shall be compelled by the king to pay (as a fine) one quarter (of the sum) and to his (creditor) the money (due).

verses.text:
कर्मणा-अपि समं कुर्याद् धनिकाय-अधमर्णिकः ।
समो ऽवकृष्टजातिस् तु दद्यात्-श्रेयांस् तु तत्- शनैः ॥
                                    १७७ ॥
verses.english: Even by (personal) labour shall the debtor make good (what he owes) to his creditor, if he be of the same caste or of a lower one; but a (debtor) of a higher caste shall pay it gradually (when he earns something).

verses.text:
अनेन विधिना राजा मिथो विवदतां नृणाम् ।
साक्षिप्रत्ययसिद्धानि कार्याणि समतां नयेत् ॥ १७८
                                    ॥
verses.english: According to these rules let the king equitably decide between men, who dispute with each other the matters, which are proved by witnesses and (other) evidence.

verses.text:
कुलजे वृत्तसम्पन्ने धर्मज्ञे सत्यवादिनि ।
महापक्षे धनिन्य् आर्ये निक्षेपं निक्षिपेद् बुधः ॥ १७९
                                ॥
verses.english: A sensible man should make a deposit (only) with a person of (good) family, of good conduct, well acquainted with the law, veracious, having many relatives, wealthy, and honourable (arya).

verses.text:
यो यथा निक्षिपेद्द् हस्ते यम् अर्थं यस्य मानवः ।
स तथा-एव ग्रहीतव्यो यथा दायस् तथा ग्रहः ॥ १८०
                                ॥
verses.english: In whatever manner a person shall deposit anything in the hands of another, in the same manner ought the same thing to be received back (by the owner); as the delivery (was, so must be) the re-delivery.

verses.text:
यो निक्षेपं याच्यमानो निक्षेप्तुर् न प्रयच्छति ।
स याच्यः प्राड्विवाकेन तत्-निक्षेप्तुर् असन्निधौ ॥ १८१
                                ॥
verses.english: He who restores not his deposit to the depositor at his request, may be tried by the judge in the depositor's absence.

verses.text:
साक्षि.अभावे प्रणिधिभिर् वयो.रूप.समन्वितैः ।
अपदेशैश् च सन्न्यस्य हिरण्यं तस्य तत्त्वतः ॥ १८२
                                ॥
verses.english: On failure of witnesses let the (judge) actually deposit gold with that (defendant) under some pretext or other through spies of suitable age and appearance (and afterwards demand it back).

verses.text:
स यदि प्रतिपद्येत यथान्यस्तं यथाकृतम् ।
न तत्र विद्यते किं चिद् यत् परैर् अभियुज्यते ॥ १८३
                                ॥
verses.english: If the (defendant) restores it in the manner and shape in which it was bailed, there is nothing (of that description) in his hands, for which others accuse him.

verses.text:
तेषां न दद्याद् यदि तु तद्द् हिरण्यं यथाविधि ।
उभौ निगृह्य दाप्यः स्याद् इति धर्मस्य धारणा ॥ १८४ ॥
                                    ८.१८४च्व्/ म्: 
                                    स निगृह्य-उभयं दाप्य इति धर्मस्य धारणा ॥ 8.184 ॥
verses.english: But if he restores not that gold, as be ought, to those (spies), then he shall be compelled by force to restore both (deposits); that is a settled rule of law.

verses.text:
निक्षेप.उपनिधी नित्यं न देयौ प्रत्यनन्तरे ।
नश्यतो विनिपाते ताव् अनिपाते त्व् अनाशिनौ ॥ १८५ ॥
verses.english: An open or a sealed deposit must never be returned to a near relative (of the depositor during the latter's lifetime); for if (the recipient) dies (without delivering them), they are lost, but if he does not die, they are not lost.

verses.text:
स्वयम् एव तु यौ दद्यान् मृतस्य प्रत्यनन्तरे ।
न स राज्ञा-अभियोक्तव्यो न निक्षेप्तुश् च बन्धुभिः ॥ १८६
                                ॥
verses.english: But (a depositary) who of his own accord returns them to a near relative of a deceased (depositor), must not be harassed (about them) by the king or by the depositor's relatives.

verses.text:
अच्छलेन-एव च-अन्विच्छेत् तम् अर्थं प्रीतिपूर्वकम् ।
विचार्य तस्य वा वृत्तं साम्ना-एव परिसाधयेत् ॥ १८७ ॥
verses.english: And (in doubtful cases) he should try to obtain that object by friendly means, without (having recourse to) artifice, or having inquired into (depositary's) conduct, he should settle (the matter) with gentle means.

verses.text:
