निक्षेपेष्व् एषु सर्वेषु विधिः स्यात् परिसाधने ।
स.मुद्रे न-आप्नुयात् किं चिद् यदि तस्मान् न संहरेत् ॥ १८८
                                ॥
verses.english: Such is the rule for obtaining back all those open deposits; in the case of a sealed deposit (the depositary) shall incur no (censure), unless he has taken out something.

verses.text:
चौरैर् हृतं जलेन-ऊढम् अग्निना दग्धम् एव वा ।
न दद्याद् यदि तस्मात् स न संहरति किं चन ॥ १८९ ॥
verses.english: (A deposit) which has been stolen by thieves or washed away by water or burned by fire, (the bailee) shall not make it good, unless he took part of it (for himself).

verses.text:
निक्षेपस्य-अपहर्तारम् अनिक्षेप्तारम् एव च ।
सर्वैर् उपायैर् अन्विच्छेत्-शपथैश् च-एव वैदिकैः ॥ १९०
                                ॥
verses.english: Him who appropriates a deposit and him (who asks for it) without having made it, (the judge) shall try by all (sorts of) means, and by the oaths prescribed in the Veda.

verses.text:
यो निक्षेपं न-अर्पयति यश् च-अ.निक्षिप्य याचते ।
ताव् उभौ चौरवत्-शास्यौ दाप्यौ वा तत्समं दमम् ॥ १९१
                                ॥
verses.english: He who does not return a deposit and he who demands what he never bailed shall both be punished like thieves, or be compelled to pay a fine equal (to the value of the object retained or claimed).

verses.text:
निक्षेपस्य-अपहर्तारं तत्समं दापयेद् दमम् ।
तथा-उपनिधिहर्तारम् अविशेषेण पार्थिवः ॥ १९२ ॥
verses.english: The king should compel him who does not restore an open deposit, and in like manner him who retains a sealed deposit, to pay a fine equal (to its value).

verses.text:
उपधाभिश् च यः कश् चित् परद्रव्यं हरेन् नरः ।
स.सहायः स हन्तव्यः प्रकाशं विविधैर् वधैः ॥ १९३
                                ॥
verses.english: That man who by false pretences may possess himself of another's property, shall be publicly punished by various (modes of) corporal (or capital) chastisement, together with his accomplices.

verses.text:
निक्षेपो यः कृतो येन यावांश् च कुलसन्निधौ ।
तावान् एव स विज्ञेयो विब्रुवन् दण्डम् अर्हति ॥ १९४ ॥
verses.english: If a deposit of a particular description or quantity is bailed by anybody in the presence of a number (of witnesses), it must be known to be of that particular (description and quantity; the depositary) who makes a false statement (regarding it) is liable to a fine.

verses.text:
मिथो दायः कृतो येन गृहीतो मिथ एव वा ।
मिथ एव प्रदातव्यो यथा दायस् तथा ग्रहः ॥ १९५ ॥
verses.english: But if anything is delivered or received privately, it must be privately returned; as the bailment (was, so should be) the re-delivery.

verses.text:
निक्षिप्तस्य धनस्य-एवं प्रीत्या-उपनिहितस्य च ।
राजा विनिर्णयं कुर्याद् अक्षिण्वन् न्यासधारिणम् ॥ १९६ ॥
verses.english: Thus let the king decide (causes) concerning a deposit and a friendly loan (for use) without showing (undue) rigour to the depositary.

verses.text:
विक्रीणीते परस्य स्वं यो ऽस्वामी स्वाम्यसम्मतः ।
न तं नयेत साक्ष्यं तु स्तेनम् अस्तेनमानिनम् ॥ १९७ ॥
verses.english: If anybody sells the property of another man, without being the owner and without the assent of the owner, the (judge) shall not admit him who is a thief, though he may not consider himself as a thief, as a witness (in any case).

verses.text:
अवहार्यो भवेत्-च-एव स.अन्वयः षट्शतं दमम् ।
निर्.अन्वयो ऽन्.अपसरः प्राप्तः स्याच् चौरकिल्बिषम् ॥ १९८
                                ॥
verses.english: If the (offender) is a kinsman (of the owner), he shall be fined six hundred panas; if he is not a kinsman, nor has any excuse, he shall be guilty of theft.

verses.text:
अस्वामिना कृतो यस् तु दायो विक्रय एव वा ।
अकृतः स तु विज्ञेयो व्यवहारे यथा स्थितिः ॥ १९९ ॥
verses.english: A gift or sale, made by anybody else but the owner, must be considered as null and void, according to the rule in judicial proceedings.

verses.text:
सम्भोगो दृश्यते यत्र न दृश्येत-आगमः क्व चित् ।
आगमः कारणं तत्र न सम्भोग इति स्थितिः ॥ २०० ॥
verses.english: Where possession is evident, but no title is perceived, there the title (shall be) a proof (of ownership), not possession; such is the settled rule.

verses.text:
विक्रयाद् यो धनं किं चिद् गृह्णीयत् कुलसन्निधौ ।
क्रयेण स विशुद्धं हि न्यायतो लभते धनम् ॥ २०१ ॥
verses.english: He who obtains a chattel in the market before a number (of witnesses), acquires that chattel with a clear legal title by purchase.

verses.text:
अथ मूलम् अनाहार्यं प्रकाशक्रयशोधितः ।
अदण्ड्यो मुच्यते राज्ञा नाष्टिको लभते धनम् ॥ २०२ ॥
verses.english: If the original (seller) be not producible, (the buyer) being exculpated by a public sale, must be dismissed by the king without punishment, but (the former owner) who lost the chattel shall receive it (back from the buyer).

verses.text:
न-अन्यद् अन्येन संसृष्टरूपं विक्रयम् अर्हति ।
न च-अ.सारं न च न्यूनं न दूरेण तिरोहितम् ॥ २०३ ॥
                                        ८.२०३च्व्/
                                        म्: न सावद्यं न च न्यूनं न दूरे न तिरोहितम् ॥ 8.203 ॥
verses.english: One commodity mixed with another must not be sold (as pure), nor a bad one (as good), nor less (than the proper quantity or weight), nor anything that is not at hand or that is concealed.

verses.text:
अन्यां चेद् दर्शयित्वा-अन्या वोढुः कन्या प्रदीयते ।
उभे त एकशुल्केन वहेद् इत्य् अब्रवीन् मनुः ॥ २०४ ॥
verses.english: If, after one damsel has been shown, another be given to the bridegroom, he may marry them both for the same price; that Manu ordained.

verses.text:
न-उन्मत्ताया न कुष्ठिन्या न च या स्पृष्ट.मैथुना ।
पूर्वं दोषान् अभिख्याप्य प्रदाता दण्डम् अर्हति ॥ २०५
                                    ॥
verses.english: He who gives (a damsel in marriage), having first openly declared her blemishes, whether she be insane, or afflicted with leprosy, or have lost her virginity, is not liable to punishment.

verses.text:
ऋत्विग् यदि वृतो यज्ञे स्वकर्म परिहापयेत् ।
तस्य कर्मानुरूपेण देयो ऽंशः सहकर्तृभिः ॥ २०६ ॥
verses.english: If an officiating priest, chosen to perform a sacrifice, abandons his work, a share only (of the fee) in proportion to the work (done) shall be given to him by those who work with him.

verses.text:
दक्षिणासु च दत्तासु स्वकर्म परिहापयन् ।
कृत्स्नम् एव लभेत-अंशम् अन्येन-एव च कारयेत् ॥ २०७
                                ॥
verses.english: But he who abandons his work after the sacrificial fees have been given, shall obtain his full share and cause to be performed (what remains) by another (priest).

verses.text:
यस्मिन् कर्मणि यास् तु स्युर् उक्ताः प्रत्यङ्गदक्षिणाः ।
स एव ता आदिदीत भजेरन् सर्व एव वा ॥ २०८ ॥
verses.english: But if (specific) fees are ordained for the several parts of a rite, shall he (who performs the part) receive them, or shall they all share them?

verses.text:
रथं हरेत् च-अध्वर्युर् ब्रह्मा-आधाने च वाजिनम् ।
होता वा-अपि हरेद् अश्वम् उद्गाता च-अप्य् अनः क्रये ॥ २०९
                                ॥
verses.english: The Adhvaryu priest shall take the chariot, and the Brahman at the kindling of the fires (Agnyadhana) a horse, the Hotri priest shall also take a horse, and the Udgatri the cart, (used) when (the Soma) is purchased.

verses.text:
सर्वेषाम् अर्धिनो मुख्यास् तदर्धेन-अर्धिनो ऽपरे ।
तृतीयिनस् तृतीयांशाश् चतुर्थांशाश् च पादिनः ॥ २१० ॥
verses.english: The (four) chief priests among all (the sixteen), who are entitled to one half, shall receive a moiety (of the fee), the next (four) one half of that, the set entitled to a third share, one third, and those entitled to a fourth a quarter.

verses.text:
सम्भूय स्वानि कर्माणि कुर्वद्भिर् इह मानवैः ।
अनेन विधियोगेन कर्तव्या-अंशप्रकल्पना ॥ २११ ॥
verses.english: By the application of these principles the allotment of shares must be made among those men who here (below) perform their work conjointly.

verses.text:
धर्मार्थं येन दत्तं स्यात् कस्मै चिद् याचते धनम् ।
पश्चाच् च न तथा तत् स्यान् न देयं तस्य तद् भवेत् ॥ २१२
                                ॥
verses.english: Should money be given (or promised) for a pious purpose by one man to another who asks for it, the gift shall be void, if the (money is) afterwards not (used) in the manner (stated).

verses.text:
यदि संसाधयेत् तत् तु दर्पात्-लोभेन वा पुनः ।
राज्ञा दाप्यः सुवर्णं स्यात् तस्य स्तेयस्य निष्कृतिः ॥ २१३
                                ॥
verses.english: But if the (recipient) through pride or greed tries to enforce (the fulfilment of the promise), he shall be compelled by the king to pay one suvarna as an expiation for his theft.

verses.text:
दत्तस्य-एषा-उदिता धर्म्या यथावद् अनपक्रिया ।
अत ऊर्ध्वं प्रवक्ष्यामि वेतनस्य-अनपक्रियाम् ॥ २१४ ॥
verses.english: Thus the lawful subtraction of a gift has been fully explained; I will next propound (the law for) the non-payment of wages.

verses.text:
भृतो न-आर्तो न कुर्याद् यो दर्पात् कर्म यथाअ.उदितम् ।
                                    ८.२१५अव्/ म्: 
                                    अनार्तो
स दण्ड्यः कृष्णलान्य् अष्टौ न देयं च-अस्य वेतनम् ॥ २१५
                                ॥
verses.english: A hired (servant or workman) who, without being ill, out of pride fails to perform his work according to the agreement, shall be fined eight krishnalas and no wages shall be paid to him.

verses.text:
आर्तस् तु कुर्यात् स्वस्थः सन् यथाभाषितम् आदितः ।
स दीर्घस्य-अपि कालस्य तत्-लभेत(-एव वेतनम् ॥ २१६
                                ॥
verses.english: But (if he is really) ill, (and) after recovery performs (his work) according to the original agreement, he shall receive his wages even after (the lapse of) a very long time.

verses.text:
यथा.उक्तम् आर्तः सुस्थो वा यस् तत् कर्म न कारयेत् ।
न तस्य वेतनं देयम् अल्प.ऊनस्य-अपि कर्मणः ॥ २१७
                                ॥
verses.english: But if he, whether sick or well, does not (perform or) cause to be performed (by others) his work according to his agreement, the wages for that work shall not be given to him, even (if it be only) slightly incomplete.

verses.text:
एष धर्मो ऽखिलेन-उक्तो वेतनादानकर्मणः ।
अत ऊर्ध्वं प्रवक्ष्यामि धर्मं समयभेदिनाम् ॥ २१८ ॥
verses.english: Thus the law for the non-payment of wages has been completely stated; I will next explain the law concerning men who break an agreement.

verses.text:
यो ग्राम.देश.सङ्घानां कृत्वा सत्येन संविदम् ।
विसंवदेन् नरो लोभात् तं राष्ट्राद् विप्रवासयेत् ॥ २१९
                                ॥
verses.english: If a man belonging to a corporation inhabiting a village or a district, after swearing to an agreement, breaks it through avarice, (the king) shall banish him from his realm,

verses.text:
निगृह्य दापयेच् च-एनं समयव्यभिचारिणम् ।
चतुःसुवर्णान् षण्निष्कांश्-शतमानं च राजकम् ॥ २२० ॥
verses.english: And having imprisoned such a breaker of an agreement, he shall compel him to pay six nishkas, (each of) four suvarnas, and one satamana of silver.

verses.text:
एतद् दण्डविधिं कुर्याद् धार्मिकः पृथिवीपतिः ।
ग्राम.जाति.समूहेषु समयव्यभिचारिणाम् ॥ २२१ ॥
verses.english: A righteous king shall apply this law of fines in villages and castes (gati) to those who break an agreement.

verses.text:
क्रीत्वा विक्रीय वा किं चिद् यस्य-इहानुशयो भवेत् ।
सो ऽन्तर् दशाहात् तद् द्रव्यं दद्याच् च-एवाददीत वा ॥ २२२
                                ॥
verses.english: If anybody in this (world), after buying or selling anything, repent (of his bargain), he may return or take (back) that chattel within ten days.

verses.text:
परेण तु दशाहस्य न दद्यान् नापि दापयेत् ।
आददानो ददत् च-एव राज्ञा दण्ड्यौ शतानि षट् ॥ २२३ ॥
verses.english: But after (the lapse of) ten days he may neither give nor cause it to be given (back); both he who takes it (back) and he who gives it (back, except by consent) shall be fined by the king six hundred (panas).

verses.text:
यस् तु दोषवतीं कन्याम् अनाख्याय प्रयच्छति ।
तस्य कुर्यान् नृपो दण्डं स्वयं षण्णवतिं पणान् ॥ २२४
                                ॥
verses.english: But the king himself shall impose a fine of ninety-six panas on him who gives a blemished damsel (to a suitor) without informing (him of the blemish).

verses.text:
अकन्या-इति तु यः कन्यां ब्रूयाद् द्वेषेण मानवः ।
स शतं प्राप्नुयाद् दण्डं तस्या दोषम् अदर्शयन् ॥ २२५
                                ॥
verses.english: But that man who, out of malice, says of a maiden, 'She is not a maiden,' shall be fined one hundred (panas), if he cannot prove her blemish.

verses.text:
पाणिग्रहणिका मन्त्राः कन्यास्व् एव प्रतिष्ठिताः ।
न-अकन्यासु क्व चिन् नॄणां लुप्त.धर्मक्रिया हि ताः ॥ २२६
                                ॥
verses.english: The nuptial texts are applied solely to virgins, (and) nowhere among men to females who have lost their virginity, for such (females) are excluded from religious ceremonies.

verses.text:
पाणिग्रहणिका मन्त्रा नियतं दारलक्षणम् ।
तेषां निष्ठा तु विज्ञेया विद्वद्भिः सप्तमे पदे ॥ २२७
                                ॥
verses.english: The nuptial texts are a certain proof (that a maiden has been made a lawful) wife; but the learned should know that they (and the marriage ceremony are complete with the seventh step (of the bride around the sacred fire).

verses.text:
यस्मिन् यस्मिन् कृते कार्ये यस्य-इहानुशयो भवेत् ।
तम् अनेन विधानेन धर्म्ये पथि निवेशयेत् ॥ २२८ ॥
verses.english: If anybody in this (world) repent of any completed transaction, (the king) shall keep him on the road of rectitude in accordance with the rules given above.

verses.text:
पशुषु स्वामिनां च-एव पालानां च व्यतिक्रमे ।
विवादं सम्प्रवक्ष्यामि यथावद् धर्मतत्त्वतः ॥ २२९
                                ॥
verses.english: I will fully declare in accordance with the true law (the rules concerning) the disputes, (arising) from the transgressions of owners of cattle and of herdsmen.

verses.text:
दिवा वक्तव्यता पाले रात्रौ स्वामिनि तद्गृहे ।
योगक्षेमे ऽन्यथा चेत् तु पालो वक्तव्यताम् इयात् ॥ २३०
                                    ॥
verses.english: During the day the responsibility for the safety (of the cattle rests) on the herdsman, during the night on the owner, (provided they are) in his house; (if it be) otherwise, the herdsman will be responsible (for them also during the night).

verses.text:
गोपः क्षीरभृतो यस् तु स दुह्याद् दशतो वराम् ।
गोस्वाम्यनुमते भृत्यः सा स्यात् पाले ऽभृते भृतिः ॥ २३१
                                    ॥
verses.english: A hired herdsman who is paid with milk, may milk with the consent of the owner the best (cow) out of ten; such shall be his hire if no (other) wages (are paid).

verses.text:
नष्टं विनष्टं कृमिभिः श्वहतं विषमे मृतम् ।
हीनं पुरुषकारेण प्रदद्यात् पाल एव तु ॥ २३२ ॥
verses.english: The herdsman alone shall make good (the loss of a beast) strayed, destroyed by worms, killed by dogs or (by falling) into a pit, if he did not duly exert himself (to prevent it).

verses.text:
विघुष्य तु हृतं चौरैर् न पालो दातुम् अर्हति ।
यदि देशे च काले च स्वामिनः स्वस्य शंसति ॥ २३३
                                    ॥
verses.english: But for (an animal) stolen by thieves, though he raised an alarm, the herdsman shall not pay, provided he gives notice to his master at the proper place and time.

verses.text:
कर्णौ चर्म च वालांश् च बस्तिं स्नायुं च रोचनाम् ।
पशुषु स्वामिनां दद्यान् मृतेष्व् अङ्कानि दर्शयेत् ॥ २३४ ॥
                                        ८.२३४च्व्/
                                        म्: अङ्कांश् च दर्शयेत् ॥ 8.234 ॥
verses.english: If cattle die, let him carry to his master their ears, skin, tails, bladders, tendons, and the yellow concrete bile, and let him point out their particular. marks.

verses.text:
अज.अविके तु संरुद्धे वृकैः पाले त्व् अन्.आयति ।
यां प्रसह्य वृको हन्यात् पाले तत् किल्बिषं भवेत् ॥ २३५
                                    ॥
verses.english: But if goats or sheep are surrounded by wolves and the herdsman does not hasten (to their assistance), lie shall be responsible for any (animal) which a wolf may attack and kill.

verses.text:
तासां चेद् अवरुद्धानां चरन्तीनां मिथो वने ।
याम् उत्प्लुत्य वृको हन्यान् न पालस् तत्र किल्बिषी ॥ २३६
                                    ॥
verses.english: But if they, kept in (proper) order, graze together in the forest, and a wolf, suddenly jumping on one of them, kills it, the herdsman shall bear in that case no responsibility.

verses.text:
धनुःशतं परीहारो ग्रामस्य स्यात् समन्ततः ।
शम्यापातास् त्रयो वा-अपि त्रिगुणो नगरस्य तु ॥ २३७
                                    ॥
verses.english: On all sides of a village a space, one hundred dhanus or three samya-throws (in breadth), shall be reserved (for pasture), and thrice (that space) round a town.

verses.text:
तत्र-अपरिवृतं धान्यं विहिंस्युः पशवो यदि ।
न तत्र प्रणयेद् दण्डं नृपतिः पशुरक्षिणाम् ॥ २३८
                                    ॥
verses.english: If the cattle do damage to unfenced crops on that (common), the king shall in that case not punish the herdsmen.

verses.text:
वृतिं तत्र प्रकुर्वीत याम् उष्त्रो न विलोकयेत् ।
छिद्रं च वारयेत् सर्वं श्व.सूकरमुखानुगम् ॥ २३९
                                    ॥
verses.english: (The owner of the field) shall make there a hedge over which a camel cannot look, and stop every gap through which a dog or a boar can thrust his head.

verses.text:
पथि क्षेत्रे परिवृते ग्रामान्तीये ऽथ वा पुनः ।
स.पालः शतदण्ड.अर्हो विपालान् वारयेत् पशून् ॥ २४०
                                    ॥
verses.english: (If cattle do mischief) in an enclosed field near a highway or near a village, the herdsman shall be fined one hundred (panas);

verses.text:
क्षेत्रेष्व् अन्येषु तु पशुः स.पादं पणम् अर्हति ।
सर्वत्र तु सदो देयः क्षेत्रिकस्य-इति धारणा ॥ २४१
                                    ॥
verses.english: (For damage) in other fields (each head of) cattle shall (pay a fine of one (pana) and a quarter, and in all (cases the value of) the crop (destroyed) shall be made good to the owner of the field; that is the settled rule.

verses.text:
अ.निर्दशाहां गां सूतां वृषान् देवपशूंस् तथा ।
स.पालान् वा वि.पालान् वा न दण्ड्यान् मनुर् अब्रवीत् ॥ २४२
                                    ॥
verses.english: But Manu has declared that no fine shall be paid for (damage done by) a cow within ten days after her calving, by bulls and by cattle sacred to the gods, whether they are attended by a herdsman or not.

verses.text:
क्षेत्रियस्य-अत्यये दण्डो भागाद् दशगुणो भवेत् । ८.२४३अव्/ म्: 
                                        क्षेत्रिकस्य-अत्यये
ततो ऽर्धदण्डो भृत्यानाम् अज्ञानात् क्षेत्रिकस्य तु ॥ २४३
                                    ॥
verses.english: If (the crops are destroyed by) the husbandman's (own) fault, the fine shall amount to ten times as much as (the king's) share; but the fine (shall be) only half that amount if (the fault lay) with the servants and the farmer had no knowledge of it.

verses.text:
एतद् विधानम् आतिष्ठेद् धार्मिकः पृथिवीपतिः ।
स्वामिनां च पशूनां च पालानां च व्यतिक्रमे ॥ २४४
                                    ॥
verses.english: To these rules a righteous king shall keep in (all cases of) transgressions by masters, their cattle, and herdsmen.

verses.text:
सीमां प्रति समुत्पन्ने विवादे ग्रामयोर् द्वयोः ।
ज्येष्ठे मासि नयेत् सीमां सु.प्रकाशेषु सेतुषु ॥ २४५ ॥
verses.english: If a dispute has arisen between two villages concerning a boundary, the king shall settle the limits in the month of Gyaishtha, when the landmarks are most distinctly visible.

verses.text:
सींआवृक्षांश् च कुर्वीत न्यग्रोध.अश्वत्थ.किंशुकान् ।
शाल्मलीन् सालतालांश् च क्षीरिणश् च-एव पादपान् ॥ २४६
                                    ॥
verses.english: Let him mark the boundaries (by) trees, (e.g.) Nyagrodhas, Asvatthas, Kimsukas, cotton-trees, Salas, Palmyra palms, and trees with milky juice,

verses.text:
गुल्मान् वेणूंश् च विविधान् शमी.वल्ली.स्थलानि च ।
शरान् कुब्जकगुल्मांश् च तथा सीमा न नश्यति ॥ २४७
                                    ॥
verses.english: By clustering shrubs, bamboos of different kinds, Samis, creepers and raised mounds, reeds, thickets of Kubgaka; thus the boundary will not be forgotten.

verses.text:
[म्२५०अ] तडागान्य् उदपानानि वाप्यः प्रस्रवणानि च ।
[म्२५०च्] सीमासन्धिषु कार्याणि देवतायतनानि च ॥ २४८
                                    ॥
verses.english: Tanks, wells, cisterns, and fountains should be built where boundaries meet, as well as temples,

verses.text:
उपछन्नानि चान्यानि सीमालिङ्गानि कारयेत् ।
सीमाज्ञाने नृणां वीक्ष्य नित्यं लोके विपर्ययम् ॥ २४९
                                    ॥
verses.english: And as he will see that through men's ignorance of the boundaries trespasses constantly occur in the world, let him cause to be made other hidden marks for boundaries,

verses.text:
[म्२४८अ] अश्मनो ऽस्थीनि गोवालांस् तुषान् भस्म कपालिकाः
                                    ।
[म्२४८च्] करीषम् इष्टका.अङ्गारांश्-शर्करा वालुकास् तथा ॥
                                    २५० ॥
verses.english: Stones, bones, cow's hair, chaff, ashes, potsherds, dry cowdung, bricks, cinders, pebbles, and sand,

verses.text:
यानि च-एवम्प्रकाराणि कालाद् भूमिर् न भक्षयेत् ।
तानि सन्धिषु सीमायाम् अ.प्रकाशानि कारयेत् ॥ २५१ ॥
                                        ८.२५१च्व्/
                                        म्: सीमाया ॥ 8.251 ॥
verses.english: And whatever other things of a similar kind the earth does not corrode even after a long time, those he should cause to be buried where one boundary joins (the other).

verses.text:
एतैर् लिङ्गैर् नयेत् सीमां राजा विवदमानयोः ।
पूर्वभुक्त्या च सततम् उदकस्य-आगमेन च ॥ २५२
                                    ॥
verses.english: By these signs, by long continued possession, and by constantly flowing streams of water the king shall ascertain the boundary (of the land) of two disputing parties.

verses.text:
यदि स्ंशय एव स्यात्-लिङ्गानाम् अपि दर्शने ।
साक्षिप्रत्यय एव स्यात् सीमावादविनिर्णयः ॥ २५३ ॥
                                        ८.२५३च्व्/
                                        म्: सीमावादविनिश्चयः ॥ 8.253 ॥
verses.english: If there be a doubt even on inspection of the marks, the settlement of a dispute regarding boundaries shall depend on witnesses.

verses.text:
ग्रामीयक.कुलानां च समक्षं सीम्नि साक्षिणः । ८.२५४अव्/ म्: 
                                        ग्रामेयक.
प्रष्टव्याः सीमलिङ्गानि तयोश् च-एव विवादिनोः ॥ २५४ ॥
                                        ८.२५४च्व्/
                                        म्: सीमालिङ्गानि ॥ 8.254 ॥
verses.english: The witnesses, (giving evidence) regarding a boundary, shall be examined concerning the landmarks in the presence of the crowd of the villagers and also of the two litigants.

verses.text:
ते पृष्तास् तु यथा ब्रूयुः समस्ताः सीम्नि निश्चयम् ।
निबध्नीयात् तथा सीमां सर्वांस् तांश् च-एव नामतः ॥
                                    २५५ ॥
verses.english: As they, being questioned, unanimously decide, even so he shall record the boundary (in writing), together with their names.

verses.text:
शिरोभिस् ते गृहीत्वा-उर्वीं स्रग्विणो रक्त.वाससः ।
सुकृतैः शापिथाः स्वैः स्वैर् नयेयुस् ते समञ्जसम् ॥
                                    २५६ ॥
verses.english: Let them, putting earth on their heads, wearing chaplets (of red flowers) and red dresses, being sworn each by (the rewards for) his meritorious deeds, settle (the boundary) in accordance with the truth.

verses.text:
यथा.उक्तेन नयन्तस् ते पूयन्ते सत्यसाक्षिणः ।
विपरीतं नयन्तस् तु दाप्याः स्युर् द्विशतं दमम् ॥ २५७
                                    ॥
verses.english: If they determine (the boundary) in the manner stated, they are guiltless (being) veracious witnesses; but if they determine it unjustly, they shall be compelled to pay a fine of two hundred (panas).

verses.text:
साक्ष्यभावे तु चत्वारो ग्रामाः सामन्तवासिनः । ८.२५८अव्/ म्: 
                                        ग्रामसीमान्तवासिनः
सीमाविनिर्णयं कुर्युः प्रयता राजसन्निधौ ॥ २५८
                                    ॥
verses.english: On failure of witnesses (from the two villages, men of) the four neighbouring villages, who are pure, shall make (as witnesses) a decision concerning the boundary in the presence of the king.

verses.text:
सामन्तानाम् अभावे तु मौलानां सीम्नि साक्षिणाम् ।
इमान् अप्य् अनुयुञ्जीत पुरुषान् वन.गोचरान् ॥ २५९ ॥
verses.english: On failure of neighbours (who are) original inhabitants (of the country and can be) witnesses with respect to the boundary, (the king) may hear the evidence even of the following inhabitants of the forest.

verses.text:
व्याधान्-शाकुनिकान् गोपान् कैवर्तान् मूलखानकान् ।
व्यालग्राहान् उञ्छवृत्तीन् अन्यांश् च वनचारिणः ॥ २६०
                                    ॥
verses.english: (Viz.) hunters, fowlers, herdsmen, fishermen, root-diggers, snake-catchers, gleaners, and other foresters.

verses.text:
ते पृष्टास् तु यथा ब्रूयुः सीमासन्धिषु लक्षणम् ।
तत् तथा स्थापयेद् राजा धर्मेण ग्रामयोर् द्वयोः ॥ २६१
                                    ॥
verses.english: As they, being examined, declare the marks for the meeting of the boundaries (to be), even so the king shall justly cause them to be fixed between the two villages.

verses.text:
क्षेत्र.कूप.तडागानाम् आरामस्य गृहस्य च ।
सामन्तप्रत्ययो ज्ञेयः सीमासेतुविनिर्णयः ॥ २६२ ॥
verses.english: The decision concerning the boundary-marks of fields, wells, tanks, of gardens and houses depends upon (the evidence of) the neighbours.

verses.text:
सामन्ताश् चेत्-मृषा ब्रूयुः सेतौ विवादतां नृणाम् ।
सर्वे पृथक् पृथग् दण्ड्या राज्ञा मध्यमसाहसम् ॥ २६३
                                    ॥
verses.english: Should the neighbours give false evidence, when men dispute about a boundary-mark, the king shall make each of them pay the middlemost amercement as a fine.

verses.text:
गृहं तडागम् आरामं क्षेत्रं वा भीषया हरन् ।
शतानि पञ्च दण्ड्यः स्याद् अज्ञानाद् द्विशतो दमः ॥ २६४
                                    ॥
verses.english: He who by intimidation possesses himself of a house, a tank, a garden, or a field, shall be fined five hundred (panas); (if he trespassed) through ignorance, the fine (shall be) two hundred (panas).

verses.text:
सीमायाम् अ.विषह्यायां स्वयं राजा-एव धर्मवित् ।
प्रदिशेद् भूमिम् एकेषाम् उपकाराद् इति स्थितिः ॥ २६५
                                    ॥
verses.english: If the boundary cannot be ascertained (by any evidence), let a righteous king with (the intention of) benefiting them (all), himself assign (his) land (to each); that is the settled rule.

verses.text:
एषो ऽखिलेन-अभिहितो धर्मः सीमाविनिर्णये ।
अत ऊर्ध्वं प्रवक्ष्यामि वाक्पारुष्यविनिर्णयम् ॥ २६६
                                    ॥
verses.english: Thus the law for deciding boundary (disputes) has been fully declared, I will next propound the (manner of) deciding (cases of) defamation.

verses.text:
शतं ब्राह्मणम् आक्रुश्य क्षत्रियो दण्डम् अर्हति ।
वैश्यो ऽप्य् अर्धशतं द्वे वा शूद्रस् तु वधम् अर्हति ॥ २६७
                                ॥
verses.english: A Kshatriya, having defamed a Brahmana, shall be fined one hundred (panas); a Vaisya one hundred and fifty or two hundred; a Sudra shall suffer corporal punishment.

verses.text:
पञ्चाशद् ब्राह्मणो दण्ड्यः क्षत्रियस्य-अभिशंसने ।
वैश्ये स्याद् अर्धपञ्चाशत्-शूद्रे द्वादशको दमः ॥ २६८
                                ॥
verses.english: A Brahmana shall be fined fifty (panas) for defaming a Kshatriya; in (the case of) a Vaisya the fine shall be twenty-five (panas); in (the case of) a Sudra twelve.

verses.text:
समवर्णे द्विजातीनां द्वादश-एव व्यतिक्रमे ।
वादेष्व् अ.वचनीयेषु तद् एव द्विगुणं भवेत् ॥ २६९ ॥
verses.english: For offences of twice-born men against those of equal caste (varna, the fine shall be) also twelve (panas); for speeches which ought not to be uttered, that (and every fine shall be) double.

verses.text:
एकजातिर् द्विजातींस् तु वाचा दारुणया क्षिपन् ।
जिह्वायाः प्राप्नुयाच् छेदं जघन्य.प्रभवो हि सः ॥ २७०
                                ॥
verses.english: A once-born man (a Sudra), who insults a twice-born man with gross invective, shall have his tongue cut out; for he is of low origin.

verses.text:
नाम.जातिग्रहं त्व् एषाम् अभिद्रोहेण कुर्वतः ।
निक्षेप्यो ऽयोमयः शङ्कुर् ज्वलन्न् आस्ये दशाङ्गुलः ॥ २७१
                                ॥
verses.english: If he mentions the names and castes (gati) of the (twice-born) with contumely, an iron nail, ten fingers long, shall be thrust red-hot into his mouth.

verses.text:
धर्म.उपदेशं दर्पेण विप्राणाम् अस्य कुर्वतः ।
तप्तम् आसेचयेत् तैलं वक्त्रे श्रोत्रे च पार्थिवः ॥ २७२ ॥
                                    ८.२७२च्व्/ म्: 
                                    श्रौत्रे ॥ 8.272 ॥
verses.english: If he arrogantly teaches Brahmanas their duty, the king shall cause hot oil to be poured into his mouth and into his ears.

verses.text:
श्रुतं देशं च जातिं च कर्म शरीरम् एव च ।
वितथेन ब्रुवन् दर्पाद् दाप्यः स्याद् द्विशतं दमम् ॥ २७३
                                ॥
verses.english: He who through arrogance makes false statements regarding the learning (of a caste-fellow), his country, his caste (gati), or the rites by which his body was sanctified, shall be compelled to pay a fine of two hundred (panas).

verses.text:
काणं वा-अप्य् अथ वा खञ्जम् अन्यं वा-अपि तथाविधम् ।
तथ्येन-अपि ब्रुवन् दाप्यो दण्डं कार्षापण.अवरम् ॥ २७४
                                ॥
verses.english: He who even in accordance with the true facts (contemptuously) calls another man one-eyed, lame, or the like (names), shall be fined at least one karshapana.

verses.text:
मातरं पितरं जायां भ्रातरं तनयं गुरुम् ।
आक्षारयन्-शतं दाप्यः पन्थानं च-अददद् गुरोः ॥ २७५
                                ॥
verses.english: He who defames his mother, his father, his wife, his brother, his son, or his teacher, and he who gives not the way to his preceptor, shall be compelled to pay one hundred (panas).

verses.text:
ब्राह्मण.क्षत्रियाभ्यां तु दण्डः कार्यो विजानता ।
ब्राह्मणे साहसः पूर्वः क्षत्रिये त्व् एव मध्यमः ॥ २७६
                                ॥
verses.english: (For mutual abuse) by a Brahmana and a Kshatriya a fine must be imposed by a discerning (king), on the Brahmana the lowest amercement, but on the Kshatriya the middlemost.

verses.text:
विश्.शूद्रयोर् एवम् एव स्वजातिं प्रति तत्त्वतः ।
छेद.वर्जं प्रणयनं दण्डस्य-इति विनिश्चयः ॥ २७७
                                ॥
verses.english: A Vaisya and a Sudra must be punished exactly in the same manner according to their respective castes, but the tongue (of the Sudra) shall not be cut out; that is the decision.

verses.text:
एष दण्डविधिः प्रोक्तो वाक्पारुष्यस्य तत्त्वतः ।
अत ऊर्ध्वं प्रवक्ष्यामि दण्डपारुष्यनिर्णयम् ॥ २७८ ॥
verses.english: Thus the rules for punishments (applicable to cases) of defamation have been truly declared; I will next propound the decision (of cases) of assault.

verses.text:
येन केन चिद् अङ्गेन हिंस्याच् चेत्-श्रेष्ठम् अन्त्यजः ।
छेत्तव्यं तद् तद् एव-अस्य तन् मनोर् अनुशासनम् ॥ २७९
                                    ॥
verses.english: With whatever limb a man of a low caste does hurt to (a man of the three) highest (castes), even that limb shall be cut off; that is the teaching of Manu.

verses.text:
पाणिम् उद्यम्य दण्डं वा पाणिच्छेदनम् अर्हति ।
पादेन प्रहरन् कोपात् पादच्छेदनम् अर्हति ॥ २८० ॥
verses.english: He who raises his hand or a stick, shall have his hand cut off; he who in anger kicks with his foot, shall have his foot cut off.

verses.text:
सहासनम् अभिप्रेप्सुर् उत्कृष्टस्य-अपकृष्टजः ।
कट्यां कृत.अङ्को निर्वास्यः स्फिचं वा-अस्य-अवकर्तयेत्
                                    ॥ २८१ ॥
verses.english: A low-caste man who tries to place himself on the same seat with a man of a high caste, shall be branded on his hip and be banished, or (the king) shall cause his buttock to be gashed.

verses.text:
अवनिष्ठीवतो दर्पाद् द्वाव् ओष्ठौ छेदयेन् नृपः ।
अवमूत्रयतो मेढ्रम् अवशर्धयतो गुदम् ॥ २८२ ॥
verses.english: If out of arrogance he spits (on a superior), the king shall cause both his lips to be cut off; if he urines (on him), the penis; if he breaks wind (against him), the anus.

verses.text:
केशेषु गृह्णतो हस्तौ छेदयेद् अविचारयन् ।
पादयोर् दाढिकायां च ग्रीवायां वृषणेषु च ॥ २८३ ॥
verses.english: If he lays hold of the hair (of a superior), let the (king) unhesitatingly cut off his hands, likewise (if he takes him) by the feet, the beard, the neck, or the scrotum.

verses.text:
त्वग्भेदकः शतं दण्ड्यो लोहितस्य च दर्शकः ।
मांसभेत्ता तु षट्.निष्कान् प्रवास्यस् त्व् अस्थिभेदकः ॥
                                    २८४ ॥
verses.english: He who breaks the skin (of an equal) or fetches blood (from him) shall be fined one hundred (panas), he who cuts a muscle six nishkas, he who breaks a bone shall be banished.

verses.text:
वनस्पतीनां सर्वेषाम् उपभोगो यथा यथा ।
यथा तथा दमः कार्यो हिंसायाम् इति धारणा ॥ २८५
                                    ॥
verses.english: According to the usefulness of the several (kinds of) trees a fine must be inflicted for injuring them; that is the settled rule.

verses.text:
मनुष्याणां पशूनां च दुःखाय प्रहृते सति ।
यथा यथा महद् दुःखं दण्डं कुर्यात् तथा तथा ॥
                                    २८६ ॥
verses.english: If a blow is struck against men or animals in order to (give them) pain, (the judge) shall inflict a fine in proportion to the amount of pain (caused).

verses.text:
अङ्गावपीडनायां च व्रण.शोनितयोस् तथा । ८.२८७अव्/ म्: 
                                        प्राण.शोनितयोस्
समुत्थानव्ययं दाप्यः सर्वदण्डम् अथ-अपि वा ॥ २८७
                                    ॥
verses.english: If a limb is injured, a wound (is caused), or blood (flows, the assailant) shall be made to pay (to the sufferer) the expenses of the cure, or the whole (both the usual amercement and the expenses of the cure as a) fine (to the king).

verses.text:
द्रव्याणि हिंस्याद् यो यस्य ज्ञानतो ऽज्ञानतो ऽपि वा ।
स तस्य-उत्पादयेत् तुष्टिं राज्ञे दद्याच् च तत्समम् ॥
                                    २८८ ॥
verses.english: He who damages the goods of another, be it intentionally or unintentionally, shall give satisfaction to the (owner) and pay to the king a fine equal to the (damage).

verses.text:
चर्म.चार्मिकभाण्डेषु काष्ठ.लोष्टमयेषु ।
मूल्यात् पञ्चगुणो दण्डः पुष्प.मूल.फलेषु च ॥ २८९
                                    ॥
verses.english: In the case of (damage done to) leather, or to utensils of leather, of wood, or of clay, the fine (shall be) five times their value; likewise in the case of (damage to) flowers, roots, and fruit.

verses.text:
यानस्य च-एव यातुश् च यानस्वामिन एव च ।
दशातिवर्तनान्य् आहुः शेषे दण्डो विधीयते ॥ २९० ॥
verses.english: They declare with respect to a carriage, its driver and its owner, (that there are) ten cases in which no punishment (for damage done) can be inflicted; in other cases a fine is prescribed.

verses.text:
छिन्न.नास्ये भग्न.युगे तिर्यक्.प्रतिमुख.आगते ।
अक्ष.भङ्गे च यानस्य चक्र.भङ्गे तथा-एव च ॥ २९१
                                    ॥
verses.english: When the nose-string is snapped, when the yoke is broken, when the carriage turns sideways or back, when the axle or a wheel is broken,

verses.text:
छेदने च-एव यन्त्राणां योक्त्र.रश्म्योस् तथा-एव च
                                    ।
आक्रन्दे च-अप्य् अपैहि-इति न दण्डं मनुर् अब्रवीत् ॥ २९२
                                    ॥
verses.english: When the leather-thongs, the rope around the neck or the bridle are broken, and when (the driver) has loudly called out, 'Make way,' Manu has declared (that in all these cases) no punishment (shall be inflicted).

verses.text:
यत्र-अपवर्तते युग्यं वैगुण्यात् प्राजकस्य तु ।
तत्र स्वामी भवेद् दण्ड्यो हिंसायां द्विशतं दमम् ॥ २९३
                                    ॥
verses.english: But if the cart turns off (the road) through the driver's want of skill, the owner shall be fined, if damage (is done), two hundred (panas).

verses.text:
प्राजकश् चेद् भवेद् आप्तः प्राजको दण्डम् अर्हति ।
युग्यस्थाः प्राजके ऽनाप्ते सर्वे दण्ड्याः शतं शतम् ॥
                                    २९४ ॥
verses.english: If the driver is skilful (but negligent), he alone shall be fined; if the driver is unskilful, the occupants of the carriage (also) shall be each fined one hundred (panas).

verses.text:
स चेत् तु पथि संरुद्धः पशुभिर् वा रथेन वा ।
प्रमापयेत् प्राणभृतस् तत्र दण्डो ऽविचारितः ॥ २९५
                                    ॥
verses.english: But if he is stopped on his way by cattle or by (another) carriage, and he causes the death of any living being, a fine shall without doubt be imposed.

verses.text:
मनुष्यमारणे क्षिप्रं चौरवत् किल्बिषं भवेत् ।
प्राणभृत्सु महत्स्व् अर्धं गो.गज.उष्ट्र.हयादिषु ॥ २९६
                                    ॥
verses.english: If a man is killed, his guilt will be at once the same as (that of) a thief; for large animals such as cows, elephants, camels or horses, half of that.

verses.text:
क्षुद्रकाणां पशूनां तु हिंसायां द्विशतो दमः ।
पञ्चाशत् तु भवेद् दण्डः शुभेषु मृगपक्षिषु ॥ २९७
                                    ॥
verses.english: For injuring small cattle the fine (shall be) two hundred (panas); the fine for beautiful wild quadrupeds and birds shall amount to fifty (panas).

verses.text:
गर्धभ.अज.आविकानां तु दण्डः स्यात् पञ्चमाषिकः ।
                                        ८.२९८अव्/
                                        म्: पाञ्चमाषिकः
माषिकस् तु भवेद् दण्डः श्व.सूकरनिपातने ॥ २९८
                                    ॥
verses.english: For donkeys, sheep, and goats the fine shall be five mashas; but the punishment for killing a dog or a pig shall be one masha.

verses.text:
भार्या पुत्रश् च दासश् च प्रेष्यो भ्रात्रा च स.उदरः
                                    ।
प्राप्त.अपराधास् ताड्याः स्यू रज्ज्वा वेणुदलेन वा ॥ २९९
                                    ॥
verses.english: A wife, a son, a slave, a pupil, and a (younger) brother of the full blood, who have committed faults, may be beaten with a rope or a split bamboo,

verses.text:
पृष्ठतस् तु शरीरस्य न-उत्तमाङ्गे कथं चन ।
अतो ऽन्यथा तु प्रहरन् प्राप्तः स्याच् चौरकिल्बिषम् ॥
                                    ३०० ॥
verses.english: But on the back part of the body (only), never on a noble part; he who strikes them otherwise will incur the same guilt as a thief.

verses.text:
एषो ऽखिलेन-अभिहितो दण्डपारुष्यनिर्णयः ।
स्तेनस्य-अतः प्रवक्ष्यामि विधिं दण्डविनिर्णये ॥ ३०१
                                    ॥
verses.english: Thus the whole law of assault (and hurt) has been declared completely; I will now explain the rules for the decision (in cases) of theft.

verses.text:
परमं यत्नम् आतिष्ठेत् स्तेनानां निग्रहे नृपः ।
स्तेनानां निग्रहाद् अस्य यशो राष्ट्रं च वर्धते ॥ ३०२
                                    ॥
verses.english: Let the king exert himself to the utmost to punish thieves; for, if he punishes thieves, his fame grows and his kingdom prospers.

verses.text:
अभयस्य हि यो दाता स पूज्यः सततं नृपः ।
सत्त्रं हि वर्धते तस्य सदा-एव-अभय.दक्षिणम् ॥
                                    ३०३ ॥
verses.english: That king, indeed, is ever worthy of honour who ensures the safety (of his subjects); for the sacrificial session (sattra, which he, as it were, performs thereby) ever grows in length, the safety (of his subjects representing) the sacrificial fee.

verses.text:
सर्वतो धर्मषड्भागो राज्ञो भवति रक्षतः ।
अधर्माद् अपि षड्भागो भवत्य् अस्य ह्य् अ.रक्षतः ॥ ३०४
                                    ॥
verses.english: A king who (duly) protects (his subjects) receives from each and all the sixth part of their spiritual merit; if he does not protect them, the sixth part of their demerit also (will fall on him).

verses.text:
यद् अधीते यद् यजते यद् ददाति यद् अर्चति ।
तस्य षड्भागभाग् राजा सम्यग् भवति रक्षणात् ॥ ३०५
                                    ॥
verses.english: Whatever (merit a man gains by) reading the Veda, by sacrificing, by charitable gifts, (or by) worshipping (Gurus and gods), the king obtains a sixth part of that in consequence of his duly protecting (his kingdom).

verses.text:
रक्षन् धर्मेण भूतानि राजा वध्यांश् च घातयन् ।
यजते ऽहर् अहर् यज्ञैः सहस्रशत.दक्षिणैः ॥ ३०६
                                    ॥
verses.english: A king who protects the created beings in accordance with the sacred law and smites those worthy of corporal punishment, daily offers (as it were) sacrifices at which hundred thousands (are given as) fees.

verses.text:
यो ऽ.रक्षन् बलिम् आदत्ते करं शुल्कं च पार्थिवः ।
प्रतिभागं च दण्डं च स सद्यो नरकं व्रजेत् ॥ ३०७
                                    ॥
verses.english: A king who does not afford protection, (yet) takes his share in kind, his taxes, tolls and duties, daily presents and fines, will (after death) soon sink into hell.

verses.text:
अरक्षितारम् राजानं बलिषड्भाग.हारिणम् । ८.३०८अव्/ क्:
                                        अरक्षितारं अत्तारं
तम् आहुः सर्वलोकस्य समग्रमल.हारकम् ॥ ३०८ ॥
verses.english: They declare that a king who affords no protection, (yet) receives the sixth part of the produce, takes upon himself all the foulness of his whole people.

verses.text:
अनपेक्षित.मर्यादं नास्तिकं विप्रलुम्पकम् । ८.३०९अव्/ म्: 
                                        अनवेक्षित.मर्यादं
अरक्षितारम् अत्तारं नृपं विद्याद् अधो.गतिम् ॥ ३०९
                                    ॥
verses.english: Know that a king who heeds not the rules (of the law), who is an atheist, and rapacious, who does not protect (his subjects, but) devours them, will sink low (after death).

verses.text:
अधार्मिकं त्रिभिर् न्यायैर् निगृह्णीयात् प्रयत्नतः ।
निरोधनेन बन्धेन विविधेन वधेन च ॥ ३१० ॥
verses.english: Let him carefully restrain the wicked by three methods,- by imprisonment by putting them in fetters, and by various (kinds of) corporal punishments.

verses.text:
निग्रहेण हि पापानां साधूनां सङ्ग्रहेण च ।
द्विजातय इव-इज्याभिः पूयन्ते सततं नृपाः ॥ ३११
                                    ॥
verses.english: For by punishing the wicked and by favouring the virtuous, kings are constantly sanctified, just as twice-born men by sacrifices.

verses.text:
क्षन्तव्यं प्रभुणा नित्यं क्षिपतां कार्यिणां नृणाम् ।
बाल.वृद्ध.आतुराणां च कुर्वता हितम् आत्मनः ॥ ३१२
                                    ॥
verses.english: A king who desires his own welfare must always forgive litigants, infants, aged and sick men, who inveigh against him.

verses.text:
यः क्षिप्तो मर्षयत्य् आर्तैस् तेन स्वर्गे महीयते ।
यस् त्व् ऐश्वर्यान् न क्षमते नरकं तेन गच्छति ॥ ३१३
                                    ॥
verses.english: He who, being abused by men in pain, pardons (them), will in reward of that (act) be exalted in heaven; but he who, (proud) of his kingly state, forgives them not, will for that (reason) sink into hell.

verses.text:
राजा स्तेनेन गन्तव्यो मुक्त.केशेन धावता । ८.३१४अव्/ म्: 
                                        धीमता
आचक्षाणेन तत् स्तेयम् एवङ्कर्मा-अस्मि शाधि माम् ॥ ३१४
                                    ॥
verses.english: A thief shall, running, approach the king, with flying hair, confessing that theft (and saying), 'Thus have I done, punish me;'

verses.text:
स्कन्धेन-आदाय मुसलं लगुडं वा-अपि खादिरम् । ८.३१५अव्/ म्: 
                                        मुशलं
शक्तिं च-उभयतस् तीक्ष्णाम् आयसं दण्डम् एव वा ॥ ३१५
                                    ॥
verses.english: (And he must) carry on his shoulder a pestle, or a club of Khadira wood, or a spear sharp at both ends, or an iron staff.

verses.text:
शासनाद् वा विमोक्षाद् वा स्तेनः स्तेयाद् विमुच्यते ।
अ.शासित्वा तु तं राजा स्तेनस्य-आप्नोति किल्बिषम् ॥ ३१६
                                    ॥
verses.english: Whether he be punished or pardoned, the thief is freed from the (guilt of) theft; but the king, if he punishes not, takes upon himself the guilt of the thief.

verses.text:
अन्नादे भ्रूणहा मार्ष्टि पत्यौ भार्या-अपचारिणी ।
गुरौ शिष्यश् च याज्यश् च स्तेनो राजनि किल्बिषम् ॥ ३१७
                                    ॥
verses.english: The killer of a learned Brahmana throws his guilt on him who eats his food, an adulterous wife on her (negligent) husband, a (sinning) pupil or sacrificer on (their negligent) teacher (or priest), a thief on the king (who pardons him).

verses.text:
राजभिः कृतदण्डास् तु कृत्वा पापानि मानवाः । ८.३१८अव्/ म्: 
                                        राजभिर् धृतदण्डास् तु
निर्.मलाः स्वर्गम् आयान्ति सन्तः सुकृतिनो यथा ॥ ३१८
                                    ॥
verses.english: But men who have committed crimes and have been punished by the king, go to heaven, being pure like those who performed meritorious deeds.

verses.text:
यस् तु रज्जुं घटं कूपाद्द् हरेद् भिन्द्याच् च यः प्रपाम्
                                    ।
स दण्डं प्राप्नुयान् माषं तच् च तस्मिन् समाहरेत् ॥ ३१९
                                    ॥
verses.english: He who steals the rope or the water-pot from a well, or damages a hut where water is distributed, shall pay one masha as a fine and restore the (article abstracted or damaged) in its (proper place).

verses.text:
धान्यं दशभ्यः कुम्भेभ्यो हरतो ऽभ्यधिकं वधः
                                    ।
शेषे ऽप्य् एकादशगुणं दाप्यस् तस्य च तद् धनम् ॥ ३२०
                                    ॥
verses.english: On him who steals more than ten kumbhas of grain corporal punishment (shall be inflicted); in other cases he shall be fined eleven times as much, and shall pay to the (owner the value of his) property.

verses.text:
तथा धरिममेयानां शताद् अभ्यधिके वधः ।
सुवर्ण.रजतादीनाम् उत्तमानां च वाससाम् ॥ ३२१ ॥
verses.english: So shall corporal punishment be inflicted for stealing more than a hundred (palas) of articles sold by the weight, (i.e.) of gold, silver, and so forth, and of most excellent clothes.

verses.text:
पञ्चाशतस् त्व् अभ्यधिके हस्तच्छेदनम् इष्यते ।
शेषे त्व् एकादशगुणं मूल्याद् दण्डं प्रकल्पयेत् ॥ ३२२
                                    ॥
verses.english: For (stealing) more than fifty (palas) it is enacted that the hands (of the offender) shall be cut off; but in other cases, let him inflict a fine of eleven times the value.

verses.text:
पुरुषाणां कुलीनानां नारीणां च विशेषतः ।
मुख्यानां च-एव रत्नानां हरणे वधम् अर्हति ॥ ३२३
                                    ॥
verses.english: For stealing men of noble family and especially women and the most precious gems, (the offender) deserves corporal (or capital) punishment.

verses.text:
महापशूनां हरणे शस्त्राणाम् औषधस्य च ।
कालम् आसाद्य कार्यं च दण्डं राजा प्रकल्पयेत् ॥ ३२४
                                    ॥
verses.english: For stealing large animals, weapons, or medicines, let the king fix a punishment, after considering the time and the purpose (for which they were destined).

verses.text:
गोषु ब्राह्मणसंस्थासु छुरिकायाश् च भेदने । ८.३२५अव्/ म्: 
                                        खरिकायाश् च
पशूनां हरणे च-एव सद्यः कार्यो ऽर्धपादिकः ॥ ३२५
                                    ॥
verses.english: For (stealing) cows belonging to Brahmanas, piercing (the nostrils of) a barren cow, and for stealing (other) cattle (belonging to Brahmanas, the offender) shall forthwith lose half his feet.

verses.text:
सूत्र.कार्पास.किण्वानां गोमयस्य गुडस्य च ।
दध्नः क्षीरस्य तक्रस्य पानीयस्य तृणस्य च ॥ ३२६
                                    ॥
verses.english: (For stealing) thread, cotton, drugs causing fermentation, cowdung, molasses, sour milk, sweet milk, butter-milk, water, or grass,

verses.text:
वेणुवैदलभाण्डानां लवणानां तथा-एव च ।
मृण्मयानां च हरणे मृदो भस्मन एव च ॥ ३२७ ॥
verses.english: Vessels made of bamboo or other cane, salt of various kinds, earthen (vessels), earth and ashes,

verses.text:
मत्स्यानां पक्षिणां च-एव तैलस्य च घृतस्य च ।
मांसस्य मधुनश् च-एव यच् च-अन्यत् पशु.सम्भवम् ॥
                                    ३२८ ॥
verses.english: Fish, birds, oil, clarified butter, meat, honey, and other things that come from beasts,

verses.text:
अन्येषां च-एवम्.आदीनां मद्यानाम् ओदनस्य च । ८.३२९अव्/ म्: 
                                        च-एवमादीनाम् अद्यानाम्
पक्वान्नानां च सर्वेषां तन्मुल्याद् द्विगुणो दमः ॥ ३२९
                                    ॥
verses.english: Or other things of a similar kind, spirituous liquor, boiled rice, and every kind of cooked food, the fine (shall be) twice the value (of the stolen article).

verses.text:
पुष्पेषु हरिते धान्ये गुल्म.वल्ली.नगेषु च ।
अन्येष्व् अ.परिपूतेषु दण्डः स्यात् पञ्चकृष्णलः ॥ ३३०
                                    ॥
verses.english: For flowers, green corn, shrubs, creepers, trees, and other unhusked (grain) the fine (shall be) five krishnalas.

verses.text:
परिपूतेषु धान्येषु शाक.मूल.फलेषु च ।
निरन्वये शतं दण्डः सान्वये ऽर्धशतं दमः ॥ ३३१
                                    ॥
verses.english: For husked grain, vegetables, roots, and fruit the fine (shall be) one hundred (panas) if there is no connexion (between the owner and the thief), fifty (panas) if such a connexion exists.

verses.text:
स्यात् साहसं त्व् अन्वयवत् प्रसभं कर्म यत् कृतम्
                                    ।
निरन्वयं भवेत् स्तेयं हृत्वा-अपव्ययते च यत् ॥ ३३२
                                    ॥
verses.english: An offence (of this description), which is committed in the presence (of the owner) and with violence, will be robbery; if (it is committed) in his absence, it will be theft; likewise if (the possession of) anything is denied after it has been taken.

verses.text:
यस् त्व् एतान्य् उपकॢप्तानि द्रव्याणि स्तेनयेन् नरः ।
तम् आद्यं दण्डयेद् राजा यश् चाग्निं चोरयेद् गृहात् ॥ ३३३
                                    ॥ ८.३३३च्व्/
                                        म्: तं शतं ॥ 8.333 ॥
verses.english: On that man who may steal (any of) the above-mentioned articles, when they are prepared for (use), let the king inflict the first (or lowest) amercement; likewise on him who may steal (a sacred) fire out of the room (in which it is kept).

verses.text:
येन येन यथाङ्गेन स्तेनो नृषु विचेष्टते ।
तत् तद् एव हरेत् तस्य प्रत्यादेशाय पार्थिवः ॥ ३३४
                                    ॥
verses.english: With whatever limb a thief in any way commits (an offence) against men, even of that (the king) shall deprive him in order to prevent (a repetition of the crime).

verses.text:
पिता-आचार्यः सुहृत्-माता भार्या पुत्रः पुरोहितः ।
न-अदण्ड्यो नाम राज्ञो ऽस्ति यः स्वधर्मे न तिष्ठति ॥
                                    ३३५ ॥
verses.english: Neither a father, nor a teacher, nor a friend, nor a mother, nor a wife, nor a son, nor a domestic priest must be left unpunished by a king, if they do not keep within their duty.

verses.text:
कार्षापणं भवेद् दण्ड्यो यत्र-अन्यः प्राकृतो जनः ।
तत्र राजा भवेद् दण्ड्यः सहस्रम् इति धारणा ॥ ३३६
                                    ॥
verses.english: Where another common man would be fined one karshapana, the king shall be fined one thousand; that is the settled rule.

verses.text:
अष्टापाद्यं तु शूद्रस्य स्तेये भवति किल्बिषम् ।
षोडश-एव तु वैश्यस्य द्वात्रिंशत् क्षत्रियस्य च ॥ ३३७
                                    ॥
verses.english: In (a case of) theft the guilt of a Sudra shall be eightfold, that of a Vaisya sixteenfold, that of a Kshatriya two-and-thirtyfold,

verses.text:
ब्राह्मणस्य चतुःषष्टिः पूर्णं वा-अपि शतं भवेत् ।
द्विगुणा वा चतुःषष्टिस् तद्दोषगुणविद्द् हि सः ॥ ३३८
                                    ॥
verses.english: That of a Brahmana sixty-fourfold, or quite a hundredfold, or (even) twice four-and-sixtyfold; (each of them) knowing the nature of the offence.

verses.text:
वानस्पत्यं मूल.फलं दारु-अग्न्य्.अर्थं तथा-एव च
                                    ।
तृणं च गोभ्यो ग्रास.अर्थम् अस्तेयं मनुर् अब्रवीत् ॥
                                    ३३९ ॥
verses.english: (The taking of) roots and of fruit from trees, of wood for a (sacrificial) fire, and of grass for feeding cows, Manu has declared (to be) no theft.

verses.text:
यो ऽदत्तादायिनो हस्तात्-लिप्सेत ब्राह्मणो धनम् ।
याजन.अध्यापनेन-अपि यथा स्तेनस् तथा-एव सः ॥ ३४०
                                    ॥
verses.english: A Brahmana, seeking to obtain property from a man who took what was not given to him, either by sacrificing for him or by teaching him, is even like a thief.

verses.text:
द्विजो ऽध्वगः क्षीण.वृत्तिर् द्वाव् इक्षू द्वे च मूलके
                                    ।
आददानः परक्षेत्रात्-न दण्डं दातुम् अर्हति ॥ ३४१
                                    ॥
verses.english: A twice-born man, who is travelling and whose provisions are exhausted, shall not be fined, if he takes two stalks of sugar-cane or two (esculent) roots from the field of another man.

verses.text:
अ.सन्दितानां सन्दाता सन्दितानां च मोक्षकः ।
दास.अश्व.रथहर्ता च प्राप्तः स्याच् चोरकिल्बिषम् ॥ ३४२
                                    ॥
verses.english: He who ties up unbound or sets free tied up (cattle of other men), he who takes a slave, a horse, or a carriage will have incurred the guilt of a thief.

verses.text:
अनेन विधिना राजा कुर्वाणः स्तेननिग्रहम् ।
यशो ऽस्मिन् प्राप्नुयात्-लोके प्रेत्य च-अनुत्तमं सुखम् ॥
                                    ३४३ ॥
verses.english: A king who punishes thieves according to these rules, will gain fame in this world and after death unsurpassable bliss.

verses.text:
ऐन्द्रं स्थानम् अभिप्रेप्सुर् यशश् च-अक्षयम् अव्ययम् ।
न-उपेक्षेत क्षणम् अपि राजा साहसिकं नरम् ॥ ३४४ ॥
verses.english: A king who desires to gain the throne of Indra and imperishable eternal fame, shall not, even for a moment, neglect (to punish) the man who commits violence.

verses.text:
वाग्दुष्टात् तस्कराच् च-एव दण्डेन-एव च हिंसतः ।
साहसस्य नरः कर्ता विज्ञेयः पापकृत्तमः ॥ ३४५ ॥
verses.english: He who commits violence must be considered as the worst offender, (more wicked) than a defamer, than a thief, and than he who injures (another) with a staff.

verses.text:
साहसे वर्तमानं तु यो मर्षयति पार्थिवः ।
स विनाशं व्रजत्य् आशु विद्वेषं च-अधिगच्छति ॥ ३४६
                                ॥
verses.english: But that king who pardons the perpetrator of violence quickly perishes and incurs hatred.

verses.text:
न मित्रकारणाद् राजा विपुलाद् वा धनागमात् ।
समुत्सृजेत् साहसिकान् सर्वभूतभयावहान् ॥ ३४७ ॥
verses.english: Neither for friendship's sake, nor for the sake of great lucre, must a king let go perpetrators of violence, who cause terror to all creatures.

verses.text:
शस्त्रं द्विजातिभिर् ग्राह्यं धर्मो यत्र-उपरुध्यते
                                    ।
द्विजातीनां च वर्णानां विप्लवे कालकारिते ॥ ३४८ ॥
verses.english: Twice-born men may take up arms when (they are) hindered (in the fulfilment of their duties, when destruction (threatens) the twice-born castes (varna) in (evil) times,

verses.text:
आत्मनश् च परित्राणे दक्षिणानां च सङ्गरे ।
स्त्री.विप्राभ्युपपत्तौ च घ्नन् धर्मेण न दुष्यति ॥
                                    ३४९ ॥
verses.english: In their own defence, in a strife for the fees of officiating priests, and in order to protect women and Brahmanas; he who (under such circumstances) kills in the cause of right, commits no sin.

verses.text:
गुरुं वा बाल.वृद्धौ वा ब्राह्मणं वा बहु.श्रुतम् ।
आततायिनम् आयान्तं हन्याद् एव-अ.विचारयन् ॥ ३५० ॥
verses.english: One may slay without hesitation an assassin who approaches (with murderous intent), whether (he be one's) teacher, a child or an aged man, or a Brahmana deeply versed in the Vedas.

verses.text:
न-आततायिवधे दोषो हन्तुर् भवति कश् चन ।
प्रकाशं वा-अप्रकाशं वा मन्युस् तं मन्युम् ऋच्छति ॥
                                    ३५१ ॥
verses.english: By killing an assassin the slayer incurs no guilt, whether (he does it) publicly or secretly; in that case fury recoils upon fury.

verses.text:
परदाराभिमर्शेषु प्रवृत्तान् नॄन् महीपतिः ।
उद्वेजनकरैर् दण्डैश् छिन्नयित्वा प्रवासयेत् ॥ ३५२ ॥
                                        ८.३५२च्व्/
                                        म्: चिह्नयित्वा ॥ 8.352 ॥
verses.english: Men who commit adultery with the wives of others, the king shall cause to be marked by punishments which cause terror, and afterwards banish.

verses.text:
तत्.समुत्थो हि लोकस्य जायते वर्णसङ्करः ।
येन मूलहरो ऽधर्मः सर्वनाशाय कल्पते ॥ ३५३ ॥
verses.english: For by (adultery) is caused a mixture of the castes (varna) among men; thence (follows) sin, which cuts up even the roots and causes the destruction of everything.

verses.text:
परस्य पत्न्या पुरुषः सम्भाषां योजयन् रहः ।
पूर्वम् आक्षारितो दोषैः प्राप्नुयात् पूर्वसाहसम् ॥ ३५४
                                    ॥
verses.english: A man formerly accused of (such) offences, who secretly converses with another man's wife, shall pay the first (or lowest) amercement.

verses.text:
यस् त्व् अन्.आक्षारितः पूर्वम् अभिभाषते कारणात् ।
न दोषं प्राप्नुयात् किं चिन् न हि तस्य व्यतिक्रमः ॥
                                    ३५५ ॥
verses.english: But a man, not before accused, who (thus) speaks with (a woman) for some (reasonable) cause, shall not incur any guilt, since in him there is no transgression.

verses.text:
परस्त्रियं यो ऽभिवदेत् तीर्थे ऽरण्ये वने ऽपि वा ।
नदीनां वा-अपि सम्भेदे स सङ्ग्रहणम् आप्नुयात् ॥ ३५६
                                    ॥
verses.english: He who addresses the wife of another man at a Tirtha, outside the village, in a forest, or at the confluence of rivers, suffer (the punishment for) adulterous acts (samgrahana).

verses.text:
उपचारक्रिया केलिः स्पर्शो भूषण.वाससाम् । ८.३५७अव्/ म्: 
                                        उपकारक्रिया
सह खट्वा-आसनं च-एव सर्वं सङ्ग्रहणं स्मृतम् ॥
                                    ३५७ ॥
verses.english: Offering presents (to a woman), romping (with her), touching her ornaments and dress, sitting with her on a bed, all (these acts) are considered adulterous acts (samgrahana).

verses.text:
स्त्रियं स्पृशेद् अदेशे यः स्पृष्टो वा मर्षयेत् तया ।
परस्परस्य-अनुमते सर्वं सङ्ग्रहणं स्मृतम् ॥ ३५८
                                    ॥
verses.english: If one touches a woman in a place (which ought) not (to be touched) or allows (oneself to be touched in such a spot), all (such acts done) with mutual consent are declared (to be) adulterous (samgrahana).

verses.text:
अब्राह्मणः सङ्ग्रहणे प्राणान्तं दण्डम् अर्हति ।
चतुर्णाम् अपि वर्णानां दारा रक्ष्यतमाः सदा ॥ ३५९
                                    ॥
verses.english: A man who is not a Brahmana ought to suffer death for adultery (samgrahana); for the wives of all the four castes even must always be carefully guarded.

verses.text:
भिक्षुका बन्दिनश् च-एव दीक्षिताः कारवस् तथा ।
सम्भाषनं सह स्त्रीभिः कुर्युर् अ.प्रतिवारिताः ॥ ३६०
                                    ॥
verses.english: Mendicants, bards, men who have performed the initiatory ceremony of a Vedic sacrifice, and artisans are not prohibited from speaking to married women.

verses.text:
न सम्भाषां परस्त्रीभिः प्रतिषिद्धः समाचरेत् ।
निषिद्धो भाषमाणस् तु सुवर्णं दण्डम् अर्हति ॥ ३६१
                                    ॥
verses.english: Let no man converse with the wives of others after he has been forbidden (to do so); but he who converses (with them), in spite of a prohibition, shall be fined one suvarna.

verses.text:
न-एष चारणदारेषु विधिर् न-आत्म.उपजीविषु ।
सज्जयन्ति हि ते नारीर् निगूढाश् चारयन्ति च ॥ ३६२
                                    ॥
verses.english: This rule does not apply to the wives of actors and singers, nor (of) those who live on (the intrigues of) their own (wives); for such men send their wives (to others) or, concealing themselves, allow them to hold criminal intercourse.

verses.text:
किं चिद् एव तु दाप्यः स्यात् सम्भाषां ताभिर् आचरन् ।
प्रैष्यासु च-एकभक्तासु रहः प्रव्रजितासु च ॥ ३६३ ॥
                                        ८.३६३च्व्/
                                        म्: प्रेष्यासु ॥ 8.363 ॥
verses.english: Yet he who secretly converses with such women, or with female slaves kept by one (master), and with female ascetics, shall be compelled to pay a small fine.

verses.text:
यो ऽ.कामां दूषयेत् कन्यां स सद्यो वधम् अर्हति ।
स.कामां दूषयंस् तुल्यो न वधं प्राप्नुयान् नरः ॥ ३६४
                                    ॥
verses.english: He who violates an unwilling maiden shall instantly suffer corporal punishment; but a man who enjoys a willing maiden shall not suffer corporal punishment, if (his caste be) the same (as hers).

verses.text:
कन्याम् भजन्तीम् उत्कृष्टं न किं चिद् अपि दापयेत् ।
जघन्यं सेवमानां तु संयतां वासयेद् गृहे ॥ ३६५
                                    ॥
verses.english: From a maiden who makes advances to a (man of) high (caste), he shall not take any fine; but her, who courts a (man of) low (caste), let him force to live confined in her house.

verses.text:
उत्तमां सेवमानस् तु जघन्यो वधम् अर्हति ।
शुल्कं दद्यात् सेवमानः समाम् इच्छेत् पिता यदि ॥ ३६६
                                    ॥
verses.english: A (man of) low (caste) who makes love to a maiden (of) the highest (caste) shall suffer corporal punishment; he who addresses a maiden (on) equal (caste) shall pay the nuptial fee, if her father desires it.

verses.text:
अभिषह्य तु यः कन्यां कुर्याद् दर्पेण मानवः ।
तस्य-आशु कर्त्ये अङ्गुल्यौ दण्डं च-अर्हति षट्शतम् ॥
                                    ३६७ ॥ ८.३६७च्व्/ म्: कर्त्या अङ्गुल्यो ॥ 8.367 ॥
verses.english: But if any man through insolence forcibly contaminates a maiden, two of his fingers shall be instantly cut off, and he shall pay a fine of six hundred (panas).

verses.text:
स.कामां दूषयंस् तुल्यो न-अङ्गुलिछेदम् आप्नुयात् ।
द्विशतं तु दमम् दाप्यः प्रसङ्गविनिवृत्तये ॥ ३६८
                                    ॥
verses.english: A man (of) equal (caste) who defiles a willing maiden shall not suffer the amputation of his fingers, but shall pay a fine of two hundred (panas) in order to deter him from a repetition (of the offence).

verses.text:
कन्या-एव कन्यां या कुर्यात् तस्याः स्याद् द्विशतो दमः
                                    ।
शुल्कं च द्विगुणं दद्यात्-शिफाश् च-एव-आप्नुयाद् दश ॥
                                    ३६९ ॥
verses.english: A damsel who pollutes (another) damsel must be fined two hundred (panas), pay the double of her (nuptial) fee, and receive ten (lashes with a) rod.

verses.text:
या तु कन्यां प्रकुर्यात् स्त्री सा सद्यो मौण्ड्यम् अर्हति
                                    ।
अङ्गुल्योर् एव वा छेदं खरेण-उद्वहनं तथा ॥ ३७०
                                    ॥
verses.english: But a woman who pollutes a damsel shall instantly have (her head) shaved or two fingers cut off, and be made to ride (through the town) on a donkey.

verses.text:
भर्तारं लङ्घयेद् या तु स्त्री ज्ञाति.गुणदर्पिता ।
तां श्वभिः खादयेद् राजा संस्थाने बहुसंस्थिते ॥ ३७१
                                    ॥
verses.english: If a wife, proud of the greatness of her relatives or (her own) excellence, violates the duty which she owes to her lord, the king shall cause her to be devoured by dogs in a place frequented by many.

verses.text:
पुमांसं दाहयेत् पापं शयने तप्त आयसे ।
अभ्यादध्युश् च काष्ठानि तत्र दह्येत पापकृत् ॥ ३७२
                                    ॥
verses.english: Let him cause the male offender to be burnt on a red-hot iron bed; they shall put logs under it, (until) the sinner is burned (to death).

verses.text:
संवत्सराभिशस्तस्य दुष्टस्य द्विगुणो दमः । ८.३७३अव्/ म्: 
                                        संवत्सरे ऽभिशस्तस्य
व्रात्यया सह संवासे चाण्डाल्या तावद् एव तु ॥ ३७३
                                    ॥
verses.english: On a man (once) convicted, who is (again) accused within a year, a double fine (must be inflicted); even thus (must the fine be doubled) for (repeated) intercourse with a Vratya and a Kandali.

verses.text:
शूद्रो गुप्तम् अगुप्तं वा द्वैजातं वर्णम् आवसन् ।
अगुप्तम् अङ्ग.सर्वस्वैर् गुप्तं सर्वेण हीयते ॥ ३७४ ॥
                                        ८.३७४च्व्/
                                        म्: अङ्ग.सर्वस्वी ॥ 8.374 ॥
verses.english: A Sudra who has intercourse with a woman of a twice-born caste (varna), guarded or unguarded, (shall be punished in the following manner): if she was unguarded, he loses the part (offending) and all his property; if she was guarded, everything (even his life).

verses.text:
वैश्यः सर्वस्व.दण्डः स्यात् संवत्सरनिरोधतः ।
सहस्रं क्षत्रियो दण्ड्यो मौण्ड्यं मूत्रेण च-अर्हति ॥
                                    ३७५ ॥
verses.english: (For intercourse with a guarded Brahmana a Vaisya shall forfeit all his property after imprisonment for a year; a Kshatriya shall be fined one thousand (panas) and be shaved with the urine (of an ass).

verses.text:
ब्राह्मणीं यद्य् अगुप्तां तु गच्छेतां वैश्य.पार्थिवौ
                                    ।
वैश्यं पञ्चशतं कुर्यात् क्षत्रियं तु सहस्रिणम् ॥ ३७६
                                    ॥
verses.english: If a Vaisya or a Kshatriya has connexion with an unguarded Brahmana, let him fine the Vaisya five hundred (panas) and the Kshatriya one thousand.

verses.text:
उभाव् अपि तु ताव् एव ब्राह्मण्या गुप्तया सह ।
विप्लुतौ शूद्रवद् दण्ड्यौ दग्धव्यौ वा कटाग्निना ॥ ३७७
                                    ॥
verses.english: But even these two, if they offend with a Brahmani (not only) guarded (but the wife of an eminent man), shall be punished like a Sudra or be burnt in a fire of dry grass.

verses.text:
सहस्रं ब्राह्मणो दण्ड्यो गुप्तां विप्रां बलाद् व्रजन्
                                    ।
शतानि पञ्च दण्ड्यः स्याद् इच्छन्त्या सह सङ्गतः ॥ ३७८
                                    ॥
verses.english: A Brahmana who carnally knows a guarded Brahmani against her will, shall be fined one thousand (panas); but he shall be made to pay five hundred, if he had connexion with a willing one.

verses.text:
मौण्ड्यं प्राणान्तिकं दण्डो ब्राह्मणस्य विधीयते । ८.३७९अव्/ म्:
                                        प्राणान्तको. म्ऽस् चोम्. रेफ़ेर्स् तो थे रेअदिन्ग् ओफ़्
                                        प्राणान्तिक-.
इतरेषां तु वर्णानां दण्डः प्राणान्तिको भवेत् ॥ ३७९ ॥
                                        ८.३७९च्व्/
                                        म्: प्राणान्तको ॥ 8.379 ॥
verses.english: Tonsure (of the head) is ordained for a Brahmana (instead of) capital punishment; but (men of) other castes shall suffer capital punishment.

verses.text:
न जातु ब्राह्मणं हन्यात् सर्वपापेष्व् अपि स्थितम् ।
राष्ट्राद् एनं बहिः कुर्यात् समग्र.धनम् अ.क्षतम् ॥ ३८०
                                    ॥
verses.english: Let him never slay a Brahmana, though he have committed all (possible) crimes; let him banish such an (offender), leaving all his property (to him) and (his body) unhurt.

verses.text:
न ब्राह्मणवधाद् भूयान् अधर्मो विद्यते भुवि ।
तस्माद् अस्य वधं राजा मनसा-अपि न चिन्तयेत् ॥ ३८१
                                    ॥
verses.english: No greater crime is known on earth than slaying a Brahmana; a king, therefore, must not even conceive in his mind the thought of killing a Brahmana.

verses.text:
वैश्यश् चेत् क्षत्रियां गुप्तां वैश्यां वा क्षत्रियो व्रजेत्
                                    ।
यो ब्राह्मण्याम् अगुप्तायां ताव् उभौ दण्डम् अर्हतः ॥ ३८२
                                    ॥
verses.english: If a Vaisya approaches a guarded female of the Kshatriya caste, or a Kshatriya a (guarded) Vaisya woman, they both deserve the same punishment as in the case of an unguarded Brahmana female.

verses.text:
सहस्रं ब्राह्मणो दण्डं दाप्यो गुप्ते तु ते व्रजन् ।
शूद्रायां क्षत्रिय.विशोः साहस्रो वै भवेद् दमः ॥ ३८३
                                    ॥ ८.३८३च्व्/
                                        म्: शूद्राया ॥ 8.383 ॥
verses.english: A Brahmana shall be compelled to pay a fine of one thousand (panas) if he has intercourse with guarded (females of) those two (castes); for (offending with) a (guarded) Sudra female a fine of one thousand (panas shall be inflicted) on a Kshatriya or a Vaisya.

verses.text:
क्षत्रियायाम् अगुप्तायां वैश्ये पञ्चशतं दमः ।
मूत्रेण मौण्ड्यम् इच्छेत् तु क्षत्रियो दण्डम् एव वा ॥ ३८४
                                    ॥ ८.३८४च्व्/
                                        म्: ऋच्छेत् तु ॥ 8.384 ॥
verses.english: For (intercourse with) an unguarded Kshatriya a fine of five hundred (panas shall fall) on a Vaisya; but (for the same offence) a Kshatriya shall be shaved with the urine (of a donkey) or (pay) the same fine.

verses.text:
अगुप्ते क्षत्रिया.वैश्ये शूद्रां वा ब्राह्मणो व्रजन् ।
शतानि पञ्च दण्ड्यः स्यात् सहस्रं त्व् अन्त्यजस्त्रियम् ॥
                                    ३८५ ॥
verses.english: A Brahmana who approaches unguarded females (of the) Kshatriya or Vaisya (castes), or a Sudra female, shall be fined five hundred (panas); but (for intercourse with) a female (of the) lowest (castes), one thousand.

verses.text:
यस्य स्तेनः पुरे न-अस्ति न-अन्यस्त्रीगो न दुष्ट.वाक्
                                    ।
न साहसिक.दण्डघ्नो स राजा शक्रलोकभाक् ॥ ३८६
                                    ॥
verses.english: That king in whose town lives no thief, no adulterer, no defamer, no man guilty of violence, and no committer of assaults, attains the world of Sakra (Indra).

verses.text:
एतेषां निग्रहो राज्ञः पञ्चानां विषये स्वके ।
सांराज्यकृत् सजात्येषु लोके च-एव यशस्करः ॥ ३८७
                                    ॥
verses.english: The suppression of those five in his dominions secures to a king paramount sovereignty among his peers and fame in the world.

verses.text:
ऋत्विजं यस् त्यजेद् याज्यो याज्यं च र्त्विक् त्यजेद् यदि
                                    ।
शक्तं कर्मण्य् अदुष्टं च तयोर् दण्डः शतं शतम् ॥
                                    ३८८ ॥
verses.english: A sacrificer who forsakes an officiating priest, and an officiating priest who forsakes a sacrificer, (each being) able to perform his work and not contaminated (by grievous crimes), must each be fined one hundred (panas).

verses.text:
न माता न पिता न स्त्री न पुत्रस् त्यागम् अर्हति ।
त्यजन्न् अपतितान् एतान् राज्ञा दण्ड्यः शतानि षट् ॥ ३८९
                                    ॥
verses.english: Neither a mother, nor a father, nor a wife, nor a son shall be cast off; he who casts them off, unless guilty of a crime causing loss of caste, shall be fined six hundred (panas).

verses.text:
आश्रमेषु द्विजातीनां कार्ये विवदतां मिथः ।
न विब्रूयान् नृपो धर्मं चिकीर्षन् हितम् आत्मनः ॥ ३९०
                                    ॥
verses.english: If twice-born men dispute among each other concerning the duty of the orders, a king who desires his own welfare should not (hastily) decide (what is) the law.

verses.text:
यथार्हम् एतान् अभ्यर्च्य ब्राह्मणैः सह पार्थिवः ।
सान्त्वेन प्रशमय्य-आदौ स्वधर्मं प्रतिपादयेत् ॥ ३९१
                                    ॥
verses.english: Having shown them due honor, he should, with (the assistance of) Brahmanas, first soothe them by gentle (speech) and afterwards teach them their duty.

verses.text:
प्रतिवेश्य.अनुवेश्यौ च कल्याणे विंशतिद्विजे ।
अर्हाव् अ.भोजयन् विप्रो दण्डम् अर्हति माषकम् ॥ ३९२
                                    ॥
verses.english: A Brahmana who does not invite his next neighbour and his neighbour next but one, (though) both (he) worthy (of the honour), to a festival at which twenty Brahmanas are entertained, is liable to a fine of one masha.

verses.text:
श्रोत्रियः श्रोत्रियं साधुं भूतिकृत्येष्व् अ.भोजयन् ।
तद्.अन्नं द्विगुणं दाप्यो हिरण्यं च-एव माषकम् ॥ ३९३
                                    ॥ ८.३९३च्व्/
                                        म्: हैरण्यं ॥ 8.393 ॥
verses.english: A Srotriya who does not entertain a virtuous Srotriya at auspicious festive rites, shall be made to pay him twice (the value of) the meal and a masha of gold (as a fine to the king).

verses.text:
अन्धो जडः पीठसर्पी सप्तत्या स्थविरश् च यः ।
श्रोत्रियेषूपकुर्वंश् च न दाप्याः केन चित् करम् ॥ ३९४
                                    ॥
verses.english: A blind man, an idiot, (a cripple) who moves with the help of a board, a man full seventy years old, and he who confers benefits on Srotriyas, shall not be compelled by any (king) to pay a tax.

verses.text:
श्रोत्रियं व्याधित.आर्तौ च बाल.वृद्धाव् अ.किञ्चनम्
                                    ।
महाकुलीनम् आर्यं च राजा सम्पूजयेत् सदा ॥ ३९५ ॥
verses.english: Let the king always treat kindly a Srotriya, a sick or distressed man, an infant and an aged or indigent man, a man of high birth, and an honourable man (Arya).

verses.text:
शाल्मलीफलके श्लक्ष्णे नेनिज्यान् नेजकः शनैः ।
न च वासांसि वासोभिर् निर्हरेन् न च वासयेत् ॥ ३९६
                                    ॥
verses.english: A washerman shall wash (the clothes of his employers) gently on a smooth board of Salmaliwood he shall not return the clothes (of one person) for those (of another), nor allow anybody (but the owner) to wear them.

verses.text:
तन्तुवायो दशपलं दद्याद् एकपल.अधिकम् ।
अतो ऽन्यथा वर्तमानो दाप्यो द्वादशकं दमम् ॥ ३९७
                                    ॥
verses.english: A weaver (who has received) ten palas (of thread), shall return (cloth weighing) one pala more; he who acts differently shall be compelled to pay a fine of twelve (panas).

verses.text:
शुल्कस्थानेषु कुशलाः सर्वपण्य.विचक्षणाः ।
कुर्युर् अर्घं यथापण्यं ततो विंशं नृपो हरेत् ॥ ३९८
                                    ॥
verses.english: Let the king take one-twentieth of that (amount) which men, well acquainted with the settlement of tolls and duties (and) skilful in (estimating the value of) all kinds of merchandise, may fix as the value for each saleable commodity.

verses.text:
राज्ञः प्रख्यातभाण्डानि प्रतिषिद्धानि यानि च ।
ताणि निर्हरतो लोभात् सर्वहारं हरेन् नृपः ॥ ३९९
                                    ॥
verses.english: Let the king confiscate the whole property of (a trader) who out of greed exports goods of which the king has a monopoly or (the export of which is) forbidden.

verses.text:
शुल्कस्थानं परिहरन्न् अकाले क्रय.विक्रयी ।
मिथ्यावादी च सङ्ख्याने दाप्यो ऽष्टगुणम् अत्ययम् ॥ ४००
                                    ॥
verses.english: He who avoids a custom-house (or a toll), he who buys or sells at an improper time, or he who makes a false statement in enumerating (his goods), shall be fined eight times (the amount of duty) which he tried to evade.

verses.text:
आगमं निर्गमं स्थानं तथा वृद्धि.क्षयाव् उभौ ।
विचार्य सर्वपण्यानां कारयेत् क्रय.विक्रयौ ॥ ४०१
                                    ॥
verses.english: Let (the king) fix (the rates for) the purchase and sale of all marketable goods, having (duly) considered whence they come, whither they go, how long they have been kept, the (probable) profit and the (probable) outlay.

verses.text:
पञ्चरात्रे पञ्चरात्रे पक्षे पक्षे ऽथ वा गते ।
कुर्वीत च-एषां प्रत्यक्षम् अर्घसंस्थापनं नृपः ॥
                                    ४०२ ॥
verses.english: Once in five nights, or at the close of each fortnight, let the king publicly settle the prices for the (merchants).

verses.text:
तुलामानं प्रतीमानं सर्वं च स्यात् सुलक्षितम् ।
षट्सु षट्सु च मासेषु पुनर् एव परीक्षयेत् ॥ ४०३ ॥
verses.english: All weights and measures must be duly marked, and once in six months let him re-examine them.

verses.text:
पणं यानं तरे दाप्यं पौरुषो ऽर्धपणं तरे ।
पादं पशुश् च योषित्-च पादार्धं रिक्तकः पुमान् ॥ ४०४
                                    ॥ ८.४०४च्व्/
                                        म्: पादे ॥ 8.404 ॥
verses.english: At a ferry an (empty) cart shall be made to pay one pana, a man's (load) half a pana, an animal and a woman one quarter of a (pana), an unloaded man one-half of a quarter.

verses.text:
भाण्डपूर्णानि यानानि तार्यं दाप्यानि सारतः ।
रिक्तभाण्डानि यत् किं चित् पुमांसश् च्-अपरिच्छदाः ॥ ४०५
                                    ॥
verses.english: Carts (laden) with vessels full (of merchandise) shall be made to pay toll at a ferry according to the value (of the goods), empty vessels and men without luggage some trifle.

verses.text:
दीर्घाध्वनि यथादेशं यथाकालं तरो भवेत् ।
नदीतीरेषु तद् विद्यात् समुद्रे न-अस्ति लक्षणम् ॥ ४०६
                                    ॥
verses.english: For a long passage the boat-hire must be proportioned to the places and times; know that this (rule refers) to (passages along) the banks of rivers; at sea there is no settled (freight).

verses.text:
गर्भिणी तु द्विमासादिस् तथा प्रव्रजितो मुनिः ।
ब्राह्मणा लिङ्गिनश् च-एव न दाप्यास् तारिकं तरे ॥ ४०७
                                    ॥
verses.english: But a woman who has been pregnant two months or more, an ascetic, a hermit in the forest, and Brahmanas who are students of the Veda, shall not be made to pay toll at a ferry.

verses.text:
यन् नावि किं चिद् दाशानां विशीर्येत-अपराधतः ।
तद् दाशैर् एव दातव्यं समागम्य स्वतो ऽंशतः ॥ ४०८
                                    ॥
verses.english: Whatever may be damaged in a boat by the fault of the boatmen, that shall be made good by the boatmen collectively, (each paying) his share.

verses.text:
एष नौयायिनाम् उक्तो व्यवहारस्य निर्णयः ।
दाशापराधतस् तोये दैविके न-अस्ति निग्रहः ॥ ४०९
                                    ॥
verses.english: This decision in suits (brought) by passengers (holds good only) in case the boatmen are culpably negligent on the water; in the case of (an accident) caused by (the will of) the gods, no fine can be (inflicted on them).

verses.text:
वाणिज्यं कारयेद् वैश्यं कुसीदं कृषिम् एव च ।
पशूनां रक्षणं च-एव दास्यं शूद्रं द्विजन्मनाम् ॥ ४१०
                                    ॥
verses.english: (The king) should order a Vaisya to trade, to lend money, to cultivate the land, or to tend cattle, and a Sudra to serve the twice-born castes

verses.text:
क्षत्रियं च-एव वैश्यं च ब्राह्मणो वृत्तिकर्शितौ ।
बिभृयाद् आनृशंस्येन स्वानि कर्माणि कारयेत् ॥ ४११ ॥
verses.english: (Some wealthy) Brahmana shall compassionately support both a Kshatriya and a Vaisya, if they are distressed for a livelihood, employing them on work (which is suitable for) their (castes).

verses.text:
दास्यं तु कारयन्-लोभाद् ब्राह्मणः संस्कृतान् द्विजान्
                                    ।
अनिच्छतः प्राभवत्याद् राज्ञा दण्ड्यः शतानि षट् ॥ ४१२
                                    ॥
verses.english: But a Brahmana who, because he is powerful, out of greed makes initiated (men of the) twice-born (castes) against their will do the work of slaves, shall be fined by the king six hundred (panas).

verses.text:
शूद्रं तु कारयेद् दास्यं क्रीतम् अक्रीतम् एव वा ।
दास्याय-एव हि सृष्टो ऽसौ ब्राह्मणस्य स्वयम्भुवा ॥ ४१३
                                    ॥
verses.english: But a Sudra, whether bought or unbought, he may compel to do servile work; for he was created by the Self-existent (Svayambhu) to be the slave of a Brahmana.

verses.text:
न स्वामिना निसृष्टो ऽपि शूद्रो दास्याद् विमुच्यते ।
निसर्गजं हि तत् तस्य कस् तस्मात् तद् अपोहति ॥ ४१४
                                    ॥
verses.english: A Sudra, though emancipated by his master, is not released from servitude; since that is innate in him, who can set him free from it?

verses.text:
ध्वजाहृतो भक्तदासो गृहजः क्रीत.दत्त्रिमौ ।
पैत्रिको दण्डदासश् च सप्त-एते दासयोनयः ॥ ४१५
                                    ॥
verses.english: There are slaves of seven kinds, (viz.) he who is made a captive under a standard, he who serves for his daily food, he who is born in the house, he who is bought and he who is given, he who is inherited from ancestors, and he who is enslaved by way of punishment.

verses.text:
भार्या पुत्रश् च दासश् च त्रय एव-अ.धनाः स्मृताः
                                    ।
यत् ते समधिगच्छन्ति यस्य ते तस्य तद् धनम् ॥ ४१६
                                    ॥
verses.english: A wife, a son, and a slave, these three are declared to have no property; the wealth which they earn is (acquired) for him to whom they belong.

verses.text:
विस्रब्धं ब्राह्मणः शूद्राद् द्रव्य.उपादानम् आचरेत् ।
न हि तस्य-अस्ति किं चित् स्वं भर्तृहार्य.धनो हि सः
                                    ॥ ४१७ ॥
verses.english: A Brahmana may confidently seize the goods of (his) Sudra (slave); for, as that (slave) can have no property, his master may take his possessions.

verses.text:
वैश्य.शूद्रौ प्रयत्नेन स्वानि कर्माणि कारयेत् ।
तौ हि च्युतौ स्वकर्मभ्यः क्षोभयेताम् इदं जगत् ॥
                                    ४१८ ॥
verses.english: (The king) should carefully compel Vaisyas and Sudra to perform the work (prescribed) for them; for if these two (castes) swerved from their duties, they would throw this (whole) world into confusion.

verses.text:
अहन्य् अहन्य् अवेक्षेत कर्मान्तान् वाहनानि च ।
आय.व्ययौ च नियताव् आकरान् कोशम् एव च ॥ ४१९ ॥
verses.english: Let him daily look after the completion of his undertakings, his beasts of burden, and carriages, (the collection of) his revenues and the disbursements, his mines and his treasury.

verses.text:
एवं सर्वान् इमान् राजा व्यवहारान् समापयन् ।
व्यपोह्य किल्बिषं सर्वं प्राप्नोति परमां गतिम् ॥ ४२०
                                    ॥
verses.english: A king who thus brings to a conclusion. all the legal business enumerated above, and removes all sin, reaches the highest state (of bliss).

title: मनुस्मृति: अध्याय ९: दायभाग एवं स्त्री-पुरुष धर्म
subtitle: Inheritance, Family & Property Law (336 Shlokas)

verses.text:
पुरुषस्य स्त्रियाश् च-एव धर्मे वर्त्मनि तिष्ठतोः । ९.०१अव्/ म्: 
                                    धर्म्ये
संयोगे विप्रयोगे च धर्मान् वक्ष्यामि शाश्वतान् ॥ १ ॥
verses.english: I will now propound the eternal laws for a husband and his wife who keep to the path of duty, whether they be united or separated.

verses.text:
अस्वतन्त्राः स्त्रियः कार्याः पुरुषैः स्वैर् दिवा.निशम्
                                    ।
विषयेषु च सज्जन्त्यः संस्थाप्या आत्मनो वशे ॥ २ ॥
