ये नियुक्तास् तु कार्येषु हन्युः कार्याणि कार्यिणाम् ।
धन.उष्मणा पच्यमानास् तान् निः.स्वान् कारयेन् नृपः ॥ २३१
                                ॥
verses.english: But those appointed (to administer public) affairs, who, baked by the fire of wealth, mar the business of suitors, the king shall deprive of their property.

verses.text:
कूटशासनकर्तॄंश् च प्रकृतीनां च दूषकान् ।
स्त्री.बाल.ब्राह्मणघ्नांश् च हन्याद् द्विष्.सेविनस् तथा ॥ २३२
                                ॥
verses.english: Forgers of royal edicts, those who corrupt his ministers, those who slay women, infants, or Brahmanas, and those who serve his enemies, the king shall put to death.

verses.text:
तीरितं च-अनुशिष्टं च यत्र क्व चन यद् भवेत् ।
कृतं तद् धर्मतो विद्यात्-न तद् भूयो निवर्तयेत् ॥ २३३
                                ॥
verses.english: Whenever any (legal transaction) has been completed or (a punishment) been inflicted according to the law, he shall sanction it and not annul it.

verses.text:
अमात्याः प्राड्विवाको वा यत् कुर्युः कार्यम् अन्यथा ।
तत् स्वयं नृपतिः कुर्यात् तान् सहस्रं च दण्डयेत् ॥ २३४ ॥
                                    ९.२३४च्व्/ म्: 
                                    तं ॥ 9.234 ॥
verses.english: Whatever matter his ministers or the judge may settle improperly, that the king himself shall (re-) settle and fine (them) one thousand (panas).

verses.text:
ब्रह्महा च सुरापश् च स्तेयी च गुरुतल्पगः । ९.२३५अव्/ म्: 
                                        तस्करो गुरुतल्पगः
एते सर्वे पृथग् ज्ञेया महापातकिनो नराः ॥ २३५ ॥
verses.english: The slayer of a Brahmana, (A twice-born man) who drinks (the spirituous liquor called) Sura, he who steals (the gold of a Brahmana), and he who violates a Guru's bed, must each and all be considered as men who committed mortal sins (mahapataka).

verses.text:
चतुर्णाम् अपि च-एतेषां प्रायश्चित्तम् अ.कुर्वताम् ।
शारीरं धनसंयुक्तं दण्डं धर्म्यं प्रकल्पयेत् ॥
                                    २३६ ॥
verses.english: On those four even, if they do not perform a penance, let him inflict corporal punishment and fines in accordance with the law.

verses.text:
गुरुतल्पे भगः कार्यः सुरापाने सुराध्वजः ।
स्तेये च श्वपदं कार्यं ब्रह्महण्य् अ.शिराः पुमान् ॥ २३७
                                    ॥ ९.२३७च्व्/
                                        म्: तस्करे श्वपदं कार्यं ॥ 9.237 ॥
verses.english: For violating a Guru's bed, (the mark of) a female part shall be (impressed on the forehead with a hot iron); for drinking (the spirituous liquor called) Sura, the sign of a tavern; for stealing (the gold of a Brahmana), a dog's foot; for murdering a Brahmana, a headless corpse.

verses.text:
अ.सम्भोज्या ह्य् अ.संयाज्या अ.सम्पाठ्या ऽ.विवाहिनः ।
चरेयुः पृथिवीं दीनाः सर्वधर्मबहिष्कृताः ॥ २३८
                                    ॥
verses.english: Excluded from all fellowship at meals, excluded from all sacrifices, excluded from instruction and from matrimonial alliances, abject and excluded from all religious duties, let them wander over (this) earth.

verses.text:
ज्ञाति.सम्बन्धिभिस् त्व् एते त्यक्तव्याः कृत.लक्षणाः
                                    ।
निर्.दया निर्.नमस्कारास् तन् मनोर् अनुशासनम् ॥ २३९
                                    ॥
verses.english: Such (persons) who have been branded with (indelible) marks must be cast off by their paternal and maternal relations, and receive neither compassion nor a salutation; that is the teaching of Manu.

verses.text:
प्रायश्चित्तं तु कुर्वाणाः सर्ववर्णा यथोदितम् । ९.२४०अव्/ म्: 
                                        पूर्वे वर्णा यथा.उदितम्
न-अङ्क्या राज्ञा ललाटे स्युर् दाप्यास् तु-उत्तमसाहसम् ॥
                                    २४० ॥
verses.english: But (men of) all castes who perform the prescribed penances, must not be branded on the forehead by the king, but shall be made to pay the highest amercement.

verses.text:
आगःसु ब्राह्मणस्य-एव कार्यो मध्यमसाहसः ।
विवास्यो वा भवेद् राष्ट्रात् स.द्रव्यः स.परिच्छदः ॥
                                    २४१ ॥
verses.english: For (such) offences the middlemost amercement shall be inflicted on a Brahmana, or he may be banished from the realm, keeping his money and his chattels.

verses.text:
इतरे कृतवन्तस् तु पापान्य् एतान्य् अकामतः ।
सर्वस्वहारम् अर्हन्ति कामतस् तु प्रवासनम् ॥ २४२
                                    ॥
verses.english: But (men of) other (castes), who have unintentionally committed such crimes, ought to be deprived of their whole property; if (they committed them) intentionally, they shall be banished.

verses.text:
न-आददीत नृपः साधुर् महापातकिनो धनम् ।
आददानस् तु तत्-लोभात् तेन दोषेण लिप्यते ॥ २४३ ॥
verses.english: A virtuous king must not take for himself the property of a man guilty of mortal sin; but if he takes it out of greed, he is tainted by that guilt (of the offender).

verses.text:
अप्सु प्रवेश्य तं दण्डं वरुणाय-उपपादयेत् ।
श्रुत.वृत्त.उपपन्ने वा ब्राह्मणे प्रतिपादयेत् ॥ २४४
                                    ॥
verses.english: Having thrown such a fine into the water, let him offer it to Varuna, or let him bestow it on a learned and virtuous Brahmana.

verses.text:
ईशो दण्डस्य वरुणो राज्ञां दण्डधरो हि सः ।
ईशः सर्वस्य जगतो ब्राह्मणो वेदपारगः ॥ २४५ ॥
verses.english: Varuna is the lord of punishment, for he holds the sceptre even over kings; a Brahmana who has learnt the whole Veda is the lord of the whole world.

verses.text:
यत्र वर्जयते राजा पापकृद्भ्यो धनागमम् ।
तत्र कालेन जायन्ते मानवा दीर्घजीविनः ॥ २४६ ॥
verses.english: In that (country), where the king avoids taking the property of (mortal) sinners, men are born in (due) time (and are) long-lived,

verses.text:
निष्पद्यन्ते च सस्यानि यथा.उप्तानि विशां पृथक् ।
बालाश् च न प्रमीयन्ते विकृतं च न जायते ॥ २४७
                                    ॥
verses.english: And the crops of the husbandmen spring up, each as it was sown, and the children die not, and no misshaped (offspring) is born.

verses.text:
ब्राह्मणान् बाधमानं तु कामाद् अवरवर्णजम् ।
हन्याच् चित्रैर् वध.उपायैर् उद्वेजनकरैर् नृपः ॥ २४८
                                    ॥
verses.english: But the king shall inflict on a base-born (Sudra), who intentionally gives pain to Brahmanas, various (kinds of) corporal punishment which cause terror.

verses.text:
यावान् अ.वध्यस्य वधे तावान् वध्यस्य मोक्षणे ।
अधर्मो नृपतेर् दृष्टो धर्मस् तु विनियच्छतः ॥ २४९
                                    ॥
verses.english: When a king punishes an innocent (man), his guilt is considered as great as when he sets free a guilty man; but (he acquires) merit when he punishes (justly).

verses.text:
उदितो ऽयं विस्तरशो मिथो विवादमानयोः ।
अष्टादशसु मार्गेषु व्यवहारस्य निर्णयः ॥ २५० ॥
verses.english: Thus the (manner of) deciding suits (falling) under the eighteen titles, between two litigant parties, has been declared at length.

verses.text:
एवं धर्म्याणि कार्याणि सम्यक् कुर्वन् महीपतिः ।
देशान् अलब्धान्-लिप्सेत लब्धांश् च परिपालयेत् ॥ २५१ ॥
verses.english: A king who thus duly fulfils his duties in accordance with justice, may seek to gain countries which he has not yet gained, and shall duly protect them when he has gained them.

verses.text:
सम्यक्.निविष्ट.देशस् तु कृत.दुर्गश् च शास्त्रतः ।
कण्टक.उद्धरणे नित्यम् आतिष्ठेद् यत्नम् उत्तमम् ॥ २५२
                                ॥
verses.english: Having duly settled his country, and having built forts in accordance with the Institutes, he shall use his utmost exertions to remove (those men who are nocuous like) thorns.

verses.text:
रक्षनाद् आर्यवृत्तानां कण्टकानां च शोधनात् ।
नरेन्द्रास् त्रिदिवं यान्ति प्रजापालन.तत्पराः ॥ २५३ ॥
verses.english: By protecting those who live as (becomes) Aryans and by removing the thorns, kings, solely intent on guarding their subjects, reach heaven.

verses.text:
अ.शासंस् तस्करान् यस् तु बलिं गृह्णाति पार्थिवः ।
तस्य प्रक्षुभ्यते राष्ट्रं स्वर्गाच् च परिहीयते ॥ २५४
                                ॥
verses.english: The realm of that king who takes his share in kind, though he does not punish thieves, (will be) disturbed and he (will) lose heaven.

verses.text:
निर्भयं तु भवेद् यस्य राष्ट्रं बाहु.बलाश्रितम् ।
तस्य तद् वर्धते नित्यं सिच्यमान इव द्रुमः ॥ २५५ ॥
verses.english: But if his kingdom be secure, protected by the strength of his arm, it will constantly flourish like a (well)- watered tree.

verses.text:
द्विविधांस् तस्करान् विद्यात् परद्रव्यापहारकान् ।
प्रकाशांश् च-अप्रकाशांश् च चार.चक्षुर् महीपतिः ॥ २५६
                                ॥
verses.english: Let the king who sees (everything) through his spies, discover the two sorts of thieves who deprive others of their property, both those who (show themselves) openly and those who (lie) concealed.

verses.text:
प्रकाशवञ्चकास् तेषां नानापण्य-उपजीविनः ।
प्रच्छन्नवञ्चकास् त्व् एते ये स्तेन.अटविकादयः ॥ २५७
                                ॥
verses.english: Among them, the open rogues (are those) who subsist by (cheating in the sale of) various marketable commodities, but the concealed rogues are burglars, robbers in forests, and so forth.

verses.text:
उत्कोचकाश् च-औपधिका वञ्चकाः कितवास् तथा ।
मङ्गलादेश.वृत्ताश् च भद्राश् च-ईक्षणिकैः सह ॥ २५८ ॥
                                    ९.२५८च्व्/ म्: 
                                    भद्रप्रेक्षणिकैः सह ॥ 9.258 ॥
verses.english: Those who take bribes, cheats and rogues, gamblers, those who live by teaching (the performance of) auspicious ceremonies, sanctimonious hypocrites, and fortune-tellers,

verses.text:
असम्यक्कारिणश् च-एव महामात्राश् चिकित्सकाः ।
शिल्प.उपचारयुक्ताश् च निपुणाः पण्ययोषितः ॥ २५९ ॥
verses.english: Officials of high rank and physicians who act improperly, men living by showing their proficiency in arts, and clever harlots,

verses.text:
एवमादीन् विजानीयात् प्रकाशांल् लोककण्टकान् । ९.२६०अव्/ म्: 
                                    एवमाद्यान्
निगूढचारिणश् च-अन्यान् अनार्यान् आर्यलिङ्गिनः ॥ २६० ॥
verses.english: These and the like who show themselves openly, as well as others who walk in disguise (such as) non-Aryans who wear the marks of Aryans, he should know to be thorns (in the side of his people).

verses.text:
तान् विदित्वा सुचरितैर् गूढैस् तत्कर्मकारिभिः ।
चारैश् च-अनेक.संस्थानैः प्रोत्साद्य वशम् आनयेत् ॥ २६१
                                ॥
verses.english: Having detected them by means of trustworthy persons, who, disguising themselves, (pretend) to follow the same occupations and by means of spies, wearing various disguises, he must cause them to be instigated (to commit offences), and bring them into his power.

verses.text:
तेषां दोषान् अभिख्याप्य स्वे स्वे कर्मणि तत्त्वतः ।
कुर्वीत शासनं राजा सम्यक् सार.अपराधतः ॥ २६२ ॥
verses.english: Then having caused the crimes, which they committed by their several actions, to be proclaimed in accordance with the facts, the king shall duly punish them according to their strength and their crimes.

verses.text:
न हि दण्डाद् ऋते शक्यः कर्तुं पाप.विनिग्रहः ।
स्तेनानां पापबुद्धीनां निभृतं चरतां क्षितौ ॥ २६३ ॥
verses.english: For the wickedness of evil-minded thieves, who secretly prowl over this earth, cannot be restrained except by punishment.

verses.text:
सभा.प्रपा.अपूप.शालावेश.मद्य.अन्न.विक्रयाः ।
चतुष्पथांश् चैत्यवृक्षाः समाजाः प्रेक्षणानि च ॥ २६४
                                ॥
verses.english: Assembly-houses, houses where water is distributed or cakes are sold, brothels, taverns and victualler's shops, cross-roads, well-known trees, festive assemblies, and play-houses and concert-rooms,

verses.text:
जीर्ण.उद्यानान्य् अरण्यानि कारुकावेशनानि च ।
शून्यानि च-अप्य् अगाराणि वनान्य् उपवनानि च ॥ २६५ ॥
verses.english: Old gardens, forests, the shops of artisans, empty dwellings, natural and artificial groves,

verses.text:
एवंविधान् नृपो देशान् गुल्मैः स्थावर.जङ्गमैः ।
तस्करप्रतिषेधार्थं चारैश् च-अप्य् अनुचारयेत् ॥ २६६
                                ॥
verses.english: These and the like places the king shall cause to be guarded by companies of soldiers, both stationary and patrolling, and by spies, in order to keep away thieves.

verses.text:
तत्सहायैर् अनुगतैर् नानाकर्मप्रवेदिभिः ।
विद्याद् उत्सादयेच् च-एव निपुणैः पूर्वतस्करैः ॥ २६७
                                ॥
verses.english: By the means of clever reformed thieves, who associate with such (rogues), follow them and know their various machinations, he must detect and destroy them.

verses.text:
भक्ष्य.भोज्य.उपदेशैश् च ब्राह्मणानां च दर्शनैः ।
शौर्यकर्मापदेशैश् च कुर्युस् तेषां समागमम् ॥ २६८ ॥
verses.english: Under the pretext of (offering them) various dainties, of introducing them to Brahmanas, and on the pretence of (showing them) feats of strength, the (spies) must make them meet (the officers of justice).

verses.text:
ये तत्र न-उपसर्पेयुर् मूलप्रणिहिताश् च ये ।
तान् प्रसह्य नृपो हन्यात् स.मित्र.ज्ञाति.बान्धवान् ॥ २६९
                                ॥
verses.english: Those among them who do not come, and those who suspect the old (thieves employed by the king), the king shall attack by force and slay together with their friends, blood relations, and connexions.

verses.text:
न ह-ऊढेन विना चौरं घातयेद् धार्मिको नृपः ।
सह-ऊढं स.उपकरणं घातयेद् अ.विचारयन् ॥ २७० ॥
verses.english: A just king shall not cause a thief to be put to death, (unless taken) with the stolen goods (in his possession); him who (is taken) with the stolen goods and the implements (of burglary), he may, without hesitation, cause to be slain.

verses.text:
ग्रामेष्व् अपि च ये के चिच् चौराणां भक्तदायकाः ।
भाण्ड.अवकाशदाश् च-एव सर्वांस् तान् अपि घातयेत् ॥ २७१
                                ॥
verses.english: All those also who in villages give food to thieves or grant them room for (concealing their implements), he shall cause to be put to death.

verses.text:
राष्ट्रेषु रक्षाधिकृतान् सामन्तांश् च-एव चोदितान् ।
अभ्याघातेषु मध्यस्थाञ् शिष्याच् चौरान् इव द्रुतम् ॥ २७२
                                ॥
verses.english: Those who are appointed to guard provinces and his vassals who have been ordered (to help), he shall speedily punish like thieves, (if they remain) inactive in attacks (by robbers).

verses.text:
यश् च-अपि धर्मसमयात् प्रच्युतो धर्म.जीवनः ।
दण्डेन-एव तम् अप्य् ओषेत् स्वकाद् धर्माद्द् हि विच्युतम् ॥ २७३
                                ॥
verses.english: Moreover if (a man), who subsists by (the fulfilment of) the law, departs from the established rule of the law, the (king) shall severely punish him by a fine, (because he) violated his duty.

verses.text:
ग्रामघाते हिताभङ्गे पथि मोषाभिदर्शने ।
शक्तितो न-अभिधावन्तो निर्वास्याः स.परिच्छदाः ॥ २७४
                                ॥
verses.english: Those who do not give assistance according to their ability when a village is being plundered, a dyke is being destroyed, or a highway robbery committed, shall be banished with their goods and chattels.

verses.text:
राज्ञः कोशापहर्तॄंश् च प्रतिकूलेषु च स्थितान् । ९.२७५अव्/ म्: 
                                    प्रातिकूल्येष्व् अवस्थितान्
घातयेद् विविधैर् दण्डैर् अरीणां च-उपजापकान् ॥ २७५
                                ॥
verses.english: On those who rob the king's treasury and those who persevere in opposing (his commands), he shall inflict various kinds of capital punishment, likewise on those who conspire with his enemies.

verses.text:
सन्धिं छित्त्वा तु ये चौर्यं रात्रौ कुर्वन्ति तस्कराः ।
                                    ९.२७६अव्/ म्: 
                                    सन्धिं भित्त्वा
तेषां छित्त्वा नृपो हस्तौ तीक्ष्णे शूले निवेशयेत् ॥ २७६
                                ॥
verses.english: But the king shall cut off the hands of those robbers who, breaking into houses, commit thefts at night, and cause them to be impaled on a pointed stake.

verses.text:
अङ्गुलीर् ग्रन्थिभेदस्य छेदयेत् प्रथमे ग्रहे ।
द्वितीये हस्त.चरणौ तृतीये वधम् अर्हति ॥ २७७ ॥
verses.english: On the first conviction, let him cause two fingers of a cut-purse to be amputated; on the second, one hand and one foot; on the third, he shall suffer death.

verses.text:
अग्निदान् भक्तदांश् च-एव तथा शस्त्र.अवकाशदान् ।
सन्निधातॄंश् च मोषस्य हन्याच् चौरम् इव-ईश्वरः ॥ २७८
                                ॥
verses.english: Those who give (to thieves) fire, food, arms, or shelter, and receivers of stolen goods, the ruler shall punish like thieves.

verses.text:
तडागभेदकं हन्याद् अप्सु शुद्धवधेन वा ।
यद् वा-अपि प्रतिसंस्कुर्याद् दाप्यस् तु-उत्तमसाहसम् ॥ २७९
                                ॥
verses.english: Him who breaks (the dam of) a tank he shall slay (by drowning him) in water or by (some other) (mode of) capital punishment; or the offender may repair the (damage), but shall be made to pay the highest amercement.

verses.text:
कोष्ठागार.आयुधागार.देवतागार.भेदकान् ।
हस्ति.अश्व.रथहर्तॄंश् च हन्याद् एव-अ.विचारयन् ॥ २८०
                                ॥
verses.english: Those who break into a (royal) storehouse, an armoury, or a temple, and those who steal elephants, horses, or chariots, he shall slay without hesitation.

verses.text:
यस् तु पूर्वनिविष्टस्य तडागस्य-उदकं हरेत् ।
आगमं वा-अप्य् अपां भिन्द्यात् स दाप्यः पूर्वसाहसम् ॥ २८१
                                ॥
verses.english: But he who shall take away the water of a tank, made in ancient times, or shall cut off the supply of water, must be made to pay the first (or lowest) amercement.

verses.text:
समुत्सृजेद् राजमार्गे यस् त्व् अमेध्यम् अनापदि ।
स द्वौ कार्षापणौ दद्याद् अमेध्यं च-आशु शोधयेत् ॥ २८२
                                ॥
verses.english: But he who, except in a case of extreme necessity, drops filth on the king's high-road, shall pay two karshapanas and immediately remove (that) filth.

verses.text:
आपद्गतो ऽथ वा वृद्धा गर्भिणी बाल एव वा ।
परिभाषणम् अर्हन्ति तच् च शोध्यम् इति स्थितिः ॥ २८३
                                ॥
verses.english: But a person in urgent necessity, an aged man, a pregnant woman, or a child, shall be reprimanded and clean the (place); that is a settled rule.

verses.text:
चिकित्सकानां सर्वेषां मिथ्याप्रचरतां दमः ।
अमानुषेषु प्रथमो मानुषेषु तु मध्यमः ॥ २८४ ॥
verses.english: All physicians who treat (their patients) wrongly (shall pay) a fine; in the case of animals, the first (or lowest); in the case of human beings, the middlemost (amercement).

verses.text:
सङ्क्रम.ध्वज.यष्टीनां प्रतिमानां च भेदकः ।
प्रतिकुर्याच् च तत् सर्वं पञ्च दद्यात्-शतानि च ॥ २८५
                                ॥
verses.english: He who destroys a bridge, the flag (of a temple or royal palace), a pole, or images, shall repair the whole (damage) and pay five hundred (panas).

verses.text:
अदूषितानां द्रव्याणां दूषणे भेदने तथा ।
मणीनाम् अपवेधे च दण्डः प्रथमसाहसः ॥ २८६ ॥
verses.english: For adulterating unadulterated commodities, and for breaking gems or for improperly boring (them), the fine is the first (or lowest) amercement.

verses.text:
समैर् हि विषमं यस् तु चरेद् वै मूल्यतो ऽपि वा ।
समाप्नुयाद् दमं पूर्वं नरो मध्यमम् एव वा ॥ २८७ ॥
verses.english: But that man who behaves dishonestly to honest (customers) or cheats in his prices, shall be fined in the first or in the middlemost amercement.

verses.text:
बन्धनानि च सर्वाणि राजा मार्गे निवेशयेत् । ९.२८८अव्/ म्: 
                                    राजमार्गे
दुःखिता यत्र दृश्येरन् विकृताः पापकारिणह् ॥ २८८ ॥
verses.english: Let him place all prisons near a high-road, where the suffering and disfigured offenders can be seen.

verses.text:
प्राकारस्य च भेत्तारं परिखाणां च पूरकम् ।
द्वाराणां च-एव भङ्क्तारं क्षिप्रम् एव प्रवासयेत् ॥ २८९
                                ॥
verses.english: Him who destroys the wall (of a town), or fills up the ditch (round a town), or breaks a (town)- gate, he shall instantly banish.

verses.text:
अभिचारेषु सर्वेषु कर्तव्यो द्विशतो दमः ।
मूलकर्मणि च-अनाप्तेः कृत्यासु विविधासु च ॥ २९० ॥ ९.२९०च्व्/ म्: 
                                    च-अनाप्तैः ॥ 9.290 ॥
verses.english: For all incantations intended to destroy life, for magic rites with roots (practised by persons) not related (to him against whom they are directed), and for various kinds of sorcery, a fine of two hundred (panas) shall be inflicted.

verses.text:
अबीजविक्रयी च-एव बीज.उत्कृष्टा तथा-एव च ।
मर्यादाभेदकश् च-एव विकृतं प्राप्नुयाद् वधम् ॥ २९१
                                ॥
verses.english: He who sells (for seed-corn that which is) not seed-corn, he who takes up seed (already sown), and he who destroys a boundary (-mark), shall be punished by mutilation.

verses.text:
सर्वकण्टकपापिष्ठं हेमकारं तु पार्थिवः ।
प्रवर्तमानम् अन्याये छेदयेत्-लवशः क्षुरैः ॥ २९२ ॥
                                    ९.२९२च्व्/ म्: 
                                    छेदयेत् खण्डशः क्षुरैः ॥ 9.292 ॥
verses.english: But the king shall cause a goldsmith who behaves dishonestly, the most nocuous of all the thorns, to be cut to pieces with razors.

verses.text:
सीता.द्रव्यापहरणे शस्त्राणाम् औषधस्य च ।
कालम् आसाद्य कार्यं च राजा दण्डं प्रकल्पयेत् ॥ २९३ ॥
verses.english: For the theft of agricultural implements, of arms and of medicines, let the king award punishment, taking into account the time (of the offence) and the use (of the object).

verses.text:
स्वाम्य्.अमात्यौ पुरं राष्ट्रं कोश.दण्डौ सुहृत् तथा
                                    ।
सप्त प्रकृतयो ह्य् एताः सप्ताङ्गं राज्यम् उच्यते ॥ २९४
                                    ॥
verses.english: The king and his minister, his capital, his realm, his treasury, his army, and his ally are the seven constituent parts (of a kingdom); (hence) a kingdom is said to have seven limbs (anga).

verses.text:
सप्तानां प्रकृतीनां तु राज्यस्य-आसां यथाक्रमम् ।
पूर्वं पूर्वं गुरुतरं जानीयाद् व्यसनं महत् ॥ २९५
                                    ॥
verses.english: But let him know (that) among these seven constituent parts of a kingdom (which have been enumerated) in due order, each earlier (named) is more important and (its destruction) the greater calamity.

verses.text:
सप्त.अङ्गस्य-इह राज्यस्य विष्टब्धस्य त्रिदण्डवत्
                                    ।
अन्योन्यगुणवैशेष्यात्-न किं चिद् अतिरिच्यते ॥ २९६ ॥
verses.english: Yet in a kingdom containing seven constituent parts, which is upheld like the triple staff (of an ascetic), there is no (single part) more important (than the others), by reason of the importance of the qualities of each for the others.

verses.text:
तेषु तेषु तु कृत्येषु तत् तद् अङ्गं विशिष्यते ।
येन यत् साध्यते कार्यं तत् तस्मिन्-श्रेष्ठम् उच्यते ॥
                                    २९७ ॥
verses.english: For each part is particularly qualified for (the accomplishment of) certain objects, (and thus) each is declared to be the most important for that particular purpose which is effected by its means.

verses.text:
चारेण-उत्साहयोगेन क्रियया-एव च कर्मणाम् ।
स्वशक्तिं परशक्तिं च नित्यं विद्यात्-महीपतिः ॥ २९८
                                    ॥ ९.२९८च्व्/
                                        म्: विद्यात् पर.आत्मनोः ॥ 9.298 ॥
verses.english: By spies, by a (pretended) display of energy, and by carrying out (various) undertakings, let the king constantly ascertain his own and his enemy's strength;

verses.text:
पीडनानि च सर्वाणि व्यसनानि तथा-एव च ।
आरभेत ततः कार्यं सञ्चिन्त्य गुरु.लाघवम् ॥ २९९
                                    ॥
verses.english: Moreover, all calamities and vices; afterwards, when he has fully considered their relative importance, let him begin his operations.

verses.text:
आरभेत-एव कर्माणि श्रान्तः श्रान्तः पुनः पुनः ।
कर्माण्य् आरभमाणं हि पुरुषं श्रीर् निषेवते ॥ ३००
                                    ॥
verses.english: (Though he be) ever so much tired (by repeated failures), let him begin his operations again and again; for fortune greatly favours the man who (strenuously) exerts himself in his undertakings.

verses.text:
कृतं त्रेतायुगं च-एव द्वापरं कलिर् एव च ।
राज्ञो वृत्तानि सर्वाणि राजा हि युगम् उच्यते ॥ ३०१ ॥
verses.english: The various ways in which a king behaves (resemble) the Krita, Treta, Dvapara, and Kali ages; hence the king is identified with the ages (of the world).

verses.text:
कलिः प्रसुप्तो भवति स जाग्रद् द्वापरं युगम् ।
कर्मस्व् अभ्युद्यतस् त्रेता विचरंस् तु कृतं युगम् ॥ ३०२
                                    ॥
verses.english: Sleeping he represents the Kali (or iron age), waking the Dvapara (or brazen) age, ready to act the Treta (or silver age), but moving (actively) the Krita (or golden) age.

verses.text:
इन्द्रस्य-अर्कस्य वायोश् च यमस्य वरुणस्य च ।
चन्द्रस्य-अग्नेः पृथिव्याश् च तेजोवृत्तं नृपश् चरेत् ॥
                                    ३०३ ॥
verses.english: Let the king emulate the energetic action of Indra, of the Sun, of the Wind, of Yama, of Varuna, of the Moon, of the Fire, and of the Earth.

verses.text:
वार्षिकांश् चतुरो मासान् यथा-इन्द्रो ऽभिप्रवर्षति ।
तथा-अभिवर्षेत् स्वं राष्ट्रं कामैर् इन्द्रव्रतं चरन्
                                    ॥ ३०४ ॥
verses.english: As Indra sends copious rain during the four months of the rainy season, even so let the king, taking upon himself the office of Indra, shower benefits on his kingdom.

verses.text:
अष्टौ मासान् यथा-आदित्यस् तोयं हरति रश्मिभिः ।
तथा हरेत् करं राष्ट्रात्-नित्यम् अर्कव्रतं हि तत् ॥
                                    ३०५ ॥
verses.english: As the Sun during eight months (imperceptibly) draws up the water with his rays, even so let him gradually draw his taxes from his kingdom; for that is the office in which he resembles the Sun.

verses.text:
प्रविश्य सर्वभूतानि यथा चरति मारुतः ।
तथा चारैः प्रवेष्टव्यं व्रतम् एतद्द् हि मारुतम् ॥ ३०६
                                    ॥
verses.english: As the Wind moves (everywhere), entering (in the shape of the vital air) all created beings, even so let him penetrate (everywhere) through his spies; that is the office in which he resembles the Wind.

verses.text:
यथा यमः प्रिय.द्वेष्यौ प्राप्ते काले नियच्छति ।
तथा राज्ञा नियन्तव्याः प्रजास् तद्द् हि यमव्रतम् ॥ ३०७
                                    ॥
verses.english: As Yama at the appointed time subjects to his rule both friends and foes, even so all subjects must be controlled by the king; that is the office in which he resembles Yama.

verses.text:
वरुणेन यथा पाशैर् बद्ध एव-अभिदृश्यते ।
तथा पापान् निगृह्णीयाद् व्रतम् एतद्द् हि वारुणम् ॥ ३०८
                                    ॥
verses.english: As (a sinner) is seen bound with ropes by Varuna, even so let him punish the wicked; that is his office in which he resembles Varuna.

verses.text:
परिपूर्णं यथा चन्द्रं दृष्ट्वा हृष्यन्ति मानवाः ।
तथा प्रकृतयो यस्मिन् स चान्द्रव्रतिको नृपः ॥ ३०९
                                    ॥
verses.english: He is a king, taking upon himself the office of the Moon, whose (appearance) his subjects (greet with as great joy) as men feel on seeing the full moon.

verses.text:
प्रतापयुक्तस् तेजस्वी नित्यं स्यात् पापकर्मसु ।
दुष्टसामन्तहिंस्रश् च तद् आग्नेयं व्रतं स्मृतम् ॥ ३१०
                                    ॥
verses.english: (If) he is ardent in wrath against criminals and endowed with brilliant energy, and destroys wicked vassals, then his character is said (to resemble) that of Fire.

verses.text:
यथा सर्वाणि भूतानि धरा धारयते समम् ।
तथा सर्वाणि भूतानि बिभ्रतः पार्थिवं व्रतम् ॥ ३११
                                    ॥
verses.english: As the Earth supports all created beings equally, thus (a king) who supports all his subjects, (takes upon himself) the office of the Earth.

verses.text:
एतैर् उपायैर् अन्यैश् च युक्तो नित्यम् अतन्द्रितः ।
स्तेनान् राजा निगृह्णीयात् स्वराष्ट्रे पर एव च ॥ ३१२
                                    ॥
verses.english: Employing these and other means, the king shall, ever untired, restrain thieves both in his own dominions and in (those of) others.

verses.text:
पराम् अप्य् आपदं प्राप्तो ब्राह्मणान् न प्रकोपयेत् ।
ते ह्य् एनं कुपिता हन्युः सद्यः स.बल.वाहनम् ॥ ३१३
                                    ॥
verses.english: Let him not, though fallen into the deepest distress, provoke Brahmanas to anger; for they, when angered, could instantly destroy him together with his army and his vehicles.

verses.text:
यैः कृतः सर्वभक्ष्यो ऽग्निर् अपेयश् च महोदधिः ।
                                        ९.३१४अव्/
                                        म्: सर्वभक्षो
क्षयी च-आप्यायितः सोमः को न नश्येत् प्रकोप्य तान् ॥
                                    ३१४ ॥
verses.english: Who could escape destruction, when he provokes to anger those (men), by whom the fire was made to consume all things, by whom the (water of the) ocean was made undrinkable, and by whom the moon was made to wane and to increase again?

verses.text:
लोकान् अन्यान् सृजेयुर् ये लोकपालांश् च कोपिताः ।
देवान् कुर्युर् अदेवांश् च कः क्षिण्वंस् तान् समृध्नुयात् ॥
                                    ३१५ ॥
verses.english: Who could prosper, while he injures those (men) who provoked to anger, could create other worlds and other guardians of the world, and deprive the gods of their divine station?

verses.text:
यान् उपाश्रित्य तिष्ठन्ति लोका देवाश् च सर्वदा ।
ब्रह्म च-एव धनं येषां को हिंस्यात् ताञ् जिजीविषुः ॥
                                    ३१६ ॥
verses.english: What man, desirous of life, would injure them to whose support the (three) worlds and the gods ever owe their existence, and whose wealth is the Veda?

verses.text:
अ.विद्वांश् च-एव विद्वांश् च ब्राह्मणो दैवतं महत्
                                    ।
प्रणीतश् च-अ.प्रणीतश् च यथा-अग्निर् दैवतं महत् ॥
                                    ३१७ ॥
verses.english: A Brahmana, be he ignorant or learned, is a great divinity, just as the fire, whether carried forth (for the performance of a burnt-oblation) or not carried forth, is a great divinity.

verses.text:
श्मशानेष्व् अपि तेजस्वी पावको न-एव दुष्यति ।
हूयमानश् च यज्ञेषु भूय एव-अभिवर्धते ॥ ३१८
                                    ॥
verses.english: The brilliant fire is not contaminated even in burial-places, and, when presented with oblations (of butter) at sacrifices, it again increases mightily.

verses.text:
एवं यद्य् अप्य् अनिष्टेषु वर्तन्ते सर्वकर्मसु ।
सर्वथा ब्राह्मणाः पूज्याः परमं दैवतम् हि तत् ॥ ३१९
                                    ॥
verses.english: Thus, though Brahmanas employ themselves in all (sorts of) mean occupations, they must be honoured in every way; for (each of) them is a very great deity.

verses.text:
क्षत्रस्य-अतिप्रवृद्धस्य ब्राह्मणान् प्रति सर्वशः ।
ब्रह्म-एव सन्नियन्तृ स्यात् क्षत्रं हि ब्रह्म.सम्भवम्
                                    ॥ ३२० ॥
verses.english: When the Kshatriyas become in any way overbearing towards the Brahmanas, the Brahmanas themselves shall duly restrain them; for the Kshatriyas sprang from the Brahmanas.

verses.text:
अद्भ्यो ऽग्निर् ब्रह्मतः क्षत्रम् अश्मनो लोहम् उत्थितम्
                                    ।
तेषां सर्वत्रगं तेजः स्वासु योनिषु शाम्यति ॥ ३२१
                                    ॥
verses.english: Fire sprang from water, Kshatriyas from Brahmanas, iron from stone; the all-penetrating force of those (three) has no effect on that whence they were produced.

verses.text:
न-अ.ब्रह्म क्षत्रम् ऋध्नोति न-अ.क्षत्रं ब्रह्म वर्धते
                                    ।
ब्रह्म क्षत्रं च सम्पृक्तम् इह च-अमुत्र वर्धते ॥
                                    ३२२ ॥
verses.english: Kshatriyas prosper not without Brahmanas, Brahmanas prosper not without Kshatriyas; Brahmanas and Kshatriyas, being closely united, prosper in this (world) and in the next.

verses.text:
दत्त्वा धनं तु विप्रेभ्यः सर्वदण्डसमुत्थितम् ।
पुत्रे राज्यं समासृज्य कुर्वीत प्रायणं रणे ॥ ३२३ ॥
                                        ९.३२३च्व्/
                                        म्: समासाद्य ॥ 9.323 ॥
verses.english: But (a king who feels his end drawing nigh) shall bestow all his wealth, accumulated from fines, on Brahmanas, make over his kingdom to his son, and then seek death in battle.

verses.text:
एवं चरन् सदा युक्तो राजधर्मेषु पार्थिवः ।
हितेषु च-एव लोकस्य सर्वान् भृत्यान् नियोजयेत् ॥ ३२४ ॥
                                    ९.३२४च्व्/ म्: 
                                    हितेषु च-एव लोकेभ्यः ॥ 9.324 ॥
verses.english: Thus conducting himself (and) ever intent on (discharging) his royal duties, a king shall order all his servants (to work) for the good of his people.

verses.text:
एषो ऽ.खिलः कर्मविधिर् उक्तो राज्ञः सनातनः ।
इमं कर्मविधिं विद्यात् क्रमशो वैश्य.शूद्रयोः ॥ ३२५
                                ॥
verses.english: Thus the eternal law concerning the duties of a king has been fully declared; know that the following rules apply in (due) order to the duties of Vaisyas and Sudras.

verses.text:
वैश्यस् तु कृत.संस्कारः कृत्वा दारपरिग्रहम् ।
वार्तायां नित्ययुक्तः स्यात् पशूनां च-एव रक्षणे ॥ ३२६
                                ॥
verses.english: After a Vaisya has received the sacraments and has taken a wife, he shall be always attentive to the business whereby he may subsist and to (that of) tending cattle.

verses.text:
प्रजापतिर् हि वैश्याय सृष्ट्वा परिददे पशून् ।
ब्राह्मणाय च राज्ञे च सर्वाः परिददे प्रजाः ॥ ३२७ ॥
verses.english: For when the Lord of creatures (Pragapati) created cattle, he made them over to the Vaisya; to the Brahmana, and to the king he entrusted all created beings.

verses.text:
न च वैश्यस्य कामः स्यान् न रक्षेयं पशून् इति ।
वैश्ये च-इच्छति न-अन्येन रक्षितव्याः कथं चन ॥ ३२८
                                ॥
verses.english: A Vaisya must never (conceive this) wish, I will not keep cattle; and if a Vaisya is willing (to keep them), they must never be kept by (men of) other (castes).

verses.text:
मणि.मुक्ता.प्रवालानां लोहानां तान्तवस्य च ।
गन्धानां च रसानां च विद्याद् अर्घ.बल.अबलम् ॥ ३२९
                                ॥
verses.english: (A Vaisya) must know the respective value of gems, of pearls, of coral, of metals, of (cloth) made of thread, of perfumes, and of condiments.

verses.text:
बीजानाम् उप्तिविद्-च स्यात् क्षेत्रदोष.गुणस्य च ।
मानयोगं च जानीयात् तुलायोगांश् च सर्वशः ॥ ३३० ॥
verses.english: He must be acquainted with the (manner of) sowing of seeds, and of the good and bad qualities of fields, and he must perfectly know all measures and weights.

verses.text:
सार.असारं च भाण्डानां देशानां च गुण.अगुणान् ।
लाभ.अलाभं च पण्यानां पशूनां परिवर्धनम् ॥ ३३१
                                ॥
verses.english: Moreover, the excellence and defects of commodities, the advantages and disadvantages of (different) countries, the (probable) profit and loss on merchandise, and the means of properly rearing cattle.

verses.text:
भृत्यानां च भृतिं विद्याद् भाषाश् च विविधा नृणां ।
द्रव्याणां स्थान.योगांश् च क्रय.विक्रयम् एव च ॥ ३३२
                                ॥
verses.english: He must be acquainted with the (proper), wages of servants, with the various languages of men, with the manner of keeping goods, and (the rules of) purchase and sale.

verses.text:
धर्मेण च द्रव्यवृद्धाव् आतिष्ठेद् यत्नम् उत्तमम् ।
दद्याच् च सर्वभूतानाम् अन्नम् एव प्रयत्नतः ॥ ३३३ ॥
verses.english: Let him exert himself to the utmost in order to increase his property in a righteous manner, and let him zealously give food to all created beings.

verses.text:
विप्राणां वेदविदुषां गृहस्थानां यशस्विनाम् ।
शुश्रूषा-एव तु शूद्रस्य धर्मो नैश्रेयसः परः ॥ ३३४ ॥
                                    ९.३३४च्व्/ क्:
                                    परम् ॥ 9.334 ॥
verses.english: But to serve Brahmanas (who are) learned in the Vedas, householders, and famous (for virtue) is the highest duty of a Sudra, which leads to beatitude.

verses.text:
शुचिर् उत्कृष्टशुश्रूषुर् मृदु.वाग् अन्.अहङ्कृतः ।
ब्राह्मणादि.आश्रयो नित्यम् उत्कृष्टां जातिम् अश्नुते ॥ ३३५ ॥
                                    ९.३३५च्व्/ म्: 
                                    ब्राह्मण.अपाश्रयो ॥ 9.335 ॥
verses.english: (A Sudra who is) pure, the servant of his betters, gentle in his speech, and free from pride, and always seeks a refuge with Brahmanas, attains (in his next life) a higher caste.

verses.text:
एषो ऽनापदि वर्णानाम् उक्तः कर्मविधिः शुभः ।
आपद्य् अपि हि यस् तेषां क्रमशस् तन् निबोधत ॥ ३३६ ॥
verses.english: The excellent law for the conduct of the (four) castes (varna), (when they are) not in distress, has been thus promulgated; now hear in order their (several duties) in times of distress.

verses.text:
अधीयीरंस् त्रयो वर्णाः स्वकर्मस्था द्विजातयः ।
प्रब्रूयाद् ब्राह्मणस् त्व् एषां न-इतराव् इति निश्चयः ॥ १
                                    ॥
verses.english: Let the three twice-born castes (varna), discharging their (prescribed) duties, study (the Veda); but among them the Brahmana (alone) shall teach it, not the other two; that is an established rule.

verses.text:
सर्वेषां ब्राह्मणो विद्याद् वृत्त्युपायान् यथाविधि ।
प्रब्रूयाद् इतरेभ्यश् च स्वयं च-एव तथा भवेत् ॥ २
                                    ॥
verses.english: The Brahmana must know the means of subsistence (prescribed) by law for all, instruct the others, and himself live according to (the law)

verses.text:
वैशेष्यात् प्रकृतिश्रैष्ठ्यात्-नियमस्य च धारणात् ।
संस्कारस्य विशेषाच् च वर्णानां ब्राह्मणः प्रभुः ॥ ३
                                    ॥
verses.english: On account of his pre-eminence, on account of the superiority of his origin, on account of his observance of (particular) restrictive rules, and on account of his particular sanctification the Brahmana is the lord of (all) castes (varna).

verses.text:
ब्राह्मणः क्षत्रियो वैश्यस् त्रयो वर्णा द्विजातयः ।
चतुर्थ एकजातिस् तु शूद्रो न-अस्ति तु पञ्चमः ॥ ४
                                    ॥
verses.english: Brahmana, the Kshatriya, and the Vaisya castes (varna) are the twice-born ones, but the fourth, the Sudra, has one birth only; there is no fifth (caste).

verses.text:
सर्ववर्णेषु तुल्यासु पत्नीष्व् अक्षत.योनिषु ।
आनुलोम्येन सम्भूता जात्या ज्ञेयास् त एव ते ॥ ५ ॥
verses.english: In all castes (varna) those (children) only which are begotten in the direct order on wedded wives, equal (in caste and married as) virgins, are to be considered as belonging to the same caste (as their fathers)

verses.text:
स्त्रीष्व् अनन्तरजातासु द्विजैर् उत्पादितान् सुतान् ।
सदृशान् एव तान् आहुर् मातृदोषविगर्हितान् ॥ ६ ॥
verses.english: Sons, begotten by twice-born man on wives of the next lower castes, they declare to be similar (to their fathers, but) blamed on account of the fault (inherent) in their mothers.

verses.text:
अनन्तरासु जातानां विधिर् एष सनातनः ।
द्वि.एकान्तरासु जातानां धर्म्यं विद्याद् इमं विधिम् ॥ ७
                                    ॥
verses.english: Such is the eternal law concerning (children) born of wives one degree lower (than their husbands); know (that) the following rule (is applicable) to those born of women two or three degrees lower.

verses.text:
ब्राह्मणाद् वैश्यकन्यायाम् अम्बष्ठो नाम जायते ।
निषादः शूद्रकन्यायां यः पारशव उच्यते ॥ ८ ॥
verses.english: From a Brahmana a with the daughter of a Vaisya is born (a son) called an Ambashtha, with the daughter of a sudra a Nishada, who is also called Parasava.

verses.text:
क्षत्रियात्-शूद्रकन्यायां क्रूराचारविहारवान् ।
क्षत्र.शूद्र.वपुर् जन्तुर् उग्रो नाम प्रजायते ॥ ९
                                    ॥
verses.english: From a Kshatriya and the daughter of a Sudra springs a being, called Ugra, resembling both a Kshatriya and a Sudra, ferocious in his manners, and delighting in cruelty.

verses.text:
विप्रस्य त्रिषु वर्णेषु नृपतेर् वर्णयोर् द्वयोः ।
वैश्यस्य वर्णे च-एकस्मिन् षड् एते ऽपसदाः स्मृताः ॥ १०
                                    ॥
verses.english: Children of a Brahmana by (women of) the three (lower) castes, of a Kshatriya by (wives of) the two (lower) castes, and of a Vaisya by (a wife of) the one caste (below him) are all six called base-born (apasada).

verses.text:
क्षत्रियाद् विप्रकन्यायां सूतो भवति जातितः ।
वैश्यान् मागध.वैदेहौ राज.विप्र.अङ्गनासुतौ ॥ ११
                                    ॥
verses.english: From a Kshatriya by the daughter of a Brahmana is born (a son called) according to his caste (gati) a Suta; from a Vaisya by females of the royal and the Brahmana (castes) spring a Magadha and a Vaideha.

verses.text:
शूद्राद् आयोगवः क्षत्ता चण्डालश् च-अधमो नृणाम् ।
वैश्य.राजन्य.विप्रासु जायन्ते वर्णसङ्कराः ॥ १२
                                    ॥
verses.english: From a Sudra are born an Ayogava, a Kshattri, and a Kandala, the lowest of men, by Vaisya, Kshatriya, and Brahmana) females, (sons who owe their origin to) a confusion of the castes.

verses.text:
एकान्तरे त्व् आनुलोम्याद् अम्बष्ठ.उग्रौ यथा स्मृतौ ।
क्षत्तृ.वैदेहकौ तद्वत् प्रातिलोम्ये ऽपि जन्मनि ॥ १३
                                    ॥
verses.english: As an Ambashtha and an Ugra, (begotten) in the direct order on (women) one degree lower (than their husbands) are declared (to be), even so are a Kshattri and a Vaidehaka, though they were born in the inverse order of the castes (from mothers one degree higher than the fathers).

verses.text:
पुत्रा ये ऽनन्तरस्त्रीजाः क्रमेण-उक्ता द्विजन्मनाम् ।
तान् अनन्तर.नाम्नस् तु मातृदोषात् प्रचक्षते ॥ १४ ॥
verses.english: Those sons of the twice-born, begotten on wives of the next lower castes, who have been enumerated in due order, they call by the name Anantaras (belonging to the next lower caste), on account of the blemish (inherent) in their mothers.

verses.text:
ब्राह्मणाद् उग्रकन्यायाम् आवृतो नाम जायते ।
आभीरो ऽम्बष्ठकन्यायाम् आयोगव्यां तु धिग्वणः ॥ १५
                                    ॥
verses.english: A Brahmana begets on the daughter of an Ugra an Avrita, on the daughter of an Ambashtha an Abhira, but on a female of the Ayogava (caste) a Dhigvana.

verses.text:
आयोगवश् च क्षत्ता च चण्डालश् च-अधमो नृणाम् ।
प्रातिलोम्येन जायन्ते शूद्राद् अपसदास् त्रयः ॥ १६ ॥
verses.english: From a Sudra spring in the inverse order (by females of the higher castes) three base-born (sons, apasada), an Ayogava, a Kshattri, and a Kandala, the lowest of men;

verses.text:
वैश्यान् मागध.वैदेहौ क्षत्रियात् सूत एव तु ।
प्रतीपम् एते जायन्ते परे ऽप्य् अपसदास् त्रयः ॥ १७
                                    ॥
verses.english: From a Vaisya are born in the inverse order of the castes a Magadha and a Vaideha, but from a Kshatriya a Suta only; these are three other base-born ones (apasada).

verses.text:
जातो निषादात्-शूद्रायां जात्या भवति पुक्कसः ।
शूद्राज् जातो निषाद्यां तु स वै कुक्कुटकः स्मृतः ॥ १८
                                    ॥
verses.english: The son of a Nishada by a Sudra female becomes a Pukkasa by caste (gati), but the son of a Sudra by a Nishada female is declared to be a Kukkutaka.

verses.text:
क्षत्तुर् जातस् तथा-उग्रायां श्वपाक इति कीर्त्यते ।
वैदेहकेन त्व् अम्बष्ठ्याम् उत्पन्नो वेण उच्यते ॥ १९
                                    ॥
verses.english: Moreover, the son of by Kshattri by an Ugra female is called a Svapaka; but one begotten by a Vaidehaka on an Ambashtha female is named a Vena.

verses.text:
द्विजातयः सवर्णासु जनयन्त्य् अ.व्रतांस् तु यान् ।
तान् सावित्रीपरिभ्रष्टान् व्रात्यान् इति विनिर्दिशेत् ॥ २०
                                    ॥
verses.english: Those (sons) whom the twice-born beget on wives of equal caste, but who, not fulfilling their sacred duties, are excluded from the Savitri, one must designate by the appellation Vratyas.

verses.text:
व्रात्यात् तु जायते विप्रात् पाप.आत्मा भूर्जकण्टकः। १०.२१अव्/ म्: 
                                        भृज्जकण्टकः
आवन्त्य.वाटधानौ च पुष्पधः शैख एव च ॥ २१
                                    ॥
verses.english: But from a Vratya (of the) Brahmana (caste) spring the wicked Bhriggakantaka, the Avantya, the Vatadhana, the Pushpadha, and the Saikha.

verses.text:
झल्लो मल्लश् च राजन्याद् व्रात्यात्-निच्छिविर् एव च ।
                                        १०.२२अव्/
                                        म्: व्रात्यात्-लिच्छविर् एव च
नटश् च करणश् च-एव खसो द्रविड एव च ॥ २२
                                    ॥
verses.english: From a Vratya (of the) Kshatriya (caste), the Ghalla, the Malla, the Likkhivi, the Nata, the Karana, the Khasa, and the Dravida.

verses.text:
वैश्यात् तु जायते व्रात्यात् सुधन्वा-आचार्य एव च ।
कारुषश् च विजन्मा च मैत्रः सात्वत एव च ॥ २३
                                    ॥
verses.english: From a Vratya (of the) Vaisya (caste) are born a Sudhanvan, an Akarya, a Karusha, a Viganman, a Maitra, and a Satvata.

verses.text:
व्यभिचारेण वर्णानाम् अवेद्यावेदनेन च ।
स्वकर्मणां च त्यागेन जायन्ते वर्णसङ्कराः ॥ २४
                                    ॥
verses.english: By adultery (committed by persons) of (different) castes, by marriages with women who ought not to be married, and by the neglect of the duties and occupations (prescribed) to each, are produced (sons who owe their origin) to a confusion the castes.

verses.text:
सङ्कीर्ण.योनयो ये तु प्रतिलोम.अनुलोम.जाः ।
अन्योन्यव्यतिषक्ताश् च तान् प्रवक्ष्याम्य् अशेषतः ॥ २५
                                    ॥
verses.english: I will (now) fully enumerate those (sons) of mixed origin, who are born of Anulomas and of Pratilomas, and (thus) are mutually connected.

verses.text:
सूतो वैदेहकश् च-एव चण्डालश् च नराधमः ।
मागधः तथा-आयोगव एव च क्षत्रजातिश् च ॥ २६ ॥
                                        १०.२६च्व्/
                                        म्: क्षत्तृजातिश् च ॥ 10.26 ॥
verses.english: The Suta, the Vaidehaka, the Kandala, that lowest of mortals, the Magadha, he of the Kshattri caste (gati), and the Ayogava,

verses.text:
एते षट् सदृशान् वर्णाञ् जनयन्ति स्वयोनिषु ।
मातृजात्यां प्रसूयन्ते प्रवारासु च योनिषु ॥ २७ ॥ १०.२७च्व्/ म्: 
                                        मातृजात्याः ॥ 10.27 ॥
verses.english: These six (Pratilomas) beget similar races (varna) on women of their own (caste), they (also) produce (the like) with females of their mother's caste (gati), and with females (of) higher ones.

verses.text:
यथा त्रयाणां वर्णानां द्वयोर् आत्मा-अस्य जायते ।
आनन्तर्यात् स्वयोन्यां तु तथा बाह्येष्व् अपि क्रमात् ॥ २८
                                    ॥ १०.२८च्व्/
                                        म्: क्रमः ॥ 10.28 ॥
verses.english: As a (Brahmana) begets on (females of) two out of the three (twice-born castes a son similar to) himself, (but inferior) on account of the lower degree (of the mother), and (one equal to himself) on a female of his own race, even so is the order in the case of the excluded (races, vahya).

verses.text:
ते च-अपि बाह्यान् सुबहूंस् ततो ऽप्य् अधिकदूषितान् ।
परस्परस्य दारेषु जनयन्ति विगर्हितान् ॥ २९ ॥
verses.english: Those (six mentioned above) also beget, the one on the females of the other, a great many (kinds of) despicable (sons), even more sinful than their (fathers), and excluded (from the Aryan community, vahya).

verses.text:
यथा-एव शूद्रो ब्राह्मण्यां बाह्यं जन्तुं प्रसूयते ।
तथा बाह्यतरं बाह्यश् चातुर्वर्ण्ये प्रसूयते ॥ ३०
                                    ॥
verses.english: Just as a Sudra begets on a Brahmana female a being excluded (from the Aryan community), even so (a person himself) excluded pro creates with (females of) the four castes (varna, sons) more (worthy of being) excluded (than he himself).

verses.text:
प्रतिकूलं वर्तमाना बाह्या बाह्यतरान् पुनः ।
हीना हीनान् प्रसूयन्ते वर्णान् पञ्चदश-एव तु ॥ ३१
                                    ॥
verses.english: But men excluded (by the Aryans, vahya), who approach females of higher rank, beget races (varna) still more worthy to be excluded, low men (hina) still lower races, even fifteen (in number).

verses.text:
प्रसाधन.उपचारज्ञम् अदासं दासजीवनम् । १०.३२अव्/ म्: 
                                        दास्यजीविनम्
सैरिन्ध्रं वागुरा.वृत्तिं सूते दस्युर् अयोगवे ॥ ३२ ॥
                                        १०.३२च्व्/
                                        म्: सैरन्ध्रं ॥ 10.32 ॥
verses.english: A Dasyu begets on an Ayogava (woman) a Sairandhra, who is skilled in adorning and attending (his master), who, (though) not a slave, lives like a slave, (or) subsists by snaring (animals).

verses.text:
मैत्रेयकं तु वैदेहो माधूकं सम्प्रसूयते ।
नॄन् प्रशंसत्य् अजस्रं यो घण्टाताडो ऽरुण.उदये ॥ ३३
                                    ॥
verses.english: A Vaideha produces (with the same) a sweet-voiced Maitreyaka, who, ringing a bell at the appearance of dawn, continually. praises (great) men.

verses.text:
निषादो मार्गवं सूते दासं नौकर्मजीविनम् ।
कैवर्तम् इति यं प्राहुर् आर्यावर्तनिवासिनः ॥ ३४ ॥
verses.english: A Nishada begets (on the same) a Margava (or) Dasa, who subsists by working as a boatman, (and) whom the inhabitants of Aryavarta call a Kaivarta.

verses.text:
मृतवस्त्रभृत्स्व् नारीषु गर्हित.अन्न.अशनासु च । १०.३५अव्/ म्: 
                                        अनार्याषु
भवन्त्य् आयोगवीष्व् एते जातिहीनाः पृथक् त्रयः ॥ ३५
                                    ॥
verses.english: Those three base-born ones are severally begot on Ayogava women, who wear the clothes of the dead, are wicked, and eat reprehensible food.

verses.text:
कारावरो निषादात् तु चर्मकारः प्रसूयते । १०.३६अव्/ म्: 
                                        चर्मकारं
वैदेहिकाद् अन्ध्र.मेदौ बहिर्ग्राम.प्रतिश्रयौ ॥ ३६
                                    ॥
verses.english: From a Nishada springs (by a woman of the Vaideha caste) a Karavara, who works in leather; and from a Vaidehaka (by women of the Karavara and Nishada castes), an Andhra and a Meda, who dwell outside the village.

verses.text:
चण्डालात् पाण्डुसोपाकस् त्वक्सारव्यवहारवान् ।
आहिण्डिको निषादेन वैदेह्याम् एव जायते ॥ ३७ ॥
verses.english: From a Kandala by a Vaideha woman is born a Pandusopaka, who deals in cane; from a Nishada (by the same) an Ahindika.

verses.text:
चण्डालेन तु सोपाको मूलव्यसनवृत्तिमान् ।
पुक्कस्यां जायते पापः सदा सज्जनगर्हितः ॥ ३८ ॥
                                        १०.३८च्व्/
                                        म्: पुल्कस्यां ॥ 10.38 ॥
verses.english: But from a Kandala by a Pukkasa woman is born the sinful Sopaka, who lives by the occupations of his sire, and is ever despised by good men.

verses.text:
निषादस्त्री तु चण्डालात् पुत्रम् अन्त्यावसायिनम् ।
श्मशान.गोचरं सूते बाह्यानाम् अपि गर्हितम् ॥ ३९ ॥
verses.english: A Nishada woman bears to a Kandala a son (called) Antyavasayin, employed in burial-grounds, and despised even by those excluded (from the Aryan community).

verses.text:
सङ्करे जातयस् त्व् एताः पितृ.मातृ.प्रदर्शिताः ।
प्रछन्ना वा प्रकाशा वा वेदितव्याः स्वकर्मभिः ॥ ४०
                                    ॥
verses.english: These races, (which originate) in a confusion (of the castes and) have been described according to their fathers and mothers, may be known by their occupations, whether they conceal or openly show themselves.

verses.text:
स्वजातिज.अनन्तरजाः षट् सुता द्विजधर्मिणः ।
शूद्राणां तु स.धर्माणः सर्वे ऽपध्वंसजाः स्मृताः ॥
                                    ४१ ॥
verses.english: Six sons, begotten (by Aryans) on women of equal and the next lower castes (Anantara), have the duties of twice-born men; but all those born in consequence of a violation (of the law) are, as regards their duties, equal to Sudras.

verses.text:
तपो.बीज.प्रभावैस् तु ते गच्छन्ति युगे युगे ।
उत्कर्षं च-अपकर्षं च मनुष्येष्व् इह जन्मतः ॥ ४२
                                    ॥
verses.english: By the power of austerities and of the seed (from which they sprang), these (races) obtain here among men more exalted or lower rank in successive births.

verses.text:
शनकैस् तु क्रियालोपाद् इमाः क्षत्रिय.जातयः ।
वृषलत्वं गता लोके ब्राह्मणादर्शनेन च ॥ ४३ ॥ १०.४३च्व्/ म्: 
                                        ब्राह्मणातिक्रमेण च ॥ 10.43 ॥
verses.english: But in consequence of the omission of the sacred rites, and of their not consulting Brahmanas, the following tribes of Kshatriyas have gradually sunk in this world to the condition of Sudras;

verses.text:
पौण्ड्रकाश् चौड्र.द्रविडाः काम्बोजा यवनाः शकाः । १०.४४अव्/ म्: 
                                        पुण्ड्रकाश् चोड.द्रविडाः
पारदा.पह्लवाश् चीनाः किराता दरदाः खशाः ॥ ४४ ॥
verses.english: (Viz.) the Paundrakas, the Kodas, the Dravidas, the Kambogas, the Yavanas, the Sakas, the Paradas, the Pahlavas, the Kinas, the Kiratas, and the Daradas.

verses.text:
मुख.बाहु.ऊरु.पद्.जानां या लोके जातयो बहिः ।
म्लेच्छ.वाचश् च-आर्य.वाचः सर्वे ते दस्यवः स्मृताः ॥
                                    ४५ ॥
verses.english: All those tribes in this world, which are excluded from (the community of) those born from the mouth, the arms, the thighs, and the feet (of Brahman), are called Dasyus, whether they speak the language of the Mlekkhas (barbarians) or that of the Aryans.

verses.text:
ये द्विजानाम् अपसदा ये च-अपध्वंसजाः स्मृताः ।
ते निन्दितैर् वर्तयेयुर् द्विजानाम् एव कर्मभिः ॥ ४६
                                    ॥
verses.english: Those who have been mentioned as the base-born (offspring, apasada) of Aryans, or as produced in consequence of a violation (of the law, apadhvamsaga), shall subsist by occupations reprehended by the twice-born.

verses.text:
सूतानाम् अश्व.सारथ्यम् अम्बष्ठानां चिकित्सनम् ।
वैदेहकानां स्त्रीकार्यं मागधानां वणिक्पथः ॥ ४७
                                    ॥
verses.english: To Sutas (belongs) the management of horses and of chariots; to Ambashthas, the art of healing; to Vaidehakas, the service of women; to Magadhas, trade;

verses.text:
मत्स्यघातो निषादानां त्वष्टिस् त्व् आयोगवस्य च ।
मेद.अन्ध्र.चुञ्चु.मद्गूनाम् आरण्यपशुहिंसनम् ॥ ४८
                                    ॥
verses.english: Killing fish to Nishadas; carpenters' work to the Ayogava; to Medas, Andhras, Kunkus, and Madgus, the slaughter of wild animals;

verses.text:
क्षत्तृ.उग्र.पुक्कसानां तु बिलौकोवध.बन्धनम् ।
धिग्वणानां चर्मकार्यं वेणानां भाण्डवादनम् ॥ ४९
                                    ॥
verses.english: To Kshattris, Ugras, and Pukkasas, catching and killing (animals) living in holes; to Dhigvanas, working in leather; to Venas, playing drums.

verses.text:
चैत्यद्रुम.श्मशानेषु शैलेषु-उपवनेषु च ।
वसेयुर् एते विज्ञाता वर्तयन्तः स्वकर्मभिः ॥ ५०
                                    ॥
verses.english: Near well-known trees and burial-grounds, on mountains and in groves, let these (tribes) dwell, known (by certain marks), and subsisting by their peculiar occupations.

verses.text:
चण्डाल.श्वपचानां तु बहिर् ग्रामात् प्रतिश्रयः ।
अपपात्राश् च कर्तव्या धनम् एषां श्व.गर्दभम् ॥ ५१
                                    ॥
verses.english: But the dwellings of Kandalas and Svapakas shall be outside the village, they must be made Apapatras, and their wealth (shall be) dogs and donkeys.

verses.text:
वासांसि मृतचैलानि भिन्नभाण्डेषु भोजनम् ।
कार्ष्णायसम् अलङ्कारः परिव्रज्या च नित्यशः ॥ ५२
                                    ॥
verses.english: Their dress (shall be) the garments of the dead, (they shall eat) their food from broken dishes, black iron (shall be) their ornaments, and they must always wander from place to place.

verses.text:
न तैः समयम् अन्विच्छेत् पुरुषो धर्मम् आचरन् ।
व्यवहारो मिथस् तेषां विवाहः सदृशैः सह ॥ ५३
                                    ॥
verses.english: A man who fulfils a religious duty, shall not seek intercourse with them; their transactions (shall be) among themselves, and their marriages with their equals.

verses.text:
अन्नम् एषां पराधीनं देयं स्याद् भिन्नभाजने ।
रात्रौ न विचरेयुस् ते ग्रामेषु नगरेषु च ॥ ५४ ॥
verses.english: Their food shall be given to them by others (than an Aryan giver) in a broken dish; at night they shall not walk about in villages and in towns.

verses.text:
दिवा चरेयुः कार्यार्थं चिह्निता राजशासनैः ।
अ.बान्धवं शवं च-एव निर्हरेयुर् इति स्थितिः ॥ ५५
                                    ॥
verses.english: By day they may go about for the purpose of their work, distinguished by marks at the king's command, and they shall carry out the corpses (of persons) who have no relatives; that is a settled rule.

verses.text:
वध्यांश् च हन्युः सततं यथाशास्त्रं नृपाज्ञया ।
वध्यवासांसि गृह्णीयुः शय्याश् च-आभरणानि च ॥ ५६
                                    ॥
verses.english: By the king's order they shall always execute the criminals, in accordance with the law, and they shall take for themselves the clothes, the beds, and the ornaments of (such) criminals.

verses.text:
वर्णापेतम् अविज्ञातं नरं कलुषयोनिजम् ।
आर्य.रूपम् इव-अनार्यं कर्मभिः स्वैर् विभावयेत् ॥ ५७
                                    ॥
verses.english: A man of impure origin, who belongs not to any caste, (varna, but whose character is) not known, who, (though) not an Aryan, has the appearance of an Aryan, one may discover by his acts.

verses.text:
अनार्यता निष्ठुरता क्रूरता निष्क्रियात्मता ।
पुरुषं व्यञ्जयन्ति-इह लोके कलुषयोनिजम् ॥ ५८ ॥
verses.english: Behaviour unworthy of an Aryan, harshness, cruelty, and habitual neglect of the prescribed duties betray in this world a man of impure origin.

verses.text:
पित्र्यं वा भजते शीलं मातुर् वा-उभयम् एव वा ।
न कथं चन दुर्योनिः प्रकृतिं स्वां नियच्छति ॥ ५९
                                    ॥
verses.english: A base-born man either resembles in character his father, or his mother, or both; he can never conceal his real nature.

verses.text:
कुले मुख्ये ऽपि जातस्य यस्य स्याद् योनिसङ्करः ।
संश्रयत्य् एव तत्.शीलं नरो ऽल्पम् अपि वा बहु ॥ ६०
                                    ॥
verses.english: Even if a man, born in a great family, sprang from criminal intercourse, he will certainly possess the faults of his (father), be they small or great.

verses.text:
यत्र त्व् एते परिध्वंसाज् जायन्ते वर्णदूषकाः ।
राष्ट्रिकैः सह तद् राष्ट्रं क्षिप्रम् एव विनश्यति ॥ ६१
                                    ॥ १०.६१च्व्/
                                        म्: राष्ट्रियैः ॥ 10.61 ॥
verses.english: But that kingdom in which such bastards, sullying (the purity of) the castes, are born, perishes quickly together with its inhabitants.

verses.text:
ब्राह्मणार्थे गवार्थे वा देहत्यागो ऽन्.उपस्कृतः ।
स्त्री.बालाभ्युपपत्तौ च बाह्यानां सिद्धिकारणम् ॥ ६२ ॥
                                        १०.६२च्व्/
                                        म्: स्त्री.बालाभ्यवपत्तौ च ॥ 10.62 ॥
verses.english: Dying, without the expectation of a reward, for the sake of Brahmanas and of cows, or in the defence of women and children, secures beatitude to those excluded (from the Aryan community, vahya.)

verses.text:
अहिंसा सत्यम् अस्तेयं शौचम् इन्द्रियनिग्रहः ।
एतं सामासिकं धर्मं चातुर्वर्ण्ये ऽब्रवीन् मनुः ॥ ६३
                                    ॥
verses.english: Abstention from injuring (creatures), veracity, abstention from unlawfully appropriating (the goods of others), purity, and control of the organs, Manu has declared to be the summary of the law for the four castes.

verses.text:
शूद्रायां ब्राह्मणाज् जातः श्रेयसा चेत् प्रजायते ।
अश्रेयान् श्रेयसीं जातिं गच्छत्य् आ सप्तमाद् युगात् ॥ ६४
                                    ॥
verses.english: If (a female of the caste), sprung from a Brahmana and a Sudra female, bear (children) to one of the highest caste, the inferior (tribe) attains the highest caste within the seventh generation.

verses.text:
शूद्रो ब्राह्मणताम् एति ब्राह्मणश् च-एति शूद्रताम् ।
क्षत्रियाज् जातम् एवं तु विद्याद् वैश्यात् तथा-एव च ॥
                                    ६५ ॥
verses.english: (Thus) a Sudra attains the rank of a Brahmana, and (in a similar manner) a Brahmana sinks to the level of a Sudra; but know that it is the same with the offspring of a Kshatriya or of a Vaisya.

verses.text:
अनार्यायां समुत्पन्नो ब्राह्मणात् तु यदृच्छया ।
ब्राह्मण्याम् अप्य् अनार्यात् तु श्रेयस्त्वं क्व-इति चेद् भवेत्
                                    ॥ ६६ ॥ १०.६६च्व्/ म्: कस्य चिद् भवेत् ॥ 10.66 ॥
verses.english: If (a doubt) should arise, with whom the preeminence (is, whether) with him whom an Aryan by chance begot on a non-Aryan female, or (with the son) of a Brahmana woman by a non-Aryan,

verses.text:
जातो नार्याम् अनार्यायाम् आर्याद् आर्यो भवेद् गुणैः ।
जातो ऽप्य् अनार्याद् आर्यायाम् अनार्य इति निश्चयः ॥ ६७
                                    ॥
verses.english: The decision is as follows: 'He who was begotten by an Aryan on a non-Aryan female, may become (like to) an Aryan by his virtues; he whom an Aryan (mother) bore to a non-Aryan father (is and remains) unlike to an Aryan.'

verses.text:
ताव् उभाव् अप्य् असंस्कार्याव् इति धर्मो व्यवस्थितः ।
वैगुण्याज् जन्मनः पूर्व उत्तरः प्रतिलोमतः ॥ ६८ ॥
                                        १०.६८च्व्/
                                        म्: जन्मतः ॥ 10.68 ॥
verses.english: The law prescribes that neither of the two shall receive the sacraments, the first (being excluded) on account of the lowness of his origin, the second (because the union of his parents was) against the order of the castes.

verses.text:
सुबीजं च-एव सुक्षेत्रे जातं सम्पद्यते यथा ।
तथा-आर्याज् जात आर्यायां सर्वं संस्कारम् अर्हति ॥ ६९
                                    ॥
verses.english: As good seed, springing up in good soil, turns out perfectly well, even so the son of an Aryan by an Aryan woman is worthy of all the sacraments.

verses.text:
बीजम् एके प्रशंसन्ति क्षेत्रम् अन्ये मनीषिणः ।
बीज.क्षेत्रे तथा-एव-अन्ये तत्र-इयं तु व्यवस्थितिः ॥
                                    ७० ॥
verses.english: Some sages declare the seed to be more important, and others the field; again others (assert that) the seed and the field (are equally important); but the legal decision on this point is as follows:

verses.text:
अक्षेत्रे बीजम् उत्सृष्टम् अन्तरा-एव विनश्यति ।
अ.बीजकम् अपि क्षेत्रं केवलं स्थण्डिलं भवेत् ॥ ७१
                                    ॥
verses.english: Seed, sown on barren ground, perishes in it; a (fertile) field also, in which no (good) seed (is sown), will remain barren.

verses.text:
यस्माद् बीजप्रभावेण तिर्यग्जा ऋषयो ऽभवन् ।
पूजिताश् च प्रशस्ताश् च तस्माद् बीजं प्रशस्यते ॥ ७२ ॥
                                        १०.७२च्व्/
                                        म्: विशिष्यते ॥ 10.72 ॥
verses.english: As through the power of the seed (sons) born of animals became sages who are honoured and praised, hence the seed is declared to be more important.

verses.text:
अनार्यम् आर्य.कर्माणम् आर्यं च-अनार्यकर्मिणम् ।
सम्प्रधार्य-अब्रवीद् धाता न समौ न-असमाव् इति ॥ ७३
                                    ॥
verses.english: Having considered (the case of) a non-Aryan who acts like an Aryan, and (that of) an Aryan who acts like a non-Aryan, the creator declared, 'Those two are neither equal nor unequal.'

verses.text:
ब्राह्मणा ब्रह्मयोनिस्था ये स्वकर्मण्य् अवस्थिताः ।
ते सम्यग् उपजीवेयुः षट् कर्माणि यथाक्रमम् ॥ ७४ ॥
verses.english: Brahmanas who are intent on the means (of gaining union with) Brahman and firm in (discharging) their duties, shall live by duly performing the following six acts, (which are enumerated) in their (proper) order.

verses.text:
अध्यापनम् अध्ययनं यजनं याजनं तथा ।
दानं प्रतिग्रहश् च-एव षट् कर्माण्य् अग्रजन्मनः ॥ ७५
                                ॥
verses.english: Teaching, studying, sacrificing for himself, sacrificing for others, making gifts and receiving them are the six acts (prescribed) for a Brahmana.

verses.text:
षण्णां तु कर्मणाम् अस्य त्रीणि कर्माणि जीविका ।
याजन.अध्यापने च-एव विशुद्धाच् च प्रतिग्रहः ॥ ७६
                                ॥
verses.english: But among the six acts (ordained) for him three are his means of subsistence, (viz.) sacrificing for others, teaching, and accepting gifts from pure men.

verses.text:
त्रयो धर्मा निवर्तन्ते ब्राह्मणात् क्षत्रियं प्रति ।
अध्यापनं याजनं च तृतीयश् च प्रतिग्रहः ॥ ७७ ॥
verses.english: (Passing) from the Brahmana to the Kshatriya, three acts (incumbent on the former) are forbidden, (viz.) teaching, sacrificing for others, and, thirdly, the acceptance of gifts.

verses.text:
वैश्यं प्रति तथा-एव-एते निवर्तेरन्न् इति स्थितिः ।
न तौ प्रति हि तान् धर्मान् मनुर् आह प्रजापतिः ॥ ७८ ॥
                                    १०.७८च्व्/ म्: 
                                    प्रति हितान् धर्मान् ॥ 10.78 ॥
verses.english: The same are likewise forbidden to a Vaisya, that is a settled rule; for Manu, the lord of creatures (Pragapati), has not prescribed them for (men of) those two (castes).

verses.text:
शस्त्र.अस्त्रभृत्त्वं क्षत्रस्य वणिक्.पशु.कृषिर् विषः ।
आजीवनार्थं धर्मस् तु दानम् अध्ययनं यजिः ॥ ७९ ॥
verses.english: To carry arms for striking and for throwing (is prescribed) for Kshatriyas as a means of subsistence; to trade, (to rear) cattle, and agriculture for Vaisyas; but their duties are liberality, the study of the Veda, and the performance of sacrifices.

verses.text:
वेदाभ्यासो ब्राह्मणस्य क्षत्रियस्य च रक्षणम् ।
वार्ताकर्म-एव वैश्यस्य विशिष्टानि स्वकर्मसु ॥ ८० ॥
verses.english: Among the several occupations the most commendable are, teaching the Veda for a Brahmana, protecting (the people) for a Kshatriya, and trade for a Vaisya.

verses.text:
अ.जीवंस् तु यथा.उक्तेन ब्राह्मणः स्वेन कर्मणा ।
जीवेत् क्षत्रियधर्मेण स ह्य् अस्य प्रत्य् अनन्तरः ॥ ८१
                                    ॥
verses.english: But a Brahmana, unable to subsist by his peculiar occupations just mentioned, may live according to the law applicable to Kshatriyas; for the latter is next to him in rank.

verses.text:
उभाभ्याम् अप्य् अ.जीवंस् तु कथं स्याद् इति चेद् भवेत्
                                    ।
कृषि.गोरक्षम् आस्थाय जीवेद् वैश्यस्य जीविकाम् ॥ ८२
                                    ॥
verses.english: If it be asked, 'How shall it be, if he cannot maintain himself by either (of these occupations?' the answer is), he may adopt a Vaisya's mode of life, employing himself in agriculture and rearing cattle.

verses.text:
वैश्यवृत्त्या-अपि जीवंस् तु ब्राह्मणः क्सत्रियो ऽपि वा
                                    ।
हिंसा.प्रायां पराधीनां कृषिं यत्नेन वर्जयेत् ॥ ८३
                                    ॥
verses.english: But a Brahmana, or a Kshatriya, living by a Vaisya's mode of subsistence, shall carefully avoid (the pursuit of) agriculture, (which causes) injury to many beings and depends on others.

verses.text:
कृषिं साधु-इति मन्यन्ते सा वृत्तिः सद्विगर्हिताः ।
भूमिं भूमिशयांश् च-एव हन्ति काष्ठम् अयो.मुखम् ॥ ८४
                                    ॥
verses.english: (Some) declare that agriculture is something excellent, (but) that means of subsistence is blamed by the virtuous; (for) the wooden (implement) with iron point injuries the earth and (the beings) living in the earth.

verses.text:
इदं तु वृत्तिवैकल्यात् त्यजतो धर्मनैपुणं ।
विश्.पण्यम् उद्धृत.उद्धारं विक्रेयं वित्तवर्धनम् ॥
                                    ८५ ॥
verses.english: But he who, through a want of means of subsistence, gives up the strictness with respect to his duties, may sell, in order to increase his wealth, the commodities sold by Vaisyas, making (however) the (following) exceptions.

verses.text:
सर्वान् रसान् अपोहेत कृतान्नं च तिलैः सह ।
अश्मनो लवणं च-एव पशवो ये च मानुषाः ॥ ८६ ॥
verses.english: He must avoid (selling) condiments of all sorts, cooked food and sesamum, stones, salt, cattle, and human (beings),

verses.text:
सर्वं च तान्तवं रक्तं शाण.क्षौम.आविकानि च ।
अपि चेत् स्युर् अरक्तानि फल.मूले तथा-ओषधीः ॥ ८७
                                    ॥
verses.english: All dyed cloth, as well as cloth made of hemp, or flax, or wool, even though they be not dyed, fruit, roots, and (medical) herbs

verses.text:
अपः शस्त्रं विषं मांसं सोमं गन्धांश् च सर्वशः
                                    ।
क्षीरं क्षौद्रं दधि घृतं तैलं मधु गुडं कुशान् ॥
                                    ८८ ॥
verses.english: Water, weapons, poison, meat, Soma, and perfumes of all kinds, fresh milk, honey, sour milk, clarified butter, oil, wax, sugar, Kusa-grass;

verses.text:
आरण्यांश् च पशून् सर्वान् दंष्ट्रिणश् च वयांसि च ।
मद्यं नीलिं च लाक्षां च सर्वांश् च-एक.शफांस् तथा
                                    ॥ ८९ ॥ १०.८९च्व्/ म्: नीलीं ॥ 10.89 ॥
verses.english: All beasts of the forest, animals with fangs or tusks, birds, spirituous liquor, indigo, lac, and all one-hoofed beasts.

verses.text:
कामम् उत्पाद्य कृष्यां तु स्वयम् एव कृषीवलः ।
विक्रीणीत तिलान्-शूद्रान् धर्मार्थम् अचिरस्थितान् ॥ ९० ॥
                                        १०.९०च्व्/
                                        म्: तिलान्-शुद्धान् ॥ 10.90 ॥
verses.english: But he who subsists by agriculture, may at pleasure sell unmixed sesamum grains for sacred purposes, provided he himself has grown them and has not kept them long.

verses.text:
भोजन.अभ्यञ्जनाद् दानाद् यद् अन्यत् कुरुते तिलैः ।
कृमिभूतः श्वविष्ठायां पितृभिः सह मज्जति ॥ ९१
                                    ॥
verses.english: If he applies sesamum to any other purpose but food, anointing, and charitable gifts, he will be born (again) as a worm and, together with his ancestors, be plunged into the ordure of dogs.

verses.text:
सद्यः पतति मांसेन लाक्षया लवणेन च ।
त्र्यहेण शूद्रो भवति ब्राह्मणः क्षीरविक्रयात् ॥ ९२
                                    ॥
verses.english: By (selling) flesh, salt, and lac a Brahmana at once becomes an outcast; by selling milk he becomes (equal to) a Sudra in three days.

verses.text:
इतरेषां तु पण्यानां विक्रयाद् इह कामतः ।
ब्राह्मणः सप्तरात्रेण वैश्यभावं नियच्छति ॥ ९३
                                    ॥
verses.english: But by willingly selling in this world other (forbidden) commodities, a Brahmana assumes after seven nights the character of a Vaisya.

verses.text:
रसा रसैर् निमातव्या न त्व् एव लवणं रसैः ।
कृतान्नं च कृतान्नेन तिला धान्येन तत्समाः ॥ ९४
                                    ॥
verses.english: Condiments may be bartered for condiments, but by no means salt for (other) condiments; cooked food (may be exchanged) for (other kinds of) cooked food, and sesamum seeds for grain in equal quantities.

verses.text:
जीवेद् एतेन राजन्यः सर्वेण-अप्य् अनयं गतः ।
न त्व् एव ज्यायंसीं वृत्तिम् अभिमन्येत कर्हि चित् ॥ ९५
                                    ॥
verses.english: A Kshatriya who has fallen into distress, may subsist by all these (means); but he must never arrogantly adopt the mode of life (prescribed for his) betters.

verses.text:
यो लोभाद् अधमो जात्या जीवेद् उत्कृष्ट.कर्मभिः ।
तं राजा निर्धनं कृत्वा क्षिप्रम् एव प्रवासयेत् ॥ ९६
                                    ॥
verses.english: A man of low caste who through covetousness lives by the occupations of a higher one, the king shall deprive of his property and banish.

verses.text:
वरं स्वधर्मो विगुणो न पारक्यः स्वनुष्ठितः । १०.९७अव्/ म्: 
                                        विगुणः परधर्मात् स्वधिष्ठितात्
परधर्मेण जीवन् हि सद्यः पतति जातितः ॥ ९७ ॥
verses.english: It is better (to discharge) one's own (appointed) duty incompletely than to perform completely that of another; for he who lives according to the law of another (caste) is instantly excluded from his own.

verses.text:
वैश्यो ऽ.जीवन् स्वधर्मेण शूद्रवृत्त्या-अपि वर्तयेत्
                                    ।
अन्.आचरन्न् अ.कार्याणि निवर्तेत च शक्तिमान् ॥ ९८ ॥
verses.english: A Vaisya who is unable to subsist by his own duties, may even maintain himself by a Sudra's mode of life, avoiding (however) acts forbidden (to him), and he should give it up, when he is able (to do so).

verses.text:
अ.शक्नुवंस् तु शुश्रूषां शूद्रः कर्तुं द्विजन्मनाम् ।
पुत्र.दारात्ययं प्राप्तो जीवेत् कारुक.कर्मभिः ॥ ९९
                                    ॥
verses.english: But a Sudra, being unable to find service with the twice-born and threatened with the loss of his sons and wife (through hunger), may maintain himself by handicrafts.

verses.text:
यैः कर्मभिः प्रचरितैः शुश्रूष्यन्ते द्विजातयः ।
तानि कारुक.कर्माणि शिल्पानि विविधानि च ॥ १०० ॥
verses.english: (Let him follow) those mechanical occupations and those various practical arts by following which the twice-born are (best) served.

verses.text:
वैश्यवृत्तिम् अन्.आतिष्ठन् ब्राह्मणः स्वे पथि स्थितः
                                    ।
अवृत्तिकर्षितः सीदन्न् इमं धर्मं समाचरेत् ॥ १०१
                                    ॥
verses.english: A Brahmana who is distressed through a want of means of subsistence and pines (with hunger), (but) unwilling to adopt a Vaisya's mode of life and resolved to follow his own (prescribed) path, may act in the following manner.

verses.text:
सर्वतः प्रतिगृह्णीयाद् ब्राह्मणस् त्व् अनयं गतः ।
पवित्रं दुष्यति-इत्य् एतद् धर्मतो न-उपपद्यते ॥ १०२
                                    ॥
verses.english: A Brahmana who has fallen into distress may accept (gifts) from anybody; for according to the law it is not possible (to assert) that anything pure can be sullied.

verses.text:
न-अध्यापनाद् याजनाद् वा गर्हिताद् वा प्रतिग्रहात् ।
दोषो भवति विप्राणां ज्वलन.अम्बु.समा हि ते ॥ १०३
                                    ॥
verses.english: By teaching, by sacrificing for, and by accepting gifts from despicable (men) Brahmanas (in distress) commit not sin; for they (are as pure) as fire and water.

verses.text:
जीवितात्ययम् आपन्नो यो ऽन्नम् अत्ति ततस् ततः ।
आकाशम् इव पङ्केन न स पापेन लिप्यते ॥ १०४ ॥
verses.english: He who, when in danger of losing his life, accepts food from any person whatsoever, is no more tainted by sin than the sky by mud.

verses.text:
अजीगर्तः सुतं हन्तुम् उपासर्पद् बुभुक्षितः ।
न च-आलिप्यत पापेन क्षुत्प्रतीकारम् आचरन् ॥ १०५
                                    ॥
verses.english: Agigarta, who suffered hunger, approached in order to slay (his own) son, and was not tainted by sin, since he (only) sought a remedy against famishing.

verses.text:
श्वमांसम् इच्छन् आर्तो ऽत्तुं धर्म.अधर्मविचक्षणः
                                    ।
प्राणानां परिरक्षार्थं वामदेवो न लिप्तवान् ॥ १०६
                                    ॥
verses.english: Vamadeva, who well knew right and wrong, did not sully himself when, tormented (by hunger), he desired to eat the flesh of a dog in order to save his life.

verses.text:
भरद्वाजः क्षुधार्तस् तु स.पुत्रो विजने वने ।
बह्वीर् गाः प्रतिजग्राह वृधोस् तक्ष्णो महातपाः ॥ १०७
                                    ॥
verses.english: Bharadvaga, a performer of great austerities, accepted many cows from the carpenter Bribu, when he was starving together with his sons in a lonely forest.

verses.text:
क्षुधार्तश् च-अत्तुम् अभ्यागाद् विश्वामित्रः श्वजाघनीम्
                                    ।
चण्डालहस्ताद् आदाय धर्म.अधर्मविचक्षणः ॥ १०८
                                    ॥
verses.english: Visvamitra, who well knew what is right or wrong, approached, when he was tormented by hunger, (to eat) the haunch of a dog, receiving it the hands of a Kandala.

verses.text:
प्रतिग्रहाद् याजनाद् वा तथा-एव-अध्यापनाद् अपि ।
प्रतिग्रहः प्रत्यवरः प्रेत्य विप्रस्य गर्हितः ॥ १०९
                                    ॥
verses.english: On (comparing) the acceptance (of gifts from low men), sacrificing (for them), and teaching (them), the acceptance of gifts is the meanest (of those acts) and (most) reprehensible for a Brahmana (on account of its results) in the next life.

verses.text:
याजन.अध्यापने नित्यं क्रियेते संस्कृत.आत्मनाम् ।
प्रतिग्रहस् तु क्रियते शूद्राद् अप्य् अन्त्य.जन्मनः ॥ ११०
                                    ॥
verses.english: (For) assisting in sacrifices and teaching are (two acts) always performed for men who have received the sacraments; but the acceptance of gifts takes place even in (case the giver is) a Sudra of the lowest class.

verses.text:
जप.होमैर् अपैत्य् एनो याजन.अध्यापनैः कृतम् ।
प्रतिग्रहनिमित्तं तु त्यागेन तपसा-एव च ॥ १११
                                    ॥
verses.english: The guilt incurred by offering sacrifices for teaching (unworthy men) is removed by muttering (sacred texts) and by burnt offerings, but that incurred by accepting gifts (from them) by throwing (the gifts) away and by austerities.

verses.text:
शिल.उञ्छम् अप्य् आददीत विप्रो ऽ.जीवन् यतस् ततः ।
प्रतिग्रहात्-शिलः श्रेयांस् ततो ऽप्य् उञ्छः प्रशस्यते ॥
                                    ११२ ॥
verses.english: A Brahmana who is unable to maintain himself, should (rather) glean ears or grains from (the field of) any (man); gleaning ears is better than accepting gifts, picking up single grains is declared to be still more laudable.

verses.text:
सीदद्भिः कुप्यम् इच्छद्भिर् धने वा पृथिवीपतिः ।
                                        १०.११३अव्/ म्: धनं वा
याच्यः स्यात् स्नातकैर् विप्रैर् अदित्संस् त्यागम् अर्हति ॥
                                    ११३ ॥
verses.english: If Brahmanas, who are Snatakas, are pining with hunger, or in want of (utensils made of) common metals, or of other property, they may ask the king for them; if he is not disposed to be liberal, he must be left.

verses.text:
अकृतं च कृतात् क्षेत्राद् गौर् अजाविकम् एव च ।
हिरण्यं धान्यम् अन्नं च पूर्वं पूर्वम् अदोषवत् ॥ ११४
                                    ॥
verses.english: (The acceptance on an untilled field is less blamable than (that of) a tilled one; (with respect to) cows, goats, sheep, gold, grain, and cooked food, (the acceptance of) each earlier-named (article is less blamable than of the following ones).

verses.text:
सप्त वित्तागमा धर्म्या दायो लाभः क्रयो जयः ।
प्रयोगः कर्मयोगश् च सत्प्रतिग्रह एव च ॥ ११५
                                    ॥
verses.english: There are seven lawful modes of acquiring property, (viz.) inheritance, finding or friendly donation, purchase, conquest, lending at interest, the performance of work, and the acceptance of gifts from virtuous men.

verses.text:
विद्या शिल्पं भृतिः सेवा गोरक्ष्यं विपणिः कृषिः ।
धृतिर् भैक्षं कुसीदं च दश जीवनहेतवः ॥ ११६
                                    ॥
verses.english: Learning, mechanical arts, work for wages, service, rearing cattle, traffic, agriculture, contentment (with little), alms, and receiving interest on money, are the ten modes of subsistence (permitted to all men in times of distress).

verses.text:
ब्राह्मणः क्षत्रियो वा-अपि वृद्धिं न-एव प्रयोजयेत्
                                    ।
कामं तु खलु धर्मार्थं दद्यात् पापीयसे ऽल्पिकाम् ॥
                                    ११७ ॥
verses.english: Neither a Brahmana, nor a Kshatriya must lend (money at) interest; but at his pleasure (either of them) may, in times of distress when he requires money) for sacred purposes, lend to a very sinful man at a small interest.

verses.text:
चतुर्थम् आददानो ऽपि क्षत्रियो भागम् आपदि ।
प्रजा रक्षन् परं शक्त्या किल्बिषात् प्रतिमुच्यते ॥ ११८
                                    ॥
verses.english: A Kshatriya (king) who, in times of distress, takes even the fourth part (of the crops), is free from guilt, if he protects his subjects to the best of his ability.

verses.text:
स्वधर्मो विजयस् तस्य न-आहवे स्यात् पराङ्.मुखः
                                    ।
शस्त्रेण वैश्यान् रक्षित्वा धर्म्यम् आहारयेद् बलिम् ॥
                                    ११९ ॥ १०.११९च्व्/ म्: वैश्याद् रक्षित्वा ॥ 10.119 ॥
verses.english: His peculiar duty is conquest, and he must not turn back in danger; having protected the Vaisyas by his weapons, he may cause the legal tax to be collected;

verses.text:
धान्ये ऽष्टमं विशां शुल्कं विंशं कार्षापण.अवरम्
                                    ।
कर्म.उपकरणाः शूद्राः कारवः शिल्पिनस् तथा ॥ १२०
                                    ॥
verses.english: (Viz.) from Vaisyas one-eighth as the tax on grain, one-twentieth (on the profits on gold and cattle), which amount at least to one Karshapana; Sudras, artisans, and mechanics (shall) benefit (the king) by (doing) work (for him).

verses.text:
शूद्रस् तु वृत्तिम् आकाङ्क्षन् क्षत्रम् आराधयेद् यदि ।
                                        १०.१२१अव्/ म्: आराधयेद् इति
धनिनं वा-अप्य् उपाराध्य वैश्यं शूद्रो जिजीविषेत् ॥
                                    १२१ ॥
verses.english: If a Sudra, (unable to subsist by serving Brahmanas,) seeks a livelihood, he may serve Kshatriyas, or he may also seek to maintain himself by attending on a wealthy Vaisya.

verses.text:
स्वर्गार्थम् उभयार्थं वा विप्रान् आराधयेत् तु सः
                                    ।
जातब्राह्मण.शब्दस्य सा ह्य् अस्य कृतकृत्यता ॥ १२२
                                    ॥
verses.english: But let a (Sudra) serve Brahmanas, either for the sake of heaven, or with a view to both (this life and the next); for he who is called the servant of a Brahmana thereby gains all his ends.

verses.text:
विप्रसेवा-एव शूद्रस्य विशिष्टं कर्म कीर्त्यते ।
यद् अतो ऽन्यद्द् हि कुरुते तद् भवत्य् अस्य निष्फलम् ॥
                                    १२३ ॥
verses.english: The service of Brahmanas alone is declared (to be) an excellent occupation for a Sudra; for whatever else besides this he may perform will bear him no fruit.

verses.text:
प्रकल्प्या तस्य तैर् वृत्तिः स्वकुटुम्बाद् यथार्हतः
                                    ।
शक्तिं च-अवेक्ष्य दाक्ष्यं च भृत्यानां च परिग्रहम् ॥
                                    १२४ ॥
verses.english: They must allot to him out of their own family (-property) a suitable maintenance, after considering his ability, his industry, and the number of those whom he is bound to support.

verses.text:
उच्छिष्टम् अन्नं दातव्यं जीर्णानि वसनानि च ।
पुलाकाश् च-एव धान्यानां जीर्णाश् च-एव परिच्छदाः ॥
                                    १२५ ॥
