verses.english: The remnants of their food must be given to him, as well as their old clothes, the refuse of their grain, and their old household furniture.

verses.text:
न शूद्रे पातकं किं चिन् न च संस्कारम् अर्हति ।
न-अस्य-अधिकारो धर्मे ऽस्ति न धर्मात् प्रतिषेधनम्
                                    ॥ १२६ ॥
verses.english: A Sudra cannot commit an offence, causing loss of caste (pataka), and he is not worthy to receive the sacraments; he has no right to (fulfil) the sacred law (of the Aryans, yet) there is no prohibition against (his fulfilling certain portions of) the law.

verses.text:
धर्म.इप्सवस् तु धर्मज्ञाः सतां वृत्तम् अनुष्ठिताः ।
                                        १०.१२७अव्/ म्: सतां धर्मम्
मन्त्रवर्ज्यं न दुष्यन्ति प्रशंसां प्राप्नुवन्ति च ॥
                                    १२७ ॥ १०.१२७च्व्/ म्: मन्त्रवर्जं ॥ 10.127 ॥
verses.english: (Sudras) who are desirous to gain merit, and know (their) duty, commit no sin, but gain praise, if they imitate the practice of virtuous men without reciting sacred texts.

verses.text:
यथा यथा हि सद्वृत्तम् आतिष्ठत्य् अनसूयकः ।
तथा तथा-इमं च-अमुं च लोकं प्राप्नोत्य् अनिन्दितः ॥
                                    १२८ ॥
verses.english: The more a (Sudra), keeping himself free from envy, imitates the behaviour of the virtuous, the more he gains, without being censured, (exaltation in) this world and the next.

verses.text:
शक्तेन-अपि हि शूद्रेण न कार्यो धनसञ्चयः ।
शूद्रो हि धनम् आसाद्य ब्राह्मणान् एव बाधते ॥ १२९
                                    ॥
verses.english: No collection of wealth must be made by a Sudra, even though he be able (to do it); for a Sudra who has acquired wealth, gives pain to Brahmanas.

verses.text:
एते चतुर्णां वर्णानाम् आपद्धर्माः प्रकीर्तिताः ।
यान् सम्यग् अनुतिष्ठन्तो व्रजन्ति परमं गतिम् ॥ १३०
                                ॥
verses.english: The duties of the four castes (varna) in times of distress have thus been declared, and if they perform them well, they will reach the most blessed state.

verses.text:
एष धर्मविधिः कृत्स्नश् चातुर्वर्ण्यस्य कीर्तितः ।
अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि प्रायश्चित्तविधिं शुभम् ॥ १३१
                                ॥
verses.english: Thus all the legal rules for the four castes have been proclaimed; I next will promulgate the auspicious rules for penances.

verses.text:
सान्तानिकं यक्ष्यमाणम् अध्वगं सार्ववेदसम् ।
गुरु.अर्थं पितृ.मातृ.अर्थं स्वाध्यायार्थ्य् उपतापिनः ॥ १
                                ॥
verses.english: Him who wishes (to marry for the sake of having) offspring, him who wishes to perform a sacrifice, a traveller, him who has given away all his property, him who begs for the sake of his teacher, his father, or his mother, a student of the Veda, and a sick man,

verses.text:
न वै तान् स्नातकान् विद्याद् ब्राह्मणान् धर्मभिक्षुकान् ।
निःस्वेभ्यो देयम् एतेभ्यो दानं विद्याविशेषतः ॥ २ ॥
verses.english: These nine Brahmanas one should consider as Snatakas, begging in order to fulfil the sacred law; to such poor men gifts must be given in proportion to their learning.

verses.text:
एतेभ्यो हि द्विजाग्र्येभ्यो देयम् अन्नं स.दक्षिणम् ।
इतरेभ्यो बहिर्वेदि कृतान्नं देयम् उच्यते ॥ ३ ॥
verses.english: To these most excellent among the twice-born, food and presents (of money) must be given; it is declared that food must be given to others outside the sacrificial enclosure.

verses.text:
सर्वरत्नानि राजा तु यथार्हं प्रतिपादयेत् ।
ब्राह्मणान् वेदविदुषो यज्ञार्थं च-एव दक्षिणाम् ॥ ४ ॥
verses.english: But a king shall bestow, as is proper, jewels of all sorts, and presents for the sake of sacrifices on Brahmanas learned in the Vedas.

verses.text:
कृत.दारो ऽपरान् दारान् भिक्षित्वा यो ऽधिगच्छति ।
रति.मात्रं फलं तस्य द्रव्यदातुस् तु सन्ततिः ॥ ५ ॥
verses.english: If a man who has a wife weds a second wife, having begged money (to defray the marriage expenses, he obtains) no advantage but sensual enjoyment; but the issue (of his second marriage belongs) to the giver of the money.

verses.text:
धनानि तु यथाशक्ति विप्रेषु प्रतिपादयेत् । ११.०६अव्/ नोत् इन्
                                    म्
वेदवित्सु विविक्तेषु प्रेत्य स्वर्गं समश्नुते ॥ ६ ॥ ११.०६च्व्/ नोत् इन्
                                    म् ॥ 11.6 ॥
verses.english: One should give, according to one's ability, wealth to Brahmanas learned in the Veda and living alone; (thus) one obtains after death heavenly bliss.

verses.text:
[०६म] यस्य त्रैवार्षिकं भक्तं पर्याप्तं भृत्यवृत्तये
                                ।
[०६म्च्] अधिकं वा-अपि विद्येत स सोमं पातुम् अर्हति ॥ ७
                                ॥
verses.english: He who may possess (a supply of) food sufficient to maintain those dependant on him during three years or more than that, is worthy to drink the Soma-juice.

verses.text:
[०७म] अतः स्वल्पीयसि द्रव्ये यः सोमं पिबति द्विजः ।
[०७म्च्] स पीतसोम.पूर्वो ऽपि न तस्य-आप्नोति तत्फलम् ॥ ८
                                ॥
verses.english: But a twice-born man, who, though possessing less than that amount of property, nevertheless drinks the Soma-juice, does not derive any benefit from that (act), though he may have formerly drunk the Soma-juice.

verses.text:
[०८म] शक्तः परजने दाता स्वजने दुःखजीविनि ।
[०८म्च्] मध्व्.आपातो विष.आस्वादः स धर्म.प्रतिरूपकः ॥ ९
                                ॥
verses.english: (If) an opulent man (is) liberal towards strangers, while his family lives in distress, that counterfeit virtue will first make him taste the sweets (of fame, but afterwards) make him swallow the poison (of punishment in hell).

verses.text:
[०९म] भृत्यानाम् उपरोधेन यत् करोत्य् और्ध्वदेहिकम् ।
[०९म्च्] तद् भवत्य् असुख.उदर्कं जीवतश् च मृतस्य च ॥ १०
                                ॥
verses.english: If (a man) does anything for the sake of his happiness in another world, to the detriment of those whom he is bound to maintain, that produces evil results for him, both while he lives and when he is dead.

verses.text:
[१०म] यज्ञश् चेत् प्रतिरुद्धः स्याद् एकेन-अङ्गेन यज्वनः
                                ।
[१०म्च्] ब्राह्मणस्य विशेषेन धार्मिके सति राजनि ॥ ११ ॥
verses.english: If a sacrifice, (offered) by (any twice-born) sacrificer, (and) especially by a Brahmana, must remain incomplete through (the want of) one requisite, while a righteous king rules,

verses.text:
[११म] यो वैश्यः स्याद् बहुपशुर् हीन.क्रतुर् असोमपः ।
[११म्च्] कुटुम्बात् तस्य तद् द्रव्यम् आहरेद् यज्ञसिद्धये ॥ १२
                                ॥
verses.english: That article (required) for the completion of the sacrifice, may be taken (forcibly) from the house of any Vaisya, who possesses a large number of cattle, (but) neither performs the (minor) sacrifices nor drinks the Soma-juice;

verses.text:
[१२म] आहरेत् त्रीणि वा द्वे वा कामं शूद्रस्य वेश्मनः ।
[१२म्च्] न हि शूद्रस्य यज्ञेषु कश् चिद् अस्ति परिग्रहः ॥ १३
                                ॥
verses.english: (Or) the (sacrificer) may take at his pleasure two or three (articles required for a sacrifice) from the house of a Sudra; for a Sudra has no business with sacrifices.

verses.text:
[१३म] यो ऽनाहित.अग्निः शतगुर् अ.यज्वा च सहस्रगुः । ११.१४अ[१३म]व्/ क्:
                                    अयज्ञश्
[१३म्च्] तयोर् अपि कुटुम्बाभ्याम् आहरेद् अ.विचारयन् ॥ १४ ॥
verses.english: If (a man) possessing one hundred cows, kindles not the sacred fire, or one possessing a thousand cows, drinks not the Soma-juice, a (sacrificer) may unhesitatingly take (what he requires) from the houses of those two, even (though they be Brahmanas or Kshatriyas);

verses.text:
[१४म] आदान.नित्याच् च-आदातुर् आहरेद् अ.प्रयच्छतः ।
[१४म्च्] तथा यशो ऽस्य प्रथते धर्मश् च-एव प्रवर्धते ॥
                                १५ ॥
verses.english: (Or) he may take (it by force or fraud) from one who always takes and never gives, and who refuses to give it; thus the fame (of the taker) will spread and his merit increase.

verses.text:
[१५म] तथाअ-एव सप्तमे भक्ते भक्तानि षड् अन्.अश्नता ।
[१५म्च्] अश्वस्तनविधानेन हर्तव्यं हीन.कर्मणः ॥ १६
                                ॥
verses.english: Likewise he who has not eaten at (the time of) six meals, may take at (the time of) the seventh meal (food) from a man who neglects his sacred duties, without (however) making a provision for the morrow,

verses.text:
[१६म] खलात् क्षेत्राद् अगाराद् वा यतो वा-अप्य् उपलभ्यते ।
[१६म्च्] आख्यातव्यं तु तत् तस्मै पृच्छते यदि पृच्छति ॥ १७
                                ॥
verses.english: Either from the threshing-floor, or from a field, or out of the house, or wherever he finds it; but if (the owner) asks him, he must confess to him that (deed and its cause).

verses.text:
[१७म] ब्राह्मणस्वं न हर्तव्यं क्षत्रियेण कदा चन ।
[१७म्च्] दस्यु.निष्क्रिययोस् तु स्वम् अ.जीवन् हर्तुम् अर्हति ॥ १८
                                ॥
verses.english: (On such occasions) a Kshatriya must never take the property of a (virtuous Brahmana; but he who is starving may appropriate the possessions of a Dasyu, or of one who neglects his sacred duties.

verses.text:
[१८म] यो ऽसाधुभ्यो ऽर्थम् आदाय साधुभ्यः सम्प्रयच्छति
                                ।
[१८म्च्] स कृत्वा प्लवम् आत्मानं सन्तारयति ताव् उभौ ॥ १९
                                ॥
verses.english: He who takes property from the wicked and bestows it on the virtuous, transforms himself into a boat, and carries both (over the sea of misfortune).

verses.text:
[१९म] यद् धनं यज्ञशीलानां देवस्वं तद् विदुर् बुधाः
                                ।
[१९म्च्] अ.यज्वनां तु यद् वित्तम् आसुरस्वं तद् उच्यते ॥ २०
                                ॥
verses.english: The property of those who zealously offer sacrifices, the wise call the property of the gods; but the wealth of those who perform no sacrifices is called the property of the Asuras.

verses.text:
[२०म] न तस्मिन् धारयेद् दण्डं धार्मिकः पृथिवीपतिः ।
[२०म्च्] क्षत्रियस्य हि बालिश्याद् ब्राह्मणः सीदति क्षुधा ॥ २१
                                ॥
verses.english: On him (who, for the reasons stated, appropriates another's possessions), a righteous king shall not inflict punishment; for (in that case) a Brahmana pines with hunger through the Kshatriya's want of care.

verses.text:
[२१म] तस्य भृत्यजनं ज्ञात्वा स्वकुटुम्बान् महीपतिः ।
[२१म्च्] श्रुत.शीले च विज्ञाय वृत्तिं धर्म्यां प्रकल्पयेत् ॥
                                २२ ॥
verses.english: Having ascertained the number of those dependent on such a man, and having fully considered his learning and his conduct, the king shall allow him, out of his own property, a maintenance whereon he may live according to the law;

verses.text:
[२२म] कल्पयित्वा-अस्य वृत्तिं च रक्षेद् एनं समन्ततः ।
[२२म्च्] राजा हि धर्मषड्भागं तस्मात् प्राप्नोति रक्षितात् ॥ २३
                                ॥
verses.english: And after allotting to him a maintenance, the king must protect him in every way; for he obtains from such (a man) whom he protects, the part of his spiritual merit.

verses.text:
[२३म] न यज्ञार्थं धनं शूद्राद् विप्रो भिक्षेत कर्हि चित्
                                ।
[२३म्च्] यजमानो हि भिक्षित्वा चण्डालः प्रेत्य जायते ॥ २४
                                ॥
verses.english: A Brahmana shall never beg from a Sudra property for a sacrifice; for a sacrificer, having begged (it from such a man), after death is born (again) as a Kandala.

verses.text:
[२४म] याज्ञार्थम् अर्थं भिक्षित्वा यो न सर्वं प्रयच्छति
                                ।
[२४म्च्] स याति भासतां विप्रः काकतां वा शतं समाः ॥ २५
                                ॥
verses.english: A Brahmana who, having begged any property for a sacrifice, does not use the whole (for that purpose), becomes for a hundred years a (vulture of the kind called) Bhasa, or a crow.

verses.text:
[२५म] देवस्वं ब्राह्मणस्वं वा लोभेन-उपहिनस्ति यः ।
[२५म्च्] स पाप.आत्मा परे लोके गृध्र.उच्छिष्टेन जीवति ॥ २६
                                ॥
verses.english: That sinful man, who, through covetousness, seizes the property of the gods, or the property of Brahmanas, feeds in another world on the leavings of vultures.

verses.text:
[२६म] इष्टिं वैश्वानरीं नित्यं निर्वपेद् अब्दपर्यये
                                    ।
[२६म्च्] कॢप्तानां पशु.सोमानां निष्कृत्यर्थम् असम्भवे ॥
                                    २७ ॥
verses.english: In case the prescribed animal and Soma-sacrifices cannot be performed, let him always offer at the change of the year a Vaisvanari Ishti as a penance (for the omission).

verses.text:
[२७म] आपत्कल्पेन यो धर्मं कुरुते ऽनापदि द्विजः ।
[२७म्च्] स न-आप्नोति फलं तस्य परत्र-इति विचारितम् ॥
                                    २८ ॥
verses.english: But a twice-born, who, without being in distress, performs his duties according to the law for times of distress, obtains no reward for them in the next world; that is the opinion (of the sages).

verses.text:
[२८म] विश्वैश् च देवैः साध्यैश् च ब्राह्मणैश् च
                                    महर्षिभिः ।
[२८म्च्] आपत्सु मरणाद् भीतैर् विधेः प्रतिनिधिः कृतः ॥
                                    २९ ॥
verses.english: By the Visve-devas, by the Sadhyas, and by the great sages (of the) Brahmana (caste), who were afraid of perishing in times of distress, a substitute was made for the (principal) rule.

verses.text:
[२९म] प्रभुः प्रथमकल्पस्य यो ऽनुकल्पेन वर्तते
                                    ।
[२९म्च्] न साम्परायिकं तस्य दुर्.मतेर् विद्यते फलम् ॥
                                    ३० ॥
verses.english: That evil-minded man, who, being able (to fulfil) the original law, lives according to the secondary rule, reaps no reward for that after death.

verses.text:
[३०म] न ब्राह्मणो वेदयेत किं चिद् राजनि धर्मवित्
                                    ।
[३०म्च्] स्ववीर्येण-एव तान्-शिष्यान् मानवान् अपकारिणः ॥ ३१
                                    ॥
verses.english: A Brahmana who knows the law need not bring any (offence) to the notice of the king; by his own power alone be can punish those men who injure him.

verses.text:
[३१म] स्ववीर्याद् राजवीर्याच् च स्ववीर्यं बलवत्तरम्
                                    ।
[३१म्च्] तस्मात् स्वेन-एव वीर्येण निगृह्णीयाद् अरीन् द्विजः ॥
                                    ३२ ॥
verses.english: His own power is greater than the power of the king; the Brahmana therefore, may punish his foes by his own power alone.

verses.text:
[३२म] श्रुतीर् अथर्वाङ्गिरसीः कुर्याद् इत्य् अ.विचारयन्
                                    ।
[३२म्च्] वाक्शस्त्रं वै ब्राह्मणस्य तेन हन्याद् अरीन् द्विजः
                                    ॥ ३३ ॥
verses.english: Let him use without hesitation the sacred texts, revealed by Atharvan and by Angiras; speech, indeed, is the weapon of the Brahmana, with that he may slay his enemies.

verses.text:
[३३म] क्षत्रियो बाहुवीर्येण तरेद् आपदम् आत्मनः ।
[३३म्च्] धनेन वैश्य.शूद्रौ तु जप.होमैर् द्विजोत्तमः
                                    ॥ ३४ ॥
verses.english: A Kshatriya shall pass through misfortunes which have befallen him by the strength of his arms, a Vaisya and a Sudra by their wealth, the chief of the twice-born by muttered prayers and burnt-oblations.

verses.text:
[३४म] विधाता शासिता वक्ता मैत्रो ब्राह्मण उच्यते ।
[३४म्च्] तस्मै न-अकुशलं ब्रूयान् न शुष्कां गिरम् ईरयेत्
                                    ॥ ३५ ॥
verses.english: The Brahmana is declared (to be) the creator (of the world), the punisher, the teacher, (and hence) a benefactor (of all created beings); to him let no man say anything unpropitious, nor use any harsh words.

verses.text:
[३५म] न वै कन्या न युवतिर् न-अल्प.विद्यो न बालिशः
                                    ।
[३५म्च्] होता स्याद् अग्निहोत्रस्य न-आर्तो न-असंस्कृतस् तथा
                                    ॥ ३६ ॥
verses.english: Neither a girl, nor a (married) young woman, nor a man of little learning, nor a fool, nor a man in great suffering, nor one uninitiated, shall offer an Agnihotra.

verses.text:
[३६म] नरके हि पतन्त्य् एते जुह्वन्तः स च यस्य तत् ।
                                        ११.३७अ[३६म]व्/ म्: जुह्वतः
[३६म्च्] तस्माद् वैतानकुशलो होता स्याद् वेदपारगः ॥ ३७
                                    ॥
verses.english: For such (persons) offering a burnt-oblation sink into hell, as well as he to whom that (Agnihotra) belongs; hence the person who sacrifices (for another) must be skilled in (the performance of) Vaitana (rites), and know the whole Veda.

verses.text:
[३७म] प्राजापत्यम् अ.दत्त्वा-अश्वम् अग्न्याधेयस्य दक्षिणाम्
                                    ।
[३७म्च्] अनाहिताग्निर् भवति ब्राह्मणो विभवे सति ॥ ३८
                                    ॥
verses.english: A Brahmana who, though wealthy, does not give, as fee for the performance of an Agnyadheya, a horse sacred to Pragapati, becomes (equal to one) who has not kindled the sacred fires.

verses.text:
[३८म] पुण्यान्य् अन्यानि कुर्वीत श्रद्दधानो जित.इन्द्रियः
                                    ।
[३८म्च्] न त्व् अल्प.दक्षिणैर् यज्ञैर् यजेत-इह कथं
                                    चन ॥ ३९ ॥
verses.english: Let him who has faith and controls his senses perform other meritorious acts, but let him on no account offer sacrifices at which he gives smaller fees (than those prescribed).

verses.text:
[३९म] इन्द्रियाणि यशः स्वर्गम् आयुः कीर्तिं प्रजाः पशून्
                                    ।
[३९म्च्] हन्त्य् अल्प.दक्षिणो यज्ञस् तस्मान् न-अल्प.धनो
                                    यजेत् ॥ ४० ॥
verses.english: The organs (of sense and action), honour, (bliss in) heaven, longevity, fame, offspring, and cattle are destroyed by a sacrifice at which (too) small sacrificial fees are given; hence a man of small means should not offer a (Srauta) sacrifice.

verses.text:
[४०म] अग्निहोत्र्य् अपविध्य-अग्नीन् ब्राह्मणः कामकारतः
                                    ।
[४०म्च्] चान्द्रायणं चरेन् मासं वीरहत्यासमं हि तत् ॥
                                    ४१ ॥
verses.english: A Brahmana who, being an Agnihotrin, voluntarily neglects the sacred fires, shall perform a lunar penance during one month; for that (offence) is equal to the slaughter of a son.

verses.text:
[४१म] ये शूद्राद् अधिगम्य-अर्थम् अग्निहोत्रम् उपासते
                                    ।
[४१म्च्] ऋत्विजस् ते हि शूद्राणां ब्रह्मवादिषु गर्हिताः ॥ ४२
                                    ॥
verses.english: Those who, obtaining wealth from Sudras, (and using that) offer an Agnihotra, are priests officiating for Sudras, (and hence) censured among those who recite the Veda.

verses.text:
[४२म] तेषां सततम् अज्ञानां वृषलाग्न्युपसेविनाम् ।
[४२म्च्] पदा मस्तकम् आक्रम्य दाता दुर्गाणि सन्तरेत् ॥ ४३
                                    ॥
verses.english: Treading with his foot on the heads of those fools who worship a fire (kindled at the expense) of a Sudra, the giver (of the wealth) shall always pass over his miseries (in the next world).

verses.text:
[४३म] अ.कुर्वन् विहितं कर्म निन्दितं च समाचरन् ।
[४३म्च्] प्रसक्तश् च-इन्द्रियार्थेषु प्रायश्चित्तीयते नरः ॥ ४४
                                ॥ ११.४४च्[४३म्च्]व्/ म्: प्रसज्जन् इन्द्रियार्थेषु ॥ 11.44 ॥
verses.english: A man who omits a prescribed act, or performs a blamable act, or cleaves to sensual enjoyments, must perform a penance.

verses.text:
[४४म] अकामतः कृते पापे प्रायश्चित्तं विदुर् बुधाः ।
[४४म्च्] कामकारकृते ऽप्य् आहुर् एके श्रुतिनिदर्शनात् ॥ ४५ ॥
verses.english: (All) sages prescribe a penance for a sin unintentionally committed; some declare, on the evidence of the revealed texts, (that it may be performed) even for an intentional (offence).

verses.text:
[४५म] अकामतः कृतं पापं वेदाभ्यासेन शुध्यति ।
[४५म्च्] कामतस् तु कृतं मोहात् प्रायश्चित्तैः पृथग्विधैः ॥
                                ४६ ॥
verses.english: A sin unintentionally committed is expiated by the recitation of Vedic texts, but that which (men) in their folly commit intentionally, by various (special) penances.

verses.text:
[४६म] प्रायश्चित्तीयतां प्राप्य दैवात् पूर्वकृतेन वा ।
[४६म्च्] न संसर्गं व्रजेत् सद्भिः प्रायश्चित्ते ऽकृते द्विजः
                                ॥ ४७ ॥
verses.english: A twice-born man, having become liable to perform a penance, be it by (the decree of) fate or by (an act) committed in a former life, must not, before the penance has been performed, have intercourse with virtuous men.

verses.text:
[४७म] इह दुश्चरितैः के चित् के चित् पूर्वकृतैस् तथा ।
[४७म्च्] प्राप्नुवन्ति दुर्.आत्मानो नरा रूपविपर्ययम् ॥ ४८
                                ॥
verses.english: Some wicked men suffer a change of their (natural) appearance in consequence of crimes committed in this life, and some in consequence of those committed in a former (existence).

verses.text:
[४८म] सुवर्णचौरः कौनख्यं सुरापः श्यावदन्तताम् ।
[४८म्च्] ब्रह्महा क्षयरोगित्वं दौश्चर्म्यं गुरुतल्पगः ॥ ४९
                                ॥
verses.english: He who steals the gold (of a Brahmana) has diseased nails; a drinker of (the spirituous liquor called) Sura, black teeth; the slayer of a Brahmana, consumption; the violator of a Guru's bed, a diseased skin;

verses.text:
[४९म] पिशुनः पौतिनासिक्यं सूचकः पूतिवक्त्रताम् ।
[४९म्च्] धान्यचौरो ऽङ्गहीनत्वम् आतिरैक्यं तु मिश्रकः ॥ ५०
                                ॥
verses.english: An informer, a foul-smelling nose; a calumniator, a stinking breath; a stealer of grain, deficiency in limbs; he who adulterates (grain), redundant limbs;

verses.text:
[५०म] अन्नहर्ता-आमयावित्वं मौक्यं वागपहारकः ।
[५०म्च्] वस्त्रापहारकः श्वैत्र्यं पङ्गुताम् अश्वहारकः ॥ ५१
                                ॥
verses.english: A stealer of (cooked) food, dyspepsia; a stealer of the words (of the Veda), dumbness a stealer of clothes, white leprosy; a horse-stealer, lameness.

verses.text:
[५१म] एवं कर्मविशेषेण जायन्ते सद्विगर्हिताः ।
[५१म्च्] जड.मूक.अन्ध.बधिरा विकृत.आकृतयस् तथा ॥ ५२
                                ॥
verses.english: The stealer of a lamp will become blind; he who extinguishes it will become one-eyed; injury (to sentient beings) is punished by general sickliness; an adulterer (will have) swellings (in his limbs).

verses.text:
[५२म] चरितव्यम् अतो नित्यं प्रायश्चित्तं विशुद्धये ।
[५२म्च्] निन्द्यैर् हि लक्षणैर् युक्ता जायन्ते ऽनिष्कृत.एनसः ॥
                                ५३ ॥
verses.english: Thus in consequence of a remnant of (the guilt of former) crimes, are born idiots, dumb, blind, deaf, and deformed men, who are (all) despised by the virtuous.

verses.text:
[५३म] ब्रह्महत्या सुरापानं स्तेयं गुर्वङ्गनागमः ।
[५३म्च्] महान्ति पातकान्य् आहुः संसर्गश् च-अपि तैः सह ॥ ५४
                                ॥
verses.english: Penances, therefore, must always be performed for the sake of purification, because those whose sins have not been expiated, are born (again) with disgraceful marks.

verses.text:
[५४म] अनृतं च समुत्कर्षे राजगामि च पैशुनम् ।
[५४म्च्] गुरोश् चालीक.निर्बन्धः समानि ब्रह्महत्यया ॥ ५५
                                    ॥
verses.english: Killing a Brahmana, drinking (the spirituous liquor called) Sura, stealing (the gold of a Brahmana), adultery with a Guru's wife, and associating with such (offenders), they declare (to be) mortal sins (mahapataka).

verses.text:
[५५म] ब्रह्म.उज्झता वेदनिन्दा कौटसाक्ष्यं सुहृद्वधः
                                    ।
[५५म्च्] गर्हित.अनाद्ययोर् जग्धिः सुरापानसमानि षट् ॥ ५६
                                    ॥
verses.english: Falsely attributing to oneself high birth, giving information to the king (regarding a crime), and falsely accusing one's teacher, (are offences) equal to slaying a Brahmana.

verses.text:
[५६म] निक्षेपस्य-अपहरणं नर.अश्व.रजतस्य च ।
[५६म्च्] भूमि.वज्र.मणीनां च रुक्मस्तेयसमं स्मृतम् ॥
                                    ५७ ॥
verses.english: Forgetting the Veda, reviling the Vedas, giving false evidence, slaying a friend, eating forbidden food, or (swallowing substances) unfit for food, are six (offences) equal to drinking Sura.

verses.text:
[५७म] रेतःसेकः स्वयोनीषु कुमारीष्व् अन्त्यजासु च ।
[५७म्च्] सख्युः पुत्रस्य च स्त्रीषु गुरुतल्पसमं विदुः ॥
                                    ५८ ॥
verses.english: Stealing a deposit, or men, a horse, and silver, land, diamonds and (other) gems, is declared to be equal to stealing the gold (of a Brahmana).

verses.text:
[५८म] गोवधो ऽयाज्य.संयाज्यं पारदार्य.आत्मविक्रयः
                                    ।
[५८म्च्] गुरु.मातृ.पितृ.त्यागः स्वाध्याय.अग्न्योः सुतस्य च
                                    ॥ ५९ ॥
verses.english: Carnal intercourse with sisters by the same mother, with (unmarried) maidens, with females of the lowest castes, with the wives of a friend, or of a son, they declare to be equal to the violation of a Guru's bed.

verses.text:
[५९म] परिवित्तिता-अनुजे ऽनूढे परिवेदनम् एव च ।
[५९म्च्] तयोर् दानं च कन्यायास् तयोर् एव च याजनम् ॥ ६०
                                    ॥
verses.english: Slaying kine, sacrificing for those who are unworthy to sacrifice, adultery, selling oneself, casting off one's teacher, mother, father, or son, giving up the (daily) study of the Veda, and neglecting the (sacred domestic) fire,

verses.text:
[६०म] कन्याया दूषणं च-एव वार्धुष्यं व्रतलोपनम्
                                    ।
[६०म्च्] तडाग.आराम.दाराणाम् अपत्यस्य च विक्रयः ॥ ६१
                                    ॥
verses.english: Allowing one's younger brother to marry first, marrying before one's elder brother, giving a daughter to, or sacrificing for, (either brother),

verses.text:
[६१म] व्रात्यता बान्धवत्यागो भृत्याध्यापनम् एव च
                                    ।
[६१म्च्] भृत्या च-अध्ययनादानम् अपण्यानां च विक्रयः ॥
                                    ६२ ॥ ११.६२च्[६१म्च्]व्/ म्: भृताच् च-अध्ययनादानम् ॥ 11.62 ॥
verses.english: Defiling a damsel, usury, breaking a vow, selling a tank, a garden, one's wife, or child,

verses.text:
[६२म] सर्वाकारेष्व् अधीकारो महायन्त्रप्रवर्तनम् ।
[६२म्च्] हिंसा-ओषधीनां स्त्रि.आजीवो ऽभिचारो मूलकर्म च
                                    ॥ ६३ ॥
verses.english: Living as a Vratya, casting off a relative, teaching (the Veda) for wages, learning (the Veda) from a paid teacher, and selling goods which one ought not to sell,

verses.text:
[६३म] इन्धनार्थम् अशुष्काणां द्रुमाणाम् अवपातनम् ।
[६३म्च्] आत्मार्थं च क्रियारम्भो निन्दितान्नादनं तथा ॥
                                    ६४ ॥
verses.english: Superintending mines (or factories) of any sort, executing great mechanical works, injuring (living) plants, subsisting on (the earnings of) one's wife, sorcery (by means of sacrifices), and working (magic by means of) roots, (and so forth),

verses.text:
[६४म] अनाहिताग्निता स्तेयम् ऋणानाम् अनपक्रिया ।
[६४म्च्] असत्.शाष्त्राधिगमनं कौशीलव्यस्य च क्रिया ॥ ६५
                                    ॥
verses.english: Cutting down green trees for firewood, doing acts for one's own advantage only, eating prohibited food,

verses.text:
[६५म] धान्य.कुप्य.पशुस्तेयं मद्यपस्त्रीनिषेवणम् ।
[६५म्च्] स्त्री.शूद्र.विश्.क्षत्रवधो नास्तिक्यं च-उपपातकम्
                                    ॥ ६६ ॥
verses.english: Neglecting to kindle the sacred fires, theft, non-payment of (the three) debts, studying bad books, and practising (the arts of) dancing and singing,

verses.text:
[६६म] ब्राह्मणस्य रुजः कृत्वा घ्रातिर् अघ्रेय.मद्ययोः ।
                                        ११.६७अ[६६म]व्/ म्: रुजःकृत्यं
[६६म्च्] जैह्म्यं च मैथुनं पुंसि जातिभ्रंशकरं
                                    स्मृतम् ॥ ६७ ॥
verses.english: Stealing grain, base metals, or cattle, intercourse with women who drink spirituous liquor, slaying women, Sudras, Vaisyas, or Kshatriyas, and atheism, (are all) minor offences, causing loss of caste (Upapataka).

verses.text:
[६७म] खर.अश्व.उष्ट्र.मृग.इभानाम् अज.आविकवधस्
                                    तथा ।
[६७म्च्] सङ्करीकरणं ज्ञेयं मीन.अहि.महिषस्य च ॥ ६८
                                    ॥
verses.english: Giving pain to a Brahmana (by a blow), smelling at things which ought not to be smelt at, or at spirituous liquor, cheating, and an unnatural offence with a man, are declared to cause the loss of caste (Gatibhramsa)

verses.text:
[६८म] निन्दितेभ्यो धनादानं वाणिज्यं शूद्रसेवनम् ।
[६८म्च्] अपात्रीकरणं ज्ञेयम् असत्यस्य च भाषणम् ॥ ६९
                                    ॥
verses.english: Killing a donkey, a horse, a camel, a deer, an elephant, a goat, a sheep, a fish, a snake, or a buffalo, must be known to degrade (the offender) to a mixed caste (Samkarikarana).

verses.text:
[६९म] कृमि.कीट.वयो.हत्या मद्यानुगतभोजनम् ।
[६९म्च्] फल.एधः.कुसुम.स्तेयम् अधैर्यं च मलावहम्
                                    ॥ ७० ॥
verses.english: Accepting presents from blamed men, trading, serving Sudras, and speaking a falsehood, make (the offender) unworthy to receive gifts (Apatra).

verses.text:
[७०म] एतान्य् एनांसि सर्वाणि यथा.उक्तानि पृथक् पृथक्
                                    ।
[७०म्च्] यैर् यैर् व्रतैर् अपोह्यन्ते तानि सम्यङ् निबोधत
                                    ॥ ७१ ॥
verses.english: Killing insects, small or large, or birds, eating anything kept close to spirituous liquors, stealing fruit, firewood, or flowers, (are offences) which make impure (Malavaha).

verses.text:
[७१म] ब्रह्महा द्वादश समाः कुटीं कृत्वा वने वसेत्
                                    ।
[७१म्च्] भैक्षाश्य् आत्मविशुद्ध्यर्थं कृत्वा शवशिरो
                                    ध्वजम् ॥ ७२ ॥
verses.english: Learn (now) completely those penances, by means of which all the several offences mentioned (can) be expiated.

verses.text:
[७२म] लक्ष्यं शस्त्रभृतां वा स्याद् विदुषाम्
                                    इच्छया-आत्मनः ।
[७२म्च्] प्रास्येद् आत्मानम् अग्नौ वा समिद्धे त्रिर् अवाक्.शिराः
                                    ॥ ७३ ॥
verses.english: For his purification the slayer of a Brahmana shall make a hut in the forest and dwell (in it) during twelve years, subsisting on alms and making the skull of a dead man his flag.

verses.text:
[७३म] यजेत वा-अश्वमेधेन स्वर्जिता गोसवेन वा ।
[७३म्च्] अभिजिद्.विश्वजिद्भ्यां वा त्रिवृता-अग्निष्टुता-अपि वा
                                    ॥ ७४ ॥
verses.english: Or let him, of his own free will, become (in a battle) the target of archers who know (his purpose); or he may thrice throw himself headlong into a blazing fire;

verses.text:
[७४म] जपन् वा-अन्यतमं वेदं योजनानां शतं व्रजेत्
                                    ।
[७४म्च्] ब्रह्महत्यापनोदाय मितभुज्-नियत.इन्द्रियः ॥ ७५
                                    ॥
verses.english: Or he may offer a horse-sacrifice, a Svargit, a Gosava, an Abhigit, a Visvagit, a Trivrit, or an Agnishtut;

verses.text:
[७५म] सर्वस्वं वेदविदुषे ब्राह्मणाय-उपपादयेत् ।
[७५म्च्] धनं हि जीवनाय-अलं गृहं वा स.परिच्छदम् ॥
                                    ७६ ॥
verses.english: Or, in order to remove (the guilt of) slaying a Brahmana, he may walk one hundred yoganas, reciting one of the Vedas, eating little, and controlling his organs;

verses.text:
[७६म] हविष्यभुग् वा-अनुसरेत् प्रतिस्रोतः सरस्वतीम्
                                    ।
[७६म्च्] जपेद् वा नियत.आहारस् त्रिर् वै वेदस्य संहिताम्
                                    ॥ ७७ ॥
verses.english: Or he may present to a Brahmana, learned in the Vedas, whole property, as much wealth as suffices for the maintenance (of the recipient), or a house together with the furniture;

verses.text:
[७७म] कृत.वापनो निवसेद् ग्रामान्ते गोव्रजे ऽपि वा ।
[७७म्च्] आश्रमे वृक्षमूले वा गो.ब्राह्मणहिते रतः ॥ ७८
                                    ॥
verses.english: Or, subsisting on sacrificial food, he may walk against the stream along (the whole course of the river) Sarasvati; or, restricting his food (very much), he may mutter thrice the Samhita of a Veda.

verses.text:
[७८म] ब्राह्मणार्थे गवार्थे वा सद्यः प्राणान् परित्यजेत्
                                    । ११.७९अ[७८म]व्/ म्: संयक् प्राणान्
[७८म्च्] मुच्यते ब्रह्महत्याया गोप्ता गोर् ब्राह्मणस्य च ॥
                                    ७९ ॥
verses.english: Having shaved off (all his hair), he may dwell at the extremity of the village, or in a cow-pen, or in a hermitage, or at the root of a tree, taking pleasure in doing good to cows and Brahmanas.

verses.text:
[७९म] त्रिवारं प्रतिरोद्धा वा सर्वस्वम् अवजित्य वा ।
                                        ११.८०अ[७९म]व्/ म्: त्र्यवरं
[७९म्च्] विप्रस्य तन्निमित्ते वा प्राणालाभे विमुच्यते ॥ ८०
                                    ॥ ११.८०च्[७९म्च्]व्/ म्: प्राणालाभे ऽपि मुच्यते ॥ 11.80 ॥
verses.english: He who unhesitatingly abandons life for the sake of Brahmanas or of cows, is freed from (the guilt of) the murder of a Brahmana, and (so is he) who saves (the life of) a cow, or of a Brahmana.

verses.text:
[८०म] एवं दृढ.व्रतो नित्यं ब्रह्मचारी समाहितः ।
[८०म्च्] समाप्ते द्वादशे वर्षे ब्रह्महत्याम् व्यपोहति ॥ ८१
                                    ॥
verses.english: If either he fights at least three times (against robbers in defence of) a Brahmana's (property), or reconquers the whole property of a Brahmana, or if he loses his life for such a cause, he is freed (from his guilt).

verses.text:
[८१म] शिष्ट्वा वा भूमिदेवानां नरदेवसमागमे ।
[८१म्च्] स्वम् एनो ऽवभृथस्नातो हयमेधे विमुच्यते ॥ ८२
                                    ॥
verses.english: He who thus (remains) always firm in his vow, chaste, and of concentrated mind, removes after the lapse of twelve years (the guilt of) slaying a Brahmana.

verses.text:
[८२म] धर्मस्य ब्राह्मणो मूलम् अग्रं राजन्य उच्यते
                                    ।
[८२म्च्] तस्मात् समागमे तेषाम् एनो विख्याप्य शुध्यति ॥ ८३
                                    ॥
verses.english: Or he who, after confessing his crime in an assembly of the gods of the earth (Brahnanas), and the gods of men (Kshatriyas), bathes (with the priests) at the close of a horse-sacrifice, is (also) freed (from guilt).

verses.text:
[८३म] ब्रह्मणः सम्भवेन-एव देवानाम् अपि दैवतम्
                                    ।
[८३म्च्] प्रमाणं च-एव लोकस्य ब्रह्मात्र-एव हि कारणम्
                                    ॥ ८४ ॥
verses.english: The Brahmana is declared (to be) the root of the sacred law and the Kshatriya its top; hence he who has confessed his sin before an assembly of such men, becomes pure.

verses.text:
[८४म] तेषां वेदविदो ब्रूयुस् त्रयो ऽप्य् एनः सुनिष्कृतिम्
                                    ।
[८४म्च्] सा तेषां पावनाय स्यात् पवित्रा विदुषां हि वाक् ॥
                                    ८५ ॥ ११.८५च्[८४म्च्]व्/ म्: पवित्रं ॥ 11.85 ॥
verses.english: By his origin alone a Brahmana is a deity even for the gods, and (his teaching is) authoritative for men, because the Veda is the foundation for that.

verses.text:
[८५म] अतो ऽन्यतमम् आस्थाय विधिं विप्रः समाहितः
                                    ।
[८५म्च्] ब्रह्महत्याकृतं पापं व्यपोहत्य् आत्मवत्तया ॥ ८६
                                    ॥
verses.english: (If) only three of them who are learned in the Veda proclaim the expiation for offences, that shall purify the (sinners); for the words of learned men are a means of purification.

verses.text:
[८६म] हत्वा गर्भम् अविज्ञातम् एतद् एव व्रतं चरेत्
                                    ।
[८६म्च्] राजन्य.वैश्यौ च-ईजानाव् आत्रेयीम् एव च स्त्रियम्
                                    ॥ ८७ ॥
verses.english: A Brahmana who, with a concentrated mind, follows any of the (above-mentioned) rules, removes the sin committed by slaying a Brahmana through his self-control.

verses.text:
[८७म] उक्त्वा च-एव-अनृतं साक्ष्ये प्रतिरुध्य गुरुं तथा
                                    । ११.८८अ[८७म]व्/ म्: प्रतिरभ्य
[८७म्च्] अपहृत्य च निःक्षेपं कृत्वा च स्त्री.सुहृत्.वधम्
                                    ॥ ८८ ॥ ११.८८च्[८७म्च्]व्/ म्: निक्षेपं ॥ 11.88 ॥
verses.english: For destroying the embryo (of a Brahmana, the sex of which was) unknown, for slaying a Kshatriya or a Vaisya who are (engaged in or) have offered a (Vedic) sacrifice, or a (Brahmana) woman who has bathed after temporary uncleanness (Atreyi), he must perform the same penance,

verses.text:
[८८म] इयं विशुद्धिर् उदिता प्रमाप्य-अकामतो द्विजम् ।
[८८म्च्] कामतो ब्राह्मणवधे निष्कृतिर् न विधीयते ॥ ८९
                                    ॥
verses.english: Likewise for giving false evidence (in an important cause), for passionately abusing the teacher, for stealing a deposit, and for killing (his) wife or his friend:

verses.text:
[८९म] सुरां पीत्वा द्विजो मोहाद् अग्नि.वर्णां सुरां पिबेत्
                                    ।
[८९म्च्] तया स काये निर्दग्धे मुच्यते किल्बिषात् ततः ॥
                                    ९० ॥
verses.english: This expiation has been prescribed for unintentionally killing a Brahmana; but for intentionally slaying a Brahmana no atonement is ordained.

verses.text:
[९०म] गोमूत्रम् अग्नि.वर्णं वा पिबेद् उदकम् एव वा ।
[९०म्च्] पयो घृतं वा-आ मरणाद् गोशकृद्रसम् एव वा ॥ ९१
                                    ॥
verses.english: A twice-born man who has (intentionally) drunk, through delusion of mind, (the spirituous liquor called) Sura shall drink that liquor boiling-hot; when his body has been completely scalded by that, he is freed from his guilt;

verses.text:
[९१म] कणान् वा भक्षयेद् अब्दं पिण्याकं वा सकृत्-निशि
                                    ।
[९१म्च्] सुरापानापनुत्त्यर्थं वालवासा जटी ध्वजी ॥ ९२
                                    ॥
verses.english: Or he may drink cow's urine, water, milk, clarified butter or (liquid) cowdung boiling-hot, until he dies;

verses.text:
[९२म] सुरा वै मलम् अन्नानां पाप्मा च मलम् उच्यते ।
[९२म्च्] तस्माद् ब्राह्मण.राजन्यौ वैश्यश् च न सुरां पिबेत्
                                    ॥ ९३ ॥
verses.english: Or, in order to remove (the guilt of) drinking Sura, he may eat during a year once (a day) at night grains (of rice) or oilcake, wearing clothes made of cowhair and his own hair in braids and carrying (a wine cup as) a flag.

verses.text:
[९३म] गौडी पैष्टी च माध्वी च विज्ञेया त्रिविधा सुरा
                                    ।
[९३म्च्] यथा-एव-एका तथा सर्वा न पातव्या द्विजोत्तमैः
                                    ॥ ९४ ॥
verses.english: Sura, indeed, is the dirty refuse (mala) of grain, sin also is called dirt (mala); hence a Brahmana, a Kshatriya, and a Vaisya shall not drink Sura.

verses.text:
[९४म] यक्ष.रक्षः.पिशाच.अन्नं मद्यं मांसं सुरासवम्
                                    ।
[९४म्च्] तद् ब्राह्मणेन न-अत्तव्यं देवानाम् अश्नता हविः ॥
                                    ९५ ॥
verses.english: Sura one must know to be of three kinds, that distilled from molasses (gaudi), that distilled from ground rice, and that distilled from Madhuka-flowers (madhvi); as the one (named above) even so are all (three sorts) forbidden to the chief of the twice-born.

verses.text:
[९५म] अमेध्ये वा पतेन् मत्तो वैदिकं वा-अप्य् उदाहरेत्
                                    ।
[९५म्च्] अकार्यम् अन्यत् कुर्याद् वा ब्राह्मणो मदमोहितः ॥ ९६
                                    ॥
verses.english: Sura, (all other) intoxicating drinks and decoctions and flesh are the food of the Yakshas, Rakshasas, and Pisakas; a Brahmana who eats (the remnants of) the offerings consecrated to the gods, must not partake of such (substances).

verses.text:
[९६म] यस्य कायगतं ब्रह्म मद्येन-आप्लाव्यते सकृत्
                                    ।
[९६म्च्] तस्य व्यपैति ब्राह्मण्यं शूद्रत्वं च स गच्छति
                                    ॥ ९७ ॥
verses.english: A Brahmana, stupefied by drunkenness, might fall on something impure, or (improperly) pronounce Vedic (texts), or commit some other act which ought not to be committed.

verses.text:
[९७म] एषा विचित्राभिहिता सुरापानस्य निष्कृतिः ।
[९७म्च्] अत ऊर्ध्वं प्रवक्ष्यामि सुवर्णस्तेयनिष्कृतिम् ॥ ९८
                                    ॥
verses.english: When the Brahman (the Veda) which dwells in his body is (even) once (only) deluged with spirituous liquor, his Brahmanhood forsakes him and he becomes a Sudra.

verses.text:
[९८म] सुवर्णस्तेयकृद् विप्रो राजानम् अभिगम्य तु ।
[९८म्च्] स्वकर्म ख्यापयन् ब्रूयात्-मां भवान् अनुशास्त्व् इति
                                    ॥ ९९ ॥
verses.english: The various expiations for drinking (the spirituous liquors called) Sura have thus been explained; I will next proclaim the atonement for stealing the gold (of a Brahmana).

verses.text:
[९९म] गृहीत्वा मुसलं राजा सकृद्द् हन्यात् तु तं स्वयम्
                                    ।
[९९म्च्] वधेन शुध्यति स्तेनो ब्राह्मणस् तपसा-एव तु ॥
                                    १०० ॥
verses.english: A Brahmana who has stolen the gold (of a Brahmana) shall go to the king and, confessing his deed, say, 'Lord, punish me!'

verses.text:
[१००म] तपसापनुनुत्सुस् तु सुवर्णस्तेयजं मलम् ।
[१००म्च्] चीरवासा द्विजो ऽरण्ये चरेद् ब्रह्महणो व्रतम् ॥
                                    १०१ ॥
verses.english: Taking (from him) the club (which he must carry), the king himself shall strike him once, by his death the thief becomes pure; or a Brahmana (may purify himself) by austerities.

verses.text:
[१०१म] एतैर् व्रतैर् अपोहेत पापं स्तेयकृतं द्विजः
                                    ।
[१०१म्च्] गुरुस्त्रीगमनी-इयं तु व्रतैर् एभिर् अपानुदेत् ॥
                                    १०२ ॥
verses.english: He who desires to remove by austerities the guilt of stealing the gold (of a Brahmana), shall perform the penance (prescribed) for the slayer of a Brahmana, (living) in a forest and dressed in (garments) made of bark.

verses.text:
[१०२म] गुरुतल्प्य् अभिभाष्य-एनस् तप्ते स्वप्याद् अयोमये
                                    । ११.१०३अ[१०२म]व्/ म्: तल्पे स्वप्याद्
[१०२म्च्] सूर्मीं ज्वलन्तीं स्वाश्लिष्येन् मृत्युना स
                                    विशुध्यति ॥ १०३ ॥ ११.१०३च्[१०२म्च्]व्/ म्: वा-आश्लिष्येन् ॥ 11.103 ॥
verses.english: By these penances a twice-born man may remove the guilt incurred by a theft (of gold); but he may atone for connexion with a Guru's wife by the following penances.

verses.text:
[१०३म] स्वयं वा शिष्ण.वृषणाव् उत्कृत्य-आधाय
                                    च-अञ्जलौ ।
[१०३म्च्] नैरृतीं दिशम् आतिष्ठेद् आ निपाताद् अजिह्मगः ॥
                                    १०४ ॥
verses.english: He who has violated his Guru's bed, shall, after confessing his crime, extend himself on a heated iron bed, or embrace the red-hot image (of a woman); by dying he becomes pure;

verses.text:
[१०४म] खट्वाङ्गी चीर.वासा वा श्मश्रुलो विजने वने
                                    ।
[१०४म्च्] प्राजापत्यं चरेत् कृच्छ्रम् अब्दम् एकं समाहितः
                                    ॥ १०५ ॥
verses.english: Or, having himself cut off his organ and his testicles and having taken them in his joined hands, he may walk straight towards the region of Nirriti (the south-west), until he falls down (dead);

verses.text:
[१०५म] चान्द्रायणं वा त्रीन् मासान् अभ्यस्येन्
                                    नियत.इन्द्रियः ।
[१०५म्च्] हविष्येण यवाग्वा वा गुरुतल्पापनुत्तये ॥ १०६
                                    ॥
verses.english: Or, carrying the foot of a bedstead, dressed in (garments of) bark and allowing his beard to grow, he may, with a concentrated mind, perform during a whole year the Krikkhra (or hard, penance), revealed by Pragapati, in a lonely forest;

verses.text:
[१०६म] एतैर् व्रतैर् अपोहेयुर् महापातकिनो मलम् ।
[१०६म्च्] उपपातकिनस् त्व् एवम् एभिर् नानाविधैर् व्रतैः
                                    ॥ १०७ ॥
verses.english: Or, controlling his organs, he may during three months continuously perform the lunar penance, (subsisting) on sacrificial food or barley-gruel, in order to remove (the guilt of) violating a Guru's bed.

verses.text:
[१०७म] उपपातकसंयुक्तो गोघ्नो मासं यवान् पिबेत् ।
[१०७म्च्] कृत.वापो वसेद् गोष्ठे चर्मणा तेन संवृतः ॥
                                    १०८ ॥
verses.english: By means of these penances men who have committed mortal sins (Mahapataka) may remove their guilt, but those who committed minor offences, causing loss of caste, (Upapataka, can do it) by the various following penances.

verses.text:
[१०८म] चतुर्थकालम् अश्नीयाद् अ.क्षार.लवणं मितम्
                                    ।
[१०८म्च्] गोमूत्रेण-आचरेत् स्नानं द्वौ मासौ
                                    नियत.इन्द्रियः ॥ १०९ ॥
verses.english: He who has committed a minor offence by slaying a cow (or bull) shall drink during (the first) month (a decoction of) barley-grains; having shaved all his hair, and covering himself with the hide (of the slain cow), he must live in a cow-house.

verses.text:
[१०९म] दिवा-अनुगच्छेद् गास् तास् तु तिष्ठन्न् ऊर्ध्वं
                                    रजः पिबेत् ।
[१०९म्च्] शुश्रूषित्वा नमस्कृत्य रात्रौ वीरासनं वसेत् ॥
                                    ११० ॥ ११.११०च्[१०९म्च्]व्/ म्: वीरासनो ॥ 11.110 ॥
verses.english: During the two (following) months he shall eat a small (quantity of food) without any factitious salt at every fourth meal-time, and shall bathe in the urine of cows, keeping his organs under control.

verses.text:
[११०म] तिष्ठन्तीष्व् अनुतिष्ठेत् तु व्रजन्तीष्व् अप्य्
                                    अनुव्रजेत् ।
[११०म्च्] आसीनासु तथा-आसीनो नियतो वीत.मत्सरः ॥ १११
                                    ॥
verses.english: During the day he shall follow the cows and, standing upright, inhale the dust (raised by their hoofs); at night, after serving and worshipping them, he shall remain in the (posture, called) virasana.

verses.text:
[१११म] आतुराम् अभिशस्तां वा चौर.व्याघ्रादिभिर् भयैः
                                    ।
[१११म्च्] पतितां पङ्कलग्नं वा सर्व.उपायैर् विमोचयेत्
                                    ॥ ११२ ॥ ११.११२च्[१११म्च्]व्/ क्: सर्वप्राणैर् ॥ 11.112 ॥
verses.english: Controlling himself and free from anger, he must stand when they stand, follow them when they walk, and seat himself when they lie down.

verses.text:
[११२म] उष्णे वर्षति शीते वा मारुते वाति वा भृशम् ।
[११२म्च्] न कुर्वीत-आत्मनस् त्राणं गोर् अ.कृत्वा तु
                                    शक्तितः ॥ ११३ ॥
verses.english: (When a cow is) sick, or is threatened by danger from thieves, tigers, and the like, or falls, or sticks in a morass, he must relieve her by all possible means:

verses.text:
[११३म] आत्मनो यदि वा-अन्येषां गृहे क्षेत्रे ऽथ वा खले
                                    ।
[११३म्च्] भक्षयन्तीं न कथयेत् पिबन्तं च-एव
                                    वत्सकम् ॥ ११४ ॥
verses.english: In heat, in rain, or in cold, or when the wind blows violently, he must not seek to shelter himself, without (first) sheltering the cows according to his ability.

verses.text:
[११४म] अनेन विधिना यस् तु गोघ्नो गाम् अनुगच्छति
                                    ।
[११४म्च्] स गोहत्याकृतं पापं त्रिभिर् मासैर् व्यपोहति
                                    ॥ ११५ ॥
verses.english: Let him not say (a word), if a cow eats (anything) in his own or another's house or field or on the threshing-floor, or if a calf drinks (milk).

verses.text:
[११५म] वृषभ.एकादशा गाश् च दद्यात् सुचरित.व्रतः
                                    ।
[११५म्च्] अ.विद्यमाने सर्वस्वं वेदविद्भ्यो निवेदयेत् ॥
                                    ११६ ॥
verses.english: The slayer of a cow who serves cows in this manner, removes after three months the guilt which he incurred by killing a cow.

verses.text:
[११६म] एतद् एव व्रतं कुर्युर् उपपातकिनो द्विजाः ।
[११६म्च्] अवकीर्णिवर्ज्यं शुद्ध्यर्थं चान्द्रायणम्
                                    अथ-अपि वा ॥ ११७ ॥ ११.११७च्[११६म्च्]व्/ म्: 
                                    अवकीर्णिवर्जं ॥ 11.117 ॥
verses.english: But after he has fully performed the penance, he must give to (Brahmanas) learned in the Veda ten cows and a bull, (or) if he does not possess (so much property) he must offer to them all he has.

verses.text:
[११७म] अवकीर्णी तु काणेन गर्दभेन चतुष्पथे ।
[११७म्च्] पाकयज्ञविधानेन यजेत निरृतिं निशि ॥ ११८
                                    ॥
verses.english: Twice-born men who have committed (other) minor offences (Upapataka), except a student who has broken his vow (Avakirnin), may perform, in order to purify themselves, the same penance or also a lunar penance.

verses.text:
[११८म] हुत्वा-अग्नौ विधिवद्द् होमान् अन्ततश् च सम-इत्य्
                                    ऋचा ।
[११८म्च्] वात.इन्द्र.गुरु.वह्नीनां जुहुयात् सर्पिषा-आहुतीः
                                    ॥ ११९ ॥
verses.english: But a student who has broken his vow shall offer at night on a crossway to Nirriti a one-eyed ass, according to the rule of the Pakayagnas.

verses.text:
[११९म] कामतो रेतसः सेकं व्रतस्थस्य द्विजन्मनः
                                    ।
[११९म्च्] अतिक्रमं व्रतस्य-आहुर् धर्मज्ञा ब्रह्मवादिनः
                                    ॥ १२० ॥
verses.english: Having offered according to the rule oblations in the fire, he shall finally offer (four) oblations of clarified butter to Vata, to Indra, to the teacher (of the gods, Brihaspati) and to Agni, reciting the Rik verse 'May the Maruts grant me,' &c.

verses.text:
[१२०म] मारुतं पुरुहूतं च गुरुं पावकम् एव च ।
[१२०म्च्] चतुरो व्रतिनो ऽभ्येति ब्राह्मं तेजो ऽवकीर्णिनः
                                    ॥ १२१ ॥
verses.english: Those who know the Veda declare that a voluntary effusion of semen by a twice-born (youth) who fulfils the vow (of studentship constitutes) a breach of that vow.

verses.text:
[१२१म] एतस्मिन्न् एनसि प्राप्ते वसित्वा गर्दभाजिनम्
                                    ।
[१२१म्च्] सप्तागारांश् चरेद् भैक्षं स्वकर्म परिकीर्तयन्
                                    ॥ १२२ ॥
verses.english: The divine light which the Veda imparts to the student, enters, if he breaks his vow, the Maruts, Puruhuta (Indra), the teacher (of the gods, Brihaspati) and Pavaka (Fire).

verses.text:
[१२२म] तेभ्यो लब्धेन भैक्षेण वर्तयन्न् एककालिकम्
                                    ।
[१२२म्च्] उपस्पृशंस् त्रिषवणं त्व् अब्देन स विशुध्यति ॥
                                    १२३ ॥ ११.१२३च्[१२२म्च्]व्/ म्: त्रिषवणम् अब्देन ॥ 11.123 ॥
verses.english: When this sin has been committed, he shall go begging to seven houses, dressed in the hide of the (sacrificed) ass, proclaiming his deed.

verses.text:
[१२३म] जातिभ्रंशकरं कर्म कृत्वा-अन्यतमम् इच्छया
                                    ।
[१२३म्च्] चरेत् सान्तपनं कृच्छ्रं प्राजापत्यम् अनिच्छया
                                    ॥ १२४ ॥
verses.english: Subsisting on a single (daily meal that consists) of the alms obtained there and bathing at (the time of) the three savanas (morning, noon, and evening), he becomes pure after (the lapse of) one year.

verses.text:
[१२४म] सङ्कर.अपात्रकृत्यासु मासं शोधनम् ऐन्दवम् ।
                                    ११.१२५अ[१२४म]व्/ म्: ऐन्दवः
[१२४म्च्] मलिनीकरणीयेषु तप्तः स्याद् यावकैस् त्र्यहम् ॥ १२५
                                ॥
verses.english: For committing with intent any of the deeds which cause loss of caste (Gatibhramsakara), (the offender) shall perform a Samtapana Krikkhra; (for doing it) unintentionally, (the Krikkhra) revealed by Pragapati.

verses.text:
[१२५म] तुरीयो ब्रह्महत्यायाः क्षत्रियस्य वधे स्मृतः ।
[१२५म्च्] वैश्ये ऽष्टमांशो वृत्तस्थे शूद्रे ज्ञेयस् तु षोडशः
                                ॥ १२६ ॥
verses.english: As atonement for deeds which degrade to a mixed caste (Samkara), and for those which make a man unworthy to receive gifts (Apatra), (he shall perform) the lunar (penance) during a month; for (acts) which render impure (Malinikaraniya) he shall scald himself during three days with (hot) barley-gruel.

verses.text:
[१२६म] अकामतस् तु राजन्यं विनिपात्य द्विजोत्तमः ।
[१२६म्च्] वृषभ.एकसहस्रा गा दद्यात् सुचरित.व्रतः ॥
                                    १२७ ॥
verses.english: One fourth (of the penance) for the murder of a Brahmana is prescribed (as expiation) for (intentionally) killing a Kshatriya, one-eighth for killing a Vaisya; know that it is one-sixteenth for killing a virtuous Sudra.

verses.text:
[१२७म] त्र्यब्दं चरेद् वा नियतो जटी ब्रह्महणो व्रतम्
                                    ।
[१२७म्च्] वसन् दूरतरे ग्रामाद् वृक्षमूल.निकेतनः ॥ १२८
                                    ॥
verses.english: But if a Brahmana unintentionally kills a Kshatriya, he shall give, in order to purify himself, one thousand cows and a bull;

verses.text:
[१२८म] एतद् एव चरेद् अब्दं प्रायश्चित्तं द्विजोत्तमः
                                    ।
[१२८म्च्] प्रमाप्य वैश्यं वृत्तस्थं दद्याच् च-एकशतं
                                    ॥ १२९ ॥ ११.१२९च्[१२८म्च्]व्/ म्: दद्याद् वा-एकशतं गवाम् ॥ 11.129 ॥
verses.english: Or he may perform the penance prescribed for the murderer of a Brahmana during three years, controlling himself, wearing his hair in braids, staying far away from the village, and dwelling at the root of a tree.

verses.text:
[१२९म] एतद् एव व्रतं कृत्स्नं षण्मासान्-शूद्रहा चरेत्
                                    ।
[१२९म्च्] वृषभ.एकादशा वा-अपि दद्याद् विप्राय गाः सिताः
                                    ॥ १३० ॥
verses.english: A Brahmana who has slain a virtuous Vaisya, shall perform the same penance during one year, or he may give one hundred cows and one (bull).

verses.text:
[१३०म] मार्जार.नकुलौ हत्वा चाषं मण्डूकम् एव च
                                    ।
[१३०म्च्] श्व.गोधा.उलूक.काकांश् च शूद्रहत्याव्रतं चरेत्
                                    ॥ १३१ ॥
verses.english: He who has slain a Sudra, shall perform that whole penance during six months, or he may also give ten white cows and one bull to a Brahmana.

verses.text:
[१३१म] पयः पिबेत् त्रिरात्रं वा योजनं वा-अध्वनो
                                    व्रजेत् ।
[१३१म्च्] उपस्पृशेत् स्रवन्त्यां वा सूक्तं वा-अब्.दैवतं
                                    जपेत् ॥ १३२ ॥
verses.english: Having killed a cat, an ichneumon, a blue jay, a frog, a dog, an iguana, an owl, or a crow, he shall perform the penance for the murder of a Sudra;

verses.text:
[१३२म] अभ्रिं कार्ष्णायसीं दद्यात् सर्पं हत्वा
                                    द्विजोत्तमः ।
[१३२म्च्] पलालभारकं षण्ढे सैसकं च-एकमाषकम् ॥
                                    १३३ ॥
verses.english: Or he may drink milk during three days, or walk one hundred yoganas, or bathe in a river, or mutter the hymn addressed to the Waters.

verses.text:
[१३३म] घृतकुम्भं वराहे तु तिलद्रोणं तु तित्तिरौ
                                    ।
[१३३म्च्] शुके द्विहायनं वत्सं क्रौञ्चं हत्वा त्रिहायनम्
                                    ॥ १३४ ॥
verses.english: For killing a snake, a Brahmana shall give a spade of black iron, for a eunuch a load of straw and a masha of lead;

verses.text:
[१३४म] हत्वा हंसं बलाकां च बकं बर्हिणम् एव च
                                    ।
[१३४म्च्] वानरं श्येन.भासौ च स्पर्शयेद् ब्राह्मणाय गाम्
                                    ॥ १३५ ॥
verses.english: For a boar a pot of clarified butter, for a partridge a drona of sesamum-grains, for a parrot a calf two years old, for a crane (a calf) three years old.

verses.text:
[१३५म] वासो दद्याद्द् हयं हत्वा पञ्च नीलान् वृषान् गजम्
                                    ।
[१३५म्च्] अज.मेषाव् अनड्वाहं खरं हत्वा-एकहायनम् ॥
                                    १३६ ॥
verses.english: If he has killed a Hamsa, a Balaka, a heron, a peacock, a monkey, a falcon, or a Bhasa, he shall give a cow to a Brahmana.

verses.text:
[१३६म] क्रव्यादांस् तु मृगान् हत्वा धेनुं दद्यात्
                                    पयस्विनीम् ।
[१३६म्च्] अक्रव्यादान् वत्सतरीम् उष्ट्रं हत्वा तु कृष्णलम्
                                    ॥ १३७ ॥
verses.english: For killing a horse, he shall give a garment, for (killing) an elephant, five black bulls, for (killing) a goat, or a sheep, a draught-ox, for killing a donkey, (a calf) one year old;

verses.text:
[१३७म] जीन.कार्मुक.बस्त.अवीन् पृथग् दद्याद् विशुद्धये
                                    ।
[१३७म्च्] चतुर्णाम् अपि वर्णानां नारीर् हत्वा-अन्.अवस्थिताः
                                    ॥ १३८ ॥
verses.english: But for killing carnivorous wild beasts, he shall give a milch-cow, for (killing) wild beasts that are not carnivorous, a heifer, for killing a camel, one krishnala.

verses.text:
[१३८म] दानेन वधनिर्णेकं सर्पादीनाम् अ.शक्नुवन् ।
[१३८म्च्] एकैकशश् चरेत् कृच्छ्रं द्विजः पापापनुत्तये ॥
                                    १३९ ॥
verses.english: For killing adulterous women of the four castes, he must give, in order to purify himself, respectively a leathern bag, a bow, a goat, or a sheep.

verses.text:
[१३९म] अस्थिमतां तु सत्त्वानां सहस्रस्य प्रमापणे
                                    ।
[१३९म्च्] पूर्णे च-अनस्य् अन्.अस्थ्नां तु शूद्रहत्याव्रतं
                                    चरेत् ॥ १४० ॥
verses.english: A twice-born man, who is unable to atone by gifts for the slaughter of a serpent and the other (creatures mentioned), shall perform for each of them, a Krikkhra (penance) in order to remove his guilt.

verses.text:
[१४०म] किं चिद् एव तु विप्राय दद्याद् अस्थिमतां वधे
                                    ।
[१४०म्च्] अन्.अस्थ्नां च-एव हिंसायां प्राणायामेन शुध्यति
                                    ॥ १४१ ॥
verses.english: But for destroying one thousand (small) animals that have bones, or a whole cart-load of boneless (animals), he shall perform the penance (prescribed) for the murder of a Sudra.

verses.text:
[१४१म] फलदानां तु वृक्षाणां छेदने जप्यम् ऋच्.शतम्
                                    ।
[१४१म्च्] गुल्म.वल्ली.लतानां च पुष्पितानां च वीरुधाम् ॥
                                    १४२ ॥
verses.english: But for killing (small) animals which have bones, he should give some trifle to a Brahmana; if he injures boneless (animals), he becomes pure by a suppressing his breath (pranayama).

verses.text:
[१४२म] अन्नाद्यजानां सत्त्वानां रसजानां च सर्वशः
                                    ।
[१४२म्च्] फल.पुष्प.उद्भवानां च घृतप्राशो विशोधनम्
                                    ॥ १४३ ॥
verses.english: For cutting fruit-trees, shrubs, creepers, lianas, or flowering plants, one hundred Rikas must be muttered.

verses.text:
[१४३म] कृष्तजानाम् ओषधीनां जातानां च स्वयं वने
                                    ।
[१४३म्च्] वृथालम्भे ऽनुगच्छेद् गां दिनम् एकं
                                    पयो.व्रतः ॥ १४४ ॥
verses.english: (For destroying) any kind of creature, bred in food, in condiments, in fruit, or in flowers, the expiation is to eat clarified butter.

verses.text:
[१४४म] एतैर् व्रतैर् अपोह्यं स्याद् एनो हिंसा.समुद्भवम्
                                    ।
[१४४म्च्] ज्ञान.अज्ञानकृतं कृत्स्नं शृणुत-अनाद्यभक्षणे
                                    ॥ १४५ ॥
verses.english: If a man destroys for no good purpose plants produced by cultivation, or such as spontaneously spring up in the forest, he shall attend a cow during one day, subsisting on milk alone.

verses.text:
[१४५म] अज्ञानाद् वारुणीं पीत्वा संस्कारेण-एव शुध्यति
                                    ।
[१४५म्च्] मतिपूर्वम् अनिर्देश्यं प्राणान्तिकम् इति स्थितिः ॥
                                    १४६ ॥
verses.english: The guilt incurred intentionally or unintentionally by injuring (created beings) can be removed by means of these penances; hear (now, how) all (sins) committed by partaking of forbidden food (or drink, can be expiated).

verses.text:
[१४६म] अपः सुराभाजनस्था मद्यभाण्डस्थितास् तथा ।
[१४६म्च्] पञ्चरात्रं पिबेत् पीत्वा शङ्खपुष्पीशृतं पयः ॥
                                १४७ ॥
verses.english: He who drinks unintentionally (the spirituous liquor, called) Varuni, becomes pure by being initiated (again); (even for drinking it) intentionally (a penance) destructive to life must not be imposed; that is a settled rule.

verses.text:
[१४७म] स्पृष्ट्व दत्त्वा च मदिरां विधिवत् प्रतिगृह्य च
                                ।
[१४७म्च्] शूद्र.उच्छिष्टाश् च पीत्वा-अपः कुशवारि पिबेत् त्र्यहम्
                                ॥ १४८ ॥
verses.english: He who has drunk water which has stood in a vessel used for keeping (the spirituous liquor, called) Sura, or other intoxicating drinks, shall drink during five (days and) nights (nothing but) milk in which the Sankhapushpi (plant) has been boiled.

verses.text:
[१४८म] ब्राह्मणस् तु सुरापस्य गन्धम् आघ्राय सोमपः ।
[१४८म्च्] प्राणान् अप्सु त्रिर् आयम्य घृतं प्राश्य विशुध्यति ॥
                                १४९ ॥
verses.english: He who has touched spirituous liquor, has given it away, or received it in accordance with the rule, or has drunk water left by a Sudra, shall drink during three days water in which Kusa-grass has been boiled.

verses.text:
[१४९म] अज्ञानात् प्राश्य विष्.मूत्रं सुरासंस्पृष्टम् एव च
                                ।
[१४९म्च्] पुनः संस्कारम् अर्हन्ति त्रयो वर्णा द्विजातयः ॥
                                १५० ॥
verses.english: But when a Brahmana who has partaken of Soma-juice, has smelt the odour exhaled by a drinker of Sura, he becomes pure by thrice suppressing his breath in water, and eating clarified butter.

verses.text:
[१५०म] वपनं मेखला दण्डो भैक्षचर्या व्रतानि च ।
                                    ११.१५१अ[१५०म]व्/ म्: भैक्ष्यचर्या
[१५०म्च्] निवर्तन्ते द्विजातीनां पुनःसंस्कारकर्मणि ॥ १५१
                                ॥
verses.english: (Men of) the three twice-born castes who have unintentionally swallowed ordure or urine, or anything that has touched Sura, must be initiated again.

verses.text:
[१५१म] अभोज्यानां तु भुक्त्वा-अन्नं स्त्री.शूद्र.उच्छिष्टम् एव
                                च ।
[१५१म्च्] जग्ध्वा मांसम् अभक्ष्यं च सप्तरात्रं यवान् पिबेत्
                                ॥ १५२ ॥
verses.english: The tonsure, (wearing) the sacred girdle, (carrying) a staff, going to beg, and the vows (incumbent on a student), are omitted on the second initiation of twice-born men.

verses.text:
[१५२म] शुक्तानि च कषायांश् च पीत्वा मेध्यान्य् अपि द्विजः
                                ।
[१५२म्च्] तावद् भवत्य् अ.प्रयतो यावत् तन् न व्रजत्य् अधः
                                ॥ १५३ ॥
verses.english: But he who has eaten the food of men, whose food must not be eaten, or the leavings of women and Sudras, or forbidden flesh, shall drink barley (-gruel) during seven (days and) nights.

verses.text:
[१५३म] विड्वराह.खर.उष्त्राणां गोमायोः कपि.काकयोः ।
[१५३म्च्] प्राश्य मूत्र.पुरीषाणि द्विजश् चान्द्रायणं चरेत् ॥
                                १५४ ॥
verses.english: A twice-born man who has drunk (fluids that have turned) sour, or astringent decoctions, becomes, though (these substances may) not (be specially) forbidden, impure until they have been digested.

verses.text:
[१५४म] शुष्काणि भुक्त्वा मांसानि भौमानि कवकानि च ।
[१५४म्च्] अज्ञातं च-एव सूनास्थम् एतद् एव व्रतं चरेत् ॥
                                १५५ ॥
verses.english: A twice-born man, who has swallowed the urine or ordure of a village pig, of a donkey, of a camel, of a jackal, of a monkey, or of a crow, shall perform a lunar penance.

verses.text:
[१५५म] क्रव्याद.सूकर.उष्ट्राणां कुक्कुटानां च भक्षणे
                                ।
[१५५म्च्] नर.काक.खराणां च तप्तकृच्छ्रं विशोधनम् ॥
                                १५६ ॥
verses.english: He who has eaten dried meat, mushrooms growing on the ground, or (meat, the nature of) which is unknown, (or) such as had been kept in a slaughter-house, shall perform the same penance.

verses.text:
[१५६म] मासिकान्नं तु यो ऽश्नीयाद् असमावर्तको द्विजः ।
[१५६म्च्] स त्रीण्य् अहान्य् उपवसेद् एकाहं च-उदके वसेत् ॥ १५७
                                ॥
verses.english: The atonement for partaking of (the meat of) carnivorous animals, of pigs, of camels, of cocks, of crows, of donkeys, and of human flesh, is a Tapta Krikkhra (penance).

verses.text:
[१५७म] ब्रह्मचारी तु यो ऽश्नीयान् मधु मांसं कथं चन ।
                                    ११.१५८अ[१५७म]व्/ म्: व्रतचारी तु
[१५७म्च्] स कृत्वा प्राकृतं कृच्छ्रं व्रतशेषं समापयेत् ॥
                                १५८ ॥
verses.english: If a twice-born man, who has not returned (home from his teacher's house), eats food, given at a monthly (Sraddha,) he shall fast during three days and pass one day (standing) in water.

verses.text:
[१५८म] बिडाल.काक.आखु.उच्छिष्टं जग्ध्वा श्व.नकुलस्य च
                                ।
[१५८म्च्] केश.कीटावपन्नं च पिबेद् ब्रह्मसुवर्चलाम् ॥ १५९
                                ॥
verses.english: But a student who on any occasion eats honey or meat, shall perform an ordinary Krikkhra (penance), and afterwards complete his vow (of studentship).

verses.text:
[१५९म] अभोज्यम् अन्नं न-अत्तव्यम् आत्मनः शुद्धिम् इच्छता
                                ।
[१५९म्च्] अज्ञानभुक्तं तु-उत्तार्यं शोध्यं वा-अप्य् आशु
                                शोधनैः ॥ १६० ॥
verses.english: He who eats what is left by a cat, by a crow, by a mouse (or rat), by a dog, or by an ichneumon, or (food) into which a hair or an insect has fallen, shall drink (a decoction of) the Brahmasuvarkala (plant).

verses.text:
[१६०म] एषो ऽनाद्य.अदनस्य-उक्तो व्रतानां विविधो विधिः
                                ।
[१६०म्च्] स्तेयदोषापहर्तॄणां व्रतानां श्रूयतां विधिः ॥ १६१
                                ॥
verses.english: He who desires to be pure, must not eat forbidden food, and must vomit up such as he has eaten unintentionally, or quickly atone for it by (various) means of purification.

verses.text:
[१६१म] धान्य.अन्न.धनचौर्याणि कृत्वा कामाद् द्विजोत्तमः
                                ।
[१६१म्च्] स्वजातीयगृहाद् एव कृच्छ्राब्देन विशुध्यति ॥ १६२
                                ॥
verses.english: The various rules respecting penances for eating forbidden food have been thus declared; hear now the law of those penances which remove the guilt of theft.

verses.text:
[१६२म] मनुष्याणां तु हरणे स्त्रीणां क्षेत्र.गृहस्य च ।
[१६२म्च्] कूप.वापीजलानां च शुद्धिश् चान्द्रायणं स्मृतम् ॥
                                १६३ ॥
verses.english: The chief of the twice-born, having voluntarily stolen (valuable) property, grain, or cooked food, from the house of a caste-fellow, is purified by performing Krikkhra (penances) during a whole year.

verses.text:
[१६३म] द्रव्याणाम् अल्प.साराणां स्तेयं कृत्वा-अन्यवेश्मतः ।
                                    ११.१६४अ[१६३म]व्/ म्: कृत्वा-अन्यवेश्मनि
[१६३म्च्] चरेत् सान्तपनं कृच्छ्रं तन् निर्यात्य् आत्मशुद्धये
                                ॥ १६४ ॥
verses.english: The lunar penance has been declared to be the expiation for stealing men and women, and (for wrongfully appropriating) a field, a house, or the water of wells and cisterns.

verses.text:
[१६४म] भक्ष्य.भोज्यापहरणे यान.शय्या.आसनस्य च ।
[१६४म्च्] पुष्प.मूल.फलानां च पञ्चगव्यं विशोधनम् ॥ १६५
                                ॥
verses.english: He who has stolen objects of small value from the house of another man, shall, after restoring the (stolen article), perform a Samtapana Krikkhra for his purification.

verses.text:
[१६५म] तृण.काष्ठ.द्रुमाणां च शुष्कान्नस्य गुडस्य च ।
[१६५म्च्] चेल.चर्म.आमिषाणां च त्रिरात्रं स्याद् अभोजनम् ॥
                                १६६ ॥ ११.१६६च्[१६५म्च्]व्/ म्: चैल.चर्म.आमिक्षाणां ॥ 11.166 ॥
verses.english: (To swallow) the five products of the cow (pankagavya) is the atonement for stealing eatables of various kinds, a vehicle, a bed, a seat, flowers, roots, or fruit.

verses.text:
[१६६म] मणि.मुक्ता.प्रवालानां ताम्रस्य रजतस्य च ।
[१६६म्च्] अयः.कांस्य.उपलानां च द्वादशाहं कणान्नता ॥ १६७
                                ॥
verses.english: Fasting during three (days and) nights shall be (the penance for stealing) grass, wood, trees, dry food, molasses, clothes, leather, and meat.

verses.text:
[१६७म] कार्पास.कीटज.ऊर्णानां द्विशफ.एकशफस्य च ।
                                    ११.१६८अ[१६७म]व्/ म्: द्वेशफ.एकखुरस्य च
[१६७म्च्] पक्षि.गन्ध.ओषधीनां च रज्ज्वाश् च-एव त्र्यहं
                                पयः ॥ १६८ ॥
verses.english: To subsist during twelve days on (uncooked) grains (is the penance for stealing) gems, pearls, coral, copper, silver, iron, brass, or stone.

verses.text:
[१६८म] एतैर् व्रतैर् अपोहेत पापं स्तेयकृतं द्विजः ।
[१६८म्च्] अगम्यागमनीयं तु व्रतैर् एभिर् अपानुदेत् ॥ १६९
                                ॥
verses.english: (For stealing) cotton, silk, wool, an animal with cloven hoofs, or one with uncloven hoofs, a bird, perfumes, medicinal herbs, or a rope (the penance is to subsist) during three days (on) milk.

verses.text:
[१६९म] गुरुतल्पव्रतं कुर्याद् रेतः सिक्त्वा स्वयोनिषु ।
[१६९म्च्] सख्युः पुत्रस्य च स्त्रीषु कुमारीष्व् अन्त्यजासु च ॥
                                १७० ॥
verses.english: By means of these penances, a twice-born man may remove the guilt of theft; but the guilt of approaching women who ought not to be approached (agamya), he may expiate by (the following) penances.

verses.text:
[१७०म] पैतृस्वसेयीं भगिनीं स्वस्रीयां मातुर् एव च ।
[१७०म्च्] मातुश् च भ्रातुस् तनयां गत्वा चान्द्रायणं चरेत् ॥
                                १७१ ॥ ११.१७१च्[१७०म्च्]व्/ ?: भ्रातुर् आप्तस्य गत्वा ॥ 11.171 ॥
verses.english: He who has had sexual intercourse with sisters by the same mother, with the wives of a friend, or of a son, with unmarried maidens, and with females of the lowest castes, shall perform the penance, prescribed for the violation of a Guru's bed.

verses.text:
[१७१म] एतास् तिस्रस् तु भार्यार्थे न-उपयच्छेत् तु बुद्धिमान्
                                ।
[१७१म्च्] ज्ञातित्वेन-अन्.उपेयास् ताः पतति ह्य् उपयन्न् अधः ॥
                                १७२ ॥
verses.english: He who has approached the daughter of his father's sister, (who is almost equal to) a sister, (the daughter) of his mother's sister, or of his mother's full brother, shall perform a lunar penance.

verses.text:
[१७२म] अमानुषीषू पुरुष उदक्यायाम् अयोनिषु ।
[१७२म्च्] रेतः सिक्त्वा जले च-एव कृच्छ्रं सान्तपनं चरेत्
                                ॥ १७३ ॥
verses.english: A wise man should not take as his wife any of these three; they must not be wedded because they are (Sapinda-) relatives, he who marries (one of them), sinks low.

verses.text:
[१७३म] मैथुनं तु समासेव्य पुंसि योषिति वा द्विजः ।
[१७३म्च्] गो.याने ऽप्सु दिवा च-एव स.वासाः स्नानम् आचरेत् ॥
                                १७४ ॥
verses.english: A man who has committed a bestial crime, or an unnatural crime with a female, or has had intercourse in water, or with a menstruating woman, shall perform a Samtapana Krikkhra.

verses.text:
[१७४म] चण्डाल.अन्त्यस्त्रियो गत्वा भुक्त्वा च प्रतिगृह्य च
                                ।
[१७४म्च्] पतत्य् अज्ञानतो विप्रो ज्ञानात् साम्यं तु गच्छति ॥
                                १७५ ॥
verses.english: A twice-born man who commits an unnatural offence with a male, or has intercourse with a female in a cart drawn by oxen, in water, or in the day-time, shall bathe, dressed in his clothes.

verses.text:
[१७५म] विप्रदुष्टां स्त्रियं भर्ता निरुन्ध्याद् एकवेश्मनि
                                ।
[१७५म्च्] यत् पुंसः परदारेषु तच् च-एनां चारयेद् व्रतम् ॥
                                १७६ ॥
verses.english: A Brahmana who unintentionally approaches a woman of the Kandala or of (any other) very low caste, who eats (the food of such persons) and accepts (presents from them) becomes an outcast; but (if he does it) intentionally, he becomes their equal.

verses.text:
[१७६म] सा चेत् पुनः प्रदुष्येत् तु सदृशेन-उपमन्त्रिता ।
                                    ११.१७७अ[१७६म]व्/ क्: सदृशेन-उपयन्त्रिता?
[१७६म्च्] कृच्छ्रं चान्द्रायणं च-एव तद् अस्याः पावनं स्मृतम्
                                ॥ १७७ ॥
verses.english: An exceedingly corrupt wife let her husband confine to one apartment, and compel her to perform the penance which is prescribed for males in cases of adultery.

verses.text:
[१७७म] यत् करोत्य् एकरात्रेण वृषलीसेवनाद् द्विजः ।
[१७७म्च्] तद् भैक्षभुज्-जपन् नित्यं त्रिभिर् वर्षैर्
                                व्यपोहति ॥ १७८ ॥
verses.english: If, being solicited by a man (of) equal (caste), she (afterwards) is again unfaithful, then a Krikkhra and a lunar penance are prescribed as the means of purifying her.

verses.text:
[१७८म] एषा पापकृताम् उक्ता चतुर्णाम् अपि निष्कृतिः ।
[१७८म्च्] पतितैः सम्प्रयुक्तानाम् इमाः शृणुत निष्कृतीः ॥ १७९
                                ॥
verses.english: The sin which a twice-born man commits by dallying one night with a Vrishali, he removes in three years, by subsisting on alms and daily muttering (sacred texts).

verses.text:
[१७९म] संवत्सरेण पतति पतितेन सह-आचरन् ।
[१७९म्च्] याजन.अध्यापनाद् यौनात्-न तु यान.आसन.अशनात् ॥
                                १८० ॥
verses.english: The atonement (to be performed) by sinners (of) four (kinds) even, has been thus declared; hear now the penances for those who have intercourse with outcasts.

verses.text:
[१८०म] यो येन पतितेन-एषां संसर्गं याति मानवः ।
[१८०म्च्] स तस्य-एव व्रतं कुर्यात् तत्संसर्गविशुद्धये ॥
                                १८१ ॥
verses.english: He who associates with an outcast, himself becomes an outcast after a year, not by sacrificing for him, teaching him, or forming a matrimonial alliance with him, but by using the same carriage or seat, or by eating with him.

verses.text:
[१८१म] पतितस्य-उदकं कार्यं सपिण्डैर् बान्धवैर् बहिः
                                ।
[१८१म्च्] निन्दिते ऽहनि सायाह्ने ज्ञाति.ऋत्विज्.गुरुसन्निधौ ॥
                                १८२ ॥
verses.english: He who associates with any one of those outcasts, must perform, in order to atone for (such) intercourse, the penance prescribed for that (sinner).

verses.text:
[१८२म] दासी घटम् अपां पूर्णं पर्यस्येत् प्रेतवत् पदा
                                    ।
[१८२म्च्] अहोरात्रम् उपासीरन्न् अशौचं बान्धवैः सह ॥
                                    १८३ ॥
verses.english: The Sapindas and Samanodakas of an outcast must offer (a libation of) water (to him, as if he were dead), outside (the village), on an inauspicious day, in the evening and in the presence of the relatives, officiating priests, and teachers.

verses.text:
[१८३म] निवर्तेरंश् च तस्मात् तु सम्भाषण.सहासने
                                    ।
[१८३म्च्] दायाद्यस्य प्रदानं च यात्रा च-एव हि लौकिकी
                                    ॥ १८४ ॥
verses.english: A female slave shall upset with her foot a pot filled with water, as if it were for a dead person; (his Sapindas) as well as the Samanodakas shall be impure for a day and a night;

verses.text:
[१८४म] ज्येष्ठता च निवर्तेत ज्येष्ठावाप्यं च यद्
                                    धनम् । ११.१८५अ[१८४म]व्/ म्: यद् वसु
[१८४म्च्] ज्येष्ठांशं प्राप्नुयाच् च-अस्य यवीयान् गुणतो
                                    ऽधिकः ॥ १८५ ॥
verses.english: But thenceforward it shall be forbidden to converse with him, to sit with him, to give him a share of the inheritance, and to hold with him such intercourse as is usual among men;

verses.text:
[१८५म] प्रायश्चित्ते तु चरिते पूर्णकुम्भम् अपां नवम्
                                    ।
[१८५म्च्] तेन-एव सार्धं प्रास्येयुः स्नात्वा पुण्ये जलाशये
                                    ॥ १८६ ॥
verses.english: And (if he be the eldest) his right of primogeniture shall be withheld and the additional share, due to the eldest son; and his stead a younger brother, excelling in virtue, shall obtain the share of the eldest.

verses.text:
[१८६म] स त्व् अप्सु तं घटं प्रास्य प्रविश्य भवनं
                                    स्वकम् ।
[१८६म्च्] सर्वाणि ज्ञातिकार्याणि यथापूर्वं समाचरेत् ॥
                                    १८७ ॥
verses.english: But when he has performed his penance, they shall bathe with him in a holy pool and throw down a new pot, filled with water.

verses.text:
[१८७म] एतद् एव विधिं कुर्याद् योषित्सु पतितास्व् अपि ।
                                        ११.१८८अ[१८७म]व्/ म्: एतम् एव विधिं
[१८७म्च्] वस्त्र.अन्न.पानं देयं तु वसेयुश् च गृहान्तिके
                                    ॥ १८८ ॥
verses.english: But he shall throw that pot into water, enter his house and perform, as before, all the duties incumbent on a relative.

verses.text:
[१८८म] एनस्विभिर् अ.निर्णिक्तैर् न-अर्थं किं चित्
                                    सह-आचरेत् ।
[१८८म्च्] कृतनिर्णेजनांश् च-एव न जुगुप्सेत कर्हि चित् ॥
                                    १८९ ॥ ११.१८९च्[१८८म्च्]व्/ म्: कृतनिर्णेजनांश् च-एतान् ॥ 11.189 ॥
verses.english: Let him follow the same rule in the case of female outcasts; but clothes, food, and drink shall be given to them, and they shall live close to the (family-) house.

verses.text:
[१८९म] बालघ्नांश् च कृतघ्नांश् च विशुद्धान् अपि
                                    धर्मतः ।
[१८९म्च्] शरणागतहन्तॄंश् च स्त्रीहन्तॄंश् च न संवसेत्
                                    ॥ १९० ॥
verses.english: Let him not transact any business with unpurified sinners; but let him in no way reproach those who have made atonement.

verses.text:
[१९०म] येषां द्विजानां सावित्री न-अनूच्येत यथाविधि ।
[१९०म्च्] तांश् चारयित्वा त्रीन् कृच्छ्रान् यथाविधि-उपनाययेत्
                                ॥ १९१ ॥
verses.english: Let him not dwell together with the murderers of children, with those who have returned evil for good, and with the slayers of suppliants for protection or of women, though they may have been purified according to the sacred law.

verses.text:
[१९१म] प्रायश्चित्तं चिकीर्षन्ति विकर्मस्थास् तु ये द्विजाः
                                ।
[१९१म्च्] ब्रह्मणा च परित्यक्तास् तेषाम् अप्य् एतद् आदिशेत् ॥ १९२
                                ॥
verses.english: Those twice-born men who may not have been taught the Savitri (at the time) prescribed by the rule, he shall cause to perform three Krikkhra (penances) and afterwards initiate them in accordance with the law.

verses.text:
[१९२म] यद् गर्हितेन-अर्जयन्ति कर्मणा ब्राह्मणा धनम्
                                ।
[१९२म्च्] तस्य-उत्सर्गेण शुध्यन्ति जप्येन तपसा-एव च ॥
                                १९३ ॥
verses.english: Let him prescribe the same (expiation) when twice-born men, who follow forbidden occupations or have neglected (to learn) the Veda, desire to perform a penance.

verses.text:
[१९३म] जपित्वा त्रीणि सावित्र्याः सहस्राणि समाहितः ।
[१९३म्च्] मासं गोष्ठे पयः पीत्वा मुच्यते ऽसत्प्रतिग्रहात् ॥
                                १९४ ॥
verses.english: If Brahmanas acquire property by a reprehensible action, they become pure by relinquishing it, muttering prayers, and (performing) austerities.

verses.text:
[१९४म] उपवासकृशं तं तु गोव्रजात् पुनर् आगतम् ।
[१९४म्च्] प्रणतं प्रति पृच्छेयुः साम्यं सौम्य-इच्छसि-इति
                                किम् ॥ १९५ ॥
verses.english: By muttering with a concentrated mind the Savitri three thousand times, (dwelling) for a month in a cow-house, (and) subsisting on milk, (a man) is freed from (the guilt of) accepting presents from a wicked man.

verses.text:
[१९५म] सत्यम् उक्त्वा तु विप्रेषु विकिरेद् यवसं गवाम् ।
[१९५म्च्] गोभिः प्रवर्तिते तीर्थे कुर्युस् तस्य परिग्रहम् ॥
                                १९६ ॥
verses.english: But when he returns from the cow-house, emaciated with his fast, and reverently salutes, (the Brahmanas) shall ask him, 'Friend, dost thou desire to become our equal?'

verses.text:
[१९६म] व्रात्यानां याजनं कृत्वा परेषाम् अन्त्यकर्म च ।
[१९६म्च्] अभिचारम् अहीनं च त्रिभिः कृच्छ्रैर् व्यपोहति ॥
                                १९७ ॥
verses.english: If he answers to the Brahmanas, 'Forsooth, (I will not offend again), 'he shall scatter (some) grass for the cows; if the cows hallow that place (by eating the grass) the (Brahmana) shall re-admit him (into their community).

verses.text:
[१९७म] शरणागतं परित्यज्य वेदं विप्लाव्य च द्विजः
                                ।
[१९७म्च्] संवत्सरं यवाहारस् तत् पापम् अपसेधति ॥ १९८
                                ॥
verses.english: He who has sacrificed for Vratyas, or has performed the obsequies of strangers, or a magic sacrifice (intended to destroy life) or an Ahina sacrifice, removes (his guilt) by three Krikkhra (penances).

verses.text:
[१९८म] श्व.शृगाल.खरैर् दष्टो ग्राम्यैः क्रव्याद्भिर् एव च
                                ।
[१९८म्च्] नर.अश्व.उष्ट्र.वराहैश् च प्राणायामेन शुध्यति ॥
                                १९९ ॥
verses.english: A twice-born man who has cast off a suppliant for protection, or has (improperly) divulged the Veda, atones for his offence, if he subsists during a year on barley.

verses.text:
[१९९म] षष्ठान्नकालता मासं संहिताजप एव वा ।
[१९९म्च्] होमाश् च सकला नित्यम् अपाङ्क्त्यानां विशोधनम् ॥ २००
                                ॥ ११.२००च्[१९९म्च्]व्/ म्: होमाश् च शाकला ॥ 11.200 ॥
verses.english: He who has been bitten by a dog, a jackal, or a donkey, by a tame carnivorous animal, by a man, a horse, a camel, or a (village-) pig, becomes pure by suppressing his breath (Pranayama).

verses.text:
[२००म] उष्ट्रयानं समारुह्य खरयानं तु कामतः ।
[२००म्च्] स्नात्वा तु विप्रो दिग्.वासाः प्राणायामेन शुध्यति ॥
                                २०१ ॥
verses.english: To eat during a month at each sixth mealtime (only), to recite the Samhita (of a Veda), and (to perform) daily the Sakala oblations, are the means of purifying those excluded from society at repasts (Apanktya).

verses.text:
[२०१म] विना-अद्भिर् अप्सु वा-अप्य् आर्तः शारीरं सन्निषेव्य च
                                ।
[२०१म्च्] स.चैलो बहिर् आप्लुत्य गाम् आलभ्य विशुध्यति ॥ २०२
                                ॥
