verses.english: A Brahmana who voluntarily rode in a carriage drawn by camels or by asses, and he who bathed naked, become pure by suppressing his breath (Pranayama).

verses.text:
[२०२म] वेद.उदितानां नित्यानां कर्मणां समतिक्रमे ।
[२०२म्च्] स्नातकव्रतलोपे च प्रायश्चित्तम् अभोजनम् ॥ २०३
                                ॥
verses.english: He who has relieved the necessities of nature, being greatly pressed, either without (using) water or in water, becomes pure by bathing outside (the village) in his clothes and by touching a cow.

verses.text:
[२०३म] हुङ्कारं ब्राह्मणस्य-उक्त्वा त्वम्कारं च गरीयसः
                                ।
[२०३म्च्] स्नात्वा-अन्.अश्नन्न् अहः शेषम् अभिवाद्य प्रसादयेत् ॥
                                २०४ ॥
verses.english: Fasting is the penance for omitting the daily rites prescribed by the Veda and for neglecting the special duties of a Snataka.

verses.text:
[२०४म] ताडयित्वा तृणेन-अपि कण्ठे वा-आबध्य वाससा ।
[२०४म्च्] विवादे वा विनिर्जित्य प्रणिपत्य प्रसादयेत् ॥ २०५
                                ॥
verses.english: He who has said 'Hum' to a Brahmana, or has addressed one of his betters with 'Thou,' shall bathe, fast during the remaining part of the day, and appease (the person offended) by a reverential salutation.

verses.text:
[२०५म] अवगूर्य त्व् अब्दशतं सहस्रम् अभिहत्य च ।
[२०५म्च्] जिघांसया ब्राह्मणस्य नरकं प्रतिपद्यते ॥ २०६
                                ॥
verses.english: He who has struck (a Brahmana) even with a blade of grass, tied him by the neck with a cloth, or conquered him in an altercation, shall appease him by a prostration.

verses.text:
[२०६म] शोणितं यावतः पांसून् सङ्गृह्णाति महीतले ।
[२०६म्च्] तावन्त्य् अब्दसहस्राणि तत्कर्ता नरके वसेत् ॥ २०७
                                ॥ ११.२०७च्[२०६म्च्]व्/ म्: नरके व्रजेत् ॥ 11.207 ॥
verses.english: But he who, intending to hurt a Brahmana, has threatened (him with a stick and the like) shall remain in hell during a hundred years; he who (actually) struck him, during one thousand years.

verses.text:
[२०७म] अवगूर्य चरेत् कृच्छ्रम् अतिकृच्छ्रं निपातने ।
[२०७म्च्] कृच्छ्र.अतिकृच्छ्रौ कुर्वीत विप्रस्य-उत्पाद्य शोणितम्
                                ॥ २०८ ॥
verses.english: As many particles of dust as the blood of a Brahmana causes to coagulate, for so many thousand years shall the shedder of that (blood) remain in hell.

verses.text:
[२०८म] अनुक्तनिष्कृतीनां तु पापानाम् अपनुत्तये ।
[२०८म्च्] शक्तिं च-अवेक्ष्य पापं च प्रायश्चित्तं प्रकल्पयेत्
                                ॥ २०९ ॥
verses.english: For threatening a Brahmana, (the offender) shall perform a Krikkhra, for striking him an Atikrikkhra, for shedding his blood a Krikkhra and an Atikrikkhra.

verses.text:
[२०९म] यैर् अभ्युपायैर् एनांसि मानवो व्यपकर्षति ।
[२०९म्च्] तान् वो ऽभ्युपायान् वक्ष्यामि देव.ऋषि.पितृसेवितान् ॥
                                २१० ॥
verses.english: For the expiation of offences for which no atonement has been prescribed, let him fix a penance after considering (the offender's) strength and the (nature of the) offence.

verses.text:
[२१०म] त्र्यहं प्रातस् त्र्यहं सायं त्र्यहम् अद्याद् अयाचितम्
                                ।
[२१०म्च्] त्र्यहं परं च न-अश्नीयात् प्राजापत्यं चरन् द्विजः
                                ॥ २११ ॥
verses.english: I will (now) describe to you those means, adopted by the gods, the sages, and the manes, through which a man may remove his sins.

verses.text:
[२११म] गोमूत्रं गोमयं क्षीरं दधि सर्पिः कुश.उदकम्
                                    ।
[२११म्च्] एकरात्र.उपवासश् च कृच्छ्रं सान्तपनं स्मृतम्
                                    ॥ २१२ ॥
verses.english: A twice-born man who performs (the Krikkhra penance), revealed by Pragapati, shall eat during three days in the morning (only), during (the next) three days in the evening (only), during the (following) three days (food given) unasked, and shall fast during another period of three days.

verses.text:
[२१२म] एकैकं ग्रासम् अश्नीयात् त्र्यहाणि त्रीणि पूर्ववत्
                                    ।
[२१२म्च्] त्र्यहं च-उपवसेद् अन्त्यम् अतिकृच्छ्रं चरन्
                                    द्विजः ॥ २१३ ॥
verses.english: (Subsisting on) the urine of cows, cowdung, milk, sour milk, clarified butter, and a decoction of Kusa-grass, and fasting during one (day and) night, (that is) called a Samtapana Krikkhra.

verses.text:
[२१३म] तप्तकृच्छ्रं चरन् विप्रो
                                    जल.क्षीर.घृत.अनिलान् ।
[२१३म्च्] प्रति.त्र्यहं पिबेद् उष्णान् सकृत्स्नायी समाहितः
                                    ॥ २१४ ॥
verses.english: A twice-born man who performs an Atikrikkhra (penance), must take his food during three periods of three days in the manner described above, (but) one mouthful only at each meal, and fast during the last three days.

verses.text:
[२१४म] यत.आत्मनो ऽप्रमत्तस्य द्वादशाहम् अभोजनम्
                                    ।
[२१४म्च्] पराको नाम कृच्छ्रो ऽयं सर्वपाप.अपनोदनः ॥
                                    २१५ ॥
verses.english: A Brahmana who performs a Taptakrikkhra (penance) must drink hot water, hot milk, hot clarified butter and (inhale) hot air, each during three days, and bathe once with a concentrated mind.

verses.text:
[२१५म] एकैकं ह्रासयेत् पिण्डं कृष्णे शुक्ले च वर्धयेत्
                                    ।
[२१५म्च्] उपस्पृशंस् त्रिषवणम् एतत्-चाण्द्रायणं स्मृतम् ॥
                                    २१६ ॥
verses.english: A fast for twelve days by a man who controls himself and commits no mistakes, is called a Paraka Krikkhra, which removes all guilt.

verses.text:
[२१६म] एतम् एव विधिं कृत्स्नम् आचरेद् यवमध्यमे
                                    ।
[२१६म्च्] शुक्लपक्षादिनियतश् चरंश् चान्द्रायणं व्रतम् ॥
                                    २१७ ॥
verses.english: If one diminishes (one's food daily by) one mouthful during the dark (half of the month) and increases (it in the same manner) during the bright half, and bathes (daily) at the time of three libations (morning, noon, and evening), that is called a lunar penance (Kandrayana).

verses.text:
[२१७म] अष्टाव् अष्टौ समश्नीयात् पिण्डान् मध्यन्दिने स्थिते
                                    ।
[२१७म्च्] नियत.आत्मा हविष्याशी यतिचान्द्रायणं चरन् ॥
                                    २१८ ॥
verses.english: Let him follow throughout the same rule at the (Kandrayana, called) yavamadhyama (shaped like a barley-corn), (but) let him (in that case) begin the lunar penance, (with a) controlled (mind), on the first day of the bright half (of the month).

verses.text:
[२१८म] चतुरः प्रातर् अश्नीयात् पिण्डान् विप्रः समाहितः
                                    ।
[२१८म्च्] चतुरो ऽस्तम् इते सूर्ये शिशुचान्द्रायणं स्मृतम् ॥
                                    २१९ ॥
verses.english: He who performs the lunar penance of ascetics, shall eat (during a month) daily at midday eight mouthfuls, controlling himself and consuming sacrificial food (only).

verses.text:
[२१९म] यथा कथं चित् पिण्डानां तिस्रो ऽशीतीः समाहितः
                                    ।
[२१९म्च्] मासेन-अश्नन् हविष्यस्य चन्द्रस्य-एति सलोकताम्
                                    ॥ २२० ॥
verses.english: If a Brahmana, with concentrated mind, eats (during a month daily) four mouthfuls in a morning and four after sunset, (that is) called the lunar penance of children.

verses.text:
[२२०म] एतद् रुद्रास् तथा-आदित्या वसवश् च-आचरन्
                                    व्रतम् ।
[२२०म्च्] सर्वाकुशलमोक्षाय मरुतश् च महर्षिभिः ॥ २२१
                                    ॥
verses.english: He who, concentrating his mind, eats during a month in any way thrice eighty mouthfuls of sacrificial food, dwells (after death) in the world of the moon.

verses.text:
[२२१म] महाव्याहृतिभिर् होमः कर्तव्यः स्वयम् अन्वहम्
                                    ।
[२२१म्च्] अहिंसा सत्यम् अक्रोधम् आर्जवं च समाचरेत् ॥
                                    २२२ ॥
verses.english: The Rudras, likewise the Adityas, the Vasus and the Maruts, together with the great sages, practised this (rite) in order to remove all evil.

verses.text:
[२२२म] त्रिर् अह्नस् त्रिर् निशायां च स.वासा जलम् आविशेत्
                                    ।
[२२२म्च्] स्त्री.शूद्र.पतितांश् च-एव न-अभिभाषेत कर्हि
                                    चित् ॥ २२३ ॥
verses.english: Burnt oblations, accompanied by (the recitation of) the Mahavyahritis, must daily be made (by the penitent) himself, and he must abstain from injuring (sentient creatures), speak the truth, and keep himself free from anger and from dishonesty.

verses.text:
[२२३म] स्थान.आसनाभ्यां विहरेद् अशक्तो ऽधः शयीत वा
                                    ।
[२२३म्च्] ब्रह्मचारी व्रती च स्याद् गुरु.देव.द्विज.अर्चकः
                                    ॥ २२४ ॥
verses.english: Let him bathe three times each day and thrice each night, dressed in his clothes; let him on no account talk to women, Sudras, and outcasts.

verses.text:
[२२४म] सावित्रीं च जपेन् नित्यं पवित्राणि च शक्तितः
                                    ।
[२२४म्च्] सर्वेष्व् एव व्रतेष्व् एवं प्रायश्चित्तार्थम् आदृतः
                                    ॥ २२५ ॥
verses.english: Let him pass the time standing (during the day) and sitting (during the night), or if he is unable (to do that) let him lie on the (bare) ground; let him be chaste and observe the vows (of a student) and worship his Gurus, the gods, and Brahmanas.

verses.text:
[२२५म] एतैर् द्विजातयः शोध्या व्रतैर् आविष्कृत.एनसः
                                    ।
[२२५म्च्] अनाविष्कृत.पापांस् तु मन्त्रैर् होमैश् च शोधयेत्
                                    ॥ २२६ ॥
verses.english: Let him constantly mutter the Savitri and (other) purificatory texts according to his ability; (let him) carefully (act thus) on (the occasion of) all (other) vows (performed) by way of penance.

verses.text:
[२२६म] ख्यापनेन.अनुतापेन तपसा-अध्ययनेन च ।
[२२६म्च्] पापकृत्-मुच्यते पापात् तथा दानेन च-आपदि ॥
                                    २२७ ॥
verses.english: By these expiations twice-born men must be purified whose sins are known, but let him purify those whose sins are not known by (the recitation of) sacred texts and by (the performance of) burnt oblations.

verses.text:
[२२७म] यथा यथा नरो ऽधर्मं स्वयं
                                    कृत्वा-अनुभाषते ।
[२२७म्च्] तथा तथा त्वचा-इव-अहिस् तेन-अधर्मेण
                                    मुच्यते ॥ २२८ ॥
verses.english: By confession, by repentance, by austerity, and by reciting (the Veda) a sinner is freed from guilt, and in case no other course is possible, by liberality.

verses.text:
[२२८म] यथा यथा मनस् तस्य दुष्कृतं कर्म गर्हति
                                    ।
[२२८म्च्] तथा तथा शरीरं तत् तेन-अधर्मेण मुच्यते
                                    ॥ २२९ ॥
verses.english: In proportion as a man who has done wrong, himself confesses it, even so far he is freed from guilt, as a snake from its slough.

verses.text:
[२२९म] कृत्वा पापं हि सन्तप्य तस्मात् पापात् प्रमुच्यते
                                    ।
[२२९म्च्] न-एवं कुर्यां पुनर् इति निवृत्त्या पूयते तु सः
                                    ॥ २३० ॥
verses.english: In proportion as his heart loathes his evil deed, even so far is his body freed from that guilt.

verses.text:
[२३०म] एवं सञ्चिन्त्य मनसा प्रेत्य कर्मफल.उदयम्
                                    ।
[२३०म्च्] मनो.वाच्.मूर्तिभिर् नित्यं शुभं कर्म समाचरेत्
                                    ॥ २३१ ॥
verses.english: He who has committed a sin and has repented, is freed from that sin, but he is purified only by (the resolution of) ceasing (to sin and thinking) 'I will do so no more.'

verses.text:
[२३१म] अज्ञानाद् यदि वा ज्ञानात् कृत्वा कर्म विगर्हितम्
                                    ।
[२३१म्च्] तस्माद् विमुक्तिम् अन्विच्छन् द्वितीयं न समाचरेत्
                                    ॥ २३२ ॥
verses.english: Having thus considered in his mind what results will arise from his deeds after death, let him always be good in thoughts, speech, and actions.

verses.text:
[२३२म] यस्मिन् कर्मण्य् अस्य कृते मनसः स्याद् अलाघवम्
                                    ।
[२३२म्च्] तस्मिंस् तावत् तपः कुर्याद् यावत् तुष्टिकरं
                                    भवेत् ॥ २३३ ॥
verses.english: He who, having either unintentionally or intentionally committed a reprehensible deed, desires to be freed from (the guilt on it, must not commit it a second time.

verses.text:
[२३३म] तपोमूलम् इदं सर्वं दैव.मानुषकं सुखम्
                                    ।
[२३३म्च्] तपोमध्यं बुधैः प्रोक्तं तपो.ऽन्तं
                                    वेददर्शिभिः ॥ २३४ ॥
verses.english: If his mind be uneasy with respect to any act, let him repeat the austerities (prescribed as a penance) for it until they fully satisfy (his conscience).

verses.text:
[२३४म] ब्राह्मणस्य तपो ज्ञानं तपः क्षत्रस्य रक्षणम्
                                    ।
[२३४म्च्] वैश्यस्य तु तपो वार्ता तपः शूद्रस्य सेवनम्
                                    ॥ २३५ ॥
verses.english: All the bliss of gods and men is declared by the sages to whom the Veda was revealed, to have austerity for its root, austerity for its middle, and austerity for its end.

verses.text:
[२३५म] ऋषयः संयत.आत्मानः फल.मूल.अनिल.अशनाः
                                    ।
[२३५म्च्] तपसा-एव प्रपश्यन्ति त्रैलोक्यं स.चराचरम्
                                    ॥ २३६ ॥
verses.english: (The pursuit of sacred) knowledge is the austerity of a Brahmana, protecting (the people) is the austerity of a Kshatriya, (the pursuit of) his daily business is the austerity of a Vaisya, and service the austerity of a Sudra.

verses.text:
[२३६म] औषधान्य् अगदो विद्या दैवी च विविधा स्थितिः
                                    ।
[२३६म्च्] तपसा-एव प्रसिध्यन्ति तपस् तेषां हि साधनम्
                                    ॥ २३७ ॥
verses.english: The sages who control themselves and subsist on fruit, roots, and air, survey the three worlds together with their moving and immovable (creatures) through their austerities alone.

verses.text:
[२३७म] यद् दुस्तरं यद् दुरापं यद् दुर्गं यच् च
                                    दुष्करम् ।
[२३७म्च्] सर्वं तु तपसा साध्यं तपो हि दुरतिक्रमम् ॥
                                    २३८ ॥ ११.२३८च्[२३७म्च्]व्/ म्: सर्वं तत् तपसा ॥ 11.238 ॥
verses.english: Medicines, good health, learning, and the various divine stations are attained by austerities alone; for austerity is the means of gaining them.

verses.text:
[२३८म] महापातकिनश् च-एव शेषाश् च-अकार्यकारिणः
                                    ।
[२३८म्च्] तपसा-एव सुतप्तेन मुच्यन्ते किल्बिषात् ततः ॥
                                    २३९ ॥
verses.english: Whatever is hard to be traversed, whatever is hard to be attained, whatever is hard to be reached, whatever is hard to be performed, all (this) may be accomplished by austerities; for austerity (possesses a power) which it is difficult to surpass.

verses.text:
[२३९म] कीताश् च-अहि.पतङ्गाश् च पशवश् च वयांसि च
                                    ।
[२३९म्च्] स्थावराणि च भूतानि दिवं यान्ति तपोबलात् ॥
                                    २४० ॥
verses.english: Both those who have committed mortal sin (Mahapataka) and all other offenders are severally freed from their guilt by means of well-performed austerities.

verses.text:
[२४०म] यत् किं चिद् एनः कुर्वन्ति मनो.वाच्.मूर्तिभिर्
                                    जनाः । ११.२४१अ[२४०म]व्/ म्: मनो.वाच्.कर्मभिर्
[२४०म्च्] तत् सर्वं निर्दहन्त्य् आशु तपसा-एव तपो.धनाः
                                    ॥ २४१ ॥
verses.english: Insects, snakes, moths, bees, birds and beings, bereft of motion, reach heaven by the power of austerities.

verses.text:
[२४१म] तपसा-एव विशुद्धस्य ब्राह्मणस्य दिव.ओकसः
                                    ।
[२४१म्च्] इज्याश् च प्रतिगृह्णन्ति कामान् संवर्धयन्ति च
                                    ॥ २४२ ॥
verses.english: Whatever sin men commit by thoughts, words, or deeds, that they speedily burn away by penance, if they keep penance as their only riches.

verses.text:
[२४२म] प्रजापतिर् इदं शास्त्रं तपसा-एव-असृजत्
                                    प्रभुः ।
[२४२म्च्] तथा-एव वेदान् ऋषयस् तपसा प्रतिपेदिरे ॥ २४३
                                    ॥
verses.english: The gods accept the offerings of that Brahmana alone who has purified himself by austerities, and grant to him all he desires.

verses.text:
[२४३म] इत्य् एतत् तपसो देवा महाभाग्यं प्रचक्षते ।
                                        ११.२४४अ[२४३म]व्/ म्: यद् एतत् तपसो
[२४३म्च्] सर्वस्य-अस्य प्रपश्यन्तस् तपसः पुण्यम्
                                    उत्तमम् ॥ २४४ ॥ ११.२४४च्[२४३म्च्]व्/ म्: पुण्यं
                                    उद्भवम् ॥ 11.244 ॥
verses.english: The lord, Pragapati, created these Institutes (of the sacred law) by his austerities alone; the sages likewise obtained (the revelation of) the Vedas through their austerities.

verses.text:
[२४४म] वेदाभ्यासो ऽन्वहं शक्त्या महायज्ञक्रिया क्षमा
                                    ।
[२४४म्च्] नाशयन्त्य् आशु पापानि महापातकजान्य् अपि ॥ २४५
                                    ॥
verses.english: The gods, discerning that the holy origin of this whole (world) is from austerity, have thus proclaimed the incomparable power of austerity.

verses.text:
[२४५म] यथा-एधस् तेजसा वह्निः प्राप्तं निर्दहति
                                    क्षणात् ।
[२४५म्च्] तथा ज्ञानाग्निना पापं सर्वं दहति वेदवित् ॥
                                    २४६ ॥
verses.english: The daily study of the Veda, the performance of the great sacrifices according to one's ability, (and) patience (in suffering) quickly destroy all guilt, even that caused by mortal sins.

verses.text:
[२४६म] इत्य् एतद् एनसाम् उक्तं प्रायश्चित्तं यथाविधि
                                    ।
[२४६म्च्] अत ऊर्ध्वं रहस्य-अनां प्रायश्चित्तं निबोधत
                                    ॥ २४७ ॥
verses.english: As a fire in one moment consumes with its bright flame the fuel that has been placed on it, even so he who knows the Veda destroys all guilt by the fire of knowledge.

verses.text:
[२४७म] स.व्याहृति.प्रणवकाः प्राणायामास् तु षोडश ।
[२४७म्च्] अपि भ्रूणहनं मासात् पुनन्त्य् अहर् अहः कृताः ॥
                                    २४८ ॥
verses.english: The penances for sins (made public) have been thus declared according to the law; learn next the penances for secret (sins).

verses.text:
[२४८म] कौत्सं जप्त्वा-अप इत्य् एतद् वसिष्ठं च
                                    प्रति-इत्य् ऋचम् ।
[२४८म्च्] माहित्रं शुद्धवत्यश् च सुरापो ऽपि विशुध्यति
                                    ॥ २४९ ॥
verses.english: Sixteen suppressions of the breath (Pranayama) accompanied by (the recitation of) the Vyahritis and of the syllable Om, purify, if they are repeated daily, after a month even the murderer of a learned Brahmana.

verses.text:
[२४९म] सकृत्-जप्त्वा-आस्यवामीयं शिवसङ्कल्पम् एव च
                                    ।
[२४९म्च्] अपहृत्य सुवर्णं तु क्षणाद् भवति निर्.मलः ॥
                                    २५० ॥
verses.english: Even a drinker of (the spirituous liquor called) Sura becomes pure, if he mutters the hymn (seen) by Kutsa, 'Removing by thy splendour our guilt, O Agni,' &c., (that seen) by Vasishtha, 'With their hymns the Vasishthas woke the Dawn,' &c., the Mahitra (hymn) and (the verses called) Suddhavatis.

verses.text:
[२५०म] हविष्पान्तीयम् अभ्यस्य न तमं ह इति-इति च
                                    ।
[२५०म्च्] जपित्वा पौरुषं सूक्तं मुच्यते गुरुतल्पगः ॥
                                    २५१ ॥
verses.english: Even he who has stolen gold, instantly becomes free from guilt, if he once mutters (the hymn beginning with the words) 'The middlemost brother of this beautiful, ancient Hotri-priest' and the Sivasamkalpa.

verses.text:
[२५१म] एनसां स्थूल.सूक्ष्माणां चिकीर्षन्न् अपनोदनम्
                                    ।
[२५१म्च्] अव-इत्य् ऋचं जपेद् अब्दं यत् किं च-इदम् इति-इति
                                    वा ॥ २५२ ॥
verses.english: The violator of a Guru's bed is freed (from sin), if he repeatedly recites the Havishpantiya (hymn), (that beginning) 'Neither anxiety nor misfortune,' (and that beginning) 'Thus, verily, thus,' and mutters the hymn addressed to Purusha.

verses.text:
[२५२म] प्रतिगृह्य-अप्रतिग्राह्यं भुक्त्वा च-अन्नं
                                    विगर्हितम् ।
[२५२म्च्] जपंस् तरत्समन्दीयं पूयते मानवस् त्र्यहात् ॥
                                    २५३ ॥
verses.english: He who desires to expiate sins great or small, must mutter during a year the Rit-verse 'May we remove thy anger, O Varuna,' &c., or 'Whatever offence here, O Varuna,' &c.

verses.text:
[२५३म] सोमारौद्रम् तु बह्व्.एनाः मासम् अभ्यस्य शुध्यति
                                    । ११.२५४अ[२५३म]व्/ म्: समाम् अभ्यस्य
[२५३म्च्] स्रवन्त्याम् आचरन् स्नानम् अर्यम्णाम् इति च तृचम्
                                    ॥ २५४ ॥
verses.english: That man who, having accepted presents which ought not to be accepted, or having eaten forbidden food, mutters the Taratsamandiya (Rikas), becomes pure after three days.

verses.text:
[२५४म] अब्दार्धम् इन्द्रम् इत्य् एतद् एनस्वी सप्तकं जपेत्
                                    ।
[२५४म्च्] अप्रशस्तं तु कृत्वा-अप्सु मासम् आसीत भैक्षभुक्
                                    ॥ २५५ ॥
verses.english: But he who has committed many sins, becomes pure, if he recites during a month the (four verses) addressed to Soma and Rudra, and the three verses (beginning) 'Aryaman, Varuna, and Mitra,' while he bathes in a river.

verses.text:
[२५५म] मन्त्रैः शाकलहोमीयैर् अब्दं हुत्वा घृतं
                                    द्विजः ।
[२५५म्च्] सुगुर्व् अप्य् अपहन्त्य् एनो जप्त्वा वा नम इत्य् ऋचम्
                                    ॥ २५६ ॥
verses.english: A grievous offender shall mutter the seven verses (beginning with) 'Indra,' for half a year; but he who has committed any blamable act in water, shall subsist during a month on food obtained by begging.

verses.text:
[२५६म] महापातकसंयुक्तो ऽनुगच्छेद् गाः समाहितः
                                    ।
[२५६म्च्] अभ्यस्य-अब्दं पावमानीर् भैक्ष.आहारो
                                    विशुध्यति ॥ २५७ ॥
verses.english: A twice-born man removes even very great guilt by offering clarified butter with the sacred texts belonging to the Sakala-homas, or by muttering the Rik, (beginning) 'Adoration.'

verses.text:
[२५७म] अरण्ये वा त्रिर् अभ्यस्य प्रयतो वेदसंहिताम्
                                    ।
[२५७म्च्] मुच्यते पातकैः सर्वैः पराकैः शोधितस्
                                    त्रिभिः ॥ २५८ ॥
verses.english: He who is stained by mortal sin, becomes pure, if, with a concentrated mind, he attends cows for a year, reciting the Pavamani (hymns) and subsisting on alms.

verses.text:
[२५८म] त्र्यहं तु-उपवसेद् युक्तस् त्रिर् अह्नो ऽभ्युपयन्न्
                                    अपः ।
[२५८म्च्] मुच्यते पातकैः सर्वैस् त्रिर्
                                    जपित्वा-अघमर्षणम् ॥ २५९ ॥
verses.english: Or if, pure (in mind and in body), he thrice repeats the Samhita of the Veda in a forest, sanctified by three Paraka (penances), he is freed from all crimes causing loss of caste (pataka).

verses.text:
[२५९म] यथा-अश्वमेधः क्रतुराज्-सर्वपापाप.नोदनः
                                    ।
[२५९म्च्] तथा-अघमर्षणं सूक्तं सर्वपापाप.नोदनम् ॥
                                    २६० ॥
verses.english: But if (a man) fasts during three days, bathing thrice a day, and muttering (in the water the hymn seen by) Aghamarshana, he is (likewise) freed from all sins causing loss of caste.

verses.text:
[२६०म] हत्वा लोकान् अपि-इमांस् त्रीन् अश्नन्न् अपि यतस्
                                    ततः ।
[२६०म्च्] ऋग्वेदं धारयन् विप्रो न-एनः प्राप्नोति किं चन
                                    ॥ २६१ ॥
verses.english: As the horse-sacrifice, the king of sacrifices, removes all sin, even so the Aghamarshana hymn effaces all guilt.

verses.text:
[२६१म] ऋक्संहितां त्रिर् अभ्यस्य यजुषां वा समाहितः
                                    ।
[२६१म्च्] साम्नां वा स.रहस्यानां सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते
                                    ॥ २६२ ॥
verses.english: A Brahmana who retains in his memory the Rig-veda is not stained by guilt, though he may have destroyed these three worlds, though he may eat the food of anybody.

verses.text:
[२६२म] यथा महाह्रदं प्राप्य क्षिप्तं लोष्टं विनश्यति
                                    ।
[२६२म्च्] तथा दुश्चरितं सर्वं वेदे त्रिवृति मज्जति ॥
                                    २६३ ॥
verses.english: He who, with a concentrated mind, thrice recites the Riksamhita, or (that of the) Yagur-veda; or (that of the) Sama-veda together with the secret (texts, the Upanishads), is completely freed from all sins.

verses.text:
[२६३म] ऋचो यजूंषि च-अन्यानि सामानि विविधानि च ।
[२६३म्च्] एष ज्ञेयस् त्रिवृद्वेदो यो वेद-एनं स वेदवित् ॥
                                    २६४ ॥
verses.english: As a clod of earth, falling into a great lake, is quickly dissolved, even so every sinful act is engulfed in the threefold Veda.

verses.text:
[२६४म] आद्यं यत् त्र्यक्षरं ब्रह्म त्रयी यस्मिन्
                                    प्रतिष्ठिता ।
[२६४म्च्] स गुह्यो ऽन्यस् त्रिवृद्वेदो यस् तं वेद स
                                    वेदवित् ॥ २६५ ॥
verses.english: The Rikas, the Yagus (-formulas) which differ (from the former), the manifold Saman (-songs), must be known (to form) the triple Veda; he who knows them, (is called) learned in the Veda.
The initial triliteral Brahman on which the threefold (sacred science) is based, is another triple Veda which must be kept secret; he who knows that, (is called) learned in the Veda.

title: मनुस्मृति: अध्याय १२: कर्मफल एवं मोक्ष
subtitle: Law of Karma, 3 Gunas & Moksha (126 Shlokas)

verses.text:
चातुर्वर्ण्यस्य कृत्स्नो ऽयम् उक्तो धर्मस् त्वया-अनघः ।
कर्मणां फलनिर्वृत्तिं शंस नस् तत्त्वतः पराम् ॥ १ ॥
verses.english: 'O sinless One, the whole sacred law, (applicable) to the four castes, has been declared by thee; communicate to us (now), according to the truth, the ultimate retribution for (their) deeds.'

verses.text:
स तान् उवाच धर्म.आत्मा महर्षीन् मानवो भृगुः ।
अस्य सर्वस्य शृणुत कर्मयोगस्य निर्णयम् ॥ २ ॥
verses.english: To the great sages (who addressed him thus) righteous Bhrigu, sprung from Manu, answered, 'Hear the decision concerning this whole connexion with actions.'

verses.text:
शुभ.अशुभ.फलं कर्म मनो.वाच्.देह.सम्भवम् ।
कर्मजा गतयो नॄणाम् उत्तम.अधम.मध्यमः ॥ ३ ॥
verses.english: Action, which springs from the mind, from speech, and from the body, produces either good or evil results; by action are caused the (various) conditions of men, the highest, the middling, and the lowest.

verses.text:
तस्य-इह त्रिविधस्य-अपि त्र्यधिष्ठानस्य देहिनः ।
दशलक्षणयुक्तस्य मनो विद्यात् प्रवर्तकम् ॥ ४ ॥
verses.english: Know that the mind is the instigator here below, even to that (action) which is connected with the body, (and) which is of three kinds, has three locations, and falls under ten heads.

verses.text:
परद्रव्येष्व् अभिध्यानं मनसा-अनिष्टचिन्तनम् ।
वितथाभिनिवेशश् च त्रिविधं कर्म मानसम् ॥ ५ ॥
verses.english: Coveting the property of others, thinking in one's heart of what is undesirable, and adherence to false (doctrines), are the three kinds of (sinful) mental action.

verses.text:
पारुष्यम् अनृतं च-एव पैशुन्यं च-अपि सर्वशः ।
असम्बद्धप्रलापश् च वाच्.मयं स्याच् चतुर्विधम् ॥ ६ ॥
verses.english: Abusing (others, speaking) untruth, detracting from the merits of all men, and talking idly, shall be the four kinds of (evil) verbal action.

verses.text:
अदत्तानाम् उपादानं हिंसा च-एव-अविधानतः ।
परदार.उपसेवा च शारीरं त्रिविधं स्मृतम् ॥ ७ ॥
verses.english: Taking what has not been given, injuring (creatures) without the sanction of the law, and holding criminal intercourse with another man's wife, are declared to be the three kinds of (wicked) bodily action.

verses.text:
मानसं मनसा-एव-अयम् उपभुङ्क्ते शुभ.अशुभम् ।
वाचा वाचा कृतं कर्म कायेन-एव च कायिकम् ॥ ८ ॥
verses.english: (A man) obtains (the result of) a good or evil mental (act) in his mind, (that of) a verbal (act) in his speech, (that of) a bodily (act) in his body.

verses.text:
शरीरजैः कर्मदोषैर् याति स्थावरतां नरः ।
वाचिकैः पक्षि.मृगतां मानसैर् अन्त्यजातिताम् ॥ ९ ॥
verses.english: In consequence of (many) sinful acts committed with his body, a man becomes (in the next birth) something inanimate, in consequence (of sins) committed by speech, a bird, or a beast, and in consequence of mental (sins he is re-born in) a low caste.

verses.text:
वाग्दण्डो ऽथ मनोदण्डः कायदण्डस् तथा-एव च ।
यस्य-एते निहिता बुद्धौ त्रिदण्डी-इति स उच्यते ॥ १० ॥
verses.english: That man is called a (true) tridandin in whose mind these three, the control over his speech (vagdanda), the control over his thoughts (manodanda), and the control over his body (kayadanda), are firmly fixed.

verses.text:
त्रिदण्डम् एतन् निक्षिप्य सर्वभूतेषु मानवः ।
काम.क्रोधौ तु संयम्य ततः सिद्धिं नियच्छति ॥ ११ ॥
                                    १२.११च्व्/ म्: 
                                    काम.क्रोधौ सुसंयम्य ततः सिद्धिं निगच्छति ॥ 12.11 ॥
verses.english: That man who keeps this threefold control (over himself) with respect to all created beings and wholly subdues desire and wrath, thereby assuredly gains complete success.

verses.text:
यो ऽस्य-आत्मनः कारयिता तं क्षेत्रज्ञं प्रचक्षते ।
यः करोति तु कर्माणि स भूतात्मा-उच्यते बुधैः ॥ १२
                                    ॥
verses.english: Him who impels this (corporeal) Self to action, they call the Kshetragna (the knower of the field); but him who does the acts, the wise name the Bhutatman (the Self consisting of the elements).

verses.text:
जीवसञ्ज्ञो ऽन्तरात्मा-अन्यः सहजः सर्वदेहिनाम् ।
येन वेदयते सर्वं सुखं दुःखं च जन्मसु ॥ १३
                                    ॥
verses.english: Another internal Self that is generated with all embodied (Kshetragnas) is called Giva, through which (the Kshetragna) becomes sensible of all pleasure and pain in (successive) births.

verses.text:
ताव् उभौ भूतसम्पृक्तौ महान् क्षेत्रज्ञ एव च ।
उच्चावचेषु भूतेषु स्थितं तं व्याप्य तिष्ठतः ॥ १४
                                    ॥
verses.english: These two, the Great One and the Kshetragna, who are closely united with the elements, pervade him who resides in the multiform created beings.

verses.text:
अ.सङ्ख्या मूर्तयस् तस्य निष्पतन्ति शरीरतः ।
उच्चावचानि भूतानि सततं चेष्टयन्ति याः ॥ १५ ॥
verses.english: From his body innumerable forms go forth, which constantly impel the multiform creatures to action.

verses.text:
पञ्चभ्य एव मात्राभ्यः प्रेत्य दुष्कृतिनां नृणाम् । १२.१६अव्/ म्: 
                                        पञ्चभ्य एव भूतेभ्यः
शरीरं यातनार्थीयम् अन्यद् उत्पद्यते ध्रुवम् ॥ १६
                                    ॥
verses.english: Another strong body, formed of particles (of the) five (elements and) destined to suffer the torments (in hell), is produced after death (in the case) of wicked men.

verses.text:
तेन-अनुभूय ता यामीः शरीरेण-इह यातनाः ।
तास्व् एव भूतमात्रासु प्रलीयन्ते विभागशः ॥ १७ ॥
verses.english: When (the evil-doers) by means of that body have suffered there the torments imposed by Yama, (its constituent parts) are united, each according to its class, with those very elements (from which they were taken).

verses.text:
सो ऽनुभूय-असुख.उदर्कान् दोषान् विषयसङ्गजान् ।
व्यपेत.कल्मषो ऽभ्येति ताव् एव-उभौ महा.ओजसौ ॥ १८
                                    ॥
verses.english: He, having suffered for his faults, which are produced by attachment to sensual objects, and which result in misery, approaches, free from stains, those two mighty ones.

verses.text:
तौ धर्मं पश्यतस् तस्य पापं च-अतन्द्रितौ सह
                                    ।
याभ्यां प्राप्नोति सम्पृक्तः प्रेत्य-इह च सुख.असुखम्
                                    ॥ १९ ॥
verses.english: Those two together examine without tiring the merit and the guilt of that (individual soul), united with which it obtains bliss or misery both in this world and the next.

verses.text:
यद्य् आचरति धर्मं स प्रायशो ऽधर्मम् अल्पशः । १२.२०अव्/ म्: 
                                        यथ-आचरति
तैर् एव च-आवृतो भूतैः स्वर्गे सुखम् उपाश्नुते ॥ २०
                                    ॥
verses.english: If (the soul) chiefly practises virtue and vice to a small degree, it obtains bliss in heaven, clothed with those very elements.

verses.text:
यदि तु प्रायशो ऽधर्मं सेवते धर्मम् अल्पशः ।
तैर् भूतैः स परित्यक्तो यामीः प्राप्नोति यातनाः ॥ २१
                                    ॥
verses.english: But if it chiefly cleaves to vice and to virtue in a small degree, it suffers, deserted by the elements, the torments inflicted by Yama.

verses.text:
यामीस् ता यातनाः प्राप्य स जीवो वीत.कल्मषः ।
तान्य् एव पञ्च भूतानि पुनर् अप्येति भागशः ॥ २२
                                    ॥
verses.english: The individual soul, having endured those torments of Yama, again enters, free from taint, those very five elements, each in due proportion.

verses.text:
एता दृष्ट्वा-अस्य जीवस्य गतीः स्वेन-एव चेतसा ।
धर्मतो ऽधर्मतश् च-एव धर्मे दध्यात् सदा मनः ॥
                                    २३ ॥
verses.english: Let (man), having recognised even by means of his intellect these transitions of the individual soul (which depend) on merit and demerit, always fix his heart on (the acquisition of) merit.

verses.text:
सत्त्वं रजस् तमस्-च-एव त्रीन् विद्याद् आत्मनो गुणान्
                                    ।
यैर् व्याप्य-इमान् स्थितो भावान् महान् सर्वान् अशेषतः ॥
                                    २४ ॥
verses.english: Know Goodness (sattva), Activity (ragas), and Darkness (tamas) to be the three qualities of the Self, with which the Great One always completely pervades all existences.

verses.text:
यो यदा-एषां गुणो देहे साकल्येन-अतिरिच्यते ।
स तदा तद्गुणप्रायं तं करोति शरीरिणम् ॥ २५ ॥
verses.english: When one of these qualities wholly predominates in a body, then it makes the embodied (soul) eminently distinguished for that quality.

verses.text:
सत्त्वं ज्ञानं तमो ऽज्ञानं राग.द्वेषौ रजः स्मृतम्
                                    ।
एतद् व्याप्तिमद् एतेषां सर्वभूताश्रितं वपुः ॥ २६
                                    ॥
verses.english: Goodness is declared (to have the form of) knowledge, Darkness (of) ignorance, Activity (of) love and hatred; such is the nature of these (three) which is (all-) pervading and clings to everything created.

verses.text:
तत्र यत् प्रीतिसंयुक्तं किं चिद् आत्मनि लक्षयेत् ।
प्रशान्तम् इव शुद्धाभं सत्त्वं तद् उपधारयेत् ॥ २७
                                    ॥
verses.english: When (man) experiences in his soul a (feeling) full of bliss, a deep calm, as it were, and a pure light, then let him know (that it is) among those three (the quality called) Goodness.

verses.text:
यत् तु दुःखसमायुक्तम् अप्रीतिकरम् आत्मनः ।
तद् रजो प्रतीपं विद्यात् सततं हारि देहिनाम् ॥ २८ ॥
                                        १२.२८च्व्/
                                        म्: हर्तृ ॥ 12.28 ॥
verses.english: What is mixed with pain and does not give satisfaction to the soul one may know (to be the quality of) Activity, which is difficult to conquer, and which ever draws embodied (souls towards sensual objects).

verses.text:
यत् तु स्यान् मोहसंयुक्तम् अव्यक्तं विषयात्मकम् ।
अप्रतर्क्यम् अविज्ञेयं तमस् तद् उपधारयेत् ॥ २९ ॥
verses.english: What is coupled with delusion, what has the character of an undiscernible mass, what cannot be fathomed by reasoning, what cannot be fully known, one must consider (as the quality of) Darkness.

verses.text:
त्रयाणाम् अपि च-एतेषां गुणानां यः फल.उदयः ।
अग्र्यो मध्यो जघन्यश् च तं प्रवक्ष्याम्य् अशेषतः ॥ ३०
                                    ॥
verses.english: I will, moreover, fully describe the results which arise from these three qualities, the excellent ones, the middling ones, and the lowest.

verses.text:
वेदाभ्यासस् तपो ज्ञानं शौचम् इन्द्रियनिग्रहः ।
धर्मक्रिया-आत्मचिन्ता च सात्त्विकं गुणलक्षणम् ॥ ३१
                                    ॥
verses.english: The study of the Vedas, austerity, (the pursuit of) knowledge, purity, control over the organs, the performance of meritorious acts and meditation on the Soul, (are) the marks of the quality of Goodness.

verses.text:
आरम्भरुचिता-अधैर्यम् असत्कार्य.परिग्रहः ।
विषय.उपसेवा च-अजस्रं राजसं गुणलक्षणम् ॥ ३२
                                    ॥
verses.english: Delighting in undertakings, want of firmness, commission of sinful acts, and continual indulgence in sensual pleasures, (are) the marks of the quality of Activity.

verses.text:
लोभः स्वप्नो ऽधृतिः क्रौर्यं नास्तिक्यं भिन्नवृत्तिता
                                    ।
याचिष्णुता प्रमादश् च तामसं गुणलक्षणम् ॥ ३३ ॥
verses.english: Covetousness, sleepiness, pusillanimity, cruelty, atheism, leading an evil life, a habit of soliciting favours, and inattentiveness, are the marks of the quality of Darkness.

verses.text:
त्रयाणाम् अपि च-एतेषां गुणानां त्रिषु तिष्ठताम् ।
इदं सामासिकं ज्ञेयं क्रमशो गुणलक्षणम् ॥ ३४ ॥
verses.english: Know, moreover, the following to be a brief description of the three qualities, each in its order, as they appear in the three (times, the present, past, and future).

verses.text:
यत् कर्म कृत्वा कुर्वंश् च करिष्यंश् च-एव लज्जति
                                    ।
तज् ज्ञेयं विदुषा सर्वं तामसं गुणलक्षणम् ॥ ३५
                                    ॥
verses.english: When a (man), having done, doing, or being about to do any act, feels ashamed, the learned may know that all (such acts bear) the mark of the quality of Darkness.

verses.text:
येन-अस्मिन् कर्मना लोके ख्यातिम् इच्छति पुष्कलाम् ।
न च शोचत्य् असम्पत्तौ तद् विज्ञेयं तु राजसम् ॥ ३६
                                    ॥
verses.english: But, when (a man) desires (to gain) by an act much fame in this world and feels no sorrow on failing, know that it (bears the mark of the quality of) Activity.

verses.text:
यत् सर्वेण-इच्छति ज्ञातुं यन् न लज्जति च-आचरन्
                                    ।
येन तुष्यति च-आत्मा-अस्य तत् सत्त्वगुणलक्षणम् ॥ ३७
                                    ॥
verses.english: But that (bears) the mark of the quality of Goodness which with his whole (heart) he desires to know, which he is not ashamed to perform, and at which his soul rejoices.

verses.text:
तमसो लक्षणं कामो रजसस् त्व् अर्थ उच्यते ।
सत्त्वस्य लक्षणं धर्मः श्रैष्ठ्यम् एषां यथा.उत्तरम्
                                    ॥ ३८ ॥
verses.english: The craving after sensual pleasures is declared to be the mark of Darkness, (the pursuit of) wealth (the mark) of Activity, (the desire to gain) spiritual merit the mark of Goodness; each later) named quality is) better than the preceding one.

verses.text:
येन यस् तु गुणेन-एषां संसरान् प्रतिपद्यते । १२.३९अव्/ म्: 
                                        येन यांस् तु
तान् समासेन वक्ष्यामि सर्वस्य-अस्य यथाक्रमम् ॥ ३९
                                    ॥
verses.english: I will briefly declare in due order what transmigrations in this whole (world a man) obtains through each of these qualities.

verses.text:
देवत्वं सात्त्विका यान्ति मनुष्यत्वं च राजसाः ।
तिर्यक्त्वं तामसा नित्यम् इत्य् एषा त्रिविधा गतिः ॥ ४०
                                    ॥
verses.english: Those endowed with Goodness reach the state of gods, those endowed with Activity the state of men, and those endowed with Darkness ever sink to the condition of beasts; that is the threefold course of transmigrations.

verses.text:
त्रिविधा त्रिविधा-एषा तु विज्ञेया गौणिकी गतिः ।
अधमा मध्यम.अग्र्या च कर्म.विद्या.विशेषतः ॥ ४१
                                    ॥
verses.english: But know this threefold course of transmigrations that depends on the (three) qualities (to be again) threefold, low, middling, and high, according to the particular nature of the acts and of the knowledge (of each man).

verses.text:
स्थावराः कृमि.कीटाश् च मत्स्याः सर्पाः स.कच्छपाः
                                    ।
पशवश् च मृगाश् च-एव जघन्या तामसी गतिः ॥ ४२
                                    ॥
verses.english: Immovable (beings), insects, both small and great, fishes, snakes, and tortoises, cattle and wild animals, are the lowest conditions to which (the quality of) Darkness leads.

verses.text:
हस्तिनश् च तुरङ्गाश् च शूद्रा म्लेच्छाश् च गर्हिताः ।
सिंहा व्याघ्रा वराहाश् च मध्यमा तामसी गतिः ॥ ४३
                                    ॥
verses.english: Elephants, horses, Sudras, and despicable barbarians, lions, tigers, and boars (are) the middling states, caused by (the quality of) Darkness.

verses.text:
चारणाश् च सुपर्णाश् च पुरुषाश् च-एव दाम्भिकाः ।
रक्षांसि च पिशाचाश् च तामसीषु-उत्तमा गतिः ॥ ४४
                                    ॥
verses.english: Karanas, Suparnas and hypocrites, Rakshasas and Pisakas (belong to) the highest (rank of) conditions among those produced by Darkness.

verses.text:
झल्ला मल्ला नटाश् च-एव पुरुषाः शस्त्र.वृत्तयः ।
द्यूत.पान.प्रसक्ताश् च जघन्या राजसी गतिः ॥ ४५
                                    ॥
verses.english: Ghallas, Mallas, Natas, men who subsist by despicable occupations and those addicted to gambling and drinking (form) the lowest (order of) conditions caused by Activity.

verses.text:
राजानः क्षत्रियाश् च-एव राज्ञां च-एव पुरोहिताः ।
वाद.युद्ध.प्रधानाश् च मध्यमा राजसी गतिः ॥ ४६
                                    ॥
verses.english: Kings and Kshatriyas, the domestic priests of kings, and those who delight in the warfare of disputations (constitute) the middling (rank of the) states caused by Activity.

verses.text:
गन्धर्वा गुह्यका यक्षा विबुधानुचराश् च ये ।
तथा-एव-अप्सरसः सर्वा राजसीषु-उत्तमा गतिः ॥ ४७
                                    ॥
verses.english: The Gandharvas, the Guhyakas, and the servants of the gods, likewise the Apsarases, (belong all to) the highest (rank of) conditions produced by Activity.

verses.text:
तापसा यतयो विप्रा ये च वैमानिका गणाः ।
नक्षत्राणि च दैत्याश् च प्रथमा सात्त्विकी गतिः ॥ ४८
                                    ॥
verses.english: Hermits, ascetics, Brahmanas, the crowds of the Vaimanika deities, the lunar mansions, and the Daityas (form) the first (and lowest rank of the) existences caused by Goodness.

verses.text:
यज्वान ऋषयो देवा वेदा ज्योतींषि वत्सराः ।
पितरश् च-एव साध्याश् च द्वितीया सात्त्विकी गतिः ॥ ४९
                                    ॥
verses.english: Sacrificers, the sages, the gods, the Vedas, the heavenly lights, the years, the manes, and the Sadhyas (constitute) the second order of existences, caused by Goodness.

verses.text:
ब्रह्मा विश्वसृजो धर्मो महान् अव्यक्तम् एव च ।
उत्तमां सात्त्विकीम् एतां गतिम् आहुर् मनीषिणः ॥ ५० ॥
verses.english: The sages declare Brahma, the creators of the universe, the law, the Great One, and the Undiscernible One (to constitute) the highest order of beings produced by Goodness.

verses.text:
एष सर्वः समुद्दिष्टस् त्रि.प्रकारस्य कर्मणः । १२.५१अव्/ म्: 
                                        त्रिः.प्रकारस्य
त्रिविधस् त्रिविधः कृत्स्नः संसारः सार्वभौतिकः ॥
                                    ५१ ॥
verses.english: Thus (the result) of the threefold action, the whole system of transmigrations which (consists) of three classes, (each) with three subdivisions, and which includes all created beings, has been fully pointed out.

verses.text:
इन्द्रियाणां प्रसङ्गेन धर्मस्य-असेवनेन च ।
पापान् संयान्ति संसारान् अविद्वांसो नराधमाः ॥ ५२
                                    ॥
verses.english: In consequence of attachment to (the objects of) the senses, and in consequence of the non-performance of their duties, fools, the lowest of men, reach the vilest births.

verses.text:
यां यां योनिं तु जीवो ऽयं येन येन-इह कर्मणा ।
क्रमशो याति लोके ऽस्मिंस् तत् तत् सर्वं निबोधत ॥ ५३
                                    ॥
verses.english: What wombs this individual soul enters in this world and in consequence of what actions, learn the particulars of that at large and in due order.

verses.text:
बहून् वर्षगणान् घोरान् नरकान् प्राप्य तत्क्षयात् ।
संसारान् प्रतिपद्यन्ते महापातकिनस् त्व् इमान् ॥ ५४
                                    ॥
verses.english: Those who committed mortal sins (mahapataka), having passed during large numbers of years through dreadful hells, obtain, after the expiration of (that term of punishment), the following births.

verses.text:
श्व.सूकर.खर.उष्ट्राणां गो.ऽज.अवि.मृग.पक्षिणां ।
चण्डाल.पुक्कसानां च ब्रह्महा योनिम् ऋच्छति ॥ ५५
                                    ॥
verses.english: The slayer of a Brahmana enters the womb of a dog, a pig, an ass, a camel, a cow, a goat, a sheep, a deer, a bird, a Kandala, and a Pukkasa.

verses.text:
कृमि.कीट.पतङ्गानां विष्.भुजां च-एव पक्षिणाम् ।
हिंस्राणां च-एव सत्त्वानां सुरापो ब्राह्मणो व्रजेत् ॥ ५६
                                    ॥
verses.english: A Brahmana who drinks (the spirituous liquor called) Sura shall enter (the bodies) of small and large insects, of moths, of birds, feeding on ordure, and of destructive beasts.

verses.text:
लूता.अहि.सरटानां च तिरश्चां च-अम्बुचारिणाम् ।
हिंस्राणां च पिशाचानां स्तेनो विप्रः सहस्रशः ॥ ५७
                                    ॥
verses.english: A Brahmana who steals (the gold of a Brahmana shall pass) a thousand times (through the bodies) of spiders, snakes and lizards, of aquatic animals and of destructive Pisakas.

verses.text:
तृण.गुल्म.लतानां च क्रव्यादां दंष्ट्रिणाम् अपि ।
क्रूरकर्मकृतां च-एव शतशो गुरुतल्पगः ॥ ५८ ॥
verses.english: The violator of a Guru's bed (enters) a hundred times (the forms) of grasses, shrubs, and creepers, likewise of carnivorous (animals) and of (beasts) with fangs and of those doing cruel deeds.

verses.text:
हिंस्रा भवन्ति क्रव्यादाः कृमयो ऽमेध्यभक्षिणः ।
परस्परादिनः स्तेनाः प्रेत्य-अन्त्यस्त्रीनिषेविणः ॥ ५९
                                    ॥
verses.english: Men who delight in doing hurt (become) carnivorous (animals); those who eat forbidden food, worms; thieves, creatures consuming their own kind; those who have intercourse with women of the lowest castes, Pretas.

verses.text:
संयोगं पतितैर् गत्वा परस्य-एव च योषितम् ।
अपहृत्य च विप्रस्वं भवति ब्रह्मराक्षसः ॥ ६०
                                    ॥
verses.english: He who has associated with outcasts, he who has approached the wives of other men, and he who has stolen the property of a Brahmana become Brahmarakshasas.

verses.text:
मणि.मुक्ता.प्रवालानि हृत्वा लोभेन मानवः ।
विविधाणि च रत्नानि जायते हेमकर्तृषु ॥ ६१ ॥
verses.english: A man who out of greed has stolen gems, pearls or coral, or any of the many other kinds of precious things, is born among the goldsmiths.

verses.text:
धान्यं हृत्वा भवत्य् आखुः कांस्यं हंसो जलं प्लवः
                                    ।
मधु दंशः पयः काको रसं श्वा नकुलो घृतम् ॥ ६२
                                    ॥
verses.english: For stealing grain (a man) becomes a rat, for stealing yellow metal a Hamsa, for stealing water a Plava, for stealing honey a stinging insect, for stealing milk a crow, for stealing condiments a dog, for stealing clarified butter an ichneumon;

verses.text:
मांसं गृध्रो वपां मद्गुस् तैलं तैलपकः खगः
                                    ।
चीरीवाकस् तु लवणं बलाका शकुनिर् दधि ॥ ६३ ॥
verses.english: For stealing meat a vulture, for stealing fat a cormorant, for stealing oil a winged animal (of the kind called) Tailapaka, for stealing salt a cricket, for stealing sour milk a bird (of the kind called) Balaka.

verses.text:
कौशेयं तित्तिरिर् हृत्वा क्षौमं हृत्वा तु दर्दुरः ।
कार्पासतान्तवं क्रौञ्चो गोधा गां वाग्गुदो गुडम् ॥ ६४
                                    ॥
verses.english: For stealing silk a partridge, for stealing linen a frog, for stealing cotton-cloth a crane, for stealing a cow an iguana, for stealing molasses a flying-fox;

verses.text:
छुच्छुन्दरिः शुभान् गन्धान् पत्रशाकं तु बर्हिणः ।
                                        १२.६५अव्/
                                        म्: छुच्छुन्दरीः
श्वावित् कृतान्नं विविधम् अकृतान्नं तु शल्यकः ॥ ६५
                                    ॥
verses.english: For stealing fine perfumes a musk-rat, for stealing vegetables consisting of leaves a peacock, for stealing cooked food of various kinds a porcupine, for stealing uncooked food a hedgehog.

verses.text:
बको भवति हृत्वा-अग्निं गृहकारी ह्य् उपस्करम् ।
रक्तानि हृत्वा वासांसि जायते जीवजीवकः ॥ ६६ ॥
verses.english: For stealing fire he becomes a heron, for stealing household-utensils a mason-wasp, for stealing dyed clothes a francolin-partridge;

verses.text:
वृको मृग.इभं व्याघ्रो ऽश्वं फल.मूलं तु मर्कटः
                                    ।
स्त्रीम् ऋक्षः स्तोकको वारि यानान्य् उष्ट्रः पशून् अजः ॥ ६७
                                    ॥
verses.english: For stealing a deer or an elephant a wolf, for stealing a horse a tiger, for stealing fruit and roots a monkey, for stealing a woman a bear, for stealing water a black-white cuckoo, for stealing vehicles a camel, for stealing cattle a he-goat.

verses.text:
यद् वा तद् वा परद्रव्यम् अपहृत्य बलात्-नरः ।
अवश्यं याति तिर्यक्त्वं जग्ध्वा च-एव-अहुतं हविः ॥
                                    ६८ ॥
verses.english: That man who has forcibly taken away any kind of property belonging to another, or who has eaten sacrificial food (of) which (no portion) had been offered, inevitably becomes an animal.

verses.text:
स्त्रियो ऽप्य् एतेन कल्पेन हृत्वा दोषम् अवाप्नुयुः ।
एतेषाम् एव जन्तूनां भार्यात्वम् उपयान्ति ताः ॥ ६९ ॥
verses.english: Women, also, who in like manner have committed a theft, shall incur guilt; they will become the females of those same creatures (which have been enumerated above).

verses.text:
स्वेभ्यः स्वेभ्यस् तु कर्मभ्यश् च्युता वर्णा ह्य् अनापदि
                                    ।
पापान् संसृत्य संसारान् प्रेष्यतां यान्ति शत्रुषु ॥ ७० ॥
                                        १२.७०च्व्/
                                        म्: यान्ति दस्युषु ॥ 12.70 ॥
verses.english: But (men of the four) castes who have relinquished without the pressure of necessity their proper occupations, will become the servants of Dasyus, after migrating into despicable bodies.

verses.text:
वान्ताश्य् उल्कामुखः प्रेतो विप्रो धर्मात् स्वकाच् च्युतः
                                    ।
अमेध्य.कुणपाशी च क्षत्रियः कटपूतनः ॥ ७१ ॥ १२.७१च्व्/ म्: 
                                        कूटपूतनः ॥ 12.71 ॥
verses.english: A Brahmana who has fallen off from his duty (becomes) an Ulkamukha Preta, who feeds on what has been vomited; and a Kshatriya, a Kataputana (Preta), who eats impure substances and corpses.

verses.text:
मैत्राक्षज्योतिकः प्रेतो वैश्यो भवति पूयभुक् । १२.७२अव्/ म्: 
                                        मैत्राक्षिज्योतिकः
चैलाशकश् च भवति शूद्रो धर्मात् स्वकाच् च्युतः ॥ ७२
                                    ॥
verses.english: A Vaisya who has fallen off from his duty becomes a Maitrakshagyotika Preta, who feeds on pus; and a Sudra, a Kailasaka (Preta, who feeds on moths).

verses.text:
यथा यथा निषेवन्ते विषयान् विषय.आत्मकाः ।
तथा तथा कुशलता तेषां तेषु-उपजायते ॥ ७३ ॥
verses.english: In proportion as sensual men indulge in sensual pleasures, in that same proportion their taste for them grows.

verses.text:
ते ऽभ्यासात् कर्मणां तेषां पापानाम् अल्प.बुद्धयः ।
सम्प्राप्नुवन्ति दुःखानि तासु तास्व् इह योनिषु ॥ ७४
                                    ॥
verses.english: By repeating their sinful acts those men of small understanding suffer pain here (below) in various births;

verses.text:
तामिस्रादिषु च-उग्रेषु नरकेषु विवर्तनम् ।
असिपत्रवनादीनि बन्धन.छेदनानि च ॥ ७५ ॥
verses.english: (The torture of) being tossed about in dreadful hells, Tamisra and the rest, (that of) the Forest with sword-leaved trees and the like, and (that of) being bound and mangled;

verses.text:
विविधाश् च-एव सम्पीडाः काक.उलूकैश् च भक्षणम् ।
करम्भवालुकातापान् कुम्भीपाकांश् च दारुणान् ॥ ७६ ॥
verses.english: And various torments, the (pain of) being devoured by ravens and owls, the heat of scorching sand, and the (torture of) being boiled in jars, which is hard to bear;

verses.text:
सम्भवांश् च वियोनीषु दुःख.प्रायासु नित्यशः ।
शीत.आतप.अभिघातांश् च विविधानि भयानि च ॥ ७७
                                    ॥
verses.english: And births in the wombs (of) despicable (beings) which cause constant misery, and afflictions from cold and heat and terrors of various kinds,

verses.text:
असकृद् गर्भवासेषु वासं जन्म च दारुणम् ।
बन्धनानि च काष्ठानि परप्रेष्यत्वम् एव च ॥ ७८ ॥
                                        १२.७८च्व्/
                                        म्: कष्टानि ॥ 12.78 ॥
verses.english: The (pain of) repeatedly lying in various wombs and agonizing births, imprisonment in fetters hard to bear, and the misery of being enslaved by others,

verses.text:
बन्धु.प्रिय.वियोगांश् च संवासं च-एव दुर्जनैः ।
द्रव्यार्जनं च नाशं च मित्र.अमित्रस्य च-अर्जनम् ॥
                                    ७९ ॥
verses.english: And separations from their relatives and dear ones, and the (pain of) dwelling together with the wicked, (labour in) gaining wealth and its loss, (trouble in) making friends and (the appearance of) enemies,

verses.text:
जरां च-एव-अ.प्रतीकारां व्याधिभिश् च-उपपीडनम् ।
क्लेशांश् च विविधांस् तांस् तान् मृत्युम् एव च दुर्.जयम् ॥
                                    ८० ॥
verses.english: Old age against which there is no remedy, the pangs of diseases, afflictions of many various kinds, and (finally) unconquerable death.

verses.text:
यादृशेन तु भावेन यद् यत् कर्म निषेवते ।
तादृशेन शरीरेण तत् तत् फलम् उपाश्नुते ॥ ८१ ॥
verses.english: But with whatever disposition of mind (a man) forms any act, he reaps its result in a (future) body endowed with the same quality.

verses.text:
एष सर्वः समुद्दिष्टः कर्मणां वः फल.उदयः ।
नैःश्रेयसकरं कर्म विप्रस्य-इदं निबोधत ॥ ८२
                                    ॥
verses.english: All the results, proceeding from actions, have been thus pointed out; learn (next) those acts which secure supreme bliss to a Brahmana.

verses.text:
वेदाभ्यासस् तपो ज्ञानम् इन्द्रियाणां च संयमः ।
अहिंसा गुरुसेवा च निःश्रेयसकरं परम् ॥ ८३ ॥
verses.english: Studying the Veda, (practising) austerities, (the acquisition of true) knowledge, the subjugation of the organs, abstention from doing injury, and serving the Guru are the best means for attaining supreme bliss.

verses.text:
सर्वेषाम् अपि च-एतेषां शुभानाम् इह कर्मणाम् ।
किं चित्-श्रेयस्करतरं कर्म-उक्तं पुरुषं प्रति ॥ ८४
                                ॥
verses.english: (If you ask) whether among all these virtuous actions, (performed) here below, (there be) one which has been declared more efficacious (than the rest) for securing supreme happiness to man,

verses.text:
सर्वेषाम् अपि च-एतेषाम् आत्मज्ञानं परं स्मृतम् ।
तद्द् ह्य् अग्र्यं सर्वविद्यानां प्राप्यते ह्य् अमृतं ततः ॥ ८५
                                ॥
verses.english: (The answer is that) the knowledge of the Soul is stated to be the most excellent among all of them; for that is the first of all sciences, because immortality is gained through that.

verses.text:
षण्णाम् एषां तु सर्वेषां कर्मणां प्रेत्य च-इह च ।
श्रेयस्करतरं ज्ञेयं सर्वदा कर्म वैदिकम् ॥ ८६ ॥
verses.english: Among those six (kinds of) actions (enumerated) above, the performance of) the acts taught in the Veda must ever be held to be most efficacious for ensuring happiness in this world and the next.

verses.text:
वैदिके कर्मयोगे तु सर्वाण्य् एतान्य् अशेषतः ।
अन्तर्भवन्ति क्रमशस् तस्मिंस् तस्मिन् क्रियाविधौ ॥ ८७
                                ॥
verses.english: For in the performance of the acts prescribed by the Veda all those (others) are fully comprised, (each) in its turn in the several rules for the rites.

verses.text:
सुखाभ्युदयिकं च-एव नैःश्रेयसिकम् एव च ।
प्रवृत्तं च निवृत्तं च द्विविधं कर्म वैदिकम् ॥ ८८
                                ॥
verses.english: The acts prescribed by the Veda are of two kinds, such as procure an increase of happiness and cause a continuation (of mundane existence, pravritta), and such as ensure supreme bliss and cause a cessation (of mundane existence, nivritta).

verses.text:
इह च-अमुत्र वा काम्यं प्रवृत्तं कर्म कीर्त्यते ।
निष्.कामं ज्ञातपूर्वं तु निवृत्तम् उपदिश्यते ॥ ८९ ॥
verses.english: Acts which secure (the fulfilment of) wishes in this world or in the next are called pravritta (such as cause a continuation of mundane existence); but acts performed without any desire (for a reward), preceded by (the acquisition) of (true) knowledge, are declared to be nivritta (such as cause the cessation of mundane existence).

verses.text:
प्रवृत्तं कर्म संसेव्यं देवानाम् एति साम्यताम् ।
निवृत्तं सेवमानस् तु भूतान्य् अत्येति पञ्च वै ॥ ९० ॥
verses.english: He who sedulously performs acts leading to future births (pravritta) becomes equal to the gods; but he who is intent on the performance of those causing the cessation (of existence, nivritta) indeed, passes beyond (the reach of) the five elements.

verses.text:
सर्वभूतेषु च-आत्मानं सर्वभूतानि च-आत्मनि ।
समं पश्यन्न् आत्मयाजी स्वाराज्यम् अधिगच्छति ॥ ९१ ॥
verses.english: He who sacrifices to the Self (alone), equally recognising the Self in all created beings and all created beings in the Self, becomes (independent like) an autocrat and self-luminous.

verses.text:
यथा.उक्तान्य् अपि कर्माणि परिहाय द्विजोत्तमः ।
आत्मज्ञाने शमे च स्याद् वेदाभ्यासे च यत्नवान् ॥ ९२ ॥
verses.english: After giving up even the above-mentioned sacrificial rites, a Brahmana should exert himself in (acquiring) the knowledge of the Soul, in extinguishing his passions, and in studying the Veda.

verses.text:
एतद्द् हि जन्मसाफल्यं ब्राह्मणस्य विशेषतः ।
प्राप्य-एतत् कृत.कृत्यो हि द्विजो भवति न-अन्यथा ॥ ९३
                                ॥
verses.english: For that secures the attainment of the object of existence, especially in the case of a Brahmana, because by attaining that, not otherwise, a twice-born man has gained all his ends.

verses.text:
पितृ.देव.मनुष्याणां वेदश् चक्षुः सनातनम् ।
अशक्यं च-अप्रमेयं च वेदशास्त्रम् इति स्थितिः ॥ ९४ ॥
verses.english: The Veda is the eternal eye of the manes, gods, and men; the Veda-ordinance (is) both beyond the sphere of (human) power, and beyond the sphere of (human) comprehension; that is a certain fact.

verses.text:
या वेदबाह्याः स्मृतयो याश् च काश् च कुदृष्टयः । १२.९५अव्/ म्: 
                                    श्रुतयो
सर्वास् ता निष्.फलाः प्रेत्य तमो.निष्ठा हि ताः स्मृताः ॥ ९५
                                ॥
verses.english: All those traditions (smriti) and those despicable systems of philosophy, which are not based on the Veda, produce no reward after death; for they are declared to be founded on Darkness.

verses.text:
उत्पद्यन्ते च्यवन्ते च यान्य् अतो ऽन्यानि कानि चित् । १२.९६अव्/ म्: 
                                    उत्पद्यन्ते विनश्यन्ति
तान्य् अर्वाक्कालिकतया निष्.फलान्य् अनृतानि च ॥ ९६ ॥
verses.english: All those (doctrines), differing from the (Veda), which spring up and (soon) perish, are worthless and false, because they are of modern date.

verses.text:
चातुर्वर्ण्यं त्रयो लोकाश् चत्वारश् च-आश्रमाः पृथक् ।
भूतं भव्यं भविष्यं च सर्वं वेदात् प्रसिध्यति ॥ ९७
                                ॥ १२.९७च्व्/ म्: 
                                    भूतं भवद् भविष्यं च ॥ 12.97 ॥
verses.english: The four castes, the three worlds, the four orders, the past, the present, and the future are all severally known by means of the Veda.

verses.text:
शब्दः स्पर्शश् च रूपं च रसो गन्धश् च पञ्चमः ।
वेदाद् एव प्रसूयन्ते प्रसूतिर् गुण.कर्मतः ॥ ९८ ॥
verses.english: Sound, touch, colour, taste, and fifthly smell are known through the Veda alone, (their) production (is) through the (Vedic rites, which in this respect are) secondary acts.

verses.text:
बिभर्ति सर्वभूतानि वेदशास्त्रं सनातनम् ।
तस्माद् एतत् परं मन्ये यत्-जन्तोर् अस्य साधनम् ॥ ९९
                                ॥
verses.english: The eternal lore of the Veda upholds all created beings; hence I hold that to be supreme, which is the means of (securing happiness to) these creatures.

verses.text:
सेनापत्यं च राज्यं च दण्डनेतृत्वम् एव च । १२.१००अव्/ म्: 
                                    सैनापत्यं
सर्वलोकाधिपत्यं च वेदशास्त्रविद् अर्हति ॥ १०० ॥
verses.english: Command of armies, royal authority, the office of a judge, and sovereignty over the whole world he (only) deserves who knows the Veda-science.

verses.text:
यथा जात.बलो वह्निर् दहत्य् आर्द्रान् अपि द्रुमान् ।
तथा दहति वेदज्ञः कर्मजं दोषम् आत्मनः ॥ १०१ ॥
verses.english: As a fire that has gained strength consumes even trees full of sap, even so he who knows the Veda burns out the taint of his soul which arises from (evil) acts.

verses.text:
वेदशास्त्रार्थतत्त्वज्ञो यत्र तत्र-आश्रमे वसन् ।
इह-एव लोके तिष्ठन् स ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते ॥ १०२ ॥
verses.english: In whatever order (a man) who knows the true meaning of the Veda-science may dwell, he becomes even while abiding in this world, fit for the union with Brahman.

verses.text:
अज्ञेभ्यो ग्रन्थिनः श्रेष्ठा ग्रन्थिभ्यो धारिणो वराः ।
धारिभ्यो ज्ञानिनः श्रेष्ठा ज्ञानिभ्यो व्यवसायिनः ॥ १०३
                                ॥
verses.english: (Even forgetful) students of the (sacred) books are more distinguished than the ignorant, those who remember them surpass the (forgetful) students, those who possess a knowledge (of the meaning) are more distinguished than those who (only) remember (the words), men who follow (the teaching of the texts) surpass those who (merely) know (their meaning).

verses.text:
तपो विद्या च विप्रस्य निःश्रेयसकरं परम् ।
तपसा किल्बिषं हन्ति विद्यया-अमृतम् अश्नुते ॥ १०४ ॥
verses.english: Austerity and sacred learning are the best means by which a Brahmana secures supreme bliss; by austerities he destroys guilt, by sacred learning he obtains the cessation of (births and) deaths.

verses.text:
प्रत्यक्षं च-अनुमानं च शास्त्रं च विविधा.आगमम् ।
त्रयं सुविदितं कार्यं धर्मशुद्धिम् अभीप्सता ॥ १०५
                                ॥
verses.english: The three (kinds of evidence), perception, inference, and the (sacred) Institutes which comprise the tradition (of) many (schools), must be fully understood by him who desires perfect correctness with respect to the sacred law.

verses.text:
आर्षं धर्म.उपदेशं च वेदशास्त्र.अविरोधिना ।
यस् तर्केण-अनुसन्धत्ते स धर्मं वेद न-इतरः ॥ १०६
                                ॥
verses.english: He alone, and no other man, knows the sacred law, who explores the (utterances) of the sages and the body of the laws, by (modes of) reasoning, not repugnant to the Veda-lore.

verses.text:
नैःश्रेयसम् इदं कर्म यथा.उदितम् अशेषतः ।
मानवस्य-अस्य शास्त्रस्य रहस्यम् उपदिश्यते ॥ १०७ ॥
                                    १२.१०७च्व्/ म्: 
                                    उपदेक्ष्यते ॥ 12.107 ॥
verses.english: Thus the acts which secure supreme bliss have been exactly and fully described; (now) the secret portion of these Institutes, proclaimed by Manu, will be taught.

verses.text:
अन्.आम्नातेषु धर्मेषु कथं स्याद् इति चेद् भवेत् ।
यं शिष्टा ब्राह्मणा ब्रूयुः स धर्मः स्याद् अशङ्कितः ॥ १०८
                                ॥
verses.english: If it be asked how it should be with respect to (points of) the law which have not been (specially) mentioned, (the answer is), 'that which Brahmanas (who are) Sishtas propound, shall doubtlessly have legal (force).'

verses.text:
धर्मेण-अधिगतो यैस् तु वेदः स.परिबृंहणः ।
ते शिष्टा ब्राह्मणा ज्ञेयाः श्रुति.प्रत्यक्षहेतवः ॥ १०९
                                ॥
verses.english: Those Brahmanas must be considered as Sishtas who, in accordance with the sacred law, have studied the Veda together with its appendages, and are able to adduce proofs perceptible by the senses from the revealed texts.

verses.text:
दश.अवरा वा परिषद्यं धर्मं परिकल्पयेत् ।
त्र्य्.अवरा वा-अपि वृत्तस्था तं धर्मं न विचालयेत् ॥ ११०
                                ॥
verses.english: Whatever an assembly, consisting either of at least ten, or of at least three persons who follow their prescribed occupations, declares to be law, the legal (force of) that one must not dispute.

verses.text:
त्रैविद्यो हेतुकस् तर्की नैरुक्तो धर्मपाठकः ।
त्रयश् च-आश्रमिणः पूर्वे परिषत् स्याद् दश.अवरा ॥ १११
                                ॥
verses.english: Three persons who each know one of the three principal Vedas, a logician, a Mimamsaka, one who knows the Nirukta, one who recites (the Institutes of) the sacred law, and three men belonging to the first three orders shall constitute a (legal) assembly, consisting of at least ten members.

verses.text:
ऋग्वेदविद् यजुर्विद्-च सामवेदविद् एव च ।
त्र्य्.अवरा परिषद्-ज्ञेया धर्मसंशयनिर्णये ॥ ११२ ॥
verses.english: One who knows the Rig-veda, one who knows the Yagur-veda, and one who knows the Sama-veda, shall be known (to form) an assembly consisting of at least three members (and competent) to decide doubtful points of law.

verses.text:
एको ऽपि वेदविद् धर्मं यं व्यवस्येद् द्विजोत्तमः ।
स विज्ञेयः परो धर्मो न-अज्ञानाम् उदितो ऽयुतैः ॥ ११३
                                ॥
verses.english: Even that which one Brahmana versed in the Veda declares to be law, must be considered (to have) supreme legal (force, but) not that which is proclaimed by myriads of ignorant men.

verses.text:
अ.व्रतानाम् अ.मन्त्राणां जातिमात्र.उपजीविनाम् ।
सहस्रशः समेतानां परिषत्त्वं न विद्यते ॥ ११४ ॥
verses.english: Even if thousands of Brahmanas, who have not fulfilled their sacred duties, are unacquainted with the Veda, and subsist only by the name of their caste, meet, they cannot (form) an assembly (for settling the sacred law).

verses.text:
यं वदन्ति तमोभूता मूर्खा धर्मम् अतद्विदः ।
तत्पापं शतधा भूत्वा तद्वक्तॄन् अनुगच्छति ॥ ११५ ॥
verses.english: The sin of him whom dunces, incarnations of Darkness, and unacquainted with the law, instruct (in his duty), falls, increased a hundredfold, on those who propound it.

verses.text:
एतद् वो ऽभिहितं सर्वं निःश्रेयसकरं परम् ।
अस्माद् अप्रच्युतो विप्रः प्राप्नोति परमां गतिम् ॥ ११६ ॥
verses.english: All that which is most efficacious for securing supreme bliss has been thus declared to you; a Brahmana who does not fall off from that obtains the most excellent state.

verses.text:
एवं स भगवान् देवो लोकानां हितकाम्यया ।
धर्मस्य परमं गुह्यं मम-इदं सर्वम् उक्तवान् ॥ ११७
                                ॥
verses.english: Thus did that worshipful deity disclose to me, through a desire of benefiting mankind, this whole most excellent secret of the sacred law.

verses.text:
सर्वम् आत्मनि सम्पश्येत् सत्-च-असत्-च समाहितः ।
सर्वं ह्य् आत्मनि सम्पश्यन् न-अधर्मे कुरुते मनः ॥ ११८
                                ॥ १२.११८च्व्/ म्: 
                                    मतिम् ॥ 12.118 ॥
verses.english: Let (every Brahmana), concentrating his mind, fully recognise in the Self all things, both the real and the unreal, for he who recognises the universe in the Self, does not give his heart to unrighteousness.

verses.text:
आत्मा-एव देवताः सर्वाः सर्वम् आत्मन्य् अवस्थितम् ।
आत्मा हि जनयत्य् एषां कर्मयोगं शरीरिणाम् ॥ ११९ ॥
verses.english: The Self alone is the multitude of the gods, the universe rests on the Self; for the Self produces the connexion of these embodied (spirits) with actions.

verses.text:
खं सन्निवेशयेत् खेषु चेष्टन.स्पर्शने ऽनिलम् ।
पक्ति.दृष्ट्योः परं तेजः स्नेहे ऽपो गां च मूर्तिषु ॥ १२०
                                ॥
verses.english: Let him meditate on the ether as identical with the cavities (of the body), on the wind as identical with the organs of motions and of touch, on the most excellent light as the same with his digestive organs and his sight, on water as the same with the (corporeal) fluids, on the earth as the same with the solid parts (of his body);

verses.text:
मनसि-इन्दुं दिशः श्रोत्रे क्रान्ते विष्णुं बले हरम् ।
वाच्य् अग्निं मित्रम् उत्सर्गे प्रजने च प्रजापतिम् ॥ १२१
                                ॥
verses.english: On the moon as one with the internal organ, on the quarters of the horizon as one with his sense of hearing, on Vishnu as one with his (power of) motion, on Hara as the same with his strength, on Agni (Fire) as identical with his speech, on Mitra as identical with his excretions, and on Pragapati as one with his organ of generation.

verses.text:
प्रशासितारं सर्वेषाम् अणीयांसम् अणोर् अपि ।
रुक्म.आभं स्वप्नधीगम्यं विद्यात् तं पुरुषं परम् ॥ १२२
                                ॥
verses.english: Let him know the supreme Male (Purusha, to be) the sovereign ruler of them all, smaller even than small, bright like gold, and perceptible by the intellect (only when) in (a state of) sleep (-like abstraction).

verses.text:
एतम् एके वदन्त्य् अग्निं मनुम् अन्ये प्रजापतिम् ।
इन्द्रम् एके परे प्राणम् अपरे ब्रह्म शाश्वतम् ॥ १२३ ॥
verses.english: Some call him Agni (Fire), others Manu, the Lord of creatures, others Indra, others the vital air, and again others eternal Brahman.

verses.text:
एष सर्वाणि भूतानि पञ्चभिर् व्याप्य मूर्तिभिः ।
जन्म.वृद्धि.क्षयैर् नित्यं संसारयति चक्रवत् ॥ १२४
                                ॥
verses.english: He pervades all created beings in the five forms, and constantly makes them, by means of birth, growth and decay, revolve like the wheels (of a chariot).

verses.text:
एवं यः सर्वभूतेषु पश्यत्य् आत्मानम् आत्मना ।
स सर्वसमताम् एत्य ब्रह्म-अभ्येति परं पदम् ॥ १२५
                                ॥
verses.english: He who thus recognises the Self through the Self in all created beings, becomes equal (-minded) towards all, and enters the highest state, Brahman.

verses.text:
इत्य् एतन् मानवं शास्त्रं भृगुप्रोक्तं पठन् द्विजः ।
भवत्य् आचारवान् नित्यं यथा.इष्टां प्राप्नुयाद् गतिम् ॥ १२६
                                ॥
verses.english: A twice-born man who recites these Institutes, revealed by Manu, will be always virtuous in conduct, and will reach whatever condition he desires.
